title: Finite set
description: A set X is finite if it is bijective with {1,…,n} for some natural number n≥0; its cardinality is n.

title: Integer
description: An integer is an element of the ordered ring ℤ, obtained by adjoining additive inverses to the natural numbers.

title: Real number
description: A real number is an element of a complete ordered field ℝ; completeness means every nonempty subset bounded above has a least upper bound.

title: Real sequence
description: A real sequence is a function a:ℕ₊→ℝ, written (aₙ)ₙ≥1.

title: Limit of a real sequence
description: A sequence (aₙ) converges to L∈ℝ if for every ε>0 there is N such that n≥N implies abs(aₙ−L)<ε.

title: Convergent real series
description: The series ∑ₙ≥1aₙ converges to S if its sequence of partial sums converges to S.

title: Sum of a nonnegative series
description: For aₙ≥0, define ∑ₙ≥1aₙ as the supremum of its finite partial sums; the value may be infinite.

title: Factorial
Factorial domination of fixed exponentials
description: For every fixed real C>0, the sequence Cⁿ/n! tends to zero.

title: Real polynomial
description: A real polynomial is a finite sum ∑ⱼ₌₀ᵐaⱼxʲ with real coefficients and nonnegative integer m.

title: Integer polynomial
description: An integer polynomial is a real polynomial all of whose coefficients lie in ℤ.

title: Derivative of a real function
description: The derivative f′(x) is the finite limit of (f(x+h)−f(x))/h as h→0, when it exists. Higher derivatives are defined by iteration.

title: Riemann integral
description: A bounded f:[a,b]→ℝ has Riemann integral I if all tagged Riemann sums approach I as the maximum length of the partition intervals tends to zero.

title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for continuous integrands
description: If f is continuous on [a,b], then F(x)=∫ₐˣf(t)dt has derivative f on (a,b); any antiderivative G of f satisfies ∫ₐᵇf=G(b)−G(a).

title: Integration by parts for C¹ real functions
description: For u,v∈C¹([a,b]), ∫ₐᵇuv′=u(b)v(b)−u(a)v(a)−∫ₐᵇu′v.

title: Rational number
description: A real x is rational if x=a/b for integers a,b with b≠0; otherwise it is irrational.

title: Real sine function
description: The sine function is defined by the everywhere convergent power series sin(x)=∑ₖ≥0(−1)ᵏx²ᵏ⁺¹/(2k+1)!.

title: π
description: π is the least positive zero of the real sine function and equals the circumference-to-diameter ratio of a Euclidean circle.

title: Irrationality of π
description: There are no integers a,b with b≠0 such that π=a/b.

title: Cesàro convergence theorem
description: If aₙ→L, then (a₁+···+aₙ)/n→L.

title: Prime number
description: An integer p>1 is prime if its only positive divisors are 1 and p.

title: Congruence modulo an integer
description: The relation a≡b (mod m) means that m divides a−b.

title: Involution of a finite set
description: An involution of a finite set X is a map f:X→X with f(f(x))=x for all x∈X.

title: Fixed point of a self-map
description: A fixed point of f:X→X is an x∈X satisfying f(x)=x. The fixed-point set is Fix(f)={x∈X:f(x)=x}.

title: Fixed-point parity lemma for finite involutions
description: If f is an involution of a finite set X, then X and Fix(f) have the same cardinality modulo two.

title: Zagier's involution
description: For a prime p≡1 (mod 4), let Sₚ={(x,y,z)∈ℤ₊³:x²+4yz=p}. Send (x,y,z) to (x+2z,z,y−x−z) if x<y−z, to (2y−x,y,x−y+z) if y−z<x<2y, and to (x−2y,x−y+z,y) if x>2y. These cases exhaust Sₚ and define an involution with the unique fixed point (1,1,(p−1)/4).

title: Fermat's two-square theorem
description: A prime p is a²+b² for integers a,b if and only if p=2 or p≡1 (mod 4).

title: Euclidean space ℝᵈ
description: For d≥1, ℝᵈ consists of d-tuples of real numbers with distance dist(x,y)=(∑ᵢ(xᵢ−yᵢ)²)¹ᐟ².

title: Convex subset of ℝᵈ
description: C⊆ℝᵈ is convex if (1−t)x+ty∈C whenever x,y∈C and 0≤t≤1.

title: Convex hull
description: The smallest convex set containing a given set of points.

title: Convex position
description: A finite P⊂ℝ² is in convex position if no point of P is in the convex hull of the other points.

title: General position for planar point sets
description: A finite P⊂ℝ² is in general position here if no three distinct points of P lie on one line.

title: Coloring of r-element subsets
description: An r-subset coloring is a map from the r-element subsets of X to C.

title: Homogeneous set for a subset coloring
description: H⊆X is homogeneous for c if c is constant on the r-element subsets of H.

title: Finite Ramsey theorem for uniform subset colorings
description: For integers r≥1 and s,t≥r, there is N such that every red–blue coloring of r-subsets of an N-element set has a red-homogeneous s-set or a blue-homogeneous t-set.

title: Two-color uniform Ramsey number Rᵣ(s,t)
description: Rᵣ(s,t) is the least N such that every red–blue r-subset coloring on N elements has a red-homogeneous s-set or a blue-homogeneous t-set; set it to ∞ if there is no such N.

title: Finite simple undirected graph
description: A finite simple graph is (V,E), where V is finite and E is a set of two-element subsets of V.

title: Clique
description: A set of vertices of a graph, every two of which are adjacent.

title: Independent set in a graph
description: A set of vertices in a graph containing no edge.

title: Monotone subsequence
description: A strictly increasing subsequence has indices i₁<···<iₖ and values aᵢ₁<···<aᵢₖ; a decreasing subsequence reverses the value comparisons and retains increasing indices.

title: Erdős–Szekeres monotone subsequence theorem
description: For integers r,s≥2, every sequence of (r−1)(s−1)+1 distinct real numbers has an increasing subsequence of length r or a decreasing subsequence of length s, both strict. The threshold is sharp.

title: Cups and caps of planar point sets
description: For planar points p₁,…,pₖ with strictly increasing x-coordinates, a k-cup has strictly increasing successive slopes, and a k-cap has strictly decreasing successive slopes.

title: Binomial coefficient
description: For integers 0≤k≤n, binom(n,k) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set and equals n!/(k!(n−k)!).

title: Erdős–Szekeres cups–caps theorem
description: For r,s≥3, any binom(r+s−4,r−2)+1 planar points with no three collinear and with distinct x-coordinates contain an r-cup or an s-cap. This threshold is sharp for the cups–caps problem.

title: Erdős–Szekeres convex polygon theorem
description: For each n≥3 there is N such that every planar set of at least N points in general position contains n points in convex position. The 1935 proof gives N≤binom(2n−4,n−2)+1.

title: Esther Klein's five-point theorem
description: Every set of five planar points in general position contains four points in convex position.

title: Monotone-gap selection theorem for points on a line
description: For r,s≥2, any binom(r+s−4,r−2)+1 distinct points on a line contain r points with nondecreasing consecutive gaps or s points with nonincreasing consecutive gaps.

title: Rooted finitely branching tree
description: A rooted tree is a connected acyclic graph with a distinguished root. It is finitely branching if every vertex has finitely many children, meaning adjacent vertices one edge farther from the root.

title: König's infinity lemma
description: Every infinite rooted finitely branching tree has an infinite simple path starting at its root.

title: Geometric n-simplex
description: An n-simplex is conv(v₀,…,vₙ), where v₁−v₀,…,vₙ−v₀ are linearly independent. Its faces are the hulls of subsets of its vertices.

title: Triangulation of a geometric simplex
description: A triangulation of S is a finite collection of simplices covering S, closed under faces, such that any two members intersect in a common face or not at all.

title: Barycentric subdivision
description: Vertices are the barycenters b(F) of nonempty faces F; a simplex corresponds to a chain F₀⊊···⊊Fₖ and has vertices b(F₀),…,b(Fₖ).

title: Sperner labeling of a triangulated simplex
description: For S=conv(v₀,…,vₙ), label each triangulation vertex by an element of {0,…,n}; a vertex on conv(vᵢ:i∈I) must have a label in I.

title: Sperner's lemma
description: Every Sperner-labeled triangulation of an n-simplex has an odd number of elementary n-simplices carrying all n+1 labels. In particular there is at least one.

title: Dual Sperner labeling on a barycentrically subdivided simplex
description: On a barycentric subdivision of the standard n-simplex Δⁿ, n≥1, label vertices by {0,…,n}. A boundary vertex x must receive a label i with xᵢ=0; interior labels are unrestricted.

title: Dual Sperner lemma for barycentric subdivisions
description: For m≥1, the m-fold barycentric subdivision of a simplex satisfying the dual zero-coordinate boundary labeling rule contains an elementary n-simplex with all n+1 labels.

title: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem in ℝᵈ
description: Every bounded sequence in Euclidean space ℝᵈ has a subsequence converging coordinatewise to a point of ℝᵈ.

title: Closed preference correspondence with finite alternatives
description: For metric X and finite alternatives A, P:X→nonempty subsets of A is a closed preference correspondence if {x:a∈P(x)} is closed in X for every a∈A. Ties are allowed.

title: Envy-free allocation of finitely many shares
description: An allocation is envy-free if each participant weakly prefers their own assigned share to every other share, evaluated at that same allocation.

title: Envy-free interval cake division theorem
description: For n participants and consecutive pieces of [0,1] parametrized by Δⁿ⁻¹, suppose preferred-piece sets are nonempty and closed and exclude empty pieces whenever a positive-length piece exists. Then some partition admits a bijection assigning every participant a preferred piece.

title: Su's rental harmony theorem
description: For n participants and rooms, let pᵢ≥0 and ∑pᵢ=R>0. Suppose preferred-room sets are nonempty and closed, and contain only free rooms whenever some room is free. Then some price vector admits a bijection assigning every participant a preferred room.

title: Envy-free division of an interval of chores
description: For n participants and consecutive chore pieces parametrized by Δⁿ⁻¹, suppose preferred-piece sets are nonempty and closed and contain only empty pieces whenever an empty piece is available. Then there is a partition and bijection assigning each participant a preferred piece.

title: Brouwer fixed-point theorem
description: Every continuous f:Δⁿ→Δⁿ has a fixed point. The equivalent closed-ball formulation belongs to this same theorem concept.

title: σ-algebra
description: A σ-algebra on Ω contains Ω and is closed under complements in Ω and countable unions.

title: Measure
description: A measure μ maps a σ-algebra to [0,∞], sends ∅ to 0, and satisfies μ(⋃ₙAₙ)=∑ₙμ(Aₙ) for every pairwise disjoint sequence of measurable sets.

title: Lebesgue integral
description: For measurable f≥0, ∫f dμ is the supremum of integrals of nonnegative simple functions below f. For signed f with ∫abs(f)dμ<∞, define ∫f=∫f⁺−∫f⁻.

title: Probability space
description: A probability space is (Ω,𝔽,P), where 𝔽 is a σ-algebra on Ω and P is a measure on 𝔽 with P(Ω)=1.

title: Real-valued random variable
description: A real-valued random variable is a measurable map from a probability space to ℝ with its Borel σ-algebra.

title: Distribution of a real random variable
description: The distribution μₓ of X is defined by μₓ(B)=P(X∈B) for Borel B⊆ℝ.

title: Expectation of an integrable real random variable
description: If E abs(X)=∫abs(X)dP<∞, the expectation of X is EX=∫X dP.

title: Variance of a real random variable
description: If EX²<∞, then Var(X)=E[(X−EX)²].

title: Pairwise independent random variables
description: A family (Xᵢ) is pairwise independent if P(Xᵢ∈A,Xⱼ∈B)=P(Xᵢ∈A)P(Xⱼ∈B) for all i≠j and Borel A,B⊆ℝ.

title: Independent family of random variables
description: For distinct i₁,…,iₖ and Borel A₁,…,Aₖ, independence requires P(⋂ⱼ{Xᵢⱼ∈Aⱼ})=∏ⱼP(Xᵢⱼ∈Aⱼ).

title: Identically distributed random variables
description: A family is identically distributed when all its random variables have the same distribution.

title: Almost-sure convergence of real random variables
description: Xₙ→X almost surely means P({ω:limₙXₙ(ω)=X(ω)})=1.

title: Chebyshev's inequality
description: If EX²<∞ and t>0, then P(abs(X−EX)≥t)≤Var(X)/t².

title: First Borel–Cantelli lemma
description: If ∑ₙP(Aₙ)<∞, then P(⋂ₘ⋃ₙ≥ₘAₙ)=0: almost surely only finitely many Aₙ occur.

title: Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals
description: If 0≤fₙ≤fₙ₊₁ and fₙ→f pointwise, then ∫fₙdμ increases to ∫f dμ, allowing infinity.

title: Etemadi's strong law of large numbers
description: If (Xₙ) is pairwise independent and identically distributed with E abs(X₁)<∞, then (X₁+···+Xₙ)/n→EX₁ almost surely.

title: Kolmogorov's strong law for iid real random variables
description: If (Xₙ) is jointly independent and identically distributed with E abs(X₁)<∞, then (X₁+···+Xₙ)/n→EX₁ almost surely.

title: Kolmogorov's maximal inequality
description: If X₁,…,Xₙ are independent with EXᵢ=0 and EXᵢ²<∞, then for λ>0, P(max₁≤ₖ≤ₙ abs(∑ᵢ≤ₖXᵢ)≥λ)≤(∑ᵢ≤ₙVar(Xᵢ))/λ².

title: Rectangular average of a real random array
description: For positive integer indices, the rectangular average at (n₁,…,nᵣ) is (∏ⱼnⱼ)⁻¹∑₁≤ᵢⱼ≤ₙⱼXᵢ₁,…,ᵢᵣ. Its joint limit means that every nⱼ tends to infinity.

title: L(log L)ᵏ moment condition
description: X∈L(log L)ᵏ means E[abs(X)(log⁺abs(X))ᵏ]<∞, where log⁺t=max(0,log t) for t>0 and log⁺0=0.

title: Divisor function d(n)
description: d(n) is the number of positive divisors of n, equivalently the number of ordered positive integer pairs (a,b) satisfying ab=n.

title: Divisor summatory bound ∑ₙ≤ₓd(n)=O(x log x)
description: There is an absolute constant C such that ∑₁≤ₙ≤ₓd(n)≤Cx log x for x≥2; the sum counts positive integer pairs (a,b) with ab≤x.

title: Abel's summation formula
description: If Aₖ=∑ⱼ₌₁ᵏaⱼ, then ∑ₖ₌₁ᴺaₖbₖ=A_N b_N+∑ₖ₌₁ᴺ⁻¹Aₖ(bₖ−bₖ₊₁).

title: Etemadi's strong law for random arrays
description: For an r-indexed pairwise independent identically distributed real array with E[abs(X)(log⁺abs(X))ʳ⁻¹]<∞, its rectangular averages converge almost surely to EX as every side length tends to infinity.

title: k-linear category
description: A category whose morphism spaces are vector spaces over a field k and whose composition is k-bilinear. This convention does not require finite sums or a zero object.

title: Monoidal category
description: A category C with a tensor bifunctor C×C→C, a unit object, and natural associativity and unit isomorphisms satisfying the pentagon and triangle identities.

title: Rigid monoidal category
description: A monoidal category in which every object has left and right duals, with evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the zigzag identities.

title: Braided monoidal category
description: A monoidal category with natural isomorphisms c(X,Y):X⊗Y→Y⊗X satisfying the two hexagon identities.

title: Pivotal category
description: A rigid monoidal category with a monoidal natural isomorphism from the identity functor to the double-dual functor.

title: Ribbon category
description: A braided rigid monoidal category with a twist compatible with both the braiding and duality.

title: Trace in a pivotal monoidal category
description: Closing an endomorphism using evaluation, coevaluation and the pivotal structure gives its left and right traces, which lie in End(1). They are scalars when End(1) is the ground field; the two traces need not agree.

title: Karoubi envelope of a category
description: The category obtained by formally splitting idempotent endomorphisms. Its objects are pairs (X,e) with e²=e; a map (X,e)→(Y,f) is a map a:X→Y with a=fae.

title: Negligible morphism in a spherical linear category
description: In a spherical k-linear category with End(1)=k, f:X→Y is negligible if tr(gf)=0 for every g:Y→X. Such morphisms form a tensor ideal.

title: Semisimplification by negligible morphisms
description: Quotient a spherical linear category by its negligible morphisms and take the Karoubi envelope. Under the usual finiteness and nondegeneracy hypotheses this gives a semisimple category; the construction does not guarantee semisimplicity for an arbitrary pivotal category.

title: Simple object in an abelian category
description: A nonzero object whose only subobjects are zero and itself.

title: Semisimple abelian category
description: An abelian category in which every object is a finite direct sum of simple objects.

title: Split simple object in a k-linear abelian category
description: A simple object X in a k-linear abelian category is split if its scalar map k→End(X) is an isomorphism.

title: Split semisimple k-linear category
description: A semisimple k-linear abelian category in which every simple object is split.

title: Primitive idempotent in an algebra
description: A nonzero idempotent that is not a sum of two nonzero orthogonal idempotents. In a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra A, e is primitive exactly when the left ideal Ae is a simple A-module.

title: Schur's lemma
description: A nonzero morphism between simple objects of an abelian category is an isomorphism. Consequently, the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division ring.

title: Braid group
description: Bₙ is generated by σ₁,…,σₙ₋₁, with σᵢσⱼ=σⱼσᵢ for abs(i−j)>1 and σᵢσᵢ₊₁σᵢ=σᵢ₊₁σᵢσᵢ₊₁.

title: Group algebra
description: For a group G and field k, k[G] consists of finite k-linear combinations of group elements, with multiplication extending the group law bilinearly.

title: Hopf algebra
description: A unital associative algebra H with coassociative coproduct Δ:H→H⊗H and counit ε:H→k that are algebra homomorphisms, and an antipode S satisfying m(S⊗id)Δ=m(id⊗S)Δ=ηε, where m and η are multiplication and unit.

title: Lie algebra 𝔤₂
description: The 14-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra of exceptional type G₂.

title: Quantum group U_q(𝔤₂)
description: The Drinfeld–Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra of 𝔤₂; in the braid-generation theorem q is indeterminate and the coefficient field is ℂ(q).

title: Seven-dimensional fundamental representation of U_q(𝔤₂)
description: The irreducible fundamental U_q(𝔤₂)-module of dimension seven, deforming the smallest nontrivial representation of 𝔤₂.

title: Intertwiner of algebra representations
description: A linear map T between modules over an algebra A such that T(av)=aT(v) for every a∈A and v in the source module.

title: Tensor power of a Hopf-algebra representation
description: The representation on V⊗n obtained by applying the iterated coproduct before acting on its n factors.

title: Centralizer algebra of a representation
description: For an H-module W, End_H(W) is the algebra of linear endomorphisms commuting with H; multiplication is composition.

title: Universal R-matrix
description: An invertible element R in a suitable completion of H⊗H that conjugates the coproduct to its opposite and satisfies the two coproduct compatibility identities; on modules, flip∘R gives a braiding.

title: Braid-group action on a tensor power
description: For an object V in a braided monoidal category, σᵢ acts on V⊗n as the braiding c(V,V) on factors i,i+1 and the identity on all other factors.

title: Strongly multiplicity-free highest-weight representation
description: A finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight representation of a complex semisimple Lie algebra or its generic Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group, with one-dimensional weight spaces and weights totally ordered by the root order. The root order compares weights whose difference is a nonnegative integral combination of simple roots.

title: Kuperberg's G₂ spider
description: Kuperberg’s G₂ spider T(G₂) is the ℂ(q)-linear monoidal category whose objects are natural numbers and whose morphisms n→m are ℂ(q)-linear combinations of G₂ webs in a rectangle with n bottom and m top boundary points, modulo Kuperberg’s local relations: a loop equals q¹⁰+q⁸+q²+1+q⁻²+q⁻⁸+q⁻¹⁰, a monogon vanishes, and bigons, triangles, squares and pentagons reduce to webs with fewer vertices. Composition is vertical stacking, tensor product is juxtaposition, and Kuperberg’s crossing formula, a combination of four webs, makes it braided. Here q is Morrison’s parameter; Kuperberg’s parameter is q².

title: G₂ web
description: A compact one-dimensional subset of a closed disc or rectangle that near each point looks, up to homeomorphism, like an empty disc, an open arc or three arcs meeting at a trivalent vertex, and near the boundary like an empty half-disc or one arc ending on the boundary; closed loop components are allowed and webs are considered up to isotopy fixing the boundary. These planar trivalent graphs present the morphisms of Kuperberg’s G₂ spider.

title: Non-elliptic G₂ web
description: A G₂ web with no closed loop components and with at least six edges on every internal face.

title: Euler measure of a surface with assigned corner angles
description: For a compact surface F with finitely many assigned boundary corner angles θᵢ, its Euler measure is e(F)=χ(F)−∑ᵢ(π−θᵢ)/(2π). Smooth portions of the boundary contribute no corner correction.

title: Tilting module for a quantum group
description: A finite-dimensional module admitting both a filtration by Weyl modules and a filtration by dual Weyl modules.

title: Kuperberg's G₂ web-basis theorem
description: Over ℂ(q), each morphism space in the G₂ spider has a basis consisting of the non-elliptic webs.

title: Kuperberg's G₂ spider equivalence theorem
description: Over ℂ(q), the G₂ spider is equivalent, as a braided tensor category, to the category whose objects are tensor powers of the seven-dimensional U_q(𝔤₂)-module and whose morphisms are intertwiners.

title: Braid generation of the G₂ tensor centralizer
description: For the seven-dimensional U_q(𝔤₂)-module V over ℂ(q), the R-matrix representation induces a surjective algebra map ℂ(q)[Bₙ]→End_{U_q(𝔤₂)}(V⊗n) for every n.

title: Lehrer–Zhang braid-generation theorem
description: For a strongly multiplicity-free irreducible representation V of a generic Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group, the braid-group image generates End_U(V⊗n) as an algebra for every n.

title: Fusion category
description: A k-linear semisimple abelian rigid monoidal category with finitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects, finite-dimensional morphism spaces, a k-bilinear tensor product and End(1)=k. Over a non-algebraically closed field, simple objects need not be split.

title: Split fusion category
description: A fusion category in which every simple object has endomorphism algebra k.

title: Scalar extension of a linear category
description: For k⊂K, replace each morphism space Hom(X,Y) by Hom(X,Y)⊗_k K, keeping the same objects and extending composition.

title: Rational form of a tensor category
description: For fields k⊂K and a semisimple K-linear abelian tensor category C_K, a rational form over k is a semisimple k-linear abelian tensor category C_k with a tensor equivalence Kar(C_k⊗_k K)≃C_K. The additional tensor structure must be preserved.

title: Complete rational form of a tensor category
description: A rational form C_k of C_K for which C_k⊗_k K is already idempotent complete, so C_k⊗_k K≃C_K without adding new summands.

title: Cyclotomic field
description: A number field ℚ(ζₙ) generated by a primitive nth root of unity.

title: Cyclotomic integer
description: An algebraic integer lying in a cyclotomic field.

title: Galois conjugate of a fusion category
description: For a fusion category over ℂ with a complete form over a number field k, apply an embedding k→ℂ to its associativity and other structure coefficients and extend scalars to ℂ. This gives a conjugate tensor category, up to tensor equivalence.

title: Frobenius–Perron dimension in a fusion category
description: For a simple object X of a fusion category over ℂ, FPdim(X) is the spectral radius of its fusion matrix, whose entries are multiplicities in X⊗Y. Extend this additively to other objects.

title: Global dimension of a fusion category
description: For a fusion category over ℂ, the global dimension is the sum of the intrinsic squared norms of its simple objects. For a spherical structure it is the sum of their squared categorical dimensions.

title: Brauer's cyclotomic splitting-field theorem
description: If a finite group G has exponent n, then ℚ(ζₙ) is a splitting field for G: every irreducible complex representation of G has a model over ℚ(ζₙ).

title: Cyclotomicity of Frobenius–Perron dimensions
description: The Frobenius–Perron dimension of every object in a fusion category over ℂ is a cyclotomic integer.

title: Cyclotomicity of global dimensions of fusion categories
description: The global dimension of a fusion category over ℂ is a cyclotomic integer.

title: II₁ subfactor
description: An inclusion N⊂M of von Neumann factors of type II₁.

title: Jones index
description: For a II₁ subfactor N⊂M, its index [M:N] is the von Neumann dimension of L²(M) as an N-module, possibly infinite.

title: Principal even part of a subfactor
description: For a finite-index II₁ subfactor N⊂M, the tensor category of N–N bimodules generated by L²(M), closing under finite sums, summands and duals.

title: Dual even part of a subfactor
description: For a finite-index II₁ subfactor N⊂M, the tensor category of M–M bimodules generated by L²(M)⊗_N L²(M), closing under finite sums, summands and duals.

title: Principal graph pair of a finite-index subfactor
description: The pair of rooted bipartite graphs recording tensoring with the generating N–M Hilbert bimodule and its dual. Even vertices are simple N–N or M–M bimodules, odd vertices are simple mixed bimodules, and edge multiplicities count their summands. The graphs may be infinite.

title: Finite-depth subfactor
description: A finite-index subfactor whose principal graphs are finite, equivalently whose even parts have only finitely many simple objects.

title: Haagerup subfactor
description: The finite-depth hyperfinite II₁ subfactor with index (5+√13)/2 and the Haagerup principal graph pair.

title: Extended Haagerup subfactor
description: The finite-depth hyperfinite II₁ subfactor with the extended Haagerup principal graph pair, of index approximately 4.3772.

title: Principal Haagerup fusion category
description: The principal even part of the Haagerup subfactor, considered as a fusion category over ℂ.

title: Dual Haagerup fusion category
description: The dual even part of the Haagerup subfactor, considered as a fusion category over ℂ.

title: Principal extended Haagerup fusion category
description: The principal even part of the extended Haagerup subfactor, considered as a fusion category over ℂ.

title: Dual extended Haagerup fusion category
description: The dual even part of the extended Haagerup subfactor, considered as a fusion category over ℂ.

title: Drinfeld center of the Haagerup fusion category
description: The common braided center of the principal and dual Haagerup fusion categories, with the ribbon structure coming from their subfactor construction.

title: Haagerup planar algebra
description: The shaded subfactor planar algebra of the Haagerup subfactor. Morrison–Snyder use a rescaled generator and lopsided normalization of it.

title: Extended Haagerup planar algebra
description: The shaded subfactor planar algebra of the extended Haagerup subfactor. Morrison–Snyder use a rescaled generator and lopsided normalization of it.

title: Shaded planar tangle
description: A disc with interior discs and nonintersecting strings, with an even number of endpoints on each boundary, checkerboard-shaded complementary regions and marked boundary intervals; considered up to the prescribed isotopy.

title: Shaded planar algebra
description: Vector spaces P_{n,+},P_{n,−} acted on multilinearly by shaded planar tangles, compatibly with gluing and identity tangles.

title: Uncappable element of a planar algebra
description: A box killed by every operation that caps two adjacent boundary points.

title: Rotational eigenvector in a planar algebra
description: A nonzero n-box S, n>0, satisfying ρ(S)=ωS for the shading-preserving two-click rotation ρ. Since ρⁿ=id, its eigenvalue ω is an nth root of unity.

title: Lopsided planar algebra
description: A connected shaded planar algebra, with one-dimensional 0-box spaces, normalized so the shaded contractible circle evaluates to 1. The unshaded circle then evaluates to the index, the product of the two circle moduli.

title: Quantum integer
description: For n≥1, [n]_q=qⁿ⁻¹+qⁿ⁻³+⋯+q¹⁻ⁿ, and [0]_q=0. Equivalently [n]_q=(qⁿ−q⁻ⁿ)/(q−q⁻¹) when the quotient is defined; the Laurent polynomial also specializes at q=±1.

title: Jones–Wenzl idempotent
description: The idempotent fₙ in TLₙ(δ) with identity-diagram coefficient 1 and eᵢfₙ=fₙeᵢ=0 for every adjacent cap–cup generator. It exists for all n at generic δ; special parameters require care.

title: Non-cyclotomicity of the principal Haagerup fusion categories
description: The principal even parts of the Haagerup and extended Haagerup subfactors have no complete rational form over any cyclotomic field.

title: Fields of definition of the Haagerup and extended Haagerup fusion categories
description: For ℓ=0,1 write Hℓᵖ,Hℓᵈ for the principal and dual even parts and Dℓ for the index. Put n=4ℓ+4, choose q with q+q⁻¹=√Dℓ, and let λℓ²=−[n+2]_q/([2]_q²[n]_q). Both even parts have rational forms over ℚ(Dℓ); for ℚ⊂k⊂ℂ, Hℓᵈ has a complete rational form over k iff Dℓ∈k, and Hℓᵖ iff λℓ∈k. The center Z(H₀ᵖ) has a complete rational form as a ribbon category over k iff ζ₃₉∈k.

title: Galois conjugates of the Haagerup and extended Haagerup fusion categories
description: Up to tensor equivalence, the principal Haagerup even part has two Galois conjugates and the principal extended Haagerup even part has three. All the nonoriginal conjugates are nonunitary. The normal closures of their complete fields of definition have Galois groups D₈ (order eight) and C₂×A₄, respectively.

title: Half-braiding
description: For an object X of a monoidal category C, a natural family of isomorphisms c_Y:X⊗Y→Y⊗X, compatible with tensor products and the unit: c_{Y⊗Z}=(id_Y⊗c_Z)∘(c_Y⊗id_Z), with associators inserted.

title: Drinfeld center of a monoidal category
description: For a monoidal category C, its center Z(C) has objects (X,c), where c is a half-braiding on X, and morphisms f:X→X′ compatible with the half-braidings. Tensoring these pairs makes Z(C) braided; C itself need not be braided.

title: Induction to the Drinfeld center of a fusion category
description: For a fusion category C over ℂ, the induction functor I:C→Z(C) is the left adjoint to the functor forgetting the half-braiding. Its underlying object is ⊕_V V⊗X⊗V*, summed over simple representatives V.

title: Module category over a tensor category
description: A category M with an action C×M→M and coherent associativity and unit isomorphisms.

title: Dual fusion category
description: For an indecomposable semisimple module category M over a fusion category C, the category Fun_C(M,M) of module endofunctors, with composition as tensor product.

title: Internal Hom in a module category
description: For objects M,N of a module category over C, an internal Hom is an object [M,N] of C with natural bijections Hom_C(X,[M,N])≅Hom_M(X⊗M,N). It exists in the finite semisimple setting used here.

title: S-matrix of a ribbon fusion category
description: For a ribbon fusion category over ℂ, the S-matrix is indexed by simple objects; its (X,Y) entry is the categorical trace of c(Y,X)c(X,Y) on X⊗Y. This is the unnormalized Hopf-link convention.

title: T-matrix of a ribbon fusion category
description: For a ribbon fusion category over ℂ, the T-matrix is diagonal, with entry at a simple object X equal to the scalar of its ribbon twist θ_X. No additional anomaly scalar is included.

title: Modular tensor category
description: A ribbon fusion category over ℂ whose S-matrix is invertible.

title: Rational forms pass to Drinfeld centers
description: In the characteristic-zero fusion-category setting, if C_k is a rational form of C_K, the natural functor Z(C_k)⊗_k K→Z(C_K) is fully faithful, dominant, and commutes with induction. Thus Z(C_k) is a braided rational form, with idempotent completion understood.

title: Rational forms pass to dual fusion categories
description: In the characteristic-zero fusion-category setting, let M_K be an indecomposable finite semisimple module category over D_K and let D_k,M_k be compatible rational forms. Scalar extension induces a fully faithful dominant functor Fun_{D_k}(M_k,M_k)⊗_k K→Fun_{D_K}(M_K,M_K), so the dual category over k is a rational form of the dual over K.

title: Category
description: Objects and morphisms with associative composition and identity morphisms.

title: Functor
description: A map of categories preserving objects, morphisms, identities and composition.

title: Natural transformation
description: A family of maps between the values of two functors, commuting with every morphism in their source category.

title: Equivalence of categories
description: A functor with an inverse up to natural isomorphism.

title: Strong monoidal functor
description: A functor equipped with coherent isomorphisms preserving tensor products and the tensor unit.

title: Tensor equivalence
description: A strong monoidal functor whose underlying functor is an equivalence of categories.

title: Monoidal natural transformation
description: A natural transformation between strong monoidal functors compatible with their tensor-product and unit isomorphisms.

title: Dual object in a monoidal category
description: An object paired with another by evaluation and coevaluation maps satisfying the two zigzag identities; left and right duals reverse the order of the factors.

title: Double-dual functor
description: The covariant monoidal endofunctor X↦X** obtained by taking a chosen dual twice in a rigid monoidal category.

title: Endomorphism algebra of an object in a linear category
description: The vector space End(X), with multiplication given by composition and unit the identity of X.

title: Idempotent endomorphism
description: An endomorphism e:X→X satisfying e∘e=e.

title: Splitting of an idempotent endomorphism
description: Maps r:X→Y and i:Y→X with ir=e and ri=id_Y exhibit Y as the image of the idempotent e.

title: Additive category
description: A category with abelian-group morphism sets, composition additive in each variable, a zero object and finite biproducts.

title: Abelian category
description: An additive category with kernels and cokernels in which every monomorphism is a kernel and every epimorphism is a cokernel.

title: Subobject in a category
description: An equivalence class of monomorphisms into a fixed object, where two are equivalent if an isomorphism of their domains commutes with the maps.

title: Zero object in a category
description: An object 0 of a category such that for every object X there is exactly one morphism 0→X and exactly one morphism X→0.

title: Finite biproduct in a category
description: An object with injections and projections making it simultaneously the product and coproduct of a finite family of objects, with the usual compatible identity and zero composites.

title: Adjoint functors
description: Functors F:C→D and G:D→C with natural bijections Hom_D(FX,Y)≅Hom_C(X,GY); F is left adjoint to G.

title: Representable functor
description: A functor naturally isomorphic to Hom(A,−), or to Hom(−,A) in the contravariant case.

title: Tensor category over a field
description: A k-linear abelian rigid monoidal category with a k-bilinear tensor product and End(1)=k, finite-dimensional morphism spaces, and finite length for every object. Semisimplicity and finitely many simple isomorphism classes are not required.

title: Twist in a braided monoidal category
description: A natural automorphism θ of the identity with θ₁=id and θ_{X⊗Y}=c_{Y,X}c_{X,Y}(θ_X⊗θ_Y).

title: Tensor ideal of morphisms in a linear monoidal category
description: A family of linear subspaces of morphism spaces closed under composition on either side and tensoring with arbitrary morphisms.

title: Quotient of a linear category by an ideal
description: For a k-linear category C and a linear ideal I closed under composition on either side, C/I has the same objects and morphism spaces Hom_C(X,Y)/I(X,Y), with induced composition.

title: Vector space
description: An abelian group with scalar multiplication by a field satisfying a(v+w)=av+aw, (a+b)v=av+bv, (ab)v=a(bv), and 1v=v.

title: Bilinear map
description: A map of two vector-space variables that is linear in each variable separately.

title: Tensor product of vector spaces
description: The vector space V⊗W with its universal bilinear map from V×W.

title: Field
description: A commutative ring in which 1≠0 and every nonzero element is invertible.

title: Associative algebra over a field
description: A vector space with an associative bilinear multiplication and a multiplicative identity.

title: Module over an associative algebra
description: A vector space on which the algebra acts linearly, compatibly with multiplication and the identity.

title: Idempotent element of an algebra
description: An element e satisfying e²=e.

title: Orthogonal idempotents in an algebra
description: Idempotents e and f satisfying ef=fe=0.

title: Invertible element of an algebra
description: An element with a two-sided multiplicative inverse.

title: Split semisimple algebra
description: A finite-dimensional algebra isomorphic to a finite product of full matrix algebras over its base field.

title: Temperley–Lieb algebra
description: TL_n(δ) is spanned by planar noncrossing pairings of n top and n bottom points. Multiply by stacking and replace every closed loop by δ; equivalently its generators satisfy eᵢ²=δeᵢ, eᵢeᵢ₊₁eᵢ=eᵢ and eᵢeⱼ=eⱼeᵢ for abs(i−j)>1.

title: Colored operad
description: A collection of operations with specified input and output types, with associative substitution into inputs and identity operations.

title: Planar isotopy of tangle diagrams
description: A continuous deformation of embedded diagrams preserving their incidences, boundary components and marked data.

title: Fusion matrix
description: For an object X in a fusion category over ℂ, the matrix (N_X)_{Z,Y} records the multiplicity of the simple object Z in X⊗Y. Rows and columns are indexed by simple isomorphism classes.

title: Grothendieck ring of a fusion category
description: For a fusion category, the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with addition induced by direct sum and multiplication by tensor product.

title: Spectral radius of a finite matrix
description: The maximum absolute value of the complex eigenvalues of the matrix.

title: Perron–Frobenius theorem for nonnegative matrices
description: A nonnegative real matrix has a nonnegative eigenvalue equal to its spectral radius. If it is irreducible, that eigenvalue is simple and has a strictly positive eigenvector, unique up to scalar.

title: Intrinsic squared norm of a simple object in a fusion category
description: For a simple X in a fusion category over ℂ, choose an isomorphism a:X→X**. The product Tr(a)Tr((a⁻¹)*) is independent of this choice and is called |X|². With a pivotal structure it equals dim(X)dim(X*).

title: Type II₁ factor
description: An infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra with center ℂ1 admitting a faithful normal tracial state.

title: Hilbert bimodule over von Neumann algebras
description: An M–N Hilbert bimodule is a Hilbert space with commuting normal unital *-representations of von Neumann algebras M and Nᵒᵖ, giving left M and right N actions.

title: Tracial L²-space of a finite von Neumann algebra
description: The Hilbert completion of M for the inner product ⟨x,y⟩=τ(y*x), with the natural left and right multiplication actions.

title: Connes fusion of Hilbert bimodules
description: The relative tensor product of an M–N and an N–P Hilbert bimodule, formed using bounded vectors and completion in the canonical relative inner product, producing an M–P Hilbert bimodule.

title: Von Neumann dimension of a Hilbert module
description: A Hilbert module over a finite factor is represented by a projection on a sum of copies of L²(M); its dimension is the extended matrix trace of that projection.

title: Hyperfinite von Neumann algebra
description: A von Neumann algebra that is the weak closure of an increasing union of finite-dimensional *-subalgebras.

title: Field extension
description: An inclusion of one field into another.

title: Number field
description: A finite extension of ℚ.

title: Algebraic integer
description: A complex number satisfying a monic polynomial with integer coefficients.

title: Root of unity
description: In a field, a root of unity is an element ζ with ζⁿ=1 for some positive integer n; its order is the least such n.

title: Field embedding
description: An injective homomorphism of fields preserving the multiplicative identity.

title: Splitting field for a semisimple algebra
description: For a finite-dimensional semisimple k-algebra A, a splitting field is an extension K/k for which K⊗_k A is a finite product of full matrix algebras over K.

title: Galois group of a finite Galois extension
description: The group of field automorphisms of the extension that fix the base field pointwise.

title: Normal closure of a number field
description: The smallest normal extension of ℚ inside a fixed algebraic closure that contains the given number field.

title: Fundamental theorem of finite Galois theory
description: For a finite Galois extension L/k, intermediate fields correspond bijectively, with inclusions reversed, to subgroups of Gal(L/k), by taking fixed fields.

title: Set
description: A collection of distinct elements, regarded as one object.

title: Natural number
description: One of 0, 1, 2, …; natural numbers count finite collections.

title: Function between sets
description: An assignment taking each element of a specified domain set to exactly one element of a specified codomain set.

title: Composition of functions
description: For f:A→B and g:B→C, the composite g∘f:A→C sends x to g(f(x)).

title: Ordered pair
description: A pair (x,y) with distinguished first and second entries; (x,y)=(x′,y′) exactly when x=x′ and y=y′.

title: Cartesian product of sets
description: A×B is the set of ordered pairs (a,b) with a∈A and b∈B.

title: Subset
description: A⊆B means every element of A is an element of B.

title: Union of a family of sets
description: The set of elements belonging to at least one member of the family.

title: Intersection of a family of sets
description: Inside a specified ambient set, the elements belonging to every member of the family.

title: Complement of a subset
description: For A⊆Ω, its complement Ω∖A consists of the elements of Ω that do not belong to A.

title: Disjoint sets
description: Two sets are disjoint when they have no common element; a family is pairwise disjoint when every two distinct members are disjoint.

title: Bijection between sets
description: A function for which each element of the codomain is the image of exactly one element of the domain.

title: Sequence in a set
description: A function from the natural numbers, or the positive natural numbers, to that set.

title: Binary relation on a set
description: A subset R⊆S×S; writing xRy means (x,y)∈R.

title: Partial order
description: A reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive binary relation, usually written ≤.

title: Total order
description: A partial order in which any two elements are comparable.

title: Least upper bound in a partially ordered set
description: For A⊆P, its least upper bound is an upper bound s satisfying s≤b for every upper bound b of A, when such an s exists.

title: Binary operation on a set
description: A function S×S→S.

title: Group
description: A set with an associative binary operation, an identity element, and a two-sided inverse for each element.

title: Abelian group
description: A group whose operation is commutative.

title: Commutative ring with identity
description: An abelian group under addition, together with an associative commutative multiplication with identity, distributing over addition. The zero ring is allowed.

title: Ordered field
description: A field with a total order preserved by addition, in which the product of two positive elements is positive.

title: Isomorphism in a category
description: A morphism f:X→Y having an inverse g:Y→X, so gf=id_X and fg=id_Y.

title: Natural isomorphism
description: A natural transformation whose component at every object is an isomorphism.

title: Product of categories
description: C×D has pairs of objects and pairs of morphisms, with identities and composition defined componentwise.

title: Bifunctor
description: A functor C×D→E from a product of two categories to another category.

title: Extended nonnegative real numbers
description: The nonnegative real numbers together with a greatest element ∞. Sums involving ∞ equal ∞, and 0·∞ is taken to be 0 when integrating simple functions.

title: Open interval in the real line
description: For real a<b, the set (a,b)={x∈ℝ:a<x<b}.

title: σ-algebra generated by a family of subsets
description: The smallest σ-algebra containing that family, equivalently the intersection of all σ-algebras on the ambient set that contain it.

title: Borel σ-algebra on the real line
description: The σ-algebra on ℝ generated by the open intervals.

title: Measurable space
description: A set equipped with a specified σ-algebra of subsets.

title: Preimage of a subset under a function
description: For f:A→B and E⊆B, f⁻¹(E)={x∈A:f(x)∈E}.

title: Measurable map between measurable spaces
description: A function for which the preimage of each measurable subset of the codomain is measurable in the domain.

title: Indicator function of a subset
description: For A⊆Ω, the real function 1_A is 1 on A and 0 on its complement.

title: Measurable simple real function
description: A measurable real function with finite range. It can be written as a finite sum ∑ a_i 1_{A_i} with measurable level sets A_i.

title: Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral
description: If 0≤f≤g are measurable functions on a measure space, then ∫f dμ≤∫g dμ, allowing infinite integrals.

title: Linearity of the Lebesgue integral
description: If f and g are integrable real functions and a,b are real scalars, then af+bg is integrable and ∫(af+bg)dμ=a∫f dμ+b∫g dμ.

title: Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables
description: If Y is a nonnegative integrable real random variable and t>0, then P(Y≥t)≤E[Y]/t.

title: Complex number
description: A complex number is a pair of real numbers, written a+bi. Addition is componentwise and multiplication is (a+bi)(c+di)=(ac−bd)+(ad+bc)i, so i²=−1.

title: Linear map between vector spaces
description: A map between vector spaces over the same field preserving addition and scalar multiplication.

title: Normed vector space
description: A real or complex vector space X with a function ∥·∥:X→[0,∞) that is positive except at zero, absolutely homogeneous, and subadditive.

title: Complex inner-product space
description: A complex vector space with a positive definite Hermitian form ⟨x,y⟩, linear in x and conjugate-linear in y. Its induced norm is ∥x∥=√⟨x,x⟩.

title: Complex Hilbert space
description: A complex inner-product space complete in the metric d(x,y)=∥x−y∥ induced by its inner product.

title: Bounded linear operator
description: A linear map T:X→Y between normed vector spaces is bounded if ∥Tx∥≤C∥x∥ for one finite constant C and every x∈X.

title: Operator norm of a bounded linear operator
description: For a bounded linear map T:X→Y between normed spaces, ∥T∥=sup{∥Tx∥:∥x∥≤1}.

title: Adjoint of a bounded Hilbert-space operator
description: The adjoint of a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space is the unique bounded operator T* satisfying ⟨Tx,y⟩=⟨x,T*y⟩ for every x,y.

title: Bounded self-adjoint operator
description: A bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space is self-adjoint if T=T*.

title: Bounded positive operator
description: A bounded self-adjoint operator A is positive, written A≥0, if ⟨Ax,x⟩≥0 for every vector x.

title: Numerical range of a Hilbert-space operator
description: For a bounded operator T on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, W(T)={⟨Tx,x⟩:∥x∥=1}.

title: Numerical radius of a Hilbert-space operator
description: For a bounded Hilbert-space operator T, w(T)=sup{|z|:z∈W(T)}.

title: Spectrum of a bounded operator
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Banach space, σ(T) is the set of complex λ for which λI−T has no bounded two-sided inverse.

title: Holomorphic function of one complex variable
description: A function on an open subset of ℂ is holomorphic if its complex derivative exists at every point of that subset.

title: Disk algebra
description: The algebra A(𝔻) of complex functions continuous on the closed unit disk and holomorphic on the open unit disk, with the supremum norm.

title: Finite Blaschke product
description: A function B(z)=c∏ₖ₌₁ⁿ(z−aₖ)/(1−āₖz), with |c|=1 and |aₖ|<1. Constant unimodular functions are allowed when n=0.

title: Biholomorphic automorphism of the unit disk
description: A bijective holomorphic map 𝔻→𝔻 with holomorphic inverse; these maps are z↦c(z−a)/(1−āz), where |c|=1 and |a|<1.

title: Polynomial over a field
description: A formal finite sum a₀+a₁x+⋯+aₙxⁿ with coefficients in a field, with the usual coefficientwise addition and multiplication.

title: Rational function over a field
description: An element of k(x), represented by a quotient p(x)/q(x) of polynomials over k with q≠0; two quotients are equal when their cross-products agree.

title: Partial-fraction decomposition over ℂ
description: A complex rational function is a polynomial plus a finite sum of terms c/(z−a)^j, one collection for each finite pole, with j bounded by its multiplicity.

title: Riesz–Dunford holomorphic functional calculus
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Banach space and f holomorphic near σ(T), define f(T)=(2πi)⁻¹∮Γ f(z)(zI−T)⁻¹ dz, where Γ encloses σ(T) inside that neighborhood.

title: Spectral mapping theorem for holomorphic functional calculus
description: If f is holomorphic near the spectrum of a bounded operator T, then σ(f(T))=f(σ(T)).

title: Carathéodory’s approximation theorem by finite Blaschke products
description: Every holomorphic f:𝔻→ℂ with |f|≤1 is a locally uniform limit of finite Blaschke products. If f(0)=0, the approximating products can also be chosen to vanish at zero.

title: Comparison of numerical radius and operator norm
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space, w(T)≤∥T∥≤2w(T). If T is self-adjoint, w(T)=∥T∥.

title: Toeplitz–Hausdorff theorem
description: The numerical range of every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space is convex.

title: Berger’s power inequality for numerical radius
description: For every bounded Hilbert-space operator T and integer n≥1, w(Tⁿ)≤w(T)ⁿ.

title: Berger–Stampfli numerical-radius mapping theorem
description: If w(T)≤1 and f∈A(𝔻) has f(0)=0, then f(T)=lim_{r↑1}f(rT) exists in operator norm and w(f(T))≤∥f∥∞.

title: Local norm estimate from numerical radius
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space with w(T)≤1 and a vector x with ∥x∥≤1, ∥Tx∥²≤2+2√(1−|⟨Tx,x⟩|²).

title: Drury’s teardrop theorem
description: If w(T)≤1 and f∈A(𝔻) satisfies ∥f∥∞≤1, then W(f(T)) lies in the convex hull of the closed unit disk and the closed disk centered at f(0) with radius 1−|f(0)|². Consequently w(f(T))≤1+|f(0)|−|f(0)|²≤5/4.

title: Aleksandrov–Clark probability measures for a Schur function vanishing at zero
description: For holomorphic f:𝔻→𝔻 with f(0)=0 and |γ|=1, the Aleksandrov–Clark measure μγ is the probability measure on the unit circle satisfying (1−γ̄f(z))⁻¹=∫(1−ζ̄z)⁻¹ dμγ(ζ) for z∈𝔻.

title: Crouzeix’s numerical-range functional-calculus theorem
description: There is an absolute finite constant C such that ∥f(T)∥≤C sup_{z∈W(T)}|f(z)| for every bounded Hilbert-space operator T and f holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closure of W(T).

title: Vector subspace
description: A subset of a vector space containing zero and closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Linear span of a set of vectors
description: The subspace consisting of all finite linear combinations of a specified set of vectors.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Linearly independent family of vectors
description: A family of vectors is linearly independent if every finite linear combination equalling zero has all coefficients zero.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Basis of a vector space
description: A linearly independent family of vectors whose linear span is the whole vector space.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Dimension of a vector space
description: The cardinality of a basis of the vector space; a finite basis with n vectors gives dimension n.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Finite-dimensional vector space
description: A vector space having a finite basis.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Sum of vector subspaces
description: For subspaces U and W of the same vector space, U+W={u+w:u∈U,w∈W}, the smallest subspace containing both.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Quotient vector space
description: For a subspace U⊆V, the cosets V/U form a vector space with addition and scalar multiplication induced from V.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Direct sum of vector spaces
description: The algebraic direct sum of a family of vector spaces consists of tuples with only finitely many nonzero coordinates, with coordinatewise operations.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Image of a linear map
description: For a linear map f:V→W, its image is the subspace {f(v):v∈V} of W.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Kernel of a linear map
description: For a linear map f:V→W, its kernel is the subspace {v∈V:f(v)=0}.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Cokernel of a linear map
description: For a linear map f:V→W, its cokernel is the quotient W/im(f).
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Exact sequence of vector spaces
description: A sequence of linear maps is exact at a vector space if the image of the incoming map equals the kernel of the outgoing map; it is exact if this holds everywhere.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Snake lemma for vector spaces
description: For a commuting diagram with exact rows 0→A→B→C→0 and 0→A′→B′→C′→0 and vertical maps a,b,c, there is a natural exact sequence 0→ker(a)→ker(b)→ker(c)→coker(a)→coker(b)→coker(c)→0.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Dimension formula for sums of subspaces
description: For finite-dimensional subspaces U,W, dim(U+W)+dim(U∩W)=dim(U)+dim(W).
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Nondegenerate bilinear form
description: A bilinear form b:V×V→F is nondegenerate if b(v,w)=0 for all w forces v=0, and b(v,w)=0 for all v forces w=0.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Orthogonal complement for a bilinear form
description: For a bilinear form b on V and subspace U, its right orthogonal complement is U⊥={v∈V:b(u,v)=0 for every u∈U}. This definition does not assume a positive inner product.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Algebraic element of a field extension
description: An element α of L/F is algebraic over F if a nonzero polynomial in F[x] vanishes at α.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Separable algebraic field extension
description: An algebraic extension L/F is separable if the minimal polynomial over F of every element of L has distinct roots in an algebraic closure.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Subfield generated by a subset
description: For S⊆L in a field extension L/F, F(S) is the smallest subfield of L containing F and S.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Product of finite-dimensional subspaces of a field extension
description: For a field extension L/F and finite-dimensional F-subspaces S,T⊆L, their product ST is the F-linear span of {st:s∈S,t∈T}. It is spanned by products of basis vectors of S and T.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Stabilizer field of a finite-dimensional subspace
description: For a nonzero finite-dimensional F-subspace V⊆L in L/F, its stabilizer field is H(V)={x∈L:xV⊆V}. It contains F; every nonzero x in H(V) satisfies xV=V.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Hou–Leung–Xiang linear Kneser theorem
description: Let L/F be a field extension in which every element algebraic over F is separable. For nonzero finite-dimensional F-subspaces S,T⊆L, dim_F(ST)≥dim_F S+dim_F T−dim_F H(ST), where H(ST) is the stabilizer field of ST.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Uniform subfield stabilizer theorem for subspace products
description: Let L/F be any field extension and S⊆L a nonzero finite-dimensional F-subspace. Either dim_F(ST)≥dim_F S+dim_F T−1 for every nonzero finite-dimensional F-subspace T, or there is a subfield F⊊K⊆L, depending only on S, such that STK=ST for every T violating this bound. No separability assumption is required.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Subgroup
description: A subset of a group containing the identity and closed under multiplication and inverses.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Sumset in an abelian group
description: For subsets A,B of an additive abelian group, A+B={a+b:a∈A,b∈B}.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Translation stabilizer of a subset of an abelian group
description: For a subset A of an abelian group G, H(A)={g∈G:g+A=A}, a subgroup of G.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Kneser’s addition theorem for finite sumsets
description: For finite nonempty subsets A,B of an abelian group, |A+B|≥|A|+|B|−|H(A+B)|, where H(A+B) is the translation stabilizer of the sumset.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Balandraud’s uniform stabilizer theorem for sumsets
description: Fix a finite nonempty subset S of an abelian group. Either |S+T|≥|S|+|T|−1 for every finite nonempty T, or there is a finite nontrivial subgroup H, depending only on S, such that S+T+H=S+T for every T violating that bound.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Nonnegative real square root
description: For t≥0, √t is the unique real number y≥0 satisfying y²=t.

title: Complex conjugation
description: The complex conjugate of z=a+bi is z̄=a−bi.

title: Modulus of a complex number
description: For z=a+bi, its modulus is the nonnegative real number |z|=√(a²+b²).

title: Metric space
description: A set X with a function d:X×X→[0,∞) such that d(x,y)=0 exactly when x=y, d(x,y)=d(y,x), and d(x,z)≤d(x,y)+d(y,z).

title: Convergence of a sequence in a metric space
description: A sequence (xₙ) in a metric space (X,d) converges to x∈X if for every ε>0 there is N such that d(xₙ,x)<ε whenever n≥N.

title: Cauchy sequence in a metric space
description: A sequence (xₙ) in a metric space (X,d) is Cauchy if for every ε>0 there is N such that d(xₙ,xₘ)<ε whenever n,m≥N.

title: Complete metric space
description: A metric space is complete if every Cauchy sequence in it converges to a point of that same space.

title: Metric induced by a norm
description: The metric induced by a norm on a real or complex vector space is d(x,y)=‖x−y‖.

title: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for complex inner-product spaces
description: In a complex inner-product space, |⟨u,v⟩|²≤⟨u,u⟩⟨v,v⟩ for all u,v.

title: Linear combination of vectors
description: A finite sum a₁v₁+⋯+aₙvₙ of vectors multiplied by scalars from their vector space’s ground field; the empty sum is zero.

title: Divisibility of integers
description: An integer a divides b if b=ac for some integer c.

title: p-integral rational number
description: For a prime p, a rational number is p-integral if it can be written a/b with integers a,b and p not dividing b.

title: Matrix over a ring
description: A rectangular array of elements of a ring; addition is entrywise and matrix multiplication uses row-by-column sums.

title: Symmetric matrix
description: A square matrix A equal to its transpose, so aᵢⱼ=aⱼᵢ.

title: Positive semidefinite real matrix
description: A symmetric real matrix A such that xᵀAx≥0 for every real column vector x.

title: Positive definite real matrix
description: A symmetric real matrix A such that xᵀAx>0 for every nonzero real column vector x.

title: Symplectic group over a commutative ring
description: Sp₂g(R) is the group of invertible 2g×2g matrices M over R satisfying MᵀJM=J for J=[[0,I],[-I,0]].

title: Siegel upper half-space
description: The set ℍ_g of symmetric complex g×g matrices whose imaginary part is positive definite.

title: Scalar-valued Siegel modular form for the full modular group
description: A holomorphic function F on ℍ_g with F((AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹)=det(CZ+D)^k F(Z) for integral symplectic matrices [[A,B],[C,D]], and a Fourier expansion supported on positive semidefinite half-integral symmetric matrices. For g=1 the cusp-holomorphy condition is included.

title: Linear representation of a group
description: A group homomorphism from a group G to the invertible linear maps of a vector space, equivalently a linear action of G.

title: Vector-valued Siegel modular form of finite-quotient type
description: A holomorphic map F:ℍ_g→V transforming by det(CZ+D)^kρ(M), where ρ is a representation of the integral symplectic group with finite-index kernel; its Fourier expansion satisfies the usual holomorphy condition.

title: Fourier expansion of a Siegel modular form
description: The expansion F(Z)=∑_T c(T)exp(2πi tr(TZ)), with T positive semidefinite and half-integral in the full-level scalar case.

title: Jacobi form of Siegel degree g
description: A holomorphic function φ(τ,z) on ℍ_g×ℂ^g with the weight-k, index-m transformation laws under the integral Jacobi group, whose Fourier coefficients c(T,R) vanish unless 4mT−RRᵀ is positive semidefinite.

title: Fourier–Jacobi expansion of a Siegel modular form
description: Expand a degree-(g+1) Siegel form along the last diagonal variable: F([[τ,zᵀ],[z,τ′]])=∑_{m≥0}φ_m(τ,z)exp(2πimτ′), where φ_m are degree-g Jacobi forms.

title: Torsion point of a complex torus
description: A point of a complex torus V/Λ killed by multiplication by a positive integer; an N-torsion point is represented by a vector in (1/N)Λ.

title: Specialization of a Jacobi form at torsion points
description: Evaluate a Jacobi form after its Jacobi-group slash action at z=0 with rational translation parameters; collecting the N-torsion evaluations gives a vector-valued modular form.

title: Field of p-adic numbers
description: For a prime p, ℚ_p is the completion of ℚ for the p-adic absolute value |x|_p=p^{-v_p(x)}.

title: Finite unramified extension of a nonarchimedean local field
description: A finite extension of a complete discretely valued field whose ramification index is one and whose residue-field extension is separable.

title: Vandermonde determinant formula
description: The determinant of (xᵢ^{j−1})_{1≤i,j≤n} equals ∏_{i<j}(xⱼ−xᵢ).

title: Sturm’s congruence bound for elliptic modular forms
description: For a weight-k holomorphic modular form on SL₂(ℤ) with p-integral rational Fourier coefficients a(n), vanishing a(n) modulo p for 0≤n≤⌊k/12⌋ forces all coefficients to vanish modulo p.

title: Sturm bound k/10 for degree-two Siegel modular forms
description: For p≥5 and an even-weight k Siegel modular form of degree two with p-integral coefficients, if all coefficients indexed by T have zero reduction whenever both diagonal entries are at most ⌊k/10⌋, then the form vanishes modulo p.

title: Richter–Westerholt-Raum Sturm bound for Siegel modular forms
description: For a degree-g≥2, weight-k Siegel modular form with p-integral rational Fourier coefficients, vanishing modulo p of all c(T) with every tᵢᵢ≤(4/3)^g k/16 forces vanishing of every coefficient. For p≥5 the bound improves to (4/3)^g·9k/160.

title: Finite coefficient criterion for integrality of Siegel modular forms
description: For a degree-g≥2, weight-k Siegel modular form with rational coefficients, if every c(T) with all diagonal entries tᵢᵢ≤(4/3)^g k/16 is integral, then every coefficient is integral. The same implication holds for p-integrality.

title: Syndetic subset of the positive integers
description: A set S⊆ℕ₊ is syndetic if some finite bound L makes every interval {a,…,a+L} meet S.

title: Thick subset of the positive integers
description: A subset of ℕ₊ is thick if it contains intervals of arbitrarily large finite length.

title: Finite-sums set of a sequence
description: For a finite or infinite sequence (xᵢ) of positive integers, FS(xᵢ) consists of sums over finite nonempty sets of distinct indices.

title: IP-set of positive integers
description: A subset of ℕ₊ is an IP-set if it contains FS(xᵢ) for some infinite sequence of positive integers.

title: Admissible tuple of integer shifts
description: A finite set H={h₁,…,hₖ} of distinct integers is admissible if its residue classes fail to cover all classes modulo p for every prime p.

title: Pigeonhole principle
description: If more than n objects are assigned to n boxes, at least one box receives two objects; more generally some box receives at least the average number.

title: Bounded prime-cluster theorem for admissible tuples
description: There is an integer k₀ such that every admissible set H of at least k₀ integer shifts has infinitely many translates n+H containing at least two primes.

title: Finite arithmetic progression of integers
description: A sequence a,a+d,…,a+(k−1)d with integers a,d and positive integer k; nonconstant progressions have d≠0.

title: Green–Tao theorem
description: The prime numbers contain nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

title: Maillet’s prime-difference conjecture
description: Every positive even integer is a difference of two primes.

title: Kronecker’s prime-difference conjecture
description: Every positive even integer occurs infinitely often as a difference of two primes.

title: de Polignac’s conjecture on consecutive prime gaps
description: Every positive even integer occurs infinitely often as the gap between consecutive primes.

title: Twin-prime conjecture
description: There are infinitely many primes p for which p+2 is prime.

title: Syndeticity of infinitely recurring prime differences
description: The set D of positive integers occurring infinitely often as differences p−q of primes is syndetic. In particular the set of all positive prime differences is syndetic.

title: Pythagorean triple
description: A triple of positive integers (a,b,c) satisfying a²+b²=c².

title: Pythagorean theorem
description: In a Euclidean right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse length is the sum of the squares of the two leg lengths.

title: Perfect cuboid
description: A rectangular box whose three edges, three face diagonals and space diagonal all have positive integer lengths.

title: Euler brick
description: A rectangular box whose edges and all three face diagonals have integer lengths; its space diagonal need not have integer length.

title: Diophantine equation
description: A polynomial equation, usually with integer coefficients, whose solutions are required to be integers or rational numbers.

title: Greatest common divisor of integers
description: For integers a,b not both zero, gcd(a,b) is their greatest positive common divisor.

title: Coprime integers
description: Integers whose greatest common divisor is1.

title: Irreducible polynomial
description: A nonzero nonunit polynomial over a specified coefficient ring that cannot be written as a product of two nonunits. Over a field, both factors would have smaller positive degree.

title: Multiplicity of a polynomial root
description: The multiplicity of a root a of a polynomial P is the largest m≥1 for which (x−a)^m divides P. A root of multiplicity1 is simple.

title: Asymptotic expansion in a scale of functions
description: An expansion f∼∑aₙφₙ along a limit means that after every finite truncation at n, the remainder is o(φₙ), where each successive scale function is of smaller order than the preceding one. Convergence of the series is not required.

title: Newton polygon of a bivariate polynomial
description: The convex hull in ℝ² of exponent pairs (i,j) whose monomial coefficients in P(x,y)=∑cᵢⱼxⁱyʲ are nonzero.

title: Intermediate value theorem for real functions
description: A continuous real function on an interval takes every value between any two of its values.

title: Perfect cuboid existence problem
description: The open existence question asks whether any rectangular box has integer edges, face diagonals and space diagonal.

title: Sharipov’s second cuboid conjecture
description: For distinct coprime positive integers p,q, the polynomial Qₚq(t)=t¹⁰+(2q²+p²)(3q²−2p²)t⁸+(q⁸+10p²q⁶+4p⁴q⁴−14p⁶q²+p⁸)t⁶−p²q²(q⁸−14p²q⁶+4p⁴q⁴+10p⁶q²+p⁸)t⁴−p⁶q⁶(q²+2p²)(3p²−2q²)t²−p¹⁰q¹⁰ is irreducible in ℤ[t]. The family comes from the second special case of the cuboid parametrization.

title: Topological space
description: A set X with a family τ of subsets, called open sets, containing ∅ and X and closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections.

title: Continuous map between topological spaces
description: A map is continuous if the preimage of every open subset of its target is open in its domain.

title: Homeomorphism
description: A bijection between topological spaces that is continuous and has a continuous inverse.

title: Smooth map between open Euclidean sets
description: A map on an open subset of ℝⁿ is smooth if all of its component partial derivatives of every order exist and are continuous.

title: Diffeomorphism between open Euclidean sets
description: A bijection between open subsets of Euclidean spaces that is smooth and has a smooth inverse.

title: Lipschitz map between metric spaces
description: A map f:(X,d)→(Y,e) is Lipschitz if e(f(x),f(y))≤L d(x,y) for one finite constant L and all x,y∈X.

title: Bi-Lipschitz map
description: A bijection between metric spaces for which both the map and its inverse are Lipschitz.

title: Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space
description: The completion of the Borel measure on ℝⁿ assigning each rectangular box the product of its side lengths.

title: Lebesgue Lᵖ space
description: For a measure space and 1≤p<∞, Lᵖ consists of measurable scalar functions modulo equality almost everywhere with ∫|f|ᵖ<∞, normed by (∫|f|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ. For p=∞ use the essential-supremum norm.

title: Weak partial derivative of a locally integrable function
description: A locally integrable v is the ith weak derivative of u on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ if ∫Ω u ∂ᵢφ=−∫Ω vφ for every smooth compactly supported test function φ.

title: First-order Sobolev space W¹,ᵖ
description: For an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and 1≤p≤∞, W¹,ᵖ(Ω) consists of Lᵖ functions whose first weak partial derivatives are also in Lᵖ, with norm combining the function and derivative Lᵖ norms; vector-valued versions are componentwise.

title: Uniform convergence of functions into a metric space
description: A sequence fₙ:X→(Y,d) converges uniformly to f if for every ε>0, d(fₙ(x),f(x))<ε for every x∈X once n is sufficiently large independently of x.

title: Affine map between real vector spaces
description: A map of the form x↦Ax+b, where A is linear and b is fixed.

title: Piecewise affine homeomorphism on a planar domain
description: A homeomorphism on an open subset of ℝ² that is affine on every triangle of a locally finite triangulation; the triangulation need not be finite.

title: Lebesgue point of a locally integrable function
description: A point x is a Lebesgue point of f if the average of |f(y)−f(x)| over balls centered at x tends to zero as their radii tend to zero.

title: Lebesgue differentiation theorem
description: Almost every point of a locally integrable function on ℝⁿ is a Lebesgue point.

title: Vitali covering lemma for balls
description: From a family of Euclidean balls with bounded radii one can choose pairwise disjoint balls whose fivefold concentric dilations cover the union of the original family.

title: Jordan curve theorem
description: A simple closed curve in the plane separates the plane into exactly two connected components, one bounded and one unbounded, and is the boundary of both.

title: Mora-Corral–Pratelli smoothing of planar piecewise affine homeomorphisms
description: A planar piecewise affine homeomorphism in W¹,¹ can be approximated arbitrarily closely, both uniformly and in W¹,¹, by smooth diffeomorphisms, preserving boundary values when the continuous boundary extension is prescribed.

title: Diffeomorphic approximation of planar W¹,¹ homeomorphisms
description: For an open Ω⊆ℝ², every homeomorphism f∈W¹,¹(Ω,ℝ²) admits smooth diffeomorphisms and locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphisms arbitrarily close both uniformly and in W¹,¹. If f extends continuously to ∂Ω, approximants can have the same boundary values. On a polygonal domain, when f is piecewise affine on the boundary, the affine approximant can use a finite triangulation.

title: Schwartz space
description: The space S(ℝⁿ) of smooth functions φ for which supₓ|xᵅ∂ᵝφ(x)| is finite for every pair of multi-indices α,β, with the topology of these seminorms.

title: Tempered distribution
description: A continuous linear functional on the Schwartz space S(ℝⁿ).

title: Fourier transform on Euclidean space
description: For an integrable f on ℝⁿ, its Fourier transform is f̂(ξ)=∫f(x)e⁻ⁱˣ·ξ dx; extend it to Schwartz functions and tempered distributions by duality.

title: Convolution on Euclidean space
description: For functions with an appropriate integrability condition, (f*g)(x)=∫f(x−y)g(y)dy; convolution of a tempered distribution with a Schwartz function is defined by duality.

title: Dyadic cube in Euclidean space
description: A half-open cube 2⁻ʲ([0,1)ⁿ+k), with j∈ℤ and k∈ℤⁿ.

title: Variable-exponent Lebesgue space
description: For measurable p:ℝⁿ→(0,∞) with 0<ess inf p≤ess sup p<∞, L^{p(·)} consists of measurable functions of finite Luxemburg quasi-norm inf{λ>0:∫|f(x)/λ|^{p(x)}dx≤1}, modulo equality almost everywhere.

title: Log-Hölder continuous variable exponent
description: An exponent p is locally log-Hölder if |p(x)−p(y)|≤C/log(e+1/|x−y|); global log-Hölder continuity additionally requires |p(x)−p∞|≤C/log(e+|x|) for a constant p∞.

title: Mixed variable Lebesgue–sequence space L^{p(·)}(ℓ^{q(·)})
description: A sequence of measurable functions (fⱼ) has quasi-norm ∥(∑ⱼ|fⱼ(·)|^{q(·)})^{1/q(·)}∥_{L^{p(·)}}; functions are identified almost everywhere.

title: Peetre maximal function of a band-limited function
description: For scale j and a>0, the Peetre maximal function is f*_{j,a}(x)=sup_y |f(y)|/(1+2ʲ|x−y|)^a, used for functions localized to a frequency band of size 2ʲ.

title: Smooth atom for dyadic function-space decompositions
description: A smooth atom associated to a dyadic cube Q is supported in a fixed dilation of Q, obeys scale-normalized derivative bounds up to a specified order, and has vanishing polynomial moments up to a specified order.

title: Smooth molecule for dyadic function-space decompositions
description: A smooth molecule associated to a dyadic cube has prescribed vanishing moments and scale-normalized derivative bounds with polynomial decay away from that cube, instead of compact support.

title: Frazier–Jawerth φ-transform
description: A discrete analysis map sends a tempered distribution to its scale-normalized convolutions with admissible band-limited Schwartz functions sampled at dyadic cube corners; a dual family reconstructs it by summing the associated atoms.

title: Vector-valued convolution inequality in variable Lebesgue spaces
description: If p,q are globally log-Hölder with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞ and 1<q⁻≤q⁺<∞, then for m>n the kernels ηⱼ,m(x)=2ʲⁿ(1+2ʲ|x|)⁻ᵐ satisfy ∥(ηⱼ,m*fⱼ)ⱼ∥_{L^{p(·)}(ℓ^{q(·)})}≤C∥(fⱼ)ⱼ∥_{L^{p(·)}(ℓ^{q(·)})}.

title: Triebel–Lizorkin-type space with variable exponents and cube weight
description: For bounded positive exponents p,q with globally log-Hölder reciprocals, bounded locally log-Hölder smoothness s, and a positive doubling/locally comparable cube weight φ, F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)} consists of tempered distributions with finite sup_P φ(P)⁻¹∥(∑_{j≥max(0,−log₂ℓ(P))}(2^{js(·)}|ϕⱼ*f|)^{q(·)})^{1/q(·)}∥_{L^{p(·)}(P)}. Here P ranges over dyadic cubes and the admissible Schwartz family includes a low-frequency term at j=0.

title: φ-transform characterization of variable-exponent Triebel–Lizorkin-type spaces
description: For the admissible p,q,s,φ defining F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)}, the Frazier–Jawerth analysis and synthesis maps are bounded between this function space and its matching dyadic coefficient space, and analysis followed by synthesis reconstructs the distribution: TψSϕ=id. In particular the function-space quasi-norm is independent, up to equivalence, of the admissible Schwartz pair.

title: Almost-everywhere property on a measure space
description: A property holds almost everywhere if the set where it fails is contained in a measurable set of measure zero.

title: Lower semicontinuous extended-real function
description: A function u:X→(−∞,∞] on a topological space is lower semicontinuous if {x:u(x)>a} is open for every real a.

title: Hardy space H² on the unit disk
description: The holomorphic functions f(z)=∑ₙ≥0aₙzⁿ on the unit disk with ∑|aₙ|²<∞, normed by (∑|aₙ|²)¹ᐟ²; boundary values identify it with the nonnegative-frequency subspace of L² of the unit circle.

title: Hardy space H∞ on the unit disk
description: The bounded holomorphic functions on the unit disk, with the supremum norm.

title: Superharmonic function on a planar domain
description: A lower semicontinuous function u:Ω→(−∞,∞], not identically∞ on a component, is superharmonic if its value at each center is at least its circle average whenever the closed disk lies in Ω.

title: Weighted holomorphic Dirichlet space
description: For a nonnegative integrable weight ω on the unit disk, Dω consists of holomorphic f with Dω(f)=∫D|f′(z)|²ω(z)dA(z)<∞. When Dω⊆H², its Hilbert norm is ∥f∥²H²+Dω(f), with normalized area measure dA.

title: Reproducing kernel Hilbert space
description: A Hilbert space of scalar functions on a set X in which evaluation at every x∈X is a bounded linear functional; its reproducing kernel satisfies f(x)=⟨f,kₓ⟩.

title: Positive definite complex kernel
description: A kernel K:X×X→ℂ is positive definite if ∑ᵢⱼcᵢc̄ⱼK(xᵢ,xⱼ)≥0 for every finite choice of points xᵢ and scalars cᵢ.

title: Toeplitz operator on H² of the unit disk
description: For ψ∈L∞ of the unit circle, Tψf=P₊(ψf), where P₊ is orthogonal projection from boundary L² onto H².

title: de Branges–Rovnyak space H(b)
description: For b holomorphic on the unit disk with ∥b∥∞≤1, H(b) is the reproducing kernel Hilbert space with kernel Kb(z,w)=(1−b(z)b(w)̄)/(1−zw̄). Equivalently it is the range of (I−TbTb*)¹ᐟ² with the induced range norm.

title: Outer function in Hardy H²
description: A function a∈H² is outer if the linear span of a,z a,z²a,… is dense in H²; this is equivalent to the usual exponential Poisson-integral definition.

title: Inner function on the unit disk
