description: A bounded holomorphic function on the unit disk whose radial boundary values have modulus one almost everywhere on the unit circle.

title: Inner–outer factorization in Hardy H²
description: Every nonzero H² function is the product of an inner function and an outer H² function; the factors are unique up to opposite unimodular constants.

title: Smirnov class on the unit disk
description: The holomorphic functions on the unit disk expressible as b/a with a,b∈H∞ and a outer.

title: Poisson kernel of the unit disk
description: For ζ on the unit circle and z in the disk, Pζ(z)=(1−|z|²)/|ζ−z|²; integrating it against boundary data gives harmonic extensions.

title: Riesz decomposition for positive superharmonic functions on the disk
description: A positive superharmonic function on the unit disk decomposes uniquely into a Green potential of a positive locally finite measure and a positive harmonic function; the harmonic part has a positive boundary-measure Poisson representation.

title: Bergman projection on the unit disk
description: The orthogonal projection from area L² of the disk onto its holomorphic subspace; with normalized area its kernel is Qψ(z)=∫D ψ(w)/(1−zw̄)² dA(w), whenever the formula is meaningful.

title: Berezin transform on the unit disk
description: For an integrable weight ψ on the disk, Bψ(z)=∫D (1−|z|²)²|1−zw̄|⁻⁴ψ(w)dA(w), the average against the normalized Bergman kernel density.

title: Isometric identification of superharmonic Dirichlet and de Branges–Rovnyak spaces
description: Let μ be a nonzero finite positive measure on the closed unit disk, representing a superharmonic Dirichlet weight, and let b be non-extreme with associated outer a normalized by a(0)>0 and |a|²+|b|²=1 on the circle. Then Dμ=H(b) with equal norms exactly when μ=|α|²δζ and b(z)/a(z)=αz/(1−ζ̄z) for some ζ in the closed disk and α≠0.

title: Dilation inequality for superharmonic Dirichlet integrals
description: For a positive superharmonic Dirichlet weight represented by a finite positive closed-disk measure μ, f∈Dμ and fᵣ(z)=f(rz), Dμ(fᵣ)≤2r/(1+r)Dμ(f) for 0≤r<1.

title: Banach space
description: A real or complex normed vector space complete for the metric induced by its norm.

title: Real inner-product space
description: A real vector space with a symmetric bilinear form ⟨x,y⟩ that is positive on ⟨x,x⟩ for x≠0; its induced norm is √⟨x,x⟩.

title: Real Hilbert space
description: A real inner-product space complete for its induced norm metric.

title: Bounded linear functional
description: A linear map from a real or complex normed vector space to its scalar field satisfying |ℓ(x)|≤C∥x∥ for one finite C and every x.

title: Weak convergence in a Banach space
description: A sequence xₙ converges weakly to x if ℓ(xₙ)→ℓ(x) for every bounded linear functional ℓ on the space.

title: Weak sequential compactness in a Banach space
description: A subset is weakly sequentially compact if every sequence in it has a weakly convergent subsequence whose limit belongs to that same subset.

title: Proper convex extended-real functional
description: A function R:V→(−∞,∞] on a real vector space is proper if it is finite somewhere and is convex if R((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)R(x)+tR(y) for 0≤t≤1.

title: Weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous functional
description: An extended-real functional R satisfies R(x)≤liminfₙR(xₙ) whenever xₙ converges weakly to x.

title: Variational Tikhonov regularization
description: For an operator equation Fx=y, approximate noisy data yδ by minimizing ∥Fx−yδ∥²+αR(x), where α>0 and R is a chosen penalty functional.

title: Penalty-minimizing solution of an inverse problem
description: An R-minimizing solution of Fx=y minimizes the penalty R among all exact solutions of that equation.

title: Embedded smooth surface in ℝ³
description: A subset of ℝ³ that near each point is, after a rigid change of coordinates, the graph of a smooth real function of two variables.

title: Tangent space of an embedded surface
description: At x on a smooth embedded surface M, TₓM is the two-dimensional vector subspace of velocities γ′(0) of smooth surface curves with γ(0)=x.

title: Tangent vector field on an embedded surface
description: A map v:M→ℝ³ with v(x)∈TₓM at each x; smoothness or Sobolev regularity is an additional stated condition.

title: Orthogonal projection onto a closed Hilbert subspace
description: For a closed subspace V of a Hilbert space H, Pᵥx is the unique v∈V for which x−v is orthogonal to V; Pᵥ is a bounded self-adjoint idempotent operator.

title: Surface gradient on an embedded surface
description: For a smooth real f on a surface M⊂ℝ³, ∇Mf is the tangent vector field satisfying ⟨∇Mf,v⟩=df(v) for tangent vectors v; equivalently it is the tangential projection of an ambient smooth extension’s gradient.

title: Levi-Civita covariant derivative on an embedded surface
description: For tangent vector fields X,Y on a surface in ℝ³ with its induced metric, ∇XY is the tangential projection of the ambient directional derivative DXY.

title: First-order Sobolev vector fields on an embedded surface
description: Vector fields with square-integrable components and square-integrable first weak surface derivatives, defined using smooth charts and the surface measure; tangent Sobolev fields additionally lie in each tangent plane almost everywhere.

title: Pullback of a scalar or ambient-valued function between surfaces
description: For a diffeomorphism Φ:M→N, the pullback of f:N→V is Φ*f=f∘Φ. This is composition of functions, not the derivative-based pullback of tangent vector fields.

title: Bochner connection Laplacian on tangent vector fields
description: The rough or connection Laplacian ∇*∇ on tangent vector fields, defined from covariant differentiation and its formal L² adjoint. In the selected surface problem it is the weak operator associated to the squared norm of the tangential covariant derivative, not the Hodge Laplacian on differential forms.

title: Convergence of Tikhonov regularization under surface perturbation
description: For a bounded linear tangent-field inverse operator and its bounded linear ambient approximations on uniformly regular parametrized surfaces with C² surface error γ→0, transported operator error ρ→0 and data error δ→0, minimize squared data discrepancy plus normal-component penalty plus α times the squared first-order surface seminorm. Under weakly lower semicontinuous convex penalties with weakly sequentially compact level sets and existence of a seminorm-minimizing exact tangent solution, α→0 and (ρ²+γ²+δ²)/α→0 imply that weak cluster points of the pulled-back minimizers are seminorm-minimizing solutions.

title: Probability mass function on a finite set
description: A function p from a finite set Ω to [0,1] satisfying ∑_{ω∈Ω}p(ω)=1; the probability of A⊆Ω is ∑_{ω∈A}p(ω).

title: Real exponential function
description: The real function exp(x)=∑_{n≥0}xⁿ/n!, whose series converges for every real x.

title: Natural logarithm
description: The inverse ln:(0,∞)→ℝ of the real exponential function.

title: Product distribution on a finite product space
description: For probability mass functions p_i on finite sets Ω_i, the product distribution on ∏_iΩ_i assigns (ω_i)_i the probability ∏_ip_i(ω_i).

title: Marginal distribution on a finite product space
description: The marginal on a set of coordinates is obtained by summing the joint mass over all other coordinates.

title: Conditional probability given an event
description: If P(B)>0, the conditional probability of A given B is P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B).

title: Total variation distance between finite probability distributions
description: For probability mass functions p,q on the same finite set, d_TV(p,q)=½∑_ω|p(ω)−q(ω)|=sup_A|p(A)−q(A)|.

title: Shannon entropy of a finite distribution
description: For a finite probability mass function p, H(p)=−∑_ωp(ω)ln p(ω), with 0ln0=0.

title: Relative entropy of finite probability distributions
description: D(p∥q)=∑_ωp(ω)ln(p(ω)/q(ω)), with a positive p(ω) and zero q(ω) giving +∞ and zero p terms contributing zero.

title: Gibbs distribution on a finite configuration space
description: For a finite set Ω, energy H:Ω→ℝ and inverse temperature β≥0, the Gibbs distribution is μ(σ)=exp(−βH(σ))/Z, where Z=∑_{τ∈Ω}exp(−βH(τ)).

title: Partition function of a finite Gibbs model
description: The normalizing sum Z=∑_σ exp(−βH(σ)); equivalently Z=∑_σ∏_aψ_a(σ) for positive factor weights. Its logarithm records the model’s free energy up to normalization.

title: Undirected multigraph
description: A vertex set and an edge set, with two unordered endpoints assigned to each edge; distinct edges can have the same endpoints and loops are allowed.

title: Bipartite multigraph
description: An undirected multigraph whose vertices are partitioned into two classes and whose edges join opposite classes.

title: Path in an undirected graph
description: A finite sequence of adjacent edges joining successive vertices; a simple path has no repeated vertex. Its length is the number of edges.

title: Graph distance
description: The distance between two vertices is the minimum length of a path joining them, or infinity if no such path exists.

title: Girth of a graph
description: The length of a shortest cycle, with girth infinity for an acyclic graph. In a multigraph a loop has length one and two parallel edges form a cycle of length two.

title: Finite factor graph
description: A finite bipartite graph with variable nodes, factor nodes, and a nonnegative function at each factor depending on its adjacent variables. Multiplying the factor functions gives the weight of an assignment.

title: Configuration model for a prescribed degree sequence
description: Attach the prescribed number of half-edges to each vertex and match half-edges uniformly at random; collapsing each half-edge bundle gives a random multigraph with those degrees. Bipartite typed versions match compatible half-edge classes.

title: Ising model on a finite graph
description: Spins σ_v∈{−1,+1} receive Gibbs weight exp(β∑_{uv∈E}J_{uv}σ_uσ_v+∑_vh_vσ_v), for specified couplings and external fields.

title: Potts model on a finite graph
description: A finite-state spin at every vertex receives Gibbs weight determined by whether adjacent spins agree; the antiferromagnetic model penalizes agreement.

title: Uniform random k-SAT model
description: A Boolean formula on n variables formed by m independent clauses, each uniformly chosen from the 2ᵏ·binomial(n,k) clauses containing k distinct variables, each independently negated or unnegated.

title: Conditional expectation given a σ-algebra
description: For integrable X and a sub-σ-algebra G, E[X|G] is a G-measurable integrable random variable satisfying ∫_AE[X|G]dP=∫_AXdP for every A∈G, defined up to almost-sure equality.

title: Conditional variance
description: For square-integrable X, Var(X|G)=E[(X−E[X|G])²|G]=E[X²|G]−E[X|G]².

title: Convex function on a real interval
description: A real function φ on an interval I is convex if φ(tx+(1−t)y)≤tφ(x)+(1−t)φ(y) for x,y∈I and 0≤t≤1.

title: Partition of a set
description: A family of nonempty pairwise disjoint subsets whose union is the set.

title: Totally bounded metric space
description: A metric space is totally bounded if for every ε>0 it is covered by finitely many open balls of radius ε.

title: Law of total variance
description: For square-integrable X and sub-σ-algebra G, Var(X)=E[Var(X|G)]+Var(E[X|G]).

title: Discrete-time martingale
description: An integrable process (M_n) adapted to an increasing sequence of σ-algebras (F_n) such that E[M_{n+1}|F_n]=M_n almost surely.

title: Bounded martingale convergence theorem
description: A martingale uniformly bounded by a deterministic constant converges almost surely and in L¹. In particular, conditional expectations of a bounded X along increasing σ-algebras converge to E[X|σ(∪_nF_n)].

title: Azuma–Hoeffding inequality
description: If a real martingale has increments bounded in absolute value by c_i, then P(|M_n−M_0|≥t)≤2exp(−t²/(2∑_{i=1}^nc_i²)) for t>0.

title: Chernoff bound for sums of independent Bernoulli variables
description: If S is a sum of independent Bernoulli variables with mean μ, then for δ>0, P(S≥(1+δ)μ)≤[e^δ/(1+δ)^(1+δ)]^μ; for 0<δ<1, P(S≤(1−δ)μ)≤exp(−μδ²/2).

title: Paley–Zygmund inequality
description: For nonnegative X with 0<E[X²]<∞ and 0<θ<1, P(X>θEX)≥(1−θ)²(EX)²/E[X²].

title: Jensen’s inequality for expectations
description: For an integrable real random variable X and convex φ with E|φ(X)|<∞, φ(EX)≤Eφ(X), when φ is defined on an interval containing the range of X.

title: Stirling’s formula
Rooted locally finite graph
description: A connected graph with a distinguished root and finitely many incident edges at every vertex; finite-radius rooted neighborhoods retain their induced graph structure.

title: Local weak convergence of bounded-degree graphs
description: A bounded-degree graph sequence converges locally to a random rooted graph if, for each finite radius and rooted neighborhood type, the proportion of vertices with that neighborhood converges to the corresponding root-neighborhood probability. For random graphs this convergence may be in probability.

title: Weak convergence of probability measures on a metric space
description: Measures μ_n converge weakly to μ if ∫f dμ_n→∫f dμ for every bounded continuous real function f on the space.

title: Polish space
description: A topological space admitting a complete separable metric that induces its topology.

title: Bethe free energy of factor-graph marginals
description: For consistent variable and factor marginals p_x,p_a, the Bethe log-partition functional is ∑_a[H(p_a)+E_{p_a}lnψ_a]−∑_x(d_x−1)H(p_x). On a limiting rooted factor-tree law one uses the corresponding expected local terms, normalized per variable node.

title: Size-biased change of measure
description: Given a probability measure P and a nonnegative random variable W with 0<E_PW<∞, the W-biased measure is Q(A)=E_P[W·1_A]/E_PW; equivalently dQ/dP=W/E_PW.

title: Non-reconstruction for Gibbs measures on sparse graphs
description: The spin at a typical vertex becomes asymptotically independent of a randomly sampled distant boundary condition, measured by the expected total variation change of its conditional marginal as the boundary radius tends to infinity.

title: Decay of boundary influence for Gibbs measures on trees
description: On rooted factor trees, the root marginal changes by arbitrarily little in total variation under every possible boundary condition at sufficiently large distance. This uniform condition yields uniqueness of the limiting root marginal.

title: Bapst–Coja-Oghlan regularity lemma for probability measures on discrete cubes
description: For finite Ω and ε>0, every measure on Ωⁿ for sufficiently large n admits coordinate and state partitions of bounded total size N(ε,Ω), refining any coordinate partition with at most 1/ε classes. Apart from total mass ε and εn exceptional coordinates, conditioning on a state makes empirical spin distributions regular on each coordinate class: all subsets of relative size at least ε have expected total variation discrepancy below ε from the full class’s empirical distribution. Within each state, empirical distributions on each class have diameter below ε; the unconditioned measure is regular as well.

title: Bethe free-energy limit under local Gibbs decorrelation
description: For a locally convergent sequence of bounded-degree typed factor models with finite spins and positive weights from a fixed finite family, assume every fixed short-cycle-free event has nonvanishing probability in both ordinary and locally conditioned partition-function-biased models. Let p be a consistent limiting-tree marginal assignment. If average two-variable Gibbs marginals converge in total variation to the corresponding products from p, then limsup n⁻¹ElnZ≤B(p). If the same holds in the locally conditioned partition-function-biased model, the limit equals B(p). Non-reconstruction implies the required decorrelation; uniform tree boundary-influence decay yields equality in both models.

title: σ-finite measure
description: A measure whose whole underlying space is a countable union of measurable sets of finite measure.

title: Complete measure
description: A measure is complete if every subset of a measurable null set is measurable and has measure zero.

title: Product measure
description: For σ-finite measure spaces, the product measure on the product σ-algebra assigns a measurable rectangle A×B the value μ(A)ν(B); its completion also includes subsets of product-null sets.

title: Almost-everywhere convergence of measurable functions
description: Measurable functions fₙ converge almost everywhere to f if the pointwise limit fₙ(x)→f(x) holds outside a measurable null set.

title: Probability density relative to a measure
description: A nonnegative measurable function P with ∫P dμ=1; the measure P dμ is the corresponding probability measure.

title: Marginal density on a product measure space
description: A joint density on a product space induces a marginal density by integrating out the coordinates not retained.

title: Fubini’s theorem for integrable functions
description: An integrable function on the product of σ-finite measure spaces has integrable almost-everywhere sections, and its product integral equals either iterated integral.

title: Tonelli’s theorem for nonnegative functions
description: For a nonnegative measurable function on the product of σ-finite measure spaces, the product integral equals either iterated integral, allowing∞.

title: Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem
description: If measurable fₙ converge almost everywhere to f and |fₙ|≤g for an integrable g, then f is integrable and ∫|fₙ−f|→0; consequently their integrals converge.

title: Baire category theorem for complete metric spaces
description: Every countable intersection of dense open subsets of a complete metric space is dense.

title: Generalized N-mean of a kernel of order m
description: For 1≤m≤N, set G_{m,N}(u)(x₁,…,x_N)=binom(N,m)⁻¹∑_{i₁<⋯<i_m}u(x_{i₁},…,x_{i_m}). Kernels need not be symmetric; equalities in measure-theoretic applications are understood almost everywhere.

title: U-statistic with symmetric kernel
description: For independent identically distributed observations X₁,…,X_N and a symmetric kernel u of m variables, the U-statistic is binom(N,m)⁻¹∑_{i₁<⋯<i_m}u(X_{i₁},…,X_{i_m}).

title: Almost-everywhere convergence of generalized means and their kernels
description: On a nonzero complete σ-finite measure space, fix 1≤m≤N. A sequence G_{m,N}(uₙ) has an almost-everywhere finite limit U exactly when uₙ has an almost-everywhere finite limit u; then U=G_{m,N}(u) almost everywhere. In particular a generalized mean has a unique kernel modulo null sets.

title: Measurability and essential boundedness in generalized-mean kernel recovery
description: On a nonzero complete σ-finite measure space, G_{m,N}(u) is measurable exactly when its almost-everywhere finite kernel u is measurable. Moreover G_{m,N}(u)∈L∞ exactly when u∈L∞, with ∥G_{m,N}(u)∥∞≤∥u∥∞≤C(m,N)∥G_{m,N}(u)∥∞.

title: Weighted Lʳ equivalence for generalized means under a marginal lower bound
description: Let P>0 be a symmetric probability density on Λᴺ over a complete nonzero σ-finite measure space. Suppose on a positive-measure set of final coordinates x_N there is γ(x_N)>0 with P(·,x_N)≥γ(x_N)P_{N−1} almost everywhere. For 1≤m≤N and 1≤r<∞, G_{m,N}(u)∈Lʳ(P) exactly when u∈Lʳ(P_m), and the two norms are comparable by constants independent of u.

title: Schauder basis of a Banach space
description: A sequence (eₙ) in a Banach space for which every vector x has a unique expansion x=∑ₙaₙeₙ converging in norm.

title: Unconditional Schauder basis
description: A Schauder basis for which each vector’s expansion converges unconditionally, equivalently converges to the same vector after every permutation of its terms.

title: Block sequence relative to a Schauder basis
description: A sequence of nonzero finitely supported vectors xₙ such that max supp(xₙ)<min supp(xₙ₊₁); its closed linear span is a block subspace.

title: Strictly singular bounded operator
description: A bounded linear operator whose restriction to no infinite-dimensional closed subspace is an isomorphism onto its image, equivalently is bounded below on no such subspace.

title: Diagonal bounded operator relative to a Schauder basis
description: A bounded linear operator D satisfying Deₙ=λₙeₙ for a fixed Schauder basis (eₙ).

title: Tight-by-support Schauder basis
description: A Schauder basis is tight by support if no two infinite-dimensional closed subspaces with disjoint coordinate supports are isomorphic as Banach spaces.

title: Hereditarily indecomposable Banach space
description: An infinite-dimensional Banach space in which no infinite-dimensional closed subspace is a topological direct sum of two infinite-dimensional closed subspaces.

title: Spreading model generated by a basic sequence
description: A basic sequence (xₙ) generates (ẽₙ) as a spreading model when for each finite scalar list (aᵢ), the asymptotic limits of ∥∑ᵢaᵢx_{nᵢ}∥ as the ordered indices move to infinity equal ∥∑ᵢaᵢẽᵢ∥.

title: Schlumprecht’s arbitrarily distortable Banach space
description: The completion of c₀₀ in the least norm satisfying ∥x∥=max{∥x∥∞,sup_{n≥2}(log₂(n+1))⁻¹ sup_{E₁<⋯<Eₙ}∑ᵢ∥Eᵢx∥}, where Eᵢ are successive finite coordinate sets. Its unit vector basis is unconditional and subsymmetric.

title: Gowers’s unconditional space from the hyperplane construction
description: The Banach space X_U from Gowers’s 1994 construction, obtained by completing c₀₀ in a norm combining Schlumprecht-type successive-coordinate averages and specially coded functionals using absolute coordinate data. Its unit vector basis is unconditional and tight by support; admissible coding data are fixed in the construction.

title: ℓ₁ block average in a Banach space with basis
description: An ℓ₁ⁿ average with constant c≥1 is x=n⁻¹(x₁+⋯+xₙ), where the xᵢ are successive block vectors with ∥xᵢ∥≤1 and ∥x∥≥1/c.

title: Failure of diagonal-plus-strictly-singular decomposition on a Gowers-space subspace
description: There is a closed subspace Y of Gowers’s unconditional space X_U and a bounded operator T:Y→X_U which cannot be written D|Y+S with D a bounded diagonal operator on X_U and S strictly singular.

title: Subsequential diagonal decomposition in tight-by-support spaces
description: If X has a tight-by-support unconditional basis, (xₙ) is a seminormalized weakly null sequence in X and T:[xₙ]→X is bounded, then some subsequence (xₙ)_{n∈M} satisfies T|[xₙ:n∈M]=D|[xₙ:n∈M]+S, with D a bounded diagonal operator on X and S strictly singular.

title: Complex exponential function
description: The entire function exp(z)=∑ₙ₌₀∞zⁿ/n!; on imaginary arguments exp(it)=cos(t)+i sin(t).

title: Complex *-algebra, possibly nonunital
description: A complex vector space with associative bilinear multiplication and a conjugate-linear involution a↦a* satisfying (ab)*=b*a*. A multiplicative identity is not required.

title: C*-algebra
description: A complex *-algebra with a complete submultiplicative norm satisfying ∥a*a∥=∥a∥²; an identity is not required.

title: Positive element and order in a C*-algebra
description: An element is positive if it has the form b*b. For self-adjoint a,b, write a≤b when b−a is positive.

title: Positive square root in a C*-algebra
description: Every positive element a of a C*-algebra has a unique positive element b with b²=a. For any a, its absolute value is |a|=(a*a)¹ᐟ².

title: Right module over a complex algebra
description: A complex vector space X with a bilinear action X×A→X satisfying (xa)b=x(ab); for a unital algebra the action is taken to satisfy x1=x.

title: Semi-inner-product C*-module
description: A right module X over a C*-algebra A with an A-valued form ⟨x,y⟩, complex linear and A-linear in y, conjugate symmetric, additive in each argument, and satisfying ⟨x,x⟩≥0. Zero length need not imply x=0; this is not the nonsymmetric semi-inner product used in Banach-space geometry.

title: Inner-product C*-module
description: A semi-inner-product C*-module with ⟨x,x⟩=0 only for x=0. Its norm is ∥x∥=∥⟨x,x⟩∥¹ᐟ²; completeness is not assumed.

title: Hilbert C*-module
description: An inner-product C*-module complete in the norm induced by its C*-algebra-valued inner product.

title: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for semi-inner-product C*-modules
description: For x,y in a semi-inner-product C*-module, |⟨x,y⟩|²≤∥⟨x,x⟩∥⟨y,y⟩ in the order on the coefficient C*-algebra.

title: Positive linear functional on a C*-algebra
description: A complex linear map φ:A→ℂ satisfying φ(a*a)≥0 for every a∈A.

title: Spectral radius in a complex Banach algebra
description: For an element a of a complex Banach algebra, its spectral radius is sup{|λ|:λ belongs to the spectrum of a}, using the unitization when the algebra has no identity.

title: Grüss inequality for bounded real functions
description: If m≤f≤M and n≤g≤N almost everywhere on [a,b], with a<b, then the absolute difference between the average of fg and the product of the averages of f and g is at most (M−m)(N−n)/4. The constant 1/4 is optimal.

title: Vector-valued discrete Fourier transform
description: For x₀,…,xₙ₋₁ in a complex vector space, its discrete Fourier transform has components ∑ₖ₌₀ⁿ⁻¹exp(−2πimk/n)xₖ, m=0,…,n−1. Sign and scalar normalization conventions may vary.

title: Grüss inequality for finite families in semi-inner-product C*-modules
description: Let pᵢ≥0 sum to one, and let xᵢ,yᵢ lie in a semi-inner-product C*-module with ∥xᵢ−a∥≤r and ∥yᵢ−b∥≤s. Then ∥∑pᵢ⟨xᵢ,yᵢ⟩−⟨∑pᵢxᵢ,∑pᵢyᵢ⟩∥≤rs; the constant one is optimal.

title: Compact topological space
description: A topological space in which every open cover has a finite subcover.

title: Absolute continuity of measures
description: A measure ν is absolutely continuous with respect to μ on the same σ-algebra if μ(A)=0 implies ν(A)=0.

title: Radon–Nikodym derivative of a measure
description: A nonnegative measurable function f representing ν relative to μ by ν(A)=∫_A f dμ for every measurable A; it is defined up to μ-almost-everywhere equality when such a density exists.

title: Real polynomial in finitely many variables
description: A finite real linear combination of monomials x₁^{a₁}⋯x_d^{a_d} with nonnegative integer exponents.

title: Convex body in Euclidean space
description: A compact convex subset of ℝᵈ with nonempty interior.

title: Star body about the origin
description: A compact set star shaped about 0 whose radial function ρ(u)=max{t≥0:tu∈K} on the unit sphere is positive and continuous.

title: Support function of a convex body
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝᵈ, h_K(u)=max{x·u:x∈K}; it may be restricted to the unit sphere or extended positively homogeneously to ℝᵈ.

title: Minkowski sum of subsets of a vector space
description: For subsets A,B of a vector space, A+B={a+b:a∈A,b∈B}.

title: Hausdorff distance between compact sets
description: For nonempty compact sets A,B in a metric space, d_H(A,B) is the maximum of sup_{a∈A}inf_{b∈B}d(a,b) and sup_{b∈B}inf_{a∈A}d(a,b).

title: Banach–Mazur distance between origin-symmetric convex bodies
description: For origin-symmetric convex bodies K,L⊂ℝᵈ, d_BM(K,L)=inf{t≥1:L⊆TK⊆tL for an invertible linear map T}.

title: Surface area measure of a convex body
description: The measure S_K on the unit sphere assigning a Borel set of directions the boundary area of points of K whose outer unit normal lies in that set; points with nonunique normals form a boundary-area null set.

title: Curvature function of a convex body
description: When the surface area measure S_K is absolutely continuous with respect to spherical area measure, its Radon–Nikodym density f_K is called the curvature function.

title: Projection body of a convex body
description: The origin-symmetric convex body ΠK whose support function at a unit vector u is the (d−1)-dimensional volume of the orthogonal projection of K onto u⊥.

title: Cauchy’s projection formula for convex bodies
description: For a convex body K and unit u, the volume of K projected onto u⊥ equals ½∫|u·v| dS_K(v).

title: Intersection body of a star body
description: The star body IK with radial function ρ_IK(u) equal to the (d−1)-dimensional volume of K∩u⊥.

title: Zonoid
description: A compact convex set that is a Hausdorff limit of finite Minkowski sums of line segments.

title: Mixed volume of convex bodies
description: The symmetric coefficient V(K₁,…,K_d) in the homogeneous degree-d volume polynomial |∑tᵢKᵢ| for nonnegative scalars tᵢ, normalized by V(K,…,K)=|K|.

title: Quermassintegral of a convex body
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝᵈ, W_i(K)=V(K[d−i],B₂ᵈ[i]), where brackets denote repeated arguments and B₂ᵈ is the unit Euclidean ball.

title: Projection body associated with a quermassintegral
description: For 0≤i≤d−2, Π_iK is the convex body with support function h_{Π_iK}(u)=W_i(K|u⊥), where the quermassintegral is taken in the (d−1)-dimensional space u⊥.

title: Aleksandrov–Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes
description: For convex bodies K₁,…,K_d⊂ℝᵈ, V(K₁,K₂,K₃,…,K_d)²≥V(K₁,K₁,K₃,…,K_d)V(K₂,K₂,K₃,…,K_d).

title: Spherical harmonic
description: The restriction to the unit sphere in ℝᵈ of a homogeneous polynomial annihilated by the Euclidean Laplacian. Its degree is the degree of that polynomial.

title: Normalized spherical Radon transform
description: For a function f on S^{d−1}, Rf(u) is its average over the equatorial sphere S^{d−1}∩u⊥; the normalization gives R1=1.

title: Schneider’s projection-functional monotonicity theorem
description: For a full-dimensional convex body K⊂ℝᵈ, set P(K)=|ΠK|/|K|^{d−1}. Then P(K)≥P(ΠK), with equality exactly when K is homothetic to Π²K.

title: Local attraction of the ball under projection-body iteration
description: For each d≥3 there is ε_d>0 such that if a convex body K has absolutely continuous surface area measure and ∥f_{TK}−1∥∞<ε_d for some invertible linear T, then ΠᵐK converges to the Euclidean ball up to linear equivalence, in Banach–Mazur distance.

title: Local strict minimum in Petty’s conjectured projection inequality
description: For each d≥3 there is ε_d>0 such that a nonellipsoidal convex body K with absolutely continuous surface area measure and ∥f_{TK}−1∥∞<ε_d for some invertible linear T satisfies |ΠK|/|K|^{d−1}>|ΠB₂ᵈ|/|B₂ᵈ|^{d−1}.

title: Saroglou–Zvavitch refinement of Lutwak’s quermassintegral inequality
description: For every convex body K⊂ℝᵈ, d≥3, W_{d−2}(Π_{d−2}K)≥[d(d−2)ω_{d−1}²/((d−1)²ω_d)]W_{d−1}(K)²+[ω_{d−1}²/(d−1)²]W_{d−2}(K), where ω_j is the j-dimensional unit ball volume. Equality holds for balls; the inequality is strict for bodies that are not centrally symmetric.

title: Compact set star shaped about the origin
description: A nonempty compact set K⊂ℝⁿ such that [0,x]⊆K for every x∈K. It need not be convex, have interior, or have a continuous positive radial function.

title: Support function of a nonempty compact Euclidean set
description: For nonempty compact K⊂ℝⁿ, h_K(u)=max{x·u:x∈K}; this equals the support function of its convex hull.

title: Mean support function on the unit sphere
description: For nonempty compact K⊂ℝⁿ, M*(K)=∫_{S^{n−1}}h_K(u)dσ(u), with σ normalized to total mass one. This is half the mean width under the convention that width in direction u is h_K(u)+h_K(−u).

title: Reflection in a linear hyperplane in Euclidean space
description: For a unit vector u, reflection in u⊥ is R_u(x)=x−2(x·u)u.

title: Minkowski symmetrization of a Euclidean set
description: For K⊂ℝⁿ and a unit u, M_u(K)=½(K+R_uK), where R_u is reflection in u⊥.

title: ε-net of a subset of a metric space
description: A set N is an ε-net of A if every point of A is within distance ε of some point of N. Unless specified otherwise, N need not be a subset of A.

title: Klartag’s quantitative Minkowski symmetrization theorem
description: For n≥2, 0<ε<1/2 and a nonempty compact convex set K⊂ℝⁿ with M*(K)=M₀, at most cn|log ε| Minkowski symmetrizations produce K̃ with (1−ε)M₀B₂ⁿ⊆K̃⊆(1+ε)M₀B₂ⁿ, for a universal c.

title: Florentin–Segal quantitative symmetrization theorem for star-shaped sets
description: For n≥2, 0<ε<1/2 and a nonempty compact set K⊂ℝⁿ star shaped about 0, at most Cn|log ε| Minkowski symmetrizations produce K̃ with (1−ε)M*(K)B₂ⁿ⊆K̃⊆(1+ε)M*(K)B₂ⁿ, for a universal C.

title: Special linear group SL₂(ℤ)
description: The group of2×2 integer matrices [[a,b],[c,d]] satisfying ad−bc=1, with matrix multiplication.

title: Congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ)
description: A subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) containing Γ(N)={M:M≡I moduloN} for some positive integer N.

title: Congruence subgroup Γ₁(N)
description: The subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) whose matrices [[a,b],[c,d]] satisfy a≡d≡1 and c≡0 moduloN.

title: Modular form of integer weight on a congruence subgroup
description: A holomorphic function f on the upper half-plane satisfying f((aτ+b)/(cτ+d))=(cτ+d)^k f(τ) for matrices in a specified congruence subgroup, and holomorphic at every cusp.

title: Weight-k slash operator on the upper half-plane
description: For γ=[[a,b],[c,d]]∈SL₂(ℤ), (f|ₖγ)(τ)=(cτ+d)^{-k}f((aτ+b)/(cτ+d)).

title: Almost holomorphic modular form
description: For a specified congruence subgroup and integer weight k, a function obeying the scalar modular weight-k transformation, polynomial in 1/Im(τ) with holomorphic coefficients and of at most polynomial growth in Im(τ) after normalization at every cusp. This is the almost holomorphic convention called nearly holomorphic by Larson, and excludes cusp poles.

title: Quasimodular form
description: A holomorphic function whose weight-k modular transformation differs by a finite polynomial in c/(cτ+d), with holomorphic coefficient functions and the required cusp-growth conditions; equivalently the holomorphic part of an almost holomorphic modular form.

title: Classical Jacobi form
description: For an integer weight k and integer index m≥0, a holomorphic function φ(τ,z) on H×C with φ((aτ+b)/(cτ+d),z/(cτ+d))=(cτ+d)^k exp(2πimcz²/(cτ+d))φ(τ,z) for γ in a specified congruence subgroup, φ(τ,z+rτ+s)=exp(−2πim(r²τ+2rz))φ(τ,z), and Fourier support 4mn−ℓ²≥0 at every cusp. This is the scalar trivial-multiplier convention.

title: Almost holomorphic Jacobi form
description: For integer weight k and nonnegative integer index m, a function with the scalar Jacobi modular and elliptic transformations, polynomial in 1/(τ−τ̄) and (z−z̄)/(τ−τ̄) with holomorphic coefficients, and satisfying |φ(τ,z)|≤C·Im(τ)^N exp(2πm Im(z)²/Im(τ)) in a Jacobi translation strip after each cusp normalization.

title: Jacobi theta function
description: The holomorphic series θ(τ,z)=∑_{n∈ℤ}exp(πin²τ+2πinz) for Im(τ)>0; this specifies the zero-characteristic theta convention.

title: Complex partial derivative
description: The complex derivative in one coordinate of a function of several complex variables, holding the other coordinates fixed.

title: Dedekind eta function
description: For Im(τ)>0 and q=exp(2πiτ), η(τ)=exp(πiτ/12)∏_(n≥1)(1−qⁿ). The explicit exponential prefactor specifies the meaning of q^(1/24) without choosing a complex root.

title: Infinite q-Pochhammer symbol
Rose’s generalized sum-of-divisor functions
description: For a positive integer n,a set S⊆{1,…,n} stable under negation modulo n,and k≥1, A_{S,n,k}(q)=∑_{0<m₁<⋯<mₖ, mᵢ mod n∈S}q^{m₁+⋯+mₖ}/∏ᵢ(1−q^{mᵢ})² for∣q∣<1.

title: Multinomial theorem
description: For commuting variables,(x₁+⋯+xᵣ)^n=∑_{n₁+⋯+nᵣ=n}n!/(n₁!⋯nᵣ!)x₁^{n₁}⋯xᵣ^{nᵣ}, summing over nonnegative indices.

title: Larson’s Γ₁(n) level theorem for generalized divisor sums
description: For every symmetric residue set S modulo n and k≥1, Rose’s A_{S,n,k} is a quasimodular form of mixed weight at most2k on Γ₁(n).

title: Positional base-b expansion of a nonnegative integer
description: For an integer base b≥2, write x=∑_{i=0}^{n−1}aᵢbⁱ with digits0≤aᵢ<b and a nonzero leading digit when x>0;0 has the zero expansion.

title: Digit-power sum map
description: For base b≥2 and integer e≥1, S_{e,b}(x) is the sum of the e-th powers of the base-b digits of the positive integer x.

title: Iteration of a self-map
description: For f:X→X, define f⁰=id_X and f^{n+1}=f∘fⁿ for natural n.

title: Generalized happy number
description: A positive integer x is happy for base b and exponent e if some iterate of the digit-power map S_{e,b} sends x to1; ordinary happy numbers have b=10 and e=2.

title: Attraction height for a digit-power sum map
description: For fixed b,e and target u, the attraction height of x is the least h≥0 with S_{e,b}^h(x)=u, when such an h exists.

title: Smallest integer of a specified digit-power attraction height
description: For fixed b,e,u and h, σ_h(u) is the least positive integer whose first hit of u under S_{e,b} occurs at exactly h iterations, when this set is nonempty.

title: Asymptotic density of a subset of the positive integers
description: For S⊆ℕ₊, its asymptotic density is lim_{N→∞}|S∩{1,…,N}|/N when this limit exists.

title: Waring number g(k)
description: For k≥1, g(k) is the least s such that every nonnegative integer is a sum of s nonnegative integer k-th powers, allowing zero summands.

title: Hilbert–Waring theorem
description: For every positive integer k, the Waring number g(k) is finite.

title: Mei–Read-McFarland recurrence for large minimal attracted numbers
description: Fix b≥2 and e≥1. There is an explicit threshold M(b,e) such that, whenever the exact-height minima σ_h(u),σ_{h+1}(u) exist and σ_h(u) exceeds M(b,e), S_{e,b}(σ_{h+1}(u))=σ_h(u). The paper gives a threshold on the size of σ_h(u), not a uniform threshold on h.

title: Stochastic transition matrix
description: A square real matrix P with nonnegative entries and row sums one; P(x,y) is the one-step transition probability from x to y.

title: Time-homogeneous Markov chain on a finite state space
description: A sequence of random states in a finite set whose conditional next-state distribution given its whole past depends only on the present state, through one fixed stochastic transition matrix.

title: Stationary distribution of a finite Markov chain
description: A probability row vector π satisfying πP=π for the chain’s transition matrix P.

title: Irreducible finite Markov chain
description: A finite Markov chain is irreducible if for any states x,y some number of steps n has Pⁿ(x,y)>0.

title: Aperiodic finite Markov chain
description: A state has period equal to the gcd of its possible positive return times. An irreducible chain is aperiodic when this common period is one.

title: Detailed balance for a finite Markov chain
description: A positive probability vector π satisfies detailed balance for P if π(x)P(x,y)=π(y)P(y,x) for every pair of states.

title: Reversible finite Markov chain
description: A finite Markov chain with a positive stationary distribution π satisfying detailed balance; under π its finite path laws are invariant under reversal of time.

title: Filtration of σ-algebras
description: An increasing family (F_t) of sub-σ-algebras on a fixed probability space, indexed by ordered time: F_s⊆F_t for s≤t.

title: Stopping time for a filtration
description: A random time T taking values in the time index together with infinity, such that {T≤t}∈F_t for every t; by time t one can determine whether T has occurred.

title: Uniform distribution on the unit interval
description: The real probability law on [0,1] whose probability of an interval [a,b]⊆[0,1] is b−a.

title: Randomized stopping time
description: A stopping time after the process filtration has been enlarged by auxiliary randomization independent of the original process.

title: Hitting time of a set for a Markov chain
description: For A in the state space, T_A=inf{t≥0:X_t∈A}, with infinity if A is never visited. The starting state or initial law is specified separately.

title: Coupling of finite probability distributions
description: A joint probability distribution on a product of finite state spaces whose marginals are the specified distributions.

title: Maximal coupling of finite probability distributions
description: A coupling (X,Y) of p and q with P(X≠Y)=d_TV(p,q), attaining the smallest possible disagreement probability.

title: Strong stationary time of a Markov chain
description: A randomized stopping time T such that X_T has the stationary distribution and is independent of T.

title: Separation distance from a positive finite distribution
description: For a probability mass function p and a strictly positive π, sep(p,π)=max_x(1−p(x)/π(x)). It is generally not symmetric.

title: Total variation mixing time
description: For a finite chain and chosen initial law, t_mix(ε)=inf{t:d_TV(Law(X_t),π)≤ε}. Worst-case mixing time takes the maximum over starting states.

title: Total variation cutoff for a family of finite Markov chains
description: For chosen initial laws, a family has cutoff at t_N if d_N(ct_N)→1 for every 0<c<1 and d_N(ct_N)→0 for every c>1, where d_N is distance to stationarity.

title: Cutoff window in total variation
description: A scale w_N=o(t_N) is a cutoff window if lim_{γ→∞}liminf_N d_N(t_N−γw_N)=1 and lim_{γ→∞}limsup_N d_N(t_N+γw_N)=0, with integer times rounded in discrete time.

title: Finite birth-and-death chain
description: A finite Markov chain on {0,…,N} that can move only to neighboring states or remain at its current state; continuous-time versions have jump rates only between neighbors.

title: Stochastically monotone Markov kernel
description: On a partially ordered finite state space, P is monotone if Pf is increasing whenever f is increasing, equivalently P(x,·) is stochastically dominated by P(y,·) whenever x≤y.

title: Halting set for total variation mixing
description: For a Markov chain with specified initial distribution, a set A is halting for total variation if d_TV(Law(X_t),π)≤P(T_A>t) for every t≥0.

title: Eigenvalue of a linear endomorphism
description: A scalar λ for which a linear endomorphism T has a nonzero vector v with Tv=λv.

title: Spectral gap of a reversible finite Markov chain
description: For an irreducible reversible transition matrix with eigenvalues 1=λ₀>λ₁≥⋯, its spectral gap is 1−λ₁; the absolute spectral gap instead uses max_{i≥1}|λ_i|.

title: Killed transition matrix of a finite Markov chain
description: For a set A, retain the submatrix P_{Aᶜ,Aᶜ}; missing row mass records killing when the chain enters A. Its powers give survival transition probabilities before hitting A.

title: Time-homogeneous continuous-time Markov chain on a finite set
description: A right-continuous jump process on a finite state space whose future conditional law depends only on its current state and elapsed time. Its transition matrices form a semigroup.

title: Generator of a finite continuous-time Markov chain
description: The real matrix Q with Q(x,y)=lim_{h↓0}(P_h(x,y)−1_{x=y})/h, nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums; off-diagonal entries are jump rates.

title: Matrix exponential
description: For a finite square real or complex matrix A, exp(A)=∑_{n≥0}Aⁿ/n!, with convergence in any matrix norm.

title: Sequence of orthogonal polynomials
description: A sequence of real polynomials of successive degrees, orthogonal under ∫p(x)q(x)dμ(x) for a specified positive measure with the necessary finite moments.

title: Gilbert–Shannon–Reeds riffle shuffle
description: Split a deck at a binomially chosen position and interleave the two packets uniformly while preserving each packet’s internal order. Repeating gives a Markov chain on permutations.

title: Ehrenfest urn chain
description: A chain tracking the number of particles in one of two urns when particles switch urns, equivalently the number of ones in a collection of two-state coordinates. Discrete and continuous rates must be specified.

title: Bernoulli–Laplace urn chain
description: Two urns hold fixed numbers of red and black balls; choose one ball uniformly in each urn and swap them. The number of red balls in one urn is a birth-and-death chain.

title: Aldous–Diaconis optimal strong stationary time theorem
description: For an irreducible aperiodic finite Markov chain with positive stationary law, there exists a strong stationary time T with P(T>n)=sep(Law(X_n),π) for every n; any strong stationary time has tail at least this separation distance.

title: Griffeath’s maximal coupling theorem for Markov chains
description: Finite Markov chains with the same transition kernel can be coupled so that their coalescence time T satisfies P(T>n)=d_TV(Law(X_n),Law(Y_n)) for every n. Such a coupling need not be co-adapted.

title: Coquio’s total variation halting-set criterion
description: For a finite Markov chain with stationary law π and specified initial law, the set M={x:Law(X_t)(x)≤π(x) for every t≥0} is halting: d_TV(Law(X_t),π)≤P(T_M>t). The empty set gives only the trivial bound.

title: Coquio’s cutoff criterion from a concentrated halting time
description: For a family of finite irreducible reversible chains with halting sets A_N and irreducible aperiodic killed kernels, let m_N=ET_{A_N}→∞, s_N²=Var(T_{A_N}), and λ_N the largest killed-kernel eigenvalue. If s_N=o(m_N) and (1−λ_N)m_N→∞, there is total variation cutoff at m_N. If also liminf(1−λ_N)s_N>0, s_N is a cutoff window.

title: Middle halting states of symmetric birth-and-death chains
description: For an irreducible symmetric monotone discrete-time birth-and-death chain on {0,…,2N+1} started at0, N+1 is halting for total variation. For a symmetric continuous-time irreducible birth-and-death chain on {0,…,N} started at0, ceil(N/2) is halting. Symmetry means reflection invariance of transition probabilities or jump rates.

title: Geometric distribution on positive integers
description: For 0<p≤1, P(G=k)=p(1−p)^(k−1) for k=1,2,…; G counts trials up to and including the first success. Its tail is P(G>k)=(1−p)^k.

title: Binomial distribution
description: The law of the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli(p) trials: P(B=k)=binom(n,k)p^k(1−p)^(n−k),0≤k≤n.

title: Absolute spectral gap of a finite Markov chain
description: For an irreducible finite transition matrix P, the absolute spectral gap is 1−max{|λ|:λ≠1 is an eigenvalue of P}. Unlike 1−λ₂ for a reversible chain, this definition allows complex eigenvalues and nonreversibility.

title: Doubly stochastic matrix
description: A square real matrix with nonnegative entries and every row and column summing to one. The uniform probability vector is stationary.

title: With high probability in an asymptotic random model
description: An event A_n holds with high probability if P(A_n)→1 as n→∞. Also called asymptotically almost surely; this does not itself assert almost-sure eventual occurrence on a common probability space.

title: Big O notation
description: The assertion f=O(g) along a specified limit means |f(x)|≤C|g(x)| near that limit for a fixed finite C. Subscripts specify allowed dependence on fixed parameters. For sequences use x=n→∞.

title: Little o notation
description: The assertion f=o(g) along a specified limit means f(x)/g(x)→0, where g is nonzero near that limit. Sequences are the instance x=n→∞.

title: Asymptotic equivalence
description: The assertion f∼g along a specified limit means f(x)/g(x)→1, where g is nonzero near that limit. Sequences are the instance x=n→∞.

title: Cycle graph
description: The finite graph C_n,n≥3,whose vertices can be arranged cyclically so that each is joined to its predecessor and successor.

title: Pure drift chain on uniformly rewired cycle arcs
description: Cut a directed cycle at k uniformly chosen distinct edges into arcs. Along each remaining arc the chain moves deterministically forward; at an arc endpoint it chooses the start of one of the k arcs uniformly. Equivalently one can begin with k independent positive geometric arc lengths and then condition their sum to obtain a fixed-size model.

title: Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling
description: Use a Markov chain with a prescribed stationary distribution to generate dependent approximate samples from that distribution,with ergodic averages used to estimate expectations.

title: Spectral-gap bound for pure drift on randomly rewired cycle arcs
description: Let k arc lengths be independent Geometric(1/L) variables,with k,L→∞ and fixed 0<ρ_l<log L/log k<ρ_u<∞. For the pure drift chain that moves along arcs and chooses the next arc uniformly at endpoints, every γ>4 gives absolute spectral gap greater than 1/(L(log k)^γ) with high probability; the exceptional probability is O(k^(−c)L^(−d)) for any fixed c,d>0. Conditioning the total number of vertices to be n gives the same high-probability bound for the uniformly cut-cycle model with L=n/k.

title: Finite hypergraph
description: A finite vertex set V with a family E of subsets of V called hyperedges.

title: Fractional matching in a finite hypergraph
description: Weights φ(e)≥0 on the hyperedges such that ∑_{e∋v}φ(e)≤1 for every vertex v. The fractional matching number is the maximum of ∑_eφ(e).

title: Independent set in a hypergraph
description: A set of vertices containing no hyperedge.

title: b-fold coloring of a graph
description: An assignment of a set of b colors to every vertex such that adjacent vertices receive disjoint color sets. The b-fold chromatic number χ_b(G) is the smallest total number of colors permitting such an assignment.

title: Greatest lower bound
description: For a subset A of a partially ordered set, its greatest lower bound is a lower bound of A lying above every lower bound of A, when one exists.

title: Fractional chromatic number of a graph
description: For a finite graph G, χ_f(G)=inf_{b≥1}χ_b(G)/b, where χ_b is its b-fold chromatic number.

title: Dependency graph for random variables
description: A finite graph on the indices of random variables such that families indexed by disjoint vertex sets with no edge between them are independent. In particular, a variable is independent of the joint family of all its nonneighbors.

title: Hypergraph-correlated random variables
description: For a finite hypergraph (V,E), an E-indexed family Y_e is hypergraph-correlated if independent underlying variables X_v exist with each Y_e a measurable function only of (X_v)_{v∈e}.

title: Bernoulli distribution
description: The distribution on {0,1} assigning probability p to 1 and 1−p to 0, for 0≤p≤1.

title: Erdős–Rényi G(n,p) random graph
description: The random simple graph on n labeled vertices in which every possible edge is present independently with probability p.

title: Independence system
description: A finite set V and a nonempty family I of subsets of V closed under taking subsets.

title: k-wise independent random variables
description: A family of random variables is k-wise independent if every subfamily of at most k members is jointly independent.

title: Hölder’s inequality
description: For measurable functions f_i and exponents p_i∈[1,∞] with ∑_i1/p_i=1, ∫|∏_if_i|dμ≤∏_i‖f_i‖_{p_i}.

title: Young’s inequality for products
description: For a,b≥0 and p,q>1 with 1/p+1/q=1, ab≤aᵖ/p+bᑫ/q.

title: Concavity of the weighted geometric mean
description: For β_i≥0 with ∑_iβ_i=1, the function (x_i)↦∏_ix_i^{β_i} is concave on the nonnegative orthant, with zero-weight factors omitted.

title: Finner’s inequality
description: If nonnegative Y_e are hypergraph-correlated over a finite hypergraph and φ is a fractional matching with positive weights on the factors considered, then E∏_eY_e≤∏_e(EY_e^{1/φ(e)})^{φ(e)}. Zero-weight factors can instead be controlled by their essential suprema.

title: Hölder inequality controlled by b-fold graph coloring
description: For nonnegative random variables Y_v admitting dependency graph G and every positive integer b, E∏_vY_v≤∏_v(EY_v^{χ_b(G)/b})^{b/χ_b(G)}, with the usual extended-integral interpretation.

title: Janson’s Hoeffding bound for dependency graphs
description: If n random variables Y_v∈[0,1] have dependency graph G and q=n⁻¹∑_vEY_v, then P(∑_vY_v≥n(q+ε))≤exp(−2nε²/χ_f(G)) for ε>0.

title: Pelekis–Ramon–Wang Bennett bound for dependency graphs
description: If finitely many real random variables Y_v have dependency graph G, EY_v=0, Y_v≤1 and S=∑_vVar(Y_v)>0, then for t>0, P(∑_vY_v≥t)≤exp{−S[(1+t/S)ln(1+t/S)−t/S]/χ_f(G)}.

title: Bennett exponential-moment bound for a bounded-above variable
description: If EY=0, Y≤1 and EY²=σ²<∞, then Eexp(aY)≤exp(σ²(eᵃ−1−a)) for a≥0.

title: Fractional-matching bound for random independent sets in a hypergraph
description: Include each vertex v of a finite hypergraph independently with probability p_v. For every fractional matching φ, the probability that the chosen vertices contain no hyperedge is at most ∏_e(1−∏_{v∈e}p_v)^{φ(e)}. For k-uniform hypergraphs and constant p this is at most (1−pᵏ)^{ν*(H)}.

title: Partially ordered abelian group
description: An abelian group with a translation-invariant partial order. In this paper it is directed: every element is a difference of positive elements.

title: Order unit in a partially ordered abelian group
description: A positive element u such that every g satisfies −Nu≤g≤Nu for some positive integer N.

title: Unperforated partially ordered abelian group
description: An ordered abelian group in which ng≥0 for a positive integer n implies g≥0.

title: Riesz decomposition property for an ordered abelian group
description: Whenever0≤a≤b+c with b,c≥0, there are0≤b₁≤b and0≤c₁≤c with a=b₁+c₁.

title: Dimension group
description: A directed unperforated partially ordered abelian group with the Riesz decomposition property.

title: Simple partially ordered abelian group
description: A nontrivial directed ordered abelian group in which every nonzero positive element is an order unit.

title: Group homomorphism
description: A map f:G→H satisfying f(xy)=f(x)f(y) for all x,y.

title: Trace on a partially ordered abelian group
description: A nonzero additive homomorphism τ:G→ℝ sending positive elements to nonnegative reals; it is normalized at an order unit u when τ(u)=1.

title: Quotient of an abelian group by a subgroup
description: For an abelian group G and subgroup H,the cosets G/H form an abelian group under (g+H)+(g′+H)=g+g′+H.

title: Torsion-free abelian group
description: An abelian group in which ng=0 with a nonzero integer n forces g=0.

title: Convex subset of a real vector space
description: A subset C of a real vector space is convex if (1−t)x+ty∈C whenever x,y∈C and0≤t≤1. The vector space may be infinite-dimensional.

title: Face of a convex set
description: A convex subset F of a convex set K is a face if an interior point of a nontrivial segment in K belongs to F only when both endpoints belong to F.

title: Extreme point of a convex set
description: A point x of a convex set is extreme if x=(1−t)y+tz with0<t<1 and y,z in the set implies y=z=x.

title: Real affine function on a convex set
description: A function f:C→ℝ on a convex set satisfying f((1−t)x+ty)=(1−t)f(x)+tf(y) for0≤t≤1.

title: Space of continuous affine functions on a compact convex set
description: Aff(K) is the real vector space of continuous affine functions on a compact convex set K,equipped with the supremum norm and pointwise order.

title: Normalized trace space of an ordered abelian group
description: For an ordered abelian group with order unit u, S(G,u) is the set of positive homomorphisms τ:G→ℝ with τ(u)=1, with the topology of pointwise convergence on G.

title: Choquet simplex
description: A compact convex set in a locally convex real topological vector space for which each point has a unique maximal representing probability measure in the Choquet order. In the metrizable case this is the unique representing probability measure supported on its extreme boundary.

title: Affine representation of an ordered group with order unit
description: The homomorphism G→Aff(S(G,u)) sending g to the evaluation function τ↦τ(g). Its kernel is the infinitesimal subgroup.

title: Convex subgroup of an ordered abelian group
description: A subgroup H such that h₁≤g≤h₂ with h₁,h₂∈H forces g∈H. The quotient carries the induced order when H is convex.

title: Dense subset of a metric space
description: A subset A of a metric space X is dense if every open ball centered in X with positive radius meets A.

title: Full lattice in Euclidean space
description: A subgroup Λ⊂ℝⁿ generated overℤ by a real vector-space basis ofℝⁿ.

title: Refinable trace on an ordered abelian group
description: A positive trace τ is refinable if every equality τ(g)=∑ᵢτ(aᵢ),with g,aᵢ positive and g nonzero,can be realized by positive aᵢ′ with g=∑ᵢaᵢ′ and τ(aᵢ′)=τ(aᵢ).

title: Good trace on an ordered abelian group
description: A positive trace τ is good if for a∈G and positive nonzero g with0<τ(a)<τ(g),there is0≤a′≤g with τ(a′)=τ(a).

title: Gordan’s theorem of the alternative
description: For a real matrix A,exactly one holds: Ay=0 for some nonzero y≥0; or xA is strictly positive for some real row x.

title: Farkas’ lemma
description: For a real m×n matrix A and real row b,exactly one holds: xA≤b for some real row x; or Ay=0 for some nonzero column y≥0 with by<0.

title: Handelman–Roy criterion for one-sided linear Diophantine approximation
description: Let H⊂ℝⁿ be an additive subgroup containing no strictly positive vector,and F the smallest face of the standard simplex containing the nonnegative normalized linear functionals that vanish on H. Then for every h∈H,m≥1 and ε>0 there exists h′∈H with h−mh′>−ε coordinatewise iff for every f∈F,the subgroup f(H) is zero or dense inℝ.

title: Handelman–Roy unperforation criterion for finite-trace dimension groups
description: Let G be a simple noncyclic dimension group with finitely many pure traces,and H=ker_G Z(H) a subgroup with H∩G⁺={0},where Z(H) consists of normalized traces vanishing on H. If F is the smallest face containing Z(H),then G/H is unperforated iff f(H) is zero or dense inℝ for every f∈F.

title: Affine algebraic group over a field
description: An affine algebraic group over a field F is specified by a finitely generated commutative Hopf F-algebra A: for each commutative F-algebra R its group of R-points is Hom_(F-alg)(A,R), with multiplication induced by the coproduct. Equivalently it is a finite-type affine group scheme over F.

title: Connected reductive algebraic group
description: A smooth connected affine algebraic group whose largest connected normal unipotent subgroup over an algebraic closure is trivial.

title: Restriction of scalars of an algebraic group
description: For a finite field extension M/F and an M-group H, Res_{M/F}H is the F-group with R-points H(R⊗_F M) for each F-algebra R.

title: Algebraic torus
description: An algebraic group that becomes isomorphic over an algebraic closure to a finite product of copies of the multiplicative group.

title: Anisotropic reductive group over a field
description: A reductive group over F containing no nontrivial F-split torus; an anisotropic torus has no positive-dimensional split subtorus.

title: Parabolic subgroup of a reductive algebraic group
description: A closed algebraic subgroup P of a connected reductive F-group G such that, after base change to an algebraic closure, P contains a Borel subgroup of G. Equivalently G/P is projective.

title: Unipotent radical of an algebraic group
description: The largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of an algebraic group.

title: Place of a number field
description: An equivalence class of nontrivial absolute values on a number field; its completion is denoted F_v. Archimedean and nonarchimedean places give its infinite and finite places.

title: Adele ring of a number field
description: The restricted product A_F=∏′_v F_v of all completions of a number field,where almost every finite component lies in the valuation ring O_v.

title: Adelic points of an algebraic group
description: For an algebraic group G over a number field F,the restricted product G(A_F)=∏′_v G(F_v),using integral compact subgroups at almost all finite places.

title: Haar measure on a locally compact group
description: A nonzero Radon measure on a locally compact group, i.e. a Borel measure finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets and inner regular on open sets, invariant under left translation: μ(gA)=μ(A). A right Haar measure is defined analogously with right translations.

title: Unimodular locally compact group
description: A locally compact group whose left Haar measures are also right invariant.

title: Unitary character of a topological group
description: A continuous homomorphism from a topological group to the unit circle inℂ under multiplication.

title: Compactly supported smooth test function on an adelic group
description: A compactly supported complex function on G(A_F) that is smooth in the archimedean variables and locally constant in the nonarchimedean variables. Factorizable test functions are restricted tensors of local test functions.

title: Harish–Chandra subgroup of adelic points
description: The subgroup G(A_F)¹ of points x satisfying∣χ(x)∣_A=1 for every F-rational algebraic character χ:G→G_m; equivalently the kernel of the logarithmic Harish–Chandra map.

title: Tamagawa measure of a reductive group over a number field
description: For a connected reductive number-field group G of dimension d, choose an invariant F-rational gauge form and its standard local measures m_v. Let ρ_G be the Galois representation on X*(G)⊗C and r_G the leading nonzero Laurent coefficient of its finite-place Artin L-function at s=1. The Tamagawa measure is r_G⁻¹|d_F|^(−d/2)(∏_(v infinite)m_v)(∏_(v finite)L_v(1,ρ_G)m_v). It is independent of rescaling that gauge form by F×.

title: Hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup
description: For a reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field,a subgroup given by the valuation-ring points of a smooth affine integral group scheme whose special fiber is connected reductive.

title: First nonabelian Galois cohomology set
description: For an algebraic F-group H, H¹(F,H) is the pointed set of continuous 1-cocycles of Gal(F^sep/F) with values in the discrete group H(F^sep), modulo c′(σ)=h⁻¹c(σ)σ(h). The distinguished point is the trivial cocycle.

title: Twisted relative orbit for two involutions
description: Given G=Res_{M/F}G₀ with commuting involutions σ and τ,and θ=στ,the relative classes are double cosets G^σ(k)∖G(k)/G^θ(k); geometric relative classes permit the acting elements over an algebraic closure.

title: Relatively τ-semisimple element
description: In the commuting-involution setting θ=στ,an element γ is relatively τ-semisimple when δ=γγ^{-θ} is τ-semisimple,meaning δδ^τ is semisimple.

title: Strongly relatively τ-regular element
description: A relatively τ-semisimple γ for which the τ-centralizer of γγ^{-θ} in G^σ is a connected torus.

title: Relatively τ-elliptic element
description: In the commuting-involution setup G=Res_(M/F)G₀, θ=στ, a relatively τ-semisimple γ is relatively τ-elliptic if C^τ_(G,δ)/Z(G₀), with δ=γγ^(−θ), is anisotropic over the ground field. The centralizer here is in all G; anisotropy of a possibly disconnected reductive quotient means its identity component has no nontrivial split torus.

title: Twisted relative orbital integral
description: Over a local field k, for relatively semisimple γ∈G(k), put H=G^σ(k)×G^θ(k) and L=(G_γ^(σθ))°(k). Given a unitary character χ of H trivial on L and compatible Haar measures, the twisted relative orbital integral is ∫_(L∖H)χ(x,y)f(x⁻¹γy)d[x,y], for compactly supported smooth f. In the convention χ(x,y)=μ₁(x)μ₂(y)⁻¹, relevance requires this actual character to be trivial on L. The adelic version replaces local points by adelic points and is defined when the integral converges.

title: F-supercuspidal local test function
description: At a finite place v,a compactly supported locally constant function on G(F_v) is F-supercuspidal if every left or right translate has zero integral along the unipotent radical of each proper F-defined parabolic subgroup.

title: Automorphic cusp form on a reductive group
description: An automorphic form on a connected reductive number-field group whose constant term ∫_(N(F)∖N(A_F))φ(ng)dn vanishes for every g and every unipotent radical N of a proper F-parabolic subgroup. Its square-integrable Hilbert closure on G(F)∖G(A_F)¹ is a separate cuspidal L²-space.

title: Cuspidal automorphic representation
description: An irreducible unitary representation occurring as a closed summand in the cuspidal L²-space of the adelic group, with the chosen central or Harish–Chandra normalization. Its smooth K∞-finite vectors give the usual algebraic automorphic representation.

title: Automorphic period integral on a Harish–Chandra quotient
description: For a reductive F-group G, an F-subgroup H, a smooth cuspidal form φ on G(F)∖G(A_F)¹ and a unitary character χ trivial on H(F), the period in this normalization is ∫_(H(F)∖(H(A_F)∩G(A_F)¹))χ(h)φ(h)dh, with quotient Haar measure, when absolutely convergent.

title: Distinguished automorphic representation
description: Let G be a reductive group over a number field F, H an F-subgroup and χ a unitary character of H(A_F) trivial on H(F). A cuspidal automorphic representation π of G is (H,χ)-distinguished if the automorphic period integral of χ·φ over H(F)∖(H(A_F)∩G(A_F)¹) is nonzero for some smooth cusp form φ in the π-isotypic subspace of the cuspidal L²-space. The subgroup and character are part of the specification. The local analogue asks only for a nonzero H(F)-equivariant functional to χ.

title: Twisted relative spectral trace
description: For a cuspidal representation π,the integral of its convolution-kernel K_{π(f)}(x,y) against μ(x,y^{-1}) over the normalized G^σ and G^θ automorphic quotients. For a K-finite test function it is the sum of products of the corresponding period integrals over an orthonormal basis.

title: Lang–Steinberg theorem
description: For a smooth connected affine algebraic group over a finite field with Frobenius F, the map x↦x⁻¹F(x) is surjective over an algebraic closure; equivalently its first Galois cohomology is trivial.

title: Hahn’s simple twisted relative trace formula
description: Let G=Res_{M/F}G₀ for a quadratic or trivial extension of a number field,with commuting involutions σ,τ,θ=στ and connected G^σ. For a factorizable compact test function having local factors supported on relatively τ-elliptic and strongly relatively τ-regular elements and an F-supercuspidal factor,the weighted sum of relevant regular elliptic twisted relative orbital integrals equals the sum of twisted relative spectral traces over the cuspidal automorphic spectrum of G(A_F)¹.

title: Ideal of a commutative ring
description: An additive subgroup I of a commutative ring R such that ri belongs to I for every r in R and i in I.

title: Prime ideal of a commutative ring
description: A proper ideal P of a commutative ring R such that ab in P implies a in P or b in P.

title: Localization of a commutative ring
description: For a multiplicatively closed subset S of a commutative ring R containing 1, S⁻¹R consists of fractions r/s, identifying r/s with r′/s′ when t(rs′−r′s)=0 for some t in S, with the usual fraction operations.

title: Ring of integers of a number field
description: The subring O_K of a number field K consisting of its elements integral over Z, namely the roots in K of monic integer-coefficient polynomials.

title: Congruence subgroup of the integral symplectic group
description: A subgroup Γ of Sp(2g,Z) containing the kernel of reduction Sp(2g,Z)→Sp(2g,Z/NZ) for some positive integer N; its level is the least such N.

title: Siegel modular form for a congruence subgroup
description: A holomorphic function f on the degree-g Siegel upper half-space transforming as f((AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹)=det(CZ+D)^k f(Z) under a congruence subgroup Γ⊂Sp(2g,Z), with holomorphy at all cusps; for g>1 the usual Koecher principle makes the cusp condition automatic.

title: Formal power series over a commutative ring
description: An expression ∑a_α X^α with coefficients in a commutative ring and multi-indices α in N^n, added coefficientwise and multiplied by the finite Cauchy sums defining each coefficient, without any assertion of analytic convergence.

title: Symmetric square of a module
description: For a module M over a commutative ring R, Sym²_R(M) is (M⊗_R M) modulo the relations x⊗y−y⊗x. In small characteristic this differs from the submodule of M⊗M generated by x⊗x; the paper explicitly uses the latter convention in its integral Witt targets.

title: Alternating tensors in the tensor square of a module
description: For an R-module M, the submodule of M⊗_R M consisting of tensors t with flip(t)=−t. This is a submodule convention, not the quotient definition of the exterior square; in characteristic 2 these conventions need not agree.

title: Witt operators for genus-two Siegel modular forms
description: The restriction of a genus-two modular form to block-diagonal matrices and its first two normalized transverse Taylor coefficients: f([[τ₁,z],[z,τ₂]])=W(f)+2W′(f)(2πiz)+W″(f)(2πiz)²+O(z³). Their targets are tensor products of elliptic modular or quasimodular form spaces, with parity determined by the weight.

title: Holomorphic Eisenstein series for SL₂(Z)
description: For even k≥4, the modular form E_k(τ)=½∑_(c,d)=1(cτ+d)^(−k), normalized to constant Fourier coefficient 1. The weight-two series E₂=1−24∑_{n≥1}σ₁(n)q^n is quasimodular rather than modular.

title: Ramanujan delta modular form
description: The normalized weight-12 cusp form Δ=(E₄³−E₆²)/1728=q∏_{n≥1}(1−q^n)^24 for SL₂(Z), where q=exp(2πiτ).

title: Igusa’s generators for genus-two Siegel modular forms
description: The complex graded ring of full-group genus-two scalar Siegel modular forms is generated by E₄,E₆,χ₁₀,χ₁₂,χ₃₅, with χ₃₅² a polynomial in the first four. Over Z its even-weight subring has Igusa’s fourteen integral generators, and every integral odd-weight form is χ₃₅ times an integral even-weight form.

title: Nagaoka’s genus-two modular-form structure modulo 2 and 3
description: For p=2 or 3, every reduction modulo p of an integral even-weight full-group genus-two Siegel modular form is a unique polynomial over F_p in the reductions of Igusa’s X₁₀,Y₁₂,X₁₆, after forgetting the weight grading.

title: Borcherds automorphic product
description: For an even lattice M of signature (2,n) and a weakly holomorphic modular form F of weight 1−n/2 and type ρ_M whose principal-part coefficients c_γ(m), m≤0, are integers, the Borcherds product Ψ_M(F) is the meromorphic automorphic form of weight c₀(0)/2 with a unitary character on the orthogonal symmetric domain of M for which log|Ψ_M| is −Φ_M(F)/4 up to an explicit multiple of log|Y_M|. Its divisor is a sum of rational quadratic divisors λ^⊥ with multiplicities ∑_(x>0)c_(xλ)(x²λ²/2), and near each cusp it has a convergent infinite product expansion.

title: Kikuta–Takemori’s sharp genus-two Sturm bound
description: Let f be a scalar full-group degree-two Siegel modular form of weight k≥0 with coefficients in O_{K,𝔭}. Put b_k=⌊k/10⌋ for even k and ⌊(k−5)/10⌋ for odd k. If the coefficients indexed by T=(m,r/2;r/2,n)≥0 with m,n≤b_k vanish modulo 𝔭^ν, then all coefficients do, for every prime ideal 𝔭 and ν≥1. This bound is optimal whenever the weight-k space is nonzero.

title: Goldbach number
description: A positive integer expressible as the sum of two prime numbers.

title: Infinitely recurring prime difference
description: A positive integer d such that p−q=d for infinitely many pairs of prime numbers p,q; the two primes need not be consecutive. Benatar calls these de Polignac numbers, a convention distinguished here from consecutive prime gaps.

title: Normalized consecutive prime gap
description: For consecutive primes p_n,p_{n+1}, the real number (p_{n+1}−p_n)/log p_n. Its finite limit points are subsequential limits of this sequence.

title: Möbius function
description: The arithmetic function μ(n) equal to 0 if a squared prime divides n and to (−1)^r if n is a product of r distinct primes, including μ(1)=1.

title: Euler totient function
description: The number φ(n) of integers 1≤a≤n coprime to n.

title: Selberg sieve weight
description: A nonnegative arithmetic weight obtained by squaring a divisor sum, typically (∑_{d|P(n)}λ_d)² with coefficients λ_d supported on d≤R, designed to suppress values with small prime factors.

title: Maynard–Tao multidimensional sieve
description: A refinement of Selberg’s sieve using weights (∑_{d_i|n+h_i}λ_{d₁,…,d_k})² for an admissible tuple h₁,…,h_k, with coefficients selected by a function on a simplex. Comparing weighted prime counts with total mass produces several primes in a common translate.

title: Smooth integer
description: A positive integer whose prime factors are all at most a specified bound y; equivalently its largest prime factor P⁺(n) is at most y, with a harmless convention for n=1.

title: Dirichlet character
description: A group character of (Z/qZ)× with complex values, extended periodically to Z by zero on integers not coprime to q. A character is primitive when it is not induced from a proper divisor of q.

title: Dirichlet L-function
description: For a Dirichlet character χ, the Dirichlet series L(s,χ)=∑_{n≥1}χ(n)n^(−s) for Re(s)>1, together with its meromorphic continuation.

title: Level of distribution of the primes
description: An exponent θ for which the average error in the prime number theorem in progressions, summed over moduli q≤x^(θ−ε), is O_A,ε(x/(log x)^A) for every A,ε>0. The precise weighted prime count and allowed modulus family must be stated when using a variant.

title: Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
description: For every A>0 there is B>0 such that ∑_{q≤x^(1/2)/(log x)^B} max_(a,q)=1 |ψ(x;q,a)−x/φ(q)|≪_A x/(log x)^A, where ψ uses the von Mangoldt weight and the sum runs over all positive moduli.

title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
description: The primes have every level of distribution θ<1, in the averaged arithmetic-progression error sense, with arbitrary logarithmic saving.

title: Polymath’s smooth-modulus distribution theorem for primes
description: Put θ=1/2+7/300. Given ε>0 there is δ>0 such that, for every fixed A≥1 and any choice of a nonzero residue a_p modulo each prime p, ∑_{q≤x^(θ−ε), q squarefree and x^δ-smooth}|ψ(x;q,a_q)−x/φ(q)|≪_{A,ε,δ}x/(log x)^A, uniformly in those choices. Here a_q is the coherent Chinese-remainder residue of the a_p for p dividing q, and ψ is the von Mangoldt prime count.

title: Complete bipartite graph
description: The simple graph K_{s,t} with two disjoint vertex sets of sizes s,t, every edge between the two sets and no edges within either set.

title: Subgraph of a simple graph
description: A graph obtained from a simple graph by choosing some vertices and some of the original edges between those vertices; an induced subgraph retains all such edges.

title: Kővári–Sós–Turán theorem
description: For fixed integers s,t≥2, every n-vertex simple graph containing no K_{s,t} subgraph has O_{s,t}(n^(2−1/s)) edges. The paper uses the balanced case s=t.

title: Szemerédi’s theorem
description: Every subset of the positive integers having positive upper asymptotic density contains arbitrarily long finite arithmetic progressions.

title: Smooth bump function on Euclidean space
description: A smooth real-valued function on R^n with compact support, often chosen to be one on a specified compact set and zero outside a prescribed open neighbourhood.

title: Euler–Lagrange equation for first-order variational integrals
description: Let Ω⊂R^n be open, L∈C²(Ω×R×R^n), and u∈C²(Ω). If for every φ∈C_c^∞(Ω) the first variation at t=0 of ∫_{supp φ}[L(x,u+tφ,∇u+t∇φ)−L(x,u,∇u)]dx vanishes, then L_u(x,u,∇u)−∑ᵢ∂ᵢL_{pᵢ}(x,u,∇u)=0 throughout Ω.

title: Benatar’s Goldbach–prime-difference dichotomy
description: Either successive Goldbach numbers have bounded gaps beyond some point, or the set D of infinitely recurring positive prime differences has full relative density among the even integers, with |((2N)∖D)∩[1,N]|≪N^κ for some κ<1. Differences in D need not be consecutive prime gaps.

title: Benatar’s density bounds for normalized prime-gap limit points
description: If L is the set of finite limit points of (p_{n+1}−p_n)/log p_n, then liminf_{T→∞}m(L∩[0,T])/T≥1/4 and m(L∩[0,T])/T≥3/25 for every T>0, where m is Lebesgue measure. Under the specific level-one distribution variant in §5, the first lower bound improves to 1/2.

title: Vague convergence of Radon measures
description: On a locally compact Hausdorff space, μ_n converge vaguely to μ if ∫f dμ_n→∫f dμ for every continuous compactly supported real function f.

title: Locally finite point configuration
description: An integer-valued Radon measure ξ=∑_iδ_{x_i} assigning finite mass to every compact set; repeated points may have multiplicity. Configuration space carries the vague topology.

title: Point process
description: A random locally finite point configuration, or equivalently a probability measure on configuration space with its measurable structure generated by counting points in bounded Borel sets.

title: Correlation functions of a point process
description: Relative to a reference measure dx, the k-point correlation function ρ⁽ᵏ⁾ is the density satisfying E∑_{x₁,…,xₖ distinct in ξ}f(x₁,…,xₖ)=∫fρ⁽ᵏ⁾dx₁⋯dxₖ for nonnegative measurable f, when this density exists. The sum counts distinct particle labels.

title: Poisson point process
description: A point process with intensity measure λ for which counts in disjoint measurable sets are independent and ξ(A) has Poisson law of mean λ(A) whenever λ(A)<∞.

title: Poisson distribution
description: The distribution on nonnegative integers with masses P(N=k)=e⁻ˡλᵏ/k! for λ≥0.

title: Reduced Palm distribution of a point process
description: The disintegration μ_x of the reduced Campbell measure: E∑_{x∈ξ}F(x,ξ−δ_x)=∫E_{μ_x}F(x,η)ρ⁽¹⁾(x)dx. It describes the remaining configuration viewed conditional on a point at x, without conditioning on a usually null event.

title: Determinantal point process
description: A point process whose k-point correlation functions satisfy ρ⁽ᵏ⁾(x₁,…,xₖ)=det(K(x_i,x_j))_{i,j=1}ᵏ for a specified kernel K and reference measure.

title: Quasi-Gibbs measure for a point process
description: For specified one-body and pair potentials Φ,Ψ, a point-process law is quasi-Gibbs if its restriction to configurations with m particles in each bounded region can be approximated increasingly by submeasures whose conditional inside laws, given the outside configuration, are bounded above and below by positive multiples of exp(−H_inside) times Poisson reference measure restricted to m particles. Constants may depend on the region, particle number, approximation level and outside configuration.

title: Closed nonnegative symmetric form on a Hilbert space
description: A nonnegative symmetric bilinear form E on a dense vector subspace D of a real Hilbert space H is closed if D is complete for the norm ‖u‖_{E,1}=(‖u‖_H²+E(u,u))¹ᐟ².

title: Closable nonnegative symmetric form
description: A densely defined nonnegative symmetric form E is closable if u_n→0 in H and E(u_n−u_m,u_n−u_m)→0 imply E(u_n,u_n)→0. Equivalently it has a closed extension obtained by completing its graph norm.

title: Symmetric Dirichlet form
description: A closed densely defined nonnegative symmetric form E on real L²(X,m) satisfying the Markov contraction property: for u∈D(E), v=(0∨u)∧1 belongs to D(E) and E(v,v)≤E(u,u).

title: Nest for a Dirichlet form
description: An increasing sequence of closed sets F_n such that the union of {u∈D(E):u=0 m-a.e. outside F_n} is dense in D(E) for the E₁ norm. A set is E-exceptional if it is contained in the complement of the union of some nest.
