title: Quasi-continuity relative to a Dirichlet form
description: A real function has an E-quasi-continuous version if it agrees m-a.e. with a function whose restriction to every member of some E-nest is continuous.

title: Quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form
description: A symmetric Dirichlet form on L²(X,m) is quasi-regular if it has a nest of compact sets, an E₁-dense subset of its domain with quasi-continuous versions, and countably many domain elements with quasi-continuous versions separating all points outside an exceptional set.

title: Markov transition semigroup
description: A family of transition kernels P_t(x,A), t≥0, with P₀(x,·)=δ_x and P_{s+t}(x,A)=∫P_t(y,A)P_s(x,dy). Sub-Markov semigroups may lose mass at a cemetery state.

title: Symmetric Markov semigroup
description: A Markov transition semigroup is symmetric with respect to m if ∫fP_tg dm=∫gP_tf dm for suitable f,g. Its stationary process has time-reversal invariant finite-dimensional distributions when initialized from a probability measure m.

title: Strong Markov process
description: A Markov process whose conditional future after any finite stopping time, given the past through that time, has the transition law started from its state at that stopping time.

title: Càdlàg path
description: A path from a real time interval into a metric space that is right-continuous and has a left limit at every positive time.

title: Special standard Markov process
description: A right-continuous strong Markov process on a Lusin state space, with cemetery state, that is quasi-left-continuous: along stopping times T_n↑T, X_{T_n}→X_T on the event T is before the lifetime.

title: Process existence for quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet forms
description: A quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on a Lusin measurable state space is associated with an m-tight special standard process, unique up to the usual exceptional-set equivalence, whose L² semigroup is the semigroup of the form. The resulting process is m-symmetric; conservativeness requires an additional condition.

title: Densely defined self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space
description: A linear operator A with dense domain D(A) in a Hilbert space such that its Hilbert-space adjoint A* has the same domain and agrees with A. The adjoint domain consists of y for which x↦⟨Ax,y⟩ is bounded on D(A) in the ambient Hilbert norm.

title: Closed symmetric form–semigroup correspondence
description: Densely defined closed nonnegative symmetric forms on a Hilbert space correspond to nonnegative self-adjoint operators and strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroups T_t=exp(−tA), with E(u,v)=⟨A¹ᐟ²u,A¹ᐟ²v⟩ on D(A¹ᐟ²).

title: Lévy process
description: A càdlàg stochastic process starting at zero with stationary independent increments and continuity in probability, taking values in Euclidean space.

title: Isotropic symmetric α-stable Lévy process
description: For 0<α≤2, the Euclidean Lévy process whose characteristic function is Eexp(iξ·X_t)=exp(−t|ξ|ᵅ), up to a specified positive time-scaling constant.

title: Upper semicontinuous function
description: An extended-real-valued function f on a topological space is upper semicontinuous if {x:f(x)<a} is open for every real a.

title: Mollifier on Euclidean space
description: A nonnegative smooth compactly supported function j on ℝᵈ with integral one. Its scaled kernels j_ε(x)=ε⁻ᵈj(x/ε) produce smooth approximations by convolution.

title: Mean value theorem for real functions
description: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), there exists c∈(a,b) such that f(b)−f(a)=f′(c)(b−a).

title: Rolle’s theorem
description: If f is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and f(a)=f(b), then f′(c)=0 for some c∈(a,b).

title: Extreme value theorem on a compact real interval
description: A continuous real function on [a,b] attains both a maximum and a minimum.

title: Determinant of a square matrix
description: For an n×n matrix A over a commutative ring, det A=∑_{σ∈Sₙ}sgn(σ)∏_{i=1}ⁿA_{i,σ(i)}, with the 0×0 determinant equal to one.

title: Symmetric group of a finite set
description: The group of all bijections of a finite set to itself under composition.

title: Sign of a permutation
description: The sign of a permutation of {1,…,n} is (−1) to the number of inversions, where an inversion is a pair i<j with σ(i)>σ(j).

title: Esaki’s quasi-regularity theorem for infinite-particle jump forms
description: For a configuration law μ with locally Lᵖ finite-region particle densities (p>1), consider the closable jump form E(f,g)=½∫μ(dξ)∫ξ(dx)∫dy ν(ξ,x;y)[f(ξ−δ_x+δ_y)−f(ξ)][g(ξ−δ_x+δ_y)−g(ξ)] on local smooth functions. If ν≤Cp(|x−y|), ρ⁽¹⁾(x)=O(|x|ᵏ), p(r)=O(r⁻ᵈ⁻ᵅ) at infinity with α>κ, p(r)=O(r⁻ᵈ⁻ᵝ) near zero with 0<β<2, and Var ξ(B_r)/(Eξ(B_r))²=O(r⁻ᵟ) for some δ>0, its closure is a quasi-regular Dirichlet form.

title: Esaki’s quasi-Gibbs jump-form closability theorem
description: For the infinite-particle jump form on local smooth functions, suppose μ is (Φ,Ψ)-quasi-Gibbs and Φ,Ψ are bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of upper semicontinuous comparison potentials Φ₀,Ψ₀, locally bounded below, with Ψ₀ even and its infinite-value set compact. Under the standing symmetric jump-kernel integrability assumptions ∫(1∧|x−y|²)ν(ξ,x;y)dy<∞, the form is closable on L²(μ).

title: Normal distribution
description: The real probability distribution N(m,σ²) with density (2πσ²)⁻¹ᐟ²exp(−(x−m)²/(2σ²)) for σ>0; variance zero gives a point mass at m.

title: Standard Brownian motion
description: A continuous process B_t starting at zero with independent increments and B_t−B_s distributed N(0,t−s) for 0≤s<t. A d-dimensional standard Brownian motion has d independent standard components.

title: Wiener measure
description: The probability law of standard Brownian motion on continuous paths starting at zero, equipped with the Borel σ-algebra for uniform convergence on compact time intervals.

title: Itô integral with respect to Brownian motion
description: For an adapted process H with E∫₀ᵀ|H_s|²ds<∞, ∫H_s dB_s is the L² limit of left-endpoint adapted step-process sums. Localization extends the definition to locally square-integrable integrands.

title: Itô stochastic differential equation driven by Brownian motion
description: An adapted continuous process X solves dX_t=b(X_t)dt+σ(X_t)dB_t if it satisfies X_t=X₀+∫₀ᵗb(X_s)ds+∫₀ᵗσ(X_s)dB_s almost surely.

title: Convergence in probability
description: Random variables X_n converge in probability to X if P(|X_n−X|>ε)→0 for every ε>0; metric-valued variables use their metric in place of absolute difference.

title: Quadratic covariation of continuous semimartingales
description: For continuous semimartingales X,Y, [X,Y]_t is the limit in probability of sums ∑(X_{t_{i+1}}−X_{t_i})(Y_{t_{i+1}}−Y_{t_i}) as the partition mesh tends to zero.

title: Stratonovich integral for continuous semimartingales
description: For continuous semimartingales X,Y, ∫Y∘dX=∫YdX+½[Y,X], when the Itô integral exists. Equivalently it is obtained from symmetric stochastic Riemann sums.

title: Itô’s formula for Brownian diffusions
description: If X solves dX=b dt+σ dB and f is C¹ in time and C² in space, then df(t,X_t)=(∂_tf+b·∇f+½tr(σσᵀD²f))dt+∇f·σdB, with the usual localization hypotheses.

title: Smooth vector field on Euclidean space
description: A smooth map V:ℝⁿ→ℝⁿ, acting on smooth scalar functions by Vf=∑_iVⁱ∂_if.

title: Lie bracket of smooth vector fields
description: The vector field [V,W] characterized by [V,W]f=V(Wf)−W(Vf); in coordinates [V,W]ⁱ=∑_j(Vʲ∂_jWⁱ−Wʲ∂_jVⁱ).

title: Uniformly finitely generated condition for diffusion vector fields
description: For bounded smooth diffusion fields V₀,…,V_d, the C_b^∞ module generated by all iterated brackets except the drift field alone is generated by brackets of uniformly bounded weighted length (a drift letter has weight two, a noise letter weight one). Each longer bracket is a linear combination of these finitely many fields with bounded smooth coefficient functions.

title: Cameron–Martin space for Wiener measure
description: The Hilbert space of absolutely continuous paths h:[0,T]→ℝᵈ with h(0)=0 and square-integrable derivative, with inner product ∫₀ᵀh′(s)·k′(s)ds.

title: Malliavin derivative on Wiener space
description: For a smooth cylindrical Wiener functional F=f(B(h₁),…,B(h_n)), DF=∑_i∂_if(B(h₁),…,B(h_n))h_i in the Cameron–Martin space; its closure defines the Malliavin derivative on the corresponding Sobolev domains.

title: Closed linear operator
description: A linear map A:D(A)⊆X→Y between Banach spaces is closed if x_n→x and Ax_n→y with x_n∈D(A) imply x∈D(A) and Ax=y.

title: Skorokhod divergence on Wiener space
description: The adjoint δ of the Malliavin derivative on L² Wiener space: u belongs to D(δ) when E⟨DF,u⟩=E[Fδ(u)] for all smooth cylindrical F, for some square-integrable δ(u). It extends the adapted Itô integral.

title: Malliavin covariance matrix
description: For a random vector F=(F¹,…,Fⁿ) with Malliavin differentiable components, its covariance matrix is γ_F^{ij}=⟨DFⁱ,DFʲ⟩ in the Cameron–Martin space.

title: Monte Carlo estimator of an expectation
description: Estimate EF by the empirical mean L⁻¹∑_{ℓ=1}ᴸF(X_ℓ) of independent identically distributed samples. Variants may use dependent samples with a separately justified sampling law.

title: Stochastic mesh method for conditional expectations
description: Approximate a Markov transition expectation by weighted values at simulated future states. With transition density p(s,x;t,y) and L simulated paths, a common weight at Y_j=X_j(t) is p(s,x;t,Y_j)/(Lq(Y_j)), where q(y)=L⁻¹∑_ℓp(s,X_ℓ(s);t,y); this reuses one random mesh for many starting states.

title: Risk-neutral valuation of contingent claims
description: Under a specified probability measure making discounted traded asset prices martingales, the arbitrage-free price of a replicable claim is the conditional expectation of its discounted payoff, subject to the market model and integrability hypotheses.

title: Default intensity process
description: For a default time τ, a nonnegative predictable process λ_t such that 1_{τ≤t}−∫₀^{t∧τ}λ_sds is a local martingale in the specified information filtration. Cox-model conditional survival is exp(−∫₀ᵗλ_sds).

title: Unilateral credit valuation adjustment
description: In a model where the valuing institution cannot default, CVA is the expected discounted loss on positive counterparty exposure at counterparty default: E[D(0,τ)L_τ(V_τ)⁺1_{τ<T}], under a specified pricing measure. Here V is the default-free portfolio value and L is the fractional loss at default.

title: Morimoto’s stochastic-mesh CVA estimators
description: For a portfolio whose payoffs each depend only on a shared macro factor and one local factor, approximate each future conditional payoff with a low-dimensional stochastic mesh and time-discretize expected positive aggregate exposure. One estimator uses the approximate exposure itself; another uses the mesh only to classify its sign and averages realized discounted payoffs from independent paths on the estimated positive-exposure region.

title: Real orthogonal matrix
description: A real square matrix U with UᵀU=I, equivalently a linear map preserving the Euclidean inner product.

title: Multivariate normal distribution
description: A distribution of a real vector X for which every real linear combination of coordinates is normally distributed; it is specified by its mean vector and positive semidefinite covariance matrix.

title: Change of variables theorem for Euclidean integrals
description: For a C¹ diffeomorphism Φ:U→V between open subsets of ℝⁿ and a nonnegative measurable or integrable f on V, ∫_Vf(y)dy=∫_Uf(Φ(x))|det DΦ(x)|dx.

title: Orthogonal invariance of the standard Gaussian distribution
description: If X has n independent N(0,1) coordinates and U is a real orthogonal n×n matrix, then UX has the same distribution as X.

title: Householder reflection
description: For a nonzero real vector v, the orthogonal reflection H=I−2vvᵀ/(vᵀv) fixes the hyperplane perpendicular to v and negates v. Applying H to a vector uses O(n) arithmetic operations.

title: Principal component analysis of a random vector
description: For a square-integrable real vector, choose orthonormal eigenvectors of its covariance matrix in decreasing eigenvalue order. Projection onto the first k such vectors captures the largest possible sum of coordinate variances among k-dimensional orthogonal projections.

title: Brownian bridge on a finite interval
description: The centered Gaussian process β_t=B_t−(t/T)B_T,0≤t≤T, with endpoints zero and covariance min(s,t)−st/T. A bridge from x to y adds x+(t/T)(y−x).

title: Brownian-bridge sampling of discrete Brownian paths
description: Generate a Brownian path on a finite grid by first sampling its endpoint, then recursively sampling an interior value conditional on already generated bracketing values using its Gaussian bridge law.

title: ANOVA decomposition on a product probability space
description: For square-integrable f(X₁,…,X_n) with independent inputs, define f_∅=Ef and f_u=E[f|X_u]−∑_{v⊊u}f_v. Then f=∑_uf_u; nonconstant components have zero conditional mean after integrating any one of their active coordinates, and distinct components are orthogonal in L².

title: Effective dimension in the truncation sense
description: For a nonconstant square-integrable function of n independent inputs and tolerance ε∈(0,1), the smallest k for which ANOVA components involving only the first k coordinates account for at least 1−ε of its variance.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo integration
description: Approximate an integral on [0,1]ˢ by the average of the integrand over a deterministic point set chosen for uniform coverage, typically of low discrepancy; other input laws can be sampled by a transformation of these points.

title: Star discrepancy of a finite point set
description: For points x₁,…,x_N in [0,1]ˢ, D* is sup_{a∈[0,1]ˢ}|N⁻¹∑_i1_{x_i∈[0,a)}−∏_ja_j|.

title: Randomly shifted quasi-Monte Carlo rule
description: Add one uniform random vector in [0,1]ˢ to every point of a deterministic quadrature set, reducing coordinates modulo one. Independent shifts give independent randomized estimates; digital shifts use digitwise addition in a fixed base instead.

title: Population least-squares linear regression
description: For a square-integrable response Y and real predictors X, choose coefficients a,b minimizing E(Y−aᵀX−b)². With independent standard normal predictors, b=EY and a_j=E(YX_j).

title: Geometric Brownian motion
description: The process S_t=S₀exp((μ−σ²/2)t+σB_t), equivalently the solution of dS_t=μS_tdt+σS_tdB_t for S₀>0.

title: Black–Scholes market model
description: A market with a bank account growing at constant rate r and a stock following geometric Brownian motion with constant volatility σ. Under its pricing measure the stock drift is r.

title: Discretely monitored arithmetic Asian option
description: A contingent claim whose payoff depends on an arithmetic average of asset prices at a specified finite set of monitoring times, for example (n⁻¹∑_kS_{t_k}−K)⁺.

title: Up-and-in barrier option
description: A contingent claim activated only if the asset price reaches a specified upper barrier during the monitoring period; discrete and continuous monitoring are distinct contracts. A digital version pays a fixed amount upon activation.

title: Reflection principle for Brownian motion
description: For standard Brownian motion, a≥0 and measurable A⊆(−∞,a), P(max_{s≤t}B_s≥a,B_t∈A)=P(B_t∈2a−A). Reflection of the path after first hitting a preserves Wiener measure.

title: Girsanov change of measure for constant Brownian drift
description: On Brownian paths up to T, changing measure by exp(−νB_T−ν²T/2) makes B_t+νt standard Brownian motion for 0≤t≤T.

title: Regression-based Householder transform for Gaussian quadrature
description: For square-integrable f under standard normal input X, compute a=E[Xf(X)] and reflect e₁ onto a/‖a‖, using identity if a=0 or the directions already agree. Then the fitted linear part of f(UX) is ‖a‖X₁, capturing variance ‖a‖². For f=g∘h the direction may instead use E[Xh(X)]; sequential residual-coordinate reflections accommodate several intermediate functions. Applying k reflections costs O(nk), excluding direction computation.

title: Householder completion preserving leading orthogonal columns
description: Given the first k orthonormal columns of an n×n orthogonal transform, successive Householder transformations on trailing coordinates yield an orthogonal matrix with exactly these columns. Applying its k factors costs O(nk), while the ANOVA variance attributed to the first k transformed Gaussian coordinates agrees with that of any orthogonal completion of those columns.

title: Measure-preserving measurable flow
description: A jointly measurable family θ_t of probability-preserving maps, indexed by real t, with θ₀=id and θ_{s+t}=θ_s∘θ_t.

title: Continuous random dynamical system
description: Over a measure-preserving flow θ, a measurable cocycle φ_t(ω,x) on a Polish state space, continuous in x, with φ₀(ω,x)=x and φ_{t+s}(ω,x)=φ_t(θ_sω,φ_s(ω,x)).

title: Closed partial order on a topological space
description: A partial order whose graph {(x,y):x≤y} is closed in the product topology. For metric spaces this is equivalent to preservation of the relation under limits of convergent pairs.

title: Order interval in a partially ordered set
description: For f≤g, the order interval [f,g] consists of all x satisfying f≤x≤g.

title: Order-preserving random dynamical system
description: A random dynamical system on a partially ordered state space such that x≤y implies φ_t(ω,x)≤φ_t(ω,y) for all t≥0 and every noise realization.

title: Convergence of one-point laws for a random dynamical system
description: A random dynamical system has limiting one-point law μ from every initial state if Law(φ_t(·,x)) converges weakly to μ as t→∞ for every x. This is the paper’s “strongly mixing RDS” condition, distinct from mixing of the noise flow.

title: White-noise random dynamical system
description: A filtered random dynamical system whose noise σ-algebras generated by cocycle increments on disjoint time intervals are independent, and transform with the time shifts of the base flow.

title: Random closed set in a Polish space
description: A nonempty closed-set-valued map A(ω) for which ω↦d(x,A(ω)) is measurable for every fixed x. It is a random compact set if its values are compact almost surely.

title: Invariant random probability measure for a random dynamical system
description: A probability kernel ω↦π_ω on the state space satisfying (φ_t(ω,·))_*π_ω=π_{θ_tω} almost surely for each t. Equivalently P(dω)π_ω(dx) is invariant under the skew-product evolution.

title: Weak point attractor for a random dynamical system
description: An invariant random compact set A such that for every fixed x, d(φ_t(θ_{−t}ω,x),A(ω))→0 in probability. Attraction of every deterministic compact set uniformly is a stronger condition.

title: Weak synchronization by noise
description: Existence of a weak point attractor consisting almost surely of one random point. Its invariance is φ_t(ω,a(ω))=a(θ_tω), and every deterministic initial state converges to it in pullback probability.

title: Tight family of probability measures
description: A family of probability measures on a topological space is tight if for every ε>0 some compact K has μ(K)≥1−ε for every member μ of the family.

title: Prokhorov’s theorem on Polish spaces
description: A family of probability measures on a Polish space is relatively compact for weak convergence if and only if it is tight; in particular every tight sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.

title: Portmanteau theorem for probability measures
description: For probability measures on a metric space, weak convergence μ_n⇒μ is equivalent to limsup μ_n(F)≤μ(F) for every closed F, and equivalently to liminf μ_n(G)≥μ(G) for every open G.

title: Integral Grönwall inequality
description: If u is nonnegative and continuous on [0,T], a≥0, b≥0 is integrable, and u(t)≤a+∫₀ᵗb(s)u(s)ds for every t, then u(t)≤a exp(∫₀ᵗb(s)ds) for every t∈[0,T].

title: Continuous dual of a normed vector space
description: The vector space X* of bounded linear maps X→its scalar field, with norm ‖ℓ‖=sup_{‖x‖≤1}|ℓ(x)|.

title: Sobolev space H₀¹ of a Euclidean domain
description: The closure of smooth compactly supported functions in the W¹,² norm. Its elements have zero boundary trace in the usual regular-domain setting.

title: Sobolev space H⁻¹ of a Euclidean domain
description: The continuous dual of H₀¹, with the Hilbert-space dual norm. A locally integrable function defines an element by pairing against test functions whenever that pairing extends continuously.

title: Weak Dirichlet Laplacian from H₀¹ to H⁻¹
description: The operator −Δ:H₀¹→H⁻¹ defined by ⟨−Δu,v⟩=∫∇u·∇v. On a bounded domain it is an isomorphism when H₀¹ carries its gradient norm; its inverse solves the weak zero-boundary Poisson equation.

title: Hilbert-valued Q-Wiener process
description: A continuous Hilbert-space-valued process with independent Gaussian increments, mean zero and covariance (t−s)Q, where Q is nonnegative self-adjoint and trace class. An eigenbasis expansion is ∑_k√q_kβ_k(t)e_k with ∑_kq_k<∞.

title: Stochastic porous medium equation with additive noise
description: The evolution dX_t=[Δ(|X_t|^{m−1}X_t)+cX_t]dt+dW_t, m>1, on a specified domain with specified boundary conditions, interpreted variationally in a negative Sobolev state space when driven by Hilbert-valued additive Wiener noise.

title: Fractional Brownian motion
description: A centered continuous Gaussian process Bᴴ_t with covariance ½(|t|²ᴴ+|s|²ᴴ−|t−s|²ᴴ), H∈(0,1), normalized to start at zero. It has stationary increments, generally dependent unless H=½.

title: Subdifferential of a convex function on Euclidean space
description: For a proper lower semicontinuous convex f:ℝᵈ→ℝ∪{∞}, ∂f(x)={v:f(y)≥f(x)+v·(y−x) for every y}; it may contain multiple vectors or be empty.

title: Normally reflected diffusion in a convex domain
description: A continuous process in a closed convex domain solving an SDE plus an inward normal finite-variation correction supported on boundary times, keeping the process inside the domain.

title: Asymptotic coalescence of ordered couplings with the same limiting marginal law
description: On a Polish space with closed partial order, if X_t≤Y_t and both marginal laws converge weakly to the same probability measure μ, then d(X_t,Y_t)→0 in probability.

title: Flandoli–Gess–Scheutzow synchronization criterion for ordered random systems
description: Let a continuous order-preserving random dynamical system on a Polish space have closed partial order and one-point laws converging to μ from every initial state. If for every ε>0 there are f≤g with μ([f,g])≥1−ε, then there is a past-measurable invariant random point attracting every deterministic initial point in pullback probability. No normality, admissibility or white-noise assumption is required.

title: Flandoli–Gess–Scheutzow weak synchronization for stochastic porous media
description: On a bounded smooth domain in ℝᵈ with d≤4, the zero-Dirichlet stochastic porous medium equation dX=[Δ(|X|^{m−1}X)+X]dt+dW, m>1, with trace-class additive Wiener noise has a singleton weak point attractor whenever its associated random dynamical system has one-point laws converging to one limiting law from every H⁻¹ initial state. The point also attracts deterministic sets contained in order intervals for the usual positive-distribution order.

title: Equivalence relation
description: A reflexive, symmetric and transitive binary relation.

title: Equivalence class
description: For an equivalence relation ~ on X, [x]={y∈X:y~x}; the quotient set X/~ consists of these classes.

title: Closure of a subset of a topological space
description: The closure of A is the intersection of all closed subsets containing A; a set is closed when its complement is open.

title: Interior of a subset of a topological space
description: The interior of A is the union of all open subsets contained in A.

title: Boundary of a subset of a topological space
description: The boundary of A is its closure with its interior removed.

title: Dense subset of a topological space
description: A subset is dense if its closure is the whole space.

title: Connected topological space
description: A topological space that is not the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets.

title: Connected component of a topological space
description: A maximal connected subset, with connectedness understood in the subspace topology.

title: Completion of a metric space
description: A complete metric space containing an isometric dense copy of the given metric space. It is unique up to an isometry fixing that copy.

title: Seminorm on a real or complex vector space
description: A nonnegative function p with p(ax)=|a|p(x) and p(x+y)≤p(x)+p(y); p may vanish on nonzero vectors.

title: Topology generated by a family of seminorms
description: For seminorms (p_i) on a vector space, a neighborhood base at zero consists of finite intersections of sets {x:p_i(x)<ε}; neighborhoods at other points are translates.

title: Topological vector space over ℝ or ℂ
description: A real or complex vector space with a topology for which vector addition and scalar multiplication are continuous.

title: Locally convex topological vector space
description: A real or complex topological vector space whose zero has a neighborhood base of convex sets; equivalently its topology can be generated by seminorms.

title: Limit of a real function at a point
description: The relation lim_{x→a}f(x)=L means that for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that 0<|x−a|<δ in the domain implies |f(x)−L|<ε.

title: Partial derivative in Euclidean coordinates
description: The ith partial derivative of f at x is the derivative at zero of t↦f(x+t e_i), with all other coordinates fixed; vector-valued maps are differentiated componentwise.

title: Support of a function
description: The closure in its domain of the set on which a function is nonzero.

title: Compactly supported smooth test function on an open Euclidean set
description: A smooth function on an open Ω⊂ℝⁿ whose support is a compact subset of Ω; these form C_c^∞(Ω).

title: Borel σ-algebra of a topological space
description: The σ-algebra generated by the open subsets of the space.

title: Essential supremum of a measurable real function
description: The infimum of real a for which f≤a almost everywhere, allowing infinite values when no finite bound exists.

title: Norming family of linear functionals
description: A family F of linear functionals on a normed space X is norming when ∥x∥=sup{|f(x)|:f∈F} for every x∈X.

title: Finitely supported scalar sequence
description: A scalar sequence with only finitely many nonzero terms; these sequences form the vector space c₀₀.

title: Locally finite triangulation of a Euclidean set
description: A family of Euclidean simplices covering the set, closed under taking faces and meeting in common faces, such that every point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many simplices.

title: Formal L² adjoint of a differential operator on a surface
description: For a differential operator D between Euclidean vector-valued functions on a smooth surface, its formal adjoint D* is specified by ∫⟨Du,v⟩=∫⟨u,D*v⟩ for smooth compactly supported test fields, using the induced surface measure. This identity does not assert a bounded operator on L².

title: Homomorphism of commutative rings
description: A map between commutative rings preserving addition, multiplication and the multiplicative identity.

title: Quotient of a commutative ring by an ideal
description: For an ideal I of R, the cosets R/I form a ring under (r+I)+(s+I)=r+s+I and (r+I)(s+I)=rs+I.

title: Module over a commutative ring
description: An abelian group M with an action of a commutative ring R satisfying r(m+n)=rm+rn, (r+s)m=rm+sm, (rs)m=r(sm), and 1m=m. Unlike a vector space, its scalar ring need not be a field.

title: Homomorphism of modules over a commutative ring
description: An additive map f:M→N of modules over the same commutative ring satisfying f(rm)=rf(m).

title: Submodule of a module over a commutative ring
description: An additive subgroup of a module stable under multiplication by every scalar of its coefficient ring.

title: Quotient module
description: For a submodule N of an R-module M, the cosets M/N carry addition and scalar multiplication induced from M.

title: Tensor product of modules over a commutative ring
description: For R-modules M,N, the R-module M⊗_R N with a bilinear map (m,n)↦m⊗n through which every R-bilinear map M×N→P factors uniquely by an R-linear map.

title: Commutative algebra over a commutative ring
description: A commutative ring A with a specified unital ring homomorphism R→A; algebra homomorphisms commute with these structure maps.

title: Commutative algebra over a field
description: A unital associative algebra over a field whose multiplication is commutative, equivalently a commutative ring equipped with a unital homomorphism from that field.

title: Homomorphism of algebras over a field
description: A linear map of unital associative algebras over the same field preserving multiplication and the multiplicative identity.

title: Polynomial ring over a commutative ring
description: The ring R[X₁,…,X_n] of formal finite sums of monomials with coefficients in R, with coefficientwise addition and the usual multiplication of monomials.

title: Finitely generated commutative algebra
description: An R-algebra A generated as an algebra by finitely many elements; equivalently a quotient of R[X₁,…,X_n] for some finite n.

title: Nilpotent ideal of a commutative ring
description: An ideal I for which I^n=0 for some positive integer n, meaning every product of n elements of I is zero.

title: Finitely presented commutative algebra
description: An R-algebra isomorphic to R[X₁,…,X_n]/(f₁,…,f_m) for finite n,m.

title: Smooth finitely presented commutative algebra
description: A finitely presented R-algebra A such that, for every R-algebra B with nilpotent ideal I, every R-algebra map A→B/I lifts to A→B. This is the infinitesimal lifting formulation of smoothness for affine finite-presentation algebras.

title: Commutative Hopf algebra over a field
description: A Hopf algebra over a field whose underlying algebra multiplication is commutative; its coproduct need not be cocommutative.

title: Hopf ideal of a commutative Hopf algebra
description: An ideal I of a commutative Hopf algebra H satisfying Δ(I)⊂I⊗H+H⊗I, ε(I)=0 and S(I)⊂I, so the quotient inherits the Hopf operations.

title: Algebraically closed field
description: A field in which every nonconstant polynomial has a root.

title: Algebraic closure of a field
description: An algebraic extension of a field that is itself algebraically closed. This specifies an object, without including the existence or uniqueness-up-to-isomorphism theorem.

title: Minimal polynomial of an algebraic element
description: The unique monic polynomial of least positive degree over F vanishing at an algebraic element α; it generates the ideal of all polynomials over F vanishing at α.

title: Separable polynomial over a field
description: A polynomial having no repeated root in an algebraic closure of its coefficient field.

title: Finite field
description: A field whose underlying set is finite.

title: Frobenius endomorphism in characteristic p
description: The field endomorphism x↦x^p of a field of characteristic p; over F_q the q-power iterate x↦x^q is the corresponding q-Frobenius.

title: p-adic valuation of a rational number
description: For a prime p and nonzero rational x, v_p(x) is the unique integer r such that x=p^r a/b with integers a,b not divisible by p; put v_p(0)=+∞.

title: Absolute value on a field
description: A map |·|:K→R_{≥0} that vanishes exactly at zero, is multiplicative and satisfies |x+y|≤|x|+|y|. It is nonarchimedean if the stronger bound |x+y|≤max(|x|,|y|) holds.

title: Discrete valuation on a field
description: A surjective map v:K×→Z satisfying v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) and v(x+y)≥min(v(x),v(y)), extended by v(0)=+∞.

title: Valuation ring of a discretely valued field
description: For a discrete valuation v on K, the ring O_v={x:v(x)≥0}; its maximal ideal is m_v={x:v(x)>0}.

title: Residue field of a discretely valued field
description: The quotient O_v/m_v of the valuation ring by its maximal ideal.

title: Ramification index of a finite extension of discretely valued fields
description: For L/K with compatible normalized discrete valuations v_L,v_K, the positive integer e satisfying v_L(x)=e v_K(x) for every x in K×; equivalently [v_L(L×):v_L(K×)]=e.

title: Matching in a graph
description: A set of edges no two of which share a vertex. Unmatched vertices are called monomers in a monomer–dimer interpretation.

title: Monomer–dimer model on a finite graph
description: A probability distribution on graph matchings in which unmatched vertices are monomers and matched edges dimers, with specified nonnegative vertex and edge activities multiplying to give each matching’s unnormalized weight. The matching constraint is the hard-core exclusion.

title: Imitative monomer–dimer model on the complete graph
description: On matchings D of K_N, let S(D)=N−2|D| be the monomer count. With external field h∈ℝ and coupling J≥0, assign D probability proportional to N^{−|D|}exp((h−J)S(D)+JS(D)²/N). This is the complete-graph monomer–dimer model with attractive imitative interaction.

title: Moment generating function
description: For a real random variable X, M_X(t)=Eexp(tX) at real t for which the expectation is finite.

title: Characteristic function of a real probability distribution
description: For a real random variable X, φ_X(t)=Eexp(itX), t∈ℝ. It is always defined and determines the law of X.

title: Convolution of probability distributions on Euclidean space
description: The convolution μ*ν is the law of X+Y for independent random vectors with laws μ,ν; equivalently (μ*ν)(A)=∫∫1_A(x+y)μ(dx)ν(dy).

title: Lévy continuity theorem
description: If characteristic functions φ_n converge pointwise to a function φ continuous at zero, then φ is a characteristic function and the corresponding probability distributions converge weakly to its law. Conversely weak convergence implies pointwise characteristic-function convergence.

title: Moment-generating-function convergence theorem
description: If moment generating functions are finite on a common neighborhood of zero and converge there pointwise to the moment generating function of a probability distribution, the corresponding distributions converge weakly to that distribution.

title: Even moments of a centered Gaussian
description: For Z∼N(0,σ²), E[Z^{2k}]=(2k−1)!!σ^{2k} and odd moments vanish, with (−1)!!=1. The double factorial counts pairings of 2k labeled elements.

title: Integration by parts for real integrals
description: For continuously differentiable u,v on [a,b], ∫_a^buv′=[uv]_a^b−∫_a^bu′v; improper variants follow when boundary terms and integrals converge.

title: Taylor’s theorem with Lagrange remainder
description: If f has n continuous derivatives on an interval and an (n+1)st derivative between a and x, then f(x)=∑_{j=0}ⁿf⁽ʲ⁾(a)(x−a)ʲ/j!+f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)(x−a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! for some ξ between a and x.

title: Laplace’s method at a nondegenerate real maximum
description: If a smooth real f has a unique interior maximum x₀ with f″(x₀)<0 and integrable exponentially negligible tails, then ∫e^{Nf(x)}dx∼e^{Nf(x₀)}√(2π/(−Nf″(x₀))). Continuous prefactors multiply the leading term by their value at x₀.

title: Laplace asymptotics for varying real integrands
description: Let ψ_n be positive on a fixed compact interval K with f_n=logψ_n and f_n,f_n″ converging uniformly there to f,f″. Suppose each f_n attains its maximum at an interior x_n, f has a unique interior maximum x₀ with f″(x₀)<0, the logarithmic supremum of |ψ_n| outside K is uniformly separated below f_n(x_n), and ∫|ψ_n| is uniformly bounded. Then ∫ψ_n(x)ⁿdx∼exp(nf_n(x_n))√(2π/(−nf″(x₀))).

title: Vitali–Porter convergence theorem for holomorphic functions
description: A locally uniformly bounded sequence of holomorphic functions on a connected domain that converges pointwise on a set with an interior accumulation point converges uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function.

title: Cauchy integral formula on a disk
description: If f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of a closed disk with positively oriented boundary circle C, then for z inside the disk, f(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_Cf(ζ)/(ζ−z)dζ. Derivatives follow by differentiating the kernel.

title: Interlacing of real-rooted polynomials
description: The real zeros of degree-n and degree-(n−1) real-rooted polynomials interlace if, when listed with multiplicity, α₁≤β₁≤α₂≤⋯≤β_{n−1}≤α_n.

title: Weierstrass theorem on locally uniform holomorphic limits
description: A locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic, and every order of derivative converges locally uniformly to the corresponding derivative of the limit.

title: Heilmann–Lieb real-rootedness theorem for matching polynomials
description: For a finite graph with nonnegative edge weights, the matching polynomial μ_G(x)=∑_D(−1)^{|D|}(∏_{e∈D}w_e)x^{|V|−2|D|} has only real zeros. Equivalently the monomer-activity partition polynomial with positive dimer activities has its zeros on the imaginary axis.

title: Monomer-density limit and phase coexistence in the imitative monomer–dimer model
description: In the complete-graph imitative monomer–dimer model define g(z)=eᶻ(√(e²ᶻ+4)−eᶻ)/2, p₀(z)=−(1−g(z))/2−½log(1−g(z)), and F(m)=−Jm²+p₀((2m−1)J+h). If F has a unique global maximizer m*, then S_N/N converges in distribution to m*. On the coexistence curve, where its two nondegenerate global maxima are m₁<m₂, the limit is ρ₁δ_{m₁}+ρ₂δ_{m₂}, with ρ_l proportional to [−F″(m_l)(2−m_l)]⁻¹ᐟ².

title: Gaussian and quartic monomer-count fluctuations in the imitative monomer–dimer model
description: For the complete-graph imitative monomer–dimer model with J>0, let F and its unique maximizer m* be as in the density-limit theorem. Away from coexistence and the critical endpoint, (S_N−Nm*)/√N converges to N(0,−1/F″(m*)−1/(2J)). At the critical endpoint, F″=F‴=0,F⁽⁴⁾<0 and (S_N−Nm*)/N³ᐟ⁴ converges to the density proportional to exp(F⁽⁴⁾(m*)x⁴/24). For J=0 the Gaussian limit has mean-density g(h) and variance g′(h).

title: Exponential distribution
description: The nonnegative distribution with survival function P(T>t)=exp(−rt), t≥0, for rate r>0; its mean is 1/r.

title: Probability generating function
description: For a nonnegative integer-valued random variable A, G(s)=E[sᴬ]=∑_{k≥0}P(A=k)sᵏ for 0≤s≤1, with extension where the series converges.

title: Galton–Watson branching process
description: A population process Z_{n+1}=∑_{i=1}^{Z_n}A_{n,i}, where all offspring counts are independent with a common nonnegative-integer distribution and are independent of the past.

title: Markov process killed on leaving a domain
description: Run a Markov process until its first exit time τ_D from a specified domain and then send it to an absorbing cemetery state. Its sub-Markov semigroup is P_tᴰf(x)=E_x[f(X_t)1_{t<τ_D}].

title: Branching diffusion killed at the boundary of a domain
description: Particles move independently as a specified diffusion in D, are killed upon leaving D, and independently branch at rate β into A offspring at their current positions; offspring repeat the same dynamics independently. Start from a specified finite configuration.

title: Uniformly elliptic symmetric divergence-form operator
description: A second-order operator Lf=∑_{i,j}∂_i(a^{ij}(x)∂_jf) with symmetric coefficients for which c|ξ|²≤∑a^{ij}(x)ξ_iξ_j≤C|ξ|² uniformly in x, for fixed0<c≤C<∞; coefficients and boundary conditions determine its realization.

title: Principal Dirichlet eigenpair of a symmetric elliptic operator
description: For a connected bounded domain and a symmetric uniformly elliptic Dirichlet operator −L, the smallest eigenvalue λ₁ and its positive L²-normalized eigenfunction φ solve −Lφ=λ₁φ with zero boundary trace.

title: Doob ground-state transform of a killed semigroup
description: If a positive function h satisfies P_tᴰh=e^{−λt}h, define Q_tf(x)=e^{λt}P_tᴰ(hf)(x)/h(x). This is a Markov semigroup representing the process conditioned by h; for a killed symmetric diffusion and principal eigenfunction h it describes conditioning to stay in the domain.

title: Intrinsic ultracontractivity of a symmetric killed semigroup
description: A symmetric killed semigroup with positive ground state φ is intrinsically ultracontractive if for every t>0 its transition density satisfies p_t(x,y)≤C_tφ(x)φ(y) almost everywhere for a finite C_t. Equivalently its ground-state-transformed semigroup maps L²(φ²dx) boundedly to L∞.

title: Many-to-one lemma for constant-rate branching Markov processes
description: If particles branch independently at rate β with mean offspring m and move by a killed Markov semigroup P_tᴰ, then E_x∑_{u∈N_t}f(X_u(t))=e^{β(m−1)t}P_tᴰf(x) for nonnegative measurable f.

title: Many-to-two second-moment formula for branching Markov processes
description: For rate-β branching with offspring mean m and finite factorial second moment q=E[A(A−1)], set T_tf=e^{β(m−1)t}P_tᴰf. Then E_x[(∑_uf(X_u(t)))(∑_ug(X_u(t)))]=T_t(fg)(x)+βq∫₀ᵗT_s[(T_{t−s}f)(T_{t−s}g)](x)ds for bounded nonnegative f,g.

title: Additive-martingale spine change of measure for a branching diffusion
description: Weight the branching law up to t by M_t/M₀, where M_t=e^{(λ−β(m−1))t}∑_uφ(X_u(t)). Under the weighted law a distinguished lineage moves by the φ-ground-state transform, branches at accelerated rate mβ with size-biased offspring law kP(A=k)/m, and chooses one child uniformly to continue the spine; other children start independent original branching families.

title: Fisher–Kolmogorov–Petrovsky–Piskunov equation
description: A reaction–diffusion equation ∂_tu=DΔu+r u(1−u), with D,r>0, on a specified spatial domain and with specified initial and boundary conditions. It appears in population models and branching Brownian survival probabilities.

title: Dini’s theorem
description: If continuous real functions on a compact space converge pointwise monotonically to a continuous limit, the convergence is uniform.

title: Method of moments for convergence in distribution
description: If probability laws have all moments, each moment converges to the corresponding finite moment of a probability law uniquely determined by its moments, then the laws converge weakly to that law.

title: Moment determinacy from a finite exponential moment
description: A real probability law whose moment generating function is finite in a neighborhood of zero is uniquely determined by its moments. In particular exponential distributions are moment-determinate.

title: Poincaré inequality on H₀¹ of a bounded domain
description: For a bounded domain D⊂ℝᵈ there is C_D<∞ such that ‖u‖_{L²(D)}≤C_D‖∇u‖_{L²(D)} for all u∈H₀¹(D).

title: Parseval’s identity for an orthonormal Hilbert basis
description: For an orthonormal basis (e_k) of a separable Hilbert space, x=∑_k⟨x,e_k⟩e_k in norm and ‖x‖²=∑_k|⟨x,e_k⟩|².

title: Continuous-time martingale
description: An integrable process M_t adapted to a filtration F_t, t≥0, with E[M_t|F_s]=M_s almost surely whenever s≤t. Right-continuity of paths is an additional regularity condition when needed.

title: Nonnegative martingale convergence theorem
description: A nonnegative right-continuous martingale converges almost surely to a finite integrable random variable as t→∞. Its limiting expectation may be strictly smaller than its initial expectation.

title: Sevast’yanov–Watanabe extinction criterion for bounded-domain branching diffusions
description: For a bounded connected sufficiently regular domain D, a symmetric uniformly elliptic killed diffusion with principal Dirichlet eigenvalue λ, and independent rate-β branching of mean m>1, survival forever has positive probability exactly when β(m−1)>λ. At and below criticality extinction is almost sure; the survival probability to t tends to zero uniformly over starting positions. Lipschitz boundary suffices.

title: Critical branching-diffusion survival asymptotic on a C¹ domain
description: On a bounded connected C¹ domain, let −L be symmetric uniformly elliptic with smooth coefficients and positive L²-normalized principal eigenfunction φ, eigenvalue λ. For rate β=λ/(m−1) branching with mean m=EA>1 and finite second moment, P_x(N_t>0)∼2(m−1)φ(x)/[λE(A(A−1))∫_Dφ³·t].

title: Yaglom limit for critical bounded-domain branching diffusions
description: Under the C¹-domain, symmetric elliptic motion and finite-second-moment offspring hypotheses of the critical survival theorem, for measurable E⊆D the conditional law of N_t(E)/t given N_t>0 converges to an exponential law of mean λE[A(A−1)](∫_Eφ)(∫_Dφ³)/(2(m−1)); zero mean denotes the degenerate law at zero. The conditional empirical spatial law converges in probability on each such E to ∫_Eφ/∫_Dφ.

title: Powell’s fixed-window limit under long-survival conditioning
description: For the critical killed branching diffusion on a bounded C¹ domain under the survival-asymptotic hypotheses, for every fixed T and event B measurable through time T, lim_{t→∞}P_x(B|N_t>0)=Q_x(B), where Q_x is the additive-martingale spine law.

title: Group action on a set
description: A map G×X→X, written (g,x)↦gx, satisfying ex=x and (gh)x=g(hx).

title: Product topology
description: On a Cartesian product of topological spaces, the topology with basic open sets restricting finitely many coordinates to open subsets and leaving all other coordinates unrestricted.

title: Subspace topology
description: For A⊆X, the topology whose open sets are A∩U for U open in X.

title: Quotient topology
description: For a surjection q:X→Y, a subset U⊆Y is open exactly when q⁻¹(U) is open in X.

title: Hausdorff topological space
description: A topological space in which any two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods.

title: Locally compact Hausdorff space
description: A Hausdorff topological space in which every point has a neighbourhood with compact closure.

title: Topological group
description: A group with a topology for which multiplication G×G→G and inversion G→G are continuous.

title: Locally compact group
description: A topological group whose underlying space is locally compact and Hausdorff.

title: Topological ring
description: A ring with a topology for which addition, multiplication and additive inversion are continuous; the rings here are commutative with identity.

title: Completion of a field with an absolute value
description: The metric completion of K for d(x,y)=|x−y|, with the field operations extended continuously. A completion is regarded as containing K through its canonical isometric embedding.

title: Complete discretely valued field
description: A field with a discrete valuation v which is complete for the metric defined by any absolute value c^(−v(x)) with c>1, extended by |0|=0.

title: Nonarchimedean local field
description: A field complete for a nontrivial discrete valuation and having a finite residue field.

title: Restricted product of topological groups
description: For groups G_i with chosen open subgroups K_i, the group of tuples g_i with g_i∈K_i for all but finitely many i, with the topology whose basic opens are products of open sets equal to K_i outside finitely many coordinates.

title: Complex derivative
description: For a complex-valued function on an open subset of C, f′(z) is the limit of (f(z+h)−f(z))/h as nonzero complex h→0, when it exists.

title: Holomorphic function of several complex variables
description: A complex function on an open subset of C^n that is locally representable by a convergent power series in the n complex coordinates. Vector-valued holomorphy for a finite-dimensional target means holomorphy of its coordinates in any basis.

title: Cusp of a subgroup of SL₂(Z)
description: An orbit of a subgroup Γ⊂SL₂(Z) on Q∪{∞} under fractional linear transformations; for a congruence subgroup its cusp width is the positive translation period after sending a representative to infinity.

title: Holomorphy of a modular form at a cusp
description: After applying the weight-k slash action by a matrix sending a cusp to infinity, the resulting periodic function has a Fourier expansion in q_h=exp(2πiτ/h) with no negative powers, where h is the cusp width.

title: Complex torus
description: A quotient V/Λ of a finite-dimensional complex vector space V by a discrete subgroup Λ generated over Z by a real basis of V, with the quotient topology and the local complex coordinates induced by translations in V.

title: Convex function on a convex subset of a real vector space
description: A function f:C→R on a convex subset of a real vector space satisfying f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y) for x,y∈C and 0≤t≤1. Unlike the separate interval-convex-function identity, the domain may be infinite-dimensional.

title: Representing measure for a point of a compact convex set
description: A Borel probability measure μ on a compact convex subset K of a locally convex space represents x∈K if ∫_K f dμ=f(x) for every continuous affine real function f on K.

title: Choquet order on probability measures
description: For Borel probability measures on a compact convex set K, write μ≼ν if ∫f dμ≤∫f dν for every continuous convex real function f on K. A maximal measure has no strictly larger measure for this order.

title: Directed ordered abelian group
description: A partially ordered abelian group in which any two elements have a common upper bound; equivalently every element is a difference of two nonnegative elements.

title: General linear group over a commutative ring
description: The group GL_n(R) of square matrices over a commutative ring R having a two-sided matrix inverse, with matrix multiplication.

title: Trace of a square matrix
description: The sum of the diagonal entries of a square matrix.

title: Automorphism of a group
description: A bijective group homomorphism from a group to itself; automorphisms form a group under composition.

title: Semidirect product of groups
description: Given a homomorphism α:G→Aut(H), the group H⋊_αG has underlying set H×G and multiplication (h,g)(h′,g′)=(hα(g)(h′),gg′).

title: Integral Heisenberg group for scalar-index Jacobi forms
description: For λ,μ in Z^g and κ in Z, use the triples (λ,μ,κ) with product (λ+λ′,μ+μ′,κ+κ′+λ·μ′−μ·λ′). The dot products are the finite coordinate sums; this specifies the integral normalization used in the scalar-index Jacobi slash action.

title: Integral Jacobi group
description: The semidirect product of Sp(2g,Z) with the integral Heisenberg group, where the symplectic factor acts on the λ,μ coordinates and fixes the center; its action on H_g×C^g is the one used in Jacobi modular and elliptic transformation laws.

title: Right triangle in Euclidean space
description: A nondegenerate triangle with vertices a,a+u,a+v for nonzero Euclidean vectors u,v satisfying u·v=0, where u·v is the sum of coordinate products. The side from a+u to a+v is the hypotenuse.

title: von Mangoldt function
description: The arithmetic function Λ(n)=log p if n=p^k for a prime p and integer k≥1, and Λ(n)=0 otherwise.

title: Real power of a positive real number
description: For x>0 and p∈ℝ, define xᵖ=exp(p log x). For p>0 extend by 0ᵖ=0.

title: Quasi-normed vector space
description: A real or complex vector space with a positive definite absolutely homogeneous function q satisfying q(x+y)≤C(q(x)+q(y)) for a fixed C≥1.

title: Homogeneous real polynomial
description: A real polynomial in finitely many variables whose nonzero monomials all have the same total degree.

title: Uniform convergence on compact subsets
description: A sequence of functions converges locally uniformly on a topological space if it converges uniformly on every compact subset.

title: Complex power series
description: A series ∑ₙ₌₀∞aₙ(z−z₀)ⁿ with complex coefficients, considered at points where its partial sums converge.

title: Fréchet derivative between normed spaces
description: The Fréchet derivative of f at x is a bounded linear map A with ∥f(x+h)−f(x)−Ah∥/∥h∥→0 as h→0.

title: Complex Banach algebra, possibly nonunital
description: A complex Banach space with associative bilinear multiplication satisfying ∥ab∥≤∥a∥∥b∥. An identity is not required.

title: Unitization of a complex Banach algebra
description: For a nonunital complex Banach algebra A, its unitization is A⊕ℂ with multiplication (a,λ)(b,μ)=(ab+λb+μa,λμ), identity (0,1), and norm ∥a∥+|λ|.

title: Spectrum of an element of a complex Banach algebra
description: For a in a complex Banach algebra A, σ(a) consists of complex λ for which λ1−a has no two-sided inverse, using the unitization if A has no identity.

title: Hausdorff measure of a metric space
description: For s≥0, the s-dimensional Hausdorff measure is the limit as δ↓0 of the infimum of normalized sums of diameters^s over countable covers by sets of diameter at most δ.

title: Area measure on the Euclidean unit sphere
description: On S^{d−1}⊂ℝᵈ, spherical area is the restriction of (d−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Its probability normalization divides by its total mass.

title: Pushforward measure
description: For a measurable map f:X→Y and measure μ on X, the pushforward f_*μ on Y satisfies f_*μ(B)=μ(f⁻¹(B)).

title: Outer unit normal of a convex body
description: A unit vector u is an outer normal at x∈∂K if (y−x)·u≤0 for every y∈K; at boundary points with a unique such u, this gives the Gauss map.

title: Harmonic function on a plane domain
description: A twice continuously differentiable real function u on an open Ω⊂ℝ² satisfying ∂₁²u+∂₂²u=0.

title: Green function of the unit disk
description: For z,ζ in the disk, G(z,ζ)=log|(1−ζ̄z)/(z−ζ)|, with value∞ at z=ζ; it is zero at the boundary in the z variable and gives the disk’s logarithmic potential kernel.

title: Isomorphism of Banach spaces
description: A bounded linear bijection between Banach spaces whose inverse is bounded.

title: Independent σ-algebras
description: A family of sub-σ-algebras is independent if the probability of the intersection of events from any finite subfamily equals the product of their probabilities.

title: Stochastic process
description: A family (X_t) indexed by a specified time set, with each X_t a measurable map from a probability space into a specified measurable state space. Adaptation, joint measurability and path regularity are additional conditions when required.

title: Gaussian process
description: A real or vector-valued stochastic process whose every finite vector of coordinate evaluations has a multivariate normal law.

title: Separable metric space
description: A metric space having a countable dense subset.

title: Lusin topological space
description: A Hausdorff topological space that is a continuous bijective image of a Polish space. Its Borel measurable space is consequently standard Borel; the topology need not itself be Polish.

title: Function of bounded variation on an interval
description: A real function f has bounded variation on [a,b] if sup∑_i|f(t_i)−f(t_{i−1})| over finite ordered partitions is finite. Vector-valued paths use the corresponding norm.

title: Continuous local martingale
description: A continuous adapted process M_t for which stopping times T_n↑∞ almost surely exist such that M_{t∧T_n} is a martingale for every n.

title: Continuous semimartingale
description: A continuous adapted process expressible as M+A where M is a continuous local martingale and A is an adapted continuous process of finite variation on every bounded time interval.

title: Predictable stochastic process
description: A process measurable for the σ-algebra on time×sample space generated by adapted left-continuous processes. This formalizes choosing an integrand from information available just before the integration time.

title: Absolutely continuous function on a real interval
description: A real function f on [a,b] is absolutely continuous if for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that any finite disjoint family of intervals (a_i,b_i) with ∑(b_i−a_i)<δ has ∑|f(b_i)−f(a_i)|<ε.

title: Finite-rank linear operator
description: A linear map whose image is finite-dimensional.

title: Positive trace-class operator on a Hilbert space
description: A nonnegative bounded self-adjoint operator Q is trace class if ∑_k⟨Qe_k,e_k⟩<∞ for an orthonormal basis; the sum is independent of the basis and equals its trace.

title: Local martingale
description: An adapted càdlàg process M for which stopping times T_n↑∞ almost surely exist such that each stopped process M_{t∧T_n} is a martingale.

title: Characteristic of a field
description: The least positive integer n with n·1=0 in the field, if one exists, and zero otherwise.

title: Element integral over a commutative ring
description: For a ring inclusion R⊂A, an element a∈A is integral over R if it satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in R.

title: Normal subgroup
description: A subgroup H of G satisfying gHg⁻¹=H for every g∈G.

title: Commutator subgroup
description: The subgroup [G,G] generated by all commutators xyx⁻¹y⁻¹ with x,y∈G.

title: Solvable group
description: A group whose iterated commutator subgroups reach the trivial subgroup after finitely many steps.

title: Tensor product of commutative algebras
description: For commutative R-algebras A,B, the module A⊗_R B with multiplication (a⊗b)(a′⊗b′)=aa′⊗bb′ and unit 1⊗1; it is the coproduct of A and B among commutative R-algebras.

title: Base change of an affine algebraic group
description: For a field extension L/F and an affine F-group with coordinate Hopf algebra A, its base change to L has coordinate Hopf algebra L⊗_F A.

title: Morphism of affine algebraic groups
description: A homomorphism defined by regular coordinate functions; in coordinate algebras it is a homomorphism of commutative Hopf algebras in the opposite direction, preserving coproduct, counit and antipode.

title: Closed subgroup of an affine algebraic group
description: A subgroup represented by the quotient of its ambient group’s coordinate Hopf algebra by a Hopf ideal.

title: Rational points of an affine algebraic group
description: For an affine F-group G with coordinate Hopf algebra A and commutative F-algebra R, the group G(R)=Hom_(F-alg)(A,R), with group multiplication induced by the coproduct of A.

title: Algebraic representation of an affine algebraic group
description: A morphism of algebraic groups G→GL(V) for a finite-dimensional vector space V; equivalently an action with regular matrix coefficient functions. A faithful representation identifies G with a closed algebraic subgroup of GL(V).

title: Smooth affine algebraic group
description: An affine algebraic group over F whose coordinate algebra is smooth over F. In the finite-type characteristic-zero case all affine group schemes are smooth, but that assertion is a separate theorem.

title: Geometrically connected affine algebraic group
description: An affine F-group whose coordinate algebra after extension to an algebraic closure has no idempotents other than 0 and 1. This is the coordinate-algebra account of connectedness after base change.

title: Unipotent affine algebraic group
description: An affine algebraic group that, after extension to an algebraic closure, has a faithful algebraic representation with all matrices upper triangular and every diagonal entry 1.

title: Solvable smooth affine algebraic group
description: A smooth affine algebraic group whose group of points over an algebraic closure is solvable. For the characteristic-zero groups used here this agrees with termination of the algebraic derived series.

title: Borel subgroup of a connected affine algebraic group
description: Over an algebraically closed field, a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Over F, a subgroup is an F-Borel subgroup if its base change to an algebraic closure is such a Borel subgroup.

title: Multiplicative algebraic group
description: The affine F-group G_m with R-points R×, represented by F[t,t⁻¹], whose coproduct sends t to t⊗t.

title: Split algebraic torus
description: An algebraic F-group isomorphic over F to a finite product of copies of G_m. An F-torus need only become such a product after extending F to an algebraic closure.

title: Commutative Hopf algebra over a commutative ring
description: A commutative R-algebra A with R-algebra maps Δ:A→A⊗_R A, ε:A→R and S:A→A satisfying the coassociativity, counit and inverse identities: (Δ⊗id)Δ=(id⊗Δ)Δ and m(S⊗id)Δ=m(id⊗S)Δ=ηε.

title: Affine group scheme of finite presentation over a ring
description: A commutative Hopf R-algebra A that is finitely presented as an R-algebra, regarded through its group-valued functor B↦Hom_(R-alg)(A,B). This coordinate account defines the affine group scheme without requiring general scheme theory.

title: Base change of an affine group scheme
description: For R→S and an affine group scheme represented by A, its base change is represented by S⊗_R A with the induced Hopf operations. A residue-field fiber is this construction for S=R/𝔪.

title: Topological field
description: A field with a topology making addition, multiplication, additive inversion and inversion on the nonzero elements continuous.

title: Local field
description: A nondiscrete locally compact Hausdorff topological field. Both archimedean and nonarchimedean local fields are allowed.

title: Local-field topology on points of an affine algebraic group
description: For a local field F and an affine embedding G⊂A^n, give G(F) the subspace topology from F^n. Polynomial coordinate maps show this topology is independent of the chosen affine embedding.

title: Separable closure of a field
description: A separable algebraic extension F^sep/F that has no further nontrivial finite separable algebraic extension, equivalently the separable elements in a chosen algebraic closure.

title: Krull topology on an infinite Galois group
description: On Gal(L/F), the subgroup fixing each finite intermediate extension E/F is an open neighbourhood of the identity; their cosets form a basis. For an absolute Galois group take L=F^sep.

title: Absolute Galois group
description: The group Gal(F^sep/F), with its Krull topology, where F^sep is a separable closure.

title: Continuous nonabelian 1-cocycle
description: For a topological group Γ acting continuously on a group H, a continuous map c:Γ→H satisfying c(στ)=c(σ)σ(c(τ)). Cocycles are equivalent when c′(σ)=h⁻¹c(σ)σ(h) for one h∈H.

title: Existence of a closed algebraic-group orbit
description: A nonempty algebraic variety over an algebraically closed field, acted on morphically by an algebraic group, contains an orbit closed in that variety.

title: Fiber dimension theorem for algebraic varieties
description: For a dominant morphism of irreducible algebraic varieties, the generic fiber has dimension dim X−dim Y; if all fibers have dimension r, then dim X=dim Y+r.

title: Irreducibility of connected smooth algebraic groups
description: A connected smooth algebraic group over an algebraically closed field is irreducible, and every proper closed subvariety has strictly smaller dimension.

title: Frobenius generates the absolute Galois group of a finite field
description: For F_q, its absolute Galois group is procyclic, topologically generated by x↦x^q; equivalently the integer powers of that Frobenius are dense in Gal(F_q^sep/F_q).

title: Dynkin’s π–λ theorem
description: If a family P contains the whole space and is closed under finite intersections, every family containing P and closed under complements and countable disjoint unions contains the σ-algebra generated by P.

title: Uniqueness theorem for characteristic functions
description: Two Borel probability measures on ℝ have the same characteristic function if and only if they are equal.

title: Tower property of conditional expectation
description: For sub-σ-algebras F⊆G and integrable X, E[E[X|G]|F]=E[X|F]; also E[E[X|F]|G]=E[X|F].

title: Hoeffding’s lemma
description: If a≤X≤b almost surely and EX=0, then Eexp(tX)≤exp(t²(b−a)²/8) for every real t.

title: Taylor’s theorem with integral remainder
description: If f is C^{n+1} on the interval joining a and x, then f(x)=∑_{k=0}ⁿf⁽ᵏ⁾(a)(x−a)ᵏ/k!+∫_a^xf⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(s)(x−s)ⁿ/n! ds.

title: Orthonormal family in a Hilbert space
description: Vectors (e_i) with ⟨e_i,e_j⟩=0 for i≠j and ‖e_i‖=1.

title: Orthonormal basis of a Hilbert space
description: An orthonormal family whose linear span is dense in the Hilbert space.

title: Strongly continuous contraction semigroup
description: Bounded operators T_t on a Banach space satisfy T₀=I,T_{s+t}=T_sT_t,‖T_t‖≤1 and T_tx→x in norm as t↓0 for every x.

title: Uniqueness of finite-dimensional characteristic functions
description: Two Borel probability laws on ℝᵈ agree if their characteristic functions u↦Eexp(iu·X) agree for every u∈ℝᵈ. Equivalently, equality in law of every scalar linear combination of coordinates determines the joint law.

title: Tagged Riemann sum
description: For a partition a=x₀<⋯<x_n=b and tags t_i∈[x_{i−1},x_i], the Riemann sum of f is ∑ᵢf(t_i)(x_i−x_{i−1}); the partition mesh is maxᵢ(x_i−x_{i−1}).

title: Fatou’s lemma
description: For nonnegative measurable functions f_n on a measure space, ∫liminf_n f_n≤liminf_n∫f_n, allowing∞.

title: Approximation of nonnegative measurable functions by simple functions
description: Every nonnegative measurable function is the pointwise increasing limit of nonnegative measurable simple functions.

title: Norm of a bounded self-adjoint operator from its quadratic form
description: For a bounded self-adjoint operator A on a complex Hilbert space, ∥A∥=sup_{∥x∥=1}|⟨Ax,x⟩|.

title: Continuous functional calculus for a self-adjoint C*-algebra element
description: For self-adjoint a in a C*-algebra, continuous scalar functions on σ(a) can be evaluated at a by the unique isometric *-homomorphism sending the identity function to a and the constant one to the unit of the unitization. Functions vanishing at zero give elements of the original algebra.

title: Spectral characterization of positive C*-algebra elements
description: An element of a C*-algebra has the form b*b exactly when it is self-adjoint with spectrum contained in [0,∞).

title: Norm closedness of the positive cone of a C*-algebra
description: A norm limit of positive elements of a C*-algebra is positive.

title: Norm monotonicity for positive C*-algebra elements
description: If 0≤a≤b in a C*-algebra, then ∥a∥≤∥b∥.

title: Order-unit bound for a positive C*-algebra element
description: For positive a in a C*-algebra, a≤∥a∥1 in its unitization.

title: Path-connected topological space
description: A topological space in which every pair of points is joined by a continuous map from [0,1] with those endpoints.

title: Locally path-connected topological space
description: A space in which every neighborhood of each point contains a path-connected open neighborhood of that point.

title: Tietze extension theorem
description: Every continuous real-valued function on a closed subset of a normal topological space extends continuously to the whole space; if the function takes values in [−1,1], the extension can have the same range.

title: Pasting lemma for a finite closed cover
description: Maps on finitely many closed subsets covering a topological space glue to a continuous map if they are continuous and agree on every overlap.

title: Normality of metric spaces
description: Any two disjoint closed subsets of a metric space have disjoint open neighborhoods; equivalently every metric space is normal.

title: Components of a locally path-connected space
description: Every connected component of a locally path-connected topological space is open and path connected.

title: Real orthogonal group
description: The group O(n) of real n×n matrices U satisfying UᵀU=I; these are the linear isometries of Euclidean space.

title: Spherical harmonic decomposition of L² of a sphere
description: The real Hilbert space L²(S^{n−1}) is the orthogonal sum of the finite-dimensional spaces of spherical harmonics of degrees k≥0; a polynomial of degree m restricts to a sum of harmonics of degrees at most m.

title: Addition theorem for spherical harmonics
description: For n≥3 and an orthonormal basis Y₁,…,Y_N of degree-k real spherical harmonics under probability-normalized area, ∑ⱼYⱼ(u)Yⱼ(v)=N G_{k,n}(u·v), where G_{k,n} is the normalized zonal Gegenbauer polynomial with G_{k,n}(1)=1. In particular the diagonal sum equals N. For n=2 the corresponding zonal polynomial is the Chebyshev polynomial cos(k arccos t).

title: Jackson approximation theorem on the sphere
description: For a λ-Lipschitz real function f on S^{n−1} and positive integer k, a real polynomial P of degree at most k satisfies sup_{S^{n−1}}|f−P|≤Cλn/k for an absolute C.

title: Klartag’s linear-size isomorphic Minkowski symmetrization theorem
description: For n≥2 and a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, at most 5n Minkowski symmetrizations produce a centrally symmetric body K̃ with (1−c|log log n|/√log n)M*(K)B₂ⁿ⊆K̃⊆(1+c|log log n|/√log n)M*(K)B₂ⁿ, for an absolute c. In particular its outer radius is at most an absolute multiple of M*(K).

title: Haar’s theorem for compact groups
description: Every compact Hausdorff topological group has a unique left-invariant regular Borel probability measure, and that measure is also right invariant.

title: Zorn’s lemma
description: If every chain in a partially ordered set has an upper bound in that set, then the set has a maximal element.

title: Strong Markov property of Brownian motion
description: At every almost surely finite stopping time T, the process B_{T+t}−B_T is a standard Brownian motion independent of the information through time T.

title: Montel’s theorem for locally bounded holomorphic families
description: A locally uniformly bounded family of holomorphic functions on a complex domain is normal: every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets to a holomorphic function.

title: Identity theorem for holomorphic functions
description: Two holomorphic functions on a connected complex domain that agree on a set with an accumulation point inside the domain agree everywhere.

title: Cauchy’s integral theorem on simply connected domains
description: The integral of a holomorphic function around every closed piecewise C¹ curve in a simply connected complex domain is zero.

title: Irreducible nonnegative matrix
description: A finite square nonnegative real matrix A is irreducible if for every pair i,j some n≥0 satisfies (Aⁿ)_{ij}>0. Equivalently its directed support graph is strongly connected.

title: Right-continuous path
description: A path x:[0,∞)→E in a metric space is right-continuous if d(x(t+h),x(t))→0 as h↓0 for every t≥0.

title: Jordan normal form theorem
description: Every linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex vector space has a basis consisting of Jordan chains for its eigenvalues; its matrix in that basis is block diagonal with Jordan blocks.

title: Generalized eigenvector
description: For an endomorphism T and scalar λ, a nonzero vector v with (T−λI)ᵏv=0 for some k≥1 is a generalized eigenvector; a Jordan chain satisfies (T−λI)v₁=0 and (T−λI)v_{j+1}=v_j.

title: Fundamental theorem of Lebesgue integration
description: If g∈L¹([a,b]), F(x)=∫_a^xg is absolutely continuous and F′=g almost everywhere. Conversely every absolutely continuous F has an integrable a.e. derivative and F(x)−F(a)=∫_a^xF′.

title: Doob’s upcrossing inequality
description: If (X_n) is a submartingale and U_n(a,b) counts completed upcrossings from at most a to at least b by time n, then (b−a)EU_n(a,b)≤E(X_n−a)⁺−E(X₀−a)⁺ for a<b.

title: Discrete-time submartingale
description: An integrable adapted process X_n with E[X_{n+1}|F_n]≥X_n almost surely for every n.

title: Conditional Jensen inequality
description: For integrable X and convex φ with φ(X) integrable, φ(E[X|G])≤E[φ(X)|G] almost surely.

title: Pull-out property of conditional expectation
description: If Y is G-measurable and X,YX are integrable, then E[YX|G]=Y E[X|G] almost surely, when the right side is integrable.

title: Moment-determinate probability distribution
description: A probability law with finite moments of every nonnegative integer order is moment-determinate if no other probability law has the same sequence of moments.

title: Limit of a function between metric spaces
description: For f defined near an accumulation point a of a metric space, lim_{x→a}f(x)=L means that for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that 0<d(x,a)<δ implies d(f(x),L)<ε.

title: Cardinality of a set
description: The size of a set, with two sets having the same cardinality when there is a bijection between them. A set has finite cardinality n when it is in bijection with {1,…,n}; infinite cardinalities are distinguished by the same bijection criterion.

title: Convergence of bounded monotone real sequences
description: Every bounded monotone sequence of real numbers converges.

title: Riemann integrability of continuous functions
description: Every continuous real function on a compact interval is Riemann integrable.

title: Linearity of the Riemann integral
description: If f,g are Riemann integrable on the same compact interval and a,b are real, af+bg is integrable and ∫(af+bg)=a∫f+b∫g.

title: Interval additivity of the Riemann integral
description: For integrable f on [a,b] and c∈[a,b], ∫_a^b f=∫_a^c f+∫_c^b f, with the usual orientation convention.

title: Order bounds for the Riemann integral
description: If integrable f satisfies m≤f≤M on [a,b], then m(b−a)≤∫_a^b f≤M(b−a).

title: Extension of a linearly independent family to a finite basis
description: Every linearly independent family in a finite-dimensional vector space can be extended to a basis.

title: Closedness of finitely generated cones
description: The set of all nonnegative real linear combinations of finitely many vectors in R^n is closed.

title: Strict separation of a point from a closed convex cone
description: If C is a nonempty closed convex cone in R^n and b∉C, there is y such that y·c≥0 for every c∈C and y·b<0.

title: Special linear group over a commutative ring
description: The group SL_n(R) of square matrices over a commutative ring R whose determinant is 1, with matrix multiplication.

title: Metaplectic double cover of SL₂(R)
description: The group Mp₂(R) of pairs (γ,φ), with γ=[[a,b],[c,d]]∈SL₂(R) and φ a holomorphic function on the upper half-plane satisfying φ(τ)²=cτ+d; multiplication is (γ₁,φ₁)(γ₂,φ₂)=(γ₁γ₂,(φ₁∘γ₂)φ₂). The projection to γ is a double cover.

title: Modular form of half-integral weight with a multiplier
description: For κ∈(1/2)Z, a holomorphic function on the upper half-plane satisfying f(γτ)=χ(γ,φ)φ(τ)^(2κ)f(τ) on the metaplectic preimage of a congruence subgroup, for a fixed compatible finite-image character χ, and holomorphic at every cusp. The multiplier is specified as part of the data.

title: Jacobi form of half-integral weight with a multiplier
description: A holomorphic function on H×C of weight κ∈(1/2)Z and index m∈(1/2)Z_{≥0}, with a specified compatible finite-image multiplier, transforming by the metaplectic modular weight factor and exp(2πimcz²/(cτ+d)), and by exp(−2πim(r²τ+2rz)) times its multiplier under z↦z+rτ+s. At every cusp its Fourier indices obey 4mn−ℓ²≥0.

title: Almost holomorphic modular form of half-integral weight
description: A function obeying the metaplectic modular transformation of a specified half-integral weight and compatible finite-image multiplier, polynomial in 1/Im(τ) with holomorphic coefficients and of at most polynomial growth in Im(τ) after normalization at every cusp.

title: Almost holomorphic Jacobi form of half-integral weight
description: A function with a specified half-integral weight, half-integral nonnegative index and compatible multiplier, obeying the Jacobi transformations, polynomial in 1/(τ−τ̄) and (z−z̄)/(τ−τ̄) with holomorphic coefficients, and with Jacobi cusp growth: after each cusp normalization, |φ(τ,z)|≤C·Im(τ)^N exp(2πm Im(z)²/Im(τ)) in a Jacobi translation strip for some C,N.

title: Perfect-cuboid criterion in the second-cuboid parametrization
description: For coprime distinct positive integers p,q and an integer root t of the degree-ten Q_{p,q} from the second cuboid conjecture, the corresponding parametrized cuboid is perfect exactly when t>max(p²,pq,q²) and (p²+t)(pq+t)>2t². This is a criterion within that parametrized family, not a claim that every perfect cuboid belongs to it.

title: Masharov–Sharipov’s bound for second-cuboid searches
description: In the second-cuboid parametrization with distinct coprime positive p,q, no root giving a perfect cuboid can occur for q≥59p. Thus every possible candidate in this family has q<59p and t<61p². This does not assert nonexistence of arbitrary perfect cuboids.

title: Schwarz lemma
description: If f maps the unit disk holomorphically to itself and f(0)=0, then |f(z)|≤|z| and |f′(0)|≤1. Equality at a nonzero point or in the derivative bound forces f(z)=cz with |c|=1.

title: Maximum modulus principle
description: A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected open subset of ℂ cannot have a local maximum of its modulus in the interior.

title: Scalar Schur algorithm on the unit disk
description: For a holomorphic disk map f with |f(0)|<1, replace f by (f(z)−f(0))/(z(1−overline{f(0)}f(z))) and iterate; Schwarz’s lemma makes the removable value at zero and the disk bound valid. The successive values at zero are its Schur parameters.

title: Closure of finite Blaschke products under composition
description: The composition of two nonconstant finite Blaschke products of degrees m and n is a finite Blaschke product of degree mn; composing with a disk automorphism preserves the degree.

title: Algebra homomorphism property of holomorphic functional calculus
description: For a bounded operator T, evaluation f↦f(T) is a unital algebra homomorphism from functions holomorphic on a common neighborhood of σ(T) into bounded operators; it agrees with polynomial evaluation.

title: Riemann’s removable singularity theorem
description: A holomorphic function on a punctured neighborhood of a complex point extends holomorphically across that point if it is bounded near the point.

title: Beurling’s invariant subspace theorem for Hardy H²
description: Every nonzero closed subspace of H² invariant under multiplication by z has the form θH² for an inner function θ, unique up to multiplication by a unimodular constant.

title: Division algorithm for polynomials over a field
description: For polynomials a,b over a field with b≠0, there are unique polynomials q,r with a=bq+r and either r=0 or deg r<deg b.

title: Bézout identity for polynomials over a field
description: The monic greatest common divisor of polynomials a,b, not both zero, is ua+vb for some polynomials u,v. In particular coprime polynomials admit ua+vb=1.

title: Fundamental theorem of algebra
description: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root; equivalently it factors completely into linear factors over ℂ.

title: Hardy–Littlewood maximal function
description: For locally integrable f on ℝⁿ, Mf(x)=sup_{r>0}|B(x,r)|⁻¹∫_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|dy.

title: Hardy–Littlewood weak (1,1) maximal inequality
