title: Affine algebraic variety over a field
description: An affine algebraic variety is specified here by a finitely generated reduced commutative algebra A over a field F. Its k-points, for extensions k/F, are the F-algebra homomorphisms A→k. Morphisms are induced by algebra homomorphisms in the opposite direction. Reducible affine varieties are allowed.

title: Zariski topology on an affine variety
description: On the k-points of an affine variety with coordinate algebra A, closed sets are the common zero sets {x:f(x)=0 for all f∈I} of subsets I⊂A. Geometric closedness is tested after extension to an algebraic closure.

title: Algebraic action on an affine variety
description: An action of an affine algebraic group G on an affine variety X by a morphism G×X→X; in coordinate algebras it is a coaction O(X)→O(G)⊗O(X) satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities.

title: Orbit and stabilizer of an algebraic group action
description: For an algebraic action G on X and x∈X(k), the geometric orbit consists of gx for g∈G(k̄), and the stabilizer G_x is the closed k-subgroup fixing x after every algebra extension. An orbit is closed if it is closed in the geometric Zariski topology.

title: Subalgebra over a field
description: A vector subspace of an algebra over a field that contains the identity and is closed under multiplication; the inherited operations make it an algebra over the same field.

title: Invariant coordinate ring
description: For an algebraic action G on an affine variety X, O(X)^G is the subalgebra of regular functions f satisfying f(gx)=f(x) after every extension of the ground algebra. Equivalently the coaction sends f to1⊗f.

title: Reductive affine algebraic group, allowing components
description: A smooth affine algebraic group whose identity component is a connected reductive algebraic group. In this catalogue a disconnected group may therefore be reductive; connectedness is separately specified when required.

title: Hilbert finite generation and closed-orbit separation for reductive actions
description: For a reductive group G acting algebraically on an affine variety X over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, O(X)^G is finitely generated. The map π:X→Spec O(X)^G is surjective; two geometric points have the same image exactly when their orbit closures intersect. Every fiber contains exactly one closed orbit.

title: Reynolds operator for a reductive action
description: For a rational representation of a linearly reductive group, the natural projection onto invariant vectors, killing the sum of the nontrivial simple subrepresentations. On a coordinate algebra it satisfies E(fg)=fE(g) when f is invariant.

title: Complete reducibility for characteristic-zero reductive groups
description: Every finite-dimensional algebraic representation of a reductive group over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field is a direct sum of irreducible representations.

title: Hilbert basis theorem
description: If R is a noetherian commutative ring, then R[x] is noetherian. In particular a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field is noetherian.

title: Hilbert Nullstellensatz
description: Over an algebraically closed field, maximal ideals of a finitely generated algebra have residue field equal to the ground field, and the ideal of the zero set of an ideal is its radical.

title: Matsushima’s affineness criterion
description: For a connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and a closed subgroup H, H is reductive exactly when it occurs as the stabilizer of a point in a finite-dimensional algebraic G-representation with closed orbit. Equivalently, the homogeneous quotient G/H is affine exactly when H is reductive. Consequently stabilizers of closed orbits in affine G-varieties are reductive.

title: Equivariant linear embedding of an affine group variety
description: Every affine variety with an algebraic action of an affine algebraic group admits a closed equivariant embedding into a finite-dimensional algebraic representation.

title: Compact real form of a complex reductive group
description: A maximal compact subgroup K of a complex reductive group G whose real Lie algebra k satisfies Lie(G)=k⊕ik. Finite-dimensional G-representations admit K-invariant positive Hermitian inner products.

title: Existence of a compact real form of a complex reductive group
description: Every complex reductive algebraic group has a maximal compact subgroup K with Lie(G)=Lie(K)⊕iLie(K), and every finite-dimensional algebraic representation admits a K-invariant positive Hermitian inner product.

title: Reductivity of the Zariski closure of a compact linear group
description: The Zariski closure in GL_n(C) of a compact subgroup is a reductive algebraic group. In particular an algebraic subgroup H whose Lie algebra is the complexification of Lie(H)∩Lie(K), for a compact subgroup K, has reductive identity component.

title: Algebraically closed base-extension invariance of reductivity and closed orbits
description: For affine algebraic data over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, extending to a larger algebraically closed field preserves and reflects reductivity of a smooth affine group and geometric closedness of an orbit of an algebraic action.

title: Dimension bound for an isotropic symplectic subspace
description: For a finite-dimensional symplectic vector space (V,ω), a subspace W satisfying ω|_(W×W)=0 has dimension at most half the dimension of V.

title: Lefschetz principle for algebraically closed fields
description: Every first-order sentence in the language of rings with rational coefficients has the same truth value in all algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. Bounded finite-type algebraic data can be transported to C after choosing a finitely generated field of definition.

title: Cousin’s gauge-partition lemma
description: For every positive function δ on a compact interval [a,b], there is a finite tagged partition a=t₀<⋯<t_m=b with tags ξ_i∈[t_{i−1},t_i] and [t_{i−1},t_i]⊂(ξ_i−δ(ξ_i),ξ_i+δ(ξ_i)).

title: Jordan decomposition of a real function of bounded variation
description: A real function on a compact interval has finite total variation exactly when it is the difference of two bounded nondecreasing functions.

title: Lebesgue’s differentiability theorem for monotone functions
description: A bounded nondecreasing real function on [a,b] is differentiable with finite nonnegative derivative almost everywhere, its derivative is integrable, and ∫_a^bF′≤F(b)−F(a).

title: Regularity of Lebesgue measure
description: Every Lebesgue measurable subset of ℝⁿ has measure equal to the infimum of measures of open supersets and the supremum of measures of compact subsets.

title: Distributions with zero derivative on an interval
description: A distribution on a connected open real interval whose distributional derivative is zero is a constant distribution.

title: ACL characterization of first-order Sobolev functions
description: For an open Ω⊂ℝⁿ and1≤p≤∞, f∈W¹,ᵖ(Ω) exactly when f∈Lᵖ has a representative absolutely continuous on compact subintervals of almost every coordinate-parallel line in Ω, with its almost-everywhere classical partial derivatives in Lᵖ. Those derivatives are its weak partial derivatives.

title: Elementary-matrix factorization of an invertible matrix
description: Every invertible square matrix over a field is a finite product of elementary matrices representing row swaps, multiplication of one row by a nonzero scalar, and addition of a multiple of one row to another.

title: Affine change of variables for Lebesgue integration
description: For an invertible real n×n matrix A, b∈ℝⁿ and nonnegative measurable or integrable g, ∫_{ℝⁿ}g(Ax+b)|detA|dx=∫_{ℝⁿ}g(y)dy.

title: Planar piecewise affine extension with boundary-length control
description: For the open unit square S and an injective piecewise affine g:∂S→ℝ², there is a finitely piecewise affine homeomorphism h:S→ℝ² extending continuously as g on∂S with ∫_S|Dh|≤C∫_{∂S}|Dτg|dℋ¹, for an absolute constant C. The image is the bounded polygonal region determined by the boundary curve.

title: Rank-one W¹,¹ extension estimate for a square
description: For the open unit square S and M=diag(1,0), an injective piecewise affine g:∂S→ℝ² with ∫_{∂S}|Dτg−Mτ|dℋ¹<δ admits a finitely piecewise affine homeomorphic extension h with ∫_S|Dh−M|≤Cδ, provided0<δ≤δ₀ for absolute constants C,δ₀.

title: Polygonal domain in the plane
description: A bounded connected open subset of ℝ² whose boundary is a finite union of disjoint simple closed polygonal curves; holes are allowed. Each boundary curve consists of finitely many line segments meeting only at successive endpoints.

title: Invariant probability for a Markov semigroup
description: A probability measure μ is invariant for a Markov transition semigroup P_t if ∫P_tf,dμ=∫f,dμ for every bounded measurable f and every t≥0.

title: Progressively measurable stochastic process
description: A process X_t is progressively measurable for a filtration(F_t) if for every T≥0, (t,ω)↦X_t(ω) on[0,T]×Ω is measurable for B([0,T])⊗F_T.

title: Schauder’s theorem on compact adjoints
description: A bounded linear operator between Banach spaces is compact if and only if its continuous dual operator is compact.

title: Itô isometry for Hilbert-valued Wiener integrals
description: For predictable Hilbert–Schmidt B_s:U→H with E∫₀ᵀ‖B_s‖²_HSds<∞, E‖∫₀ᵀB_sdW_s‖²_H=E∫₀ᵀ‖B_s‖²_HSds. The integral has a continuous H-valued martingale version.

title: Variational Itô formula for the Hilbert norm
description: Let V⊂H⊂V* be a separable Gelfand triple, p>1, X₀∈L²(Ω;H), Y∈L^{p/(p−1)}(dt⊗P;V*) progressive and B predictable with E∫‖B‖²_HS<∞. If X_t=X₀+∫₀ᵗY_sds+∫₀ᵗB_sdW_s has an Lᵖ(dt⊗P;V) version, then it has continuous H paths, E sup_{t≤T}‖X_t‖²_H<∞, and ‖X_t‖²_H=‖X₀‖²_H+∫₀ᵗ(2⟨Y_s,X_s⟩+‖B_s‖²_HS)ds+2∫₀ᵗ⟨X_s,B_sdW_s⟩_H.

title: Well-posedness of monotone evolution equations in a Gelfand triple
description: Let V⊂H⊂V* be a separable reflexive Gelfand triple and p>1. Suppose measurable A(t,v) is hemicontinuous, 2⟨A(t,u)−A(t,v),u−v⟩≤C‖u−v‖²_H, 2⟨A(t,v),v⟩≤C‖v‖²_H−c‖v‖ᵖ_V+f(t), and ‖A(t,v)‖_{V*}^{p/(p−1)}≤C‖v‖ᵖ_V+f(t), with c>0 and f≥0 integrable. For x∈H, u′=A(t,u),u(0)=x has a unique solution u∈C([0,T];H)∩Lᵖ(0,T;V),u′∈L^{p/(p−1)}(0,T;V*).

title: Stationary solution for a strongly monotone additive SPDE
description: Let V⊂H⊂V* be a separable reflexive Gelfand triple and p>2. If a time-independent hemicontinuous drift M satisfies 2⟨M(u)−M(v),u−v⟩≤−c‖u−v‖ᵖ_V, coercivity 2⟨M(v),v⟩≤C−c′‖v‖ᵖ_V, and ‖M(v)‖_{V*}^{p/(p−1)}≤C(1+‖v‖ᵖ_V), then trace-class additive Wiener noise admits a strictly stationary variational solution with continuous H paths and locally Lᵖ(V) paths, obtainable as the pullback limit from fixed initial states.

title: Girsanov theorem for cylindrical Wiener noise
description: If an adapted U-valued h satisfies E exp(½∫₀ᵀ‖h_s‖²ds)<∞, then R=exp(−∫₀ᵀ⟨h_s,dW_s⟩−½∫₀ᵀ‖h_s‖²ds) has mean one, and W_t+∫₀ᵗh_sds is cylindrical Wiener noise under R,dP.

title: Krylov–Bogoliubov invariant-measure theorem
description: For a Feller Markov semigroup on a Polish space, any weak subsequential limit of a tight family of Cesàro occupation laws T⁻¹∫₀ᵀP_t(x,·)dt, with T→∞, is invariant. Feller means P_t maps bounded continuous functions to bounded continuous functions.

title: Doob’s strong-Feller irreducible mixing theorem
description: A stochastically continuous Markov semigroup on a Polish space which is strong Feller and topologically irreducible at each positive time has at most one invariant probability measure; if it exists, P_t(x,·) converges to it in total variation for every x. Strong Feller means bounded Borel functions become continuous, and irreducibility means P_t(x,O)>0 for each nonempty open O.

title: Variational well-posedness and continuous cocycle for additive stochastic porous media
description: On a bounded smooth Ω⊂ℝᵈ, m>1 and c∈ℝ, dX=[Δ(|X|^{m−1}X)+cX]dt+dW with zero Dirichlet conditions and trace-class H⁻¹-valued Wiener noise has a unique variational solution from each H⁻¹ initial state, with continuous H⁻¹ paths and locally L^{m+1}(time×Ω) paths. On the canonical two-sided noise space the solutions have a version defining a continuous random dynamical system on H⁻¹.

title: Strong mixing of nondegenerate additive stochastic porous media
description: On a bounded smooth domain, consider dX=[Δ(|X|^{m−1}X)+cX]dt+dW with m>1,c∈ℝ, zero Dirichlet conditions and covariance Q trace class onH⁻¹. Put p=m+1,V=Lᵖ,H=H⁻¹. If Q¹ᐟ² is injective and ‖u‖ᵖ_V≥a‖u‖^σ_{Q¹ᐟ²}‖u‖^{p−σ}_H for all nonzero u∈V, for some a>0,σ≥2,σ>p−2, then its transition laws converge in total variation to a unique invariant probability measure. This includes the weak one-point-law mixing required for synchronization.

title: Restriction in first Galois cohomology
description: For an extension L/F and an F-group H, the map H¹(F,H)→H¹(L,H_L) restricts a cocycle to the corresponding absolute Galois subgroup after compatible separable-closure choices. For a completion F_v it is the localization map; its pointed-set class is independent of the choices.

title: Tate–Shafarevich group of a number-field torus
description: For a torus T over a number field F, Sha¹(F,T) is the kernel of H¹(F,T)→∏_v H¹(F_v,T), over all places. Since T is commutative these H¹ sets and their kernel are abelian groups; its classes are torsors locally trivial at every place.

title: Finiteness of first cohomology of a local-field torus
description: If k is R,C, or a finite extension of Q_p and T is an algebraic torus over k, then H¹(k,T) is a finite abelian group.

title: Finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group of a torus
description: For every algebraic torus T over a number field F, Sha¹(F,T) is finite. This asserts finite kernel, not finite H¹(F,T).

title: Galois-cohomological classification of rational orbits
description: For an algebraic action H on an affine F-variety X, a point x∈X(F), and its stabilizer I, the H(F)-orbits of F-points in the geometric orbit H(Fsep)x are naturally bijective to ker[H¹(F,I)→H¹(F,H)]. The kernel means classes mapping to the distinguished point, and the orbit of x corresponds to the trivial class.

title: Finite Galois splitting of an algebraic torus
description: Every algebraic torus over a field becomes isomorphic to G_m^r over some finite Galois extension of that field.

title: Hilbert’s theorem90
description: For a field F with separable closure Fsep, H¹(Gal(Fsep/F),(Fsep)×)=0. Equivalently, for a finite Galois extension L/F every multiplicative1-cocycle c_σ is b⁻¹σ(b) for some b∈L×.

title: Inflation–restriction sequence in first group cohomology
description: For a normal subgroup N of a group Γ acting on an abelian group M, the sequence0→H¹(Γ/N,M^N)→H¹(Γ,M)→H¹(N,M)^(Γ/N) is exact. The last action is quotient conjugation. For continuous cohomology, Γ is profinite, N is closed normal, and M is a discrete continuous Γ-module.

title: Finiteness of positive-degree finite-group cohomology of lattices
description: For a finite group Γ and a finitely generated abelian Γ-module M, H^i(Γ,M) is finite for every i>0. For a finitely generated Z_p-module the same holds: cohomology is finitely generated and annihilated by |Γ|.

title: Logarithm on sufficiently small principal units of a p-adic field
description: For a finite extension L/Q_p, on1+𝔭_L^n for sufficiently large n the convergent p-adic logarithm and exponential are inverse isomorphisms to the additive group 𝔭_L^n. The latter is a finite-rank free Z_p-module; O_L×/(1+𝔭_L^n) is finite and L×/O_L×≅Z by the valuation.

title: Exact sequence of the complex exponential
description: The complex exponential is surjective C→C× with kernel2πiZ, giving0→2πiZ→C→C×→1. Coordinatewise this sequence respects conjugation and integer monomial actions.

title: Dirichlet’s unit theorem
description: For a number field L with r₁ real places and r₂ pairs of complex places, O_L× is the product of its finite roots-of-unity group and a free abelian group of rank r₁+r₂−1.

title: Finiteness of the ideal class group of a number field
description: The group of nonzero fractional ideals of a number field, modulo principal fractional ideals, is finite.

title: Shapiro’s lemma for group cohomology
description: For a subgroup Δ of a finite group Γ and a Δ-module M, H^i(Γ,Ind_Δ^Γ M)≅H^i(Δ,M); induction and coinduction agree for finite groups.

title: Long exact sequence in cohomology of a short exact module sequence
description: A short exact sequence of modules for a group induces the connecting maps and exact cohomology sequence beginning0→A^Γ→B^Γ→C^Γ→H¹(Γ,A)→H¹(Γ,B)→H¹(Γ,C)→H²(Γ,A)→⋯.

title: Weight of a split torus representation
description: For an algebraic representation ρ of a split torus T, a character α:T→G_m is a weight if V_α={v:ρ(t)v=α(t)v after every algebra extension} is nonzero. V_α is its weight space.

title: Adjoint representation of an algebraic group
description: The algebraic representation Ad:G→GL(Lie G) obtained by differentiating the conjugation maps h↦ghg⁻¹ at the identity.

title: Roots of a reductive group relative to a split torus
description: For a maximal split torus T of a connected reductive group G, the nontrivial characters occurring as weights in Ad on Lie G are the relative roots. A choice of minimal parabolic containing T specifies the positive roots; the simple roots are the positive roots not expressible as a sum of two positive roots.

title: Levi subgroup of a parabolic subgroup
description: A reductive subgroup M of a parabolic P such that multiplication identifies P with the semidirect product M⋉R_u(P), where R_u(P) is the unipotent radical. This defines a Levi subgroup without incorporating its existence theorem.

title: Derived subgroup of a smooth affine algebraic group
description: The smallest closed algebraic subgroup containing all geometric commutators xyx⁻¹y⁻¹. For a connected group it is the closed connected subgroup generated by these commutators, with the corresponding ground-field descent.

title: Siegel set for an adelic reductive group
description: Fix a minimal F-parabolic P=MN of a connected reductive number-field group, a compatible maximal compact K, and the maximal split torus T₀ of the derived group in M. Let A_(T₀)=Hom(X*(T₀),R_(>0)), embedded diagonally in T₀(F_∞), be its positive real split part. For compact Ω⊂P(A_F)∩G(A_F)¹ and t>0, a Siegel set is Ω{a∈A_(T₀):|α(a)|_∞≥t for every simple relative root α}K.

title: Rapid decrease on an automorphic quotient
description: A smooth function on G(F)∖G(A_F)¹ is rapidly decreasing if on every Siegel set, for every B>0 and every simple relative root α, its absolute value is bounded by C·|α(a)|_∞^(−B), where a is the split-torus coordinate of the point and C may depend on B and the Siegel set.

title: Smooth vector of an adelic unitary representation
description: A vector in a strongly continuous unitary representation of G(A_F) that is fixed by an open compact subgroup at finite places and whose orbit map under the real Lie group G(F_∞) is infinitely Fréchet differentiable in Hilbert norm in local coordinates.

title: Rapid decrease of smooth square-integrable cusp forms
description: For a connected reductive number-field group, every smooth vector in its cuspidal L²-space is a rapidly decreasing smooth function on G(F)∖G(A_F)¹. More precisely, for fixed compactly supported smooth f, a Siegel set S and B>0, |R(f)φ(x)|≤C_(f,S,B)‖φ‖₂|α(a_x)|_∞^(−B) for every φ in the cuspidal L²-space, x∈S and simple root α.

title: Hilbert direct sum
description: For a family of complex Hilbert spaces H_i, the Hilbert direct sum consists of families (v_i) with ∑_i‖v_i‖²<∞, with coordinatewise linear operations and inner product ∑_i⟨v_i,w_i⟩. The nonnegative sum is the supremum of its finite partial sums.

title: Discreteness and finite multiplicities of the cuspidal spectrum
description: For a connected reductive number-field group, the right regular representation on L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)¹) is a Hilbert direct sum of irreducible unitary representations, each with finite multiplicity. This is a statement about the cuspidal subspace, not discreteness of all automorphic L².

title: Smooth kernels and pointwise expansion of cuspidal convolution
description: For a compactly supported smooth f on G(A_F)¹ whose convolution operator has cuspidal image, its L²-kernel has a representative smooth separately in the two variables. Writing K_(π,f) for the kernels obtained by orthogonal projection to cuspidal isotypic components, the sum ∑_π K_(π,f)(x,y) equals that representative pointwise. Each isotypic kernel has the same separate smoothness.

title: Poisson summation on a number field
description: For a Schwartz–Bruhat function f on A_F^n, a nontrivial additive character of A_F/F and its self-dual Haar measure, ∑_(x∈F^n)f(x)=∑_(x∈F^n)f̂(x).

title: Exponential coordinates on a characteristic-zero unipotent group
description: For a connected unipotent algebraic group over a characteristic-zero field, the exponential is a polynomial isomorphism from its nilpotent Lie algebra to the group as varieties; multiplication is given by the finite Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula.

title: Adelic Iwasawa decomposition
description: For a connected reductive group G over a number field F and an F-parabolic subgroup P, there is a maximal compact subgroup K⊂G(A_F) such that G(A_F)=P(A_F)K. The local factors can be chosen hyperspecial outside finitely many places.

title: Dixmier–Malliavin factorization theorem
description: For a continuous representation π of a real Lie group on a Fréchet space, every smooth vector is a finite sum of vectors π(f_i)v_i with f_i∈C_c∞(G) and smooth v_i.

title: Trace-class property of cuspidal convolution
description: For a connected reductive number-field group and compactly supported smooth f on its central-normalized adelic group, the right convolution operator R_cusp(f) on the cuspidal L²-space is trace class.

title: Trace-class criterion for a discrete unitary representation
description: If every smooth compactly supported convolution operator in a strongly continuous unitary representation of a Lie group times a totally disconnected group is trace class, that representation is a Hilbert direct sum of irreducibles with finite multiplicities.

title: Eisenstein spectral decomposition of automorphic L²
description: The automorphic L²-space of a reductive number-field group decomposes as the orthogonal sum over cuspidal parabolic data of direct integrals of normalized parabolically induced unitary representations; Eisenstein series realize the corresponding unitary maps and residual subspaces.

title: Local fundamental solution for an elliptic operator
description: An elliptic differential operator has a distributional local fundamental solution at a point: applying the operator to the solution gives the Dirac distribution there. Sufficiently high elliptic powers have fundamental solutions with arbitrarily prescribed finite differentiability also at the source, while elliptic regularity gives smoothness away from it.

title: Peter–Weyl approximation with loss of differentiability
description: Let K be a compact subgroup of a real Lie group G. There is an integer ℓ depending only on K such that, for every integer r>ℓ and f∈C_c^r(G), its left-right compact-type projections f_(τ,σ) sum absolutely to f in C_c^(r−ℓ)(G). Supports lie in K·supp(f)·K; for every continuous seminorm p there, ∑_(τ,σ)p(f_(τ,σ)) is bounded by a continuous C_c^r seminorm of f. Each projection is the character-average projector for irreducible K-types τ,σ.

title: Maximal coupling of probability measures
description: For probabilities μ,ν on a standard Borel space, there is a joint law(X,Y) with marginalsμ,ν and P(X≠Y)=d_TV(μ,ν). Every coupling has P(X≠Y)≥d_TV(μ,ν).

title: Mandelbrot–Van Ness representation of fractional Brownian motion
description: For H∈(0,1),H≠½, a two-sided standard fractional Brownian motion can be represented as B_t^H=c_H∫_ℝ[(t−s)_+^{H−½}−(−s)_+^{H−½}]dW_s, with c_H chosen for variance1 at time1. The difference kernel is square integrable; H=½ is ordinary Brownian motion.

title: Riemann–Liouville fractional integral
description: For α>0, (I_{0+}^αf)(t)=Γ(α)⁻¹∫₀ᵗ(t−s)^{α−1}f(s)ds whenever the integral exists. On the appropriate integrability domains these operators compose by I^αI^β=I^{α+β}.

title: Foster–Lyapunov drift condition for a Markov kernel
description: A Markov kernel P satisfies a geometric Foster–Lyapunov condition with V≥1 if PV≤aV+b for constants0≤a<1 and b<∞. Compact sublevel sets of V make the resulting occupation-law bounds useful for tightness.

title: Hairer’s total-variation mixing theorem for additive fractional SDEs
description: Let dX_t=b(X_t)dt+dB_t^H onℝ with H∈(0,1),H≠½ and b∈C¹. Suppose (b(x)−b(y))(x−y)≤min(C−c|x−y|²,C|x−y|²), c>0, and |b(x)|+|b′(x)|≤C(1+|x|)^N. If H>½ also require b′ bounded. Then for each deterministic x the law of X_t^x converges in total variation to a common probability measure μ, the one-point marginal of the unique stationary solution adapted to the two-sided noise past.

title: Outer function in the Smirnov class on the unit disk
description: A holomorphic function of the form c exp(∫_T(ζ+z)/(ζ−z)u(ζ)dm(ζ)), where |c|=1, u is real and integrable on the circle, and m is normalized arc measure. No Hardy H² bound is imposed; the boundary log modulus is u almost everywhere.

title: Inner–outer factorization in the Smirnov class
description: Every nonzero function in the Smirnov class on the disk is a product of an inner function and an outer Smirnov function, uniquely up to opposite unimodular constants.

title: Poisson majorization of the logarithm of a bounded analytic function
description: For nonzero g∈H∞ on the disk, log|g(z)|≤∫_T P_z(ζ)log|g*(ζ)|dm(ζ), where the left side is−∞ at a zero and the boundary logarithm is integrable.

title: Smirnov maximum principle
description: If F belongs to the Smirnov class on the unit disk and its radial boundary values satisfy |F*|≤M almost everywhere for a finite M≥0, then F is bounded analytic and |F(z)|≤M throughout the disk.

title: Diagonal uniqueness for a sesquiholomorphic kernel
description: If K(z,w) is holomorphic in z and antiholomorphic in w on a connected disk product, and K(z,z)=0 throughout the disk, then K is identically zero. Thus such a kernel is determined by its diagonal.

title: Backward shift on Hardy H²
description: The bounded operatorLf(z)=(f(z)−f(0))/z, with the removable value at zero; on Taylor coefficients it drops the constant term.

title: Backward-shift defect identity in an extreme de Branges–Rovnyak space
description: If b is an extreme point of the unit ball of H∞, thenH(b) is invariant underLf=(f−f(0))/z and ∥Lf∥²_{H(b)}=∥f∥²_{H(b)}−|f(0)|² for everyf∈H(b).

title: Sarason’s analytic-function inclusion criterion for H(b)
description: For a scalar Schur function b, the following are equivalent: b is non-extreme; H(b) contains every analytic polynomial; H(b) contains every function holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk.

title: Isometric weighted Dirichlet–H(b) criterion for general weights
description: If a nonzero nonnegative integrable disk weightω givesDω=H(b) with the Hardy-plus-Dirichlet norm, thenb is non-extreme with inner factorz up to phase. When∫ωdA=1, suchb exists exactly whenDω⊂H², polynomials are dense inDω, andQω is outer in the Smirnov sense with(1−|z|²)|Qω(z)|²=Bω(z). Then the associated Pythagorean quotient isb/a=czQω for|c|=1.

title: Positive split central subgroup of an adelic reductive group
description: For the largest F-split torus T in the center of a connected reductive number-field group G, A_G=Hom(X*(T),R_(>0)) is its positive real split part, embedded diagonally in T(F_∞) and trivially at finite places. This is the standard central factor complementary to G(A_F)¹, not all of T(F_∞)°.

title: Absolute convergence of reductive periods of cusp forms
description: Let G be connected reductive over a number field, H⊂G a connected reductive subgroup, and φ a smooth vector in L²_cusp(A_G G(F)∖G(A_F)). For a unitary character χ of H(A_F) trivial on H(F) and A_G∩H(A_F), ∫_((A_G∩H(A_F))H(F)∖H(A_F))|χ(h)φ(h)|dh is finite. If H(A_F)=(H(A_F)∩A_G)(H(A_F)∩G(A_F)¹), this is equivalently the normalized H(F)∖(H(A_F)∩G(A_F)¹) period.

title: Siegel-set covering theorem for a reductive adelic quotient
description: For a connected reductive number-field group, there is a Siegel set S such that G(F)S=G(A_F)¹.

title: Weyl-chamber decomposition of a real split torus
description: The positive real part of a maximal split torus in a connected reductive group is the union of Weyl translates of a chosen closed positive chamber, with distinct chamber interiors disjoint and chamber boundaries of Haar measure zero.

title: Smooth Hensel lifting over a complete discrete valuation ring
description: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal 𝔭 and residue field k, and A a smooth finitely presented R-algebra. Every R-algebra homomorphism A→k lifts to A→R. Equivalently each k-point of a smooth affine finite-presentation R-space lifts to an R-point.

title: Reductivity of involution-fixed subgroups in characteristic zero
description: For a connected reductive group over a characteristic-zero field and an algebraic involution σ, the fixed subgroup G^σ is smooth and its identity component is reductive. The fixed subgroup itself need not be connected.

title: Invariant compact form for a finite automorphism group
description: A finite group of algebraic automorphisms of a connected complex reductive group preserves a compact real form of that group.

title: Smoothness of affine algebraic groups in characteristic zero
description: Every affine group scheme of finite type over a characteristic-zero field is smooth.

title: Smooth morphism of affine finite-presentation spaces
description: A morphism represented contravariantly by A→B is smooth when B, as an A-algebra, is finitely presented and satisfies the nilpotent-ideal lifting property.

title: Affine integral model over a ring of S-integers
description: For a finitely generated F-algebra A and the ring O_(F,S) of a number field with finitely many finite primes inverted, an affine integral model is a finitely generated O_(F,S)-subalgebra A₀⊂A with F⊗A₀≅A. In the group case require compatible Hopf-algebra operations. This injective coordinate-algebra convention gives the usual flat model over the Dedekind base.

title: Spreading out smooth affine morphisms over a number field
description: Finite-presentation affine algebraic data over a number field can be defined over O_(F,S) after inverting finitely many primes; if a given generic morphism is smooth, its integral model becomes smooth after enlarging S.

title: Openness of the smooth locus for finite-presentation morphisms
description: For a finite-presentation morphism of schemes, the set of source points where the morphism is smooth is open.

title: Jacobian criterion for smoothness of a finitely presented algebra
description: Locally for A=R[x₁,…,x_n]/(f₁,…,f_m), a suitable invertible Jacobian minor gives a standard smooth presentation; every smooth finitely presented algebra is locally of this form.

title: Increasing event in a Bernoulli product space
description: An event A⊆{0,1}ᴱ is increasing if ω∈A and ω′≥ω coordinatewise imply ω′∈A. The coordinates carry independent Bernoulli laws, which may have different parameters.

title: Harris’s inequality for Bernoulli product measures
description: For increasing events A,B under a finite product of Bernoulli laws, P(A∩B)≥P(A)P(B). If one event is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses.

title: Janson’s zero-count inequality for increasing product events
description: Let A_i be finitely many increasing events, each determined by coordinates S_i in a finite Bernoulli product space. Put p_i=P(A_i),μ=∑p_i,Δ=∑_{i<j:S_i∩S_j≠∅}P(A_i∩A_j) and ε=max_i p_i<1. Then P(∩A_iᶜ)≤min{exp(−μ+Δ),exp(Δ/(1−ε))∏(1−p_i)}. An arbitrary dependency graph without the product-event hypotheses does not suffice.

title: Hoeffding bound with a fractional matching for hypergraph-correlated variables
description: Let Y_e∈[0,1] be hypergraph-correlated and φ a fractional matching with Φ=∑_eφ(e)>0. For t≥0, P(∑_eφ(e)(Y_e−EY_e)≥t)≤exp(−2t²/Φ). Equivalently the weighted average has upper-tail bound exp(−2Φε²) above its own φ-weighted mean, not the unweighted mean.

title: Distribution of the maximum of Brownian motion with drift
description: For standard Brownian motion B, μ∈ℝ,t>0 and a≥0, P(max_{0≤s≤t}(B_s+μs)≤a)=Φ((a−μt)/√t)−exp(2μa)Φ((−a−μt)/√t), where Φ is the standard normal distribution function. The probability is zero for a<0.

title: Optional sampling for bounded continuous martingales
description: If M is a bounded continuous martingale and σ≤τ are stopping times, then E[M_τ|F_σ]=M_σ. Unbounded-time versions use the almost-sure terminal limit of the uniformly integrable martingale.

title: Kronecker product of matrices
description: For A=(a_ij)∈M_{m,n}(R) and B=(b_kl)∈M_{p,q}(R) over a commutative ring, A⊗B is the mp×nq block matrix whose(i,j) block is a_ijB; its((i,k),(j,l)) entry is a_ijb_kl.

title: Polynomial height bound for an arithmetic lattice kernel
description: For a connected reductive number-field group G and an adelic height, there are N and a continuous seminorm q on compactly supported continuous test functions such that ∑_(γ∈G(F))|f(x⁻¹γy)|≤q(f)‖x‖^N‖y‖^N for x,y∈G(A_F)¹. On a fixed compact support the seminorm may be bounded by a support-dependent multiple of the supremum norm.

title: Finite crystallographic root system
description: A finite spanning set Φ of nonzero vectors in a real inner-product space, preserved by the orthogonal reflection s_α in each root α, and satisfying2(β,α)/(α,α)∈Z for all α,β∈Φ. Nonreduced systems are allowed; reduced means the only multiples of α in Φ are ±α. A simple system is a basis whose root expansions are all nonnegative or all nonpositive integer combinations.

title: Coroot of a root
description: In a finite root system with specified invariant inner product, the coroot associated to α is α∨=2α/(α,α), identified with the corresponding vector in the dual space via the inner product.

title: Fundamental weight of a root system
description: For a simple system α₁,…,α_r, the fundamental weights ω_i are the dual basis to the simple coroots: (ω_i,α_j∨)=δ_ij. They belong to the real root span; integrality for a specified algebraic group is a separate lattice condition.

title: Dual Weyl chamber for a simple root system
description: The open cone of H in the real root span for which (ω_i,H)>0 for every fundamental weight ω_i of the chosen simple system. Its indicator is the dual-chamber cutoff used in Arthur truncation; partial parabolic chambers use the corresponding quotient root space.

title: Constant term along a parabolic subgroup
description: For P=MN with unipotent radical N and a suitable automorphic function φ, its constant term is φ_P(g)=∫_(N(F)∖N(A_F))φ(ng)dn. Cuspidality means these terms vanish for every proper F-parabolic.

title: Parabolic Harish–Chandra map
description: Fix compatible Iwasawa data G(A_F)=M(A_F)N(A_F)K for P=MN. The map H_P:G(A_F)→a_P=Hom(X*_F(M),R) is specified by ⟨χ,H_P(mnk)⟩=log|χ(m)|_A. It extends the Levi’s logarithmic character map using its Iwasawa component.

title: Arthur truncation operator
description: For fixed minimal-parabolic data and sufficiently regular T, Arthur’s operator on an automorphic function is Λ^Tφ(x)=∑_P(−1)^dim(a_P/a_G)∑_(δ∈P(F)∖G(F))φ_P(δx)·τ̂_P(H_P(δx)−T_P), over standard F-parabolics. Here τ̂_P is the dual-chamber indicator and T_P is the projection of T to a_P. Proper constant terms vanish for cusp forms, so Λ^Tφ=φ there.

title: Absolute rapid decay of the cuspidal spectral kernel sum
description: For compactly supported smooth f on G(A_F)¹, the sum ∑_π|K_(π,f)(x,y)| over cuspidal isotypic kernels converges and decays faster than every inverse power of every simple-root coordinate on each pair of Siegel sets. It is consequently integrable over pairs of normalized connected-reductive period quotients.

title: Reductive integral models at almost every finite place
description: Let G be connected reductive over a number field F and let 𝒢 be an affine integral group model over O_(F,S). After enlarging S by finitely many primes, 𝒢 is smooth and all its geometric fibers are connected reductive. Hence 𝒢(O_v) is hyperspecial in G(F_v) for every v outside S.

title: Openness of reductivity of identity components in smooth affine families
description: For a smooth affine group scheme G→S, the locus where the geometric identity component of the fiber is reductive is open.

title: Closedness of connected fibers in a smooth reductive-identity family
description: For a smooth affine group scheme whose geometric fiber identity components are reductive, the locus of connected fibers is closed. In particular if the base is irreducible and the generic fiber connected, every fiber is connected.

title: Dedekind property of the ring of integers
description: The ring of integers of a number field, and every localization at finitely many primes, is a Dedekind domain: it is noetherian, integrally closed and has dimension1. In particular its finitely generated algebras are finitely presented.

title: Regular C² parametrized surface patch
description: An injective C² map m from a closed planar rectangle into ℝ³, extending C² to a neighborhood, with Dm of rank two everywhere. It parametrizes its image, including the boundary; its tangent planes are the images of Dm and its metric matrix is (Dm)ᵀDm.

title: Cross product in oriented Euclidean three-space
description: The vector u×v characterized by ⟨u×v,w⟩=det(u,v,w) for every w∈ℝ³, with the standard orientation.

title: Extended real line
description: The ordered set ℝ∪{−∞,+∞}, with−∞<r<+∞ for every real r.

title: Coercive functional on a normed space
description: An extended-real functional R is coercive if R(x)→+∞ whenever ∥x∥→∞.

title: Horn–Schunck optical-flow model on a surface
description: For a Riemannian surface M, image derivative data I,J and α>0, minimize ∫_M(|⟨∇_M I,v⟩+J|²+α|∇^M v|²)dS over tangent first-order Sobolev vector fields v. The two terms impose linearized brightness constancy and covariant smoothness.

title: Weak convergence theorem for convex Tikhonov regularization
description: Let X,Y be Hilbert spaces, F:D(F)⊂X→Y bounded linear with weakly closed domain, and R:X→[0,∞] proper convex and weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous. Suppose the effective domain meetsD(F) and every positive-parameter Tikhonov level set is weakly sequentially compact. Minimizers exist and are weakly subsequentially stable for fixedα. If an exact finite-penalty solution exists, α→0 andδ²/α→0 imply that noisy-data minimizers have subsequences converging weakly toR-minimizing exact solutions.

title: Quadratic Tikhonov error rate under operator perturbations
description: Let A:X→Y andL:X→Z be bounded linear maps between real Hilbert spaces with ∥h∥≤C(∥Ah∥+∥Lh∥). LetAx†=y and⟨Lx†,Lh⟩=⟨w,Ah⟩ for allh. If∥A_ρ−A∥≤ρ,∥yδ−y∥≤δ andα is comparable toη=δ+ρ>0 tending to zero, minimizers of∥A_ρx−yδ∥²+α∥Lx∥² satisfy∥x−x†∥²=O(η) for sufficiently smallρ.

title: Algebraic positive cone of a complex *-algebra
description: The cone of finite sums∑a_i* a_i in a complex *-algebra. Writea≤b whenb−a is such a sum. No norm, completeness or spectral characterization is assumed.

title: Semi-inner-product module over a complex *-algebra
description: A complex rightA-moduleX with anA-valued sesquilinear form linear in the second variable, satisfying⟨x,ya⟩=⟨x,y⟩a,⟨x,y⟩*=⟨y,x⟩ and⟨x,x⟩ in the algebraic positive cone. Zero length need not implyx=0; noC*-norm onA is assumed.

title: Unital Banach *-algebra with continuous involution
description: A complex Banach algebra with an identity1 and a continuous conjugate-linear mapa↦a* satisfying(ab)*=b*a* and(a*)*=a. A C*-identity is not required.

title: C*-completion associated to a C*-seminorm
description: For a C*-seminormγ on a complex *-algebraA, identifya,b whenγ(a−b)=0 and complete the resulting quotient algebra in the norm induced byγ. Its multiplication and involution extend continuously, making a possibly nonunitalC*-algebra.

title: Schwarz inequality for a C*-seminorm of an algebraic module form
description: For a semi-inner-product moduleX over a complex *-algebraA and aC*-seminormγ onA, γ(⟨x,y⟩)²≤γ(⟨x,x⟩)γ(⟨y,y⟩) for allx,y∈X.

title: Spectral bound for a positive functional under conjugation
description: For a positive linear functionalφ on a unital Banach *-algebra with continuous involution, a positive elementb (a finite sum of squares) andc∈A, φ(cbc*)≤r(b)φ(cc*), where r is the Banach-algebra spectral radius.

title: Spectral-radius Schwarz bound for positive functionals on Banach *-modules
description: For a semi-inner-product moduleX over a unital Banach *-algebra with continuous involution and a positive linear functionalφ, φ(⟨x,y⟩⟨y,x⟩)≤φ(⟨x,x⟩)r(⟨y,y⟩) for allx,y∈X.

title: Scheme-theoretic image of an affine morphism
description: For an affine morphism represented contravariantly by a ring map A→B, its scheme-theoretic image has coordinate algebra A/ker(A→B), equivalently the image subalgebra of B. This is a closed affine subspace of the target; it need not have all its rational points in the set-theoretic image of the rational-point map.

title: Cartan map of an algebraic involution
description: For an involution σ of an affine algebraic group, the Cartan map is B_σ(g)=gσ(g)⁻¹. It is constant on right cosets of the fixed subgroup and equivariant for the corresponding twisted conjugation action; its affine scheme-theoretic image is often used as a model of the symmetric space. No rational-point surjectivity is included in this definition.

title: Richardson’s semisimple closed-orbit criterion for an involution
description: Let G be connected reductive over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, σ an involution, and Q the affine image of the Cartan map g↦gσ(g)⁻¹. For a semisimple q∈Q, its conjugation orbit under G^σ is Zariski closed in Q. This is the implication of Richardson’s criterion used in Hahn’s proof.

title: Local topology of an algebraic orbit in characteristic zero
description: For a smooth algebraic group acting on an affine variety over R,C or a finite extension of Q_p, the map G(k)/G_x(k)→G(k)x is a homeomorphism onto its orbit with the local-field topology. The rational orbit is open and closed inside the k-points of its geometric orbit; if that geometric orbit is Zariski closed, the rational orbit is closed in the ambient k-points.

title: Smoothness of orbit morphisms in characteristic zero
description: For an algebraic action over a characteristic-zero field, the orbit map from the smooth acting group to a geometric orbit is smooth; its fibers are translates of the smooth algebraic stabilizer.

title: Analytic inverse function theorem over a local field
description: For an analytic map between finite-dimensional manifolds over R,C or a finite extension of Q_p, an invertible derivative at a point gives an analytic local inverse. A surjective derivative gives local analytic sections after choosing complementary coordinates.

title: Integration along a closed subgroup of a local algebraic group
description: Let k be R,C or a finite extension of Q_p, G a smooth affine k-group and H a closed smooth subgroup. With Haar measure dh, q_*f(gH)=∫_(H(k))f(gh)dh maps C_c∞(G(k)) onto C_c∞(G(k)/H(k)). Here smooth means C∞ at archimedean places and locally constant at nonarchimedean places; the target is the analytic homogeneous quotient, not all rational points of an affine quotient variety.

title: Partition of unity on a local-field manifold
description: For a compact subset of a finite-dimensional manifold over R,C or a finite extension of Q_p and a finite open cover, there are compactly supported smooth functions subordinate to the cover summing to1 near that compact subset. In the nonarchimedean case they may be locally constant.

title: Borel–Harish-Chandra finite-volume theorem
description: For a connected reductive group G over a number field, G(F)∖G(A_F)¹ has finite volume for Haar measure on G(A_F)¹. Equivalently A_G G(F)∖G(A_F) has finite invariant volume.

title: Godement compactness criterion for a reductive adelic quotient
description: For a connected reductive number-field group G, the normalized quotient G(F)∖G(A_F)¹ is compact exactly when every F-split torus in G is central, equivalently G has F-rank zero after removing its split central directions. In particular an anisotropic reductive group has compact normalized adelic quotient.

title: Haar modulus formula in Iwasawa coordinates
description: For P=MN and compatible Iwasawa coordinates G(A)=N(A)M(A)K, Haar measure has its torus-density factor δ_P(a)⁻¹, where δ_P is the determinant of conjugation by a on Lie N. On the positive split chamber this is the product of inverse positive-root powers with their multiplicities.

title: Adelic Mahler compactness criterion
description: A fixed-covolume family of F-lattices in an adelic finite-dimensional vector space is relatively compact modulo F-linear changes of basis exactly when the family has a common positive lower bound on lengths of nonzero rational lattice vectors.

title: Isomorphism of undirected multigraphs
description: A pair of bijections between the vertex sets and edge sets of two undirected multigraphs that preserves the unordered endpoints of every edge. For rooted or marked graphs it must also preserve the root and all specified marks.

title: Compactness of bounded-degree rooted graphs with finite marks
description: Fix a degree bound Δ and a finite set of vertex/edge marks. Isomorphism classes of connected rooted graphs of degree at mostΔ, with those marks, form a compact metrizable space for local convergence: two rooted graphs are close when their marked balls around the root agree to a large radius. Finite and countably infinite graphs are allowed.

title: Karlin–McGregor spectral representation for a finite birth–death chain
description: For an irreducible birth–death transition matrix P on{0,…,N}, stationary lawπ, and recurrence polynomials φ₀=1 with Pφ(λ)=λφ(λ), there is a probability measureν on its real eigenvalues in[−1,1] such that ∫φ_xφ_y,dν=1_{x=y}π(0)/π(x) and Pⁿ(x,y)=π(y)/π(0)∫λⁿφ_x(λ)φ_y(λ)dν(λ), n≥0.

title: Interlacing of consecutive orthogonal-polynomial zeros
description: For n≥1 let p₀,…,p_n be monic orthogonal polynomials with positive norms for a positive measure having at least n+1 support points and the required finite moments. The next polynomial p_{n+1}=(x−a_n)p_n−b_np_{n−1}, where a_n=∫xp_n²/‖p_n‖² and b_n=‖p_n‖²/‖p_{n−1}‖², has simple real zeros strictly interlacing those of p_n. If the measure has exactly n+1 distinct support points with positive masses, p_{n+1} is their monic vanishing polynomial, even though its measure norm is zero.

title: Character of a finite-dimensional representation
description: For a finite-dimensional representation ρ of a group G, its character is the function χ_ρ(g)=trρ(g). For a unitary representation of a compact group it is a continuous class function; the character of a general representation need not be one-dimensional.

title: C^r topology on functions with compact support
description: For an integer r≥0 on a smooth real manifold, the space C_K^r of r-times continuously differentiable functions supported in a fixed compact K has the seminorms given by uniform bounds on coordinate derivatives of order≤r, using finitely many charts near K. C_c^r has the locally convex inductive-limit topology over compact supports. On a Lie group, invariant derivatives give the same topology.

title: Peter–Weyl theorem
description: For a compact Hausdorff group K, every irreducible continuous unitary representation is finite-dimensional. Its matrix coefficients, multiplied by the square root of their representation dimension, form an orthonormal basis of L²(K) as the irreducible representation varies, and their finite linear span is uniformly dense in C(K).

title: Weyl eigenvalue bound for a compact-manifold Laplacian
description: For a nonnegative elliptic Laplacian on a compact d-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifold, the eigenvalue counting function satisfies N(λ)=O((1+λ)^(d/2)). Consequently (1+Δ)^(−s) is trace class for s>d/2.

title: Casimir Laplacian of a compact Lie group
description: Choose an Ad-invariant inner product on the Lie algebra of a compact Lie group and an orthonormal basis X_j. The operator Δ=−∑X_j² is a nonnegative bi-invariant elliptic Laplacian and acts by a nonnegative scalar on each irreducible matrix-coefficient subspace.

title: Local Iwasawa decomposition
description: For a connected reductive group over R,C or a finite extension of Q_p and a parabolic P, some maximal compact K satisfies G(k)=P(k)K. If a compatible reductive integral model and parabolic model over O_k exist, K can be taken to be the hyperspecial subgroup 𝒢(O_k).

title: Spreading out a parabolic subgroup over S-integers
description: For a connected reductive number-field group G and an F-parabolic P⊂G, after inverting finitely many primes there are a reductive affine group model 𝒢 and a smooth parabolic model 𝒫⊂𝒢 with generic fibers G and P.

title: Tychonoff’s theorem
description: An arbitrary product of compact topological spaces, with the product topology, is compact.

title: Hardy inequality for boundary distance on a Lipschitz domain
description: For a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω there is C_Ω such that ∫_Ω|u(x)|²/dist(x,∂Ω)²dx≤C_Ω∫_Ω|∇u(x)|²dx for every u∈H₀¹(Ω).

title: Polynomial boundary-distance lower bound for an elliptic ground state
description: For L=∑ᵢⱼ∂ᵢ(aⁱʲ∂ⱼ), with smooth real symmetric uniformly elliptic coefficients and zero Dirichlet condition on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain, its positive L²-normalized principal eigenfunction φ satisfies φ(x)≥c,dist(x,∂Ω)^κ for some c,κ>0. The exponent may depend on the domain and ellipticity; linear decay is not asserted at corners.

title: Euclidean logarithmic Sobolev inequality with a parameter
description: For d≥1 there is C_d such that every real u∈H¹(ℝᵈ) with ‖u‖₂=1 satisfies ∫u²log(u²)dx≤ε∫|∇u|²dx+C_d−(d/2)logε for ε>0, with the usual0log0 convention.

title: Davies–Simon logarithmic Sobolev criterion for ultracontractivity
description: Let a symmetric Markov semigroup have a strongly local Dirichlet form E on L²(μ). If for every normalized f in its form domain and0<ε≤1, ∫f²log(f²)dμ≤εE(f,f)+C₀+C₁|logε|, then its operators map L²(μ) boundedly into L∞(μ) at every positive time. The criterion applies to the ground-state-transformed elliptic forms here.

title: Interior smoothness of a Dirichlet heat kernel
description: For a smooth uniformly elliptic real divergence-form operator on a domain, the killed diffusion semigroup has a transition density p_t(x,y) smooth in t>0 and in both interior spatial variables. Boundary regularity is not asserted by this statement.

title: Bounded–Lipschitz metrization of weak convergence
description: On a Polish space with a bounded compatible metric d, β(μ,ν)=sup{|∫f,dμ−∫f,dν|:‖f‖∞≤1,Lip_d(f)≤1} is a metric on Borel probability measures inducing their weak-convergence topology.

title: Isotypic subspace for a compact-group representation
description: For a continuous unitary representation of a compact group K and an irreducible finite-dimensional K-representation τ, its τ-isotypic subspace is the closed span of all subrepresentations isomorphic to τ. Equivalently it is the image of d_τ∫_K conjugate(χ_τ(k))π(k)dk.

title: Admissible unitary representation of an adelic reductive group
description: For a connected reductive number-field group, a continuous unitary representation is admissible if, for every compact open K_f⊂G(A_f) and every irreducible type τ of a maximal compact K_∞⊂G(F_∞), the subspace of K_f-fixed vectors in its τ-isotypic subspace is finite-dimensional.

title: Admissibility of irreducible unitary adelic representations
description: Every irreducible continuous unitary representation of the adelic group of a connected reductive number-field group is admissible. In particular each cuspidal automorphic isotypic block has finite-dimensional spaces of a fixed archimedean compact type and fixed finite-level invariants, after accounting for its finite automorphic multiplicity.

title: Archimedean–finite factorization of irreducible unitary adelic representations
description: Every irreducible continuous unitary representation of G(A_F)=G(F_∞)×G(A_f), for connected reductive G over a number field, is the Hilbert tensor product of irreducible unitary representations of the two factors, unique up to unitary equivalence.

title: Harish-Chandra’s admissibility theorem
description: For a real reductive algebraic group G and maximal compact subgroup K⊂G(R), every irreducible continuous unitary representation has finite multiplicity for every irreducible K-type. Complex reductive groups are included by restriction to R.

title: Admissibility of irreducible finite-adelic unitary representations
description: For a connected reductive number-field group, every irreducible continuous unitary representation V of G(A_f) has dim V^K<∞ for every compact open subgroup K. This is the finite-adelic form of nonarchimedean admissibility, not a claim about arbitrary totally disconnected groups.

title: Hilbert tensor product
description: The completion of the algebraic tensor product of complex Hilbert spaces for the inner product specified on elementary tensors by ⟨x⊗y,x′⊗y′⟩=⟨x,x′⟩⟨y,y′⟩.

title: Smooth function on a Euclidean sphere
description: A scalar function onS^{d−1} is smooth if it is the restriction of aC∞ function on a neighborhood of the sphere inℝᵈ.

title: Spherical polynomial
description: The restriction toS^{d−1} of a real polynomial in d variables; its degree is the least possible total degree of an extending polynomial.

title: Best L² approximation by spherical polynomials
description: Forf∈L²(S^{d−1}),E_N(f) is the infimum of∥f−P∥₂ over spherical polynomialsP of degree at mostN. Rates of decay ofE_N quantify polynomial approximation.

title: Finite signed measure
description: A differenceµ=µ₁−µ₂ of two finite positive measures on the sameσ-algebra. It is real-valued and countably additive.

title: Spherical cosine transform
description: For an integrable functionf onS^{d−1}, Cf(u)=∫_{S^{d−1}}|⟨u,v⟩|f(v)dσ(v), using probability-normalized spherical area. The same formula definesCµ for finite signed measuresµ.

title: Generating measure of an origin-symmetric zonoid
description: A finite even positive measureµ onS^{d−1} generating an origin-symmetric zonoidZ satisfiesh_Z(u)=∫|⟨u,v⟩|dµ(v). Even means invariance underv↦−v.

title: Uniqueness of a zonal spherical harmonic
description: For d≥3, the degree-k spherical harmonics invariant under all orthogonal transformations fixing a given unit vectoru form a one-dimensional space. Its value as a function ofv is proportional to the Gegenbauer polynomial C_k^{(d−2)/2}(u·v).

title: Gegenbauer polynomial values at zero and one
Spherical Radon transform on spherical harmonics
description: For d≥3, the normalized spherical Radon transform acts on degree-k harmonics by zero for oddk and by(−1)^{k/2}[1·3⋯(k−1)]/[(d−1)(d+1)⋯(d+k−3)] for evenk; the degree-zero multiplier is1.

title: Fischer decomposition of homogeneous polynomials
description: Every real homogeneous polynomial of degreeN inℝᵈ has a unique decomposition∑_{j=0}^{⌊N/2⌋}|x|^{2j}H_{N−2j}(x), where eachH_k is homogeneous and harmonic. ConsequentlydimH_k=binom(k+d−1,d−1)−binom(k+d−3,d−1), with a negative-degree term interpreted as zero.

title: Nikolskii inequality for spherical polynomials
description: For a spherical polynomialP of degree at mostN≥1 onS^{d−1}, ∥P∥∞≤C_dN^{(d−1)/2}∥P∥₂, with spherical area normalized to probability.

title: Spectral multipliers of the spherical cosine transform
description: For d≥3, the spherical cosine transform acts by scalar multipliers on each harmonic degree. Odd multipliers vanish; even multipliers are nonzero, and their absolute values are bounded above and below by positive dimension-dependent constants times(1+k)^{−(d+2)/2} on degree2k.

title: Smoothness characterized by spherical harmonic coefficient decay
description: AnL² function onS^{d−1} is smooth exactly when its degree-k harmonic projection hasL² normO((1+k)^{−N}) for everyN>0. In that case the harmonic expansion and all its derivatives converge to the function.

title: Invertibility of the cosine transform on smooth even functions
description: For d≥3, the spherical cosine transform is a bijection ofC∞ even functions onS^{d−1} onto itself, where even meansf(−u)=f(u).

title: Weak compactness of bounded positive measures on a compact metric space
description: A sequence of finite positive measures on a compact metric space with uniformly bounded total masses has a subsequence converging weakly against continuous functions to a finite positive measure.

title: Real Stone–Weierstrass theorem
description: A unital real subalgebra of the continuous real functions on a compact Hausdorff space is uniformly dense if it separates points.

title: Generating-measure representation theorem for symmetric zonoids
description: An origin-symmetric convex body is a zonoid exactly when it has a finite even positive generating measure on the unit sphere. That generating measure is unique.

title: Smooth symmetric support functions are generalized zonoids
description: An origin-symmetric convex body withC∞ support function is a generalized zonoid: h_K=Cν for a finite even signed measureν, equivalentlyK+M=L for symmetric zonoidsL,M.

title: Determinant formula for the volume of a zonotope
description: The volume of∑_{i=1}^m[−v_i,v_i] inℝᵈ is2ᵈ∑_{1≤i₁<⋯<i_d≤m}|det(v_{i₁},…,v_{i_d})|.

title: Weak convergence of products of finite compact-space measures
description: If finite positive measuresµ_n converge weakly toµ on a compact metric space, their fixed finite product powersµ_n^⊗d converge weakly toµ^⊗d.

title: Hausdorff continuity of convex-body volume
description: If convex compact sets inℝᵈ converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex compact set, theird-dimensional volumes converge.

title: Determinant-integral formula for zonoid volume
description: For a full-dimensional symmetric zonoidZ with generating measureµ defined byh_Z(u)=∫|u·v|dµ(v), |Z|=(2ᵈ/d!)∫⋯∫|det(v₁,…,v_d)|dµ(v₁)⋯dµ(v_d).

title: Surface-area density from a support-function Hessian
description: For aC² support functionh of a strictly convex body, with∇²_Sh+hI positive definite on each tangent space, its surface-area density isdet(∇²_Sh+hI) relative to spherical area.

title: Andréief–Cauchy–Binet determinant identity for rank-one integrals
description: For an integrable rank-one covariance matrixM=∫vvᵀdν(v) inℝ^m, detM=(1/m!)∫⋯∫det(v₁,…,v_m)²dν(v₁)⋯dν(v_m), whenν is finite with bounded support.

title: Minkowski existence and stability theorem for surface-area measures
description: A finite positive measure onS^{d−1} with centroid zero and not concentrated on a great subsphere is the surface-area measure of a convex body, uniquely up to translation. Weak convergence of such measures to a measure satisfying the same nondegeneracy condition gives Hausdorff convergence of suitably translated bodies.

title: Preservation of spherical integrals by equatorial averaging
description: For an integrable functiong onS^{d−1}, the normalized spherical Radon transform satisfies∫Rg dσ=∫g dσ, with probability-normalized spherical area.

title: Weil’s formula for bounded curvature densities of projection bodies
description: For d≥3 and a convex bodyK with bounded surface-area densityf_K relative to unnormalized spherical area, ΠK has density f_ΠK(u)=(1/(d−1)!)∫_{(S^{d−1}∩u⊥)^{d−1}}det_{u⊥}(v₁,…,v_{d−1})²∏_jf_K(v_j)dℋ^{d−2}(v_j), for almost everyu.

title: Jacobian of an invertible linear map followed by radial normalization
description: ForB∈GL(d), the sphere mapu↦Bu/|Bu| has spherical Jacobian|detB|/|Bu|ᵈ.

title: Surface-area measure under an invertible linear map
description: IfA∈GL(d), surface-area measure transforms by the normal mapu↦A^(−T)u/|A^(−T)u| with weight|detA||A^(−T)u|. Equivalently integrate a test functiong againstS_AK by integratingg of that normal map times the weight againstS_K.

title: Curvature density under an invertible linear map
description: ForA∈GL(d) and a convex bodyK with surface-area densityf_K, f_AK(v)=|detA|²|Aᵀv|^(−d−1) f_K(Aᵀv/|Aᵀv|) almost everywhere onS^{d−1}.

title: Finite-volume Gibbs probability density
description: For a reference measure m and measurable energy H with0<Z=∫exp(−H)dm<∞, the Gibbs probability measure has density Z⁻¹exp(−H) relative to m. Finite-volume particle configurations commonly use Lebesgue measure or a finite-volume Poisson law as reference.

title: Pair potential for a continuum particle system
description: A symmetric measurable function Ψ(x,y) with values in ℝ∪{+∞}, assigning interaction energy to a pair of particle positions. The energy of a finite configuration sums Ψ over its unordered distinct-particle pairs.

title: Canonical Gibbs specification for a continuum point process
description: A point process satisfies the canonical Gibbs specification for self-potentialΦ and pair potentialΨ if, conditional on the outside configurationη and exactly n particles in a bounded regionΛ, its inside positions have a Lebesgue Gibbs density proportional to exp(−∑_iΦ(x_i)−∑_{i<j}Ψ(x_i,x_j)−∑_i∑_{y∈η}Ψ(x_i,y)). The cross sums and positive finite normalizer must exist for almost every conditioning configuration; particle labels are quotiented out.

title: Lennard–Jones6–12 pair potential
description: The radial pair potential Ψ(x,y)=A|x−y|⁻¹²−B|x−y|⁻⁶ for A,B>0 and x≠y, with Ψ(x,x)=+∞. The inverse-twelfth-power term is repulsive and the inverse-sixth-power term attractive.

title: Repulsive Riesz pair potential
description: For s>0, the Euclidean pair potential Ψ(x,y)=|x−y|^{−s}, with value+∞ on the diagonal. The particle example in Esaki assumes s>d, which controls its long-distance tail.

title: Infinite Ginibre point process
description: The determinantal point process on ℂ with respect to planar Lebesgue measure and kernel K(z,w)=π⁻¹exp(z w̄−(|z|²+|w|²)/2). Its intensity is1/π; this fixes the spatial normalization.

title: Regular symmetric stable-like form with measurable variable order
description: Let α:ℝᵈ→(0,2) be measurable, with α⁻¹,(2−α)⁻¹ locally integrable and∫_{|x|>R}|x|^{−d−α(x)}dx<∞ for some R>1. Set J(x,y)=(|x−y|^{−d−α(x)}+|x−y|^{−d−α(y)})/2. The form E(u,v)=½∬(u(x)−u(y))(v(x)−v(y))J(x,y)dxdy on compactly supported Lipschitz functions is closable inL²; its closure is a regular symmetric Dirichlet form.

title: Handelman–Roy closed-complementary-face unperforation criterion
description: Let (G,u) be a dimension group, U a family of normalized traces, H=ker_G U and F=Z(H)⊂S(G,u), the traces vanishing on H. If F is a face whose complementary face is closed, then the quotient-ordered group G/H is unperforated; if G is simple, the quotient is a simple dimension group. Here complementary means the disjoint face giving the unique convex decomposition of each point between the two faces; the degenerate zero quotient is understood separately.

title: Good subset of a trace simplex
description: A subset U of the normalized trace simplex K is good if, whenever nonnegative continuous affine functions a,b satisfy a<b at every point of U, there is a nonnegative continuous affine a′ on K with a′|U=a|U and a′<b everywhere on K.

title: Handelman–Roy refinability criterion for finite-trace dimension groups
description: Let (G,u) be a simple dimension group whose normalized trace simplex K is finite-dimensional, and let τ be a trace. Put H=kerτ and Z={σ∈K:σ(H)=0}. Then τ is refinable exactly when G/H is unperforated, Z is a good subset of K, and the closure of the affine-evaluation image of H is the space of continuous affine functions on K vanishing on Z. In this situation τ is good exactly when it is refinable and Z={τ}.

title: Free abelian group
description: An abelian group with a family of elements such that every group element is a unique finite integer linear combination of them; the number of basis elements is its rank.

title: Critical dimension group
description: A dense free abelian subgroup of rank n+1 in R^n, equipped with the strict ordering whose positive cone is0 together with the vectors having every coordinate positive. It is regarded as an ordered group with that specified embedding and ordering.

title: Refinable traces on critical dimension groups
description: For a critical dimension group of rank n+1 with n≥2, a trace τ is refinable exactly when kerτ={0}.

title: Benatar’s pair-correlation bound for Maynard–Tao sieve weights
description: There are absolute δ>1/4 and σ>0 such that, for ψ(k)→0 with ψ(k)logk→∞ and all large k, a fixed admissible k-tuple admits smooth Maynard–Tao weights of level N^δ supported on the σ-simplex. Under the probability law proportional to their squared divisor sum on an admissible residue class n≤N, P(n+h_i prime)=(1+o_k(1))δψ(k)logk/k and, for i≠j, P(n+h_i,n+h_j prime)≤(1+o_k(1))δψ(k)²(logk)²/k², with N→∞ first. This is an off-diagonal bound; the diagonal terms are retained when computing a full second moment.

title: Coefficientwise congruence of formal series
description: Two formal series with coefficients in a commutative ring R are congruent modulo an ideal I when every pair of corresponding coefficients differs by an element of I. Reduction applies R→R/I to each coefficient.

title: Kernel of the genus-two Witt operator modulo2 and3
description: Let p=2 or3 and k≥0 be even; use Igusa’s integral generators and reduced forms over Z_(p). If12∤k, kerW̄_k=X̄₁₀M̄_(k−10). If k=12n, put e=4,E=X₄₈ for p=2 and e=3,E=X₃₆ for p=3. For each0≤i≤n not divisible by e, write i=es+t with1≤t<e and set m_i=X₁₂^t E^s Y₁₂^(n−i). Then kerW̄_k=(⊕_i F_p m̄_i)⊕X̄₁₀M̄_(k−10). Moreover for12|k, W(f)≡W″(f)≡0 modp implies f≡X₁₀²g modp for some g of weight k−20. Negative-weight spaces are zero.

title: Multiplicative saturation of a subspace
description: For a finite-dimensional subspace S⊂L of a field extension L/F with1∈S and an F-subspace X, its S-saturation is {x∈L:xS⊂XS}, where XS is the F-span of products. X is S-saturated when it equals this subspace.

title: Boundary-minimizing multiplicative linear kernel
description: For fixed S and an attained finite value λ, a linear kernel is a finite-dimensional S-saturated subspace of minimum dimension among such subspaces satisfying dim(XS)−dimX=λ. In the source an i-kernel refers to the i-th increasing attained boundary value. This is unrelated to the kernel of a linear map.

title: Subfield chain of multiplicative linear kernels
description: Let1∈S⊂L generate L over F, with S finite-dimensional, S≠L and {x:xS⊂S}=F. Suppose some nonzero finite-dimensional T has ST≠L and dimST<dimS+dimT−1. List the positive attained saturated-subspace boundary values below dimS as λ₁<⋯<λ_n. The minimum-dimensional kernels containing1 are unique subfields F₁⊋⋯⊋F_n=F, and every finite-dimensional S-saturated X of boundary λ_i satisfies XF_i=X.

title: Probability kernel between measurable spaces
description: A probability kernel from(S,Σ) to(E,ℰ) assigns a probability measure K(s,·) onE to each s∈S, with s↦K(s,A) Σ-measurable for every A∈ℰ. A random probability measure is such a kernel with a probability space as its domain.

title: Stable convergence of random probability kernels
description: For probability kernels K_n,K on a fixed probability space(Ω,F,P) with Polish targetE, K_n converges stably toK if E[a(ω)∫f(x)K_n(ω,dx)]→E[a(ω)∫f(x)K(ω,dx)] for every bounded F-measurable a and every bounded continuous f onE. The base probabilityP stays fixed.

title: Borel isomorphism theorem for standard Borel spaces
description: Every measurable space arising as the Borel sets of a Polish space is measurably isomorphic to a Borel subset of[0,1]. Its measurable bijection and inverse both preserve Borel measurability.

title: Radon–Nikodym theorem for finite measures
description: If finite positive measuresν,μ on one measurable space satisfyν≪μ, there is a nonnegative integrable f withν(A)=∫_Af,dμ for every measurableA, unique up toμ-null sets.

title: Probability measure determined by a distribution function
description: Every nondecreasing right-continuous F:ℝ→[0,1] with limits0 at−∞ and1 at+∞ is the distribution function of a unique Borel probability measure, characterized byμ((−∞,x])=F(x).

title: Banach–Alaoglu theorem
description: The unit ball of the continuous dual of a normed space is compact for pointwise convergence on that space, the weak-* topology. If the normed space is separable, this compact topology on the dual ball is metrizable and every bounded sequence has a weak-* convergent subsequence.

title: Duality of L¹ and L∞ for a finite measure
description: For a finite measureμ, every bounded linear functional on realL¹(μ) is uniquely integration against an element ofL∞(μ), and its operator norm is that element’s essential supremum norm.

title: Regular conditional distribution for a Polish-valued random variable
description: If X takes values in a Polish spaceE and G⊆F is a sub-σ-algebra, there is a G-measurable probability kernel K(ω,·) with∫f,dK(ω)=E[f(X)|G](ω) almost surely for every bounded Borel f. It is unique up to a common null set. Equivalently a probability measure on a product with Polish second factor disintegrates into its first marginal and such conditional probabilities.

title: Stable compactness of random probability kernels with tight mean laws
description: Let K_n be probability kernels on one probability space with Polish targetE. If their mean probability measuresν_n(A)=E[K_n(ω,A)] form a tight family, then some subsequence converges stably to a probability kernelK on the same base space.

title: Multivalued Skorohod problem for a convex subdifferential
description: For proper lower semicontinuous convex η:ℝᵈ→(−∞,∞], continuous w with w₀=0 and x∈closure(dom∂η), find continuous X and K, K₀=0, K locally of bounded variation, with X=x+w−K in closure(dom∂η) and∫_sᵗ⟨X_r−a,dK_r−a*dr⟩≥0 for every(a,a*)∈graph∂η and s≤t. For an indicator of a closed convex set, this is normal reflection.

title: Moreau–Yosida envelope and proximal map of a convex function
description: For proper lower semicontinuous convex η onℝᵈ andλ>0, η_λ(x)=inf_y{η(y)+|x−y|²/(2λ)}. The unique minimizer is prox_{λη}(x), and∇η_λ(x)=(x−prox_{λη}(x))/λ is globally Lipschitz; it approximates the maximal monotone subdifferential.

title: Helly selection theorem for bounded-variation functions
description: A sequence of real functions on a compact interval with uniformly bounded sup norms and total variations has a pointwise convergent subsequence with bounded-variation limit. The finite-dimensional vector version follows componentwise; uniform convergence needs additional continuity/oscillation control.

title: Arzelà–Ascoli theorem for Euclidean-valued paths
description: A uniformly bounded equicontinuous family inC([0,T];ℝᵈ) is relatively compact in the uniform norm.

title: Picard–Lindelöf theorem for a time-dependent Euclidean ODE
description: A vector field continuous in time and locally Lipschitz in the state has a unique local solution through each initial point, with continuous dependence on initial data and the field on compact sets. If the state stays in a compact set on each finite interval, the solution extends globally; globally Lipschitz fields of linear growth satisfy this condition.

title: One-dimensional regularity of convex functions
description: A finite convex function on an open real interval is locally Lipschitz. Its left and right derivatives exist and are monotone, disagree at at most countably many points, and equal its ordinary derivative almost everywhere.

title: Occupation-time formula for continuous semimartingales
description: A real continuous semimartingale X has local timesL_t^a with∫₀ᵗg(X_s)d[X]_s=∫_ℝg(a)L_t^a da for nonnegative Borel g. In particular if[X]_t=t, it spends zero Lebesgue time in any Lebesgue-null spatial set.

title: Finite speed measure and mixing of a one-dimensional diffusion
description: For a conservative irreducible regular diffusion on an interval with interior generator½f″+qf′ and instantaneous reflection at any regular included endpoint, the speed density is2exp(2∫q). If its total mass is finite, its normalization is the unique invariant probability measure and transition laws converge to it in total variation. Entrance or inaccessible endpoints contribute no boundary holding atom.

title: Uniform convergence after undoing a monotone clock
description: Let τ_n:[0,∞)→[0,∞) be increasing homeomorphisms fixing0, converging locally uniformly to a continuous nondecreasing unboundedτ, and let continuous y_n converge locally uniformly to y. If y is constant on each level interval ofτ, then x(t)=y(s) forτ(s)=t is well-defined and continuous, and y_n∘τ_n⁻¹ converges to x uniformly on compact intervals.

title: Cépa’s well-posedness theorem for multivalued Skorohod equations
description: Let η be proper lower semicontinuous convex onℝᵈ with int(dom∂η) nonempty and b globally Lipschitz. For every x∈closure(dom∂η) and continuous w with w₀=0, X=x+w+∫₀^.b(X_s)ds−K has a unique solution in the multivalued Skorohod sense. The map(x,w)↦X is continuous for uniform convergence on compact time intervals. Brownian inputs therefore define a continuous random dynamical system on closure(dom∂η).

title: Mixing of bounded one-dimensional convex stochastic inclusions
description: Let η:ℝ→(−∞,∞] be proper lower semicontinuous convex with bounded domain and int(dom∂η) nonempty, and let b∈C² have bounded derivatives. The solution of dX+∂η(X)dt∋b(X)dt+dW has a unique invariant probability, with density proportional to exp(2∫_{x₀}^x b(s)ds−2η(x)) on int(domη), and its laws converge in total variation from every state in closure(dom∂η).

title: Mixing of a dissipative one-dimensional additive Brownian SDE
description: If b is locally Lipschitz onℝ and xb(x)≤C−cx² for c>0, the solution of dX=b(X)dt+dW is nonexplosive, has unique invariant density proportional to exp(2∫₀^x b(s)ds), and its transition laws converge to that density in total variation from every starting point.

title: Finite-mixture approximate independence of finite-spin cube measures
description: For every finite spin set Ω, ε>0 and integer k≥2, there is η>0 such that every probability law µ on Ωⁿ with sufficiently large n has disjoint events S₁,…,S_N, each of mass at least η and together of mass at least1−ε, for which the conditional joint law at k uniformly sampled coordinates has expected total variation distance less than ε from the product of its conditional one-coordinate marginals. The number N is at most1/η.

title: Random continuous tests for stable convergence of probability kernels
description: If probability kernels µ_n on a Polish space converge stably to µ, then E∫F(ω,x)µ_n(ω,dx)→E∫F(ω,x)µ(ω,dx) for every jointly measurable F continuous in x with E sup_x|F(ω,x)|<∞. Stable convergence means convergence first for tests a(ω)f(x), with a bounded measurable and f bounded continuous.

title: Invariant random measure for a weakly mixing continuous random dynamical system
description: Let φ be a continuous random dynamical system on a Polish state space over a measure-preserving two-sided noise shift. If its one-point laws converge weakly to µ for µ-almost every initial point, then there is a random probability measure π measurable for the past generated by all solution maps ending no later than time0, with Eπ=µ and φ_t(ω)_*π_ω=π_{θ_tω} almost surely for each t≥0. Independent noise increments are not required.

title: Periodic Sobolev space H² on the circle
description: H²(S¹) consists of2π-periodic L² functions whose first and second distributional derivatives, tested against smooth periodic functions, are also in L². Functions are identified almost everywhere; the sum of the three squared L² norms defines its norm.

title: Continuity of the stochastic heat convolution on the circle
description: For space-time white noise on S¹, Z_t=∫₀ᵗe^{(t−s)∂ₓ²}dW_s has a version jointly continuous in(t,x) on every compact time interval times S¹, starting from0. Thus t↦Z_t is continuous with values in C(S¹) in the supremum norm.

title: Comparison principle for scalar periodic parabolic equations
description: Let F₁≤F₂ be continuous real functions on [0,T]×S¹×ℝ, one of them locally Lipschitz in u uniformly in (t,x). Let u,v be essentially bounded functions in L²(0,T;H¹(S¹))∩C([0,T];L²(S¹)) with weak time derivatives in L²(0,T;H¹(S¹)*) for the Gelfand triple H¹(S¹)⊂L²(S¹)⊂H¹(S¹)*, solving u_t=u_xx+F₁(t,x,u) and v_t=v_xx+F₂(t,x,v) weakly against H¹(S¹) test functions for almost every t. If u(0)≤v(0) almost everywhere, then u(t)≤v(t) almost everywhere for every t∈[0,T]. Bounded classical solutions are a special case.

title: Existence for a smooth-forced parabolic double-obstacle problem
description: For fixed H²(S¹) walls h₁<h₂, Lipschitz f, smooth forcing and smooth initial data between the walls, the periodic equation u_t=u_xx+f(u)+forcing with lower and upper normal reflection has a unique continuous variational solution. The normal corrections satisfy the two complementarity conditions; the solution is obtained by lower/upper penalty limits.

title: Supremum stability of the parabolic double-obstacle solution map
description: For fixed strictly separated continuous walls on the circle and Lipschitz drift f, subtract a continuous free driving field v from a reflected heat solution and write the remainder z. On each finite interval, changing v and the initial data changes z by at most C_T times their supremum-norm changes. The same estimate holds uniformly for the lower and upper penalized equations, independently of the penalty parameters.

title: Nualart–Pardoux well-posedness for a one-wall stochastic heat equation
description: On a one-dimensional compact interval with compatible Dirichlet boundary data, a regular lower obstacle and globally Lipschitz drift, the additive space-time-white-noise heat equation with normal reflection above that obstacle has a unique continuous adapted solution. It is the increasing limit of lower-penalty equations, with a positive complementarity measure locally finite away from the spatial boundary.

title: Skorohod representation theorem on a Polish space
description: If probability measures µ_n converge weakly to µ on a Polish space, they can be realized as laws of random variables X_n,X on one probability space with X_n→X almost surely.

title: Dambis–Dubins–Schwarz time-change theorem
description: A real continuous local martingale M starting at0 can be represented as B_{⟨M⟩_t} for a Brownian motion on its quadratic-variation clock, after extension by independent Brownian noise if the terminal bracket is finite.

title: Lévy characterization of Brownian motion
description: A continuous real local martingale starting at0 with quadratic variation t is Brownian motion relative to its filtration. The vector version requires bracket matrix tI.

title: Coupling inequality for total variation
description: For any coupling(X,Y) of probability measures µ and ν on the same measurable space, d_TV(µ,ν)≤P(X≠Y). On a standard Borel space the equality event is measurable.

title: Dobrushin contraction theorem for a Markov kernel
