description: For a Markov kernel K on a standard Borel space, let δ(K)=sup_{x,y}d_TV(K(x,·),K(y,·)). If δ(K)<1, then µ↦µK is a δ(K)-contraction in total variation on probability measures, has a unique fixed probability π, and d_TV(Kⁿ(x,·),π)≤δ(K)ⁿ.

title: Well-posedness and continuous cocycle for the periodic heat equation with two walls
description: For h₁,h₂∈H²(S¹) with h₁<h₂, globally Lipschitz f and continuous initial g between the walls, the additive-white-noise stochastic heat equation with the two normal reflection measures has a unique continuous adapted solution. On canonical two-sided white noise these solutions define a continuous random dynamical system on {g∈C(S¹):h₁≤g≤h₂}.

title: Comparison for the periodic heat equation with two reflecting walls
description: For fixed H²(S¹) walls h₁<h₂ and Lipschitz f, two reflected stochastic heat solutions driven by the same additive space-time white noise preserve pointwise order of their initial states. The order holds simultaneously for all nonnegative times on the pathwise continuous version.

title: Total-variation mixing for the periodic stochastic heat equation with two walls
description: With strictly separated H²(S¹) walls, globally Lipschitz drift and unit additive space-time white noise, the reflected heat equation has a unique invariant probability on its continuous state space, and transition laws converge to it in total variation from every initial state between the walls.

title: Coordinate support relative to a Schauder basis
description: For x=∑a_i e_i in a Banach space with a specified Schauder basis, supp_e(x)={i:a_i≠0}. The support of a subspace is the union of its vectors’ coordinate supports. These supports need not be finite.

title: Seminormalized sequence in a normed space
description: A sequence(x_n) for which0<inf_n∥x_n∥≤sup_n∥x_n∥<∞.

title: Equidistributed finitely supported basis vectors
description: Two finitely supported vectors relative to specified ordered bases are equidistributed when the increasing bijection between their nonzero coordinate supports preserves every coefficient. This means the same ordered coefficient pattern, not equality of probability laws.

title: Diagonal-free operator on a fixed block subspace
description: A bounded operatorT:[x_n]→X, with(x_n) a fixed block sequence of a specified ambient Schauder basis(e_i), is diagonal-free when supp_e(Tx_n)∩supp_e(x_n)=∅ for every n. This depends on the chosen ambient basis and block sequence.

title: Gowers–Maurey rapidly increasing sequence of ℓ₁ averages
description: Fix ε>0, ε′=min(ε,1), f(t)=log₂(t+1), and M(t)=2^(36t²)−1. A finite successive sequencex₁,…,x_N is rapidly increasing with constant1+ε when∥x_k∥=1 and x_k is a sum of n_k successive vectors of norms≤(1+ε)/n_k, with n₁≥4(1+ε)log(2)M(N/ε′)/ε′ and(ε′/2)√f(n_k)≥|supp(x_(k−1))| for k≥2. This is the original quantitative convention for these spaces.

title: Existence of arbitrarily long ℓ₁ averages in Gowers’s unconditional space
description: For every block subspace ofX_U, every integer n≥1 and every c>1, there is an ℓ₁ⁿ block average with constantc in that subspace.

title: Gowers’s disjoint-support separation estimates
description: InX_U, let(u_n),(v_n) be seminormalized block sequences with all supports of theu_n disjoint from all supports of thev_n, and letv_n be ℓ₁ⁿ averages with a common constant. There are successive finite setsJ_k and common coefficientsa_n with∥∑_{J_k}a_nu_n∥=1 and∥∑_{J_k}a_nv_n∥→0. Also, for any basis subsequence(e_(i_n)) with infinite complement there are normalized successive combinationsw_k=∑_{J_k}a_ne_(i_n) whose equidistributed copies∑_{J_k}a_ne_(j_n) have norms tending to0 uniformly over increasing sequences(j_n) disjoint from{i_n}.

title: Schlumprecht spreading model of Gowers’s unconditional basis
description: The unit vector basis ofX_U generates the unit vector basis ofSchlumprecht’s spaceS as a spreading model: for every finite scalar pattern(a_i), its iterated asymptotic norm along increasing basis indices is∥∑a_ie_i∥_S.

title: Coherent disjoint ℓ∞ configurations in Schlumprecht’s space
description: For every0<ε<1/8 there are increasing integersp_j such that, for everyn, one can choose disjointly supported vectorsv₁,…,v_n inS, eachv_j equidistributed with(f(p_j)/p_j)∑_{i=1}^{p_j}e_i, and every tail sum∑_{j=k}^n v_j has norm≤1+ε. The same sequence(p_j) works for alln.

title: Kutzarova–Lin ℓ₁ spreading model in Schlumprecht’s space
description: Schlumprecht’s spaceS contains a seminormalized block sequence generating a spreading model equivalent to the unit vector basis ofℓ₁.

title: Uniform boundedness of Schauder partial-sum projections
description: For a Schauder basis(e_i) of a Banach space, the partial-sum operatorsP_n(∑a_ie_i)=∑_{i≤n}a_ie_i are uniformly bounded. Each coordinate functional is continuous; normalized block sequences consequently have uniformly bounded coordinate functionals on their closed spans.

title: Small perturbation principle for basic sequences
description: Let(x_n) be a basic sequence with continuous coordinate functionalsx_n*. If∑∥x_n*∥∥x_n−y_n∥<1, thenx_n↦y_n extends to an isomorphism between their closed spans.

title: Bessaga–Pełczyński selection principle
description: In a Banach space with a Schauder basis, every seminormalized weakly null sequence has a subsequence equivalent to a seminormalized block sequence; the block vectors can be chosen to approximate that subsequence with any prescribed summable positive error bounds.

title: Norm closure of compact operators
description: An operator-norm limit of compact linear maps between Banach spaces is compact.

title: Compact restriction of a strictly singular operator to a further block subspace
description: IfS:[x_n]→Y is strictly singular on a block subspace of a Banach space with basis, then[x_n] contains a further normalized block sequence(u_k) such thatS|[u_k] is compact.

title: Arbitrarily small restrictions of a strictly singular operator
description: For a strictly singular mapS:X→Y between Banach spaces, every infinite-dimensional closed subspaceM⊂X andε>0 contain an infinite-dimensional closedN⊂M with∥S|N∥<ε.

title: Closed operator ideal of strictly singular maps
description: Strictly singular bounded maps between Banach spaces are closed under operator-norm limits, sums with the same domain and codomain, and composition on either side by bounded linear maps.

title: Diagonal/strictly-singular/diagonal-free decomposition in tight-by-support spaces
description: LetX have a tight-by-support unconditional basis andT:[x_n]→X be bounded on a block subspace. ThenT=D|[x_n]+S+R withD bounded diagonal,S strictly singular andR diagonal-free relative to(x_n). Ifsupp(Tx_n)∩supp(x_m)=∅ for n≠m, one may takeR=0.

title: Scalar-plus-strictly-singular block restriction in tight-by-support spaces
description: IfX has a tight-by-support unconditional basis andT:[x_n]→X is bounded on a block subspace, there are an infinite-dimensional further block subspaceW, a scalarλ and a strictly singularS:[x_n]→X withT|W=λId|W+S|W. Consequently any two isomorphic infinite-dimensional subspaces ofX have unit spheres at distance0.

title: Compact operators are strictly singular
description: A compact linear operator between Banach spaces is strictly singular.

title: Diagonal-plus-strictly-singular decomposition on Gowers block subspaces
description: For every block subspaceY ofX_U, any boundedT:Y→X_U hasT=D|Y+S, withD a bounded diagonal operator onX_U andS strictly singular. In particular every bounded operator diagonal-free relative to a fixed block basis ofY is strictly singular.

title: Block approximation of an infinite-dimensional subspace
description: LetX have a Schauder basis andM⊂X be an infinite-dimensional closed subspace. For any positive summable error boundsε_n, one can choose unit vectorsv_n∈M and successive finite block vectorsu_n with∥v_n−u_n∥<ε_n; the errors can be made small enough that(v_n) and(u_n) are equivalent basic sequences.

title: C*-algebra-valued variance bound for finite module covariance
description: Letp_i≥0 sum to1 andx_i,y_i lie in a semi-inner-productC*-module. Putx̄=∑p_ix_i,ȳ=∑p_iy_i,G=∑p_i⟨x_i,y_i⟩−⟨x̄,ȳ⟩, V_x=∑p_i⟨x_i−x̄,x_i−x̄⟩ andV_y similarly. Then|G|²≤∥V_x∥V_y in theC*-algebra order. In particular, for anya,b, |G|²≤(∑p_i∥x_i−a∥²)(∑p_i|y_i−b|²).

title: C*-algebra-valued Grüss bound after a module projection
description: In an inner-productC*-module, let⟨e,e⟩ be idempotent. Forx,y∈X and anya,b∈A, |⟨x,y⟩−⟨x,e⟩⟨e,y⟩|²≤∥x−ea∥² |y−eb|² in the order ofA. Equivalently, taking positive square roots gives the corresponding unsquared bound.

title: Order monotonicity of positive square roots
description: For positive elementsa≤b of aC*-algebra, a^(1/2)≤b^(1/2).

title: Balanced error rate for surface-perturbed Tikhonov regularization
description: For the transported surface Tikhonov problem with uniformly regular parametrizations, letη=ρ+γ+δ>0 tend to0, whereρ is operator error,γ isC² surface error andδ is data error. Assume uniformly equivalent transported norms, O(γ) errors in the quadratic penalty forms and normal projections, joint coercivity∥h∥²_H¹≤C(∥Fh∥²+∥P_nh∥²+|h|²_H¹), and a variational quadratic source condition at the exact tangent solutionx†. Ifα is comparable toη, the pulled-back minimizers satisfy∥x̂_(σ,α,δ)−x†∥²_H¹=O(η).

title: Doubling cube gauge
description: A positive measurable function φ(x,r) on ℝⁿ×(0,∞), viewed as a weight of the cube centered at x with side r, is doubling if φ(x,2r) is comparable to φ(x,r), uniformly in x,r. Write c̃₁⁻¹≤φ(x,r)/φ(x,2r)≤c₁; neither chosen constant must be at least one.

title: Locally comparable cube gauge
description: A positive measurable cube gauge φ(x,r) is locally comparable if some C≥1 satisfies C⁻¹≤φ(x,r)/φ(y,r)≤C whenever |x−y|≤r. It compares cubes of the same size at nearby centers.

title: Admissible Schwartz pair for an inhomogeneous dyadic resolution
description: An admissible pair (ϕ,Φ) consists of Schwartz functions with supp ϕ̂⊂{1/2≤|ξ|≤2}, |ϕ̂| bounded below on {3/5≤|ξ|≤5/3}, supp Φ̂⊂{|ξ|≤2}, and |Φ̂| bounded below on {|ξ|≤5/3}. Its inhomogeneous family is Φ at scale0 and ϕⱼ(x)=2ʲⁿϕ(2ʲx) for j≥1.

title: Vanishing polynomial moments of a Euclidean function
description: An integrable function with the required weighted integrability has vanishing moments of order below L if ∫xᵅf(x)dx=0 for every multi-index α with |α|<L. Here L is a nonnegative integer; L=0 imposes no moment conditions.

title: Almost orthogonality of dyadically dilated Schwartz kernels
description: If φ,ψ∈S(ℝⁿ) both have vanishing moments below the integer L≥0 and φⱼ(x)=2ʲⁿφ(2ʲx), ψₖ(x)=2ᵏⁿψ(2ᵏx), then for every M>0, |φⱼ*ψₖ(x)|≤C2^{−L|j−k|}2^{n min(j,k)}(1+2^min(j,k)|x|)⁻ᴹ. For j≥k only φ needs the moment condition; for k≥j only ψ does. Constants may depend on the fixed kernels, L,M,n, but not j,k,x.

title: Peetre maximal estimate by dyadic local means
description: Fix an admissible inhomogeneous Schwartz resolution (Φⱼ), a>0, r>0 and an integer N≥a. For f∈S′ and ℓ≥0, [sup_z |Φℓ*f(x+z)|/(1+2^ℓ|z|)^a]^r≤C∑_{v≥0}2⁻ᵛᴺʳ2⁽ᵛ⁺ℓ⁾ⁿ∫|Φᵥ₊ℓ*f(y)|^r/(1+2^ℓ|x−y|)^{ar}dy. The constant depends on the fixed resolution and parameters, not f,ℓ,x; an infinite right side is allowed.

title: Peetre submean inequality for band-limited functions
description: For r>0 and m>n there is C such that every tempered distribution g with Fourier support in {|ξ|≤2^{ν+1}}, ν≥0, satisfies |g(x)|≤C[ηᵥ,ₘ*|g|^r(x)]^{1/r}, where ηᵥ,ₘ(x)=2^{νn}(1+2^ν|x|)⁻ᵐ. The band-limited distribution is represented by a smooth function; C is independent of g,ν,x.

title: Characteristic-function norm estimates in variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: Let 0<p⁻≤p⁺<∞ and p be globally log-Hölder. For a cube Q, ∥χ_Q∥_{p(·)}≈|Q|^{1/p(x)} for |Q|≤1 and x∈Q, and ≈|Q|^{1/p∞} for |Q|≥1. If Q₁⊂Q₂, their norm ratio lies between constant multiples of (|Q₁|/|Q₂|)^{1/p⁻} and (|Q₁|/|Q₂|)^{1/p⁺}. If p⁻>1, ∥χ_Q∥_{p(·)}∥χ_Q∥_{p′(·)}≈|Q|.

title: Embedding of variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces with a common limit at infinity
description: If globally log-Hölder exponents p₁,p₂ have positive finite lower and upper bounds, p₁≤p₂, and the same limit p∞ at infinity, then L^{p₂(·)}(ℝⁿ) continuously embeds into L^{p₁(·)}(ℝⁿ).

title: Log-Hölder extension from a coordinate hyperplane
description: Every bounded globally log-Hölder real function g on ℝⁿ⁻¹ extends to a globally log-Hölder function on ℝⁿ with the same limit at infinity and values between inf g and sup g. For any prescribed A>0, the extension may be chosen equal to g(x′) throughout the strip |t|≤A.

title: Dual norm formula in variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: For measurable p with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞ and p′=p/(p−1), the associate norm sup{∫|fg|:∥g∥_{p′(·)}≤1} lies between ∥f∥_{p(·)} and 2∥f∥_{p(·)}. This formula is valid also for a measurable f whose norm is initially allowed to be infinite.

title: Power triangle inequality in variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: For a bounded positive measurable exponent p and 0<r≤min(1,p⁻), the Luxemburg quasi-norm satisfies ∥∑ᵢfᵢ∥_{p(·)}^r≤∑ᵢ∥fᵢ∥_{p(·)}^r for every finite family; the analogous countable inequality holds whenever the sum of the pointwise absolute values defines a measurable function.

title: Muckenhoupt A₁ weight
description: A locally integrable function w>0 almost everywhere is an A₁ weight if the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function satisfies Mw≤Cw almost everywhere. Its A₁ constant is the least such C.

title: A₁ extrapolation into variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: Let p be globally log-Hölder with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞. If a family of nonnegative measurable pairs (f,g) satisfies ∥f∥_{L^{r₀}(w)}≤C([w]_{A₁})∥g∥_{L^{r₀}(w)} for every A₁ weight and a fixed 0<r₀<p⁻, then ∥f∥_{p(·)}≤C_p∥g∥_{p(·)} for pairs with finite left norm; the constant is uniform over the family.

title: Weighted inhomogeneous Littlewood–Paley inequality for A₁ weights
description: For a fixed admissible inhomogeneous Schwartz resolution, 1<r<∞ and an A₁ weight w on ℝⁿ, ∥(∑_{j≥0}|ϕⱼ*f|²)^{1/2}∥_{L^r(w)}≈∥f∥_{L^r(w)}. Constants depend on the resolution, r,n and the A₁ constant, not f.

title: Density of compactly supported smooth functions in variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: For globally log-Hölder p with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞, C_c∞(ℝⁿ) is dense in L^{p(·)}(ℝⁿ).

title: Density of compactly supported smooth functions in variable-exponent Triebel–Lizorkin spaces
description: Let 1/p and 1/q be globally log-Hölder (so p,q are bounded and bounded away from 0) and let the smoothness α≥0 be bounded, locally log-Hölder and have a limit at infinity. Then C_c^∞(ℝⁿ) is dense in the unweighted inhomogeneous space F^{α(·)}_{p(·),q(·)}(ℝⁿ).

title: Convolution and Fourier multiplication for a tempered distribution
description: If f is a tempered distribution and ψ is Schwartz, then ψ*f is a smooth function of polynomial growth and its distributional Fourier transform is ψ̂·f̂. Fourier multiplication by a smooth cutoff equal to1 near supp f̂ therefore gives a reproducing convolution kernel.

title: Littlewood–Paley characterization of variable-exponent Lebesgue spaces
description: For globally log-Hölder p with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞ and a fixed admissible inhomogeneous Schwartz resolution, L^{p(·)}(ℝⁿ) consists exactly of the tempered distributions with finite ∥(∑_{j≥0}|ϕⱼ*f|²)^{1/2}∥_{p(·)}, and this square-function norm is equivalent to the Luxemburg norm.

title: Sobolev embedding for cube-weighted variable Triebel–Lizorkin spaces
description: For admissible pᵢ,q,sᵢ,φ, if p₀≤p₁, s₀≥s₁ and s₀−n/p₀=s₁−n/p₁ pointwise, then F^{s₀(·),φ}_{p₀(·),q(·)} continuously embeds into F^{s₁(·),φ}_{p₁(·),q(·)}. If inf(s₀−s₁)>0, the source and target may have different arbitrary admissible sequence exponents q₀,q₁.

title: Atomic and molecular characterization of cube-weighted variable Triebel–Lizorkin spaces
description: For admissible p,q,s,φ, put c̃₁⁻¹≤φ(x,r)/φ(x,2r). If nonnegative integers K>s⁺+max(0,log₂c̃₁) and L>n/min(1,p⁻,q⁻)−n−s⁻, then sufficiently rapidly decaying uniformly normalized (K,L)-molecules synthesize matching dyadic coefficient sequences boundedly into F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)}, with convergence in S′. Conversely every element has a smooth atomic expansion with coefficient quasi-norm bounded by its function-space quasi-norm, with arbitrarily prescribed nonnegative orders K,L; scale0 atoms require no cancellation.

title: Peetre maximal characterization of cube-weighted variable Triebel–Lizorkin spaces
description: For admissible p,q,s,φ, if a>n/min(p⁻,q⁻)+log₂c̃₁+C_log(s), the quasi-norm of F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)} is equivalent to the same cube-wise mixed quasi-norm with each |ϕⱼ*f(x)| replaced by sup_y |ϕⱼ*f(x+y)|/(1+2ʲ|y|)^a. Here c̃₁ is the lower scale-comparison constant in φ(x,r)/φ(x,2r)≥c̃₁⁻¹ and C_log(s) is a local log-Hölder constant.

title: Full-frequency cube norm for variable Triebel–Lizorkin-type spaces
description: For admissible p,q,s,φ with lower scale-comparison constant c̃₁<2^{n/p⁺}, an equivalent quasi-norm of F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)} is obtained by summing all inhomogeneous scales j≥0 inside every dyadic cube, instead of starting at max(0,−log₂ℓ(P)).

title: Variable-exponent Morrey space with a cube gauge
description: For a positive measurable cube gauge φ and a bounded positive exponent p, M_φ^{p(·)}(ℝⁿ) consists of measurable functions modulo almost-everywhere equality for which sup_P φ(P)⁻¹∥fχ_P∥_{L^{p(·)}} is finite; the supremum is over dyadic cubes P. This fixes the cube-gauge convention, which differs from some other generalized Morrey normalizations.

title: Morrey identification of zero-smoothness variable Triebel–Lizorkin-type spaces
description: For globally log-Hölder p with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞ and a doubling locally comparable cube gauge with c̃₁<2^{n/p⁺}, M_φ^{p(·)}(ℝⁿ)=F^{0,φ}_{p(·),2}(ℝⁿ) with equivalent norms.

title: Hyperplane trace theorem for cube-weighted variable Triebel–Lizorkin spaces
description: For admissible p,q,s,φ on ℝⁿ, n≥2, assume s⁻−1/p⁻−(n−1)(1/min(1,p⁻)−1)>0. Write p̄(x′)=p(x′,0), s̄(x′)=s(x′,0), and φ̄(Q′)=φ(Q′×[0,ℓ(Q′))). Restriction extends continuously and surjectively from F^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)}(ℝⁿ) onto F^{s̄(·)−1/p̄(·),φ̄}_{p̄(·),p̄(·)}(ℝⁿ⁻¹); in particular the trace range is independent of q.

title: Normal order cone in a normed space
description: An order on a real normed vector space, compatible with addition and multiplication by nonnegative scalars, has a normal positive cone if some C<∞ satisfies ‖x‖≤C‖y‖ whenever0≤x≤y. Normality bounds the norm diameters of order intervals in terms of their endpoints.

title: Lipschitz composition in W¹,ᵖ
description: For1≤p<∞, u∈W¹,ᵖ(Ω) and Lipschitz F:ℝ→ℝ with F(0)=0, F(u)∈W¹,ᵖ, with its weak gradient given by the almost-everywhere chain rule and bounded in magnitude by Lip(F)|∇u|. If u∈W₀¹,ᵖ then F(u)∈W₀¹,ᵖ. In particular |u| and its positive and negative parts are allowed.

title: Normality of the positive-distribution order on H⁻¹
description: On a bounded smooth domain, H⁻¹=(H₀¹)* with its gradient-dual norm has a normal positive-distribution cone. More precisely, if h≥0 and−h≤w≤h then ‖w‖_{H⁻¹}≤‖h‖_{H⁻¹}; hence the norm diameter of[f,g] is at most‖g−f‖_{H⁻¹}.

title: Maximum principle for a scalar linear parabolic equation
description: A classical supersolution of w_t−∑a_ij(t,x)∂_ijw−∑b_i(t,x)∂_iw−c(t,x)w≥0 on a bounded smooth spatial domain stays nonnegative if its parabolic-boundary values are nonnegative, the symmetric matrix a is positive semidefinite, and the continuous coefficients are bounded on the time interval. An exponential time factor removes any positive upper bound on c.

title: Duality theorem for Lᵖ at a finite reflexive exponent
description: For1<p<∞ and a sigma-finite measure space, every bounded linear functional on Lᵖ is uniquely f↦∫fg for g∈L^{p′},1/p+1/p′=1, and its norm is‖g‖_{p′}.

title: Separability of Lᵖ on a Euclidean domain
description: For1≤p<∞ and a Lebesgue measurable subset Ω of Euclidean space, Lᵖ(Ω) is separable. Rational-valued simple functions built from a countable family of rational boxes, with finite truncations and restriction to Ω, give a countable dense family.

title: Weak subsequences of bounded Lᵖ sequences
description: For1<p<∞ on a bounded Euclidean domain with Lebesgue measure, every norm-bounded sequence in Lᵖ has a weakly convergent subsequence with limit f∈Lᵖ and ‖f‖_p≤liminf‖f_n‖_p along that subsequence.

title: Inverse-potential comparison for a forced porous-medium equation
description: Let u₁,u₂ be bounded variational solutions of ∂_tu=Δ(|u|^{m−1}u)+cu+F on a bounded smooth domain, with m>1, zero Dirichlet conditions and the same smooth forcing F. For R=(−Δ_D)⁻¹, Ru₁(0)≤Ru₂(0) almost everywhere implies Ru₁(t)≤Ru₂(t) for every t≥0.

title: Inverse-Dirichlet order preservation for additive stochastic porous media
description: For the zero-Dirichlet equation dX=[Δ(|X|^{m−1}X)+cX]dt+dW on a bounded smooth domain, m>1 and trace-class H⁻¹-valued additive Wiener noise, set R=(−Δ_D)⁻¹. Two solutions driven by the same noise satisfy RX_t^x≤RX_t^y almost everywhere for every t≥0 whenever Rx≤Ry. This holds on the continuous cocycle version simultaneously in time and initial states.

title: Positive-distribution order preservation for additive stochastic porous media
description: For the zero-Dirichlet additive stochastic porous-medium equation with m>1 and trace-class H⁻¹ noise, solutions driven by the same noise preserve the ordinary positive-distribution order: x≤y implies X_t^x≤X_t^y for every t≥0 on the continuous cocycle version.

title: Marked temporal point process
description: A sequence of positive random event times T₁<T₂<⋯, with no finite accumulation, together with random marks Jₙ in a specified measurable space; the associated counting measure is ∑ₙδ_(Tₙ,Jₙ). Adapted versions require each event time to be a stopping time and its mark to be known at that event.

title: Compensator of a counting process
description: For an adapted càdlàg counting process N with N₀=0, a predictable increasing process A with A₀=0 is a compensator when N−A is a local martingale; the ambient filtration is part of the data.

title: Intensity of a counting process
description: A nonnegative predictable process λ is an intensity for a counting process N when its compensator is A_t=∫₀ᵗλ_s ds, relative to the specified filtration.

title: Time-inhomogeneous continuous-time Markov chain on a finite set
description: A càdlàg finite-state jump process Z for which the conditional distribution of its future given the past through time s depends only on Z_s and the absolute time s; its transition matrices P_(s,t) satisfy P_(s,u)P_(u,t)=P_(s,t).

title: Hazard rate of an absolutely continuous lifetime
description: For a nonnegative lifetime with absolutely continuous distribution function F and survival S=1−F, its hazard rate is h(t)=F′(t)/S(t) wherever S(t)>0; when S(0)=1 this gives S(t)=exp(−∫₀ᵗh(s)ds) on intervals of positive survival.

title: Lebesgue–Stieltjes integral for a càdlàg path of locally bounded variation
description: A real càdlàg path B of locally bounded variation determines a locally finite signed Stieltjes measure dB by dB((s,t])=B_t−B_s; ∫f dB denotes integration against that signed measure whenever f is integrable with respect to its total variation.

title: Cumulative payment process of an insurance policy
description: A stochastic process B of locally bounded variation whose increment B_t−B_s is the net amount paid by a policy during (s,t]; positive payments and premiums may be represented with opposite signs under a declared convention.

title: Expected cashflow rate of an insurance policy
description: If the expected cumulative policy payments A(t)=E[B_t] are locally absolutely continuous, their cashflow rate is a Radon–Nikodym derivative a(t)=dA/dt, defined almost everywhere with respect to time.

title: Expected discounted liability of an insurance policy
description: For cumulative payments B and a specified positive discount factor v(t), the time-zero liability is E[∫₀^∞v(t)dB_t] when this expectation exists; a constant deterministic short rate r gives v(t)=e^(−rt).

title: Absolute convergence of a real series
description: A real series ∑aₙ converges absolutely if ∑|aₙ| is finite; it converges conditionally if ∑aₙ converges and ∑|aₙ| diverges.

title: Irrationality exponent of an irrational real number
description: For an irrational real θ, μ(θ) is the supremum of real μ for which 0<|θ−p/q|<q^(−μ) has infinitely many solutions in integers p and positive integers q; the value may be infinite.

title: Comparison test for nonnegative real series
description: If 0≤aₙ≤bₙ, convergence of ∑bₙ implies convergence of ∑aₙ; divergence of ∑aₙ implies divergence of ∑bₙ.

title: Sum and convergence of a real geometric series
description: For a real r with |r|<1, the geometric series ∑ₙ≥0rⁿ converges absolutely and has sum 1/(1−r).

title: Convergence criterion for a real p-series
description: For p∈ℝ, the nonnegative series ∑ₙ≥1n^(−p) converges exactly when p>1.

title: Improper Riemann integral
description: An improper Riemann integral over an open endpoint or an unbounded interval is a limit of integrals over compact subintervals; with two improper endpoints both limits must exist separately.

title: Gamma function on the positive real axis
description: For s>0, Γ(s)=∫₀∞e^(−t)t^(s−1)dt, with the integral understood as an improper real integral.

title: Real polylogarithm inside the unit interval
description: For s∈ℝ and 0<z<1, Li_s(z)=∑ₙ≥1zⁿ/nˢ; this defines the real restriction of the polylogarithm by its convergent power series.

title: Leading singularity of a real polylogarithm at one
description: For each real s<1, Li_s(z)∼Γ(1−s)(log(1/z))^(s−1) as z→1 from below.

title: Roth’s theorem on irrationality exponents
description: Every irrational real number algebraic over ℚ has irrationality exponent two.

title: Irrationality exponent of e
description: The base e=exp(1) of the natural logarithm has irrationality exponent two.

title: Salikhov’s upper bound for the irrationality exponent of π
description: Put ψ(x)=Γ′(x)/Γ(x) for x>0 and χ=5−ψ(2/5)+ψ(1/3)+log5−(5/2)log2. Let t₃ be the positive real root and t₁ the upper-half-plane root of5t³−381t²−1525t−1875=0, and put h(t)=|t²+6t+25|³|t|^(3/2)/|25−t|⁵. Then the irrationality exponent ofπ satisfies μ(π)≤1−(χ+logh(t₃))/(χ+logh(t₁)), whose right-hand side is approximately7.606308520711.

title: Almost-everywhere value of the irrationality exponent
description: Lebesgue-almost every real θ is irrational and has irrationality exponent two.

title: Rational-parameter classification of trigonometric power series
description: Let θ=p/q be in lowest terms with q>0 and 0<α≤1. The cosine-power series ∑cosⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ converges conditionally if p,q are odd and otherwise diverges to +∞. The sine-power series converges absolutely if q is odd, conditionally if q≡2 mod 4, and diverges to +∞ if 4 divides q.

title: Irrationality-exponent criterion for trigonometric power series
description: If θ is irrational with finite irrationality exponent μ and α>1−1/(2μ−2), then both ∑sinⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ and ∑cosⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ converge absolutely.

title: Almost-everywhere convergence of trigonometric power series
description: For α>1/2, both ∑sinⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ and ∑cosⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ converge absolutely for Lebesgue-almost every real θ.

title: Dense irrational parameters of trigonometric power-series divergence
description: There is a dense set E of irrational real numbers such that for every θ∈E and every α≤1 both ∑sinⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ and ∑cosⁿ(πnθ)/nᵅ diverge.

title: Post-critically finite self-similar structure
description: A compact connected metrizable space K with finitely many continuous injections ψ_i:K→K and a continuous coding surjection π:S^N→K satisfying π(iω)=ψ_i(π(ω)), for which the postcritical set P=⋃_(m≥1)σ^m(π⁻¹(⋃_(i≠j)(ψ_iK∩ψ_jK))) is finite. Its boundary is V₀=π(P).

title: Regular harmonic structure on a post-critically finite self-similar set
description: For a p.c.f. self-similar structure, a symmetric nonpositive matrix D on boundary functions, with kernel the constants and nonnegative off-diagonal entries, together with weights 0<r_i<1, is a regular harmonic structure if its boundary energy E₀(u)=−uᵀDu equals the minimum of the first-level energy ∑_i r_i⁻¹E₀(v∘ψ_i) over extensions v of u to the first-level vertices.

title: Resistance energy from a regular harmonic structure
description: Given a regular harmonic structure on a p.c.f. self-similar set, define E_m(u)=∑_(|w|=m)r_w⁻¹E₀(u∘ψ_w|V₀), with r_w the product of the cell weights. The resistance-energy domain is the continuous functions with sup_m E_m(u)<∞, and their energy is lim_m E_m(u), with bilinear polarization.

title: Harmonic function for a regular harmonic structure
description: For the resistance energy induced by a regular harmonic structure on a p.c.f. self-similar set, a harmonic function is an energy-domain function minimizing energy among functions with its prescribed values on the finite boundary V₀.

title: Strong locality of a symmetric Dirichlet form
description: A symmetric Dirichlet form E is strongly local if E(u,v)=0 whenever u is constant on a neighborhood of the support of v and v has compact support, for domain functions for which this support condition applies.

title: Energy measure of a strongly local regular Dirichlet form
description: For a strongly local regular Dirichlet form E, the energy measure ν_f of a bounded domain function f is the positive measure characterized on bounded compactly supported domain test functions g by ∫g dν_f=2E(f,fg)−E(f²,g). This uses Hino’s normalization; polarization gives mutual energy measures.

title: Strongly irreducible family of invertible real matrices
description: A family of invertible endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional real vector space is strongly irreducible if no finite union of proper nonzero linear subspaces is invariant under every member of the family.

title: Positive semidefinite complex matrix
description: A Hermitian n×n complex matrix A is positive semidefinite if z*Az≥0 for every z∈ℂⁿ.

title: Positive definite complex matrix
description: A Hermitian n×n complex matrix A is positive definite if z*Az>0 for every nonzero z∈ℂⁿ.

title: Löwner order on Hermitian matrices
description: For Hermitian matrices A,B of the same size, A≤B means that B−A is positive semidefinite.

title: Invertible square matrix
description: A square matrix A over a field is invertible if there is a square matrix B with AB=BA=I; this B is denoted A⁻¹.

title: Weighted power mean of two positive numbers
description: For a,b>0 and v∈[0,1], M_t(v;a,b)=(vaᵗ+(1−v)bᵗ)¹⁄ᵗ for t≠0, with M_0(v;a,b)=aᵛb¹⁻ᵛ. The cases t=1 and −1 are the weighted arithmetic and harmonic means.

title: Weighted arithmetic mean of positive definite matrices
description: For positive definite matrices A,B of the same size and v∈[0,1], A∇ᵥB=vA+(1−v)B.

title: Weighted harmonic mean of positive definite matrices
description: For positive definite matrices A,B of the same size and v∈[0,1], A!ᵥB=(vA⁻¹+(1−v)B⁻¹)⁻¹.

title: Spectral theorem for a Hermitian complex matrix
description: Every Hermitian complex matrix A has a decomposition A=U diag(λ₁,…,λₙ)U* with U unitary and all λⱼ real.

title: Real power of a positive definite complex matrix
description: For A=U diag(λ₁,…,λₙ)U* positive definite and t∈ℝ, define Aᵗ=U diag(λ₁ᵗ,…,λₙᵗ)U*, independently of the unitary diagonalization.

title: Sharp comparison of weighted scalar arithmetic–harmonic gaps
description: For distinct a,b>0, λ≥1 and 0<v<τ<1, with Aᵥ=va+(1−v)b and Hᵥ=(v/a+(1−v)/b)⁻¹, (v/τ)^λ<(Aᵥ^λ−Hᵥ^λ)/(Aτ^λ−Hτ^λ)<((1−v)/(1−τ))^λ; both constants are sharp.

title: Comparison of weighted matrix arithmetic–harmonic gaps
description: If A,B are positive definite matrices and 0<v≤τ<1, then (v/τ)(A∇τB−A!τB)≤A∇ᵥB−A!ᵥB≤((1−v)/(1−τ))(A∇τB−A!τB) in Löwner order.

title: Space of continuous real functions on a compact Hausdorff space
description: For a compact Hausdorff space K, C(K) is the real Banach space of continuous functions K→ℝ with norm ||f||∞=max_K|f|.

title: Bounded linear extension operator for continuous functions
description: For a closed subspace L of a compact Hausdorff space K, a bounded linear operator T:C(L)→C(K) is an extension operator if (Tf)|L=f for every f∈C(L).

title: Compact space of subsets with bounded finite cardinality
description: For a set X and n∈ℕ, σ_n(2^X) is the subspace of {0,1}^X consisting of characteristic functions of subsets of X of cardinality at most n, with the product topology.

title: Infimal norm of extension operators
description: For L closed in compact Hausdorff K, η(L,K) is the infimum of ||T|| over bounded linear extension operators C(L)→C(K), with value ∞ if none exists.

title: Initial topology for a family of maps
description: For maps f_i:X→Y_i into topological spaces, the initial topology on X is generated by the sets f_i⁻¹(U), where U is open in Y_i; it is the coarsest topology making every f_i continuous.

title: Weak topology on a normed vector space
description: The weak topology on a normed space X is the coarsest topology making every bounded linear functional X→ℝ or ℂ continuous.

title: Weak-star topology on a continuous dual
description: The weak-star topology σ(X*,X) on the continuous dual of a normed space X is the topology of pointwise convergence on X.

title: Scattered topological space
description: A topological space is scattered if every nonempty subspace has an isolated point.

title: Well-ordered set
description: A totally ordered set is well ordered if every nonempty subset has a least element.

title: Ordinal number
description: An ordinal is a transitive set whose membership relation is a well ordering; ordinals represent order types of well-ordered sets.

title: Aleph sequence of infinite cardinals
description: The alephs enumerate infinite well-ordered cardinalities: ℵ₀ is countable infinity, ℵ_{α+1} is the least larger infinite cardinal, and at a limit ordinal λ, ℵ_λ=sup_{α<λ}ℵ_α.

title: Fréchet–Urysohn space
description: A topological space is Fréchet–Urysohn if, whenever x lies in the closure of A, there is a sequence in A converging to x.

title: Free-set theorem for finite-valued set mappings
description: For n∈ℕ, |X|≥ℵ_n and S:[X]^n→[X]^{<ω}, there is A∈[X]^{n+1} such that a∉S(A minus {a}) for every a∈A.

title: Extension norms between finite-subset compacta at ℵ₁
description: For 1≤m<n and |X|=ℵ₁, η(σ_m(2^X),σ_n(2^X))=2n−2m+1.

title: Nonexistence of extension operators between distinct weak Hilbert balls
description: If H is a nonseparable real Hilbert space and 0<λ<μ, there is no bounded linear extension operator C(λB_H)→C(μB_H), where both balls carry the weak topology.

title: Locally finite weighted undirected graph
description: A vertex set V has symmetric weights μ_xy≥0, only finitely many nonzero at each x, and vertex weights m(x)>0; x and y are adjacent when μ_xy>0. Loops are allowed.

title: Formal Laplacian on a locally finite weighted graph
description: For a locally finite weighted graph, Δf(x)=m(x)⁻¹∑_y μ_xy(f(y)−f(x)); local finiteness makes this defined for every real-valued function f on the vertices.

title: Carré du champ of a weighted graph Laplacian
description: For a weighted graph Laplacian Δ, Γ(f,g)=½(Δ(fg)−fΔg−gΔf)= (2m(x))⁻¹∑_y μ_xy(f(y)−f(x))(g(y)−g(x)) at x; write Γ(f)=Γ(f,f).

title: Iterated carré du champ of a weighted graph
description: For a weighted graph, Γ₂(f,g)=½(ΔΓ(f,g)−Γ(f,Δg)−Γ(g,Δf)); write Γ₂(f)=Γ₂(f,f).

title: Bakry–Émery CD(K,∞) condition on a weighted graph
description: A weighted graph satisfies CD(K,∞) if Γ₂(f)(x)≥KΓ(f)(x) for every real function f and every vertex x.

title: Pointwise convergence of functions
description: A sequence f_n:X→Y into a metric space converges pointwise to f if f_n(x)→f(x) for every x∈X.

title: Pseudometric space
description: A pseudometric on a set X is a symmetric function d:X×X→[0,∞) with d(x,x)=0 and the triangle inequality; different points may have distance zero.

title: Completeness by Γ-small cutoffs on a weighted graph
description: A weighted graph is complete in the cutoff sense if it admits finitely supported functions 0≤η_k≤1 increasing pointwise to 1 with Γ(η_k)≤1/k everywhere.

title: Intrinsic pseudometric on a weighted graph
description: A pseudometric ρ on a weighted graph is intrinsic if ∑_y μ_xyρ(x,y)²≤m(x) for every vertex x.

title: Dirichlet energy of a weighted graph
description: On ℓ²(V,m), the graph energy is Q(f,g)=½∑_{x,y}μ_xy(f(y)−f(x))(g(y)−g(x)); the Dirichlet domain is the closure of finitely supported functions in the norm (||f||₂²+Q(f,f))¹⁄².

title: Minimal heat semigroup on a weighted graph
description: For the Dirichlet realization L of the weighted graph Laplacian on ℓ²(V,m), P_t=e^{tL} is the associated self-adjoint sub-Markov semigroup, extended to bounded nonnegative functions by monotone approximation.

title: Stochastic completeness of a weighted graph
description: A weighted graph is stochastically complete if its minimal heat semigroup preserves the constant function 1: P_t1=1 for every t>0.

title: Gradient characterization of CD(K,∞) on complete weighted graphs
description: For a locally finite weighted graph complete by Γ-small cutoffs and with inf_x m(x)>0, CD(K,∞) is equivalent to Γ(P_tf)≤e^(−2Kt)P_tΓ(f) for every finitely supported f and t≥0; equivalently this holds for every f in the energy domain.

title: Stochastic completeness from graph cutoff completeness and CD(K,∞)
description: A locally finite weighted graph complete by Γ-small cutoffs, with inf_x m(x)>0 and satisfying CD(K,∞) for some real K, is stochastically complete.

title: Ring of p-adic integers
description: For a prime p, ℤ_p is the subring {x∈ℚ_p:v_p(x)≥0}, with its p-adic topology.

title: Inverse limit of groups
description: For groups G_n and homomorphisms f_n:G_(n+1)→G_n, the inverse limit is the subgroup of ∏G_n consisting of tuples (x_n) satisfying f_n(x_(n+1))=x_n for every n; for topological groups it carries the subspace topology of the product.

title: Pro-l group
description: For a prime ℓ, a pro-ℓ group is a topological group isomorphic to an inverse limit of finite groups of ℓ-power order, the finite groups having the discrete topology.

title: Galois group of an algebraic Galois extension
description: For an algebraic Galois extension L/K, Gal(L/K) is the group of K-automorphisms of L with the Krull topology, whose basic identity neighborhoods fix finite intermediate extensions pointwise.

title: Pro-l Galois extension
description: An algebraic Galois extension L/K is pro-ℓ if its topological Galois group is a pro-ℓ group. It is abelian when that Galois group is abelian.

title: Z_l-extension of a number field
description: For a prime ℓ, a ℤ_ℓ-extension of a number field K is an algebraic Galois extension L/K whose topological Galois group is isomorphic to the additive group ℤ_ℓ.

title: Cyclotomic Z_l-extension of a number field
description: The cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞/K is the unique ℤ_ℓ-extension of K contained in the extension obtained by adjoining all roots of unity of ℓ-power order. If K contains μ_(2ℓ) and |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓ^m, its degree-ℓ^n layer is K_n=K(μ_(ℓ^(m+n))).

title: Compositum of field extensions
description: For subfields L_i of one overfield containing K, their compositum is the smallest subfield containing every L_i.

title: Divisible abelian group
description: An abelian group D is divisible if for every positive integer n the map x↦nx is surjective. For a prime ℓ, ℓ-divisibility means this only for n=ℓ.

title: Prime-power torsion subgroup of an abelian group
description: For an abelian group A and a prime ℓ, A[ℓ^m]={a:ℓ^m a=0}, and A[ℓ∞]=⋃_(m≥0)A[ℓ^m].

title: Multiplicative group of a field
description: For a field F, F× is the abelian group of its nonzero elements under multiplication.

title: Universal l-primary Kummer radical of a field
description: For a field K and a prime ℓ, its universal ℓ-primary radical is ℛ_K=(ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ)⊗_ℤK×. Torsion in K× disappears in this tensor product, so a representative ℓ^(−k)⊗x is zero exactly when x is a root of unity times an ℓ^k-th power in K.

title: Kummer radical of an abelian pro-l extension
description: If F contains all ℓ-power roots of unity and L/F is abelian pro-ℓ, its Kummer radical consists of the classes ℓ^(−k)⊗x in (ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ)⊗F× for which F(x^(1/ℓ^k)) lies in L.

title: L-adified multiplicative group of a field
description: For a field F, the ℓ-adified multiplicative group used here is ℝ_F=ℤ_ℓ⊗_ℤF×. This tensor product, called the group of principal idèles in ℓ-adic class field theory, is distinct from an unrestricted inverse-limit completion unless an equivalence has been checked.

title: Invariant submodule of a group action
description: If a group G acts by R-linear automorphisms on an R-module M, its invariant submodule is M^G={m∈M:g·m=m for every g∈G}.

title: One-variable Iwasawa algebra over Z_l
description: For a prime ℓ and a procyclic group Γ with a chosen topological generator γ, its one-variable Iwasawa algebra is Λ=ℤ_ℓ[[T]], with γ represented by 1+T. This fixes the coordinate convention used for the completed group algebra.

title: L-adic cyclotomic character
description: The ℓ-adic cyclotomic character χ_ℓ of an absolute Galois group is the continuous character to ℤ_ℓ× characterized by σ(ζ)=ζ^(χ_ℓ(σ)) for every root of unity ζ of ℓ-power order.

title: Initial Kummer radical of Z_l-extensions
description: Suppose K contains μ_(2ℓ), |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓ^m, and Z is the compositum of all ℤ_ℓ-extensions of K. Its initial radical is {ℓ^(−m)⊗x∈ℛ_K:K∞(x^(1/ℓ^m))⊆Z}, regarded inside the universal radical of K∞.

title: Second Milnor K-group of a field
description: For a field F, K₂^M(F) is (F×⊗_ℤF×) modulo the subgroup generated by a⊗(1−a) for a≠0,1. The class {a,b} is its universal Steinberg symbol, bilinear in both multiplicative arguments.

title: L-adic Tate module of roots of unity
description: The Tate module T_ℓ(μ) is lim←μ_(ℓ^n), with transition maps ζ↦ζ^ℓ and the natural Galois action.

title: Universal Tate kernel in a cyclotomic Kummer radical
description: For K containing μ_(2ℓ), write Γ=Gal(K∞/K) with χ_ℓ(γ)=1+ℓ^m. Let barΓ* be generated by γ^(−1)/(1+ℓ^m), acting on ℛ_(K∞). The universal Tate kernel is the maximal divisible subgroup of ℛ_(K∞)^(barΓ*); its ℓ^m-torsion is the initial exponent-ℓ^m kernel studied here.

title: Kummer descent in a cyclotomic Z_l-tower
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), with |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓ^m, and put γ*=γ/(1+ℓ^m). The Kummer radical of K_n^ab K∞/K∞ is ℛ_(K∞)^(Γ_n*), where Γ_n* is generated by (γ*)^(ℓ^n). The radical for the compositum of all ℤ_ℓ-extensions of K_n is its maximal ℓ-divisible subgroup.

title: Jaulent’s norm-limit description of the initial Z_l radical
description: In the preceding cyclotomic setup, the initial Kummer radical is the projection to n=0 of lim←ℛ_(K_n)^(Γ*), with norm transition maps. Equivalently it is π₀ lim←(ℝ_(K_n)/(ℝ_(K_n)^(γ*−1)μ_(K_n))), where ℝ_F=ℤ_ℓ⊗F× and γ*=γ/(1+ℓ^m).

title: Jaulent’s norm-limit description of the Tate kernel
description: In the same cyclotomic setup, the ℓ^m-torsion of the universal Tate kernel is π₀ lim←ℛ_(K_n)^(barΓ*), equivalently π₀ lim←(ℝ_(K_n)/(ℝ_(K_n)^(barγ*−1)μ_(K_n))), with norm transitions and barγ*=γ^(−1)/(1+ℓ^m).

title: Rank-one harmonic energy densities on a p.c.f. self-similar set
description: Let a connected p.c.f. self-similar set carry a regular harmonic structure, with every boundary point p fixed by a cell map and K∖{p} connected. For finitely many harmonic functions h₁,…,h_m and ν=∑_i a_iν_(h_i) with a_i>0, the matrix (dν_(h_i,h_j)/dν)_(i,j) has rank at most one ν-almost everywhere; it has rank one wherever ν is nonzero.

title: Boundary-vertex harmonic extension asymptotics
description: For a regular harmonic structure on a connected p.c.f. self-similar set whose boundary pointsp_i are cell fixed points and whose complementsK∖{p_i} are connected, letA_i act on boundary values by harmonic extension into thei-th cell and letP remove constants. Letu_i be thep_i-column ofD and letv_i be the right r_i-eigenvector ofA_i normalized by(u_i,v_i)=1. Thenr_i^(−n)P A_i^n x→(u_i,x)Pv_i for every boundary vectorx.

title: Heine–Borel theorem in finite-dimensional normed spaces
description: A subset of a finite-dimensional real normed vector space is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

title: Semigroup
description: A semigroup is a set equipped with an associative binary operation.

title: Semigroup with a translation-invariant metric
description: A metric semigroup is a semigroup G with a metric d such that d(ac,bc)=d(a,b)=d(ca,cb) for all a,b,c∈G. No identity, inverses or commutativity are required.

title: Random element of a measurable space
description: A random element of a measurable space E is a measurable map from a probability space into E; a metric space is equipped with its Borel σ-algebra unless otherwise specified.

title: Independent family of random elements
description: Random elements X_i are independent if, for every finite set of distinct indices and measurable sets A_i in their respective targets, P(∩{X_i∈A_i})=∏P(X_i∈A_i).

title: Decreasing rearrangement of a nonnegative random variable
description: For a nonnegative random variable Y, its decreasing rearrangement is Y*(t)=sup{y≥0:P(Y>y)>t} for 0≤t≤1, with the empty supremum taken as 0; it is equidistributed with Y on the Lebesgue probability interval, up to endpoint conventions.

title: Maximum distance of partial products in a metric semigroup
description: For G-valued random elements X₁,…,Xₙ and z₀,z₁∈G, let S_k=X₁⋯X_k and Uₙ=max_{1≤k≤n}d(z₁,z₀S_k); let Mₙ=max_{1≤k≤n}d(z₀,z₀X_k).

title: Hoffmann–Jørgensen tail bound in metric semigroups
description: For independent random elements in a separable invariant-metric semigroup, with Uₙ,Mₙ the partial-product and increment maxima, P(Uₙ>(3K−1)t)≤P(Mₙ>t)+(P(Uₙ>t)/P(Uₙ≤t))^K/K! for positive integers K≤n+1 and t>0 with P(Uₙ≤t)>0.

title: Lévy convergence equivalence in complete metric semigroups
description: For independent random elements X_n in a complete separable invariant-metric semigroup, their ordered partial products S_n converge almost surely to a given random element X if and only if d(S_n,X)→0 in probability. The event that S_n converges has probability zero or one.

title: Moment integrability equivalence for bounded random partial products
description: Let independent random elements X_n in a separable invariant-metric semigroup be indexed by a finite initial segment or ℕ. If U=sup_n d(z₁,z₀X₁⋯X_n)<∞ almost surely, then for every p>0, E U^p<∞ if and only if E(sup_n d(z₀,z₀X_n))^p<∞.

title: Universal moment comparison for abelian metric semigroups
description: For every p₀>0 there is C(p₀) such that, in any separable abelian invariant-metric semigroup and for any finite independent sequence, ||Uₙ||_q≤C(p₀) q/max(p,log(e+q)) (||Uₙ||_p+||Mₙ||_q) for q≥p≥p₀, where Uₙ and Mₙ are the partial-product and increment maxima.

title: Pure contraction on a Hilbert space
description: A bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space is a pure contraction if ||T||≤1 and T*ⁿh→0 in norm for every vector h. This is class C_{·0}.

title: m-hypercontraction
description: For an integer m≥1, a bounded Hilbert-space operator T is an m-hypercontraction if ∑_{k=0}^p(−1)^k binom(p,k)T^kT*^k≥0 for every integer 1≤p≤m.

title: Vector-valued weighted Bergman space on the disk
description: For α≥1 and a complex Hilbert space E, A²_α(E) is the E-valued reproducing-kernel Hilbert space on the unit disk with kernel (1−z w̄)^(−α)I_E; α=1 gives the vector-valued Hardy space.

title: Multiplier between vector-valued weighted Bergman spaces
description: A holomorphic map Θ:𝔻→B(E₁,E₂) is a multiplier A²_{m₁}(E₁)→A²_{m₂}(E₂) if pointwise multiplication f↦Θf is a bounded linear operator between these spaces.

title: Doubly commuting tuple of Hilbert-space operators
description: A finite tuple (T₁,…,Tₙ) of bounded operators on one Hilbert space is doubly commuting if T_iT_j=T_jT_i and T_iT_j*=T_j*T_i for distinct i,j.

title: Hereditary polynomial functional calculus for an operator tuple
description: For a commuting tuple T and p(z,w̄)=∑a_{αβ}z^αw̄^β, the hereditary evaluation is p(T,T*)=∑a_{αβ}T^αT*^β, with all unstarred factors to the left.

title: Agler dilation of a pure m-hypercontraction
description: For a pure m-hypercontraction T and D=(∑_{k=0}^m(−1)^k binom(m,k)T^kT*^k)¹⁄², the map (Vh)(z)=D(I−zT*)^(−m)h is an isometry into A²_m(cl ran D), intertwines T* with M_z*, and realizes T as a compression of M_z.

title: Partially isometric multiplier representation of Bergman invariant subspaces
description: A closed M_z-invariant subspace S of A²_m(E*) can be written S=ΘH²(E) for an auxiliary Hilbert space E and a multiplier Θ:H²(E)→A²_m(E*) whose multiplication operator is a partial isometry.

title: Partially isometric multiplier model of a pure hypercontraction
description: Every pure m-hypercontraction T is unitarily equivalent to P_QM_z|Q on Q=A²_m(D_T)⊖ΘH²(E), for some auxiliary E and partially isometric multiplier Θ, where D_T is the closure of the m-defect operator range.

title: Banach contraction mapping theorem
description: Every map T:X→X on a nonempty complete metric space satisfying d(Tx,Ty)≤q d(x,y) for a fixed 0≤q<1 has a unique fixed point, and Tⁿx converges to it for every x.

title: Strongly continuous nonlinear contraction semigroup
description: On a closed subset X₀ of a Banach space X, maps S(t):X₀→X₀ form a strongly continuous contraction semigroup if S(0)=I, S(t+s)=S(t)S(s), ||S(t)x−S(t)y||≤||x−y||, and every orbit t↦S(t)x is continuous.

title: Dissipative relation on a real Hilbert space
description: A relation A⊆H×H is dissipative if ⟨u−v,x−y⟩≤0 whenever u∈Ax and v∈Ay. Its domain consists of x with Ax nonempty.

title: m-dissipative relation on a real Hilbert space
description: A dissipative relation A on a real Hilbert space H is m-dissipative if ran(I−A)=H. Equivalently, I−A has an everywhere-defined single-valued nonexpansive inverse.

title: Maximal monotone relation on a real Hilbert space
description: A relation M⊆H×H on a real Hilbert space is monotone if ⟨u−v,x−y⟩≥0 for u∈Mx,v∈My, and maximal monotone if it has no proper monotone extension.

title: Komura–Kato generation theorem in Hilbert space
description: An m-dissipative relation A on a real Hilbert space generates a unique strongly continuous nonlinear contraction semigroup on the closure of D(A); for initial values in D(A), the orbit solves x′(t)∈Ax(t) and its right derivative is the minimal-norm section of A.

title: Linear port-Hamiltonian differential operator on an interval
description: On L²((0,1);ℝᵈ), a port-Hamiltonian operator has Ax=∑_{k=0}^N P_k(Hx)^(k), with H bounded, symmetric and uniformly positive, P_N invertible, P_kᵀ=(−1)^{k+1}P_k for k≥1 and P₀+P₀ᵀ≤0; its maximal domain requires Hx∈H^N.

title: Impedance passive boundary control and observation system
description: A boundary system (A,B,C) with state Hilbert space X and matching input/output space U is impedance passive if Re⟨Ax,x⟩_X≤Re⟨Bx,Cx⟩_U for every x∈D(A), where B and C are its boundary input and output maps.

title: Globally exponentially stable zero equilibrium of a nonlinear semigroup
description: For a nonlinear semigroup S(t) with S(t)0=0, zero is globally exponentially stable if ||S(t)x||≤M e^(−ωt)||x|| for all t≥0 and all states x, for some M≥1 and ω>0.

title: Generation under maximal monotone static port-Hamiltonian feedback
description: For an impedance passive real port-Hamiltonian system (A,B,C) and maximal monotone relation φ on its finite-dimensional boundary space, the restriction A_φ with Bx∈−φ(Cx) generates a strongly continuous nonlinear contraction semigroup on the energy Hilbert space.

title: Exponential stability under dissipative first-order port-Hamiltonian feedback
description: For a first-order impedance passive port-Hamiltonian system with Lipschitz H and maximal monotone feedback φ containing (0,0), if its closed-loop generator satisfies Re⟨Ax,x⟩_H≤−κ x(1)*H(1)x(1) for κ>0, the generated nonlinear contraction semigroup has a globally exponentially stable zero equilibrium.

title: P-adic local field
description: A p-adic local field is a finite extension K of ℚ_p, equipped with the uniquely extended p-adic topology and valuation.

title: Uniformizer of a discretely valued field
description: For a normalized discrete valuation v on K, a uniformizer is an element π∈K with v(π)=1; it generates the maximal ideal of the valuation ring.

title: Residue degree of a finite extension of discretely valued fields
description: For a finite extension L/K of discretely valued fields, with the discrete valuation of L extending that of K, the residue degree f(L/K) is the degree [k_L:k_K] of the residue-field extension. Finite extensions of nonarchimedean local fields are the basic case.

title: Totally ramified finite extension of local fields
description: A finite extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields is totally ramified if its ramification index equals [L:K], equivalently if its residue-field extension is trivial.

title: Discriminant ideal of a finite local-field extension
description: For a finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, its discriminant ideal in O_K is generated by det(Tr_(L/K)(b_i b_j)) for an O_K-basis (b_i) of O_L. A different integral basis changes this generator by a unit square.

title: Eisenstein polynomial over a discretely valued field
description: A monic polynomial f=xⁿ+a_(n−1)x^(n−1)+⋯+a₀ over a discretely valued field is Eisenstein if every a_i lies in the valuation ring, v(a_i)≥1 for i<n, and v(a₀)=1.

title: Newton polygon of a polynomial over a discretely valued field
description: For f=∑a_i x^i over a discretely valued field, its Newton polygon is the lower convex boundary of the points (i,v(a_i)) with a_i≠0, restricted between the least and greatest such abscissas.

title: Ramification polynomial of an Eisenstein polynomial
description: If f is a degree-n Eisenstein polynomial over K with root α, its ramification polynomial is ρ_f(x)=f(αx+α)/αⁿ over K(α).

title: Ramification polygon of a totally ramified local-field extension
description: For a totally ramified finite local-field extension L/K generated by a uniformizer α with minimal polynomial f, its ramification polygon is the Newton polygon of f(αx+α)/αⁿ using the normalized valuation v_L(α)=1. The geometric polygon is independent of the uniformizer.

title: Ramification polygon with coefficient-point markings
description: A marked ramification polygon records the lower Newton polygon of an Eisenstein ramification polynomial together with the specified coefficient points (i,v_L(ρ_i)) lying on it, including intermediate p-power abscissas. These markings distinguish the finer data used in coefficient bounds and residual-polynomial supports.

title: Residual polynomial of a Newton-polygon segment
description: Let ρ=∑ρ_i x^i over a discretely valued field with uniformizer α. For a lower segment from (k,v(ρ_k)) to (k+d,v(ρ_(k+d))) with reduced slope −h/e, its residual polynomial is ∑_(j=0)^(d/e) overline(ρ_(k+je) α^(jh−v(ρ_k))) x^j in the residue field.

title: Residual-polynomial orbit invariant of a local extension
description: For the segments of a ramification polygon with slopes −h_i/e_i and residual polynomials A_i, form the tuples (γ_(δ,i) A_i(δ^(h_i)x)) as δ ranges over nonzero residue-field elements, with γ_(δ,r)=δ^(−h_r deg A_r) and γ_(δ,i)=γ_(δ,i+1)δ^(−h_i deg A_i). Their orbit is the invariant denoted A.

title: Ore’s discriminant-existence criterion for totally ramified local extensions
description: Let K be p-adic with normalized valuation v and maximal ideal 𝔭, and let J=an+b with 0≤b<n. A totally ramified degree-n extension with discriminant 𝔭^(n+J−1) exists exactly when min{n v(b),n v(n)}≤J≤n v(n), using v(0)=∞.

title: Unique extension of a complete discretely valued absolute value
description: If K is complete for a nonarchimedean discrete absolute value, that absolute value extends uniquely to every algebraic extension of K.

title: Krasner’s lemma
description: Let K be complete for a nonarchimedean discrete absolute value, and let α,β be algebraic over K with α separable over K(β). If |β−α|<|α′−α| for every distinct K-conjugate α′ of α, then K(α)⊆K(β).

title: Krasner distance between monic irreducible polynomials
description: For monic irreducible degree-n polynomials f,g over a complete nonarchimedean field, define d(f,g)=|f(β)|=|g(α)|, where α is a root of f and β a root of g. This is the root-evaluation ultrametric used here, without taking an nth root.

title: Characteristic polynomial of a matrix
description: For a square matrix A over a field, its characteristic polynomial is det(xI−A), a monic polynomial whose roots over an algebraic closure are its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity.

title: Gaussian unitary ensemble
description: The Gaussian unitary ensemble of order N is the probability distribution on complex Hermitian N×N matrices with density proportional to exp(−c Tr(H²)) with respect to Lebesgue measure on their independent real coordinates, where c>0 fixes the variance convention. Here c=2N, so the limiting spectral support is [−1,1].

title: Meromorphic gamma function
description: The meromorphic gamma function is the continuation of Γ(z)=∫₀^∞t^(z−1)e^(−t)dt from Re z>0 to the complex plane using Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z); it has simple poles at 0,−1,−2,… .

title: Barnes G-function
description: The Barnes G-function is the canonical entire function given by G(z+1)=(2π)^(z/2)exp(−(z+z²(1+γ))/2)∏_(n≥1)[(1+z/n)^n exp(z²/(2n)−z)], where γ=lim_(n→∞)(∑_(k=1)^n1/k−log n). It satisfies G(1)=1 and G(z+1)=Γ(z)G(z); the recurrence alone does not specify its canonical normalization.

title: Mellin transform of a positive random variable
description: For a positive random variable X, its Mellin transform is M_X(s)=E[X^(s−1)] on the complex strip where the expectation is absolutely integrable, with X^(s−1)=exp((s−1)log X).

title: Bilateral Laplace transform of a real probability distribution
description: For a real random variable Y, its bilateral Laplace transform is L_Y(s)=E[e^(sY)] on the complex strip where this expectation converges absolutely.

title: Standard Gumbel distribution
description: The standard Gumbel distribution has cumulative distribution function P(G≤x)=exp(−exp(−x)) for real x.

title: Gibbs partition function on a measure space
description: For a measured configuration space (X,μ), an energy V and inverse temperature β>0, the Gibbs partition function is Z(β)=∫_X e^(−βV(x))dμ(x), when finite and positive; the associated free energy is F(β)=−β⁻¹log Z(β).

title: Selberg integral evaluation
description: For n≥2, real a,b>0 and γ>−min(1/n,a/(n−1),b/(n−1)), the integral over [0,1]^n of ∏_i x_i^(a−1)(1−x_i)^(b−1)∏_(i<j)|x_i−x_j|^(2γ) equals ∏_(j=0)^(n−1) Γ(a+jγ)Γ(b+jγ)Γ(1+(j+1)γ)/[Γ(a+b+(n+j−1)γ)Γ(1+γ)].

title: Legendre duplication formula for the gamma function
description: For Re z>0, Γ(2z)=2^(2z−1)π^(−1/2)Γ(z)Γ(z+1/2), and the identity extends meromorphically wherever both sides are defined.

title: Krasovsky’s separated-bulk GUE characteristic-polynomial moment asymptotic
description: Let H_N have GUE density proportional to e^(−2NTr(H_N²)), and p_N(x)=det(xI−H_N). For fixed distinct x₁,…,x_k∈(−1,1) and fixed α_j with Re α_j>−1/2, E∏_j|p_N(x_j)|^(2α_j) equals (1+O(log N/N))∏_j[C(α_j)(1−x_j²)^(α_j²/2)(N/2)^(α_j²)e^((2x_j²−1−2log2)α_jN)]∏_(i<j)(2|x_i−x_j|)^(−2α_iα_j), where C(α)=2^(2α²)G(α+1)²/G(2α+1).

title: Fyodorov–Simm conjecture for the GUE characteristic-polynomial maximum
description: For GUE density proportional to e^(−2NTr(H²)), set M_N=max_(x∈[−1,1]){2log|det(xI−H)|−2Elog|det(xI−H)|}. The conjecture predicts 2log N−(3/2)loglog N−M_N converges in distribution to Y with bilateral Laplace transform E[e^(sY)]=C⁻¹(2π)^sΓ(s+1)Γ(s+3)G(s+7/2)²/[G(s+6)G(s+1)], where C makes the transform equal 1 at s=0.

title: Frame in a Hilbert space
description: A countable family (g_j) in a Hilbert space H is a frame if A||f||²≤∑_j|⟨f,g_j⟩|²≤B||f||² for all f∈H and some 0<A≤B<∞.

title: Bessel sequence in a Hilbert space
description: A countable family (g_j) in a Hilbert space is Bessel if ∑_j|⟨f,g_j⟩|²≤B||f||² for every f and some finite B.

title: Time-frequency shift of a Euclidean function
description: For x,ω∈ℝᵈ, the time-frequency shift of f is (M_ωT_xf)(t)=e^(2πiω·t)f(t−x). Translation is T_x and modulation is M_ω.

title: Short-time Fourier transform
description: For f,g∈L²(ℝᵈ), the short-time Fourier transform with window g is V_gf(x,ω)=⟨f,M_ωT_xg⟩.

title: Lattice Gabor frame
description: For g∈L²(ℝᵈ) and a,b>0, the family (M_{mb}T_{na}g)_{m,n∈ℤᵈ} is a lattice Gabor frame when it satisfies the Hilbert-space frame inequalities.

title: Wiener amalgam space W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ)
description: For 1≤p,q≤∞ and Q=[0,1)ᵈ, W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ)(ℝᵈ) consists of measurable f with (||f·1_{Q+k}||_p)_{k∈ℤᵈ}∈ℓᵠ, with this sequence norm.

title: Feichtinger algebra S₀ on Euclidean space
description: The Feichtinger algebra S₀(ℝᵈ) consists of f∈L²(ℝᵈ) for which V_gf∈L¹(ℝ²ᵈ) for a fixed nonzero Schwartz window g; choosing a different such window gives the same space.

title: Mixed Gabor analysis–synthesis operator
description: If g,γ generate Bessel Gabor systems for a,b>0 and ⟨γ,g⟩≠0, define S_{a,b;g,γ}f=(ab)ᵈ/⟨γ,g⟩ ∑_{m,n}⟨f,M_{mb}T_{na}g⟩M_{mb}T_{na}γ, with Hilbert-norm convergence.

title: Walnut representation on Wiener amalgam spaces
description: For g,γ∈W(L∞,ℓ¹) with ⟨γ,g⟩≠0, the mixed Gabor operator extends boundedly to every W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ), 1≤p,q≤∞, and equals ⟨γ,g⟩⁻¹∑_n aᵈG_n·T_{n/b}, where G_n(x)=∑_k conjugate(g(x−n/b−ak))γ(x−ak); the operator series converges absolutely after a uniform translation bound.

title: Strong dense-sampling limit of Gabor operators on Wiener amalgams
description: If g,γ∈W(L∞,ℓ¹) and ⟨γ,g⟩≠0, then ||S_{a,b;g,γ}f−f||_{W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ)}→0 as a,b→0 for every f∈W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ) with 1≤p,q<∞.

title: Operator-norm dense-sampling limit of Gabor operators on Wiener amalgams
description: If g,γ∈W(L∞,ℓ¹), ⟨γ,g⟩≠0, and conjugate(g)γ is locally Riemann integrable, then ||S_{a,b;g,γ}−I|| on W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ) tends to zero as a,b→0 for every 1≤p,q≤∞.

title: Power-concave function with positive exponent
description: For p>0, a nonnegative function u on a convex subset Ω of ℝⁿ is p-concave if uᵖ is concave on Ω, equivalently u((1−λ)x+λy)≥((1−λ)u(x)ᵖ+λu(y)ᵖ)¹⁄ᵖ for x,y∈Ω and 0≤λ≤1.

title: Nonnegative power mean with the Borell–Brascamp–Lieb zero convention
description: For p>0 and 0<λ<1, the BBL mean M_p(a,b;λ) is ((1−λ)aᵖ+λbᵖ)¹⁄ᵖ when a,b>0, and is defined to be 0 when ab=0. This zero convention concerns extension beyond positive supports.

title: Volume-normalized centroid-aligned Hausdorff distance of convex bodies
description: For convex bodies K,L⊂ℝⁿ, H₀(K,L) is the Hausdorff distance between their volume-one dilates after translating their centroids to the origin.

title: Relative asymmetry of two sets after volume normalization
description: For measurable K,L⊂ℝⁿ with positive finite volume, A(K,L)=inf_x |K△(x+λL)|/|K| with λ=(|K|/|L|)¹⁄ⁿ; △ denotes symmetric difference.

title: p-Minkowski supremal convolution
description: For positive p, 0<λ<1 and nonnegative functions u_i on compact convex supports Ω_i, their p-Minkowski convolution at z is the supremum of M_p(u₀(x),u₁(y);λ) over z=(1−λ)x+λy, x∈Ω₀,y∈Ω₁, using the stated BBL zero convention.

title: Brunn–Minkowski inequality for convex-body volume
description: For convex bodies K,L⊂ℝⁿ and λ∈[0,1], |(1−λ)K+λL|¹⁄ⁿ≥(1−λ)|K|¹⁄ⁿ+λ|L|¹⁄ⁿ. For 0<λ<1 equality holds exactly when K,L are homothetic.

title: Borell–Brascamp–Lieb inequality at positive power
description: For p>0, λ∈(0,1), nonnegative integrable u₀,u₁ with positive integrals I₀,I₁ and compact supports Ω₀,Ω₁, if h((1−λ)x+λy)≥M_p(u₀(x),u₁(y);λ), then ∫_{(1−λ)Ω₀+λΩ₁}h≥M_{p/(np+1)}(I₀,I₁;λ), using the BBL zero convention.

title: Variational torsional rigidity of a Euclidean domain
description: For a bounded open domain Ω, torsional rigidity is T(Ω)=sup_{0≠v∈H₀¹(Ω)}(∫_Ω|v|)²/∫_Ω|∇v|². Equivalently T(Ω)=∫_Ωu for the weak solution of −Δu=1 with zero boundary values.

title: Support-volume stability of the positive-power BBL inequality
description: Fix p>0 and λ∈(0,1). For bounded nonnegative p-concave u_i on compact convex supports Ω_i with I_i=∫u_i>0, if h dominates their p-Minkowski convolution and ∫h≤M_{p/(np+1)}(I₀,I₁;λ)+ε, then for sufficiently small ε, |(1−λ)Ω₀+λΩ₁|≤M_{1/n}(|Ω₀|,|Ω₁|;λ)[1+2(n+M_{p/(np+1)}(I₀,I₁;λ)⁻¹)ε^{p/(p+1)}].

title: Quantitative positive-power BBL inequality from support asymmetry
description: For fixed p>0 and λ∈(0,1), bounded nonnegative p-concave u_i on compact convex supports Ω_i, I_i=∫u_i>0, and h dominating their p-Minkowski convolution, sufficiently small A(Ω₀,Ω₁) gives ∫h≥M_{p/(np+1)}(I₀,I₁;λ)+δ A(Ω₀,Ω₁)^{2(p+1)/p}, with δ>0 depending only on n,λ,p,I_i and |Ω_i|.

title: Gâteaux derivative of a real functional
description: A functional f on a real normed space has Gâteaux derivative Df(x)∈E* if (f(x+th)−f(x))/t→Df(x)[h] for every direction h as t→0.

title: Fenchel conjugate of a real convex functional
description: For f:E→(−∞,∞], its Fenchel conjugate is f*(x*)=sup_{x∈E}(⟨x*,x⟩−f(x)) on the continuous dual E*.

title: Bregman distance of a differentiable convex functional
description: For a proper convex functional f differentiable on int(dom f), D_f(x,y)=f(x)−f(y)−⟨Df(y),x−y⟩ for x∈dom f and y∈int(dom f). It need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality.

title: Bregman projection onto a convex set
description: Given a differentiable convex f and a nonempty closed convex C⊂dom f, the Bregman projection of x is the unique minimizer of y↦D_f(y,x) over C whenever that minimizer exists and is unique. Existence and uniqueness require additional hypotheses.

title: Total convexity of a functional on bounded sets
description: A differentiable convex f is totally convex on bounded sets if, for every bounded B⊂int(dom f) and t>0, inf{D_f(y,x):x∈B,y∈dom f,||y−x||=t}>0 whenever the constraint set is nonempty.

title: Asymptotic fixed point of a Banach-space map
description: For T:C→C in a Banach space, p∈C is an asymptotic fixed point if some bounded sequence x_n∈C converges weakly to p while ||x_n−Tx_n||→0.

title: Bregman strongly nonexpansive map
description: Relative to a differentiable convex f, T:C→C is Bregman strongly nonexpansive with respect to its nonempty asymptotic fixed set F̂ if D_f(p,Tx)≤D_f(p,x) for p∈F̂ and, for bounded x_n, D_f(p,x_n)−D_f(p,Tx_n)→0 implies D_f(x_n,Tx_n)→0.

title: Bregman firmly nonexpansive map
description: For a differentiable convex f, a map T:C→C is Bregman firmly nonexpansive if ⟨Df(Tx)−Df(Ty),Tx−Ty⟩≤⟨Df(x)−Df(y),Tx−Ty⟩ for every x,y∈C.

title: Mixed equilibrium problem
description: For a convex set C, a bifunction Θ:C×C→ℝ and φ:C→ℝ, the mixed equilibrium problem asks for x∈C such that Θ(x,y)+φ(y)≥φ(x) for every y∈C.

title: Bregman resolvent of a mixed equilibrium problem
description: For a differentiable convex f, the mixed equilibrium resolvent sends x to the set of z∈C satisfying Θ(z,y)+φ(y)−φ(z)+⟨Df(z)−Df(x),y−z⟩≥0 for every y∈C. Domain, uniqueness and existence depend on the hypotheses.

title: Poisson summation for Euclidean Schwartz functions
description: For f∈𝒮(ℝᵈ), γ>0 and f̂(ξ)=∫f(x)e^(−2πix·ξ)dx, γᵈ∑_{n∈ℤᵈ}f(x+γn)=∑_{k∈ℤᵈ}f̂(k/γ)e^(2πik·x/γ), with absolute convergence.

title: Plancherel theorem for the Euclidean Fourier transform
description: With f̂(ξ)=∫f(x)e^(−ix·ξ)dx on Schwartz functions in ℝᵈ, f↦(2π)^(−d/2)f̂ extends uniquely to a unitary operator on L²(ℝᵈ). Equivalently the e^(−2πix·ξ) Fourier normalization is unitary without a prefactor.

title: Recursive α-DOST partition of integer frequencies
description: For α∈[0,1], set i₀=0,s₀=1 and for p≥1 let i_p=s_{p−1}, β_p=⌊i_p^α⌋, s_p=i_p+β_p. The positive frequency blocks are I_p={i_p,…,s_p−1}, with I₀={0}; negative blocks are their reflections.

title: α-DOST orthonormal basis on the unit interval
description: For the α-DOST frequency blocks I_p of size β_p, the functions B_{p,τ}(t)=β_p^(−1/2)∑_{η∈I_p}e^(2πiη(t−τ/β_p)), 0≤τ<β_p, form an orthonormal basis of L²([0,1]); α=0 is the Fourier basis and α=1 is the DOST basis.

title: α-DOST nonstationary windowed system
description: For α-DOST blocks I_p, β_p=|I_p|, μ,ν>0 and a window φ, define φ_{p,k}(t)=β_p^(−1/2)∑_{η∈μI_p}e^(2πiη(t−kν/β_p))φ(t−kν/β_p), p,k∈ℤ. Translation spacing depends on the frequency block; α=0 recovers a Gabor system.

title: Painless α-DOST frame theorem
description: Fix α∈[0,1] and μ>0 and use φ̂(ξ)=∫φ(t)e^(−2πitξ)dt. Let φ be Schwartz with 0≤φ̂≤1 and support φ̂⊂[−L,L]. Put Φ_p(ω)=∑_{η∈μI_p}φ̂(ω−η). If 0<A≤∑_p|Φ_p(ω)|²≤B<∞ uniformly, then for 0<ν<(2L+μ)⁻¹ the α-DOST system is a frame for L²(ℝ).

title: Integer partition
description: An integer partition is a finite nonincreasing sequence of positive integers, including the empty sequence. Its size is the sum of its parts.

title: Young diagram of an integer partition
description: For a partition λ, its Young diagram is the set of cells (i,j) with 1≤j≤λ_i, drawn in rows of lengths λ_i.

title: Frobenius coordinates of an integer partition
description: For a partition with r diagonal cells, its Frobenius coordinates are (r;a₁,…,a_r;b₁,…,b_r), where a_i and b_i are the arm and leg lengths at diagonal cell i.

title: Bernoulli numbers
description: The Bernoulli numbers B_n∈ℚ are determined by t/(exp(t)−1)=∑_(n≥0) B_n tⁿ/n!, as an identity of formal power series; thus B₁=−1/2.

title: Q-bracket of a function on integer partitions
description: For f from integer partitions to ℚ, its q-bracket is ⟨f⟩_q=(∑_λ f(λ)q^|λ|)/(∑_λ q^|λ|), a rational formal power series; the denominator has constant term one.

title: Bloch–Okounkov shifted power sums
description: For Frobenius coordinates (r;a_i;b_i), put C_λ={a_i+1/2,−b_i−1/2:1≤i≤r}, P_j(λ)=∑_(c∈C_λ)sgn(c)cʲ, and Q₀=1, Q_k=P_(k−1)/(k−1)!+β_k for k>0, where ∑β_k t^k=(t/2)/sinh(t/2). These are the shifted-symmetric generators in Zagier’s normalization.

title: Shifted symmetric polynomial on integer partitions
description: A shifted symmetric polynomial on partitions is a polynomial in the Bloch–Okounkov functions Q₂,Q₃,…, with rational coefficients; its weight is determined by assigning Q_k weight k.

title: Bloch–Okounkov quasimodularity theorem
description: For every homogeneous shifted symmetric polynomial f on partitions of weight k, the q-bracket ⟨f⟩_q is a weight-k quasimodular form for SL₂(ℤ).

title: Serre p-adic modular form
description: For a prime p, a series f=∑a_n qⁿ in ℚ_p[[q]] is a Serre p-adic modular form if it is a uniform p-adic limit of rational-coefficient classical level-one modular forms: the infimum over n of v_p(a_n−a_(i,n)) tends to +∞.

title: Mod-p filtration of a level-one modular q-series
description: For p≥5 and f∈𝔽_p[[q]] admitting a modular lift, its filtration w(f) is the least nonnegative integer k such that f is the reduction of a weight-k, level-one modular form with p-integral rational Fourier coefficients.

title: P-depleted Bloch–Okounkov functions
description: For a prime p and the signed half-integer coordinate set C_λ, define P_j^(p)(λ)=∑_(c∈C_λ,p∤2c)sgn(c)cʲ, Q₀^(p)=1−1/p and Q_k^(p)=P_(k−1)^(p)/(k−1)!+(1−p^(k−1))β_k for k>0. This is the paper’s regularization of the shifted power sums.

title: Normalized one-point Bloch–Okounkov q-bracket
description: For k≥1, the normalized one-point q-bracket is 𝒬_k(τ)=2^(k−2)(k−1)!⟨Q_k⟩_q. Its p-depleted version is 𝒬_k^(p)=2^(k−2)(k−1)!⟨Q_k^(p)⟩_q. All nonconstant Fourier coefficients of the undepleted series are integral, and both series vanish for odd k.

title: Euler’s totient congruence theorem
description: If a,n are integers with n≥1 and gcd(a,n)=1, then a^φ(n)≡1 modulo n.

title: Kummer congruences for p-regularized Bernoulli numbers
description: Let p≥5 be prime and r≥1. For positive even k₁,k₂ not divisible by p−1 and congruent modulo φ(pʳ), the p-integral rationals (1−p^(k_i−1))B_(k_i)/k_i are congruent modulo pʳ.

title: Quasimodular forms as Serre p-adic modular forms
description: For p≥5, every level-one quasimodular form with rational Fourier coefficients is a Serre p-adic modular form, since E₂,E₄,E₆ belong to the completion and generate the rational quasimodular ring.

title: Meromorphic Jacobi form of integral weight and index
description: For integral k,m and a specified modular subgroup, a meromorphic Jacobi form obeys the weight-k index-m modular transformation and φ(z+rτ+s;τ)=exp(−2πim(r²τ+2rz))φ(z;τ). It may have poles in z, is holomorphic in τ away from its polar divisor, and has at most meromorphic cusp growth. Negative indices are allowed; Fourier expansions are taken in chambers avoiding poles.

title: Elliptic raising operator for Jacobi transformations
description: For a function φ(z;τ) with Jacobi index m, the elliptic raising operator is Y_mφ=(2πi)^(−1)∂φ/∂z+2m(Im z/Im τ)φ. It preserves the index and raises the modular weight by one when applied to a Jacobi-transforming function.

title: Bloch–Okounkov one-point theta formula
description: With F(z;τ)=½∑_(k≥0)⟨Q_k⟩_q(4πiz)^(k−1), one has F(z;τ)=η(τ)³/(2θ₁(2z;τ)), where θ₁(z;τ)=∑_(n∈ℤ)(−1)ⁿq^((n+1/2)²/2)exp(2πiz(n+1/2)). Equivalently θ₁=−i θ[1/2,1/2] in the catalogue’s characteristic convention.

title: Partial-fraction identity for the partition-crank generating function
description: For |q|<1 and w away from the poles, ∏_(n≥1)(1−qⁿ)/((1−wqⁿ)(1−w^(−1)qⁿ))=(1−w)/(q;q)_∞ ∑_(n∈ℤ)(−1)ⁿq^(n(n+1)/2)/(1−wqⁿ).

title: P-adic congruences for depleted Bloch–Okounkov q-brackets
description: Let p≥5 and let positive even k₁,k₂ not divisible by p−1 satisfy k₁≡k₂ mod φ(pʳ). Then 𝒬_(k₁)^(p)≡𝒬_(k₂)^(p) mod pʳ. For positive even k not divisible by p−1, lim_(r→∞)𝒬_(k+φ(pʳ))=𝒬_k^(p), uniformly p-adically, so the depleted q-bracket is a Serre p-adic modular form of weight k.

title: Mod-p filtration of a Bloch–Okounkov q-bracket
description: For a prime p≥5 and a positive even integer k<p−1, the mod-p filtrations of 𝒬_k and 𝒬_k^(p) are both k(p+1)/2.

title: Legendre symbol
description: For an odd prime p and an integer a, the Legendre symbol (a/p) is zero if p divides a, one if a is a nonzero square modulo p, and minus one otherwise.

title: Quasimodularity and correction formula for depleted Bloch–Okounkov q-brackets
description: For p≥5 and positive even k, 𝒬_k^(p) is a weight-k quasimodular form on Γ₀(p²). Moreover 𝒬_k^(p)(τ)=𝒬_k(τ)−p^(k−1)𝒬_k(p²τ)−p^(k−1)f_k^(p)(τ), where f_k^(p)=−∑_(n≥1,p∤n)∑_(M≥0)(−1)ⁿ(2M+1)^(k−1)q^((n²+np(2M+1))/2). The correction is supported on N with Legendre symbols (N/p)=(2/p).

title: Quadratic form over a field of characteristic different from two
description: On a finite-dimensional vector space over a field F with char(F)≠2, a quadratic form is a map Q with Q(ax)=a²Q(x) whose polarization B(x,y)=(Q(x+y)−Q(x)−Q(y))/2 is bilinear. Thus Q(x)=B(x,x).

title: Nondegenerate quadratic space
description: A quadratic space (V,Q) over a field of characteristic different from two is nondegenerate if its polarized bilinear form has zero radical: B(x,y)=0 for every y forces x=0.

title: Positive definite rational quadratic form
description: A quadratic form on a finite-dimensional rational vector space is positive definite if its scalar extension to ℝ has Q(x)>0 for every nonzero vector x.

title: Quadratic Z-lattice
description: A quadratic ℤ-lattice N is a finitely generated free abelian subgroup spanning a finite-dimensional rational quadratic space, equipped with the restricted form Q. It is integral when Q(N)⊆ℤ; the bilinear form B=(Q(x+y)−Q(x)−Q(y))/2 need not then be integer-valued.

title: Localization of a quadratic Z-lattice
description: For a quadratic ℤ-lattice N and a prime p, its localization N_p=ℤ_p⊗_ℤN is a quadratic ℤ_p-lattice with the scalar-extended form inside ℚ_p⊗_ℤN.

title: Coset of a quadratic lattice
description: For a quadratic ℤ-lattice N and ν in its rational span, the coset ν+N carries the values Q(ν+x)=Q(ν)+2B(ν,x)+Q(x). Its conductor is the least positive integer m such that mν∈N.

title: Almost universal integer-valued polynomial
description: An integer-valued polynomial on ℤⁿ is almost universal if it represents every sufficiently large positive integer at an integral argument.

title: Norm ideal of a quadratic lattice
description: The norm ideal n(N) of a quadratic lattice over ℤ or ℤ_p is the fractional ideal generated by all values Q(x) with x∈N; it is integral when the quadratic form is integer-valued.

title: Scale ideal of a quadratic lattice
description: The scale ideal s(N) of a quadratic lattice over ℤ or ℤ_p is the fractional ideal generated by B(x,y) for x,y∈N, where B is the half-polarization of Q.

title: Discriminant square class of a quadratic lattice
description: For a basis e₁,…,e_n of a quadratic lattice, its discriminant is det(B(e_i,e_j)), regarded up to multiplication by the square of a unit of the coefficient ring. Its rational square class is independent of the chosen basis.

title: Isometry of quadratic spaces and lattices
description: An isometry of quadratic spaces is a bijective linear map preserving Q. An isometry of quadratic lattices also carries the underlying lattice onto the target lattice.

title: Isotropic and anisotropic quadratic spaces
description: A quadratic space is isotropic if it has a nonzero vector x with Q(x)=0; otherwise it is anisotropic.

title: Orthogonal direct sum of quadratic spaces
description: For quadratic spaces (V_i,Q_i), their orthogonal direct sum has underlying direct sum and Q((v_i))=∑Q_i(v_i); distinct summands are orthogonal for the polarized form. The same notation applies to lattice decompositions.

title: Orthogonal group of a quadratic space
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space V, O(V) is the group of linear automorphisms preserving Q and O⁺(V)=SO(V) is its determinant-one subgroup. For a lattice N, O(N) and O⁺(N) are the subgroups preserving N.

title: Reflection in an anisotropic vector of a quadratic space
description: If Q(v)≠0, the reflection in v is τ_v(x)=x−2B(x,v)v/Q(v), an isometry of determinant −1 fixing v-perpendicular pointwise.

title: Square-class group of a field
description: For a field F, its square-class group is F×/(F×)², where (F×)² is the subgroup of nonzero squares.

title: Spinor norm of an orthogonal transformation
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space over F of characteristic different from two, the spinor norm θ:O(V)→F×/(F×)² sends a product of reflections τ_(v₁)⋯τ_(v_r) to the square class of ∏Q(v_i). This is independent of the reflection factorization.

title: Genus of a quadratic Z-lattice
description: The genus of a quadratic ℤ-lattice N consists of the isometry classes of lattices whose rational quadratic space is isometric to that of N and which are isometric to N over ℤ_p for every prime p and over ℝ.

title: Proper spinor genus of a quadratic lattice
description: In a rational quadratic space, the proper spinor genus of a lattice is its orbit under rational determinant-one isometries and adelic determinant-one isometries with trivial local spinor norms. It refines the genus and is the spinor-genus convention used in the source’s representation arguments.

title: Primitive representation by a quadratic lattice
description: A scalar t is represented primitively by a quadratic lattice N if Q(x)=t for a primitive vector x∈N. Over ℤ, primitive means x∉mN for every integer m>1; over ℤ_p it means x∉pN.

title: Primitive spinor exception of a positive definite ternary genus
description: A positive integer t is a primitive spinor exception of a positive definite ternary lattice genus if it is represented primitively by the genus but not primitively by every proper spinor genus in it.
