title: Hilbert symbol of a local field
description: For a local field F of characteristic different from two and a,b∈F×, the Hilbert symbol (a,b)_F is +1 if ax²+by²=z² has a nonzero solution in F³ and −1 otherwise; it depends only on the square classes of a and b.

title: Norm subgroup of a finite field extension
description: For a finite field extension L/K, its norm subgroup is N_(L/K)(L×)⊆K×, the image of the multiplicative group under the field norm.

title: Square criterion in a p-adic field Q_p
description: A nonzero p-adic rational a=p^v u with u∈ℤ_p× is a square in ℚ_p exactly when v is even and, for odd p, the residue of u is a square modulo p; for p=2 the condition on u is u≡1 mod 8.

title: Furstenberg positivity for finite i.i.d. unimodular two-dimensional matrix products
description: Let A₁,A₂,… be i.i.d. matrices with a finitely supported law μ on real 2×2 matrices of determinant ±1. If the closed group generated by supp μ is noncompact and strongly irreducible, then lim_(n→∞)n⁻¹log‖A_n⋯A₁‖ exists almost surely and is a strictly positive constant.

title: Kingman’s subadditive ergodic theorem for nonnegative integrable cocycles
description: Let T preserve an ergodic probability measure and let nonnegative integrable functions f_n satisfy f_(n+m)≤f_n+f_m∘T^n. Then f_n/n converges almost surely and in L¹ to the constant inf_(n≥1)E[f_n]/n.

title: Oseledets theorem for finite i.i.d. unimodular two-dimensional products
description: For i.i.d. matrices from a finite subset of GL₂(ℝ) with determinant ±1, there is γ≥0 such that almost surely every nonzero vector has logarithmic growth exponent γ or −γ under A_n⋯A₁; if γ>0 the vectors with exponent −γ form a one-dimensional subspace, and all vectors outside it have exponent γ.

title: Birkhoff pointwise ergodic theorem
description: For a probability-preserving measurable transformation T and f∈L¹, the averages n⁻¹∑_(j=0)^(n−1)f∘T^j converge almost surely and in L¹ to E[f|I], where I is the invariant σ-algebra; if T is ergodic this limit is the constant E[f].

title: Real projective line
description: The real projective line is the space of one-dimensional linear subspaces of ℝ², with the quotient topology from ℝ²∖{0} under nonzero scalar multiplication.

title: Stationary measure for a random projective action
description: For a probability law μ on invertible real matrices acting on the real projective line, a probability measure ν is μ-stationary if ν=∫A_*ν dμ(A), with A_*ν the pushforward under the projective action.

title: Boundary averaging coefficients of harmonic energy measures
description: For a regular harmonic structure with boundary size at least three, D²=−γD (γ>0), boundary fixed points with connected punctured complements, and invertible harmonic extension operators, choose harmonic functions h_k spanning modulo constants. For a cell word w put a_j(w)=∑_k⟨u_j,A_wh_k⟩², with u_j the j-th column of D, and b_j(w)=a_j(w)/∑_i a_i(w). These positive coefficients average boundary limits of harmonic-energy densities to the cell average.

title: Hino’s sharp disk bound for three-boundary harmonic energy coefficients
description: For boundary averaging coefficients b_j(w) of a regular harmonic structure with exactly three boundary points, every finite cell word w satisfies ∑_(j=1)^3 b_j(w)²<1/2. The upper bound is sharp over all cell words.

title: Hino’s radial concentration theorem for three-boundary harmonic energy coefficients
description: For boundary averaging coefficients b_j(w) of a regular harmonic structure with three boundary points, let π:S^N→K be the coding map and ν the chosen sum of harmonic energy measures. If κ is either a full-support Bernoulli product measure with strongly irreducible projected harmonic extension matrices, or a Borel measure with π_*κ≪ν, then ∑_(j=1)^3 b_j(ω₁⋯ω_n)²→1/2 for κ-almost every ω.

title: One-dimensional energy-image density theorem
description: For a strongly local regular symmetric Dirichlet form and a bounded domain function f, the pushforward under f of its energy measure ν_f is absolutely continuous with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Consequently ν_f has no point masses.

title: Jensen gap bounds from second derivatives
description: If f is twice differentiable on [a,b] and m≤f″≤M, then for 0≤v≤1, m v(1−v)(b−a)²/2≤vf(a)+(1−v)f(b)−f(va+(1−v)b)≤M v(1−v)(b−a)²/2.

title: Minkowski product inequality for positive vectors
description: For a_i,b_i>0, (∏_i a_i)¹⁄ⁿ+(∏_i b_i)¹⁄ⁿ≤(∏_i(a_i+b_i))¹⁄ⁿ. Equality holds precisely when the vectors a and b are proportional.

title: Cardinality of finite subsets of an infinite well-ordered set
description: If X is an infinite well-ordered set of cardinality κ, then |X^{<ω}|=|[X]^{<ω}|=κ, and a countable union of sets of cardinality at most κ has cardinality at most κ.

title: Normal topological space
description: A topological space is normal if every two disjoint closed subsets have disjoint open neighborhoods.

title: Urysohn lemma for a normal space
description: If K,L are disjoint closed subsets of a normal space X, there is a continuous f:X→[0,1] with f=0 on K and f=1 on L.

title: Finite continuous partition of unity on a compact Hausdorff space
description: For a finite open cover U₁,…,U_n of compact Hausdorff K, there are continuous nonnegative ψ_i supported in U_i such that ∑ψ_i=1 on K.

title: Weierstrass polynomial approximation theorem
description: Every continuous real function on a compact real interval is a uniform limit of real polynomials.

title: Signed Riesz–Markov representation on a compact Hausdorff space
description: Every bounded real linear functional on C(K), K compact Hausdorff, is integration against a unique finite signed regular Borel measure μ; its operator norm is |μ|(K).

title: Maximal ℓ² domain of a nondegenerate locally finite graph Laplacian
description: For a locally finite weighted graph with inf_x m(x)>0, its Dirichlet and Neumann energy forms coincide, and their self-adjoint Laplacian has domain {f∈ℓ²(V,m):Δf∈ℓ²(V,m)}.

title: ℓᵖ contractivity and ℓ² smoothing of the minimal graph heat semigroup
description: The minimal heat semigroup of a locally finite weighted graph is contractive on ℓᵖ(V,m),1≤p≤∞. For t>0 and f∈ℓ² it has P_tf∈D(L); for f∈D(L), LP_tf=P_tLf.

title: Principal real power on the right half-plane
description: For Re z>0 and α∈ℝ, z^α=exp(α Log z), where Log z is the holomorphic logarithm real on positive real numbers. This fixes the branch used for Bergman kernels (1−z w̄)^(−α).

title: Dirichlet series
description: A Dirichlet series is ∑_(n≥1)a_n n^(−s), with complex coefficients and n^(−s)=exp(−s log n), considered on a right half-plane where it converges.

title: Dirichlet polynomial
description: A Dirichlet polynomial is a finite sum ∑_(n≤N)a_n n^(−s) with complex coefficients.

title: Multiplicative arithmetic function
description: An arithmetic function a:ℕ₊→ℂ is multiplicative if a(1)=1 and a(mn)=a(m)a(n) whenever gcd(m,n)=1.

title: Euler product of a Dirichlet series
description: For a multiplicative coefficient function a, an absolutely convergent Dirichlet series factors as ∑a(n)n^(−s)=∏_(p prime)(∑_(j≥0)a(pʲ)p^(−js)). An Euler-product representation specifies these local factors and its domain of convergence.

title: Entire function of finite order
description: An entire function f has finite order if for some finite positive C,A one has |f(z)|≤exp(C(1+|z|)^A) throughout ℂ.

title: Selberg class of Dirichlet series
description: The Selberg class consists of Dirichlet series L(s)=∑a(n)n^(−s) with a(1)=1 and a(n)=O_ε(n^ε) for every ε>0, for which (s−1)^mL(s) is entire of finite order for some m≥0, and Λ(s)=Qˢ∏Γ(λ_js+μ_j)L(s) satisfies Λ(s)=ω overline(Λ(1−bar(s))) with Q,λ_j>0, Re μ_j≥0 and |ω|=1. Its Euler product has log L_p(s)=∑_(j≥1)b(pʲ)p^(−js), with b(pʲ)=O(p^(jδ)) for some δ<1/2. Its degree is d_L=2∑λ_j.

title: Selberg-class function with a polynomial Euler product
description: A Selberg-class function has a polynomial Euler product of length m if L_p(s)=∏_(j=1)^m(1−α_j(p)p^(−s))^(−1) for every prime p, with fixed m; its Ramanujan bound implies |α_j(p)|≤1. The length m need not equal the functional-equation degree.

title: Right-half-plane zero-counting function
description: For a meromorphic L-function with isolated zeros, N_L(σ,T) counts its nontrivial zeros ρ=β+iγ with β>σ and 0<γ≤T, with multiplicity. A power-saving zero-density estimate bounds this by O(T^(1−η)) for some η>0.

title: Resonance method for large values of a Dirichlet series
description: Choose a Dirichlet polynomial R(t)=∑r(n)n^(−it) and a nonnegative smooth weight Φ, then compare M₂=∫L(σ+it)|R(t)|²Φ(t/T)dt with M₁=∫|R(t)|²Φ(t/T)dt. The inequality max|L|≥|M₂|/M₁ turns a coefficient choice making the weighted correlation large into a large-value bound.

title: Rankin’s trick for nonnegative arithmetic sums
description: For a_n≥0, x>0 and δ>0, one has ∑_(n>x)a_n≤x^(−δ)∑_(n≥1)a_n n^δ whenever the sum on the right is finite.

title: Distance from a real number to the nearest integer
description: For x∈ℝ, ‖x‖=min_(k∈ℤ)|x−k| is its distance to the nearest integer, taking values in [0,1/2].

title: Kronecker approximation theorem for a continuous flow
description: If λ₁,…,λ_n are real numbers linearly independent over ℚ, then for every β∈ℝⁿ and ε>0 there exists t∈ℝ with max_j‖tλ_j−β_j‖<ε.

title: Chen’s weighted quantitative Kronecker approximation theorem
description: Let M≥1, λ,β∈ℝⁿ satisfy u·β∈ℤ whenever u∈ℤⁿ, |u_j|≤M and u·λ=0. For δ_j>0, Δ=∑δ_j, T₁<T₂, and Λ=min{|u·λ|:u∈ℤⁿ, |u_j|≤M, u·λ≠0}, one has inf_(T₁≤t<T₂)∑δ_j‖tλ_j−β_j‖²≤(Δ/4)sin²(π/(2(M+1)))+ΔMⁿ/(4πΛ(T₂−T₁)), provided the defining minimum for Λ is nonempty.

title: Mellin inversion formula for the exponential function
description: For x>0 and c>0, e^(−x)=(2πi)^(−1)∫_(c−i∞)^(c+i∞)Γ(w)x^(−w)dw, interpreted as the limit of integrals over vertical segments.

title: Stirling estimate for gamma on vertical lines
description: Uniformly for σ in a fixed compact real interval and |t|→∞, |Γ(σ+it)|=sqrt(2π)|t|^(σ−1/2)e^(−π|t|/2)(1+O(1/|t|)).

title: Aistleitner–Pańkowski resonance lower bound in the Selberg class
description: Let L be in the polynomial-Euler-product Selberg class with length m and ∑_(p≤x)|a(p)|²=(κ+o(1))x/log x, κ>0. For fixed 1/2≤σ<1 and large T, max_(T≤t≤2T)|L(σ+it)|≥exp((C_L(σ)+o(1))(log T)^(1−σ)/(log log T)^θ), where θ=1/2 at σ=1/2 and θ=1 otherwise, C_L(1/2)=sqrt(κ), and C_L(σ)=κ^σ m^(1−2σ)(3−2σ)^(3/2−σ)/(2sqrt(2σ−1)) for σ>1/2.

title: Aistleitner–Pańkowski large logarithmic values from zero density
description: Let L be in the Selberg class, 1/2≤σ<1 and θ∈ℝ. Suppose N_L(σ,T)=O(T^(1−η)) for some η>0 and ∑_(p≤x)|a(p)|=(κ+o(1))x/log x, κ>0. For all large T, max_(T≤t≤2T)Re(e^(−iθ)log L(σ+it))≥c_(κ,η)(log T)^(1−σ)/log log T, with c_(κ,η)=((1−e^(−1))κ/4)(η/(4sqrt(e)))^(1−σ). The logarithm is continued from the Euler-product half-plane along zero-free horizontal paths.

title: Aistleitner–Pańkowski lower bound on the one-line
description: Suppose L is in the Selberg class and ∑_(p≤x)|a(p)|=κx/log x+O(x/log²x), κ>0. For every real θ and all sufficiently large T there are σ>1 and t∈[T,2T] with Re(e^(−iθ)log L(σ+it))≥κ log log log T+O(1). In particular |L(1+it)|=Ω((log log t)^κ) as t→∞.

title: Conditional upper bounds for Selberg-class large values
description: Let L be in the Selberg class with no zeros in Re s>1/2 and ∑_(p≤x)|a(p)|=(κ+o(1))x/log x, κ>0. For fixed 1/2≤σ<1 there is c>0 with |L(σ+it)|≪exp(c(log t)^(2−2σ)/log log t). If the prime coefficient mean has error O(x/log²x), then |L(1+it)|≪(log log t)^κ.

title: Continuous-time supermartingale
description: An integrable adapted process M on a filtered probability space is a supermartingale if E[M_t|F_s]≤M_s almost surely for every s≤t; the term refers to a continuous time parameter and does not require continuous sample paths.

title: Continuous functions vanishing at infinity
description: For a locally compact Hausdorff space E, C₀(E) is the space of continuous real functions f for which {x:|f(x)|≥ε} is compact for every ε>0, with the supremum norm.

title: Feller Markov semigroup
description: A Markov transition semigroup P_t on a locally compact separable metric space E is Feller if it maps C₀(E) into itself and ‖P_tf−f‖∞→0 as t↓0 for every f∈C₀(E).

title: Generator of a Feller semigroup
description: For a Feller semigroup P_t on C₀(E), its generator is Af=lim_(t↓0)(P_tf−f)/t in the supremum norm, with domain those f∈C₀(E) for which this limit exists. Extended generators on unbounded functions require a separately specified martingale-domain convention.

title: Usual stochastic order for finite measures on the real line
description: For finite positive Borel measures μ and ν of equal mass on ℝ, μ≤_stν means μ([a,∞))≤ν([a,∞)) for every real a; for probabilities this is equivalently domination of expectations of bounded increasing measurable functions.

title: Stochastically monotone Markov semigroup on the half-line
description: A Markov transition semigroup P_t on [0,∞) is stochastically monotone if P_t(x,·)≤_stP_t(y,·) whenever x≤y, for every t≥0.

title: Stochastic domination of Markov semigroups on the half-line
description: A Markov semigroup P_t on [0,∞) is stochastically dominated by Q_t if P_t(x,·)≤_stQ_t(x,·) for every x≥0 and t≥0.

title: Weighted total variation norm of a signed measure
description: For a measurable weight V≥1 and a signed measure μ, its weighted variation norm is ‖μ‖_V=sup{|∫f dμ|:f measurable, |f|≤V}, allowing infinity. The convention V=1 is the full total variation norm, twice the usual supremum-over-events distance for differences of probability measures.

title: V-uniform ergodicity of a continuous-time Markov process
description: A Markov semigroup P_t is V-uniformly ergodic with rate κ>0 if it has a unique invariant probability π and a finite constant D such that ‖P_t(x,·)−π‖_V≤DV(x)e^(−κt) for all x and t≥0, for a fixed measurable V≥1.

title: Geometric Foster–Lyapunov condition for a continuous-time generator
description: For a specified extended generator A of a Markov process, a continuous function V≥1 in its declared domain satisfies a geometric drift condition if AV≤−kV+b1_C for constants k>0,b<∞ and a specified compact or small set C; the domain and small-set convention are part of the chosen route.

title: Stopped modified Lyapunov function at the origin
description: For a half-line Markov process X and τ₀=inf{t≥0:X_t=0}, a function V≥1 is a stopped modified Lyapunov function with constant k>0 when V(X_(t∧τ₀))+k∫₀^(t∧τ₀)V(X_s)ds is a supermartingale for each initial state.

title: Reflected Itô diffusion on the positive half-line
description: A continuous adapted process Y_t≥0 solves a reflected Itô equation if Y_t=Y₀+∫₀ᵗg(Y_s)ds+∫₀ᵗσ(Y_s)dW_s+L_t, where L is continuous, adapted, nondecreasing, starts at zero and can increase only when Y_t=0.

title: Finite-activity reflected jump-diffusion on the half-line
description: A half-line reflected diffusion with coefficients g,σ is pieced together with jumps having a state-dependent finite destination measure ν_x: while at x, jumps occur at rate ν_x([0,∞)) and land with normalized law ν_x/ν_x([0,∞)), when this rate is positive. Bounded jump rates ensure no finite-time accumulation; the zero-rate case has no jumps.

title: Two rank-based finite-activity Lévy particles
description: Two real particles are driven by the upper and lower coordinates of a two-dimensional Lévy process with finite jump measure, drift vector (g₊,g₋) and positive definite covariance: the particle currently ranked higher uses the upper driver and the lower-ranked particle uses the lower driver, with a declared rule resolving ties. The ranked gap is the difference of their ordered positions.

title: Differentiation under an integral with an integrable derivative bound
description: Let I be an open real interval, (X,μ) a σ-finite measure space and f:I×X→ℝ measurable. Suppose f(t₀,·) is integrable for some t₀∈I and, outside one μ-null set, t↦f(t,x) is differentiable on I with |∂_tf(t,x)|≤g(x) for an integrable g. Then F(t)=∫f(t,x)dμ(x) is differentiable on I and F′(t)=∫∂_tf(t,x)dμ(x). The same conclusion is local when the bound holds on a neighborhood of the point in question.

title: Projective space over a field
description: For a field F, projective n-space consists of nonzero vectors in F^(n+1) modulo multiplication by nonzero scalars; points are written [x₀:⋯:x_n]. Homogeneous polynomial equations define its projective algebraic subsets.

title: Elliptic curve over a characteristic-zero field
description: Over a characteristic-zero field F, an elliptic curve can be presented as a nonsingular projective cubic y²z=x³+Axz²+Bz³ with A,B∈F and 4A³+27B²≠0, with distinguished point O=[0:1:0] and the chord-and-tangent abelian group law. Curves are identified by F-isomorphisms preserving O.

title: Isogeny of elliptic curves in characteristic zero
description: An isogeny φ:E→E′ over F is a nonconstant algebraic group homomorphism of elliptic curves preserving O. Its degree equals the order of its finite geometric kernel in characteristic zero. A cyclic isogeny has a cyclic kernel.

title: Dual isogeny of an elliptic-curve isogeny
description: For an isogeny φ:E→E′ of degree n, the dual isogeny φ̂:E′→E satisfies φ̂φ=[n] on E and φφ̂=[n] on E′.

title: Torsion subgroup E[n] of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over F, E[n] is the subgroup of E(F̄) annihilated by multiplication by n. In characteristic zero it is a free rank-two ℤ/nℤ-module with its natural action of Gal(F̄/F).

title: Division field of an elliptic curve
description: The n-division field F(E[n]) is the extension of F generated by the affine coordinates of all n-torsion points of an elliptic curve E/F. It is finite Galois, and its Galois group acts faithfully on E[n].

title: Galois representation on elliptic-curve torsion
description: For an elliptic curve E/F in characteristic zero, the natural action on E[n] gives ρ_(E,n):Gal(F̄/F)→Aut(E[n])≅GL₂(ℤ/nℤ) after choosing a basis; its kernel fixes the division field F(E[n]).

title: Quadratic twist of an elliptic curve
description: For E:y²=x³+Ax+B over a characteristic-zero field F and D∈F×/(F×)², the quadratic twist E^D is y²=x³+D²Ax+D³B. It becomes isomorphic to E over F(√D), with Galois descent changed by the associated quadratic character.

title: Abelian group with a group action
description: A G-module is an abelian group M equipped with an action of G by abelian-group automorphisms. A morphism is a group homomorphism commuting with the G-actions.

title: Cohomology of a group with abelian coefficients
description: For a G-module M, Hⁿ(G,M)=ker(d:Cⁿ→C^(n+1))/im(d:C^(n−1)→Cⁿ), where Cⁿ consists of maps Gⁿ→M and (df)(g₁,…,g_(n+1))=g₁f(g₂,…)+∑_(i=1)^n(−1)^if(…,g_ig_(i+1),…)+(−1)^(n+1)f(g₁,…,g_n). For a profinite G and a discrete M, use continuous cochains.

title: First group cohomology with abelian coefficients
description: For a G-module M, H¹(G,M) is the abelian group of cocycles f(gh)=f(g)+g·f(h), modulo coboundaries f(g)=g·m−m. For profinite G and discrete M, the cocycles are continuous.

title: Cyclic restriction kernel in first group cohomology
description: For a finite group G and a G-module M, H¹_loc(G,M)=ker(H¹(G,M)→∏_(C≤G cyclic)H¹(C,M)). It records cohomology classes whose restrictions to every cyclic subgroup vanish.

title: Local-global divisibility problem for elliptic-curve points
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F and an integer m>1, the local-global divisibility question asks whether a point P∈E(F) divisible by m in E(F_v) for all but finitely many finite places v must already be divisible by m in E(F).

title: Tate module of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E in characteristic zero and a prime ℓ, T_ℓ(E)=lim←E[ℓⁿ], with transition maps multiplication by ℓ. It is a rank-two ℤ_ℓ-module with a continuous Galois action.

title: Complex multiplication of an elliptic curve
description: An elliptic curve E in characteristic zero has complex multiplication if End_(F̄)(E) strictly contains ℤ; the extra endomorphisms form an order in an imaginary quadratic field.

title: Weil pairing on elliptic-curve torsion
description: For an elliptic curve E in characteristic zero, the Weil pairing e_n:E[n]×E[n]→μ_n is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear pairing, equivariant under Galois. Consequently the determinant of ρ_(E,n) is the cyclotomic character modulo n.

title: Cohomology formulas for a finite cyclic group
description: For G=⟨g⟩ of order n acting on M, put N=1+g+⋯+g^(n−1). Then H¹(G,M)=ker N/(g−1)M and H²(G,M)=M^G/NM. The formulas extend periodically to positive odd and even degrees.

title: Vanishing of finite-group cohomology when the group order is invertible
description: For a finite group G and a G-module M on which multiplication by |G| is invertible, Hⁿ(G,M)=0 for every n>0.

title: Lawson–Wuthrich classification of first torsion cohomology over Q
description: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve, p prime and G=Gal(ℚ(E[p])/ℚ). Then H¹(G,E[p]) vanishes except in exactly these cases: p=3 and E has a rational point of order 3 and a unique rational cyclic 3-isogeny; p=5 and E^5 has a rational point of order 5 and a unique rational cyclic 5-isogeny; or p=11 and E is ℚ-isomorphic to the Cremona curve 121c2, y²+xy=x³+x²−3632x+82757. In every exceptional case the cohomology group has p elements.

title: Lawson–Wuthrich classification of prime-power torsion cohomology over Q
description: Let E/ℚ be elliptic, p>3, G_i=Gal(ℚ(E[p^i])/ℚ). The groups H¹(G_i,E[p^i]) vanish for every i≥2 exactly when (E,p) is outside the following list: p∈{5,7} and E has rational p-torsion; p=5 and E has a rational 5-isogeny and E^5 has rational 5-torsion; p=5 and E→E′ is a rational 5-isogeny, E has no rational cyclic 25-isogeny, and (E′)^5 has rational 5-torsion; p=5 and E→E′→E″ is a rational cyclic 25-isogeny with rational 5-torsion on E′; or p=11 and E is Cremona 121c1 or 121c2. Vanishing for i=2 is equivalent to vanishing for all i≥2.

title: Prime-power local-global divisibility for elliptic curves over Q
description: For a prime p and i≥1, local-global divisibility by p^i has a positive answer for every elliptic curve over ℚ exactly when p>3 or p^i is 2 or 3. Thus powers of 2 or 3 of exponent at least two admit counterexamples.

title: Lawson–Wuthrich counterexample to local-global divisibility by nine
description: On the elliptic curve E:y²+y=x³+20 over ℚ, let P=(−2,3). The point 3P is divisible by 9 in E(ℚ_ℓ) for every prime ℓ≠3, but it is not divisible by 9 in E(ℚ). The curve has Cremona label 243a2.

title: Weak Feller Markov semigroup
description: A Markov transition semigroup P_t on a metric state space is weak Feller if P_tf is bounded and continuous for every bounded continuous real function f and every t≥0. This condition does not assert preservation of functions vanishing at infinity.

title: Extended martingale generator of a Markov process
description: A pair of Borel functions (f,Af) belongs to the extended martingale generator of a Markov process X when ∫₀ᵗ|Af(X_s)|ds is locally finite and f(X_t)−f(X₀)−∫₀ᵗAf(X_s)ds is a local martingale under every initial state, using the declared filtration and localization convention.

title: Well-posedness of bounded-rate reflected jump-diffusions on the half-line
description: Suppose g and σ are globally Lipschitz on [0,∞), inf σ>0, and ν_x are finite positive Borel destination measures such that x↦∫f dν_x is continuous for every bounded continuous f and sup_xν_x([0,∞))<∞. Piecing out reflected diffusions with jump measure ν_x yields a unique-in-law nonexplosive weak Feller strong Markov family. Its extended generator on bounded C² test functions with f′(0)=0 is Af(x)=g(x)f′(x)+σ(x)²f″(x)/2+∫(f(y)−f(x))dν_x(y).

title: Compact topological dynamical system with an invertible map
description: A compact topological dynamical system (X,T) consists of a compact Hausdorff space X and a homeomorphism T:X→X; in the metric version X is compact metrizable.

title: Topological entropy of a map of a compact metric space
description: For a continuous self-map T of compact metric X, let s_n(ε) be the largest size of a set whose distinct points have max_(0≤j<n)d(Tʲx,Tʲy)>ε. Its topological entropy is h_top(T)=sup_(ε>0)limsup_(n→∞)n^(−1)log s_n(ε).

title: Möbius-orthogonal bounded sequence
description: A bounded complex sequence a_n is Möbius-orthogonal if lim_(N→∞)N^(−1)∑_(n=1)^N μ(n)a_n=0, where μ is the Möbius function.

title: State of a C*-algebra
description: A state on a C*-algebra is a positive complex linear functional of norm one; on a unital C*-algebra this is equivalent to positivity and ρ(1)=1.

title: Star representation of a C*-algebra
description: A star representation of a C*-algebra A on a complex Hilbert space H is a star-preserving algebra homomorphism π:A→B(H). It is cyclic if π(A)ξ is dense in H for some vector ξ.

title: Completely positive map between C*-algebras
description: A linear map φ:A→B between C*-algebras is completely positive if every entrywise amplification M_n(A)→M_n(B) sends positive matrices to positive matrices. It is contractive if its operator norm is at most one.

title: Voiculescu–Brown entropy of a C*-algebra automorphism
description: For an exact C*-algebra A with faithful representation π and automorphism α, let rcp(π,Ω,δ) be the least rank of a finite-dimensional C*-algebra B through which contractive completely positive maps approximate π on finite Ω within δ; rank is the dimension of a maximal abelian subalgebra. The entropy is sup_(Ω,δ)limsup_(n→∞)n^(−1)log rcp(π,⋃_(j=0)^(n−1)αʲΩ,δ).

title: Contractive approximation entropy of a Banach-space isometry
description: For an isometric automorphism α of a Banach space X, choose an isometric embedding ι:X→Y admitting finite-set approximations through contractive maps X→ℓ∞^d→Y. Let rc(Ω,δ) be the least such d for error below δ on finite Ω. The contractive approximation entropy is sup_(Ω,δ)limsup_(n→∞)n^(−1)log rc(⋃_(j=0)^(n−1)αʲΩ,δ).

title: Unitary element of a unital C*-algebra
description: In a unital C*-algebra A, an element u is unitary if u*u=uu*=1; equivalently its adjoint is its inverse.

title: Noncommutative torus C*-algebra
description: For a real skew-symmetric d×d matrix Θ, the noncommutative torus A_Θ is the universal unital C*-algebra generated by unitaries u₁,…,u_d with u_ju_k=exp(2πiΘ_jk)u_ku_j. Universality means any unitary tuple satisfying these relations determines a unique unital star homomorphism from A_Θ. This denotes the C*-completion, not just its dense smooth subalgebra.

title: Noncommutative toral automorphism
description: For S=(s_ij)∈GL_d(ℤ) with SᵀΘS≡Θ modulo integer matrices, the noncommutative toral automorphism α_S of A_Θ sends the generator u_j to u₁^(s_1j)⋯u_d^(s_dj), in that fixed order.

title: Nilpotent group
description: A group G is d-step nilpotent if its lower central series G₁=G, G_(j+1)=[G_j,G], generated by the indicated commutators, satisfies G_(d+1)={1}. A nilpotent group is d-step nilpotent for some finite d.

title: Finitely generated group
description: A group is finitely generated if some finite set of elements and their inverses generates the whole group.

title: Compact nilmanifold
description: A compact d-step nilmanifold is G/Γ where G is a d-step nilpotent real Lie group and Γ is a discrete cocompact subgroup. G need not be connected in this convention.

title: Nilsystem
description: A d-step nilsystem is a compact nilmanifold X=G/Γ with the homeomorphism x↦gx given by left translation by a fixed g∈G.

title: Nilsequence
description: A basic nilsequence has the form a_n=F(gⁿx), n∈ℤ, for continuous complex F on a compact nilmanifold and a nilrotation x↦gx. A nilsequence is a uniform limit of basic nilsequences, allowing their nilpotency steps to vary; a d-step nilsequence uses a fixed step bound d.

title: Symmetric Cesàro-null bounded sequence
description: A bounded complex sequence (a_n)_(n∈ℤ) is symmetric Cesàro-null if (2N+1)^(−1)∑_(n=−N)^N|a_n|→0. For bounded sequences this is equivalent to the same condition with |a_n|².

title: Almost nilsequence with a symmetric Cesàro-null remainder
description: An almost nilsequence in this convention is a bounded complex sequence a_n=b_n+c_n where b is a nilsequence and c is symmetric Cesàro-null.

title: Integer-valued polynomial on Z
description: An integer-valued polynomial is a polynomial p∈ℚ[x] satisfying p(n)∈ℤ for every n∈ℤ. Its coefficients need not all be integers; for example x(x−1)/2 is allowed.

title: Polynomial sequence in a nilpotent group
description: For a nilpotent group G, a sequence g:ℤ→G is polynomial if some iterate of the difference Dg(n)=g(n)^(−1)g(n+1) is identically one. Equivalently it can be written U₁^(p₁(n))⋯U_r^(p_r(n)) with fixed U_j∈G and integer-valued polynomials p_j.

title: Compact vector in a unitary representation
description: For a unitary action of G on H, a vector u is compact if its orbit Gu has compact closure in Hilbert norm. The compact-vector subspace H_c(G) is the closed span of finite-dimensional invariant subspaces.

title: Equidistribution of a sequence modulo one
description: A real sequence x_n is equidistributed modulo one if, for every interval I⊆[0,1), the proportion of n with fractional part in I tends to the length of I; for a two-sided sequence use centered intervals [−N,N].

title: Weyl equidistribution theorem for real polynomials
description: If a real polynomial has at least one irrational coefficient of positive degree, then its values on the integers are equidistributed modulo one.

title: Gelfand–Naimark–Segal representation theorem for a state
description: For every state ρ on a C*-algebra A there are a Hilbert space H_ρ, a star representation π_ρ:A→B(H_ρ) and a unit cyclic vector ξ_ρ with ρ(a)=⟨π_ρ(a)ξ_ρ,ξ_ρ⟩. The cyclic representation is unique up to a unitary carrying the cyclic vector to the other one.

title: Green–Tao Möbius orthogonality for nilsequences
description: Every nilsequence (a_n) is Möbius-orthogonal: N^(−1)∑_(n=1)^N μ(n)a_n→0. This qualitative consequence extends the basic nilmanifold theorem to uniform limits.

title: Kronecker’s root-of-unity theorem
description: If a monic integer polynomial has only nonzero complex roots, all of modulus at most one, then every root is a root of unity.

title: Kerr–Li entropy lower bound for a noncommutative toral automorphism
description: If α_S is a noncommutative toral automorphism and λ_i are the eigenvalues of S, counted with multiplicity, then ht(α_S)≥½∑_(|λ_i|>1)log|λ_i|.

title: Leibman’s compact-vector criterion for nilpotent unitary actions
description: If a finitely generated nilpotent group G=⟨T₁,…,T_r⟩ acts unitarily on H, then H_c(G)=⋂_(T∈G)H_c(T)=⋂_(j=1)^rH_c(T_j).

title: Bergelson–Leibman polynomial mean-ergodic theorem on the rational complement
description: Let G be a finitely generated nilpotent unitary group on H and g:ℤ→G a polynomial sequence with g(0)=1. Let E=⟨g(ℤ)⟩ and H_rat=⋃_(l≥1){u:P^l u=u for every P∈E}. If u⊥H_rat, then (2N+1)^(−1)∑_(n=−N)^Ng(n)u→0 in Hilbert norm.

title: Nilsequence decomposition of polynomial matrix coefficients of nilpotent unitary actions
description: Let U₁,…,U_d be unitary operators generating a nilpotent group and let p_j be integer-valued polynomials. For all u,v in the Hilbert space, the sequence ⟨U₁^(p₁(n))⋯U_d^(p_d(n))u,v⟩ is the sum of a nilsequence and a symmetric Cesàro-null bounded sequence. Equivalently this holds for every polynomial sequence in a finitely generated nilpotent unitary group.

title: Almost-nilsequence states of zero-entropy noncommutative toral automorphisms
description: Let A_Θ be a noncommutative torus and α_S its noncommutative toral automorphism. If ht(α_S)=0, then for every state ρ and every a∈A_Θ the sequence ρ(α_Sⁿ(a)), n∈ℤ, is a nilsequence plus a symmetric Cesàro-null bounded sequence. Consequently it is Möbius-orthogonal.

title: Purely atomic finite measure
description: A finite measure is purely atomic if it is a countable sum ∑_j a_jδ_{x_j} of positive point masses, with ∑_j a_j<∞; finite signed measures are purely atomic when their total variation is.

title: Support of a Radon measure
description: The support of a nonnegative Radon measure on a topological space is the complement of the union of its open null sets; equivalently, it consists of points whose every open neighborhood has positive measure.

title: Atomicity of Radon measures on scattered compacta
description: Every finite Radon measure on a compact Hausdorff scattered space is purely atomic; the same holds for finite signed regular measures via total variation.

title: Fréchet–Urysohn property of finite-subset compacta
description: For every set X and n<∞, σ_n(2^X) is a compact Hausdorff Fréchet–Urysohn space.

title: Real ℓ² space indexed by an arbitrary set
description: For a set X, ℓ²(X;ℝ) consists of families a_x with sup_{F⊂X finite}∑_{x∈F}|a_x|²<∞, with norm given by the square root of that supremum and the corresponding sum inner product.

title: Orthonormal coordinates for a real Hilbert space
description: Every real Hilbert space H is linearly isometric to ℓ²(X;ℝ) for an orthonormal basis indexed by some set X; the coordinates of h are its inner products with the basis vectors.

title: Extension norms between finite-subset compacta at large cardinals
description: For 1≤m<n and |X|≥ℵ_{n−1}, η(σ_m(2^X),σ_n(2^X))=∑_{k=0}^m binom(n,k)binom(n−k−1,m−k).

title: Spectral theorem for a self-adjoint Hilbert-space operator
description: A densely defined self-adjoint operator A has a unique projection-valued measure E on ℝ such that A=∫λ dE(λ), with D(A)={x:∫λ²d⟨E(λ)x,x⟩<∞}; measurable functions of A are defined by the same spectral integration.

title: One-dimensional Sobolev interpolation into derivative sup norms
description: For integers 0≤j<N, there is C_{N,j} such that ||u^(j)||∞≤C_{N,j}(||u||₂+||u^(N)||₂)^a||u||₂^(1−a) for u∈H^N(0,1), where a=(j+1/2)/N.

title: Density of Schwartz functions in finite-exponent Euclidean Lᵖ
description: For 1≤p<∞, Schwartz functions are dense in Lᵖ(ℝᵈ); in particular compactly supported smooth functions are dense.

title: Fourier transform of a Gaussian
description: For a>0 and the transform f̂(ξ)=∫e^(−ix·ξ)f(x)dx on ℝᵈ, the transform of exp(−a|x|²) is (π/a)^(d/2)exp(−|ξ|²/(4a)).

title: Yosida approximation of a maximal monotone relation
description: For a maximal monotone relation A on a Hilbert space and λ>0, J_λ=(I+λA)⁻¹ is its resolvent and A_λ=λ⁻¹(I−J_λ) is its Yosida approximation, a single-valued Lipschitz monotone map.

title: Metric projection onto a closed convex Hilbert subset
description: For a nonempty closed convex subset C of a Hilbert space H, each x∈H has a unique nearest point P_Cx∈C, characterized by Re⟨x−P_Cx,y−P_Cx⟩≤0 for every y∈C.

title: Minimal section of a maximal monotone relation
description: The minimal section A⁰ of a maximal monotone Hilbert-space relation A sends x∈D(A) to the unique element of the nonempty closed convex set A(x) having minimum norm.

title: Strong–weak closedness of maximal monotone graphs
description: If A is maximal monotone on a Hilbert space, x_n→x strongly and y_n⇀y weakly with y_n∈Ax_n, then y∈Ax.

title: Resolvent and Yosida estimates for maximal monotone relations
description: For maximal monotone A, J_λ is nonexpansive, A_λ is λ⁻¹-Lipschitz and monotone, A_λx∈A(J_λx), and for x∈D(A), A_λx→A⁰x with ||A_λx||≤||A⁰x||.

title: Weak sequential compactness of bounded Hilbert sequences
description: Every bounded sequence in a Hilbert space has a weakly convergent subsequence.

title: Minty surjectivity theorem in Hilbert space
description: A monotone relation A on a Hilbert space is maximal monotone if and only if ran(I+λA)=H for one, equivalently every, λ>0.

title: Lipschitz monotone perturbation of a maximal monotone relation
description: If A is maximal monotone on a Hilbert space and B:H→H is monotone and globally Lipschitz, then A+B is maximal monotone.

title: Endpoint traces of one-dimensional Sobolev functions
description: Every u∈H^N(0,1;𝕂ᵈ), N≥1, has continuous representatives for derivatives of order j<N and bounded linear traces u↦u^(j)(0),u^(j)(1). The complete endpoint jet map onto 𝕂^(2Nd) is surjective.

title: Dissipative boundary interconnection with a nonlinear controller
description: Given a boundary system (𝔄,𝔅,𝔠) on X and a controller relation M_c on X_c×U, its feedback relation on X×X_c sends (x,x_c) to (𝔄x,z_c) when (z_c,𝔅x)∈M_c(x_c,𝔠x); its domain imposes that boundary condition.

title: Local Taylor remainder estimate for one-dimensional Sobolev functions
Monoid
description: A monoid is a semigroup with an element1 satisfying1x=x1=x for every x.

title: Minimal unitization of an invariant-metric semigroup
description: Every semigroup with a two-sided translation-invariant metric is either a metric monoid or the nonidentity part of a unique smallest metric monoid, up to an isomorphism fixing the original semigroup. Distances to the adjoined identity satisfy d(1,b)=d(b,b²).

title: Mogul’skii–Ottaviani–Skorohod inequalities in metric semigroups
description: For independent X_i in a separable invariant-metric semigroup, S_k=X₁⋯X_k and m≤n, P(min_{m≤k≤n}d(z₁,z₀S_k)≤a) min_{m≤k≤n}P(d(S_k,S_n)≤b)≤P(d(z₁,z₀S_n)≤a+b). Replacing the minimum event by max≥a gives the upper-tail bound with terminal distance≥a−b.

title: Kolmogorov zero-one law
description: For a sequence of independent random elements, every event in the tail σ-algebra ⋂_nσ(X_k:k≥n) has probability zero or one.

title: Tail-count comparison for independent maxima
description: For independent nonnegative random variables Y_i, let M=sup_iY_i and q(t)=∑_iP(Y_i>t). Then q(t)/(1+q(t))≤P(M>t)≤min(1,q(t)), with the left side interpreted as1 when q=∞.

title: Inverse tail-count function of a random-variable family
description: For nonnegative random variables Y_i, their inverse tail-count function on (0,1] is ℓ(t)=inf{y>0:∑_iP(Y_i>y)≤t}, extended by0 off[0,1] with endpoint conventions specified separately.

title: Convex subdifferential on a Banach space
description: For a proper convex f:X→(−∞,∞] on a real Banach space, ∂f(x)={x*∈X*:f(y)≥f(x)+⟨x*,y−x⟩ for all y∈X}, with empty value outside domf.

title: Local boundedness of a set-valued map
description: A map T:X⇒Y into a normed space is locally bounded at x if some neighborhood U of x has bounded union ⋃_{u∈U}T(u). It is locally bounded on its domain if this holds at every x with T(x)≠∅.

title: Essential smoothness of a Banach convex function
description: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function on a real Banach space is essentially smooth if its convex subdifferential is single-valued and locally bounded on its domain.

title: Strictly convex function
description: A real-valued or extended-real function f on a real vector space is strictly convex if f((1−t)x+ty)<(1−t)f(x)+tf(y) for distinct x,y in its effective domain and0<t<1.

title: Essential strict convexity in Banach space
description: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function f on a real Banach space is essentially strictly convex if (∂f)⁻¹ is locally bounded on its domain and f is strictly convex on every convex subset of dom∂f.

title: Legendre function on a Banach space
description: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function on a real Banach space is Legendre if it is both essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex.

title: Usual conditions for a filtration
description: A filtration on a probability space satisfies the usual conditions if it is right-continuous, F_t=⋂_(s>t)F_s, and F₀ contains every subset of every null set of the ambient probability space.

title: Uniformly integrable family of real random variables
description: A family of integrable real random variables (X_i) is uniformly integrable if lim_(K→∞)sup_iE[|X_i|1_(|X_i|>K)]=0.

title: Stochastic process of class D
description: An adapted process X on a declared time interval is of class D if the random variables X_τ, over all finite stopping times τ taking values in that interval, form a uniformly integrable family. On a finite horizon [0,T], this means all stopping times τ≤T.

title: Optional stochastic process
description: A process is optional if it is measurable for the optional σ-algebra on time×sample space, the σ-algebra generated by adapted càdlàg processes.

title: Strong optional supermartingale
description: An optional process X is a strong supermartingale if X_τ is integrable for every bounded stopping time τ and E[X_τ|F_σ]≤X_σ almost surely whenever σ≤τ are bounded stopping times.

title: Làdlàg path
description: A path on a real time interval into a metric space is làdlàg if it has both left and right limits at every interior time; neither limit is required to equal the value at that time.

title: Càdlàg semimartingale
description: A real adapted càdlàg process X is a semimartingale if it can locally be written as X=X₀+M+A, where M is a local martingale starting at0 and A is an adapted càdlàg process of locally finite variation starting at0.

title: Stochastic integral of a predictable process against a semimartingale
description: For a real semimartingale X and a predictable locally bounded integrand H, H·X is the canonical stochastic-integral extension of elementary predictable sums ∑H_i(X_(t∧t_(i+1))−X_(t∧t_i)), where H_i is measurable at time t_i; convergence is in probability uniformly on compact time intervals.

title: Quadratic covariation of càdlàg semimartingales
description: For real càdlàg semimartingales X,Y, their quadratic covariation is [X,Y]_t=X_tY_t−X₀Y₀−∫₀ᵗX_(s−)dY_s−∫₀ᵗY_(s−)dX_s. Its jumps satisfy Δ[X,Y]_t=ΔX_tΔY_t; [X]=[X,X] is quadratic variation.

title: Martingale orthogonal to a Brownian motion
description: A càdlàg local martingale M is orthogonal to a d-dimensional Brownian motion W if [M,W^i] is identically0 for every coordinate i. The Brownian continuity is part of this convention; orthogonality of two arbitrary jump martingales need not mean zero optional covariation.

title: Predictable stopping time
description: A stopping time τ is predictable if it admits stopping times τ_n increasing to τ with τ_n<τ on {τ>0}; such a sequence announces τ.

title: Quasi-left-continuous filtration
description: A usual filtration is quasi-left-continuous if F_τ=F_(τ−) for every predictable stopping time τ, where F_(τ−) is generated by F₀ and the events A∩{t<τ} with A∈F_t.

title: Doob–Meyer decomposition of a càdlàg class-D supermartingale
description: On a usual filtered probability space, a càdlàg supermartingale X of class D on [0,T] has a unique decomposition X=X₀+M−A, where M is a càdlàg uniformly integrable martingale starting at0 and A is predictable, càdlàg, nondecreasing and starts at0.

title: Mertens decomposition of a class-D strong optional supermartingale
description: On a usual filtration, a class-D strong optional supermartingale X has a unique decomposition X=X₀+M−A−I, where M is a càdlàg uniformly integrable martingale, A is predictable càdlàg nondecreasing, and I is predictable left-continuous nondecreasing and purely discontinuous, all starting at0. Equivalently I=C_− for an adapted càdlàg purely discontinuous increasing C with C_(0−)=0.

title: Supermartingale potential
description: A nonnegative right-continuous supermartingale X on [0,∞) is a potential if E[X_t] tends to0 as t tends to∞.

title: Doob’s Lp maximal inequality for càdlàg martingales
description: For 1<p<∞ and a càdlàg real martingale M on [0,T] with M_T∈Lᵖ, ‖sup_(t≤T)|M_t|‖_p≤p/(p−1)‖M_T‖_p.

title: Continuous approximation of the natural compensator of a potential
description: For a class-D supermartingale potential X with natural increasing process A, there are continuous increasing approximants A^n whose associated potentials X^n are bounded above by X and whose terminal values converge weakly in L¹ to A_∞.

title: Integration identity for optional projection against a continuous increasing process
description: For a nonnegative measurable process H with optional projection ^oH and an adapted continuous increasing integrable process A, E∫H_s dA_s=E∫(^oH)_s dA_s. The projection is characterized by (^oH)_τ=E[H_τ|F_τ] at finite stopping times where integrable.

title: Reflexivity and weak compactness of Lp for a finite reflexive exponent
description: For 1<p<∞ on a σ-finite measure space, Lᵖ is reflexive; every norm-bounded sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence, and the norm of a weak limit is at most the liminf of the norms.

title: Meyer’s Lp estimate for the increasing process of a supermartingale potential
description: For each 1<p<∞ there are positive constants c_p,C_p such that if X is a class-D supermartingale potential with natural predictable increasing process A, then c_p‖sup_tX_t‖_p≤‖A_∞‖_p≤C_p‖sup_tX_t‖_p, allowing infinite norms.

title: Burkholder–Davis–Gundy inequalities for càdlàg local martingales at p≥1
description: For each p≥1 there are 0<c_p≤C_p<∞ such that every real càdlàg local martingale M starting at0 satisfies c_pE([M]_T^(p/2))≤E[sup_(t≤T)|M_t|^p]≤C_pE([M]_T^(p/2)) for stopping times T, with extended expectations.

title: Supersolution of a Brownian BSDE with an orthogonal martingale
description: On a usual Brownian-carrying filtration over [0,T], a supersolution with terminal ξ and driver g is a tuple (Y,Z,M,K) satisfying Y_t=ξ−∫_t^Tg(s,Y_s,Z_s)ds−∫_t^TZ_s dW_s−(M_T−M_t)+(K_T−K_t), where Y is adapted làdlàg, Z predictable and integrable, M càdlàg martingale orthogonal to W, and K predictable nondecreasing làdlàg with K₀=0.

title: Reflected Brownian BSDE with a càdlàg lower obstacle
description: A reflected Brownian BSDE with an orthogonal martingale is a supersolution (Y,Z,M,K) with càdlàg Y,K and a càdlàg adapted obstacle S such that Y_t≥S_t on [0,T] and ∫₀^T(Y_(s−)−S_(s−))dK_s=0. The terminal constraint Y_T=ξ necessarily requires S_T≤ξ.

title: Lp a priori estimate for BSDE supersolutions in a general filtration
description: Fix p>1 and finite T. For an Lᵖ supersolution (Y,Z,M,K) of a Brownian BSDE with an orthogonal martingale in a usual filtration, with uniformly Lipschitz driver g, there is C depending only on p,T and its Lipschitz constants such that E[(∫₀^T|Z_s|²ds)^(p/2)]+E[[M]_T^(p/2)]+E[K_T^p]≤C(E|ξ|^p+E sup_(t≤T)|Y_t|^p+E[(∫₀^T|g(s,0,0)|ds)^p]). No quasi-left-continuity hypothesis is required.

title: Q-curve
description: An elliptic curve over a number field is a ℚ-curve if it is isogenous over ℚ̄ to every Galois conjugate. It is completely defined over a Galois number field K if it and the isogenies between its conjugates are defined over K. A quadratic ℚ-curve is one defined over a quadratic number field.

title: Classical cusp form with Dirichlet character
description: A weight-k cusp form with Dirichlet character χ modulo N is holomorphic on the upper half-plane, satisfies f((aτ+b)/(cτ+d))=χ(d)(cτ+d)^k f(τ) for matrices in Γ₀(N), and vanishes at every cusp. Equivalently it belongs to the χ-eigenspace of diamond operators on the cusp forms for Γ₁(N).

title: Hecke operators on classical modular forms
description: For f=∑a_nqⁿ of weight k and character χ modulo N, the Hecke operator T_p for p∤N has q-coefficients a_(pn)+χ(p)p^(k−1)a_(n/p), with a_(n/p)=0 unless p divides n. For p|N the operator U_p has coefficients a_(pn). Composite operators are obtained by the standard coprime multiplicativity and prime-power recurrences.

title: Normalized weight-two newform
description: A normalized weight-two newform of level N and character χ is a simultaneous eigenform for all classical Hecke operators in the new cuspidal subspace, with first q-coefficient one. The new subspace is the Petersson-orthogonal complement of forms obtained as g(dτ) from lower levels dividing N.

title: Compact modular curve of a congruence subgroup
description: For a finite-index congruence subgroup Γ⊆SL₂(ℤ), its compact complex modular curve is Γ\(ℍ∪ℙ¹(ℚ)), with the Riemann-surface charts at elliptic points and cusps. Its arithmetic model and the identification of its complex points must be specified separately; the marked-point and µ_N level conventions for X₁(N) can assign different cusp fields to the same analytic labels.

title: Modular parametrization of an elliptic curve
description: A modular parametrization over K is a nonconstant morphism of algebraic curves π:X₁(N)_K→E for some N; for a rational elliptic curve the source may be X₀(N). Its pullback carries invariant differentials on E to weight-two cusp differentials.

title: Optimal modular parametrization
description: For fixed source X₁(N), a modular parametrization π:X₁(N)→E is optimal if it is maximal for domination: π′ dominates π when π=φ∘π′ for an isogeny φ:E′→E over the base field, with pairs considered up to isomorphism. The analogous X₀(N) notion is called strong in §2.

title: Invariant differential of an elliptic curve
description: A nonzero invariant differential on an elliptic curve is a regular one-form unchanged by translations. For a generalized Weierstrass equation y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆, it is a scalar multiple of dx/(2y+a₁x+a₃); in short form it is a multiple of dx/(2y).

title: Minimal integral Weierstrass model over a local field
description: For an elliptic curve over a discretely valued characteristic-zero local field, an integral Weierstrass model has a_i in the valuation ring, and is minimal if the valuation of its discriminant is least among all integral Weierstrass equations for the same curve.

title: Local minimal differential of an elliptic curve
description: Over a discretely valued local field, a local minimal elliptic differential is dx/(2y+a₁x+a₃) for a minimal integral Weierstrass equation. It is determined up to multiplication by a unit of the valuation ring.

title: Fractional ideal of a number field
description: A nonzero fractional ideal of a number field K is a finitely generated O_K-submodule I⊆K with aI⊆O_K for some nonzero a∈O_K. Products and inverses give the group of nonzero fractional ideals.

title: Absolute norm of a fractional ideal
description: For a nonzero integral ideal I⊆O_K, N(I)=|O_K/I|. Extend this multiplicatively to nonzero fractional ideals by N(I/J)=N(I)/N(J); for a principal ideal (a), this equals |N_(K/ℚ)(a)|.

title: Weierstrass ideal of an elliptic differential
description: For an elliptic curve E/K and invariant differential ω, choose a local minimal differential ω_𝔭 at every finite prime. The Weierstrass ideal is δ_ω=∏_𝔭 𝔭^(v_𝔭(ω/ω_𝔭)), a fractional ideal independent of the unit choices. It can be nonprincipal, and a global minimal differential need not exist.

title: Manin ideal of a modular parametrization
description: For π:X₁(N)→E/K, let D_E be the O_K-lattice of invariant differentials integral at every finite place. If P=π*H⁰(E,Ω¹) and P_int=P∩O_K[[q]]dq/q, the Manin ideal c(π) is defined by π*D_E=c(π)P_int. It is the ideal analogue of the Manin constant when the integral differential module need not be free.

title: Generalized Manin conjecture for Q-curves
description: For an optimal modular parametrization π:X₁(N)→E of a ℚ-curve completely defined over its base number field, the Manin ideal c(π) is the unit ideal.

title: Complex uniformization theorem for an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over ℂ with nonzero invariant differential ω, there is a full lattice Λ⊆ℂ and a complex analytic group isomorphism ℂ/Λ≅E(ℂ) pulling ω back to dz. The lattice is the set of integrals of ω over integral closed cycles.

title: Period lattice of an elliptic differential
description: The period lattice Λ(E,ω) is the full lattice in ℂ for which the analytic uniformization ℂ/Λ→E(ℂ) pulls the chosen invariant differential ω back to dz. Scaling ω by a scales Λ by a. For a real pair (E,ω), its real period is the least positive element of Λ∩ℝ.

title: Intrinsic period factor of an elliptic curve over a quadratic field
description: For E/K and an invariant differential ω, let δ_ω be its Weierstrass ideal. If K is real quadratic, set Ω_E=(ω₁ω_(1,ν))/N(δ_ω), the product of the positive real periods at its two real embeddings. If K is imaginary quadratic, set Ω_E=2·covol(Λ(E,ω))/N(δ_ω). This is independent of ω by the number-field product formula.

title: Reduction type of an elliptic curve over a local field
description: Reduce a minimal integral Weierstrass equation modulo the maximal ideal. Nonsingular reduction is good; nodal reduction is multiplicative, split if both tangent directions at the node are rational over the residue field and nonsplit otherwise; the remaining singular case is additive reduction.

title: Hasse–Weil L-function of an elliptic curve over a number field
description: For E/K, its Hasse–Weil L-function is ∏_𝔭 P_𝔭((N𝔭)^(−s))^(−1). At good reduction, P_𝔭(T)=1−a_𝔭T+(N𝔭)T² with a_𝔭=N𝔭+1−|E(k_𝔭)|. At split multiplicative, nonsplit multiplicative and additive reduction the factors P_𝔭 are 1−T, 1+T and 1 respectively. The product converges for Re s>3/2.

title: Manin–Drinfel’d theorem on cuspidal divisor classes
description: For a compact modular curve associated to a congruence subgroup, every degree-zero divisor supported on its cusps has torsion class in its Jacobian. In particular a modular parametrization sends the difference of two cusps to a torsion point on an elliptic curve.

title: Newform factorization for a completely defined quadratic Q-curve
description: Let E/K be a non-CM ℚ-curve completely defined over a quadratic field K, and let μ:E→νE satisfy νμ∘μ=[m]. If m is not a square, there is a normalized weight-two newform f of level N and coefficient field ℚ(√m), with its unique Galois conjugate σf, such that L(E/K,s)=L(f,s)L(σf,s). If m is square, E is K-isogenous to a curve E₀/ℚ and the factorization is L(E₀,s)L(E₀^d,s), where K=ℚ(√d).

title: Bruin–Ferraguti construction of a quadratic Q-curve’s newform
description: Given a completely defined non-CM quadratic ℚ-curve E/K and a K-isogeny μ:E→νE with νμ∘μ=[m], m nonsquare, choose an embedding ℚ(√m)→ℂ. Compute the newform’s level from N²=N_K(E)norm·Δ_K², determine its character from the sign of m and the quadratic character of K, and match its Euler factors to those of E. At ambiguous primes the chosen μ distinguishes the sign via Frobenius and the reduced isogeny; this yields f rather than just the unordered conjugate pair.

title: Bruin–Ferraguti rationality and denominator bound for quadratic Q-curves
description: Let E/K be a non-CM ℚ-curve completely defined over a quadratic field, not K-isogenous to a curve over ℚ, with μ:E→νE and νμ∘μ=[m]. Let μ*(ωνE)=αω_E, α=p+q√Δ_K of norm m, and D_α={x∈O_K:xα∈O_K}. Put R=L(E/K,1)√|Δ_K|/Ω_E. Then R∈ℚ. Assuming the generalized Manin conjecture, 2q·|E(K)_tors|²·t·N(D_α)·s²·R∈ℤ, where t=4 if m≡1 mod4 and t=1 otherwise, and s is the lcm of minimal K-isogeny degrees from all curves in E’s K-isogeny class to E.

title: Uniform Fréchet differentiability on bounded sets
description: A differentiable real function f on a Banach space is uniformly Fréchet differentiable on bounded sets if for every bounded B, sup_{x∈B,||h||=1}|(f(x+th)−f(x))/t−Df(x)h|→0 as t→0.

title: Coercive real functional
description: A real or extended-real functional f on a normed space is coercive if f(x)→+∞ as ||x||→∞, equivalently each finite sublevel set is bounded.

title: Supercoercive real functional
description: A functional f on a normed space is supercoercive if f(x)/||x||→+∞ as ||x||→∞.

title: Sequential consistency of a Bregman distance
description: For differentiable convex f, sequential consistency means that bounded x_n and D_f(y_n,x_n)→0 imply ||y_n−x_n||→0.

title: Total convexity and Bregman sequential consistency
description: For a differentiable convex function whose effective domain contains at least two points, total convexity on bounded sets is equivalent to sequential consistency of its Bregman distance.

title: Uniform continuity of a uniformly differentiable convex gradient
description: If f:E→ℝ is convex, bounded on bounded sets and uniformly Fréchet differentiable on bounded sets, then Df:E→E* is uniformly norm-continuous on bounded sets.

title: Variational characterization of a Bregman projection
description: For differentiable strictly convex f on a Banach space and convex C, z∈C minimizes D_f(·,x) if and only if ⟨Df(x)−Df(z),y−z⟩≤0 for all y∈C. Such z satisfies D_f(y,z)+D_f(z,x)≤D_f(y,x).

title: Fenchel–Young gap
description: For a proper convex f on a Banach space, its Fenchel–Young gap is V_f(x,x*)=f(x)+f*(x*)−⟨x*,x⟩≥0; when f* is differentiable and the Legendre duality identities hold, V_f(x,x*)=D_f(x,Df*(x*)).

title: Composition theorem for Bregman strongly nonexpansive maps
description: Suppose f is Legendre, bounded and uniformly Fréchet differentiable on bounded sets, totally convex on bounded sets, with Df* bounded on bounded subsets of E*=domf*. If T₁,…,T_N:C→C are Bregman strongly nonexpansive and their asymptotic fixed sets have nonempty intersection, their composition is Bregman strongly nonexpansive and its asymptotic fixed set equals that intersection.

title: Scalar convergence lemma for vanishing convex recurrences
description: If a_n≥0,0<α_n<1, ∑α_n=∞ and a_{n+1}≤(1−α_n)a_n+β_n, then a_n→0 provided limsup β_n/α_n≤0 or ∑|β_n|<∞.

title: Complex unit disk
description: The complex unit disk is 𝔻={z∈ℂ:|z|<1}.

title: Co-invariant subspace of a Hilbert-space operator
description: A closed subspace Q of a Hilbert space is co-invariant for T if T*Q⊂Q, equivalently Q⊥ is invariant for T.

title: Unitary equivalence of operators
description: Operators T on H and S on K are unitarily equivalent if a unitary U:H→K satisfies UT=SU; tuples are unitarily equivalent if one U intertwines every corresponding coordinate.

title: Products and ranges of commuting orthogonal projections
description: For finitely many pairwise commuting orthogonal Hilbert-space projections P_i, ∏P_i is the orthogonal projection onto ⋂ranP_i, and I−∏(I−P_i) projects onto the closed sum∑ranP_i.

title: Weak operator topology
description: The weak operator topology on bounded operators H→K is the coarsest topology for which T↦⟨Tx,y⟩ is continuous for every x∈H,y∈K; a net converges exactly when all these matrix coefficients converge.

title: Standard analytic reproducing kernel Hilbert space on the disk
description: A standard analytic RKHS R_k on the disk has nonvanishing holomorphic–antiholomorphic kernel k, dense polynomials and contractive coordinate multiplication, and polynomials p_j(z,w̄)→1/k(z,w) whose hereditary evaluations p_j(M_z,M_z*) are uniformly norm bounded.

title: Operator contractive with respect to an analytic kernel
description: For a standard analytic RKHS R_k with fixed approximating p_j and polynomial orthonormal basis ψ_m, T is k-contractive if p_j(T,T*) are uniformly bounded and converge weakly to C≥0, and I−∑_{m<j}ψ_m(T)Cψ_m(T)*→0 strongly.

title: Arazy–Engliš dilation for kernel-contractive operators
description: If T is k-contractive for a standard analytic RKHS R_k and D=closure(ranC), then Vh=∑_m ψ_m⊗C^(1/2)ψ_m(T)*h is an isometry intertwining T* with M_z*, and T is unitarily equivalent to a compression of M_z on a co-invariant subspace of R_k⊗D.

title: Analytic quotient model for doubly commuting Bergman hypercontractions
description: A doubly commuting tuple of pure m_i-hypercontractions is unitarily equivalent to the coordinate multipliers compressed to A²_m(D_T)⊖∑_iΘ_i A²_mhat_i(E_i), where D_T is the closed range of the product defect and each Θ_i is a one-variable partially isometric multiplier from a tensor Hardy–Bergman space.

title: Tensor classification of scalar doubly commuting Bergman quotients
description: A joint backward-shift-invariant subspace Q of the scalar tensor weighted Bergman space has doubly commuting compressed coordinate multipliers if and only if Q is unitarily equivalent to Q₁⊗⋯⊗Q_n with each Q_i a one-variable backward-shift-invariant Bergman subspace; each factor is the orthogonal complement of a partially isometric Hardy multiplier range.

title: Darboux criterion for Riemann integrability
description: A bounded function on a compact rectangle is Riemann integrable if and only if for every ε>0 there is a rectangular partition whose upper and lower Darboux sums differ by less than ε.

title: Associate duality of Wiener amalgam spaces
description: For1≤p,q≤∞, the Köthe associate of W(Lᵖ,ℓᵠ) under the integral pairing is W(Lᵖ′,ℓᵠ′), with norm obtained as the supremum of |∫fg| over the unit ball; when p,q<∞ this represents its continuous dual.

title: Correlation summability of Wiener windows
description: For g,γ∈W(L∞,ℓ¹)(ℝᵈ), let G_{a,b;n}(x)=∑_{k∈ℤᵈ}conj(g(x−n/b−ak))γ(x−ak). Then ∑_n||G_{a,b;n}||∞≤(1+1/a)ᵈ(2+2b)ᵈ||g||_W||γ||_W, and aᵈ∑_{n≠0}||G_{a,b;n}||∞→0 as a,b→0.

title: Uniform Riemann sums for a Wiener-space function
description: If f∈W(L∞,ℓ¹)(ℝᵈ) is locally Riemann integrable, then ess sup_y|aᵈ∑_{n∈ℤᵈ}f(y+an)−∫f|→0 as a↓0.

title: L² convergence of densely sampled Gabor reconstruction
description: For g,γ∈L² with⟨γ,g⟩≠0, suppose normalized self-Gabor operators S_{a,b;g,g} and S_{a,b;γ,γ} have uniformly bounded norms for0<a,b≤1. Then the normalized cross-Gabor operators are well-defined and converge strongly to the identity onL² as a,b→0.

title: Adjoint-lattice coefficient summability for Feichtinger windows
description: If g,γ∈S₀(ℝᵈ), then for every a,b>0, ∑_{l,n∈ℤᵈ}|⟨γ,M_{l/a}T_{n/b}g⟩|<∞.

title: Logarithmic quantile bound for independent partial products
description: There is a universal c>0 such that for independent random elements in a separable invariant-metric semigroup and0<t≤s≤1/2, U_n*(t)≤c log(1/t)/max{log(1/s),loglog(4/t)}[U_n*(s)+M_n*(t/2)], where U_n andM_n are partial-product and increment maxima.

title: Moment bound for large-jump partial products
description: For independent X₁,…,X_n in a separable invariant-metric monoid, let ℓ be the inverse increment tail-count function and U_n″(r) the maximal partial-product distance after replacing every increment with distance≤ℓ(r) by the identity. Then ||U_n″(r)||_p≤2exp(2^p r/p)||ℓ||_{Lᵖ(0,1)} for0<r<1 andp>0.

title: Diameter of a Euclidean set
description: The diameter of A⊂ℝⁿ is sup{|x−y|:x,y∈A}, possibly infinite.

title: Euclidean unit sphere
description: The unit sphere S^(n−1) is {x∈ℝⁿ:|x|=1}, with the subspace topology and its rotation-invariant surface measure when needed.

title: Groemer’s Hausdorff stability of Brunn–Minkowski
description: For n≥2,λ∈(0,1) and convex bodies K,L with volume ratio and normalized diameters bounded, the relative Brunn–Minkowski deficit is at least c H₀(K,L)^(n+1), where c>0 depends only on n,λ,that ratio and diameter bound; H₀ normalizes volume and centroid.

title: Figalli–Maggi–Pratelli stability of Brunn–Minkowski
description: For convex bodies K,L⊂ℝⁿ and0<λ<1, the relative Brunn–Minkowski deficit is at least[nm/(ΛMθ_n²)] A(K,L)², where m=min(|K|^(1/n),|L|^(1/n)), M=max(|K|^(1/n),|L|^(1/n)), Λ=max(λ/(1−λ),(1−λ)/λ), and θ_n depends only on n.

title: Square-root concavity of the torsion function
description: If Ω is a bounded open convex Euclidean set and u is its zero-boundary torsion solution−Δu=c withc>0, then sqrt(u) is concave onΩ.

title: Minkowski comparison of torsion functions
description: If Ω_λ=(1−λ)Ω₀+λΩ₁ for bounded open convex sets and u_i solve−Δu_i=c>0 with zero boundary data inΩ_i, then sqrt(u_λ((1−λ)x+λy))≥(1−λ)sqrt(u₀(x))+λsqrt(u₁(y)) forx∈Ω₀,y∈Ω₁.

title: Steiner point of a convex body
description: For K⊂ℝⁿ a convex body, its Steiner point is s(K)=n∫_{S^(n−1)}u h_K(u)dσ(u), withσ the normalized rotation-invariant sphere measure. It is translation covariant and additive under Minkowski addition.

title: Hadwiger’s rotational Minkowski averaging theorem
description: For every convex body K there are rotationsρ_j for which k⁻¹(ρ₁K+⋯+ρ_kK) converges in Hausdorff distance to a ball with the same mean width asK. After translating K so s(K)=0, the limiting ball is centered at0.

title: Proper degenerate elliptic equation operator
description: A continuous scalar equation operator F(x,r,p,X) on symmetric matrices is proper degenerate elliptic in the standard sign convention if F(x,r,p,X)≤F(x,s,p,Y) wheneverr≤s andY≤X; reversing the whole equation reverses both inequalities.

title: Viscosity subsolution of an elliptic equation
description: An upper-semicontinuous u is a viscosity subsolution of F(x,u,Du,D²u)=0 if everyC² test functionφ touching u from above atx satisfies F(x,u(x),Dφ(x),D²φ(x))≤0, for the standard proper elliptic sign convention.

title: Comparison property for viscosity Dirichlet problems
description: An elliptic Dirichlet problem has the comparison property if every viscosity subsolution lying below a viscosity supersolution on the boundary lies below it throughout the domain. Supersolutions use lower semicontinuity and test functions touching from below with the reversed operator inequality.

title: Time-homogeneous Markov chain on a measurable state space
description: A discrete-time process (X_n) on a measurable space with a probability kernel P is Markov when P(X_(n+1)∈A|X₀,…,X_n)=P(X_n,A) almost surely for every measurable A; the same kernel is used at every step.

title: Invariant probability of a Markov kernel
description: A probability measure π is invariant for a Markov kernel P if ∫P(x,A)dπ(x)=π(A) for every measurable A; equivalently πP=π.

title: Coupling of probability measures
description: A coupling of probability measures μ and ν on measurable spaces E and F is a probability measure on E×F whose coordinate marginals are μ and ν.

title: Wasserstein distance of order one for a lower semicontinuous metric
description: On a Polish space E with a finite-valued metric d lower semicontinuous for its given product topology, W_d(μ,ν)=inf_(γ coupling μ,ν)∫d(x,y)dγ(x,y), allowing the value∞. The metric d need not induce the original Polish topology.

title: Wasserstein Dobrushin coefficient of a Markov kernel
description: For a Markov kernel P on a metric state space, its Wasserstein coefficient is τ_d(P)=sup_(x≠y)W_d(P(x,·),P(y,·))/d(x,y), allowing infinity.

title: Geometric Wasserstein contraction of iterated Markov kernels
description: A Markov kernel P has geometric Wasserstein contraction if τ_d(P^n)≤Cρ^n for all integers n≥0, for constants C≥1 and 0≤ρ<1. The n=0 term is the identity kernel coefficient1.

title: V-uniform ergodicity of a discrete-time Markov kernel
description: A Markov kernel P is V-uniformly ergodic if it has an invariant probability π with π(V)<∞ and there are C<∞ and 0≤ρ<1 such that ‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_V≤CV(x)ρ^n for all x and n≥0, for a measurable weight V≥1.

title: Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality for a lower semicontinuous metric
description: For probability measures μ,ν on a Polish space equipped with a finite lower semicontinuous metric d, W_d(μ,ν)=sup_f|∫f dμ−∫f dν|, where f ranges over bounded Borel functions with |f(x)−f(y)|≤d(x,y). The equality is understood in the extended nonnegative reals; finite first moments also permit arbitrary integrable1-Lipschitz tests.

title: Wasserstein contraction and submultiplicativity for Markov kernels
description: For Markov kernels P,Q on the declared lower-semicontinuous metric state space, W_d(μP,νP)≤τ_d(P)W_d(μ,ν) and τ_d(PQ)≤τ_d(P)τ_d(Q), whenever the products are unambiguous; the zero-coefficient case means all rows coincide.

title: Weighted total variation as a Wasserstein distance
description: For a lower semicontinuous weight V≥1 on a Polish space, set d_V(x,y)=(V(x)+V(y))1_(x≠y). For probabilities μ,ν with finite V-moments, W_(d_V)(μ,ν)=‖μ−ν‖_V.

title: Rudolf–Schweizer Lyapunov-weighted Wasserstein perturbation bound
description: Let P,Q be Markov kernels with τ_d(P^n)≤Cρ^n for n≥0, C≥1 and ρ<1. Suppose QV≤δV+L with V≥1,0≤δ<1, and κ=max(q₀(V),L/(1−δ))<∞. Put γ=sup_xW_d(P(x,·),Q(x,·))/V(x). Then W_d(p₀P^n,q₀Q^n)≤Cρ^nW_d(p₀,q₀)+Cγκ(1−ρ^n)/(1−ρ).

title: Rudolf–Schweizer total-variation perturbation bound from weighted geometric ergodicity
description: Suppose ‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_V≤CV(x)ρ^n with C≥1,ρ<1,V≥1, QV≤δV+L and PV≤V+L. Put κ=max(q₀(V),L/(1−δ))<∞ and γ=sup_x‖P(x,·)−Q(x,·)‖_TV/V(x). For0<γ<e^(−1), ‖p₀P^n−q₀Q^n‖_TV≤Cρ^n‖p₀−q₀‖_V+[eκ/(1−ρ)] [2C(L+1)]^(1/log(1/γ))γlog(1/γ).

title: Autoregressive process of order one
description: A real AR(1) process satisfies X_n=aX_(n−1)+Z_n, where (Z_n) are i.i.d. real innovations independent of X₀; the stable parameter range is |a|<1.

title: Metropolis–Hastings transition kernel
description: For a target probability π and proposal kernel Q, let r(x,y) be the Radon–Nikodym ratio of the reversed joint proposal law π(dy)Q(y,dx) to the forward law π(dx)Q(x,dy) on their mutually absolutely continuous part, and set r=0 on the forward-only singular part. The acceptance probability a=min(1,r) gives P(x,dy)=a(x,y)Q(x,dy)+(1−∫a(x,z)Q(x,dz))δ_x(dy).

title: Bayesian posterior density
description: For a prior density p(θ) and likelihood ℓ(y|θ), the posterior density given observation y is π(θ|y)=ℓ(y|θ)p(θ)/∫ℓ(y|u)p(u)du, when the denominator is positive and finite.

title: Unadjusted Langevin algorithm
description: For a differentiable positive target density π on ℝ^d and step h>0, the unadjusted Langevin chain is X_(n+1)=X_n+h∇logπ(X_n)+√(2h)Z_(n+1), with independent standard Gaussian vectors Z_n. It is the Euler discretization of the Langevin diffusion and generally does not preserve π exactly.

title: Quadratic form with an integral symmetric matrix
description: A quadratic form with an integral matrix is Q(x)=xᵀAx for a symmetric matrix A over ℤ. In the monomial expansion every mixed coefficient is even. This convention is stronger than merely requiring integer values on ℤⁿ.

title: Homogeneous polynomial over a field
description: A polynomial over a field in finitely many variables is homogeneous of degree d if all its nonzero monomials have total degree d. The zero polynomial is homogeneous of every degree by convention.

title: Jacobian nonsingularity of a projective plane equation
description: For a nonzero homogeneous polynomial F in three variables over a field K, its projective equation is Jacobian-nonsingular if no nonzero vector over an algebraic closure satisfies F=∂₁F=∂₂F=∂₃F=0. This tests the equation as a scheme, retaining multiplicities rather than replacing F by its square-free part.

title: Determinant polynomial of a net of quadratic forms
description: For three symmetric k×k matrices A₁,A₂,A₃ over a field, the determinant polynomial of their net is F(a₁,a₂,a₃)=det(a₁A₁+a₂A₂+a₃A₃), homogeneous of degree k. Its zero locus parametrizes singular linear combinations of the three forms.

title: Quadratic net with a nonsingular determinant equation
description: A triple of k-variable quadratic forms over a field of characteristic different from two has a nonsingular determinant equation if det(a₁A₁+a₂A₂+a₃A₃)=0 is a Jacobian-nonsingular projective plane equation. The condition is geometric, after extension to an algebraic closure.

title: Projective complete intersection
description: A projective complete intersection of codimension r in projective N-space over a field is the closed subscheme cut out by r homogeneous polynomials forming a regular sequence in the homogeneous coordinate ring. Its dimension is N−r.

title: Singular locus of a projective complete intersection
description: For a projective complete intersection cut out by f₁,…,f_r over a perfect field, the geometric singular locus consists of its points where the r×(N+1) matrix (∂f_i/∂x_j) has rank less than r. The empty locus has dimension −1.

title: Complete quadratic exponential sum
description: For an integral symmetric matrix A, positive integer q, and integer vector b, the complete quadratic exponential sum is ∑_(x∈(ℤ/qℤ)^k)exp(2πi(xᵀAx+bᵀx)/q). The sum is independent of the residue representatives.

title: Smoothly weighted representation count for quadratic forms
description: For integral-matrix quadratic forms Q₁,…,Q_r, a compactly supported smooth nonnegative function w on ℝᵏ, B>0, and n∈ℤʳ, the weighted representation count is R_(B,w)(n)=∑_(x∈ℤᵏ,Q_i(x)=n_i for all i)w(x/B). Compact support makes this sum finite.

title: Singular integral of a system of quadratic forms
description: For real quadratic forms Q₁,…,Q_r and compactly supported smooth w, put I_w(θ)=∫_(ℝᵏ)w(x)exp(2πi∑θ_iQ_i(x))dx. When I_w is integrable, the singular integral at µ∈ℝʳ is J_w(µ)=∫_(ℝʳ)I_w(θ)exp(−2πiθ·µ)dθ.

title: Singular series of a system of integral quadratic forms
description: For integral-matrix Q₁,…,Q_r in k variables and n∈ℤʳ, put T(n;q)=∑_(a mod q,gcd(a₁,…,a_r,q)=1)∑_(x mod q)exp(2πia·(Q(x)−n)/q). When absolutely convergent, the singular series is S(n)=∑_(q≥1)q^(−k)T(n;q).

title: p-adic solution density of a polynomial system
description: For r integer polynomials f_i in k variables, their p-adic solution density at n is lim_(e→∞)p^(e(r−k))#{x mod pᵉ:f_i(x)≡n_i mod pᵉ for all i}, when this limit exists. The normalization uses the expected codimension r.

title: Bounded-degree affine finite-field point upper bound
description: For an affine variety V⊆𝔸ʳ over 𝔽_q of dimension n cut out by boundedly many equations of bounded degrees, #V(𝔽_q)=O(qⁿ), with the implied constant depending only on the ambient dimension, number of equations and degree bound.

title: Deligne–Hooley point bound for projective complete intersections
description: For a projective complete intersection V of dimension n over 𝔽_q with geometric singular locus of dimension s, #V(𝔽_q)=1+q+⋯+qⁿ+O(q^((n+s+1)/2)); the constant can be bounded in terms of the ambient dimension and defining degrees. Use s=−1 if V is smooth.

title: Integer sublevel bound for a homogeneous polynomial
description: If P∈ℚ[x₁,…,x_s] is nonzero homogeneous of positive degree d, then for M,N≥1 the number of x∈ℤˢ with max|x_i|≤N and |P(x)|≤M is O_P(N^(s−1)M^(1/d)).

title: Prime-power sublevel bound for a homogeneous polynomial
description: For a nonzero homogeneous P∈ℤ[x₁,…,x_s] of positive degree d, uniformly for primes p and integers f≥0, #{x∈(ℤ/pᶠℤ)ˢ:P(x)≡0 mod pᶠ}=O_P(p^(sf−f/d)).

title: Multivariate Hensel lifting with a nonunit Jacobian determinant
description: Let F∈ℤ_p[x₁,…,x_r]ʳ and a∈ℤ_pʳ. If v_p(det DF(a))=ν<∞ and F(a)≡0 mod p^(2ν+1), then F has a zero b∈ℤ_pʳ with b≡a mod p^(ν+1).

title: Rank characterization of a nonsingular quadratic determinant net
description: For k≥4 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, a quadratic net has a Jacobian-nonsingular determinant equation exactly when every nonzero combination of its matrices has rank at least k−1 and the common projective zero set has its three gradients linearly independent at every point.

title: Discriminant polynomial detecting singular fibers of a quadratic net
description: For a k-variable integral quadratic net with nonsingular determinant equation, there is a nonzero homogeneous H_Q∈ℤ[n₁,n₂,n₃], of positive degree at most 2(k+1)k(k−1), such that, over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or odd characteristic where the specialized determinant equation remains nonsingular, H_Q(n)=0 exactly when some x with Q(x)=n has Jacobian rank below three.

title: Minor-arc mean-square estimate for three quadratic forms
description: For an integral quadratic net Q in k≥10 variables with nonsingular determinant equation, let S_B(α)=∑_(x∈ℤᵏ)w(x/B)exp(2πiα·Q(x)). For 0<Δ<1/13, remove the boxes |α_j−a_j/q|≤B^(−2+Δ) around primitive tuples with q≤B^Δ in (ℝ/ℤ)³, obtaining m(Δ). Then ∫_(m(Δ))|S_B(α)|²dα≪_(Q,w,ε,Δ)B^(2k−6−6Δ+ε).

title: Mean-square representation asymptotic for a nonsingular quadratic net
description: For an integral quadratic net Q in k≥10 variables with nonsingular determinant equation and compactly supported smooth nonnegative w, there is a polynomial H_Q detecting singular fibers, of degree at most 2(k+1)k(k−1), for which ∑_(|n|∞≤B²,H_Q(n)≠0)|R_(B,w)(n)−J_w(B^(−2)n)S(n)B^(k−6)|²≪_(Q,w)B^(2k−6−1/28).

title: Almost-all representation asymptotic for three quadratic forms
description: For an integral quadratic net Q in k≥10 variables with nonsingular determinant equation, N=B² and 0<ϖ<1/56, all but O_(Q,w,ϖ)(N^(3−(1/56−ϖ))) integer triples |n|∞≤N satisfy R_(B,w)(n)=J_w(B^(−2)n)S(n)B^(k−6)+O_(Q,w,ϖ)(B^(k−6−ϖ)).

title: Local-density bounds for three quadratic forms
description: For an integral quadratic net Q in k>6 variables with nonsingular determinant equation and H_Q(n)≠0, S(n)≪_ε|n|∞^ε. If Q(x)=n is soluble in every ℤ_p, then S(n)≫_ε|n|∞^(−ε)∏_(p≤p₀)|H_Q(n)|_p^α>0, with α=3^(k+3)(2k−6). Also J_w is bounded, and for w positive on a sufficiently large fixed ball, J_w(µ)≫_w|H_Q(µ)|^β for real-soluble fibers with 1/2≤|µ|∞≤1, where β=3^(k+3)(2k−7).

title: Average integral Hasse principle for three quadratic forms
description: For k≥10 there is ϖ(k)>0 such that, for every integral quadratic net Q in k variables with nonsingular determinant equation, the number of n∈ℤ³ with |n|∞≤N for which Q(x)=n is soluble over ℝ and every ℤ_p but not over ℤ is O_Q(N^(3−ϖ(k))).

title: Simultaneous prime values of three quadratic forms
description: Let Q be an integral quadratic net in k≥10 variables with nonsingular determinant equation. If some real x has Q_i(x)>0 for all i, and for every prime p some x_p∈ℤ_pᵏ has p∤∏_(i=1)^3Q_i(x_p), then infinitely many triples of rational primes are simultaneously represented by Q on ℤᵏ.

title: Monotone real function
description: A real function on a linearly ordered set is nondecreasing if x≤y impliesf(x)≤f(y), and nonincreasing if the reverse inequality holds; monotone means either.

title: Quasi-concave function
description: A real functionf on a convex set is quasi-concave if f((1−t)x+ty)≥min(f(x),f(y)) for0≤t≤1, equivalently all its superlevel sets are convex.

title: Rotational invariance of a scalar elliptic operator
description: An operatorF(x,r,p,X) is rotationally invariant if F(ρx,r,ρp,ρXρᵀ)=F(x,r,p,X) for everyρ∈SO(n), with the same equation domain after rotating its spatial argument.

title: Positive inward boundary derivative condition
description: A differentiable functionu>0 on a domainΩ with zero boundary data satisfies the positive inward derivative condition if for everyx∈∂Ω and every inward directionν atx, liminf_{Ω∋y→x}∂_νu(y)>0.

title: Power-transformed elliptic quasi-concavity condition
description: For0<p<1 defineG_{i,p}^θ(x,t,A)=F_i(x,t^(1/p),t^(1/p−1)θ,t^(1/p−3)A). The mixed quasi-concavity condition atλ asksG_{λ,p}^θ((1−λ)ξ₀+λξ₁)≥min(G_{0,p}^θ(ξ₀),G_{1,p}^θ(ξ₁)) forξ_i=(x_i,t_i,A_i),t_i>0 and every fixedθ. Atp=0 useG_{i,0}^θ(x,t,A)=F_i(x,e^t,e^tθ,e^tA).

title: Power-Minkowski subsolution principle for elliptic equations
description: Letu_i be positive classical zero-boundary solutions on bounded convexΩ_i,0≤p<1. If their equation operators satisfy the power-transformed mixed quasi-concavity condition atλ, and whenp>0 the positive inward boundary derivative condition holds, then theirp-Minkowski convolution is a viscosity subsolution of the equation on(1−λ)Ω₀+λΩ₁.

title: Mean-width rearrangement comparison for elliptic solutions
description: Letu solve a rotationally invariant proper elliptic zero-boundary problem on a bounded convexΩ and satisfy the positive inward boundary derivative condition. If0<p<1 and each transformedG_p^θ has convex nonnegative superlevel set in(x,t,A), then the corresponding solutionv on the ballΩ♯ of equal mean width satisfies||v||_r≥||u||_r for every0<r≤∞.

title: Uniform-limit stability of viscosity subsolutions
description: For a continuous proper degenerate elliptic operatorF, a locally uniform limitu of viscosity subsolutionsu_j is a viscosity subsolution, provided the domains eventually contain every compact subset of the limiting open domain.

title: Layer-cake representation of a nonnegative moment
