description: For a σ-finite measure μ, a measurable u≥0 and q>0, ∫u^q dμ=q∫_0^∞t^(q−1)μ({u>t})dt, allowing infinity.

title: Dirichlet rational approximation of one real number
description: For every irrational real θ and positive integer N there are integers p and 1≤q≤N with 0<|θ−p/q|<1/(qN). In particular infinitely many distinct rationals satisfy |θ−p/q|<1/q².

title: Lower bound two for the irrationality exponent
description: Every irrational real number θ has irrationality exponent μ(θ)≥2.

title: Reciprocal invariance of the irrationality exponent
description: For every nonzero irrational real θ, μ(1/θ)=μ(θ), including infinite values.

title: Wallis power-integral bounds
description: There are constants c,C>0 such that for every integer n≥1, c/√n≤∫₀^(π/2)sinⁿx dx≤C/√n; the identical bounds hold with cosine in place of sine.

title: Principal real arccosine
description: The principal real arccosine arccos:[−1,1]→[0,π] is the inverse of the restriction of cosine to [0,π].

title: Logarithmic real power-series identity
Necessary zero-term condition for a real series
description: If a real series ∑_(n≥1)a_n converges, then a_n→0.

title: Transpose of a matrix
description: For anm×n matrixA=(a_ij), the transposedn×m matrixAᵀ has entries(Aᵀ)_ij=a_ji.

title: Measure-preserving transformation
description: A measurable map T from a measure space (Ω,F,μ) to itself preserves μ if μ(T⁻¹A)=μ(A) for every measurable A.

title: Ergodic measure-preserving transformation
description: A probability-preserving transformation T is ergodic if every measurable set A with μ(T⁻¹A△A)=0 has μ(A) equal0 or1.

title: Stationary random sequence
description: A sequence (E_n) is stationary if, for every m≥1 and shift k≥0, the joint laws of (E₀,…,E_(m−1)) and (E_k,…,E_(k+m−1)) agree.

title: Ergodic stationary random sequence
description: A stationary random sequence is ergodic when its induced probability measure on sequence space is ergodic under the left shift.

title: Discrete-time random dynamical system
description: Over a measure-preserving transformation θ of an environmental probability space, a discrete random dynamical system is a measurable cocycle φ(n,ω,x) with φ(0,ω,x)=x and φ(n+m,ω,x)=φ(n,θ^mω,φ(m,ω,x)). It is continuous if x↦φ(n,ω,x) is continuous.

title: Absorbing set for a Markov chain
description: A measurable set A is absorbing for a Markov kernel P if P(x,A)=1 for every x∈A; after the chain enters A it stays in A.

title: Quasi-stationary distribution of an absorbing Markov chain
description: For a Markov chain absorbed almost surely in A, a quasi-stationary distribution is a probability μ supported on Aᶜ and a number0<λ<1 with ∫P(x,B)dμ(x)=λμ(B) for every measurable B⊆Aᶜ. Thus the law started from μ remains μ after conditioning on survival for any positive number of steps.

title: Small random perturbation of a discrete map
description: For a continuous map F:S→S on a metric space, a family of Markov kernels P_ε is a small random perturbation if for every δ>0, sup_(x∈S)P_ε(x,{y:d(y,F(x))≥δ}) tends to0 as ε tends to0.

title: Large deviation principle at small-noise speed1/ε
description: A family of probability measures μ_ε on a topological space satisfies an LDP with speed1/ε and lower semicontinuous rate I:S→[0,∞] if liminf_(ε↓0)εlogμ_ε(U)≥−inf_UI for every open U and limsup_(ε↓0)εlogμ_ε(C)≤−inf_CI for every closed C; log0=−∞.

title: Attractor of a continuous discrete map
description: For a continuous map F on a metric space, an attractor is a compact invariant set A with a neighborhood U such that for every neighborhood V of A, F^n(U)⊆V for all sufficiently large n.

title: Omega limit set of a forward orbit
description: For a forward orbit x_n=F^n(x) in a metric space, its omega limit set is the set of limits of subsequences x_(n_j) with n_j tending to positive infinity.

title: Alpha limit set of a complete orbit
description: For a complete orbit (x_n) indexed by all integers with x_(n+1)=F(x_n), its alpha limit set consists of limits of subsequences x_(n_j) with n_j tending to negative infinity.

title: Morse decomposition of discrete dynamics
description: On a compact invariant set, a Morse decomposition is a finite ordered family of disjoint isolated compact invariant sets K₁,…,K_m such that every complete orbit outside their union has its alpha limit in one K_j and omega limit in a K_i with j<i. Isolated means maximal invariant in some neighborhood.

title: Empirical measure of a discrete trajectory
description: For states X₀,…,X_n in a measurable space, their empirical measure is (n+1)⁻¹∑_(j=0)^nδ_(X_j); its mass on a measurable set is the fraction of sampled states lying in that set.

title: Stochastic persistence by empirical occupation near extinction
description: For a stochastic population process on a compact metric state space S with closed extinction set S₀, empirical stochastic persistence means that for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that, from each x∉S₀, almost surely limsup_(n→∞)(n+1)⁻¹#{0≤j≤n:d(X_j,S₀)≤δ}≤ε.

title: Top Lyapunov exponent of a matrix product
description: For a sequence of random matrices B_n, the top Lyapunov exponent is the limit r=lim_(n→∞)n⁻¹log‖B_n⋯B₁‖ when it exists almost surely and is constant. Existence and equality with a particular vector’s growth require additional hypotheses.

title: Structured stochastic population difference equation
description: For n species with state vectors X_i∈ℝ_(≥0)^(k_i), a structured stochastic population map has updates X_(i,t+1)=A_i(X_t,E_(t+1))X_(i,t), where A_i are continuous nonnegative matrix-valued functions of community state and a stationary ergodic environmental sequence.

title: Invasion growth rate of a structured population in a stationary environment
description: For a stationary ergodic community/environment trajectory and an absent species i with linearized update Z_(t+1)=A_i(X_t,E_(t+1))Z_t, its invasion growth rate is the almost-sure asymptotic per-capita rate lim_(t→∞)t⁻¹log‖Z_t‖ when the positive-matrix hypotheses make it independent of the positive initial direction.

title: Exponential discrete Lotka–Volterra map
description: For an interaction matrix A and intrinsic growth vector r, the exponential discrete Lotka–Volterra map on the nonnegative orthant is F_i(x)=x_i exp(r_i+∑_jA_(ij)x_j).

title: Poisson Lotka–Volterra process
description: With habitat scale ε>0 and an exponential discrete Lotka–Volterra map F, let population counts update conditionally independently as N_(i,t+1)|X_t∼Poisson(F_i(X_t)/ε), and set X_(i,t+1)=εN_(i,t+1). The density process lives on εℤ_(≥0)^k and coordinate extinction is absorbing.

title: Ricker population map
description: The Ricker map is the nonnegative population update F(x)=x exp(r(1−x)) with r>0, using carrying-capacity scale1.

title: Primitive nonnegative matrix
description: A square matrix with nonnegative real entries is primitive if some positive integer power has all entries strictly positive.

title: Continuity of finite-dimensional operator inversion
description: For a nonzero finite-dimensional normed space X, invertible operators form an open subset of L(X), and A↦A⁻¹ is continuous in operator norm. More precisely, if A is invertible and ‖A−B‖<1/‖A⁻¹‖ then B is invertible.

title: Lipschitz bound from a bounded Euclidean derivative
description: If U⊆ℝⁿ is convex and open, f:U→ℝᵐ is Fréchet differentiable, and ‖Df(x)‖≤M throughout U, then ‖f(x)−f(y)‖≤M‖x−y‖ for every x,y∈U.

title: Continuous partial derivatives and continuous Fréchet differentiability
description: For a map between open Euclidean sets, continuous first coordinate partial derivatives are equivalent to existence of a continuous Fréchet derivative. The derivative is represented by the matrix of those partial derivatives.

title: Dirichlet simultaneous rational approximation
description: For α∈ℝᵈ and an integer N≥1 there are integers 1≤q≤Nᵈ and p₁,…,p_d with max_j|qα_j−p_j|<1/N. If a common divisor is cancelled from (p₁,…,p_d,q), the resulting approximation errors |α_j−p_j/q| do not increase.

title: Kirszbraun extension theorem for Hilbert spaces
description: EveryL-Lipschitz map from a subset of a real Hilbert space to a real Hilbert space extends to the whole domain Hilbert space with the same Lipschitz constant. Complex Hilbert spaces may be viewed as real for this metric assertion.

title: Continuous short-time Fourier reconstruction
description: Forφ∈L²(ℝᵈ) nonzero, f∈L² andV_φf∈L¹(ℝ²ᵈ), f=||φ||₂⁻²∫_{ℝ²ᵈ}V_φf(z)π(z)φdz as an absolutely convergentL²-valued Bochner integral, whereπ(z) is the time-frequency shift.

title: Quadratic bounds for the scalar arithmetic–harmonic gap
description: For0<v<1 and0<a<b, withA_v=va+(1−v)b andH_v=(v/a+(1−v)/b)⁻¹, v(1−v)(1−a/b)²a≤A_v−H_v≤v(1−v)(1−b/a)²b. The factorv(1−v) is sharp asb/a→1.

title: Spectral-interval upper bound for the matrix arithmetic–harmonic gap
description: For positive definite matrices satisfying0<mI≤A≤B≤MI and0≤v≤1, A∇_vB−A!_vB≤v(1−v)(1−M/m)²B, whereA∇_vB=vA+(1−v)B andA!_vB=(vA⁻¹+(1−v)B⁻¹)⁻¹.

title: Powered determinant refinement of the arithmetic–harmonic inequality
description: For positive definiteA,B∈M_n(ℂ),0<v≤τ<1 andλ≥1, (v/τ)^λ det(A∇_τB−A!_τB)^(λ/n)≤det(A∇_vB)^(λ/n)−det(A!_vB)^(λ/n), using the same arithmetic/harmonic weight convention.

title: Intrinsic finite balls imply graph cutoff completeness
description: A locally finite weighted graph admitting an intrinsic pseudometricρ for which every finite-radius ball has finite cardinality isΓ-cutoff complete: there are finitely supported0≤η_k≤1 increasing pointwise to1 withΓ(η_k)≤1/k.

title: Uniqueness of natural finite-subset extension families
description: Fix1≤m<n. There is exactly one familyT_X:C(σ_m(2^X))→C(σ_n(2^X)) indexed by finite setsX, consisting of linear extension operators uniformly bounded inX, and natural under every injectionu:Y→X via pullbackf(χ_A)↦f(χ_{u⁻¹(A)}).

title: Moment equivalence with truncated partial-product quantiles
description: For everyp₀>0, constants depending only onp₀ give ||U_n||_p≈U_n*(e^(−p)/4)+||ℓ||_p≈(U_n′(e^(−p)/8))*(e^(−p)/4)+||ℓ||_p forp≥p₀ and any finite independent sequence in a separable abelian invariant-metric monoid. Hereℓ is the inverse increment tail-count function on(0,1), andU_n′(r) is the maximal partial-product distance after deleting increments larger thanℓ(r).

title: Kernel of a module homomorphism
description: For an R-module homomorphism f:M→N, its kernel is the submodule {x∈M:f(x)=0}.

title: Cokernel of a module homomorphism
description: For an R-module homomorphism f:M→N, its cokernel is the quotient module N/f(M).

title: Exact sequence of modules
description: A sequence of homomorphisms of modules over one commutative ring is exact at a module if the image of the incoming map equals the kernel of the outgoing map; it is exact if this holds at every term.

title: Snake lemma for modules
description: For a commuting diagram of R-modules with exact rows 0→A→B→C→0 and 0→A′→B′→C′→0 and vertical maps a,b,c, there is a natural exact sequence 0→ker a→ker b→ker c→coker a→coker b→coker c→0.

title: S-unit group of a number field
description: For a number field K and a finite set S of its places containing all archimedean places, its S-unit group is E_S={x∈K×:|x|_v=1 for every v∉S}. The definition is independent of the representative absolute value of each place.

title: Finite generation of the S-unit group
description: For a number field K and finite S containing the infinite places, the S-unit group is isomorphic to μ(K)×ℤʳ for a finite integer r, where μ(K) is the finite group of roots of unity in K.

title: L-primary character dual of an abelian pro-l group
description: For an abelian pro-ℓ group G, its ℓ-primary character dual is G∨=Hom_cont(G,ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ), where the target and the dual group have the discrete topology. For a discrete ℓ-primary torsion group A, write A∨=Hom(A,ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ) with the topology of pointwise convergence.

title: Character biduality for abelian pro-l groups
description: Evaluation identifies every abelian pro-ℓ group G with (G∨)∨. Under this duality the maximal divisible subgroup of G∨ corresponds to the maximal quotient of G isomorphic to a product of copies of ℤ_ℓ; its coordinate quotients correspond to continuous characters G→ℤ_ℓ.

title: Perfect Kummer character pairing
description: Let n=ℓʳ be invertible in a field F containing μ_n, D⊆F×/(F×)ⁿ a subgroup, and L=F(x^(1/n):[x]∈D). Then Gal(L/F)×D→μ_n, (σ,[x])↦σ(x^(1/n))/x^(1/n), is a perfect character pairing. Passing to limits gives Gal(L/F) and the universal ℓ-primary Kummer radical as character duals over fields containing all ℓ-power roots of unity.

title: Universal-radical invariants in a cyclotomic tower
description: For K containing μ_(2ℓ) and K∞/K its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension, the natural map ℛ_(K_n)→ℛ_(K∞) is injective and has image ℛ_(K∞)^(Gal(K∞/K_n)).

title: Tate’s cyclotomic invariant quotient for the l-primary K2
description: For K containing μ_(2ℓ), let I_n=(T_ℓ(μ)⊗_(ℤ_ℓ)ℛ_(K∞))^(Gal(K∞/K_n)). The ℓ-primary torsion subgroup of K₂^M(K_n) is canonically I_n/(I_n)_div, where (I_n)_div denotes its maximal divisible subgroup.

title: Cyclotomic binomial unit congruence
description: Let ℓ be prime and m≥1, with m≥2 if ℓ=2. For every n≥0, ((1+ℓᵐ)^(ℓⁿ)−1)/ℓ^(m+n) belongs to 1+ℓℤ_ℓ. In particular its numerator has ℓ-adic valuation m+n.

title: Exact sequence for rationalizing a Z_l-module
description: For a ℤ_ℓ-module M let M_tor={x:ℓʳx=0 for some r≥0}. There is an exact sequence 0→M/M_tor→ℚ_ℓ⊗_(ℤ_ℓ)M→(ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ)⊗_(ℤ_ℓ)M→0 induced by ℤ_ℓ⊆ℚ_ℓ.

title: Hermitian complex matrix
description: A square complex matrix A is Hermitian if its conjugate transpose A* equals A; equivalently A_(ij)=overline(A_(ji)) for every i,j.

title: John ellipsoid theorem
description: For every convex bodyK⊂ℝⁿ, an affine change of coordinates putsK between the unit Euclidean ball and then-fold dilate of that ball.

title: Brenier transport between uniform convex-body measures
description: For convex bodiesE,F of positive volume, there is a convex functionφ whose gradientT pushes the uniform probability onE to that onF; this map is unique almost everywhere among gradients of convex functions with that pushforward property.

title: Smooth boundary regularity of convex transport
description: The Brenier map between uniform measures on bounded smooth uniformly convex domains is a smooth diffeomorphism up to the boundary, and its Jacobian determinant is|F|/|E| for sourceE and targetF.

title: Coarea formula for a smooth scalar function
description: For a smooth real functionf on an open subset ofℝⁿ and a nonnegative measurableg, ∫g(x)|∇f(x)|dx=∫_ℝ∫_{f⁻¹(t)}g(x)dH^(n−1)(x)dt, allowing infinity.

title: Sard theorem for a smooth scalar function
description: For a smooth functionf:Ω⊂ℝⁿ→ℝ, the set of critical valuesf({x:Df(x)=0}) has Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Anisotropic perimeter defined by a support function
description: For a convex bodyK containing0 in its interior and a bounded Lipschitz domainE, P_K(E)=∫_{∂E}h_K(ν_E)dH^(n−1), whereν_E is the outward unit normal.

title: Wulff anisotropic isoperimetric inequality
description: For a convex bodyK containing0 in its interior and a bounded Lipschitz domainE, P_K(E)≥n|K|^(1/n)|E|^((n−1)/n).

title: Quadratic control by the arithmetic–geometric mean defect
description: For positiveλ₁≤⋯≤λ_n, letλ_A=n⁻¹∑λ_i andλ_G=(∏λ_i)^(1/n). Then ∑_i(λ_i−λ_G)²≤7n²λ_n(λ_A−λ_G).

title: Singular values of a complex matrix
description: For a complex m×n matrix M, its singular values σ₁≥⋯≥σ_q≥0, q=min(m,n), are the nonnegative square roots of the eigenvalues of M*M, with the additional forced zero eigenvalues omitted when n>m.

title: Schatten norm of a finite matrix
description: For a real or complex matrix M with singular values σ_j and1≤p<∞, its Schatten p-norm is ‖M‖_p=(∑σ_j^p)^(1/p); ‖M‖_∞=maxσ_j is the operator norm. The p=1 case is the nuclear norm and p=2 is the Frobenius norm.

title: Singular-value rank truncation
description: For an SVD M=∑_(j=1)^qσ_j u_jv_j*, choose M_r=∑_(j≤r)σ_j u_jv_j* and M_c=M−M_r. Repeated singular values can make the choice nonunique, while the singular values and Schatten norms of the head and tail are well defined.

title: Linear matrix measurement map
description: For fixed matrices A₁,…,A_m of the same size as X, a linear matrix measurement map sends X to (tr(XA_j*))_(j=1)^m. On Hermitian matrices with Hermitian A_j, this takes real values; noisy data have the form b=A(X)+w.

title: Nuclear norm minimization for noisy matrix recovery
description: Given a linear matrix measurement map A, data b and tolerance η≥0, nuclear norm recovery chooses a minimizer of ‖Z‖₁ subject to ‖A(Z)−b‖₂≤η; with η=0 this imposes A(Z)=b. Uniqueness and stable recovery require further hypotheses on A.

title: Frobenius robust rank null space property
description: A linear matrix measurement map A has the Frobenius robust rank null space property of order r with constants0<ρ<1 and τ>0 if, for every matrix M, ‖M_r‖₂≤ρ‖M_c‖₁/√r+τ‖A(M)‖_(ℓ²), where M_r is its singular-value rank-r truncation and M_c its tail.

title: Stable rank null space property
description: A linear matrix measurement map A has the stable rank null space property of order r with constant0<ρ<1 if ‖M_r‖₁≤ρ‖M_c‖₁ for every M in kerA.

title: Rank restricted isometry property
description: A linear matrix measurement map A has the rank-r restricted isometry property with constant δ∈[0,1) if (1−δ)‖X‖_F²≤‖A(X)‖_(ℓ²)²≤(1+δ)‖X‖_F² for every matrix X of rank at most r.

title: Phase retrieval from quadratic measurements
description: Phase retrieval asks to recover a real or complex vector x from intensities |a_j*x|². In the complex case x is identifiable only up to multiplication by a scalar of modulus1; lifting X=xx* turns these observations into linear rank-one matrix measurements tr(a_ja_j*X).

title: Finite-dimensional density matrix
description: A density matrix is a positive semidefinite complex matrix with trace1; its rank measures the number of nonzero eigenvalues in its spectral decomposition.

title: Finite-dimensional positive operator-valued measure
description: A finite POVM on ℂⁿ is a finite collection of positive semidefinite matrices E_j with ∑E_j=I. For a density matrix X, its outcome probabilities are tr(E_jX).

title: Rank-restricted informational completeness
description: A finite POVM is rank-r informationally complete if every two distinct density matrices X,Z of rank at most r have tr(E_jX)≠tr(E_jZ) for some POVM element E_j.

title: Weighted approximate complex projective t-design
description: For unit vectors w_i∈ℂⁿ and weights p_i≥0 summing to1, the weighted family is an approximate projective t-design of Schatten-p accuracy θ if ‖∑p_i(w_iw_i*)^(⊗t)−∫_(‖w‖₂=1)(ww*)^(⊗t)dσ(w)‖_p≤θ/binom(n+t−1,t), where σ is uniform spherical probability. Accuracy0 gives an exact design.

title: Standard complex Gaussian vector
description: A standard complex Gaussian vector has independent coordinates (g_j+ih_j)/√2, where all g_j,h_j are independent real N(0,1) variables; thus E|a_j|²=1.

title: Rademacher random sequence
description: A Rademacher sequence consists of independent random variables ε_j with P(ε_j=1)=P(ε_j=−1)=1/2.

title: Gaussian width of a Euclidean set
description: For T⊆ℝᵈ, its Gaussian width is w(T)=E sup_(x∈T)⟨g,x⟩ for a standard Gaussian vector g∈ℝᵈ, whenever the supremum is measurable; in the compact finite-dimensional sets used here it is finite.

title: Spectral condition number of an invertible matrix
description: For an invertible square real or complex matrix W, its spectral condition number is κ(W)=σ_max(W)/σ_min(W)=‖W‖_(op)‖W⁻¹‖_(op).

title: Positive semidefinite matrix square root
description: For a positive semidefinite complex matrix W=Udiag(λ_j)U*, its positive square root is W^(1/2)=Udiag(√λ_j)U*; this does not depend on the chosen orthonormal eigenbasis.

title: Nuclear singular-value perturbation inequality
description: For complex matrices X,Y of equal size with singular values in decreasing order, ∑_j|σ_j(X)−σ_j(Y)|≤‖X−Y‖₁.

title: Schatten tail bound from the nuclear norm
description: For a matrix M,1≤r≤min(m,n) and1≤p<∞, its singular-value tail satisfies ‖M_c‖_p≤r^(1/p−1)‖M‖₁.

title: Schatten error bound under the Frobenius robust rank null space property
description: If A has Frobenius robust rank null space constants0<ρ<1,τ>0 of order r, then for1≤p≤2 and all X,Z, ‖Z−X‖_p≤(1+ρ)²[(1−ρ)r^(1−1/p)]⁻¹(‖Z‖₁−‖X‖₁+2‖X_c‖₁)+τ(3+ρ)(1−ρ)⁻¹r^(1/p−1/2)‖A(Z−X)‖_(ℓ²). Consequently any nuclear-norm minimizer with noise at mostη obeys the p=2 bound2(1+ρ)²[(1−ρ)√r]⁻¹‖X_c‖₁+2τ(3+ρ)(1−ρ)⁻¹η.

title: Null space characterization of uniform nuclear-norm exact recovery
description: For a linear matrix measurement map A, every matrix X of rank at most r is the unique nuclear-norm minimizer with data A(X) if and only if ‖M_r‖₁<‖M_c‖₁ for every nonzero M∈kerA.

title: Second-countable topological space
description: A topological space is second countable if it has a countable basis: a sequence of open sets such that every open set is their union over some index set.

title: Measurable state space of a dynamical system
description: For a probability-preserving transformation S of (Y,F,m), a state space is a measurable map π:Y→X to a measurable space. It carries π_*m and is identified inside Y with the sub-σ-algebra π⁻¹F_X; S need not induce a map on X.

title: Koopman operator of a probability-preserving transformation
description: For a probability-preserving transformation S, its Koopman operator on L^p,1≤p≤∞, is U_Sf=f∘S. It is an isometry; for invertible S with measurable inverse it is unitary on complex L².

title: Multiplication by a bounded measurable function on L²
description: For a bounded measurable function h on a measure space, the multiplication operator M_h on L² sends f to hf; its operator norm is the essential supremum of|h|.

title: Compressed Koopman averaging operator
description: For a measurable dynamical state space with conditional expectation P_Xf=E[f|F_X], its averaging operator is T=P_XU_SP_X on L²(Y), restricted when desired to L²(F_X). This is a contraction and fixes constants; the family P_XU_S^nP_X need not equal T^n.

title: Markov module property for a compressed Koopman operator
description: A probability-preserving system with state σ-algebra F_X has the Markov module property if there is a closed U_S-invariant subspace M⊆L²(Y), containing L²(F_X) and stable under multiplication by every bounded F_X-measurable function, such that P_XU_SP_Xf=P_XU_Sf for every f∈M.

title: Twisted compression identity under the Markov module property
description: If a compressed Koopman state space has the Markov module property, then P_X(M_hU_SM_h)^nP_X=(M_hTM_h)^n for every bounded F_X-measurable h and n≥1. In particular P_XU_S^nP_X=T^n.

title: Binary Pinsker inequality
description: For a,b∈[0,1], the binary relative entropy D(a‖b)=a log(a/b)+(1−a)log((1−a)/(1−b)) satisfies D(a‖b)≥2(a−b)², using the usual zero/infinite endpoint conventions.

title: Large-deviation bound for a Koopman state space with the Markov module property
description: Let a probability-preserving system with state space X have the Markov module property, and let its averaging operator satisfy0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1. For an X-measurable0≤φ≤1 with p=∫φdm∈(0,1), set A_n=n⁻¹∑_(i=0)^(n−1)φ∘S^i. If η∈[p,1], k≥1 and θ=λ^k≤(η−p)/(1−p), then m(A_n≥η)≤k exp(D(η‖p)) exp(−nD(η‖θ+(1−θ)p)/k). If η∈[0,p] and θ≤(p−η)/p, the analogous lower-tail bound replaces the last entropy by D(η‖(1−θ)p).

title: Entropy of a finite measurable partition
description: For a finite measurable partition ξ of a probability space, H_m(ξ)=−∑_(A∈ξ)m(A)logm(A), with0log0=0. The join ξ∨η consists of the nonempty intersections of their atoms.

title: Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of a probability-preserving transformation
description: For a probability-preserving transformation S and finite measurable partition ξ, set h_m(S,ξ)=lim_(n→∞)n⁻¹H_m(∨_(i=0)^(n−1)S^(-i)ξ), equivalently the infimum over n by entropy subadditivity. Its measure entropy is h_m(S)=sup_ξh_m(S,ξ), possibly infinite.

title: Two-sided metric Bowen ball
description: For an invertible map S of a metric space, the two-sided Bowen ball of radius r and length2n+1 about y is {z:d(S^iz,S^iy)<r for every−n≤i≤n}.

title: Shannon–McMillan–Breiman theorem for a finite partition
description: For an invertible ergodic probability-preserving transformation S and finite measurable partition ξ, −(2n+1)⁻¹logm((∨_(i=−n)^nS^(-i)ξ)(y)) converges almost surely to h_m(S,ξ), where the expression uses the atom containing y.

title: Entropy approximation by increasing generating finite partitions
description: If finite measurable partitions ξ_l increase and their generated σ-algebra is the whole probability σ-algebra modulo null sets, then h_m(S,ξ_l) increases to h_m(S) for a probability-preserving transformation S.

title: Local entropy lower bound on a second-countable metric space
description: Let S be an invertible continuous ergodic probability-preserving transformation with measurable inverse on a second-countable metric space with Borel probability m and finite h_m(S). Then for m-almost every y, lim_(r↓0)liminf_(n→∞)−(2n+1)⁻¹logm(B_r^(-n,n)(y))≥h_m(S).

title: Lattice in a locally compact group
description: A lattice in a locally compact group G is a discrete subgroup Γ for which Γ\G carries a finite nonzero right G-invariant measure; normalize it to probability. It is cocompact if Γ\G is compact.

title: Bowen neighborhood for translation on a homogeneous quotient
description: For a group element a and identity neighborhood B, its(s,t)-Bowen neighborhood is B^(s,t)=∩_(i=s)^ta^(-i)Ba^i. On a quotient Γ\G the corresponding translate about y is yB^(s,t), using the stated right-action convention.

title: Homogeneity of Haar volume for Bowen neighborhoods
description: An identity neighborhood B in a locally compact group is(a,h)-homogeneous if some C>0 satisfies vol(B^(s,t))≥C exp(−h(t−s+1)) whenever s≤0≤t. Haar volume is a-homogeneous if for every h>h_m(a) such neighborhoods form a basis at the identity, where m is the invariant probability on a lattice quotient.

title: Cyclic group
description: A group G is cyclic if there is an element g such that every element of G equals gⁿ for some integer n. A finite cyclic group has a finite order equal to the order of a generator.

title: Cyclotomic Z_l-extension of a nonarchimedean local field
description: For a finite extension F of ℚ_p and a prime ℓ, the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension Fᶜ/F is the unique ℤ_ℓ subextension of F(μ_(ℓ∞))/F. When F contains μ_(2ℓ), adjoining all ℓ-power roots of unity already gives this extension.

title: L-primary completion of a local multiplicative group
description: For a nonarchimedean local field F and prime ℓ, the ℓ-primary completion of its multiplicative group is ℛ_F=lim←_r F×/(F×)^(ℓʳ), with the natural quotient transition maps and inverse-limit topology. It carries the continuous norm maps induced by finite local-field extensions.

title: Local logarithmic unit group
description: For a nonarchimedean local field F, let Fᶜ/F be its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension with finite layers F_n. Its logarithmic unit group is ⋂_(n≥0)N_(F_n/F)(ℛ_(F_n))⊆ℛ_F, where ℛ_F is the ℓ-primary completion of F×.

title: Global logarithmic unit group
description: For a number field K and prime ℓ, its logarithmic unit group is the subgroup of ℤ_ℓ⊗_ℤK× whose image in ℛ_(K_v) belongs to the local logarithmic unit group for every finite place v of K. These canonical local images are induced by K×→K_v×.

title: Hasse norm theorem for a cyclic number-field extension
description: Let L/K be a finite cyclic extension of number fields. An element a∈K× is a norm from L× exactly when, for every place v of K and a place w of L above v, its image in K_v× is a norm from L_w×.

title: L-adic Hasse norm theorem for cyclic l-extensions
description: For a cyclic degree-ℓⁿ number-field extension L/K with K containing μ_(2ℓ), an element of ℤ_ℓ⊗K× lies in N_(L/K)(ℤ_ℓ⊗L×) exactly when its images in every finite-place ℓ-primary multiplicative completion are local norms from L.

title: Logarithmic units as cyclotomic global norms
description: For a number field K containing μ_(2ℓ) with cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞=⋃K_n, its logarithmic unit group is ⋂_(n≥0)N_(K_n/K)(ℤ_ℓ⊗K_n×). This intersection is taken after ℓ-adification and need not equal ℤ_ℓ⊗(⋂_(n≥0)N_(K_n/K)K_n×).

title: Cyclotomic norms of logarithmic units
description: For K∞=⋃K_n the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension, its group of cyclotomic norms of logarithmic units is N_(K∞/K)(Ẽ_(K∞))=⋂_(n≥0)N_(K_n/K)(Ẽ_(K_n)), a subgroup of Ẽ_K; here Ẽ denotes the global logarithmic unit group. This is a global norm intersection inside ℤ_ℓ⊗K×.

title: Norm-coherent principal ideles and logarithmic units
description: For a cyclotomic tower K∞/K with K containing μ_(2ℓ), norm-compatible sequences in ℝ_(K_n)=ℤ_ℓ⊗K_n× are exactly the norm-compatible sequences of logarithmic units. Their projection to level zero is ⋂_n N_(K_n/K)(Ẽ_(K_n)).

title: Locally cyclotomic abelian pro-l extension
description: For a number field K containing μ_(2ℓ), an abelian pro-ℓ extension L/K is locally cyclotomic if, for every finite intermediate E/K and every finite place v of K, each completion E_w/K_v is contained in the local cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K_vᶜ/K_v.

title: L-primary logarithmic class group of a number field
description: For a number field K containing μ_(2ℓ), let K^lc be the compositum of its locally cyclotomic abelian pro-ℓ extensions. Its ℓ-primary logarithmic class group is Gal(K^lc/K∞), where K∞/K is cyclotomic. This is the degree-zero logarithmic class-group convention.

title: Hilbertian radical in a cyclotomic tower
description: For K containing μ_(2ℓ), its Hilbertian radical is the subgroup of ℛ_K consisting of classes ℓ^(−r)⊗x such that, for every finite layer K_n of K∞/K, x lies in N_(K_n/K)(K_n×)(K×)^(ℓʳ).

title: Finite group algebra over a commutative ring
description: For a finite group G and commutative ring R, R[G] is the free R-module on symbols g∈G, with multiplication extended R-bilinearly from the group law. It need not be commutative if G is not abelian.

title: One-dimensional character with values in a ring
description: A one-dimensional R-valued character of a group G is a group homomorphism χ:G→R×, where R× is the multiplicative group of units of the commutative ring R.

title: Character idempotents for a prime-to-l cyclic group over Z_l
description: Let ℓ be odd and Δ cyclic of order d dividing ℓ−1. For every character χ:Δ→ℤ_ℓ×, e_χ=d^(−1)∑_(δ∈Δ)χ(δ)^(−1)δ is an idempotent in ℤ_ℓ[Δ]. These idempotents are pairwise orthogonal and sum to one, giving M=⊕_χ e_χM for every ℤ_ℓ[Δ]-module M.

title: L-adic Tate twist of a Galois module
description: For a ℤ_ℓ-module M with a Galois action and cyclotomic character χ_ℓ, its i-th Tate twist M(i), i∈ℤ, is the same underlying module with action σ⋅_i m=χ_ℓ(σ)^i(σ⋅m). Equivalently tensor with the rank-one module ℤ_ℓ(i), using the dual tensor power for negative i.

title: Leopoldt conjecture in the Z_l-extension form
description: For every number field K and prime ℓ, if Z is the compositum of all ℤ_ℓ-extensions of K and r₂ is the number of complex places of K, then Gal(Z/K) is isomorphic as a topological group to ℤ_ℓ^(r₂+1).

title: Coincidence of initial radicals for a logarithmically principal field
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), with |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓᵐ. If its ℓ-primary logarithmic class group is trivial, then its initial ℤ_ℓ-extension radical, the ℓᵐ-torsion of its universal Tate kernel, and the ℓᵐ-torsion of its Hilbertian radical coincide.

title: Norm surjectivity on cyclotomic root-of-unity groups
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓᵐ, and K_n be its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ layers. For every j≥n the norm N_(K_j/K_n) maps μ_(ℓ∞)(K_j) onto μ_(ℓ∞)(K_n).

title: Intersection of ordinary and twisted cyclotomic radical invariants
description: In the cyclotomic setup with |μ_(ℓ∞)(K)|=ℓᵐ and γ*=γ/(1+ℓᵐ), one has ℛ_(K∞)^(Γ_n)∩ℛ_(K∞)^(Γ_n*)=ℛ_(K_n)[ℓ^(m+n)], where Γ_n is generated by γ^(ℓⁿ) and Γ_n* by (γ*)^(ℓⁿ).

title: Energy measures do not charge polar sets
description: For a regular symmetric Dirichlet form, the finite energy measure of a bounded domain function vanishes on sets of zero capacity; hence quasi-continuous representatives can be used consistently in its composition and pushforward identities.

title: Strongly local energy-measure chain rule
description: For a strongly local regular symmetric Dirichlet form, bounded domainf and C¹ functionsΦ,Ψ withΦ(0)=Ψ(0)=0 and bounded derivatives, the compositions lie in the form domain and their mutual energy measure isν_(Φ(f),Ψ(f))=Φ′(f)Ψ′(f)ν_f. In Hino’s normalization2E(Φ(f),Ψ(f))=∫Φ′(f)Ψ′(f)dν_f.

title: Inner regularity of finite Borel measures on the real line
description: For a finite Borel measureρ onℝ and a Borel setA, ρ(A)=sup{ρ(K):K⊆A compact}.

title: Smooth cutoff for a compact subset of an open real set
description: IfK⊆O⊆ℝ withK compact andO open, there is h∈C_c^∞(ℝ) with0≤h≤1,h=1onK and supporth⊆O.

title: Bounded bilinear map of normed spaces
description: A bilinear mapB:E×F→G of normed spaces is bounded if||B(x,y)||≤C||x||||y|| for someC and allx,y; its norm is the least suchC.

title: Schatten class of a compact Hilbert-space operator
description: For1≤p<∞, the Schatten classS_p(H,K) consists of compact operatorsT:H→K whose singular values belong toℓᵖ, with norm||T||_p=(∑s_n(T)^p)^(1/p);p=1 gives trace class andp=2 gives Hilbert–Schmidt operators.

title: Lévy process taking values in a real Hilbert space
description: A Lévy process in a separable real Hilbert spaceU starts at0, has stationary independent increments and is continuous in probability, with a càdlàg version. In a filtered setting its incrementL(t)−L(s) is independent ofF_s for t>s; square integrability and meanzero are additional hypotheses.

title: Covariance range Hilbert space
description: For a nonnegative trace-class operatorQ on a real Hilbert spaceU, H_Q=ranQ^(1/2) carries the inner product⟨x,y⟩_{H_Q}=⟨Q^(−1/2)x,Q^(−1/2)y⟩_U, where the inverse is taken on(kerQ)⊥. It is a Hilbert space; vectorssqrt(γ_n)e_n for positive eigenvaluesγ_n form an orthonormal basis.

title: Hilbert-valued Itô integral for square-integrable Lévy martingales
description: For a meanzero square-integrableU-valued Lévy processL with covarianceQ and predictableΦ∈L²(Ω×[0,T];S₂(H_Q,H)), the integral∫ΦdL is theL² limit of integrals of predictable step processes with finite cylindrical noise-coordinate functionals extending continuously toU, whose integrals are coefficient operators applied to Lévy increments.

title: Itô isometry for Hilbert-valued Lévy martingale integrals
description: For a meanzero square-integrable Lévy martingaleL with covarianceQ and predictableΦ∈L²(Ω×[0,T];S₂(H_Q,H)), E||∫_0^TΦdL||_H²=E∫_0^T||Φ||_{S₂(H_Q,H)}²dt; the integral process is a square-integrable martingale.

title: Tensor product of real Hilbert spaces
description: For real Hilbert spacesH,K, H⊗₂K is the completion of the algebraic real tensor product for the inner product⟨h⊗k,h′⊗k′⟩=⟨h,h′⟩⟨k,k′⟩, extended bilinearly.

title: Projective tensor product of Banach spaces
description: For Banach spacesE,F over the same scalar field, E⊗̂_πF is the completion ofE⊗F for ||u||_π=inf{∑||e_j||||f_j||:u=∑e_j⊗f_j}, where the infimum ranges over all finite tensor representations.

title: Injective tensor product of Banach spaces
description: For Banach spacesE,F, E⊗̂_εF is the completion ofE⊗F for ||∑e_j⊗f_j||_ε=sup_{||a||_{E′},||b||_{F′}≤1}|∑a(e_j)b(f_j)|.

title: Bounded operators on projective, injective and Hilbert tensor products
description: BoundedS:E→E′ andT:F→F′ induce boundedS⊗T on projective and injective tensor completions, with norm||S||||T||. The same holds for Hilbert tensor products when the spaces are Hilbert.

title: Operator identifications of Hilbert tensor norms
description: For real Hilbert spacesH,K, h⊗k corresponds tox↦⟨x,h⟩k. Under this identification, the projective, Hilbert and injective completions are respectively trace-class, Hilbert–Schmidt and compact operatorsH→K with their corresponding norms; in particular||u||_ε≤||u||₂≤||u||_π and the canonical maps are injective.

title: Trace duality for compact Hilbert-space operators
description: For real Hilbert spacesH,K, every continuous linear functional onK(H,K) has the formT↦tr(ST) for a unique trace-classS:K→H, and its functional norm is||S||₁.

title: Duality of injective and projective Hilbert tensor products
description: For separable real Hilbert spacesH,K, (H⊗̂_εK)′ is isometrically identified withH′⊗̂_πK′ by the natural bilinear pairing.

title: Tensor second moment and covariance of a Hilbert random element
description: For a square-integrable random elementX in a real Hilbert spaceH, M₂X=E[X⊗X] andCovX=E[(X−EX)⊗(X−EX)] are Bochner integrals inH⊗̂_πH, withCovX=M₂X−EX⊗EX and||M₂X||_π≤E||X||².

title: Positive self-adjoint Hilbert generator with compact inverse
description: A positive compact-inverse generator is a densely defined self-adjoint operatorA on a real Hilbert space, bounded below by a positive constant and with compact inverseA⁻¹:H→H.

title: Spectral semigroup for a positive compact-inverse generator
description: A positive compact-inverse generator has an orthonormal eigenbasisAe_n=λ_ne_n withλ_n>0 andλ_n→∞ in infinite dimension. S(t)x=∑e^(−tλ_n)⟨x,e_n⟩e_n is a strongly continuous analytic contraction semigroup, and∫₀ᵀ||A^(1/2)S(t)x||²dt≤||x||²/2.

title: Fractional domain scale of a positive self-adjoint generator
description: For a positive self-adjointA with compact inverse and eigenpairs(λ_n,e_n), Ḣ^r=D(A^(r/2)) consists ofx with∑λ_n^r|⟨x,e_n⟩|²<∞, with that square-sum norm; A^(r/2)x=∑λ_n^(r/2)⟨x,e_n⟩e_n.

title: Lions–Magenes Hilbert-triple energy identity
description: IfV⊂H⊂V′ is a Hilbert Gelfand triple andv∈L²(0,T;V) has weak derivativev′∈L²(0,T;V′), thenv has a continuousH-valued representative and ||v(t)||_H²−||v(s)||_H²=2∫_s^t⟨v′,v⟩. Ifv(T)=0, sup_t||v(t)||_H²≤||v||_{L²V}²+||v′||_{L²V′}².

title: Parabolic space-time trial and terminal test spaces
description: ForV⊂H⊂V′, the parabolic trial space isX=L²(0,T;V) and the terminal test space isY={v∈L²(0,T;V):v′∈L²(0,T;V′),v(T)=0}, with ||v||_Y²=||v||_{L²V}²+||v′||_{L²V′}².

title: Diagonal pairing on projective trial and injective test tensors
description: LetW=L²(0,T;H) and let the Banach spaceY embed contractively inC([0,T];H). The pairingD(u₁⊗u₂,v₁⊗v₂)=∫⟨u₁(t),v₁(t)⟩⟨u₂(t),v₂(t)⟩dt extends to a bounded operatorW⊗̂_πW→(Y⊗̂_εY)′ of norm≤1. Replacing one or both trial factors byH gives bounds√T andT respectively.

title: Nečas inf-sup theorem on Hilbert spaces
description: For a bounded bilinearB:H₁×H₂→ℝ, its associated mapH₁→H₂′ is boundedly invertible exactly when both primal and transposed inf-sup constants are positive. In that case both constants equal||B⁻¹||⁻¹, and the solution toB(u,·)=f satisfies||u||≤||B⁻¹||||f||.

title: Backward parabolic space-time isomorphism
description: For positive self-adjointA with compact inverse, V=D(A^(1/2)), X=L²(0,T;V) and terminalY, B(u,v)=∫⟨u,−v′+Av⟩ defines an isomorphismB:X→Y′ with||B⁻¹||≤1 under the energy norms.

title: Affine stochastic evolution equation with Hilbert Lévy noise
description: For a positive compact-inverse generatorA and a centered square-integrableHilbert Lévy processL, the affine evolutiondX+AXdt=(G₁X+G₂)dL has a mild solution whenX(t)=S(t)X₀+∫₀ᵗS(t−s)(G₁X(s)+G₂)dL(s), withpredictableX, bounded timeL² moments,F₀-measurableX₀∈L²(Ω;H), bounded linearG₁:H→S₂(H_Q,H), andG₂∈S₂(H_Q,H).

title: Closed operators and Hilbert Lévy stochastic integrals
description: LetC:D(C)⊂H→K be closed. If predictableΦ takes values inD(C) and bothΦ andCΦ are square-integrable Hilbert–Schmidt integrands, then∫ΦdL lies inD(C) almost surely andC∫ΦdL=∫CΦdL.

title: Mild well-posedness of affine Hilbert Lévy evolution
description: The affine Hilbert Lévy evolution has a unique predictable mild solution with bounded timeL²(H) norm. For0≤r≤1, it has bounded timeL²(Ḣ^r) norm ifX₀∈L²(Ḣ^r) and∫₀ᵀ||A^(r/2)S(t)G₁||_{L(Ḣ^r,S₂(H_Q,H))}²dt<∞.

title: Stochastic Fubini theorem for Hilbert Lévy integrals
description: For a jointly measurable kernelK(s,t) predictable ins and satisfying∫(E∫||K(s,t)||_{HS}²ds)^(1/2)dt<∞, deterministic integration int and square-integrableHilbert Lévy stochastic integration ins commute, asH-valuedL² random variables.

title: Weak identity for a Hilbert Lévy mild solution
description: For the affine evolution mild solutionX andv∈C¹([0,T];D(A)) withv(T)=0, ∫₀ᵀ⟨X,−v′+Av⟩dt=⟨X₀,v(0)⟩+∫₀ᵀ⟨v,G(X)dL⟩ almost surely; the scalar weak integral pairsv(t) with the operator integrand before integration.

title: Projective second-moment regularity for affine Lévy evolution
description: Suppose the affine Lévy evolution has boundedL²(Ḣ^r) moments for some0≤r≤1 and∫₀ᵀ||A^(1/2)S(t)G₁||_{L(Ḣ^r,S₂(H_Q,H))}²dt<∞. ThenX∈L²(Ω;L²(0,T;V)) forV=D(A^(1/2)), andM₂X belongs toX_space⊗̂_πX_space, X_space=L²(0,T;V).

title: Deterministic projective/injective equation for a Lévy SPDE second moment
description: For the affine Lévy evolution with the stated projective moment regularity, assumeG₁:V→L(U,H) andG₂:U→H are bounded extensions. WithB the parabolic space-time map,q the noise covariance tensor andD the diagonal pairing, u=M₂X∈X_space⊗̂_πX_space satisfies(B⊗B)u−D((G₁⊗G₁)u q)=R₀₀M₂X₀+D([G₁m⊗G₂+G₂⊗G₁m+G₂⊗G₂]q) in(Y⊗̂_εY)′, wherem(t)=S(t)EX₀ andR₀₀ pairs both initial traces.

title: Small-noise uniqueness of the tensor variational moment equation
description: In the affine Lévy tensor setting, if||G₁||_{L(V,S₂(H_Q,H))}<1, the perturbed map(B⊗B)−D((G₁⊗G₁)(·)q) is bounded below by1−||G₁||² in the projective trial norm. Its variational equation therefore has at most one solution for every test-dual right-hand side; for the moment and covariance right-hand sides, the stochastic solution supplies existence.

title: Deterministic tensor variational equation for affine Lévy covariance
description: For the affine Lévy moment setting, c=CovX∈X_space⊗̂_πX_space satisfies[(B⊗B)−D((G₁⊗G₁)(·)q)]c=R₀₀CovX₀+D([G(m)⊗G(m)]q), wherem=S(·)EX₀. This equation has the unique solutionc for every bounded affineG₁ in the stated setting; no noise-smallness assumption is required after an exponential time-weight reduction.

title: Self-dual beta-deformed Barnes G-function
description: For β>0,Q=β+β⁻¹ and Re x>0, define G_β(x)=exp(L_β(x)), where L_β(x)=(x−Q/2)log(2π)/2+∫₀^∞[(e^(−Qt/2)−e^(−xt))/((1−e^(−βt))(1−e^(−t/β)))+e^(−t)(Q/2−x)²/2+(Q/2−x)/t]dt/t. This convergent integral fixes its normalization and makes G_β=G_(1/β); in particular G_β(Q/2)=1.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Regularized logarithmic gamma integral
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Shift relation for the self-dual beta-deformed Barnes function
description: For β>0 and Re x>0, G_β(x+β)=β^(1/2−βx)(2π)^((β−1)/2)Γ(βx)G_β(x), with G_β fixed by its convergent normalized integral.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Chi distribution with integer degrees of freedom
description: For a positive integer d, the chi distribution with d degrees of freedom is the law of(∑_(j=1)^dg_j²)^(1/2), where the g_j are independent standard real normal variables.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Trotter tridiagonal representation of GUE eigenvalues
description: Let H_N have GUE density proportional to exp(−2NtrH_N²). Its eigenvalue multiset has the same law as that of(2√(2N))⁻¹T_N, where T_N is real symmetric tridiagonal, its diagonal entries are independentN(0,2), its adjacent off-diagonal entries are independentχ_(2j),j=1,…,N−1, and all these random variables are mutually independent.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Euler beta–gamma integral for positive real parameters
description: For real a,b>0, Γ(a)Γ(b)=Γ(a+b)∫₀¹t^(a−1)(1−t)^(b−1)dt.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Gaussian integral on the real line
description: The real improper integral∫_(−∞)^∞e^(−x²)dx equals√π.
field: Random matrix theory and special functions

title: Homothetic projection theorem
description: Ifn≥3 and convex bodiesK,L⊂ℝⁿ have homothetic orthogonal projections onto every hyperplane, thenK andL are themselves homothetic.

title: Mixed volume with a segment and projection volume
description: For a full-dimensional convex bodyK⊂ℝⁿ and a unit vectoru, nV(K[n−1],[0,u]) equals the(n−1)-dimensional volume of the orthogonal projection ofK onto u⊥.

title: Derivative of a generalized quantile of an integrable density
description: For nonnegative integrablef onℝ withF=∫f>0, letq(t)=inf{x:F⁻¹∫_{−∞}^x f≥t},0<t<1. Thenq is increasing, pushes Lebesgue probability tof(x)dx/F, andf(q(t))q′(t)=F for almost everyt.

title: Area inequality for a monotone real map
description: Ifw:(a,b)→ℝ is increasing andh≥0 is measurable, then∫_ℝh(x)dx≥∫_a^b h(w(t))w′(t)dt; jumps and a singular part can only increase the left-hand mass not represented by the a.e. derivative.

title: Hausdorff quantitative BBL for positive power-concave functions
description: For fixedp>0,0<λ<1 and bounded nonnegativep-concaveu_i on convex compact supportsΩ_i with positive integralsI_i, anyh dominating theirp-Minkowski convolution satisfies∫h≥M_{p/(np+1)}(I₀,I₁;λ)+cH₀(Ω₀,Ω₁)^((n+1)(p+1)/p) whenH₀ is small. Herec>0 depends on the fixed dimension,weights,p,integrals,volumes andnormalized diameters.

title: Quantitative Brunn–Minkowski for torsional rigidity
description: For bounded open convexΩ₀,Ω₁⊂ℝⁿ and0<λ<1, torsional rigidityT defined by−Δu=1 satisfies T((1−λ)Ω₀+λΩ₁)≥M_{1/(n+2)}(T(Ω₀),T(Ω₁);λ)+c₁H₀^(3(n+1)) and also≥the same mean+c₂A^6 for sufficiently small respective distances, with positive constants depending on the fixed geometric and torsional data.

title: Quantitative Urysohn inequality for torsional rigidity
description: LetΩ⊂ℝⁿ,n≥2, be bounded open convex and centered at its centroid, and letΩ♯ be the centered ball of equal mean width. For sufficiently smallH=H(Ω,Ω♯), T(Ω♯)≥T(Ω)(1+cH^(3(n+1))); also T(Ω♯)≥T(Ω)(1+c′A_rot^6) for smallA_rot=sup_ρA(Ω,ρΩ), with positive fixed-data constants.

title: Finite-exponent quantitative Minkowski comparison for elliptic solutions
description: Under the power-Minkowski viscosity/comparison hypotheses with0<p<1, suppose positive solutionsu₀,u₁ arep-concave. For0<r<∞ the deficit∫u_λ^r−M_{p/(np+r)}(∫u₀^r,∫u₁^r;λ) is bounded below bycH₀^((n+1)(p+r)/p), and separately byc′A^(2(p+r)/p), for small distances and positive fixed-data constants including the normalized diameters when needed.

title: Finite-exponent quantitative mean-width rearrangement comparison
description: Under the rotational elliptic mean-width comparison hypotheses with0<p<1 andp-concave solutionu, letv solve the corresponding problem on the equal-width ball. For0<r<∞, ∫v^r≥∫u^r+cH(Ω,Ω♯)^((n+1)(p+r)/p), and separately≥∫u^r+c′A_rot^(2(p+r)/p), for sufficiently small distances and positive fixed-data constants depending on n,p,r,the moment and relevant diameter.

title: Zagier’s leading Eisenstein coefficient of a one-point q-bracket
description: For every integer r≥1, the normalized one-point bracket 𝒬_(2r)=2^(2r−2)(2r−1)!⟨Q_(2r)⟩_q is a polynomial of degree r in G₂=−E₂/24 over the rational level-one modular-form ring. Its leading coefficient is (2r−1)!!8^(r−1)/r, where (2r−1)!!=1·3·⋯·(2r−1).

title: Serre–Swinnerton-Dyer algebra of level-one forms modulo p
description: For p≥5 let A(X,Y) be the reduction of the homogeneous weight-(p−1) polynomial expressing E_(p−1) in E₄,E₆. The algebra of reductions of rational p-integral level-one modular forms is 𝔽_p[X,Y]/(A−1). The polynomial A is square-free; for a nonzero homogeneous F of weight k, its q-series filtration is k−r(p−1), where r is the greatest exponent with Aʳ dividing F.

title: Mod-p filtration of powers of E2
description: For p≥5 and every positive integer r, the reduction of E₂ʳ has level-one modular filtration r(p+1). The same formula holds for G₂ʳ, since G₂=−E₂/24 and 24 is a p-adic unit.

title: Modular and elliptic transformations of odd theta
description: Put Θ(z;τ)=−iθ[½,½](τ,z), q=exp(2πiτ). Then Θ(z;τ+1)=exp(πi/4)Θ(z;τ), Θ(z/τ;−1/τ)=−i√(−iτ)exp(πiz²/τ)Θ(z;τ), Θ(z+1;τ)=−Θ(z;τ), and Θ(z+τ;τ)=−exp(−πiτ−2πiz)Θ(z;τ). The square root is the holomorphic branch positive at τ=i.

title: Jacobi triple product for the odd theta function
description: For Θ=−iθ[½,½], q=exp(2πiτ), one has Θ(z;τ)=exp(πiτ/4)(exp(πiz)−exp(−πiz))∏_(n≥1)(1−qⁿ)(1−exp(2πiz)qⁿ)(1−exp(−2πiz)qⁿ). The products converge locally uniformly for τ in the upper half-plane.

title: Nonvanishing of an absolutely convergent complex product
description: If ∑_(n≥1)|a_n|<∞, then ∏_(n≥1)(1+a_n) converges and is nonzero exactly when none of its factors is zero. The corresponding local uniform assertion holds when the absolute sums converge uniformly on compact sets.

title: Simple zero lattice and derivative of odd theta
description: For τ in the upper half-plane, Θ(z;τ)=−iθ[½,½](τ,z) has exactly the simple zeros z∈ℤ+τℤ, and ∂Θ/∂z(0;τ)=2πiη(τ)³. In particular η has no zeros in the upper half-plane.

title: Eisenstein exponential formula for one-point q-brackets
description: As a formal power series in t, ∑_(k≥0)⟨Q_k⟩_q t^k=exp(2∑_(j≥1)G_(2j)t^(2j)/(2j)!), where G_(2j)=−B_(2j)/(4j)+∑_(n≥1)σ_(2j−1)(n)qⁿ and Q_k has the Bloch–Okounkov normalization.

title: S and T transformations of the Dedekind eta function
description: For τ in the upper half-plane, η(τ+1)=exp(πi/12)η(τ) and η(−1/τ)=√(−iτ)η(τ), using the holomorphic square-root branch positive at τ=i.

title: Real analytic function on an open Euclidean set
description: A real-valued or complex-valued function on an open subset of ℝᵈ is real analytic if, around each point a, it equals a power series ∑_(α∈ℕᵈ)c_α(x−a)^α that converges absolutely on some neighborhood of a.

title: Covariance of the Jacobi elliptic raising operator
description: For the weight-k index-m Jacobi modular slash action and real analytic φ, the elliptic raising operator Y_m satisfies Y_m(φ|_(k,m)γ)=(Y_mφ)|_(k+1,m)γ for every γ∈SL₂(ℤ). Thus Y_m preserves the index and raises the transformation weight by one, allowing nonholomorphic dependence on the elliptic variable.

title: Modular covariance of a Jacobi circular constant term
description: Suppose φ has weight-k index-m Jacobi modular covariance on Γ and is real analytic near z=0 apart from a finite-order singularity. Put Φ(z;τ)=exp(2πimz Im(z)/Im(τ))φ(z;τ). If A(τ)=lim_(r→0)∫₀¹Φ(r exp(2πit);τ)dt exists, then A(γτ)=(cτ+d)^kA(τ) for every γ∈Γ. This assertion is a transformation law and does not alone imply holomorphy or cusp growth.

title: Countable set
description: A set is countable if it admits an injection into the natural numbers; finite sets are included.

title: One-sided Dini derivatives
description: For a real functionF, its upper and lower right Dini derivatives are limsup andliminf_{h↓0}(F(x+h)−F(x))/h; upper and lower left derivatives useh↑0. These are extended-real limits;F is differentiable exactly when all four agree and are finite.

title: Rising sun lemma
description: For continuousG on[a,b], the pointsx admitting a latery withG(y)>G(x) are covered by countably many disjoint intervals(a_j,b_j) withG(b_j)≥G(a_j), while outside those intervalsG(y)≤G(x) for every latery. Interior interval endpoints have equalG values.

title: Continuous and jump decomposition of a bounded monotone function
description: A bounded nondecreasing real function is the sum of a continuous nondecreasing function and an absolutely summable positive linear combination of unit step jumps, allowing each step an intermediate value at its jump point. It has only countably many discontinuities.

title: Sobolev regularity for the smooth Dirichlet Poisson problem
description: On a bounded smooth domainΩ, a weak zero-boundary solutionu∈H₀¹(Ω) of−Δu=f withf∈H^m(Ω),m≥0integer, belongs toH^{m+2}(Ω), with anH^{m+2} estimate controlled byf andthe domain.

title: Higher Sobolev embedding into continuous derivatives
description: On a bounded smoothΩ⊂ℝⁿ, H^m(Ω) embeds continuously intoC^k(Ω̄) wheneverm>k+n/2, for nonnegative integersm,k.

title: Weak comparison principle for the Poisson equation
description: Ifu,v∈H¹(Ω), (u−v)_+∈H₀¹(Ω) and−Δu≤−Δv weakly on a bounded domain, thenu≤v almost everywhere; continuous representatives obey the pointwise inequality.

title: Hopf boundary lemma for a positive Poisson solution
description: For a smooth domain and a positive classicalsolutionu of−Δu=c>0 with zeroDirichletdata, an interior tangent ball at a boundarypoint forces a strictly positive derivative in every strictly inward direction there.

title: Continuity of torsion functions under convex-domain convergence
description: If convex bodiesK_j converge to a full-dimensionalK in Hausdorff distance, the zero-extended weak solutionsu_j of−Δu_j=c>0 onintK_j withzeroDirichletdata converge uniformly to the corresponding zero-extendedu onintK.

title: Spectrum of a boundary-fixed harmonic extension matrix
description: For a regular harmonic structure on a connected p.c.f. self-similar set with every boundaryp_i fixed by a cell map andK\{p_i} connected, the harmonic extension matrixA_i has simple eigenvalues1 andr_i, every other eigenvalue has modulus<r_i, and thep_i-columnu_i ofD is a nonzero left r_i-eigenvector orthogonal to constants. There is a nonnegative right r_i-eigenvectorv_i uniquely normalized by(u_i,v_i)=1.

title: Cell energy formula for a p.c.f. harmonic function
description: For a regular harmonic structure(D,r), harmonicf with boundary vectorx and a cell wordw, its Hino-normalized energy measure satisfiesν_f(K_w)=−2r_w⁻¹(A_wx)^TD(A_wx), whereA_w is harmonic restriction to that cell.

title: Self-similar decomposition of energy measures
description: For the regular strongly local form associated with a regular p.c.f. harmonic structure, its energy measures obeyν_f(B)=∑_(|w|=m)r_w⁻¹ν_(f∘ψ_w)(ψ_w⁻¹B) for BorelB and each cell levelm, using quasi-continuous versions.

title: Finite complex Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization
description: In a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, every linearly independent finite listv₁,…,v_k can be transformed into an orthonormal listq₁,…,q_k with span(q₁,…,q_j)=span(v₁,…,v_j) for everyj. Every orthonormal list inℂⁿ extends to an orthonormal basis; for a prescribed nonzero first vector the completion can be chosen Borel measurably.

title: Bilateral Laplace inversion on an integrable vertical line
description: Letμ be a Borel probability onℝ andc∈ℝ with∫e^(cx)dμ(x)<∞. IfF(t)=∫e^((c+it)x)dμ(x) belongs toL¹(ℝ), thenμ has the continuous densityf(x)=e^(−cx)(2π)⁻¹∫_(−∞)^∞e^(−itx)F(t)dt.

title: Multiplier between analytic Hilbert function spaces
description: For analytic reproducing-kernel Hilbert spacesR₁(E),R₂(F), a holomorphicoperator-valuedΘ:𝔻→B(E,F) is a multiplier if pointwise multiplicationf(z)↦Θ(z)f(z) defines a bounded mapR₁(E)→R₂(F). A partially isometric multiplier has a partial-isometry multiplication operator.

title: Invariant subspaces of a contractive analytic RKHS
description: LetR be an analyticRKHS on𝔻 whose coordinate multiplier is contractive. Every closed coordinate-invariant subspaceS⊂R⊗E* isΘH²(E) for an auxiliaryHilbertE and a partially isometric multiplierΘ:H²(E)→R⊗E*.

title: Multiplier quotient model for a kernel-contractive operator
description: For a standard analyticRKHS R_k and a k-contractive operatorT with defectC, T is unitarily equivalent to the compression ofM_z to(R_k⊗D)⊖ΘH²(E), whereD=closure(ranC) andΘ is a partially isometric analytic multiplier for someE.

title: Multiplier model for doubly commuting standard-kernel tuples
description: LetT_i be doubly commuting k_i-contractive operators for standard analytic spacesR_{k_i}, with commuting positive defectsC_i andD=closure(ran∏C_i). ThenT is unitarily equivalent to coordinate compression on(R_{k₁}⊗⋯⊗R_{k_n}⊗D)⊖∑ranΘ_i, with closed sum and one-coordinate partially isometric Hardy multipliersΘ_i tensored with identities on other factors.

title: Generation for nonlinear port–controller feedback
description: For an impedance-passive port-Hamiltonian boundarysystem(𝔄,𝔅,𝔠) and anm-dissipative controllerrelationM_c onX_c×U, defineA(x,x_c)=(𝔄x,z_c) when(z_c,𝔅x)∈M_c(x_c,𝔠x). This feedbackrelation ism-dissipative and densely defined onX×closure(Π_{X_c}D(M_c)), and generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup there.

title: Exponential stability criterion for nonlinear boundary–controller feedback
description: For passive plant(𝔄,𝔅,𝔠) and controller(z_c,y_c)∈M_c(x_c,u_c), assume0∈M_c(0), Re⟨(z_c,y_c),(x_c,u_c)⟩≤−ρ(||x_c||²+||Πu_c||²), ||y_c||²≤c(||x_c||²+||Πu_c||²), and||x_c(t₀)||²≤(1−δ)||x_c(0)||²+c||Πu_c||²_{L²(0,t₀)}. If a plantfunctionalq satisfies|q(x)|≤C||x||² and||x||²+dq(x)/dt≤C(||𝔅x||²+||Π𝔠x||²), then the interconnected contraction semigroup is uniformly exponentially stable at0.

title: First-order port–controller exponential stability from one-end observability
description: Under the nonlinear boundary-controller exponential criterion’s controllerhypotheses, let the passive port-Hamiltonian plant haveorder1 and Lipschitz coerciveHamiltoniandensityH. If||(Hx)(1)||²≤C(||𝔅x||²+||Π𝔠x||²) on the plantdomain, then its nonlinear controllerfeedback generates a contraction semigroup with globally uniformly exponentially stable equilibrium0.

title: Multidimensional DOST nonstationary system
description: Partition each frequencycorona{2^(p−1)≤||ξ||∞<2^p} into half-open boxes of sideβ_p=2^(p−1), and letI_{p,ℓ} be their integerpoints, with a finitecentralblockandβ₀=1. For windowφ andµ,ν>0, the multidimensionalDOST system consists ofT_{νk/β_p}[β_p^(−d/2)∑_{η∈µI_{p,ℓ}}e^(2πiη·x)φ(x)], k∈ℤᵈ.

title: Painless multidimensional DOST frame theorem
description: Letφ be Schwartz with compactly supported nonnegativeFouriertransform and letΦ_{p,ℓ}=∑_{η∈µI_{p,ℓ}}φ̂(·−η). IfΦ are uniformly bounded byC₁, atmostC₂ are nonzero at eachfrequency, andsomeΦ≥C₃>0 at everyfrequency, then the multidimensionalDOST system is anL² frame for sufficiently smallν, with boundsC₃²/νᵈ andC₁²C₂/νᵈ. Its canonical dual is obtained by dividing eachΦ byΣ|Φ|² and multiplying byνᵈ.

title: Star homomorphism between C*-algebras
description: A star homomorphism φ:A→B between C*-algebras is a complex-linear multiplicative map satisfying φ(a*)=φ(a)*. The algebras and map need not be unital. A unital star homomorphism additionally preserves the multiplicative identities when they exist.

title: Closed two-sided ideal of a C*-algebra
description: A closed two-sided star ideal I in a C*-algebra A is a complex vector subspace, closed in norm, with AI⊆I, IA⊆I and I*=I. Closed two-sided ideals in a C*-algebra are automatically star-stable.

title: Quotient C*-algebra
description: For a closed two-sided ideal I of a C*-algebra A, the quotient vector space A/I has induced multiplication and involution and quotient norm ‖a+I‖=inf_(x∈I)‖a+x‖; this is the quotient C*-algebra.

title: Algebraic star tensor product of C*-algebras
description: For C*-algebras A,B, their algebraic tensor product A⊙B over ℂ has multiplication (a⊗b)(a′⊗b′)=aa′⊗bb′ and involution (a⊗b)*=a*⊗b*, extended linearly and conjugate-linearly. No completion or C*-norm is part of this algebraic construction.

title: Minimal C*-tensor product
description: Given faithful star representations π:A→B(H) and ρ:B→B(K), the minimal C*-tensor product A⊗_min B is the operator-norm closure of (π⊗ρ)(A⊙B) in B(H⊗K). The spatial tensor norm is independent of the faithful representations.

title: Exact C*-algebra
description: A C*-algebra A is exact if for every C*-algebra B and closed two-sided ideal I⊆B the canonical sequence 0→I⊗_min A→B⊗_min A→(B/I)⊗_min A→0 is exact as a sequence of linear maps.

title: Arveson extension for completely positive contractions
description: Let A be a C*-subalgebra of B(H). Every completely positive contraction φ:A→B(K) extends to a completely positive contraction Φ:B(H)→B(K). When A contains the identity and φ is unital, the extension may be chosen unital.

title: Representation independence of completely positive approximation rank
description: For faithful star representations π:A→B(H) and ρ:A→B(K), finite Ω⊆A and δ>0, the least finite-dimensional C*-rank through which completely positive contractions approximate π on Ω within δ equals the corresponding rank for ρ, allowing the value infinity.

title: Topological entropy by finite open covers
description: For a continuous self-map T of a nonempty compact Hausdorff space X, h_top(T)=sup_𝒰 lim_(n→∞)n⁻¹log N(⋁_(j=0)^(n−1)T^(−j)𝒰), where 𝒰 ranges over finite open covers and N is the least cardinality of a subcover. The join consists of intersections of one set from each cover.

title: C*-algebra of complex continuous functions on a compact space
description: For a compact Hausdorff space X, C(X) is the unital commutative C*-algebra of continuous complex-valued functions, with pointwise addition and multiplication, conjugation as involution, and norm ‖f‖∞=sup_(x∈X)|f(x)|.

title: Character of a C*-algebra
description: A character of a C*-algebra A is a nonzero continuous star homomorphism χ:A→ℂ. The character space carries the topology of pointwise convergence on A, equivalently the relative weak-star topology in A*.

title: Gelfand representation of a commutative unital C*-algebra
description: For a commutative unital C*-algebra A, its character space Â is compact Hausdorff, and Γ:A→C(Â), Γ(a)(χ)=χ(a), is an isometric star isomorphism.

title: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a positive functional
description: For a positive complex linear functional φ on a complex star algebra, |φ(b*a)|²≤φ(a*a)φ(b*b) for every a,b.

title: Norm of a positive functional on a unital C*-algebra
description: A positive linear functional φ on a unital C*-algebra is bounded and ‖φ‖=φ(1). In particular it is a state precisely when φ(1)=1.

title: Weak-star compactness of a unital C*-algebra state space
description: The states S(A) of a unital C*-algebra form a weak-star compact convex subset of the dual unit ball. Every star automorphism α induces the weak-star homeomorphism ρ↦ρ∘α of S(A).

title: Embedding independence of contractive approximation rank
description: For a Banach space X, a finite set Ω⊆X and δ>0, the least d admitting contractive maps X→ℓ∞ᵈ→Y approximating a CA embedding ι:X→Y on Ω within δ is independent of the CA embedding. Here a CA embedding is an isometry admitting such finite-set approximations for every Ω,δ.

title: Kerr–Li positive CA entropy and dual-ball dynamics
description: Let α be an isometric automorphism of a Banach space X and T_α(ω)=ω∘α on the weak-star compact dual unit ball. If a closed T_α-invariant set Z has evaluation X→C(Z) an isomorphism onto a closed subspace, the conditions h_c(α)>0, h_top(T_α)>0, h_top(T_α)=∞, and h_top(T_α|Z)>0 are equivalent.

title: Kerr–Li equality of classical and approximation entropies
description: For a homeomorphism T of a compact Hausdorff space X and α_T(f)=f∘T on C(X), h_t(α_T)=h_c(α_T)=h_top(T), where h_t is Voiculescu–Brown entropy and h_c is contractive approximation entropy.

title: Zero Voiculescu–Brown entropy implies zero CA entropy
description: If α is a star automorphism of an exact C*-algebra and h_t(α)=0, then h_c(α)=0.

title: Singular value decomposition of a complex matrix
description: Every complex m×n matrixM admits M=UΣV*, whereU,V are unitary andΣ is rectangular diagonal with nonnegative diagonal entries equal to the singular values ofM in decreasing order.

title: Singular-value product bound in operator norm
description: For compatible real or complex matricesA,X,B and every singular-value indexj, σ_j(AXB)≤‖A‖_(op)‖B‖_(op)σ_j(X). For invertibleA,B this also givesσ_j(X)≤‖A⁻¹‖_(op)‖B⁻¹‖_(op)σ_j(AXB).

title: Rademacher desymmetrization for independent centered matrices
description: For independent mean-zero integrable random matricesX_i and independent Rademacher signsε_i, E‖∑ε_iX_i‖_(op)≤2E‖∑X_i‖_(op), whenever the right side is finite.

title: Gaussian increment comparison for expected suprema
description: For centered separable Gaussian processes(X_t),(Y_t) on the same index set with E(X_s−X_t)²≤E(Y_s−Y_t)² for all s,t and finite expected suprema, E sup_tX_t≤E sup_tY_t.

title: Gordon Gaussian comparison for a spherical infimum
description: For a real m×d matrixA with independent standard normal entries and nonemptyT⊆S^(d−1), E inf_(x∈T)‖Ax‖₂≥E‖g_m‖₂−E sup_(x∈T)⟨g_d,x⟩, whereg_m,g_d are standard Gaussian vectors.

title: Gaussian concentration for a Lipschitz function
description: Ifg is a standard Gaussian vector andF is realL-Lipschitz in Euclidean norm, then P(F(g)≤EF(g)−t)≤exp(−t²/(2L²)) and P(F(g)≥EF(g)+t)≤exp(−t²/(2L²)) for t>0.

title: Positive and negative moments of an integer-degree chi distribution
description: Forχ_d with d positive integer and reala>−d, Eχ_d^a=2^(a/2)Γ((d+a)/2)/Γ(d/2).

title: McDiarmid bounded differences inequality
description: For independent variablesX_i and an integrable realF whose value changes by at mostc_i when only coordinatei changes, P(F−EF≥t)≤exp(−2t²/∑c_i²) for t>0.

title: Rademacher symmetrization of a centered empirical supremum
description: For independent identically distributedX_i, an integrably bounded separable classF of real measurable functions, and independent Rademacherε_i, E sup_(f∈F)∑(Ef(X_i)−f(X_i))≤2E sup_(f∈F)∑ε_i f(X_i).

title: Rademacher contraction for an expected supremum
description: For a bounded setT⊆ℝ^m andL-Lipschitz real functionsψ_i withψ_i(0)=0, E_εsup_(t∈T)∑ε_iψ_i(t_i)≤L E_εsup_(t∈T)∑ε_it_i, whereε_i are independent Rademacher signs.

title: Expected Euclidean norm of a standard Gaussian vector
description: For a standard Gaussian vectorg∈ℝ^m, E‖g‖₂=√2Γ((m+1)/2)/Γ(m/2) and m/√(m+1)≤E‖g‖₂≤√m.

title: Expected operator norm of a standard real Gaussian matrix
description: IfG is an m×n real matrix with independentN(0,1) entries, then E‖G‖_(op)≤√m+√n.

title: Gordon escape through a spherical mesh
description: LetA be an m×d real matrix with independent standard normal entries,T⊆S^(d−1) nonempty, andw(T)=E sup_(x∈T)⟨g_d,x⟩. For everyt>0, P{inf_(x∈T)‖Ax‖₂≥E‖g_m‖₂−w(T)−t}≥1−exp(−t²/2).

title: Mendelson small-ball lower bound for independent linear measurements
description: Letφ_i be independent copies of an integrable random vectorφ∈ℝ^d, and letE be a nonempty bounded deterministic subset ofℝ^d. DefineQ_ξ=inf_(u∈E)P(|⟨φ,u⟩|≥ξ) andW_m=E sup_(u∈E)⟨m^(−1/2)∑ε_iφ_i,u⟩ with independent Rademacherε_i. Forξ>0,t≥0, with probability at least1−exp(−2t²), inf_(u∈E)(∑|⟨φ_i,u⟩|²)^(1/2)≥ξ√mQ_(2ξ)−2W_m−ξt.

title: Latała fourth-moment bound for an independent-entry matrix
description: For a real random matrixX with independent mean-zero entries and finite fourth moments, E‖X‖_(op)≤C[max_i(∑_jEX_ij²)^(1/2)+max_j(∑_iEX_ij²)^(1/2)+(∑_(i,j)EX_ij⁴)^(1/4)], whereC is universal.

title: Extreme singular values of a rectangular real Gaussian matrix
description: For an m×n matrixA,1≤n≤m, with independent real standard normal entries andt>0, P{√m−√n−t≤σ_min(A)≤σ_max(A)≤√m+√n+t}≥1−2exp(−t²/2).

title: Matrix Bernstein inequality for a self-adjoint sum
description: LetX_k be independent mean-zero self-adjoint n×n random matrices with‖X_k‖_(op)≤R almost surely. Setv=‖∑EX_k²‖_(op). Then for everyt>0, P{‖∑X_k‖_(op)≥t}≤2n exp[−t²/(2(v+Rt/3))].

title: Finite-dimensional real torus
description: The d-dimensional real torus is the quotient topological abelian group ℝᵈ/ℤᵈ, equivalently the product of d copies of the unit circle via x↦exp(2πix).

title: Positive definite function on a discrete group
description: A function φ:G→ℂ on a discrete group is positive definite if ∑_(i,j)c_i conjugate(c_j)φ(g_j⁻¹g_i)≥0 for all finite choices g_i∈G and c_i∈ℂ. Equivalently (g,h)↦φ(h⁻¹g) is a positive definite kernel.

title: Bochner representation on the integer lattice
description: Every positive definite function φ:ℤᵈ→ℂ has a unique finite positive Borel measure μ on ℝᵈ/ℤᵈ such that φ(n)=∫exp(2πi⟨n,x⟩)dμ(x). Its mass is φ(0), so it is a probability measure exactly when φ(0)=1.

title: Weyl exponential-sum criterion
description: A two-sided real sequence x_n is equidistributed modulo one if and only if (2N+1)⁻¹∑_(n=−N)^N exp(2πikx_n)→0 for every nonzero integer k. The analogous equivalence holds for one-sided Cesàro averages.

title: Limit superior of a real sequence
description: For a real sequence a_n, its limit superior is limsup a_n=inf_N sup_(n≥N)a_n, with values in the extended real line. Equivalently limsup a_n=−liminf(−a_n).

title: Van der Corput correlation bound
description: If |a_n|≤1, then for every integer H≥1, limsup_(N→∞)|N⁻¹∑_(n=1)^N a_n|²≤1/H+(2/H²)∑_(h=1)^(H−1)(H−h)limsup_(N→∞)Re(N⁻¹∑_(n=1)^(N−h)a_(n+h)conjugate(a_n)).

title: Conjugate complex Hilbert space
description: For a complex Hilbert space H, its conjugate H̄ has the same additive group, scalar multiplication c·ū=(conjugate(c)u)̄, and inner product ⟨ū,v̄⟩=conjugate(⟨u,v⟩). A unitary U induces Ūū=(Uu)̄.

title: Eigenvectors of a tensor product of unitaries
description: For unitary U on H and V on K, every vector w with (U⊗V)w=λw is a norm-convergent sum ∑_j c_j u_j⊗v_j, where (u_j) and (v_j) are orthonormal families, Uu_j=α_j u_j, Vv_j=β_j v_j, and α_jβ_j=λ for nonzero terms.

title: Compact vectors of one unitary operator
description: For a unitary T, the compact-vector subspace H_c(T) is the closed linear span of its eigenvectors. For every positive integer k, H_c(Tᵏ)=H_c(T).

title: Subgroups of finitely generated nilpotent groups are finitely generated
description: Every subgroup of a finitely generated nilpotent group is itself finitely generated and nilpotent.

title: Intersections of tensor product subspaces
description: For finitely many closed subspaces M_i⊆H and N_i⊆K, ⋂_i(M_i⊗N_i)=(⋂_iM_i)⊗(⋂_iN_i), where each tensor product is the closed Hilbert tensor subspace of H⊗K.

title: Null coefficients of polynomial nilpotent unitary orbits
description: Let G be a finitely generated nilpotent unitary group, g:ℤ→G polynomial with g(0)=1, and E=⟨g(ℤ)⟩. If u is orthogonal to H_c(E), then ⟨g(n)u,v⟩ is symmetric Cesàro-null for every v.

title: Distal compact metric dynamical system
description: A homeomorphism T of a compact metric space X is distal if inf_(n∈ℤ)d(Tⁿx,Tⁿy)>0 for every pair of distinct points x,y.

title: Minimal point of a compact dynamical system
description: A point x of a compact dynamical system (X,T) is minimal if its orbit closure contains no proper nonempty closed T-invariant subset. Equivalently, the orbit of every point in that closure is dense in the closure.

title: Syndetic subset of the integers
description: A set S⊆ℤ is syndetic if some positive integer L makes every integer interval {a,a+1,…,a+L} meet S.

title: Every point of a distal compact metric system is minimal
description: Every point in a distal compact metric dynamical system is a minimal point.

title: Distality of nilrotations
description: Every translation on a compact nilmanifold is a distal homeomorphism. Connectedness of the nilpotent Lie group is not required.

title: Syndetic return times of a minimal point
description: If x is a minimal point of a compact dynamical system and U is an open neighborhood of x, then {n∈ℤ:Tⁿx∈U} is syndetic. Conversely syndetic returns to every neighborhood imply minimality.

title: Algebra and uniform closure of nilsequences
description: For a fixed d≥1, basic d-step nilsequences form a complex algebra stable under conjugation and integer shifts; the same is true with no step bound. Their uniform closures, the d-step nilsequences and nilsequences, are uniformly closed algebras with the same invariances.

title: Polynomial phases are basic nilsequences
description: For every real polynomial p, the sequence exp(2πip(n)), n∈ℤ, is a basic nilsequence.

title: Connected simply connected realization of basic nilsequences
description: Every basic nilsequence can be realized as the restriction of a continuous test function along a nilrotation on a compact nilmanifold whose ambient nilpotent Lie group is connected and simply connected, allowing an increase of the dimension.

title: Interlacing nilsequences on finitely many arithmetic progressions
description: Let m≥1 and a be a bounded complex sequence on ℤ. If each subsequence a_(mt+r), 0≤r<m, is a basic nilsequence, a nilsequence, or an almost nilsequence with symmetric Cesàro-null remainder, respectively, then a has the same respective property.

title: Uniformly closed algebra of nilsequence plus null sequences
description: The bounded sequences that are sums of a nilsequence and a symmetric Cesàro-null sequence form a uniformly closed complex algebra invariant under conjugation and shifts. The same holds for a fixed nilpotency step bound.

title: Compact and weak part of a unitary representation
description: For a unitary representation of a group G on H, the compact vectors form a closed invariant subspace H_c, equal to the closed span of finite-dimensional invariant subspaces. Its orthogonal complement H_w is invariant, and H=H_c⊕H_w. For every unitary representation on K the diagonal tensor representation on H_w⊗K has no nonzero invariant vector.

title: Product normal form of polynomial sequences in a nilpotent group
description: For a nilpotent group G, the sequences g:ℤ→G annihilated by a sufficiently high iterate of Dg(n)=g(n)⁻¹g(n+1) are exactly finite products U₁^(p₁(n))⋯U_r^(p_r(n)) with U_j∈G and integer-valued polynomials p_j. If g(0)=1, the factors can be chosen with p_j(0)=0.

title: Holomorphic logarithm
description: A holomorphic logarithm of a nowhere-zero holomorphic function f on an open complex domain U is a holomorphic g:U→ℂ with exp(g)=f; on a connected U any two differ by a constant integer multiple of 2πi.

title: Residue of a meromorphic function
description: For a meromorphic function f near an isolated singularity a, its residue is (2πi)⁻¹∮f(z)dz around a sufficiently small positively oriented circle containing no other singularity; equivalently it is the coefficient of (z−a)⁻¹ in the Laurent expansion.

title: Residue theorem
description: For a meromorphic function near the closure of a bounded region with piecewise smooth oriented boundary, with finitely many poles inside and none on the boundary, the boundary integral is 2πi times the sum of the residues, with winding-number weights for a general closed contour.

title: Borel–Carathéodory theorem
description: Let f be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z−a|≤R and 0<r<R. Then max_{|z−a|≤r}|f(z)−f(a)|≤2r/(R−r)·(max_{|z−a|≤R}Re f(z)−Re f(a)).

title: Hadamard three-circles theorem
description: For a holomorphic f on an annulus r₁≤|z−a|≤r₃, continuous on its boundary, set M(r)=max_{|z−a|=r}|f(z)|. For r₁<r₂<r₃, log M(r₂)≤[log(r₃/r₂)log M(r₁)+log(r₂/r₁)log M(r₃)]/log(r₃/r₁), with zero values interpreted by a limit.

title: Phragmén–Lindelöf principle for a finite-order strip
description: Let f be holomorphic in a<Re z<b and continuous on its closure, with |f(σ+it)|≤exp(C(1+|t|)^N) uniformly in the strip. If |f|≤M on both vertical boundary lines, then |f|≤M throughout; if the two boundary values tend uniformly to zero as t→+∞, then the interior strip supremum also tends to zero.

title: Convexity bound for the Selberg class
description: For L in the Selberg class with gamma degree d_L=2∑λ_j, every ε>0 gives |L(σ+it)|≪_{L,ε}|t|^{d_L(1−σ)/2+ε}, uniformly 0≤σ≤1 and |t|≥2.

title: Smoothed second moment of a short Dirichlet polynomial
description: Let Φ∈C_c^∞((1,2)), ε>0 and R(t)=∑_{n≤N}r_n n^{−it}, with N≤T^{1−ε}. Then ∫ℝ|R(t)|²Φ(t/T)dt=T(∫Φ)∑|r_n|²+O_{Φ,ε}(∑|r_n|²), uniformly in all complex r_n and T≥2.

title: Logarithmic integral below one
description: For 0<x<1 define li(x)=∫₀ˣdt/log t. This improper integral is finite; its derivative is 1/log x.

title: Expansion of the logarithmic integral below one
description: For 0<x<1, li(x)=C+log(−log x)+∑_{j≥1}(log x)^j/(j·j!), where C is an absolute real constant. In particular li(x)=log(−log x)+O(1) as x↑1.

title: Second mean-value theorem for integrals
description: If f is a monotone real function on [a,b] and g is continuous there, some ξ∈[a,b] satisfies ∫ₐᵇfg=f(a)∫ₐ^ξg+f(b)∫_ξᵇg.

title: Tensor moments of a uniform complex unit vector
description: Ifw is uniform on the unit sphere ofℂⁿ andt is a positive integer, E(ww*)^(⊗t)=P_sym/binom(n+t−1,t), whereP_sym is the orthogonal projector onto tensors fixed by all factor permutations.

title: Positivity and trace-norm contraction of a partial trace
description: The partial traceTr_K on finite matrix tensors is characterized byTr_K(A⊗B)=tr(B)A. It maps positive semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices and satisfies‖Tr_K Z‖₁≤‖Z‖₁ for HermitianZ.

title: Expected norm of a matrix Rademacher series
description: For deterministic self-adjoint n×n matricesA_i and independent Rademacherε_i, E‖∑ε_iA_i‖_(op)≤√(2log(2n))‖∑A_i²‖_(op)^(1/2).

title: Matrix Chernoff bound for the expected norm of a positive sum
description: For independent positive semidefinite n×n matricesX_i with‖X_i‖_(op)≤L almost surely andμ=‖∑EX_i‖_(op), E‖∑X_i‖_(op)≤(e^τ−1)μ/τ+Llog(n)/τ for everyτ>0.

title: Cardinality of a Euclidean sphere net
description: For0<ε<1, the unit sphere inℝ^d has a finiteε-net of cardinality at most(1+2/ε)^d in Euclidean distance.

title: Small-ball bound for Gaussian or exact four-design quadratic measurements
description: LetZ be Hermitian with‖Z‖_F=1. Leta either be a standard complex Gaussian vector or have the law[n(n+1)]^(1/4)w, wherew is drawn from an exact weighted complex projective4-design. For0≤ξ≤1, P(|a*Za|≥ξ)≥(1−ξ²)²/24.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Small-ball bound for trace-accurate or norm-constrained operator-accurate four-designs
description: Letw be drawn from a weighted approximate complex projective4-design andseta=[n(n+1)]^(1/4)w. Ifθ₁≤1/4, then for every HermitianZ with‖Z‖_F=1 and0≤ξ≤1/√2, P(|a*Za|≥ξ)≥(1−2ξ²)²/192. The same bound holds underθ_∞≤1/(16s²),s≥1, provided also‖Z‖₁≤2√s.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Expected norm of a Gaussian rank-one Rademacher sum
description: For independent standard complex Gaussian vectorsa_i∈ℂⁿ and independent Rademacherε_i, ifm≥cn then E‖m^(−1/2)∑_(i=1)^mε_ia_ia_i*‖_(op)≤C√n for universalc,C>0.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Expected norm of a bounded isotropic rank-one Rademacher sum
description: FixK≥1. Let independent randoma_i∈ℂⁿ satisfy‖a_i‖₂²≤Kn almost surely and‖Ea_ia_i*‖_(op)≤K. For independent Rademacherε_i andm≥2nlogn,n≥2, E‖m^(−1/2)∑ε_ia_ia_i*‖_(op)≤C_K√(nlog(2n)), whereC_K depends only onK.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Helstrom formula for distinguishing two states with equal priors
description: For density matricesX,Y and priorprobabilities1/2 each, the largest probability of correctly identifying the state using any finite POVM is1/2+‖X−Y‖₁/4. Equivalently max_(0≤E≤I)|tr(E(X−Y))|=‖X−Y‖₁/2.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Banach space of bounded complex sequences on the integers
description: The space ℓ∞(ℤ) consists of bounded complex sequences a=(a_n)_(n∈ℤ), with pointwise vector operations and supremum norm ‖a‖∞=sup_n|a_n|. This norm makes it a Banach space.

title: Compact abelian topological group
description: An abelian topological group whose underlying topological space is compact Hausdorff.

title: Almost periodic complex sequence
description: A bounded complex sequence a_n on ℤ is almost periodic if a_n=f(τⁿx) for some compact abelian topological group G, τ,x∈G and continuous f:G→ℂ.

title: Bohr characterizations of almost periodic sequences
