description: For a bounded complex sequence on ℤ, almost periodicity is equivalent both to relative norm compactness of its integer translates in ℓ∞(ℤ), and to uniform approximability by finite linear combinations of the sequences exp(2πint), t∈ℝ/ℤ.

title: Heisenberg theta sequence
description: For real α,β, the Heisenberg theta sequence is ω_n(α,β)=κ(nα,nβ)exp(πin(n−1)αβ), where κ(s,t)=∑_(k∈ℤ)exp(−π(t+k)²)exp(2πiks) for real s,t. These sequences arise by evaluating theta functions along Heisenberg nilrotations.

title: Rational independence modulo one
description: Real numbers x₁,…,x_r are rationally independent modulo one if 1,x₁,…,x_r are linearly independent over ℚ, equivalently ∑_j m_jx_j∈ℤ with integers m_j forces all m_j=0.

title: Quadratic mean norm of a nilsequence
description: For a nilsequence a on ℤ, its quadratic mean norm is ‖a‖₂=(lim_(N→∞)N⁻¹∑_(n=0)^(N−1)|a_n|²)^(1/2). The limit exists for nilsequences; it agrees with integration of |f|² on the uniquely ergodic orbit closure for basic nilsequences, and extends by uniform approximation.

title: Host–Kra density of elementary theta sequences
description: The 2-step nilsequences are the uniformly closed shift-invariant linear span of sequences exp(2πins)exp(πin(n−1)t)∏_(j=1)^dω_n(α_j,β_j), where s,t∈ℝ/ℤ, d≥0 and α₁,…,α_d,β₁,…,β_d are rationally independent modulo one. Their linear span is also dense among 2-step nilsequences in the quadratic mean norm.

title: Host–Kra–Maass local cube criterion for nilsequences
description: For d≥2, a bounded complex sequence a is a (d−1)-step nilsequence iff for every ε>0 some L≥1 and δ>0 have this property: for all k,n₁,…,n_d∈ℤ, if |a_(k+∑η_jn_j+t)−a_(k+t)|<δ for every |t|≤L and every η∈{0,1}ᵈ except η=(1,…,1), then |a_(k+∑n_j)−a_k|<ε.

title: Homotopy of continuous maps
description: A homotopy from continuous f₀:X→Y to f₁:X→Y is a continuous map F:X×[0,1]→Y with F(x,0)=f₀(x) and F(x,1)=f₁(x). A homotopy relative to A⊆X additionally keeps F(a,t) constant in t for each a∈A.

title: Simply connected topological space
description: A path-connected space X is simply connected if every continuous loop γ:[0,1]→X with γ(0)=γ(1) is homotopic relative to its endpoints to the constant loop at γ(0).

title: Exponential map of a real Lie group
description: For a real Lie group G and X in its Lie algebra, exp_G(X)=γ_X(1), where γ_X:ℝ→G is the unique smooth group homomorphism with γ_X′(0)=X under the tangent-space identification at the identity.

title: Exponential diffeomorphism for simply connected nilpotent Lie groups
description: For a connected simply connected nilpotent real Lie group G, exp_G is a diffeomorphism from its Lie algebra onto G. In particular each g∈G has a unique mth root exp_G((1/m)log_G(g)) for every positive integer m.

title: Entropy formula for an integer toral automorphism
description: For A∈GL_d(ℤ), the induced homeomorphism T_A:x↦Ax of ℝᵈ/ℤᵈ has topological entropy ∑_(j=1)^d max(0,log|λ_j|), where λ_j are the complex eigenvalues of A with multiplicity.

title: Rapidly decreasing sequence on the integer lattice
description: A complex sequence a=(a_r)_(r∈ℤᵈ) is rapidly decreasing if sup_r(1+|r|²)^k|a_r|<∞ for every nonnegative integer k. These seminorms give the space its standard locally convex topology.

title: Smooth noncommutative torus
description: For the ordered monomials u^r=u₁^(r₁)⋯u_d^(r_d) in A_Θ, the smooth noncommutative torus A_Θ^∞ consists of the norm-convergent sums ∑_(r∈ℤᵈ)a_r u^r with rapidly decreasing coefficients. It has the topology of their rapid-decrease seminorms and the product and involution inherited from A_Θ.

title: Tracial state on a C*-algebra
description: A tracial state on a C*-algebra A is a state τ satisfying τ(ab)=τ(ba) for all a,b∈A. It is faithful if τ(a*a)=0 implies a=0.

title: Canonical trace of a noncommutative torus
description: The canonical faithful tracial state τ on A_Θ is determined on finite ordered Fourier sums by τ(∑_r a_r u^r)=a_0. It extends continuously to A_Θ; the ordered monomials form an orthonormal basis of the Hilbert completion for ⟨a,b⟩=τ(b*a), so that completion identifies with ℓ²(ℤᵈ).

title: Real torus
description: The n-dimensional real torus is the compact abelian topological group (ℝ/ℤ)^n with quotient topology and coordinatewise addition; integration of a periodic function is integration over [0,1]^n.

title: Sectorial Stirling formula for gamma
description: For each δ>0, uniformly as |z|→∞ in |arg z|≤π−δ, Γ(z)=√(2π)exp((z−1/2)Log z−z)(1+Oδ(|z|⁻¹)), where Log is the principal logarithm on the slit plane.

title: Riemann zeta function
description: The Riemann zeta function is ζ(s)=∑_{n≥1}n^{−s} for Re s>1, with its meromorphic continuation to ℂ, having a simple pole at1 and residue1. Its nontrivial zeros are the zeros with0<Re s<1, counted with multiplicity.

title: Classical logarithmic zero-free region for zeta
description: There is c>0 such that ζ(σ+it)≠0 whenever σ≥1−c/log(|t|+3), except for its pole at1.

title: Local zero count for the Riemann zeta function
description: For T≥2, the number of nontrivial zeta zeros ρ with |Imρ−T|≤1, counted with multiplicity, is O(log T).

title: Truncated explicit formula for the Chebyshev function
description: For half-integers x≥3 and T≥2, ψ(x)=x−∑_{|Imρ|<T}x^ρ/ρ+O(x log²(xT)/T+log x), where ρ runs over nontrivial zeros of ζ with multiplicity and ψ(x)=∑_{n≤x}Λ(n).

title: Jensen formula on a disk
description: If f is holomorphic near |z−a|≤R, f(a)≠0 and f has no zeros on the boundary, then (2π)⁻¹∫₀^{2π}log|f(a+Re^{iθ})|dθ=log|f(a)|+∑_{|ρ−a|<R}mρ log(R/|ρ−a|).

title: Local zero count in the Selberg class
description: For a fixed L in the Selberg class and T≥2, the number of nontrivial zeros ρ with |Imρ−T|≤1 is O_L(log(T+3)), counted with multiplicity.

title: Local logarithmic-derivative expansion in the Selberg class
description: For a fixed Selberg-class L, uniformly −5/2≤σ≤7/2 and sufficiently large |t| (depending on L) at points s=σ+it which are not zeros or poles, L′(s)/L(s)=∑_{ρ:|Imρ−t|≤1}(s−ρ)⁻¹+O_L(log|t|), with nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity.

title: Smoothed prime lower approximation for log L
description: Let L be in the Selberg class with Euler logarithm b(p^k)≪p^{kδ}, δ<1/2, and a(p)=|a(p)|e^{iωp}. If1/2≤σ<1,t₀≥15 and L(σ′+it)≠0 for σ′>σ, |t−t₀|≤2(log t₀)², then for every realθ and x>2 some |t₁|≤(log t₀)² gives Re(e^{−iθ}log L(σ+i(t₀+t₁)))≥(1/2)∑_{|log(p/x)|≤1}|a(p)|p^{−σ}cos(t₀logp−ωp)(1−|log(p/x)|)−C_L[x(log t₀)⁻²+x^{2δ−2σ+1/2}logx], using the Euler-normalized logarithm continued horizontally from Re s>1 and its finite boundary values.

title: Polynomial powers of a quasi-unipotent matrix on residue classes
description: If an invertible complex d×d matrix A has all eigenvalues roots of unity, some m≥1 satisfies (Aᵐ−I)ᵈ=0, and A^(mt+r)=Aʳ∑_(j=0)^(d−1)binom(t,j)(Aᵐ−I)^j for every t∈ℤ and 0≤r<m. Thus every entry is polynomial in t; if A is real the coefficients are real.

title: Scalar-commuting unitaries generate a two-step nilpotent group
description: If unitary operators U₁,…,U_d satisfy U_iU_j=ζ_(ij)U_jU_i with scalar |ζ_(ij)|=1, their generated group is nilpotent of class at most two: every group commutator is a scalar operator and is therefore central.

title: Norm density of Fourier polynomials in a noncommutative torus
description: Finite linear combinations of the ordered monomials u₁^(r₁)⋯u_d^(r_d), r∈ℤᵈ, are norm dense in A_Θ.

title: Discrete antiderivative of a polynomial
description: For every real polynomial P there is a real polynomial Q with Q(0)=0 and Q(n+1)−Q(n)=P(n). Thus for n≥0, Σ_(j=0)^(n−1)P(j)=Q(n), and the same polynomial identity extends to signed sums for negative n.

title: Contractivity of star homomorphisms of C*-algebras
description: Every star homomorphism φ:A→B of C*-algebras is contractive: ‖φ(a)‖≤‖a‖. An injective star homomorphism is isometric; in particular every star automorphism is isometric.

title: Exactness of a noncommutative torus
description: Every finite-dimensional noncommutative torus A_Θ is an exact C*-algebra.

title: Sarnak Möbius disjointness conjecture
description: For every homeomorphism T of a compact metric space X with h_top(T)=0, every continuous f:X→ℂ and every x∈X satisfy N⁻¹∑_(n=1)^N μ(n)f(Tⁿx)→0. Equivalently all bounded sequences realized by continuous observations of zero-entropy compact metric systems are Möbius-orthogonal.

title: Centered subGaussian real random variable
description: A centered real random variableX is subGaussian if someK≥0 satisfiesEexp(tX)≤exp(K²t²/2) for every realt.

title: Gaussian orthogonal ensemble in Frobenius normalization
description: GOE(n) here is the law of a real symmetric n×n matrix whose diagonal entries are independentN(0,1) and whose upper offdiagonal entries are independentN(0,1/2), independent also of the diagonal. Equivalently its coordinates in a real orthonormal Frobenius basis are independent standard normals.

title: Trace Hölder bound for nuclear and operator norms
description: For real or complex matricesA,B of equal size, |tr(A*B)|≤‖A‖₁‖B‖_(op).

title: Statistical dimension of a closed convex cone
description: For a closed convex coneC⊆ℝ^d, its statistical dimension isδ(C)=E‖Π_Cg‖₂², whereg is a standard Gaussian vector andΠ_C is the Euclidean nearest-point projection.

title: Gaussian nullspace phase bound for a convex cone
description: For a closed convex coneC⊆ℝ^d, statisticaldimensionδ(C), and an m×d matrixA with independent real standard normal entries, ifm≤δ(C)−t√d witht>0 thenP(kerA∩C≠{0})≥1−4exp(−t²/8).

title: Positive-semidefinite nullspace obstruction for Gaussian symmetric measurements
description: LetA(X)=(tr(A_iX))_(i=1)^m with independentA_i∼GOE(n) in Frobenius normalization andd=n(n+1)/2. For0<ε<1 andm≤(1−ε)d/2, with probability at least1−4exp(−ε²d/32), kerA contains a nonzero positive semidefinite realmatrixΔ. Consequently every noiseless positive-semidefinite feasibility set through anyX≥0 contains the unboundedrayX+tΔ,t≥0.

title: Ramanujan criterion for a polynomial Euler product
description: For a multiplicative Dirichlet series with fixed-length Euler factors ∏_{j=1}^m(1−α_j(p)p^{−s})⁻¹, the coefficient bounds |a(n)|≪εn^ε for every ε>0 are equivalent to |α_j(p)|≤1 for every p,j. In this case |a(p)|≤m.

title: Hadamard logarithmic-derivative identity under Selberg RH
description: Let L be a Selberg-class function with all nontrivial zeros ρ=1/2+iγ. For1/2<σ≤2 and sufficiently large |t|, away from zeros, Re[L′(σ+it)/L(σ+it)]=∑ρ(σ−1/2)/|σ+it−ρ|²−(d_L/2)log|t|+O_L(1); the nonnegative sum converges and counts multiplicities.

title: Perron integral for the positive logarithm
description: For y>0 and c>0, (2πi)⁻¹∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞}y^w w⁻²dw=max(logy,0); the vertical integral is absolutely convergent.

title: Formal derivative of a polynomial
description: For f(x)=∑_(i=0)^n a_ix^i over a commutative ring, its formal derivative is f′(x)=∑_(i=1)^n i a_ix^(i−1).

title: Integral basis from a local Eisenstein polynomial
description: If f is Eisenstein of degree n over a p-adic local field K and α is a root, then f is irreducible, L=K(α) is totally ramified of degree n, α is a uniformizer, and O_L=O_K[α], free over O_K with basis1,α,…,α^(n−1).

title: Derivative norm of a monogenic discriminant
description: For a monic separable degree-n polynomial f over K with root α and L=K(α) of degree n, the discriminant of1,α,…,α^(n−1) is (−1)^(n(n−1)/2)N_(L/K)(f′(α)). For a local integral basis this generates the field discriminant ideal.

title: Valuation of a local field norm
description: For a finite extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields with normalized discrete valuations, v_K(N_(L/K)x)=f(L/K)v_L(x), where f is the residue degree.

title: Coefficient criterion for the discriminant of an Eisenstein polynomial
description: Let f=xⁿ+∑_(i<n)f_ix^i be Eisenstein over K and J=an+b with0≤b<n. Put l(i)=max(2+a−v_K(i),1) for i<b and max(1+a−v_K(i),1) for i≥b. Then Disc(K(α)/K)=𝔭^(n+J−1) iff v_K(f_i)≥l(i) for1≤i<n and, when b≠0,v_K(f_b)=l(b), provided J satisfies Ore’s conditions.

title: Valuations of Eisenstein ramification coefficients
description: For Eisenstein f=xⁿ+∑_(k<n)f_kx^k over K, a root α and v_L(α)=1, the coefficients of ρ(x)=f(αx+α)/αⁿ satisfy ρ_i=∑_(k=i)^n binom(k,i)f_kα^(k−n) and v_L(ρ_i)=min_(k=i)^n{n v_K(binom(k,i)f_k)+k−n} for1≤i≤n.

title: Coefficient criterion for a Newton polygon with specified markings
description: Let R be a lower convex polygon over the integer interval[a,b], and let T⊆S⊆{a,…,b} include all vertex abscissas in T. A polynomial h with nonzero endpoint coefficients has lower Newton polygon R and, among tested abscissas S, precisely the on-polygon points T iff v(h_i)≥R(i) for all i, equality holds for i∈T, and v(h_i)>R(i) for i∈S∖T, using v(0)=∞.

title: Rellich analytic eigendecomposition for Hermitian matrix families
description: If A(t) is a square complex matrix whose entries are real analytic on an open real interval I and A(t)=A(t)* for every t∈I, then A(t)=U(t)D(t)U(t)* with U(t) unitary and D(t) real diagonal, all entries of U and D real analytic throughout I.

title: Directed partially ordered set
description: A directed set is a nonempty partially ordered set D in which every pair of indices has a common upper bound.

title: Convergence of a net in a metric space
description: A net in a metric space X is a function x:D→X from a directed set. It converges to a∈X if for every ε>0 some d₀∈D satisfies d≥d₀⇒dist(x_d,a)<ε.

title: Minimal unitization of a nonunital C*-algebra
description: For a nonzero nonunital C*-algebra A, its minimal unitization Ã is A⊕ℂ with (a,λ)(b,μ)=(ab+λb+μa,λμ), (a,λ)*=(a*,λ̄), identity(0,1), and norm sup_{b∈A,‖b‖≤1}‖ab+λb‖. For A=0, set Ã=ℂ.

title: C*-algebra structure of the minimal unitization
description: The minimal unitization Ã of a nonunital C*-algebra A is a unital C*-algebra; a↦(a,0) embeds A isometrically as a closed two-sided ideal of codimension one.

title: Positive contractive approximate identity in a C*-algebra
description: A positive contractive approximate identity of a C*-algebra A is a net e_d∈A with e_d≥0,‖e_d‖≤1, and ‖e_da−a‖→0 and ‖ae_d−a‖→0 for every a∈A. No countability or monotonicity is required in this convention.

title: Existence of positive contractive approximate identities
description: Every C*-algebra admits a positive contractive approximate identity.

title: State extension to the minimal C*-unitization
description: Every state ρ on a nonunital C*-algebra A has the unique state extension ρ̃(a+λ1)=ρ(a)+λ to its minimal unitization.

title: Root valuations and Newton polygon slopes
description: For a polynomial over a complete discretely valued field, each finite lower Newton segment of slope −s and horizontal length m corresponds to exactly m nonzero roots of valuation s in an algebraic closure, counted with multiplicity. The power of x dividing the polynomial accounts separately for its zero roots.

title: Uniformizer change of leading ramification residues
description: Let α,α′ be uniformizers of the same totally ramified L/K and let δ be the residue of α′/α. Their ramification polygons and on-polygon coefficient markings agree. For an on-polygon abscissa j with ordinate R_j, the normalized leading residues γ_j=overline(ρ_j α^(−R_j)) satisfy γ′_j=δ^(−R_j)γ_j.

title: Uniformizer invariance of the residual-polynomial orbit
description: The residual-polynomial orbit attached to a totally ramified local extension is independent of its generating uniformizer, including the marked on-polygon coefficient points.

title: Leading residues of ramification coefficients from Eisenstein coefficients
description: For an on-polygon ramification point (j,J), write J=an+b with1≤b≤n. Put F_b=v_K f_b, λ_b=overline(f_bπ^(−F_b)), c=overline(f₀/π), and β(b,j)=overline(binom(b,j)π^(−v_K binom(b,j))). Then F_b=a+1−v_K binom(b,j) and γ_j=β(b,j)λ_b(−c)^(−a−1), with f_n=1.

title: Compatibility of fine ramification residues with Eisenstein coefficients
description: Fix an admissible marked ramification polygon with its exact coefficient-valuation bounds. Prescribed nonzero on-polygon residues γ_j are realizable iff there are residue units c and λ_b, with λ_n=1, satisfying γ_j=β(b,j)λ_b(−c)^(−a−1) at every marked point J=an+b,1≤b≤n. Shared indices b use the same λ_b; horizontal residues must equal overline(binom(n,j)).

title: Coordinate and root-product formulas for Eisenstein distance
description: For monic degree-n Eisenstein f,g over K, d(f,g)=|π|^w with w=min_(0≤i<n)(v_K(g_i−f_i)+i/n). If α=α₁,…,α_n are the roots of f and β is a root of g closest to α, then d(f,g)=∏_(i=1)^n max(|β−α|,|α−α_i|). In particular d is an ultrametric.

title: Krasner truncation discs for Eisenstein extensions
description: For totally ramified degree-n extensions of K with discriminant exponent n+J−1, choose an integer c>1+2J/n. Reducing Eisenstein coefficients modulo𝔭^c preserves the generated field up to K-isomorphism. The generating Eisenstein polynomials partition into closed distance discs of radius|π|^c, one for each admissible coefficient tuple modulo𝔭^c; each disc has constant extension invariants.

title: Krasner count from polynomial discs to embedded fields
description: Let X be a K-isomorphism-stable family of totally ramified degree-n extensions inside a fixed algebraic closure, all with discriminant exponent n+J−1. If c>1+2J/n is an integer and N_X is the number of radius|π|^c discs of their Eisenstein generating polynomials, then |X|=nN_X/((q−1)q^(nc−(n+J−1)−2)), where q is the residue cardinality.

title: Positive-gauge Schatten recovery bound from a robust rank null space property
description: Let A(X)=(tr(A_jX))_j on Hermitian matrices have Frobenius robust rank null space constantsρ,τ of orderr. Suppose W=Σ_jt_jA_j>0 andκ=‖W‖op‖W⁻¹‖op satisfiesκρ<1. For1≤p≤2 andX,Z≥0, ‖Z−X‖p≤2Cκr^(1/p−1)‖X_c‖₁+r^(1/p−1/2)‖A(Z−X)‖₂‖W⁻¹‖op[C‖t‖₂/√r+D‖W‖opτ], whereC=(1+κρ)²/(1−κρ) andD=(3+κρ)/(1−κρ).

title: Robust rank null space bound for Gaussian quadratic measurements
description: For independent standard complex Gaussian vectorsa_j∈ℂⁿ letA(X)=(a_j*Xa_j)_j on Hermitian matrices. There are universalc,C,c₀>0 such that for1≤r≤n,0<ρ<1 andm≥Cρ⁻²nr, with probability at least1−exp(−cm), A has Frobenius robust rank null space constantsρ andτ=c₀/√m of orderr.

title: Conditioning of a complex Gaussian sample covariance matrix
description: For independent standard complex Gaussian vectorsa_j∈ℂⁿ letW=m⁻¹Σ_ja_ja_j*. There are universalc,C>0 such that ifm≥Cn then, with probability at least1−exp(−cm), (1/2)I≤W≤(3/2)I; consequently‖W‖op≤3/2,‖W⁻¹‖op≤2 andκ(W)≤3.

title: Uniform stable positive-semidefinite recovery from Gaussian quadratic measurements
description: For independent standard complex Gaussian vectorsa_j∈ℂⁿ setA(X)=(a_j*Xa_j)_j. There are universalc,C,C₁,C₂>0 such that if1≤r≤n andm≥Cnr, with probability at least1−exp(−cm), simultaneously for allPSD X,Z and1≤p≤2, ‖Z−X‖p≤C₁r^(1/p−1)‖X_c‖₁+C₂r^(1/p−1/2)m⁻¹/²‖A(Z−X)‖₂. In particular every noiselessPSD feasibility set through a rank≤r matrix is a singleton; aPSD least-squares minimizer for noisy data has the same bound with residual at most twice the noise norm.

title: Fundamental inequality of a valued field extension
description: For a finite extension L/K of discretely valued fields with a fixed extending valuation, the ramification index e and residue degree f satisfy ef≤[L:K]. In particular e≤[L:K].

title: Krasner count of totally ramified extensions with fixed discriminant
description: Let J=an+b,0≤b<n, satisfy Ore’s conditions over a p-adic field K of residue cardinality q. Put l(i)=max(2+a−v_K(i),1) for i<b, and max(1+a−v_K(i),1) for i≥b. The number of embedded totally ramified degree-n extensions of discriminant𝔭^(n+J−1) is n q^(n+J−1−∑_(i=1)^(n−1)l(i)) if b=0, and n(q−1)q^(n+J−2−∑_(i=1)^(n−1)l(i)) otherwise.

title: Countable union of countable sets
description: A union of countably many countable sets is countable (using countable choice to choose enumerations when they are not supplied).

title: One-sided free sequence for a finite-valued set mapping
description: If X is uncountable, n≥1 and S maps finite subsets of X to finite subsets of X, there are distinct z₁,…,z_n such that z_j∉S({z_i:i∈I}) whenever I⊂{1,…,n} is nonempty and j<min I or j>max I.

title: Hoffmann–Jørgensen moment control by an increment maximum and quantile
description: For independent increments in a separable invariant-metric semigroup, let U_n and M_n be the partial-product and increment distance maxima. For p>0 and t_p=U_n*(2^(−1−2p)), E U_n^p≤2^(1+2p)(E M_n^p+t_p^p).

title: Stochastic integral increments for a right-regularized làdlàg process
description: LetX be an optional làdlàg real process whose right-limit processX⁺ is a càdlàg semimartingale, andH a predictable process bounded after localization by stopping times. PutJ_t=∫_(0,t]H_s dX⁺_s−H_t(X_(t+)−X_t), using the ordinary càdlàg integral. Define∫_s^tH_u dX_u=J_t−J_s. This fixes increments even whenX has a right jump at0; the normalized primitive isJ_t−J_0.

title: C² Itô formula for a càdlàg semimartingale
description: For a real càdlàg semimartingaleA andf∈C²(ℝ), f(A_t)=f(A_0)+∫_(0,t]f′(A_(s−))dA_s+(1/2)∫_(0,t]f″(A_(s−))d[A]^c_s+Σ_(0<s≤t)[f(A_s)−f(A_(s−))−f′(A_(s−))ΔA_s], where[A]^c is the continuous part of the quadratic variation.

title: C² Itô formula with combined left and right jumps
description: LetX be optional and làdlàg withX⁺ a càdlàg semimartingale andX_(0−)=X_0. Forf∈C²(ℝ) putR_f(a,b)=f(b)−f(a)−f′(a)(b−a). Then f(X_t)=f(X_0)+∫_0^t f′(X_(s−))dX_s+(1/2)∫_0^t f″(X_(s−))d[X⁺]^c_s+Σ_(0≤s<t)R_f(X_(s−),X_(s+))+R_f(X_(t−),X_t), using the right-regularized integral increments.

title: Kunita–Watanabe inequality for càdlàg covariation measures
description: For real càdlàg semimartingalesM,N and predictableH,K on[0,T], ∫₀ᵀ|H_sK_s| |d[M,N]|_s≤(∫₀ᵀH_s²d[M]_s)^(1/2)(∫₀ᵀK_s²d[N]_s)^(1/2) almost surely, whenever the two right-hand integrals are finite; |d[M,N]| is the total variation of the signed covariation measure.

title: Positivity and polarization of càdlàg quadratic variation
description: For real càdlàg semimartingalesX,Y, the quadratic variations[X] and[Y] are locally finite increasing processes. Covariation is symmetric and bilinear, and[aX+bY]=a²[X]+2ab[X,Y]+b²[Y] for reala,b; in particular every such quadratic combination is increasing.

title: Discrete topological space
description: A topological space is discrete if every subset is open.

title: Totally disconnected topological space
description: A topological space is totally disconnected if every nonempty connected subset has exactly one point.

title: Profinite group
description: A profinite group is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group. Finite groups have their discrete topology in this convention.

title: Discrete module for a topological group
description: A discrete module for a topological group G is an abelian G-module M with the discrete topology and continuous action G×M→M. Equivalently each element of M has an open stabilizer in G.

title: Cochain complex of modules
description: A cochain complex over a commutative ring R is a family of R-modules Cⁿ indexed by integers with R-linear maps dⁿ:Cⁿ→C^(n+1) satisfying d^(n+1)dⁿ=0. Its nth cohomology is Hⁿ(C)=ker dⁿ/im d^(n−1).

title: Map of cochain complexes
description: A cochain map f:C→D is a degree-preserving family of module homomorphisms fⁿ:Cⁿ→Dⁿ satisfying d_Dⁿfⁿ=f^(n+1)d_Cⁿ in every degree. It induces maps on cohomology by mapping a cocycle to its image.

title: Long exact cohomology sequence of complexes
description: A degreewise short exact sequence0→A→B→C→0 of cochain maps induces natural connecting homomorphisms δ:Hⁿ(C)→H^(n+1)(A) and an exact sequence⋯→Hⁿ(A)→Hⁿ(B)→Hⁿ(C)→H^(n+1)(A)→⋯.

title: Finite image of a continuous map from compact to discrete
description: Every continuous map from a compact space to a discrete space has finite image.

title: Compactness of a finite product
description: A finite Cartesian product of compact topological spaces is compact in the product topology.

title: Quotient conjugation action on first group cohomology
description: For N normal in G and a G-module M, g acts on a cocycle z:N→M by(g·z)(n)=g·z(g⁻¹ng). This induces an action of G/N on H¹(N,M), because inner N-actions induce the identity on cohomology. For profinite groups and discrete modules use continuous cocycles.

title: Convex power jump-remainder lower bound
description: For1<p<2 and reala,b withR=max(|a|,|b|)>0, |b|ᵖ−|a|ᵖ−p|a|^(p−1)sgn(a)(b−a)≥[p(p−1)/2](b−a)²R^(p−2), withsgn(0)=0. WhenR=0 bothsides are defined as0.

title: Eigenvalue density of an isotropic Hermitian Gaussian matrix
description: If a Hermitian n×n matrix has density proportional toexp(−a trH²),a>0, forLebesgue measure on its independent realcoordinates, its unordered real eigenvalues have jointdensity proportional toexp(−aΣ_jx_j²)∏_(i<j)(x_i−x_j)².
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Hankel moment determinant and orthogonal-polynomial product
description: Letw be a possibly complex integrable weight onℝ with finite absolute moments throughdegree2n−2 and nonzero leadingprincipal Hankel determinants. Ifp_j(x)=κ_jx^j+⋯ satisfy∫p_jp_kw=δ_jk for0≤j,k<n, then det(∫x^(j+k)w(x)dx)_(j,k=0)^(n−1)=(1/n!)∫_(ℝⁿ)∏_(i<j)(x_i−x_j)²∏_iw(x_i)dx_i=∏_(j=0)^(n−1)κ_j⁻².
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Three-term recurrence for normalized orthogonal polynomials
description: For a normalized polynomial sequence∫p_jp_kw=δ_jk with nonzero leadingcoefficientsκ_j and all needed Hankel determinants nonzero, multiplication byx has the recurrence xp_j=b_jp_(j+1)+a_jp_j+b_(j−1)p_(j−1), whereb_j=κ_j/κ_(j+1) andp_(−1)=0. The pairing is bilinear and may use a complexweight.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Christoffel–Darboux identity for an orthonormal polynomial kernel
description: For bilinearly normalized orthogonal polynomials p_j with leadingcoefficientsκ_j≠0, Σ_(j=0)^(n−1)p_j(x)p_j(y)=(κ_(n−1)/κ_n)[p_n(x)p_(n−1)(y)−p_(n−1)(x)p_n(y)]/(x−y); atx=y use the derivative limit.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Normalized matrix Riemann–Hilbert problem on an oriented contour
description: Given an oriented contourΣ and invertible jump matrixJ on it, a normalized matrixRiemann–Hilbert problem seeksY holomorphic offΣ with boundaryvaluesY_+=Y_-J, prescribed growth at any distinguished endpoints or singularities, and prescribed normalization at infinity. The plus side is theleftside of the orientedcontour.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Orthogonal-polynomial Cauchy-transform matrix
description: For orthonormal polynomials p_n,p_(n−1) of a real-line weightw, withleadingcoefficientsκ_n,κ_(n−1)≠0, formY(z) with firstcolumn(κ_n⁻¹p_n(z),−2πiκ_(n−1)p_(n−1)(z))ᵀ and secondcolumn given by the corresponding entries∫_(ℝ)(firstcolumn)(x)w(x)/(2πi(x−z))dx. Away from singularities it has the uppertriangular jump[[1,w],[0,1]] and degree-n normalization at infinity.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: L² Cauchy boundary operators on smooth intersecting contours
description: For an oriented contour made from finitely many smooth compact arcs and straight rays, with finitely many transverse intersections and nonzero meeting angles, C f(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_Σ f(s)/(s−z)ds has bounded nontangential boundaryoperatorsC_± onL²(Σ), satisfyingC_+f−C_-f=f almosteverywhere.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Neumann-series inversion for a bounded operator
description: IfA is a bounded linear operator on a Banach space with‖A‖<1, thenI−A is invertible and(I−A)⁻¹=Σ_(k=0)^∞A^k in operator norm, with‖(I−A)⁻¹‖≤(1−‖A‖)⁻¹.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Liouville theorem for bounded entire functions
description: Every bounded holomorphic function onℂ isconstant; consequently an entirematrix-valued function tending toI at infinity is identicallyI, entry byentry.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Modified Bessel functions I and K
description: On the principal slit plane, I_ν(z)=Σ_(k≥0)(z/2)^(ν+2k)/(k!Γ(k+ν+1)); fornonintegerν putK_ν(z)=π[I_(−ν)(z)−I_ν(z)]/[2sin(πν)], with the removable integer-order values obtained by continuation. Their continuations and derivatives give the normalized fundamental solutions ofz²y″+zy′−(z²+ν²)y=0.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Sectorial large-argument asymptotics of modified Bessel functions
description: Forν in compact sets and fixedδ>0, I_ν(z)=e^z(2πz)^(−1/2)[1−(4ν²−1)/(8z)+O(z⁻²)] uniformly for|argz|≤π/2−δ, andK_ν(z)=(π/(2z))^(1/2)e^(−z)[1+(4ν²−1)/(8z)+O(z⁻²)] uniformly for|argz|≤3π/2−δ on the continued logarithm branch. Higher inverse-power expansions hold on closed subsectors.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Airy Ai function and sectorial asymptotics
description: The entire Airy function Ai(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_Γexp(t³/3−zt)dt, whereΓ goes from∞e^(−iπ/3) to∞e^(iπ/3), satisfiesAi″=zAi andAi(z)+ωAi(ωz)+ω²Ai(ω²z)=0,ω=e^(2πi/3). Uniformly for|argz|≤π−δ, Ai(z)=e^(−2z^(3/2)/3)z^(−1/4)(2√π)⁻¹[1−5z^(−3/2)/48+O(z⁻³)] andAi′(z)=−e^(−2z^(3/2)/3)z^(1/4)(2√π)⁻¹[1+7z^(−3/2)/48+O(z⁻³)], using principalpowers.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Barnes integral identity for the logarithm of gamma
description: ForRez>−1 and holomorphic logarithms normalized bylogΓ(1)=logG(1)=0, ∫₀ᶻlogΓ(1+x)dx=(z/2)log(2π)−z(z+1)/2+zlogΓ(1+z)−logG(1+z), whereG is the canonical BarnesG-function and the integral stays inRe x>−1.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Dixon–Anderson interlacing integral
description: Let a₁>⋯>a_(n+1) be real and s₁,…,s_(n+1)>0 be real. On a₁>t₁>a₂>⋯>t_n>a_(n+1), ∫∏_(i<j)(t_i−t_j)∏_(i=1)^n∏_(j=1)^(n+1)|t_i−a_j|^(s_j−1)dt=[∏_jΓ(s_j)/Γ(Σ_js_j)]∏_(i<j)(a_i−a_j)^(s_i+s_j−1).

title: Convergence and holomorphy of the Selberg integral
description: Forn≥2 the Selberg integrand∏_it_i^(a−1)(1−t_i)^(b−1)∏_(i<j)|t_i−t_j|^(2γ) is absolutelyintegrable on[0,1]^n whenRea,Reb>0 andReγ>−min(1/n,Rea/(n−1),Reb/(n−1)). Its integral is holomorphic in(a,b,γ) on thisdomain, with positive-real bases used off the measurezero collision/endpoints.

title: Detailed balance for a Markov kernel
description: A Markov kernel P on a measurable space satisfies detailed balance with a probability π if the measure π(dx)P(x,dy) on the product space is invariant under(x,y)↦(y,x). Such a kernel is reversible with respect toπ.

title: Detailed balance implies invariance
description: If a Markov kernel P satisfies detailed balance with π, thenπP=π.

title: Detailed balance of the general Metropolis–Hastings kernel
description: For a target probabilityπ and proposal kernelQ, the general Metropolis–Hastings kernel with acceptance min(1,r), where r is the reversed/forward joint-proposal Radon–Nikodym ratio on their common part and zero on the forward-only part, satisfies detailed balance withπ and hence leavesπ invariant.

title: Irreducibility with respect to a measure
description: A Markov kernelP on(E,𝔈) is ψ-irreducible ifψ is a nonzeroσ-finite measure and every A∈𝔈 withψ(A)>0 satisfies∑_{n≥1}Pⁿ(x,A)>0 for everyx∈E.

title: Aperiodicity of a general-state irreducible Markov chain
description: A ψ-irreducible Markov chain is aperiodic if it admits no measurable cyclic decomposition of lengthd≥2: disjoint ψ-positive setsD₀,…,D_{d−1} withψ-null complement andP(x,D_{i+1 mod d})=1 for everyx∈D_i.

title: Small set for a Markov kernel
description: A measurable setC is small forP if some integerm≥1,ε>0 and probabilityν satisfyP^m(x,A)≥εν(A) for everyx∈C and measurableA.

title: Petite set for a Markov kernel
description: A measurable setC is petite forP if some probability(a_n) on the nonnegative integers,ε>0 and probabilityν satisfy∑_{n≥0}a_nP^n(x,A)≥εν(A) for allx∈C and measurableA.

title: Weak Feller Markov kernel
description: A Markov kernelP on a topological space is weak Feller ifPf is bounded continuous wheneverf is bounded continuous.

title: Positive Harris recurrence
description: A ψ-irreducible Markov chain is Harris recurrent if every ψ-positive measurable set is visited infinitely often almost surely from every initial state; it is positive Harris recurrent if it also admits an invariant probability.

title: Invariant moment bound from geometric drift
description: IfP is a Markov kernel,πP=π and a finite measurableV≥0 satisfiesPV≤aV+b with0≤a<1,0≤b<∞, thenπ(V)≤b/(1−a); no prior integrability assumption onV is required.

title: Compact small sets for a positive continuous transition density
description: LetP(x,dy)=p(x,y)dy onℝᵈ, wherep is jointly continuous and strictly positive. Every compactC⊂ℝᵈ is a one-step small set; the chain is Lebesgue-irreducible and aperiodic.

title: Harris geometric ergodicity from petite-set drift
description: LetP be ψ-irreducible and aperiodic. If a finite measurableV≥1, a petite setC withsup_CV<∞,0≤a<1 andb<∞ satisfyPV≤aV+b1_C, thenP is positive Harris recurrent andV-uniformly ergodic.

title: Kantorovich duality for a nonnegative lower semicontinuous cost
description: For Borel probabilities μ,ν on Polish spaces X,Y and nonnegative lower semicontinuous c:X×Y→[0,∞], inf_{γ∈Π(μ,ν)}∫c dγ equals sup{∫φ dμ+∫ψ dν: φ,ψ bounded continuous and φ(x)+ψ(y)≤c(x,y)}; both sides may be infinite.

title: Cost transform in optimal transport
description: For a cost c:X×Y→(−∞,∞] and a function φ on X, its c-transform is φ^c(y)=inf_{x∈X}(c(x,y)−φ(x)); the analogous transform from Y back to X is defined by the same cost. Extended values are allowed where the infimum is not finite.

title: Geometric drift bounds stopped weighted occupation
description: If a Markov chain has finite V≥1 and PV≤aV+b1_C with 0≤a<1, then for each 1<r<1/a there is K<∞ such that E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_C−1}r^k V(X_k)]≤K(V(x)+b1_C(x)), where τ_C=inf{k≥1:X_k∈C}. For a=0 any finite r>1 is allowed.

title: Geometric ergodic bound from a weighted Kendall petite set
description: Let a ψ-irreducible aperiodic chain have f≥1 and a petite set C such that for some κ>1 the stopped potential G(x)=E_x∑_{k=0}^{τ_C−1}κ^k f(X_k) is finite everywhere and bounded on C. Then the chain is positive Harris recurrent with invariant π, π(f)<∞, and there are r>1,R<∞ with ∑_{n≥0}r^n||P^n(x,·)−π||_f≤R G(x) for every x.

title: Induced module for a finite group
description: For H≤G finite and an H-module M, the induced module can be realized as functions f:G→M satisfying f(hg)=h·f(g), with pointwise addition and G-action(g₀·f)(g)=f(gg₀). This is the coinduced function model, canonically isomorphic to induction for finite groups.

title: Corestriction in finite-group cohomology
description: For H≤G finite and a G-module M, corestriction Cor:Hⁿ(H,M)→Hⁿ(G,M) is the inverse of Shapiro’s isomorphism followed by the map induced by Tr:Ind_H^G(M|H)→M. In the function model, Tr(f)=∑_s s⁻¹f(s), over representatives s of the right H-cosets, independent of the right-coset representatives.

title: Restriction–corestriction multiplication by index
description: For a subgroup H of a finite group G and a G-module M, Cor∘Res on Hⁿ(G,M) is multiplication by[G:H], for every n≥0.

title: Injective restriction to a subgroup of index prime to the coefficient characteristic
description: Let p be prime, G finite and M a G-module killed by p. If H≤G has index coprime to p, then Res:Hⁿ(G,M)→Hⁿ(H,M) is injective for all n>0. In particular this applies to a p-Sylow subgroup.

title: Sylow p-subgroup of a finite group
description: If p^a is the largest power of a prime p dividing the order of a finite group G, a Sylow p-subgroup is a subgroup of order p^a. Its index is prime to p.

title: Cauchy’s theorem on an element of prime order
description: If a prime p divides the order of a finite group G, then G contains an element of order p.

title: Degree-zero Tate cohomology of a finite group
description: For a finite group G acting on an abelian group M, Ĥ⁰(G,M)=M^G/N_GM, where N_G(m)=∑_(g∈G)g·m is the norm map. Its image lies in M^G.

title: Cup product in group cohomology
description: For G-modules M,N, cup product sends Hʳ(G,M)×Hˢ(G,N) to H^(r+s)(G,M⊗ℤN), with diagonal G-action on the tensor product. On inhomogeneous cocycles it is(a∪b)(g₁,…,g_(r+s))=a(g₁,…,g_r)⊗(g₁⋯g_r)·b(g_(r+1),…,g_(r+s)). Equivariant pairings M⊗N→P give the corresponding products into H^(r+s)(G,P).

title: Additive group of rational numbers modulo integers
description: The group ℚ/ℤ is the quotient of the additive rational group by its integer subgroup; each element is a rational residue class and has finite order. In group cohomology it is given the stated group action, often trivial.

title: Cup-product period generator for cyclic group cohomology
description: For a finite cyclic group C of order n, choose an injective character χ:C→ℚ/ℤ and let δχ∈H²(C,ℤ) be its connecting class for0→ℤ→ℚ→ℚ/ℤ→0. Cup product with δχ induces an isomorphism Ĥ⁰(C,M)→H²(C,M) for every C-module M, natural in coefficient and group automorphisms together with the chosen character.

title: Descending filtered module
description: A descending filtration on a module M is a family of submodules F^iM indexed by integers with F^(i+1)M⊆F^iM. Its ith associated graded module is F^iM/F^(i+1)M.

title: First-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence
description: A first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category consists of objects E_r^(a,b) for r≥r₀ and integers a,b, zero unless a,b≥0, with differentials d_r:E_r^(a,b)→E_r^(a+r,b−r+1), d_r∘d_r=0, and isomorphisms E_(r+1)≅ker d_r/im d_r. For fixed (a,b) the terms stabilize to E_∞^(a,b). Convergence to objects H^n means each H^n has a finite descending filtration by subobjects whose graded pieces are E_∞^(a,n−a). Modules over a ring are the basic example.

title: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence in group cohomology
description: For a normal subgroup N of G and a G-module M, there is a first-quadrant spectral sequence E₂^(a,b)=Hᵃ(G/N,Hᵇ(N,M)) converging to H^(a+b)(G,M). The quotient action is induced on cochains by(g·c)(n₁,…,n_b)=g·c(g⁻¹n₁g,…,g⁻¹n_bg).

title: Recurrence transfer from uniform future hitting probabilities
description: For a time-homogeneous Markov chainX and measurable setsB,C, suppose someβ>0 satisfiesP_x(X_s∈C for somes≥1)≥β for everyx∈B. Then almost surely, ifX visitsB infinitelyoften, it also visitsC infinitelyoften.

title: Finite substochastic matrix
description: A finite square real matrixQ is substochastic ifQ_ij≥0 andΣ_jQ_ij≤1 for everyrowi. Adding one absorbingcemetery state with transitionprobability1−Σ_jQ_ij fromrowi makesQ the transientpart of a stochasticmatrix.

title: Quasi-stationary law of an irreducible finite killed chain
description: LetQ be an irreducible finite substochastic matrix with0<ρ(Q)<1. Its cemetery-augmentedchain is absorbed almostsurely, and its unique quasi-stationary distribution is the positive left Perroneigenvector normalized tosum1; its one-stepsurvivalprobability isρ(Q), and its meansurvivaltime is1/(1−ρ(Q)).

title: Absorption or divergence for Poisson population updates
description: For a PoissonLotka–Volterra densityprocessX_t with scaleε>0, almostsurely eitherX_t=0 forsomefinite t orΣ_iX_(i,t)→∞. If its deterministicmeanmap satisfiesF(ℝ_+^k)⊆[0,M]^k, absorptionat0 isalmostsure; morepreciselyP_x(τ_0>n)≤(1−e^(−kM/ε))^n fornonzero x.

title: Weighted supremum space of measurable functions
description: For a finite measurable weight V≥1 on a measurable space E, B_V consists of real or complex measurable f with ||f||_V=sup_x|f(x)|/V(x)<∞; with pointwise operations this is a Banach space.

title: Weighted operator norm of a kernel difference
description: For Markov kernels P,Q and finite weights V,W≥1, the norm of P−Q:B_V→B_W is sup_x ||P(x,·)−Q(x,·)||_V/W(x), whenever the rows have finite V moments; the equality follows by taking the two suprema over x and |f|≤V in either order.

title: Power interpolation of weighted uniform ergodicity
description: If ||P^n(x,·)−π||_V≤Cρ^nV(x), π(V)<∞ and V≥1, then for every 0<r<1 the chain is V^r-uniformly ergodic, with bound 2^(1−r)C^rρ^(nr)V(x)^r.

title: Stationary law of a contractive first-order autoregression
description: For X_n=αX_(n−1)+Z_n on ℝ with |α|<1 and iid innovations satisfying E|Z_1|<∞, the law of ∑_{j≥0}α^j Z_(j+1) is the unique invariant probability. The series converges almost surely and in L¹; the invariant first moment is at most E|Z_1|/(1−|α|), and its mean is EZ_1/(1−α).

title: Continuity of translations in L¹
description: For f∈L¹(ℝᵈ), ||f(·−h)−f||_1→0 as h→0.

title: Weighted spectral gap for a compactly regularized contractive random iteration
description: Let iid random Lipschitz maps F on a complete separable metric space have E Lip(F)^a<1 and E d(F(x₀),x₀)^a<∞ for a≥1. Put V(x)=(1+d(x,x₀))^a. If some power P^ℓ is compact from bounded measurable functions to B_V, then P is V-uniformly ergodic and the infimum geometric rate is at most (E Lip(F)^a)^(1/a).

title: Compactness of a squared strong Feller kernel in a weighted space
description: Let (X,d) be a separable metric space with compact closed balls, V≥1 measurable with V(x)→∞ as d(x,x₀)→∞, and P a strong Feller Markov kernel with P(x,dy)=K(x,y)η(dy) for a σ-finite measure η and jointly measurable K≥0. Then P² maps bounded measurable functions compactly into B_V. Here strong Feller means bounded measurable functions become continuous.

title: Weighted geometric ergodicity of an autoregression with a density
description: For a real AR(1) kernel with |α|<1 and iid innovations having a Lebesgue density and finite first absolute moment, V(x)=1+|x| gives V-uniform ergodicity. For every ρ with |α|<ρ<1 there is C_ρ<∞ such that ||P^n(x,·)−π||_V≤C_ρρ^nV(x). This statement does not assert that the endpoint rate |α| is attained.

title: Weakly unimodal density on the real line
description: A real probability density h is weakly unimodal if some m∈ℝ makes h nondecreasing on (−∞,m) and nonincreasing on (m,∞); jumps and flat portions are allowed.

title: Translation bound for a bounded unimodal density
description: If a real probability density h is weakly unimodal and h≤H, then ∫|h(z)−h(z−a)|dz≤2H|a| for every a∈ℝ.

title: Weak and strong weighted kernel perturbations for autoregressions
description: For AR(1) kernels P_α with any innovation density of finite first moment and V=1+|x|, ||P_β−P_α||_(B_1→B_V)→0 as β→α. For fixed 0<α<1, the stronger norm ||P_β−P_α||_(B_V→B_V) need not tend to0 as β↓α; in fact its liminf is positive for every such density.

title: QSD survival and boundary mass from a trapping set
description: Letμ be aQSD with survivalλ for a kernelP absorbed inS₀. IfU⊆S₀ᶜ hasμ(U)>0 andP(x,U)≥1−β forx∈U, thenλ≥1−β. IfalsoP(x,S₀)≥a>0 forx∈V⊆S₀ᶜ, thenμ(V)≤(1−λ)/a≤β/a.

title: Invariance of a small-noise QSD limit with survival tending to one
description: LetS⊂ℝᵈ be closed,F:S→S continuous withboundedimage,andP_ε a smallrandomperturbation ofF withcommonabsorbingS₀ andQSDsμ_ε,survivalsλ_ε. Ifε_n↓0,μ_(ε_n) convergesweaklytoμ andλ_(ε_n)→1, thenμ isF-invariant.

title: Strict trapping neighborhoods of a compact attractor
description: Let F be a continuous map of a closed set S⊆ℝᵈ into itself with bounded image F(S), and let A be a compact attractor of F. Then there are a bounded open neighborhood U of A and δ>0 such that F(cl U) is compact, F(cl U)⊆U and N_δ(F(U))⊆U.

title: Positive-attractor QSD survival and boundary concentration estimate
description: LetF:S→S becontinuous withboundedimage onclosedS⊂ℝᵈ, andP_ε smallrandomperturbations withabsorbingS₀ andQSDsμ_ε. SupposeA⊂S₀ᶜ isacompactattractor andμ_ε(U)>0 foreveryneighborhoodU ofA. Then someδ>0 givesλ_ε≥1−β_δ(ε), whereβ_δ(ε)=sup_xP_ε(x,S∖N_δ(Fx)). IfV₀ isanopenneighborhoodofS₀ andβ_δ(ε)/inf_(x∈V₀∖S₀)P_ε(x,S₀)→0, everyweakQSDlimitμ satisfiesμ(V₀)=0 andisF-invariant.

title: Open-set inequality under weak convergence
description: Ifprobabilitymeasuresμ_n convergeweaklytoμ onametricspace, thenμ(U)≤liminf_nμ_n(U) foreveryopensetU.

title: Petite covering theorem for an irreducible Markov kernel
description: Every ψ-irreducible Markov kernel on a countably generated measurable state space admits an increasing sequence of petite sets whose union is the whole state space.

title: Transfer of petiteness by uniform randomized-time access
description: If C is petite for P and a set A has K_b(x,C)≥δ>0 for every x∈A, where K_b=∑_{n≥0}b_nP^n for a probability(b_n), then A is petite.

title: Closure of a petite set for an irreducible weak Feller kernel
description: For a ψ-irreducible weak Feller Markov kernel on a locally compact Polish space, the closure of every petite set is petite.

title: Compact petite sets for a Lebesgue-irreducible weak Feller kernel
description: Every compact subset of ℝᵈ is petite for a weak Feller Markov kernel that is irreducible with respect to Lebesgue measure. The full support of Lebesgue measure is essential to this version; irreducibility and weak Feller alone do not imply it for arbitrary irreducibility measures.

title: Equivalent petite-set drift from weighted uniform ergodicity
description: If a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel is V-uniformly ergodic for finite V≥1, then there are a finite V₀ with c⁻¹V≤V₀≤cV, a petite set C on which V₀ is bounded, λ<1 and b<∞ such that PV₀≤λV₀+b1_C.

title: Sharp linear Wasserstein perturbation for an autoregressive coefficient
description: For real AR(1) kernels with common iid innovation Z of finite first moment and coefficients |α|,|β|<1, W₁(π_α,π_β)≤|α−β|[1−|β|+E|Z|]/[(1−|α|)(1−|β|)]. If EZ≠0, W₁(π_α,π_β)≥|α−β||EZ|/[|1−α||1−β|], so the linear dependence on the coefficient error cannot be improved in general.

title: Lyapunov-weighted Wasserstein bound for acceptance errors
description: Let P_α,P_β share proposal Q and have acceptance errors E(x,y)=|α(x,y)−β(x,y)|. If τ_d(P_α^n)≤Cρ^n, P_βV≤δV+L and γ=sup_x V(x)⁻¹∫d(x,y)E(x,y)Q(x,dy)<∞, then for p(V)<∞, W_d(pP_α^n,pP_β^n)≤γC max{p(V),L/(1−δ)}(1−ρ^n)/(1−ρ), using the n=0 convention C≥1.

title: Weighted variation stability under bounded acceptance error
description: Suppose V≥1 is lower semicontinuous and P_α is V-uniformly ergodic with constants C,ρ, P_αV≤δV+L, and another acceptance kernel P_β shares proposal Q. If |α−β|≤s and λ=1+sup_x QV(x)/V(x)<∞ satisfy δ+λs<1, then ||pP_α^n−pP_β^n||_V≤λs C max{p(V),L/(1−δ−λs)}(1−ρ^n)/(1−ρ), for finite p(V), C≥1 and n≥0.

title: Uniform perturbation rate for bounded-statistic noisy Langevin chains
description: For a finite exponential-family likelihood ℓ_θ(y)∝exp(θs(y)) with |s|≤S, Gaussian prior variance σ_p² and 0<σ²<4σ_p², compare the exact Gaussian Euler Langevin kernel with the kernel using an iid N-sample estimate of E_θs. For every initial law of finite first moment, both invariant laws exist and the full-TV errors between invariant laws and between nth-step laws, uniformly in n, are O(logN/N). The implied constant may depend on the fixed model, step and initial moment.

title: Upper triangular subgroup of GL₂ over a field
description: For a field k, the upper triangular subgroup of GL₂(k) consists of matrices [[a,b],[0,d]] with a,d∈k× and b∈k. Its conjugates are exactly the stabilizers of one-dimensional subspaces of k².

title: Elementary generation of SL₂ over a field
description: For any field k, SL₂(k) is generated by the elementary matrices U(t)=[[1,t],[0,1]] and L(t)=[[1,0],[t,1]], t∈k.

title: Prime-field GL₂ subgroup dichotomy at the coefficient prime
description: If G≤GL₂(𝔽_p), p prime, and p divides|G|, then either G contains SL₂(𝔽_p), or G stabilizes a line and is conjugate into the upper triangular subgroup. The field is specifically the prime field.

title: Maschke splitting in characteristic prime to the group order
description: If a finite group G acts linearly on a finite-dimensional vector space V over k and|G|is nonzero in k, then every G-invariant subspace W has a G-invariant direct complement.

title: Mod-p cyclotomic character
description: For p prime and a characteristic-zero field F, the mod-p cyclotomic character ω_p:Gal(Fsep/F)→𝔽_p× is characterized by σ(ζ)=ζ^(ω_p(σ)) for every pth root of unity ζ.

title: Galois group of a prime cyclotomic field
description: For a prime p and primitive pth root ζ_p, Gal(ℚ(ζ_p)/ℚ) is isomorphic to𝔽_p× by σ↦a when σ(ζ_p)=ζ_p^a.

title: Surjectivity of the cyclotomic character under disjointness
description: For a number field F with F∩ℚ(ζ_p)=ℚ, the mod-p cyclotomic character ω_p of F is surjective onto𝔽_p×.

title: Cyclotomic determinant of an elliptic torsion representation
description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field F and a prime p, detρ_(E,p)=ω_p as characters ofGal(Fsep/F) into𝔽_p×.

title: Order of a general linear group over a finite field
description: For a finite field𝔽_q, |GL_n(𝔽_q)|=∏_(j=0)^(n−1)(qⁿ−qʲ). In particular the order of GL₂(𝔽_p) is p(p−1)²(p+1), whose p-part is p.

title: Lagrange’s theorem for a finite group
description: For a subgroup H of a finite group G, |G|=[G:H]|H|. In particular |H| divides |G|.

title: Lawson–Wuthrich second torsion cohomology classification over number fields
description: Let E/F be elliptic, p prime, F a number field withF∩ℚ(ζ_p)=ℚ, andG=Gal(F(E[p])/F). ThenH²(G,E[p])is nonzero exactly whenp>2, E has exactly one F-rational cyclic subgroup of orderp, and for its isogenyϕ:E→E′ the dual kernelE′[ϕ̂] has an F-rational point of orderp. In that caseH² has p elements.

title: Gordon lower bound for the expected least Gaussian singular value
description: For anm×n matrixG withindependentrealN(0,1) entries and1≤n≤m, Eσ_min(G)≥√m−√n.

title: Lieb concavity of the trace exponential with a logarithm
description: For a fixed Hermitian matrixH, the functionA↦tr exp(H+logA) isconcave onthepositive-definite Hermitian cone, wherelogA isdefined by spectralcalculus.

title: Operator monotonicity of the positive matrix logarithm
description: Forpositive-definite Hermitian matricesA≼B, logA≼logB, wherelogA=U diag(logλ_j)U* in a unitary eigendecompositionA=U diag(λ_j)U*.

title: Monotonicity of the trace of a matrix exponential
description: For Hermitian matricesA≼B, tr exp(A)≤tr exp(B).

title: Jensen inequality for a finite-dimensional random vector
description: LetD⊆ℝᵈ beconvex, X anintegrableD-valuedrandomvector withEX∈D, andφ:D→ℝ continuousandconvex withE|φ(X)|<∞. Thenφ(EX)≤Eφ(X); the inequalityreversesforconcaveφ.

title: Fundamental domain of a discrete group action
description: For a discrete group acting on a topological space, a fundamental domain is a region whose translates cover the space and whose interior contains at most one point of each orbit. Boundary representatives may repeat; for integration one chooses a measurable domain meeting almost every orbit once.

title: Petersson inner product of cusp forms
description: For weight-k cusp forms f,g on Γ=Γ₀(N) or Γ₁(N), the Petersson pairing is ⟨f,g⟩=∫_D f(z)overline(g(z))y^(k−2)dxdy, z=x+iy, over a fundamental domain D for Γ on the upper half-plane. It converges, is independent of D and is a positive definite Hermitian form; a common unitary character is allowed.

title: Degeneracy map between cusp-form levels
description: For M|N and d|N/M, the degeneracy map α_d:S_k(Γ₁(M))→S_k(Γ₁(N)) sends f(z) to f(dz), equivalently ∑a_nq^n to ∑a_nq^(dn). On a fixed character subspace it is used only when the character at level N is induced from level M.

title: Old and new cuspidal subspaces
description: The old subspace S_k(Γ₁(N))^old is the span of all α_d(S_k(Γ₁(M))) with proper divisors M|N and d|N/M. The new subspace is its orthogonal complement for the Petersson inner product. Character-χ old/new subspaces are the intersections with S_k(Γ₀(N),χ).

title: Uniform probability law on the complex unit sphere
description: For n≥1, the uniform probability on {z∈ℂⁿ:‖z‖₂=1} is the pushforward of a standard complex Gaussian vector g under g↦g/‖g‖₂. Define this map arbitrarily at g=0, an event of probability zero. This is the law called a Haar-random unit vector; it is invariant under unitary coordinate changes.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Sample covariance conditioning for a trace-accurate four-design
description: Let n≥2 and let w be drawn from a weighted projective 4-design of trace-norm accuracy θ₁≤1/4. Put a=[n(n+1)]^(1/4)w. Its population covariance satisfies (3/4)I≼Eaa*≼(3/2)I. For independent copies a_j and W=m⁻¹Σ_ja_ja_j*, there is a universal C such that u≥1 and m≥Cun log(2n) imply P((1/2)I≼W≼2I)≥1−e^(−u); hence ‖W‖op≤2, ‖W⁻¹‖op≤2 and κ(W)≤4 on this event.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Robust rank null space bound for trace-accurate four-design measurements
description: Let n≥2, 1≤r≤n and let w_j be independent draws from a weighted projective 4-design of trace-norm accuracy θ₁≤1/4. Set A(X)=(√(n(n+1))w_j*Xw_j)_j. Universal constants c,C,C₀>0 satisfy: if 0<ρ<1 and m≥Cρ⁻²nr log(2n), then with probability at least 1−e^(−cm), A has the Frobenius robust rank null space property of order r with constants ρ and τ=C₀/√m.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Uniform stable PSD recovery from trace-accurate four-design measurements
description: Let n≥2, 1≤r≤n and A(X)=(√(n(n+1))w_j*Xw_j)_j, where w_j are independent draws from a weighted projective 4-design of trace-norm accuracy θ₁≤1/4. There are universal C,C₁,C₂>0 such that s≥1 and m≥Csnr log(2n) give, with probability at least 1−e^(−sr), simultaneously for all positive semidefinite X,Z and 1≤p≤2, ‖Z−X‖p≤C₁r^(1/p−1)‖X_c‖₁+C₂r^(1/p−1/2)m⁻¹/²‖A(Z−X)‖₂.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Trace-norm density-matrix least squares with trace-accurate designs
description: Let n≥2, 1≤r≤n and L(X)=(√(n(n+1)/m)w_j*Xw_j)_j, with independent unit vectors drawn from a weighted projective 4-design of trace-norm accuracy θ₁≤1/4. If m≥Cnr log(2n), then with probability at least 1−e^(−cm), for every density matrix X and noise vector w, any minimizer Z of ‖L(Z)−(L(X)+w)‖₂ over density matrices satisfies ‖Z−X‖₁≤C₁‖X_c‖₁+C₂√r‖w‖₂, with universal constants.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Low-rank density identification by completed random rank-one measurements
description: For n≥2 and 1≤r≤n, draw independent uniform complex unit vectors w_j with m≥Cnr, or independent unit vectors from a weighted 4-design of trace-norm accuracy θ₁≤1/4 with m≥Cnr log(2n). Choose δ>0 with δΣ_jw_jw_j*≼I. The operators E_j=δw_jw_j* and E₀=I−Σ_jE_j form a POVM. With probability at least 1−e^(−cm), every density matrix of rank at most r is uniquely determined among all density matrices by these outcome probabilities, with suitable universal constants.
field: Random matrix recovery and quantum information

title: Maximal ideal
description: A maximal ideal of a commutative ring R is a proper ideal contained in no larger proper ideal.

title: Local commutative ring
description: A local ring is a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal. A homomorphism of local rings is local if it sends the maximal ideal of its source into the maximal ideal of its target.

title: Sheaf on a topological space
description: A sheaf of sets on X assigns a set F(U) to each open U and restriction maps compatible with identities and composition, such that sections agreeing on every overlap of any open cover glue to one unique section. Sheaves of groups, rings or modules carry the respective operations compatibly with restriction.

title: Stalk of a sheaf
description: The stalk F_x is the set of germs of sections near x: pairs(U,s) with x∈U and s∈F(U), identified when their restrictions agree on some smaller neighborhood of x. Algebraic operations on a sheaf induce the same operations on its stalks.

title: Locally ringed space
description: A locally ringed space is a topological space X with a sheaf of commutative rings O_X whose stalk at each point is a local ring. A morphism consists of a continuous map f:X→Y and compatible ring maps O_Y(U)→O_X(f⁻¹U) whose induced maps on stalks are local.

title: Prime spectrum and Zariski topology
description: Spec R is the set of prime ideals of a commutative ring R with closed sets V(I)={𝔭:I⊆𝔭}. Its standard open subsets are D(f)={𝔭:f∉𝔭}; these form a topology basis.

title: Affine scheme
description: The affine scheme Spec R is the prime spectrum of R with the structure sheaf characterized on standard opens by O(D(f))=R_f and the localization restriction maps. Its stalk at 𝔭 is R_𝔭. An affine scheme is any locally ringed space isomorphic to one of these.

title: Scheme
description: A scheme is a locally ringed space admitting an open cover by affine schemes, with the given local-ringed-space structures on those opens.

title: Morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes is a morphism of their locally ringed spaces. On affine opens it is induced contravariantly by a unital homomorphism of commutative rings. An S-scheme is a scheme with a specified morphism to S; morphisms over S commute with these structure maps.

title: Fiber product of schemes
description: For X→S and Y→S, X×_S Y is the scheme with projection morphisms whose composites to S agree, universal for pairs of morphisms T→X,T→Y over S. For affine schemes Spec A,Spec B over Spec R it is Spec(A⊗_R B).

title: Base change and fibers of a scheme
description: For X→S and S′→S, the base change is X_(S′)=X×_S S′ with its projection to S′. The fiber at s∈S is X_s=X×_S Spec κ(s), where κ(s)=O_(S,s)/𝔪_s is the residue field of the local ring. A geometric fiber extends this residue field to an algebraic closure.

title: Closed immersion of schemes
description: A scheme morphism i:Z→X is a closed immersion if it is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset and the structure-sheaf map O_X→i_*O_Z is surjective on stalks. Affinely it is induced by a quotient map of rings R→R/I.

title: Separated morphism of schemes
description: A morphism X→S is separated if its diagonal X→X×_S X is a closed immersion. A scheme is separated over a specified base if its structure morphism is separated.

title: Morphism of schemes of finite type
description: A morphism X→S is locally of finite type if locally on affine source and target charts it comes from a ring map R→A with A generated by finitely many elements as an R-algebra. It is of finite type if it is also quasi-compact: inverse images of quasi-compact open subsets are quasi-compact.

title: Smooth morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes is smooth if locally on affine source and target charts its corresponding algebra map is smooth, meaning finitely presented and formally smooth for nilpotent-ideal lifting. Smoothness over a field is used for nonsingular geometric fibers, not merely regularity over an imperfect field.

title: Proper morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: after every base change the map on underlying topological spaces sends closed sets to closed sets. A scheme over a field is complete if its structure morphism is proper.

title: Projective space as a scheme
description: Projective n-space over a field k is obtained by gluing the n+1 standard affine charts Spec k[x₀/x_i,…,x_n/x_i], omitting x_i/x_i, with the standard coordinate-ratio changes on overlaps. Its points over an extension field are nonzero vectors modulo common nonzero scaling.

title: Projective scheme over a field
description: A k-scheme is projective if it admits a closed immersion over k into some projective space Pⁿ_k. Projectivity includes the specified algebraic scheme structure, rather than only its set of geometric points.

title: Group scheme
description: A group scheme G over S is an S-scheme with multiplication G×_S G→G, an identity section S→G and inverse G→G satisfying the group axioms as identities of S-morphisms. It need not be affine, connected or proper.

title: Abelian variety
description: An abelian variety over a field k is a smooth proper geometrically connected commutative group scheme over k. Geometric connectedness means connectedness after base change to an algebraic closure; its group law and identity are defined over k.

title: Irreducible topological space
description: A topological space is irreducible if it is nonempty and cannot be written as a union of two proper closed subsets. Equivalently any two nonempty open subsets intersect.

title: Krull dimension of a topological space
description: The Krull dimension of a topological space is the supremum of the lengths r of chains Z₀⊊Z₁⊊⋯⊊Z_r of nonempty irreducible closed subsets. The dimension of a scheme is the dimension of its underlying space.

title: Smooth projective algebraic curve
description: A smooth projective geometrically connected curve over k is a one-dimensional k-scheme smooth over k, geometrically connected, and admitting a closed immersion into some projective space over k.

title: Divisor on a smooth projective curve
description: A divisor on a smooth projective curve C/k is a finite integer sum D=∑n_PP of closed points. Its degree is ∑n_P[k(P):k]. After extension to an algebraic closure, geometric points are used with degree1. A divisor is effective if all n_P≥0.

title: Rational function on a smooth projective curve
description: A rational function on a smooth projective geometrically connected curve is an equivalence class of regular functions on nonempty open subsets, with equality on a smaller nonempty open subset. They form the function field k(C), the fraction field of any nonempty affine coordinate domain.

title: Principal divisor on a smooth projective curve
description: For a nonzero rational function f on a smooth projective curve C, its principal divisor is div(f)=∑_P ord_P(f)P, with normalized orders from the discrete valuation local rings at the closed points. Divisors differing by div(f) are linearly equivalent; degree-zero divisors modulo principal divisors form Pic⁰(C).

title: Jacobian of a pointed smooth projective curve
description: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/k with P∈C(k), its Jacobian is an abelian variety J with a morphism ι_P:C→J sending P to0 such that every morphism C→A into an abelian variety sending P to0 factors uniquely through a homomorphism J→A. The underlying J is canonically independent of the chosen base point.

title: Abel–Jacobi map on curve divisors
description: For a pointed smooth projective curve C/k with Jacobian(J,ι_P), a geometric degree-zero divisor ∑n_QQ maps to ∑n_Qι_P(Q) in J(k̄). The map kills principal divisors and identifies degree-zero divisor classes with J(k̄), compatibly with the Galois action; it is independent of P on degree-zero divisors.

title: Fraction field of an integral domain
description: For an integral domain R, its fraction field Frac(R) consists of fractions a/b with a∈R,b a nonzero element of R, identified by cross multiplication. It is a field containing R and every injective homomorphism from R into a field extends uniquely to a homomorphism from Frac(R).

title: Integral domain
description: An integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring R in which ab=0 implies a=0 or b=0.

title: Exponential upper bound for a binomial coefficient
description: For integers 1≤k≤N, binom(N,k)≤(eN/k)^k.

title: Dirichlet theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
description: For coprime positive integers a and m there are infinitely many primes p with p≡a mod m.

title: Pullback and pushforward of divisors under a finite curve map
description: For a finite nonconstant map f:C→D of smooth projective curves, pullback of a closed point is the sum of its inverse points weighted by ramification indices, and pushforward weights a closed point by its residue-field degree. These operations preserve principal divisor classes through function pullback and norm and induce maps of Jacobians with f_*f^*=[deg f].

title: Analytic uniformization of a complex abelian variety
description: For a complex abelian variety A of dimension g, the exponential map identifies A(C) analytically with its complex tangent space modulo a lattice of rank2g. A homomorphism is induced by its complex-linear tangent map carrying the source lattice into the target lattice; for an endomorphism, an invertible tangent map is equivalent to having finite kernel and being an isogeny.

title: Hecke correspondence on a full-level modular curve
description: For p prime with p≡1 mod N, the determinant-p integral matrices congruent to I mod N define a degree-(p+1) correspondence on the compact full-level modular curve X(N). Its action on divisors and on the Jacobian is the sum of the maps from its branches, equivalently pullback followed by pushforward; its action on holomorphic differentials is the weight-two Hecke action under H⁰(X(N),Ω¹)≅S₂(Γ(N)).

title: Ramanujan bound for weight-two Hecke operators
description: For p∤N, every eigenvalue of the usual degree-(p+1) Hecke correspondence on weight-two cuspidal differentials of the level-N modular curve has absolute value at most2√p. On X(N) for p≡1 mod N this is the determinant-p correspondence congruent to I modulo N.

title: Isogeny class of elliptic curves over a field
description: The F-isogeny class of an elliptic curve E/F is the collection of F-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves E′/F admitting an F-defined isogeny E→E′. The dual isogeny makes this relation symmetric.

title: Cyclic isogeny of elliptic curves
description: An isogeny of elliptic curves is cyclic if its geometric kernel is a cyclic group. In characteristic zero a cyclic isogeny of degree n has geometric kernel isomorphic to ℤ/nℤ.

title: Tate-module Galois representation of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field F and a prime p, the continuous action of Gal(Fsep/F) on T_p(E) defines ρ_(E,p∞):Gal(Fsep/F)→Aut_(ℤ_p)(T_p(E)). A ℤ_p-basis identifies the target with GL₂(ℤ_p); reduction modulo pⁱ gives the action on E[pⁱ].

title: Principal congruence subgroup of a general linear group
description: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, the principal congruence subgroup GL_n(R,I) is the kernel of entrywise reduction GL_n(R)→GL_n(R/I). It consists of invertible matrices congruent to the identity modulo I.

title: Successive congruence kernel for general linear groups
description: For a prime p, n≥1 and i≥2, the kernel of GL_n(ℤ/pⁱℤ)→GL_n(ℤ/p^(i−1)ℤ) is isomorphic to the additive group M_n(𝔽_p) by I+p^(i−1)A↦A modp. Conjugation corresponds to conjugation by the reduced matrix in GL_n(𝔽_p).

title: Lifting a full congruence image from p² to all finite levels
description: Let p be odd, n≥1 and H≤GL_n(ℤ_p). Write H_i for its image modulo pⁱ. If H₂ is the entire inverse image of H₁ under reduction modulo p, then H_i is the entire inverse image of H₁ for every i≥2. No closedness assumption is needed for this finite-level assertion.

title: Conjugation action on a matrix space
description: For a subgroup G≤GL_n(k) over a field k, the matrix space M_n(k) is a linear representation of G by g·A=gAg⁻¹. The trace-zero subspace is invariant under this action.

title: Group of equivariant homomorphisms
description: For abelian G-modules M,N, Hom_G(M,N) is the abelian group of additive maps f:M→N satisfying f(gm)=g f(m), with pointwise addition. If M,N are 𝔽_p-vector spaces and the G-actions are linear, every additive map is 𝔽_p-linear, so Hom_G(M,N) is an 𝔽_p-vector space.

title: Index of a subgroup
description: For a subgroup H≤G, the index [G:H] is the cardinality of the set of left cosets gH. Left and right cosets have the same cardinality by inversion.

title: Greenberg’s 5-adic image index for a rational 5-isogeny
description: Let E/ℚ be a non-CM elliptic curve with a ℚ-rational isogeny of degree5, and let I=[GL₂(ℤ₅):imρ_(E,5∞)]. Then v₅(I)=0 if no curve in the ℚ-isogeny class of E has two distinct ℚ-rational cyclic subgroups of order5, and v₅(I)=1 otherwise.

title: Full finite congruence images for a non-CM rational p-isogeny at p≥7
description: Let E/ℚ be non-CM, p≥7 prime, and suppose E has a ℚ-rational isogeny of degreep. For every i≥2, the image of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) on E[pⁱ] is the full inverse image of its image on E[p] in GL₂(ℤ/pⁱℤ).

title: Normalizer character on first cohomology of a unipotent prime-order subgroup
description: For an odd prime p, let V=𝔽_p² and H=⟨h⟩ with h=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Then H¹(H,V)≅𝔽_p by [ξ]↦the second coordinate of ξ(h). The normalizer element [[u,w],[0,v]] acts on this group by multiplication by u⁻¹v².

title: Character criterion for first cohomology of a prime-field Borel subgroup
description: Let p be odd and H≤G≤GL₂(𝔽_p), where H={[[1,t],[0,1]]:t∈𝔽_p} and G is upper triangular. Then H¹(G,𝔽_p²) has dimension1 exactly when every [[u,w],[0,v]]∈G satisfies u=v², and vanishes otherwise. If detG=𝔽_p×, the nonzero case forces p=3 or p≡2 mod3 and G={[[v²,w],[0,v]]:v∈𝔽_p×,w∈𝔽_p}.

title: Exponential map of a commutative complex Lie group
description: For a commutative complex Lie group G, the exponential map exp:Lie(G)→G is a holomorphic homomorphism with differential equal to the identity at0. For v in its complex tangent space, z↦exp(zv) is the unique holomorphic one-parameter subgroup with derivative v at0.

title: Analytification of a smooth projective complex variety
description: A smooth projective variety over ℂ has a compact complex manifold of complex points, and algebraic morphisms induce holomorphic maps. A geometrically connected such variety has connected complex points; an algebraic group structure therefore gives a compact connected complex Lie group.

title: Path lifting for a covering map
description: For a covering map p:Y→X, every continuous path in X and specified starting point over its initial point have a unique continuous lift. Homotopies of paths lift with a prescribed initial lift; a closed loop downstairs lifts to a path whose endpoint is in the same fiber as its starting point.

title: Integration of a differential one-form along a path
description: For a smooth one-form ω on a smooth manifold and a piecewise smooth path γ:[a,b]→M, its integral is ∫_a^b ω_(γ(t))(γ′(t))dt, summed over the smooth pieces. Pullback of forms commutes with path integration, and the integral of dh equals h(γ(b))−h(γ(a)); closed forms pair with integral one-cycles through their homology classes.

title: Vanishing of finite-group cohomology under a nontrivial central scalar
description: Let G be a finite group acting linearly on an 𝔽_p-vector space V. If a central element acts as λI with λ≠1, then Hʲ(G,V)=0 for every j≥0. The representation need not be faithful.

title: Rational cyclic subgroup of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field F, a rational cyclic subgroup of order n is a cyclic subgroup C≤E[n](F̄) of order n stable under Gal(F̄/F). Individual elements of C need not be F-rational. For n prime it is equivalently a Galois-invariant line in E[n].

title: Quadratic twist of an elliptic torsion representation
description: Let E/F be elliptic in characteristic zero, D∈F× and p an odd prime. Put κ_D(σ)=σ(√D)/√D∈{±1}⊂𝔽_p×. After identifying geometric torsion by an F(√D)-isomorphism, ρ_(E^D,p)=κ_Dρ_(E,p). In particular quadratic twisting preserves the Galois-stable lines in E[p].

title: Cyclotomic expression for the quadratic character of √5
description: Over any characteristic-zero field F, the quadratic character κ_5:σ↦σ(√5)/√5, viewed in 𝔽₅×, equals the square ω₅² of the mod5 cyclotomic character.

title: Lawson–Wuthrich first torsion cohomology classification over number fields
description: Let E/F be elliptic, F a number field, p prime, F∩ℚ(ζ_p)=ℚ, and G=Gal(F(E[p])/F). Then H¹(G,E[p])≠0 exactly in these cases: p=3 and E has a rational point of order3 and exactly one F-rational cyclic subgroup of order3; p=5 and E^5 has the corresponding point and unique subgroup of order5; or p≥11, p≡2 mod3 and E has exactly one F-rational cyclic subgroup C of orderp, on which Galois acts by ω_p^((p+1)/3). In every such case H¹ has p elements.

title: Uniform nuclear-norm recovery from independent entries with bounded fourth moments
description: Let the real measurement matrices Phi_j be independent copies of a matrix with independent centered entries of variance1 and fourth moments at most C4. For 1≤r≤min(n1,n2) and 0<rho<1, constants c,C,K>0 depending only on C4 give: if m≥C rho⁻²r(n1+n2), then with probability at least 1−e^(−cm), every nuclear-norm minimizer Xsharp from data A(X)+w with ‖w‖₂≤eta obeys ‖Xsharp−X‖F≤2(1+rho)²‖X_c‖₁/((1−rho)√r)+K(3+rho)eta/((1−rho)√m), simultaneously for all X and w.

title: Explicit Gaussian measurement bound for uniform stable nuclear-norm recovery
description: Let A be a real n1×n2 matrix measurement map generated by independent standard Gaussian entries. Let 1≤r≤min(n1,n2), 0<rho<1, kappa>1 and 0<epsilon<1, and set L=sqrt(1+(1+rho⁻¹)²). If m/√(m+1)≥kappa[(√r)L(√n1+√n2)+√(2log(1/epsilon))]/(kappa−1), then with probability at least 1−epsilon every nuclear-norm minimizer Xsharp with noise tolerance eta satisfies ‖Xsharp−X‖F≤2(1+rho)²‖X_c‖₁/((1−rho)√r)+2kappa√2(3+rho)eta/((1−rho)√m), uniformly for all X and admissible noises.

title: Chi-squared divergence of probability measures
description: For probability measures P≪Q with density r=dP/dQ, the chi-squared divergence is χ²(P‖Q)=∫(r−1)²dQ, allowing +∞. It is +∞ when P is not absolutely continuous with respect to Q.

title: Total variation bound by chi-squared divergence
description: For probability measures P,Q, the full total variation norm satisfies ||P−Q||_TV≤√χ²(P‖Q), with the inequality understood in the extended sense. The convention sup_A|P(A)−Q(A)| has the additional factor1/2.

title: Homomorphism of abelian varieties
description: A homomorphism A→B of abelian varieties over k is a k-scheme morphism preserving addition and the identity. The set Hom_k(A,B) is an abelian group under pointwise addition of morphisms.

title: Abelian subvariety
description: An abelian subvariety of A/k is a closed subgroup scheme B⊆A which is itself an abelian variety over k, with the inclusion preserving the group structures.

title: Simple abelian variety
description: An abelian variety A/k of positive dimension is k-simple if it has no proper nonzero abelian subvariety over k. It is absolutely simple if its base change to an algebraic closure is simple.

title: Isogeny of abelian varieties
description: An isogeny A→B over k is a surjective homomorphism of abelian varieties whose kernel is a finite group scheme. In characteristic zero its degree is the number of geometric kernel points, equivalently the degree of the corresponding finite map; two varieties are k-isogenous if such a k-map exists.

title: Category of abelian varieties up to isogeny
description: Over a fixed characteristic-zero field k, abelian varieties up to isogeny have morphism spaces Hom⁰_k(A,B)=Hom_k(A,B)⊗_ℤℚ, with composition induced by composition of homomorphisms and extended ℚ-bilinearly. Every isogeny is invertible in this category.

title: Rational endomorphism algebra of an abelian variety
description: The algebra End⁰_k(A)=End_k(A)⊗_ℤℚ has addition induced by the group law on A and multiplication given by composition. It is a finite-dimensional associative ℚ-algebra; the subscript specifies the field over which the endomorphisms are defined.

title: Simple abelian variety of GL₂-type over ℚ
description: A ℚ-simple abelian variety A is of GL₂-type if End⁰_ℚ(A) is a number field of degree dim A over ℚ. This convention concerns simple varieties; the broader convention allowing a commutative semisimple subalgebra of dimension dim A also permits products.

title: Weil restriction of an abelian variety
description: For a finite separable field extension L/k and an abelian variety A/L, Res_(L/k)A is the abelian variety over k representing the functor T↦Hom_L(T×_k L,A) on k-schemes. It has dimension [L:k]dim A; after a separable splitting extension it becomes the product of the conjugate abelian varieties.

title: Tate module of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a characteristic-zero field k and a prime ℓ, T_ℓA=lim←A[ℓⁿ](k̄) with multiplication-by-ℓ transition maps. It is a free ℤ_ℓ-module of rank2dim A with its continuous absolute Galois action; V_ℓA=T_ℓA⊗_(ℤ_ℓ)ℚ_ℓ.

title: Hasse–Weil L-function of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K, its Hasse–Weil L-function is the Euler product L(A,s)=∏_v det(1−Fr_v^(−1)·Nv^(−s) | (V_ℓ(A)^∨)^(I_v))^(−1) over finite places v, with ℓ different from the residue characteristic of v. Here V_ℓ(A)^∨=Hom(V_ℓ(A),ℚ_ℓ) carries the dual Galois action and Fr_v^(−1) is a geometric Frobenius, the inverse of an arithmetic Frobenius, acting on inertia invariants. The rational local polynomial is independent of ℓ; the product is initially considered in a right half-plane of absolute convergence.

title: L-function of a normalized weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f=∑a_nqⁿ, its L-function is L(f,s)=∑a_n n^(−s), initially in a right half-plane of absolute convergence and then analytically continued. Its unramified Euler factor at p∤N is (1−a_pp^(−s)+χ(p)p^(1−2s))^(−1).

title: Strongly modular abelian variety over a number field
description: An abelian variety A/K is strongly modular over K if its Hasse–Weil L-function is a finite product of L-functions of normalized weight-two newforms for groups Γ₁(N_i). The base field K is part of this property; geometric modularity alone does not imply it.

title: Hecke algebra of weight-two cusp forms
description: The integral Hecke algebra at level N is the commutative ring generated by the classical Hecke operators T_n and diamond operators on S₂(Γ₁(N)); on the modular Jacobian they act through the associated algebraic correspondences. A normalized eigenform f gives a homomorphism T→ℂ by T_n↦a_n(f) and diamond d↦χ(d).

title: Quotient of an abelian variety by an abelian subvariety
description: For an abelian subvariety B⊆A over k, the quotient A/B is an abelian variety with a surjective homomorphism A→A/B having kernel B, universal among homomorphisms from A that vanish on B.

title: Modular abelian variety attached to a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f on Γ₁(N), let I_f be the kernel of its eigenvalue homomorphism on the Hecke algebra T. The modular abelian variety A_f is the quotient J₁(N)/(I_fJ₁(N)), where I_fJ₁(N) is the abelian subvariety generated by the images of the operators in I_f. It is defined over ℚ and its complex differential space pulls back to the span of all Galois conjugates of f.

title: Finite morphism of schemes
description: A scheme morphism f:X→Y is finite if for each affine open Spec R⊆Y its inverse image is affine Spec A and A is a finitely generated R-module via f. In particular a finite group scheme over a field has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra.

title: Congruence subgroup Γ₀(N)
description: For N≥1, Γ₀(N) is the subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) consisting of matrices whose lower-left entry is divisible by N. It contains Γ₁(N); the map sending a matrix to its lower-right entry modulo N identifies Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) with (ℤ/Nℤ)×.

title: Diamond operator on Γ₁(N) modular forms
description: For d∈(ℤ/Nℤ)× and a weight-k modular form on Γ₁(N), choose γ∈Γ₀(N) with lower-right entry d modulo N and set ⟨d⟩f=f|ₖγ. This is independent of γ modulo Γ₁(N); the character-χ subspace satisfies ⟨d⟩f=χ(d)f, and cusp forms are preserved.

title: Complex multiplication of a weight-two newform
