description: A normalized weight-two newform f has complex multiplication if there is a nontrivial quadratic Dirichlet character χ such that χ(p)a_p(f)=a_p(f) for almost all primes p. Equivalently f has a nontrivial quadratic self-twist; non-CM means no such character exists.

title: Inner twist of a non-CM weight-two newform
description: For a non-CM normalized weight-two newform f with coefficient field F, an inner twist is a pair(γ,χ) with γ:F→ℂ an embedding and χ a Dirichlet character satisfying γ(a_p(f))=χ(p)a_p(f) for almost all primes p. For such f the character is unique for a given γ, and the occurring embeddings are automorphisms of F.

title: Splitting field determined by newform inner twists
description: For a non-CM weight-two newform, take the finite collection of its inner-twist characters χ. A character modulo M is viewed on Gal(ℚ(ζ_M)/ℚ) through a↦(ζ_M↦ζ_M^a), and determines the fixed field of its kernel. The splitting field attached to the newform is the compositum of these fields inside ℚ̄.

title: Gauss sum of a Dirichlet character
description: For a primitive Dirichlet character χ of conductor M, its Gauss sum is g(χ)=∑_(a mod M)χ(a)exp(2πia/M). Character values are extended by0 to nonunits; the exponential fixes the chosen complex embedding of the roots of unity.

title: Splitting map for a multiplicative Galois 2-cocycle
description: Let a finite Galois group G act on a field F, and let c:G×G→F× be a multiplicative2-cocycle. A splitting map is a1-cochain β:G→F× such that c(σ,τ)=β(σ)σ(β(τ))/β(στ). Such a map exists exactly when the cohomology class of c is zero; two splitting maps differ by a1-cocycle.

title: Building block of a modular abelian variety
description: For a modular abelian variety A_f and a field L over which all its geometric endomorphisms are defined, a building block is an absolutely simple abelian variety B/L such that (A_f)_L is L-isogenous to a power of B. Its isogeny class, rather than a chosen equation or embedding into A_f, is intrinsic.

title: Sheaf of Kähler differentials of a scheme
description: For a scheme X over k, Ω¹_(X/k) is the sheaf of O_X-modules obtained by gluing the modules Ω¹_(A/k) on affine charts Spec A with their localization identifications. Its global sections are regular differential one-forms; a morphism induces pullback of these differentials.

title: Invariant differentials on an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A/k, an invariant differential is a global section of Ω¹_(A/k) unchanged by every translation after field extension. These form a k-vector space of dimension dim A, identified with the cotangent space at the identity by evaluation; homomorphisms pull them back to invariant differentials.

title: Stochastic exponential of a continuous local martingale
description: For a real continuous local martingale L with L₀=0, its stochastic exponential is the strictly positive process E(L)_t=exp(L_t−[L]_t/2), where [L] is quadratic variation. It is the solution of dE(L)=E(L)dL with initial value1.

title: Essential supremum of a family of random variables
description: On a probability space, the essential supremum of a family (X_i) of measurable extended real random variables is the almost-sure equivalence class of the least measurable upper bound: X_i≤Y almost surely for every i, and Y≤Z almost surely for every measurable Z with that property. Unlike an ordinary pointwise supremum, it is defined modulo null sets.

title: Novikov exponential-martingale criterion
description: If L is a real continuous local martingale with L₀=0 and Eexp([L]_T/2)<∞ on a finite horizon, its stochastic exponential E(L) is a uniformly integrable martingale on [0,T], with E E(L)_T=1.

title: Continuous and purely discontinuous decomposition of a local martingale
description: On a usual filtration, every real càdlàg local martingale N has a unique decomposition N=N₀+N^c+N^d, where N^c is a continuous local martingale starting at0 and N^d is purely discontinuous, meaning [N^d,C]=0 for every continuous local martingale C.

title: Optional sampling for a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale
description: For a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale M on a finite horizon [0,T] and stopping times σ≤τ≤T, E[M_τ|F_σ]=M_σ. In particular a martingale closed by an integrable terminal variable can be sampled at bounded stopping times.

title: Debut theorem for a progressively measurable set
description: On a complete right-continuous filtration, the first entrance time into a progressively measurable subset of [0,∞)×Ω is a stopping time, allowing infinity when the set is empty.

title: Brownian orthogonal decomposition of a local martingale
description: On a usual filtration carrying a d-dimensional Brownian motion W, every real càdlàg local martingale N has a unique decomposition N=N₀+∫Z_s·dW_s+M, where Z is predictable and locally square-integrable and M is a càdlàg local martingale starting at0 with [M,W^i]=0 for every i. Uniqueness of Z is modulo dt×dP.

title: Snell representation of a càdlàg reflected semimartingale
description: On a usual filtration let Y=Y₀+N−A be a càdlàg class-D process, where N is a uniformly integrable martingale and A is predictable càdlàg nondecreasing with A₀=0. Let R be adapted càdlàg with its positive stopped values uniformly integrable, Y≥R on [0,T), and ∫₀ᵀ(Y_(s−)−R_(s−))dA_s=0, using R_T=Y_T. Then Y_t is the essential supremum of E[R_τ1_(τ<T)+Y_T1_(τ=T)|F_t] over τ∈[t,T] for which the reward is integrable; the same formula holds with extended conditional expectations for other τ.

title: Digamma function on the positive real axis
description: For x>0, the real digamma function is ψ(x)=Γ′(x)/Γ(x), the logarithmic derivative of the positive-real gamma function.

title: Finite Galois field extension
description: A finite Galois extension L/k is a field extension of finite vector-space dimension which is both normal and separable. Its automorphisms fixing k form the finite Galois group Gal(L/k).

title: Fixed field of field automorphisms
description: For a group H of automorphisms of a field L, its fixed field L^H consists of all elements of L fixed by every automorphism in H. An intermediate field of L/k is a subfield M with k⊆M⊆L; Gal(L/M) denotes the subgroup fixing M pointwise.

title: Artin fixed-field degree theorem
description: For a finite subgroup H of the automorphism group of a field L, the extension L/L^H is finite Galois, has degree |H| and has Galois group exactly H.

title: Fixed-field characterization of finite Galois extensions
description: For a finite normal separable extension L/k, the group Gal(L/k) has order[L:k] and fixes exactly k. For every intermediate field M, the extension L/M is again finite normal separable, so L^(Gal(L/M))=M.

title: Lenglart–Lépingle–Pratelli comparison for increasing processes
description: Let A,B be nonnegative predictable nondecreasing processes, with the zero-time convention A₀₋=B₀₋=0. Suppose q,a>0 satisfy E[(A_T1_(T>0)−A_S1_(S>0))^q]≤a E[B_T^q1_(S<T)] for every pair of stopping times S≤T. For every p>0 there is C=C(a,q,p) such that E A_∞^p≤C E B_∞^p, with extended moments. The adapted càdlàg version replaces A_T,A_S,B_T by their left limits.

title: Garsia–Neveu Lp bound for an increasing process
description: Let A be nonnegative predictable nondecreasing and X≥0 integrable. If E[A_∞−A_S1_(S>0)]≤E[X1_(S<∞)] for every stopping time S, then ‖A_∞‖p≤p‖X‖p for p≥1, allowing infinite moments and using A₀₋=0. The adapted càdlàg version uses A_(S−) and A₀₋=0.

title: Davis decomposition of a càdlàg local martingale
description: For a real càdlàg local martingale M starting at0, write S_t=sup_(s≤t)|ΔM_s|. After localization with E S_∞<∞, M=K+L with K a finite-variation martingale, E TV(K)_∞≤4 E S_∞, and L a local martingale with |ΔL_t|≤4S_(t−). The decomposition is used locally when the expectations are not globally finite.

title: Quadratic-variation isometry for a càdlàg martingale
description: For a real square-integrable càdlàg martingale M starting at0, E|M_T|²=E[M]_T on bounded horizons; localization gives the corresponding stopped identities for locally square-integrable martingales.

title: Poincaré complete reducibility for abelian varieties
description: For an abelian subvariety B⊆A over a characteristic-zero field k, there is an abelian subvariety C⊆A over k for which addition B×C→A is a k-isogeny. Thus nontrivial decompositions up to isogeny correspond to nontrivial idempotents in End⁰_k(A).

title: Rank-one rational Hom space for non-CM isogenous elliptic curves
description: If E,E′ are geometrically non-CM elliptic curves over a characteristic-zero field k and µ:E→E′ is a k-isogeny, then Hom_k(E,E′)⊗ℚ=ℚµ and End⁰_k(E)=ℚ. Every nonzero homomorphism E→E′ is an isogeny.

title: Finite Galois descent for morphisms of schemes
description: For k-schemes X,Y and a finite Galois extension L/k, a morphism X_L→Y_L comes from a unique k-morphism X→Y exactly when it is invariant under the natural semilinear Gal(L/k) action. This applies to homomorphisms of abelian varieties and their rational Hom spaces.

title: Modularity of a simple GL₂-type abelian variety over ℚ
description: Every simple abelian variety A/ℚ with End⁰_ℚ(A) a number field of degree dim A is ℚ-isogenous to A_f for a normalized weight-two newform f. Its coefficient field is isomorphic to End⁰_ℚ(A).

title: Isogeny invariance and product formula for abelian L-functions
description: Abelian varieties isogenous over a number field have identical Hasse–Weil L-functions, including bad local factors. The L-function of a product is the product of the two L-functions.

title: L-function identity for Weil restriction of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A/L and a finite number-field extension L/k, L(Res_(L/k)A/k,s)=L(A/L,s), with every local Euler factor, including ramified and bad places, retained.

title: Newform factorization of the modular abelian variety L-function
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f with coefficient field F and attached abelian variety A_f/ℚ, L(A_f/ℚ,s)=∏_(σ:F→ℂ)L(σf,s), including the local factors at primes dividing the level.

title: Quadratic base-change factorization of an elliptic L-function
description: For an elliptic curve E₀/k and a quadratic number-field extension K=k(√d), L(E₀/K,s)=L(E₀/k,s)L(E₀^d/k,s), including all local Euler factors, where E₀^d is the quadratic twist associated to K/k.

title: Regular sequence in a commutative ring
description: An ordered sequence f₁,…,f_r in a commutative ring R is regular if R/(f₁,…,f_r)≠0 and multiplication by f_i is injective on R/(f₁,…,f_(i−1)) for every i. The order and the nonzero final quotient are part of this convention.

title: Krull dimension of a commutative ring
description: The Krull dimension of a commutative ring R is the supremum of lengths r of strictly increasing chains 𝔭₀⊊⋯⊊𝔭_r of prime ideals. For the zero ring, which has no prime ideals, use dimension−1.

title: Residue field at a prime ideal
description: For a commutative ring R and prime ideal 𝔭, its residue field is κ(𝔭)=R_𝔭/𝔭R_𝔭, equivalently the fraction field of R/𝔭. For a maximal ideal 𝔪 it is R/𝔪.

title: Radical of an ideal
description: For an ideal I in a commutative ring R, its radical is √I={a∈R:aⁿ∈I for some positive integer n}. An ideal is radical when I=√I.

title: Affine polynomial zero locus and its vanishing ideal
description: For a field k, an extension K/k and I⊆k[x₁,…,x_n], V_K(I)={a∈Kⁿ:f(a)=0 for every f∈I}. For W⊆Kⁿ, I_k(W) consists of the k-polynomials vanishing on W. An affine algebraic set is such a common zero locus, with the Zariski topology.

title: Dimension of an affine variety
description: For an affine variety with reduced finitely generated coordinate algebra A, its dimension is the Krull dimension of A. Its points over an extension K/k are the k-algebra maps A→K; reducible varieties are allowed.

title: Perfect field
description: A field k is perfect if every algebraic extension of k is separable. In characteristic zero this always holds; in characteristic p>0 it is equivalent to surjectivity of x↦xᵖ on k.

title: Jacobian matrix of a polynomial system
description: For polynomials f₁,…,f_r∈k[x₀,…,x_N], their formal Jacobian matrix is (∂f_i/∂x_j), where formal partial differentiation sends a monomial a x₀^e₀⋯x_N^e_N to e_j a x₀^e₀⋯x_j^(e_j−1)⋯x_N^e_N. It may be evaluated at points over any extension field.

title: Zariski’s lemma for a field finitely generated as an algebra
description: If a field extension K/k is finitely generated as a k-algebra, then K/k is finite algebraic.

title: Existence of a maximal ideal above a proper ideal
description: Every proper ideal of a nonzero commutative ring with identity is contained in a maximal ideal.

title: Model of an abelian variety over a discrete valuation ring
description: For an abelian variety A/K and a discrete valuation ring R with fraction field K, an R-model is a scheme 𝒜→Spec R with a specified isomorphism 𝒜_K≅A. Its generic fiber is the base change to Spec K, and its special fiber is the base change to the residue field of R.

title: Néron model of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A/K over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring R, its Néron model is a smooth separated R-scheme 𝒜 of finite type with generic fiber A such that Hom_R(Z,𝒜)→Hom_K(Z_K,A) is bijective for every smooth R-scheme Z. Its commutative group-scheme structure is the unique extension of that of A.

title: Abelian scheme
description: An abelian scheme over S is a proper smooth group scheme over S whose geometric fibers are connected. Each geometric fiber is an abelian variety.

title: Good reduction of an abelian variety
description: An abelian variety over the fraction field K of a discrete valuation ring R has good reduction if it extends to an abelian scheme over R. Equivalently its Néron model is proper over R; for elliptic curves this agrees with smooth reduction of a minimal Weierstrass model.

title: Identity component and component group of a Néron special fiber
description: For a Néron model 𝒜 over a discrete valuation ring with residue field k, the geometric identity component 𝒜⁰_(k̄) is the connected component containing the identity in its geometric special fiber. The geometric component group Φ(k̄)=𝒜_k(k̄)/𝒜⁰_k(k̄) is the finite group of connected components, with its natural Galois action. The open subgroup 𝒜⁰ has the whole generic fiber and only the identity component of the special fiber.

title: Additive group scheme
description: The additive group scheme 𝔾_a over a ring R is the affine line Spec R[t] with addition induced by t↦t⊗1+1⊗t, identity t↦0 and inverse t↦−t. Its points over an R-algebra A are the additive group of A.

title: Zariski tangent and cotangent space at a rational point
description: For a k-rational point x of a k-scheme X, its cotangent space is 𝔪_x/𝔪_x² over k, where 𝔪_x is the maximal ideal of O_(X,x). Its dual Hom_k(𝔪_x/𝔪_x²,k) is the Zariski tangent space T_xX; equivalently tangent vectors are k-morphisms Spec k[ε]/(ε²)→X reducing to x.

title: Algebraic dual of a vector space
description: For a vector space V over a field k, its algebraic dual V* is Hom_k(V,k), with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. No topology or continuity condition is imposed.

title: Boundedness in probability of a random family
description: A family (X_i) of real random variables is bounded in probability if lim_(K→∞)sup_iP(|X_i|>K)=0. The definition also applies across different probability spaces by using each variable’s own probability.

title: Uniform convergence in probability on compact time intervals
description: A sequence of processes X^n on the same probability space converges ucp to X if, for every finite T and epsilon>0, P(sup_(t≤T)|X_t^n−X_t|>epsilon)→0. Vector processes use any fixed finite-dimensional norm.

title: Uniform tightness of a sequence of semimartingales
description: A sequence of real semimartingales X^n satisfies condition UT if for every finite T the family of stochastic-integral terminal values (H·X^n)_T, over all n and elementary predictable integrands H bounded in absolute value by1, is bounded in probability. The elementary integrands use finite stopping-time intervals and coefficients measurable at the left endpoint.

title: Stability of stochastic integrals under UT and ucp convergence
description: On a common usual filtered space let X^n,X be càdlàg semimartingales and H^n,H adapted càdlàg processes. If X^n satisfies UT and (H^n,X^n)→(H,X) jointly ucp, then ∫H^n_(s−)dX_s^n→∫H_(s−)dX_s ucp.

title: Covariation stability under UT and ucp convergence
description: On a common usual filtered space let X^n,Y^n and X,Y be real càdlàg semimartingales. If each sequence X^n and Y^n satisfies UT and (X^n,Y^n)→(X,Y) jointly ucp, then [X^n,Y^n]→[X,Y] ucp.

title: Comparison for càdlàg reflected Brownian BSDE solutions
description: Let two given càdlàg reflected Brownian BSDE solutions on a usual Brownian-carrying filtration have a common finite horizon, globally Lipschitz drivers g1,g2 and some p>1 integrability: the suprema of |Y| and K_T and the square roots of the Brownian and orthogonal-martingale quadratic variations lie in Lp. Use the convention Y_t=xi−∫_t^Tg ds−∫_t^TZ dW−(M_T−M_t)+K_T−K_t. If xi1≤xi2, S1≤S2 and g1(t,y,z)≥g2(t,y,z) almost everywhere for every y,z, then Y1≤Y2 indistinguishably.

title: Snell envelope decomposition for a càdlàg reward with integrable positive maximum
description: On a usual filtration over [0,T], let a real adapted càdlàg reward R have E(sup_tR_t^+)^p<∞ for some p>1 and terminal R_T in Lp. Its stopping value U_t=esssup_(τ≥t)E[R_τ|F_t], with extended expectations when the negative part is not integrable, has a càdlàg class-D version and decomposition U=U₀+N−A with N a UI càdlàg martingale and A predictable càdlàg nondecreasing starting at0. It is the least class-D supermartingale dominating R; U_T=R_T and ∫₀ᵀ(U_(s−)−R_(s−))dA_s=0. Moreover sup|U| lies in Lp.

title: Linear reflected Brownian BSDE on a usual filtration
description: Let p>1 and let a usual filtration carry a d-dimensional Brownian motion W. Let xi∈Lp, an adapted càdlàg lower obstacle S satisfy sup S^+∈Lp and S_T≤xi, and a progressively measurable driver h satisfy ∫₀ᵀ|h_s|ds∈Lp. Then the reflected equation Y_t=xi−∫_t^Th_sds−∫_t^TZ_sdW_s−(M_T−M_t)+K_T−K_t has a unique càdlàg solution, with M orthogonal to W, K predictable nondecreasing, ∫(Y_-−S_-)dK=0, and sup|Y|, K_T, (∫|Z|²)^(1/2), [M]_T^(1/2) in Lp.

title: Affine linear subspace over a field
description: An affine linear subspace of kⁿ is a translate a+W of a vector subspace W≤kⁿ. Its dimension is dimW, independently of the chosen a.

title: Irreducible component of a topological space
description: An irreducible component of a topological space is a maximal irreducible closed subset, ordered by inclusion. Distinct irreducible components need not be disjoint.

title: Total geometric degree of an affine variety
description: Over an algebraically closed field, the degree of an irreducible affine variety W⊂kⁿ of dimensionr is the maximum number of points in a finite intersection W∩L with an affine linear subspace L of dimensionn−r. The total geometric degree of a reducible variety is the sum over all its irreducible components, including components of smaller dimension; the empty set has degree0.

title: Affine hypersurface Bézout inequality
description: Let W⊂kⁿ over an algebraically closed field be a nonempty affine variety of pure dimensionr, and let f be a nonzero polynomial of degreeD≥1 that vanishes identically on none of its irreducible components. If W∩V(f) is nonempty, it is pure of dimensionr−1 and its total geometric degree is at most D times that ofW.

title: Geometric degree bound for bounded affine equations
description: Over an algebraically closed field, the common zero locus in kⁿ of s polynomials of degrees at mostD≥1 has total geometric degree at most Dˢ. Zero polynomials and nonzero constants are allowed, using degree0 for the empty locus.

title: Lower ramification groups of a local field extension
description: For a finite Galois extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields, normalize v_L(L×)=ℤ. For real t≥−1 set G_t={σ∈Gal(L/K):v_L(σa−a)≥t+1 for every a∈O_L}. Then G_(−1) is the full Galois group, G₀ is inertia and G₁ is wild inertia.

title: Upper ramification groups of a local field
description: For a finite Galois local extension with lower groups G_t, let φ(u)=∫₀^u[G₀:G_t]^(−1)dt for u≥0, let ψ be its increasing inverse and put G^v=G_(ψ(v)). For the absolute Galois group, G_K^v is the inverse limit of these upper groups over finite Galois subextensions; the quotient-compatible upper numbering is used.

title: Local ℓ-adic Galois representation
description: For a nonarchimedean local field K of residue characteristic p and a prime ℓ≠p, a local ℓ-adic representation is a continuous linear action of Gal(K̄/K) on a finite-dimensional vector space over a finite extension F/ℚ_ℓ, with its ℓ-adic topology. Its inertia-fixed vectors form V^I_K.

title: Artin and Swan conductor of a local ℓ-adic representation
description: For a local ℓ-adic representation V, its Swan exponent is Sw(V)=∫₀^∞codim_F V^(G_K^u)du, where G_K^u are the positive upper ramification groups. The Artin conductor exponent is a(V)=codim_F V^I_K+Sw(V); its conductor ideal is 𝔭_K^(a(V)). These exponents are nonnegative integers in this setting.

title: Conductor ideal of an abelian variety over a number field
description: For an abelian variety A/K over a number field, its conductor ideal is 𝔑_K(A)=∏_v𝔭_v^(a(V_ℓA|_(G_Kv))), with ℓ different from the residue characteristic at v. The exponent uses the inertia-fixed codimension and Swan conductor of its rational Tate representation and is independent of ℓ; only finitely many exponents are nonzero.

title: Relative discriminant ideal of number fields
description: For a finite extension L/K of number fields, the relative discriminant 𝔡_(L/K) is the O_K-ideal locally generated by determinants det(Tr_(L/K)(b_i b_j)) for integral bases after localization at primes of O_K. For K=ℚ it is generated by the ordinary field discriminant up to sign.

title: Relative ideal norm of number fields
description: For a finite extension L/K of number fields, the ideal norm sends a prime 𝔓 of O_L above 𝔭 of O_K to 𝔭^[O_L/𝔓:O_K/𝔭] and extends multiplicatively to nonzero fractional ideals. For K=ℚ its positive generator is the absolute ideal norm.

title: Lp bound for the increasing parts of a strong supermartingale
description: Let p>1 and let X be a real strong optional supermartingale on a usual filtration over [0,T] with E sup_(t≤T)|X_t|^p<∞. In its Mertens decomposition X=X₀+M−A−I, with predictable càdlàg nondecreasing A and predictable left-continuous nondecreasing purely discontinuous I starting at0, one has E A_T^p+E I_T^p≤C_p E sup_(t≤T)|X_t|^p, with C_p depending only on p.

title: Optional section theorem
description: For an optional set E on a usual filtered probability space and every epsilon>0, there is a stopping time tau whose graph on {tau<∞} is contained in E and P(tau<∞)≥P(π(E))−epsilon, where π(E) is its projection on the sample space, measured in the completed probability space.

title: Càdlàg regularization of a closed martingale
description: On a usual filtration over a finite horizon, the martingale t↦E[V|F_t] for an integrable terminal variable V has a càdlàg version. This version is uniformly integrable and satisfies E[V|F_tau] at every bounded stopping time tau.

title: Riemann surface
description: A Riemann surface is a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological space covered by coordinate neighborhoods homeomorphic to open subsets of ℂ, with holomorphic transition maps. The charts define holomorphic functions and maps; its complex dimension is one.

title: Group scheme of roots of unity
description: Over a ring R, µ_N is the group scheme Spec R[t]/(t^N−1), with multiplication induced by t↦t⊗t, identity t↦1 and inverse t↦t^(N−1). Its points over an R-algebra are the units whose Nth power is1.

title: Family of elliptic curves
description: An elliptic curve over a scheme S is an abelian scheme E→S whose geometric fibers have dimension one. In particular it has a specified identity section, and its group law is part of the family; pullback gives a family over every S′→S.

title: Coarse moduli scheme
description: For a moduli functor F of isomorphism classes of families on k-schemes, a coarse moduli scheme M has a natural transformation F→Hom_k(−,M) universal among transformations to represented scheme functors, and inducing a bijection on points over every algebraically closed extension of k. It need not carry a universal family.

title: Arithmetic modular curve with µ_N level structure
description: For N≥4 over ℚ, Y₁^µ(N) represents isomorphism classes of elliptic-curve families with a closed group-scheme embedding µ_N↪E[N]; X₁^µ(N) is its smooth projective compactification. Its complex point τ corresponds to E_τ=ℂ/(ℤ+τℤ), with ζ_N↦1/N. This fixes the arithmetic model and complex identification: its cusp∞ is ℚ-rational and its local parameter is q=exp(2πiτ).

title: Arithmetic modular curve X₀(N)
description: Over ℚ, Y₀(N) is the coarse moduli curve of elliptic curves with a cyclic subgroup scheme of order N; X₀(N) is its smooth projective compactification. On complex points τ corresponds to ℂ/(ℤ+τℤ) with subgroup generated by1/N, giving Γ₀(N)\ℍ. The arithmetic curve and its moduli convention are distinguished from the bare complex quotient.

title: Continuous induction from a subgroup of finite index
description: For an open subgroup H of finite index in a profinite group G and a continuous H-action on an R-module M, Ind_H^G M can be realized as continuous functions f:G→M satisfying f(hg)=h f(g), with (g₀f)(g)=f(gg₀). It is a finite direct product of copies of M indexed by H\G; this fixes the function-model convention.

title: Tate module of a Weil restriction
description: For a finite separable extension L/k of characteristic-zero fields and an abelian variety A/L, T_ℓ(Res_(L/k)A) is canonically isomorphic as a continuous G_k-module to Ind_(G_L)^(G_k)T_ℓ(A). Rationalizing gives the same identity for V_ℓ.

title: Induction formula for a local Artin conductor
description: For a finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields of residue characteristic p and a finite-dimensional continuous ℓ-adic representation V of G_L, ℓ≠p, a_K(Ind_(G_L)^(G_K)V)=f_(L/K)a_L(V)+dim(V)v_K(𝔡_(L/K)), where f is the residue degree and 𝔡 is the local discriminant ideal.

title: Conductor formula for Weil restriction of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A/L of dimension g and a finite extension of number fields L/K, 𝔑_K(Res_(L/K)A)=Norm_(L/K)(𝔑_L(A))·𝔡_(L/K)^(2g). In particular for an elliptic curve over quadratic K/ℚ the rational conductor is the absolute norm of its K-conductor times Δ_K².

title: Local conductor of the representation of a newform
description: For a normalized primitive weight-two newform f of level N, the two-dimensional ℓ-adic representation attached to f has conductor exponent v_p(N) at each prime p≠ℓ. This includes primes dividing the nebentypus conductor and the level.

title: Tate representation decomposition of a modular abelian variety
description: For A_f attached to a weight-two newform with coefficient field F, extending coefficients from ℚ_ℓ to an algebraic closure decomposes V_ℓ(A_f) into the two-dimensional Galois representations attached to the embeddings σ:F→ℚ̄_ℓ, one for each embedding counted with multiplicity. These representations have Frobenius traces σ(a_p).

title: Conductor of the abelian variety attached to a newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f of level N and coefficient field F, its associated abelian variety A_f/ℚ has conductor N^[F:ℚ]. The integer N is the primitive newform level, not a chosen oldform ambient level.

title: Quadratic lattice over ℤ_p
description: A quadratic ℤ_p-lattice in a nondegenerate quadratic space V over ℚ_p is a free ℤ_p-submodule L of finite rank spanning V overℚ_p, equipped with the restricted quadratic form. No integrality of Q(L) or B(L,L) is assumed unless specified.

title: Dual of a local quadratic lattice
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice L inside its ℚ_p-span V with half-polarization B, its dual is L#={v∈V:B(v,L)⊆ℤ_p}. The dual is taken with respect to B, so a half-integral polarization convention changes it.

title: Modular quadratic lattice over ℤ_p
description: A nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice L is pᵃ-modular, a∈ℤ, if L#=p^(−a)L inside its rational span. Equivalently its Gram matrix divided by pᵃ is invertible overℤ_p. The case a=0 is unimodular.

title: Jordan decomposition of a local quadratic lattice
description: A Jordan decomposition of a nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice L is an orthogonal direct sum L=⊥_a L_a, with finitely many nonzero summands and each L_a pᵃ-modular. Summands of the same modularity power are grouped; the choice of the actual sublattices need not be unique.

title: Diagonalizable local quadratic lattice
description: A quadratic ℤ_p-lattice is diagonalizable overℤ_p if it admits a ℤ_p-basis e₁,…,e_r with B(e_i,e_j)=0 wheneveri≠j. Diagonalizability is a lattice condition, stronger than diagonalizing the underlying ℚ_p-quadratic space.

title: The even binary unimodular ℤ₂-lattice A(2,2)
description: The standard even binary unimodular ℤ₂-lattice A(2,2) has Gram matrix [[2,1],[1,2]] under the conventionQ(x)=B(x,x), hence Q(x,y)=2x²+2xy+2y² and determinant3. The same matrix defines its integral ℤ-model.

title: Square-free part of a positive rational number
description: For d∈ℚ_(>0), its square-free part sf(d) is the unique positive square-free integer s with d/s a rational square. Its odd square-free part sf(d)′ is sf(d) divided by2 if sf(d) is even, and otherwise sf(d).

title: Odd part of a nonzero rational number
description: The odd part of a nonzero rational a is a′=2^(−v₂(a))a, a unit ofℤ₂. If a is a nonzero integer, a′ is an odd integer; its residue modulo8 is therefore well-defined. This removes the entire2-power, not the odd square factors.

title: Orthogonal complement of a vector in a quadratic lattice
description: For a quadratic ℤ_p-lattice L and a nonisotropic vector v in its ℚ_p-span, the lattice orthogonal complement of v is L∩v⊥={x∈L:B(v,x)=0}. Its rational span is v⊥; v need not itself belong toL.

title: Representation of a scalar by a quadratic lattice
description: A scalar t is represented by a quadratic lattice L if Q(x)=t for some x∈L. Local representation uses x∈L_p; it is distinct from rational representation in ℚ_pL and from primitive lattice representation.

title: Existence of a Jordan splitting over ℤ_p
description: Every nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice has a Jordan decomposition. At oddp it can be split into orthogonal rankone blocks; atp2 one may require ranktwo modular blocks as well as rankone blocks before grouping equal modularities.

title: Shift invariance of a normalized quadratic coset polynomial
description: Let N be a quadraticℤ-lattice,ν∈ℚN andh_ν(x)=Q(x)+2B(ν,x), with h_ν(N)⊆ℤ generating dℤ for d>0. For x₀∈N putω=ν+x₀. Then h_ω(N) generates the same ideal, and h_ω(x)/d is almost universal exactly when h_ν(x)/d is.

title: Weil restriction along a finite free algebra
description: Let S be a commutative R-algebra finite free as an R-module and let X be an S-scheme. The Weil restriction Res_(S/R)X, when representable, is the R-scheme whose T-points are Hom_S(T×_(SpecR)SpecS,X), functorially in R-schemes T. This definition permits nonaffine X and nonreduced S; it does not assert representability for every X.

title: Representability and smoothness of a finite flat Weil restriction
description: For a finite locally free morphism S′→S and a quasi-projective smooth S′-scheme X, Res_(S′/S)X is representable by a smooth S-scheme. Restriction of scalars commutes with base change.

title: Néron model and finite extension Weil restriction
description: Let S/R be a finite free extension of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields L/K. If 𝒜/S is the Néron model of an abelian variety A/L, then Res_(S/R)𝒜 exists and is the Néron model over R of Res_(L/K)A.

title: Descending filtration of a group
description: A descending filtration is a chain of subgroups G=F⁰G⊇F¹G⊇⋯; whenever F^(i+1)G is normal in F^iG, the ith graded quotient is Gr^iG=F^iG/F^(i+1)G. For a group scheme the filtration is by subgroup schemes and the quotient is taken as a sheaf when needed.

title: Formal coordinates at the identity of a smooth group
description: For a smooth group scheme of relative dimension d over a complete local ring R, the completion along its identity section has formal coordinates T₁,…,T_d and group law F(T,U)=T+U plus terms of total degree at least2. Modulo a square-zero ideal the group law is therefore addition on its tangent space.

title: Greenberg filtration of a smooth group over a truncated DVR
description: Let 𝒢 be a smooth commutative group scheme over a DVR S with residue field k and maximal ideal 𝔪, and suppose the k-algebra S/𝔪^e is identified with k[t]/(t^e). Assume the indicated Weil restrictions are representable. In X=Res_((S/𝔪^e)/k)(𝒢_(S/𝔪^e)), let F⁰X=X and F^iX be the kernel of reduction to 𝒢 modulo t^i for1≤i≤e. Then Gr⁰X≅𝒢_k and Gr^iX≅Lie(𝒢_k)⊗_k(𝔪/𝔪²)^(⊗i) for1≤i<e, as additive vector groups.

title: Quasi-projectivity of a Néron model
description: The finite-type Néron model of an abelian variety over a discrete valuation ring is quasi-projective over that ring. This supplies the representability hypothesis for finite locally free restriction of scalars.

title: Quantile coupling for usual stochastic order
description: For probability measures mu,nu on the real line, write Q_mu(u)=inf{x:mu((−∞,x])≥u}, 0<u<1. If U is uniform on(0,1), then Q_mu(U) has law mu, and mu≤stnu if and only if Q_mu(u)≤Q_nu(u) for every0<u<1. For probability kernels on the real line the quantile can be chosen jointly measurable in the parameter and u.

title: Borel reconstruction of a càdlàg path from rational evaluations
description: For a Polish state space E, the space D([0,∞),E) of càdlàg paths with its evaluation sigma-algebra is standard Borel. Restriction to a fixed countable dense time set containing0 is measurable and injective, with Borel image and Borel inverse onto that image; right continuity recovers every evaluation.

title: Countable products of Polish spaces
description: A countable product of Polish spaces, equipped with the product topology, is Polish; its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by coordinate projections.

title: Ordered coupling of càdlàg half-line Markov paths
description: Let X,Y be time-homogeneous càdlàg Markov families on[0,∞) with transition semigroups P,Q, such that P_t(x,·)≤stQ_t(y,·) whenever x≤y and t≥0. For every x≤y there is a coupling of their whole path laws started at x,y with X_t≤Y_t for every t≥0 almost surely. In particular this holds for two ordered initial states of one stochastically monotone family, or when P is stochastically dominated by a monotone Q. This path-law assertion alone makes no claim that the coordinates are Markov or martingales in their common enlarged filtration.

title: Bound on the number of distinct polynomial roots
description: A nonzero polynomial of degreeN over a field has at mostN distinct roots in that field or any specified field extension.

title: Cyclicity of the multiplicative group of a finite field
description: For a finite field𝔽_q, its multiplicative group𝔽_q× is cyclic of orderq−1.

title: Teichmüller unit lifts in ℤ_ℓ
description: For an odd primeℓ, reduction moduloℓ gives a group isomorphism μ_(ℓ−1)(ℤ_ℓ)→𝔽_ℓ×. Thus every nonzero residuea has a unique liftτ(a)∈ℤ_ℓ withτ(a)^(ℓ−1)=1, andτ(ab)=τ(a)τ(b).

title: Elliptic building blocks from inner-twist splitting maps
description: Let f be a non-CM weight-two newform with abelian coefficient field F, whose inner twists range over Gal(F/ℚ), and suppose its Gauss-sum cocycle c(σ,τ)=g(χ_σ⁻¹)g(σχ_τ⁻¹)/g(χ_(στ)⁻¹) is the coboundary of β:Gal(F/ℚ)→F×. Over the inner-twist splitting field L, there is w_β∈End_L(A_f) whose image is an elliptic building block and whose differential line pulls back to the span of ∑_σ[g(χ_σ⁻¹)/β(σ)]σf. All elliptic building blocks arise by applying coefficient-field endomorphisms to this image.

title: Integrality of the Manin ideal
description: For a modular parametrization π:X₁^µ(N)→E of a completely defined non-CM ℚ-curve over a number field K, with q-expansion at the rational cusp of the µ_N arithmetic model, its Manin ideal c(π) is an integral O_K-ideal.

title: Cyclotomic Galois action on µ_N-level cusps
description: On the µ_N arithmetic model of X₁(N), and its quotients associated to Γ₁(N)⊆Γ⊆Γ₀(N), every cusp is defined over ℚ(ζ_N). If σ_d(ζ_N)=ζ_N^d, it sends the cusp with primitive residue pair(x,y) modulo N to the cusp represented by any primitive integer lift of(x,d⁻¹y) modulo N. The result is read as a cusp residue class, not by cancelling a nonprimitive fraction; in particular∞ is rational.

title: Lebesgue positivity of every positive-time half-line transition
description: A Markov transition semigroup on[0,∞) is positive with respect to Lebesgue measure at every positive time if P_t(x,B)>0 for every t>0, x≥0 and Borel B of positive Lebesgue measure. This is the assigned source’s total irreducibility convention, stronger than irreducibility of an occupation or resolvent kernel.

title: Geometric ergodicity from a half-line Lyapunov drift and positive transitions
description: Let a nonexplosive càdlàg weak Feller strong Markov family on[0,∞), with usual filtration, have positive transition probabilities to every Lebesgue-positive Borel set at every positive time. Suppose a continuous V≥1, k>0, b<∞ and compact C satisfy that V(X_t)−V(X₀)−∫₀ᵗ[−kV(X_s)+b1_C(X_s)]ds is a local supermartingale from every initial state. Then there is a unique invariant probability pi with pi(V)<∞ and constants D,rho>0 such that ‖P_t(x,·)−pi‖V≤D V(x)e^(−rho t) for every x,t. No equality rho=k or special explicit prefactor is asserted.

title: Transfer of continuous-time geometric Lyapunov drift to a skeleton
description: For a nonexplosive weak Feller strong Markov family on[0,∞) with positive transitions to every Lebesgue-positive Borel set at every positive time, a continuous geometric Lyapunov supermartingale drift with compact exception C implies: for a fixed skeleton spacing h>0 there are U≥1 equivalent to V, 0≤a<1, b_h<∞ and a petite set C_h for P_h with sup_(C_h)U<∞ such that P_hU≤aU+b_h1_(C_h). Equivalence means positive finite constants bound U/V above and below.

title: Weil–Châtelet group of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field F, H¹(F,E)=H¹_cont(Gal(F̄/F),E(F̄)) is its Weil–Châtelet group, using the discrete Galois module of geometric points. The abelian group law is the cocycle-class group law.

title: Tate–Shafarevich group of an elliptic curve
description: For E over a number field F, Sha(E/F)=ker[H¹(F,E)→∏_vH¹(F_v,E)], with v running over all finite and infinite places. Each localization restricts cocycles using compatible algebraic-closure embeddings and includes the geometric points into E(F̄_v); its cohomology class is independent of these choices. Finiteness is not part of the definition.

title: Surjectivity of an isogeny on geometric points
description: For an isogenyφ:E→E′ of elliptic curves over a characteristic-zero fieldF, the induced map E(F̄)→E′(F̄) is surjective.

title: Kummer exact sequence for an elliptic isogeny
description: For a characteristic-zero field F and an F-isogenyφ:E→E′, there is an exact sequence0→E′(F)/φE(F)→H¹(F,E[φ])→ker[H¹(F,E)→H¹(F,E′)]→0. The first map sendsP to the class ofσ↦σQ−Q for anyQ∈E(F̄) withφQ=P; all groups use continuous Galois cohomology.

title: Selmer group of an elliptic isogeny
description: For an isogenyφ:E→E′ over a number field F, Sel_φ(E/F) consists of classes c∈H¹(F,E[φ]) whose localization at every placev lies in the image of E′(F_v)/φE(F_v) under the local Kummer map. Forφ=[n] this is the n-Selmer group. The definition imposes local Kummer conditions, not local vanishing in H¹(F_v,E[φ]).

title: Selmer–Tate–Shafarevich exact sequence for an isogeny
description: For an isogenyφ:E→E′ over a number field F,0→E′(F)/φE(F)→Sel_φ(E/F)→Sha(E/F)[φ]→0 is exact, where Sha(E/F)[φ]=ker[Sha(E/F)→Sha(E′/F)]. Forφ=[n], the last term is the subgroup killed byn. No finiteness assumption onSha is needed.

title: Mordell–Weil rank of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F, its Mordell–Weil rank is dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_ℤE(F)), equivalently the number of infinite cyclic factors in E(F) when finite generation is known. It concerns rational points and is distinct from analytic rank defined by an L-function zero.

title: Mordell–Weil theorem for elliptic curves
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field F, E(F) is a finitely generated abelian group, hence is isomorphic to E(F)_tors⊕ℤʳ for a finite nonnegative integerr.

title: Well-posedness and smoothing of a Lipschitz reflected half-line diffusion
description: For globally Lipschitz g,sigma on[0,∞) with inf sigma>0, the reflected equation X_t=x+∫₀ᵗg(X_s)ds+∫₀ᵗsigma(X_s)dW_s+L_t, with L continuous nondecreasing increasing only at X=0, has a pathwise unique nonexplosive strong solution from every x≥0. Its laws form a continuous strong Markov family whose transition operators send bounded Borel functions to bounded continuous functions at every positive time.

title: Strong Markov piecing out at bounded-rate jumps
description: Let a nonexplosive right-continuous strong Markov process on a standard Borel state space be killed with bounded nonnegative measurable state rate r, and restarted after each killing from a measurable probability kernel K at its pre-killing state, using independent fresh copies. The resulting pieced process is nonexplosive, unique in law for these transition rules and strong Markov. If r=0 at a state the choice of K there is immaterial; bounded rates rule out finite accumulation of killing times.

title: Order of vanishing of a holomorphic function
description: For f holomorphic near z₀ and not identically zero, ord_(z₀)f is the unique integer r≥0 for which f(z)=(z−z₀)^rg(z) with g holomorphic and g(z₀)≠0. Equivalently r is the first index of a nonzero Taylor coefficient; the identically zero function has order+∞.

title: Analytic rank of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K whose Hasse–Weil L-function is holomorphic near s=1, its analytic rank is ord_(s=1)L(E/K,s). The definition is conditional on the needed continuation; it does not assert general modularity or equality with the Mordell–Weil rank.

title: Root number of an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve E/K whose completed Hasse–Weil L-function satisfies its functional equation, the global root number is the sign w(E/K)∈{±1} in Λ(E/K,s)=w(E/K)Λ(E/K,2−s). Here Λ(E/K,s)=(|Δ_K|²Norm(𝔑_K(E)))^(s/2)[(2π)^(−s)Γ(s)]^[K:ℚ]L(E/K,s); constant factors independent of s do not affect the sign.

title: Root number of a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f of primitive level N, its root number η_f is the unit-modulus complex constant in Λ(f,s)=η_fΛ(f*,2−s), where f* has conjugate Fourier coefficients and Λ(f,s)=N^(s/2)(2π)^(−s)Γ(s)L(f,s). If the coefficients of f are real, η_f is±1.

title: Relative logarithmic height on projective space
description: For [a₀:⋯:a_n]∈ℙⁿ(K), its relative logarithmic height over the number field K is h_K=∑_v log max_i|a_i|_v using normalized local multiplicative norms. The product formula makes this independent of homogeneous scaling; division by[K:ℚ] gives the absolute-height convention.

title: Relative Néron–Tate height pairing on an elliptic curve
description: Fix an elliptic curve E/K and let h_K(x(P)) be relative logarithmic projective height, with x(O)=∞. Put q_K(P)=lim_(n→∞)4^(−n)h_K(x([2ⁿ]P)). The relative Néron–Tate pairing is ⟨P,Q⟩_K=(q_K(P+Q)−q_K(P)−q_K(Q))/2; thus ⟨P,P⟩_K=q_K(P). This fixes the x-coordinate normalization and the relative, rather than degree-divided absolute, convention.

title: Regulator of an elliptic curve over a number field
description: For a ℤ-basis P₁,…,P_r of E(K)/E(K)_tors, the regulator is Reg(E/K)=det(⟨P_i,P_j⟩_K), using the specified relative Néron–Tate pairing. The rank-zero determinant is1. A basis change in GL_r(ℤ) does not alter it; torsion factors are not incorporated into this regulator.

title: Local Tamagawa number of an elliptic curve
description: For E over a nonarchimedean local field K with finite residue field k, let E⁰(K) be the points reducing into the identity component of its Néron special fiber. The local Tamagawa number is c_K=[E(K):E⁰(K)]=|Φ(k)|, where Φ is the component group. It is1 at good-reduction places.

title: Atkin–Lehner involution on X₀(N)
description: For an exact divisor Q|N with gcd(Q,N/Q)=1, the Atkin–Lehner involution w_Q on X₀(N) sends(E,C) to(E/C_Q,C′), where C_Q⊆C has order Q and C′ is generated by the kernel E[Q]/C_Q of the dual quotient isogeny and the image of the order-N/Q subgroup of C. It extends to the compact curve overℚ; for squarefreeN these involutions generate an elementary abelian2-group.

title: Local Haar measure induced by an elliptic differential
description: For E over a local field K, a nonzero invariant differential ω and a Haar measure dz on(K,+) define a translation-invariant measure |ω| on E(K): in a local analytic coordinate z with ω=a(z)dz, use |a(z)|_K dz. At a complex place the associated real2-dimensional measure is understood, and the chosen additive Haar normalization is part of the data.

title: Formal parameter and reduction kernel of a local elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curve given by a minimal integral Weierstrass model over a local field K with valuation ring R and maximal ideal𝔪, E¹(K) is the kernel of reduction at the identity. The parameter z=−x/y identifies this kernel with𝔪 carrying the formal group law, and a minimal invariant differential has expansion(1+O(z))dz. Reduction gives E⁰(K)/E¹(K)≅the nonsingular residue-curve group.

title: Néron local volume formula for an elliptic curve
description: Let E/K have a minimal integral Weierstrass model over a nonarchimedean local field with residue size q, let ω_min be a minimal invariant differential and normalize additive Haar measure by vol(O_K)=1. Then ∫_(E(K))|ω_min|=c_K/L_K(E,1), where c_K=[E(K):E⁰(K)] and L_K is the local Hasse–Weil Euler factor.

title: BSD period of an elliptic curve over a number field
description: For E/K choose a nonzero invariant differential ω and additive Haar measures dx_v whose product on𝔄_K gives vol(𝔄_K/K)=1. Its BSD period is P(E/K)=∏_(v finite)[L_v(E,1)∫_(E(K_v))|ω|_v]·∏_(v infinite)∫_(E(K_v))|ω|_v. Almost all finite factors are1; the product formula makes the result independent of ω, and the adelic normalization fixes its discriminant factor.

title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer rank conjecture over a number field
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, its Hasse–Weil L-function is conjectured to have analytic continuation to an entire function, with ord_(s=1)L(E/K,s) equal to its Mordell–Weil rank. No general continuation or rank equality is asserted by this conjecture record.

title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term conjecture over a number field
description: For E/K of Mordell–Weil rank r, the BSD conjecture asserts analytic continuation and analytic rank r, finiteness of Sha(E/K), and lim_(s→1)L(E/K,s)/(s−1)^r=P(E/K)Reg(E/K)|Sha(E/K)|/|E(K)_tors|². Here P is the adelically normalized BSD period and Reg is the relative height-pairing determinant on a torsion-free basis, with torsion kept separate.

title: Strictly positive killed transition density in a bounded interval
description: A one-dimensional diffusion on a bounded interval with Lipschitz coefficients and diffusion coefficient bounded above and away from0 has, before exit, a transition density strictly positive at every positive time between interior points. Consequently every interior Borel set of positive Lebesgue measure has positive killed transition probability from every interior starting point.

title: Weak well-posedness of two rank-based Brownian particles
description: For two real Brownian particles whose drift and positive definite covariance matrix are constant in the two rank chambers and are permuted with the particle ranks, with a fixed measurable lexicographic rule at ties, the corresponding rank-based stochastic equation has a nonexplosive weak solution unique in law.

title: Positive transitions of a Lipschitz reflected half-line diffusion
description: Let the reflected half-line diffusion have globally Lipschitz drift g and diffusion coefficient sigma with inf sigma>0. For every t>0, initial x≥0 and Borel set B⊆[0,∞) of positive Lebesgue measure, P_x(X_t∈B)>0.

title: Tanaka formula for the absolute value of a continuous semimartingale
description: For a real continuous semimartingale X, there is a continuous nonnegative nondecreasing process L^0 with L₀^0=0, increasing only when X=0, such that |X_t|=|X₀|+∫₀ᵗsgn(X_s)dX_s+L_t^0, with sgn(0)=0. This L^0 is the symmetric local time of X at0.

title: Exponential ergodicity criterion for a reflected jump-diffusion
description: Let g,sigma be globally Lipschitz on[0,∞), inf sigma>0, and destination measures nu_x be weakly continuous with bounded total mass and sup_x∫exp(lambda0|y−x|)nu_x(dy)<∞ for some lambda0>0. If for some0<lambda<lambda0, limsup_(x→∞)[lambda g(x)+lambda²sigma(x)²/2+∫(exp(lambda(y−x))−1)nu_x(dy)]<0, then the reflected jump-diffusion has a unique invariant probability pi with pi(exp(lambda x))<∞ and is exp(lambda x)-uniformly ergodic at some positive rate.

title: Reflected jump-diffusion representation of a two-rank Lévy gap
description: For two rank-based finite-activity Lévy particles driven in rank order by drift(g_plus,g_minus), positive definite Brownian covariance a and finite joint jump measure Lambda, their ranked gap Z is a reflected jump-diffusion with constant drift g_plus−g_minus, variance a_plusplus+a_minusminus−2a_plusminus, and destination measure nu_z equal to the pushforward of Lambda under (u_plus,u_minus)↦|z+u_plus−u_minus|. The two-particle system is weakly well-posed.

title: Gap ergodicity under negative effective drift for two rank-based Lévy particles
description: For the two-rank finite-activity Lévy system with positive definite Brownian covariance and joint jump measure Lambda, suppose ∫exp(lambda0(|u_plus|+|u_minus|))Lambda(du)<∞ for some lambda0>0 and g_plus−g_minus+∫(u_plus−u_minus)Lambda(du)<0. Then for some lambda>0 the ranked gap is exp(lambda z)-uniformly ergodic and its unique invariant law has finite exp(lambda z) moment.

title: Optional sampling for a nonnegative càdlàg supermartingale
description: On a usual filtration, if X is a nonnegative càdlàg supermartingale and sigma≤tau are bounded stopping times, then E[X_tau|F_sigma]≤X_sigma almost surely. No class-D assumption is needed for this bounded-time nonnegative formulation.

title: Local Doob–Meyer decomposition of a càdlàg supermartingale
description: On a usual filtration, a real càdlàg supermartingale X has a unique local decomposition X=X₀+N−A, where N is a càdlàg local martingale starting at0 and A is predictable càdlàg nondecreasing starting at0 and locally integrable. This is the local form; a uniformly integrable martingale conclusion requires the corresponding class-D/integrability hypotheses.

title: Prime-to-characteristic Tate module of a smooth commutative group
description: For a smooth commutative group scheme G of finite type over a perfect field k and a prime ℓ≠char(k), T_ℓG=lim←G[ℓⁿ](k̄) with multiplication-by-ℓ transition maps. It carries the natural Galois action; it applies to nonproper groups and disconnected special fibers as well as abelian varieties.

title: Reduction lifting for a smooth group over a henselian local ring
description: For a smooth commutative group scheme𝒢 over a henselian local ring R with residue field k, reduction𝒢(R)→𝒢(k) is surjective. For every positive integer n invertible in R, its reduction kernel is uniquely n-divisible; equivalently prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion lifts uniquely within a specified residue class.

title: Specialization of inertia-fixed Tate modules to a Néron special fiber
description: For an abelian variety A over a nonarchimedean local field K with Néron model𝒜 and residue field k of characteristic p, and ℓ≠p, reduction induces T_ℓ(A)^I_K≅T_ℓ(𝒜_k), equivariantly for the residue-field Galois group G_K/I_K. The whole special fiber may be used; its finite component group contributes no Tate module.

title: Tate rank and Chevalley decomposition of a smooth commutative group
description: For a smooth connected commutative algebraic group G over a perfect field, its maximal connected affine subgroup is an extension of a torus of dimension t by a unipotent group of dimension u, and the quotient is an abelian variety of dimension b. For ℓ different from the characteristic, T_ℓG has rank t+2b, while dim G=t+u+b. A finite component group does not change the Tate rank.

title: Properness from a proper special fiber over a DVR
description: For a smooth finite-type separated scheme X over a discrete valuation ring R with geometrically connected generic fiber, if its special fiber is nonempty and proper, then X is proper over R and its special fiber is geometrically connected.

title: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion
description: For an abelian variety A over a nonarchimedean local field K and a prime ℓ different from the residue characteristic, A has good reduction if and only if inertia acts trivially on T_ℓA. If this holds for one such ℓ it holds for every such ℓ.

title: Imaginary quadratic number field
description: An imaginary quadratic number field is a degree-two extension ofℚ with no embedding intoℝ, equivalently K=ℚ(√D) for a negative square-free integerD. A chosen embeddingK⊂ℂ fixes its complex realization.

title: Splitting of a prime in a number-field extension
description: A nonzero prime ideal𝔭 ofO_K splits completely in a finite extensionL/K if𝔭O_L is a product of[L:K] distinct prime ideals, each with residue-field degree1. In a quadratic extension this means two distinct primes of ramification index and residue degree1.

title: Heegner hypothesis for an elliptic curve over ℚ
description: For an elliptic curveE/ℚ of conductorN and an imaginary quadratic fieldK, the split-prime Heegner hypothesis says every rational prime dividingN splits completely inK. Extra exclusionsK≠ℚ(i),ℚ(√−3), when imposed to simplify unit factors, are separate hypotheses.

title: Hilbert class field of a number field
description: The Hilbert class fieldH of a number fieldK is its maximal abelian extension unramified at every finite prime and at infinity: every real place remains real. For an imaginary quadraticK the infinite-place condition is vacuous.

title: Order in an imaginary quadratic field
description: An order in an imaginary quadratic fieldK is a subringR⊆O_K containing1 and of finite index inO_K. It has the formR=ℤ+cO_K for a unique positive integerc, its conductor.

title: Proper invertible ideal class of a quadratic order
description: For an orderR in an imaginary quadratic fieldK, a proper invertible fractionalR-ideal is a rank-twoℤ-latticeI⊂K withaI⊆R for some nonzeroa∈R, multiplier ring{x∈K:xI⊆I}=R, andII′=R for another fractionalR-idealI′. Their products modulo principal idealsαR,α∈K×, formPic(R).

title: Ring class field of an imaginary quadratic order
description: ForR=ℤ+cO_K in an imaginary quadratic fieldK, the ring class fieldH_c/K is the abelian class field whose Artin map identifiesPic(R) withGal(H_c/K): at primes𝔭 ofO_K prime toc, the class of𝔭∩R maps to arithmeticFrobenius. H₁ is the Hilbert class field; H_c is generally smaller than the full ray class field of modulusc.

title: Galois trace of a point on an elliptic curve
description: For a finite Galois extensionL/K and an elliptic curveE/K, the point trace is Tr_(L/K)(P)=∑_(σ∈Gal(L/K))σP∈E(K) forP∈E(L), with addition inE. It is a group homomorphism and is distinct from the field trace of point coordinates.

title: Heegner CM point on X₀(N)
description: LetK⊂ℂ be imaginary quadratic with ringO_K and let𝔫⊂O_K satisfyO_K/𝔫≅ℤ/Nℤ. The cyclicN-isogenyℂ/O_K→ℂ/𝔫⁻¹ defines a Heegner CM pointx onX₀(N)(ℂ); equivalently both endpoint elliptic curves have complex multiplication byO_K. The ideal and embedding are part of the chosen construction.

title: Field of definition of a Heegner CM point
description: Under the split-prime Heegner hypothesis for levelN and imaginary quadraticK, a Heegner CM pointx onX₀(N) constructed from an ideal𝔫 ofO_K withO_K/𝔫≅ℤ/Nℤ is rational over the Hilbert class fieldH ofK.

title: Heegner point on a parametrized elliptic curve
description: Fix E/ℚ, a modular parametrizationπ:X₀(N)→E withπ(∞)=O, and a Heegner CM pointx∈X₀(N)(H) for an imaginary quadraticK satisfying the Heegner hypothesis, whereH is its Hilbert class field. The associated Heegner point is y_K=Tr_(H/K)(π(x))∈E(K). The choices are retained, and nontorsion is not part of the definition.

title: Full Mordell–Weil index of a Heegner point
description: If a Heegner pointy_K generates a finite-index subgroup ofE(K), its full index isI_K=[E(K):ℤy_K]. For rankone and nontorsiony_K, I_K=|E(K)_tors|·[E(K)/E(K)_tors:ℤȳ_K]. The full index includes torsion; if the cyclic subgroup has infinite index, no finiteI_K is assigned by this convention.

title: Weak Mordell–Weil theorem for an elliptic curve
description: For an elliptic curveE over a number fieldF and a nonzero integern, the quotientE(F)/nE(F) is finite.

title: Positivity and Northcott properties of the Néron–Tate height
description: For an elliptic curveE over a number fieldK, the relative Néron–Tate pairing is symmetric and biadditive, its diagonalq_K is nonnegative and vanishes exactly on torsion points, and for each realB the set{P∈E(K):q_K(P)≤B} is finite.

title: Coinvariant space of a group representation
description: For a linear representation ρ of a group G on a vector space V over a field F, the coinvariant space is V_G=V/span_F{ρ(g)v−v:g∈G,v∈V}. Every G-equivariant map from V to a trivial representation factors uniquely through this quotient.

title: Néron identity fiber in multiplicative elliptic reduction
description: For an elliptic curve E over a nonarchimedean local field K with residue field k, multiplicative reduction means that the identity component of its Néron special fiber is a one-dimensional k-torus. It is split precisely when the two tangent directions of the nodal minimal cubic are k-rational; otherwise the torus splits over the quadratic extension of k.

title: Tate representation at multiplicative elliptic reduction
description: Let E/K have multiplicative reduction over a nonarchimedean local field with residue cardinality q, and ℓ≠char(k). On V=T_ℓE⊗Q_ℓ, inertia is nontrivial unipotent, V^I and V_I each have dimension one, and arithmetic Frobenius acts on them by εq and ε respectively, where ε=1 for split and−1 for nonsplit reduction. Thus the local Euler polynomial on the dual invariant representation is1−εT.

title: Left Riemann-sum approximation of a semimartingale integral
description: Let H be adapted càdlàg and X a càdlàg semimartingale. For deterministic partitions of mesh tending to0 on compact intervals, the left sums ∑H_(t_i)[X_(t_(i+1)∧t)−X_(t_i∧t)] converge ucp to ∫₀ᵗH_(s−)dX_s. For an adapted left-continuous locally bounded H the limit is ∫H_s dX_s.

title: Weighted Riemann-sum approximation of quadratic covariation
description: For càdlàg semimartingales X,Y and adapted càdlàg G, the sums ∑G_(t_i)[X_(t_(i+1)∧t)−X_(t_i∧t)][Y_(t_(i+1)∧t)−Y_(t_i∧t)] along deterministic partitions of mesh tending to0 converge ucp to ∫₀ᵗG_(s−)d[X,Y]_s.

title: Fundamental quadratic discriminant
description: A nonzero integer D≠1 is a fundamental discriminant if D is squarefree and D≡1 mod4, or D=4d with d squarefree and d≡2 or3 mod4. These are exactly the discriminants of quadratic number fields.

title: Kronecker symbol with positive denominator
description: For an integer a and a positive integer n=2^e∏p^e_p with odd primes p, put(a/n)=(a/2)^e∏(a/p)^e_p, with empty product1. Here(a/p) is the Legendre symbol and(a/2)=0 for even a and(−1)^((a²−1)/8) for odd a. This convention suffices for the quadratic characters attached to discriminants.

title: Quadratic reciprocity with supplementary laws
description: For distinct odd primes p,q, (p/q)(q/p)=(−1)^((p−1)(q−1)/4). For any odd prime p, (−1/p)=(−1)^((p−1)/2) and(2/p)=(−1)^((p²−1)/8).

title: Unit groups modulo prime powers
description: For an odd prime p and a≥1, (Z/p^aZ)× is cyclic of order p^(a−1)(p−1). For a≥3, (Z/2^aZ)× is the direct product generated by−1 of order2 and5 of order2^(a−2); the cases a=1,2 have orders1,2.

title: Primitive quadratic character of a fundamental discriminant
description: For a fundamental discriminant D, χ_D(n)=(D/n) for positive n extends periodically modulo|D| to a primitive real Dirichlet character on Z, with χ_D(−1)=sign(D). Conversely every primitive real Dirichlet character of modulus≥2 is obtained uniquely in this way.

title: Evaluation of the complete quadratic Gauss sum
description: For a positive integer N, ∑_(a modN)exp(2πia²/N) is(1+i)√N if N≡0 mod4, √N if N≡1 mod4,0 if N≡2 mod4, and i√N if N≡3 mod4, with positive real square roots.

title: Gauss sum of a primitive quadratic character
description: For a fundamental discriminant D and χ_D, ∑_(a mod|D|)χ_D(a)exp(2πina/|D|)=χ_D(n)√D for every positive n, where√D is the positive real square root when D>0 and i√|D| when D<0. In particular the Gauss sum at n=1 has this exact value.

title: Fricke operator on weight-two cusp forms
description: For f∈S₂(Γ₁(N)), put(W_Nf)(z)=(Nz²)⁻¹f(−1/(Nz)). This preserves S₂(Γ₁(N)), satisfies W_N²=1, and sends the nebentypusχ subspace to the nebentypusχ̄ subspace; it need not preserve an individual complex-character eigenspace.

title: Polynomial growth of cusp-form Fourier coefficients
description: For a holomorphic cusp form f(z)=∑_(n≥1)a_ne^(2πinz) of integral weight k≥2 on Γ₁(N), one has|a_n|≪_f n^(k/2). In particular its Dirichlet series converges absolutely in a right half-plane.

title: Mellin formula for a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f of level N, Λ(f,s)=N^(s/2)(2π)^(-s)Γ(s)L(f,s)=N^(s/2)∫₀^∞f(it)t^(s−1)dt. The integral converges locally uniformly for all complex s and gives an entire continuation; at s=1 it gives L(f,1)=−2πi∫₀^(i∞)f(z)dz.

title: Fricke pseudoeigenvalue of a primitive newform
description: If f=∑a_nqⁿ is a normalized primitive weight-two newform of level N and f*=∑ā_nqⁿ, then W_Nf=w_f f* for some algebraic complex number w_f with|w_f|=1.

title: Functional equation of a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f of level N, its completed entire L-function Λ(f,s)=N^(s/2)(2π)^(-s)Γ(s)L(f,s) satisfies Λ(f,s)=η_fΛ(f*,2−s), where f* has conjugate Fourier coefficients, η_f is algebraic with|η_f|=1, and η_f=−w_f in the convention W_Nf=w_ff*. If all coefficients are real thenη_f∈{±1}.

title: Upper incomplete gamma function
description: For x>0 and s∈C, Γ(s,x)=∫_x^∞e^(−t)t^(s−1)dt, with the real logarithm used for powers of t. This is entire in s and is defined at all s even where the ordinary gamma function has poles.

title: Smoothed approximate functional equation for a weight-two newform
description: Let f=∑a_nqⁿ be a normalized weight-two newform of level N, with functional-equation factorη_f, and put b_n=2πn/√N. Then Λ(f,s)=∑_(n≥1)a_nb_n^(−s)Γ(s,b_n)+η_f∑_(n≥1)ā_nb_n^(s−2)Γ(2−s,b_n). Both series and all s-derivatives converge locally uniformly, giving exponentially convergent evaluations of values and derivatives from coefficients andη_f.

title: Rational point of a scheme
description: For a k-scheme X and a field extension L/k, an L-rational point of X is a morphism Spec L→X over Spec k. The set of these morphisms is denoted X(L); this includes k-rational points when L=k.

title: Genus of a smooth projective curve
description: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over a field k, its genus is g(C)=dim_k H⁰(C,Ω¹_(C/k)), the dimension of the space of global regular differential one-forms. This is the geometric genus convention.

title: Riemann–Hurwitz formula in characteristic zero
description: For a finite nonconstant morphism f:Y→X of smooth projective geometrically connected curves over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, let d be its degree and e_P the order of vanishing at P of the pullback of a local parameter at f(P). Then 2g(Y)−2=d(2g(X)−2)+∑_P(e_P−1).

title: Genus of a prime-level modular curve X₀(p)
description: For a prime p>3, the genus of X₀(p) is n−1 if p=12n+1, n if p=12n+5 or p=12n+7, and n+1 if p=12n+11. In particular X₀(11) and X₀(17) have genus one, and for p>17 with p≡2 mod3 it has genus at least two.

title: Good reduction of a smooth projective curve
description: A smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over a number field K has good reduction at a finite place v if it is the generic fiber of a proper smooth scheme over the discrete valuation ring O_(K,v), with geometrically connected one-dimensional fibers. Good reduction outside S means this holds at every finite place not in S.

title: Shafarevich finiteness for curves of fixed genus
description: For a number field K, a finite set S of finite places, and an integer g≥2, there are only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g with good reduction outside S.

title: Kodaira–Parshin covers associated to rational points
description: Let C/K be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field. There exist a finite extension L/K, a finite set S of finite places of L, and a bound G, all independent of P∈C(K), such that each P has a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C_P/L of genus at most G, with good reduction outside S, and a finite nonconstant map C_P→C_L branched exactly over P.

title: De Franchis finiteness in characteristic zero
description: For fixed smooth projective geometrically connected curves D and C over a characteristic-zero field k with g(C)≥2, there are only finitely many nonconstant k-morphisms D→C. The characteristic-zero qualification excludes the infinite Frobenius iterates possible in positive characteristic.

title: Faltings’s finiteness theorem for rational points
description: If C is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field K, then C(K) is finite.

title: J-invariant of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero
description: For E:y²=x³+Ax+B in characteristic zero, j(E)=1728·4A³/(4A³+27B²). It is unchanged under isomorphisms preserving the origin; over an algebraic closure, two elliptic curves are isomorphic exactly when their j-invariants agree.

title: Isomorphism between short Weierstrass models
description: In characteristic zero, an isomorphism preserving infinity from y²=x³+Ax+B to y²=x³+A′x+B′ is of the form (x,y)↦(u²x,u³y), where u≠0, A′=u⁴A and B′=u⁶B. Conversely these conditions give such an isomorphism.

title: Geometric automorphism group of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero
description: For an elliptic curve E in characteristic zero, its origin-preserving automorphism group over an algebraic closure is cyclic of order2 if j(E)∉{0,1728}, order4 if j(E)=1728, and order6 if j(E)=0. In a short Weierstrass model it consists of (x,y)↦(u²x,u³y) with u⁴A=A and u⁶B=B.

title: Finiteness of fixed-field exceptional elliptic cohomology cases
description: Fix a number field F and a prime p>17 with F∩ℚ(μ_p)=ℚ. There are only finitely many F-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves E/F for which H¹(Gal(F(E[p])/F),E[p]) is nonzero.

title: C^k map between Euclidean open sets
description: For a finite integer k≥0, a map between open Euclidean sets is C^k if all component partial derivatives of total order at most k exist and are continuous; order zero is the component itself, so C^0 means continuous. A map is C^∞ when it is C^k for every finite k.

title: Galois character attached to a Dirichlet character
description: For a Dirichlet characterχ modulo N and a fixed embedding of its values intoQ̄_ℓ, the associated Galois character sendsσ∈G_Q toχ(a_σ), whereσ(ζ_N)=ζ_N^(a_σ). Its value at arithmetic Frobenius atp∤Nℓ isχ(p).

title: Tate component of a weight-two newform
description: For a weight-two newform f with coefficient field F and modular abelian variety A_f, and a primeλ|ℓ of F, define V_(f,λ)=V_ℓ(A_f)⊗_(F⊗Q_ℓ)F_λ using the λ-factor projection. The commuting F-action makes this a continuous F_λ-linear G_Q-representation, denotedρ_(f,λ).

title: Good-prime Frobenius polynomial of a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f with nebentypusχ and λ|ℓ, its two-dimensional λ-adic representation is unramified atp∤Nℓ and has arithmetic-Frobenius characteristic polynomial X²−a_pX+χ(p)p.

title: Chebotarev density of Frobenius conjugacy classes
description: For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields, each conjugacy class C⊂Gal(L/K) occurs as the Frobenius class of unramified prime ideals of K with Dirichlet density |C|/|Gal(L/K)|. In particular every finite-quotient conjugacy class occurs at infinitely many primes outside any finite excluded set.

title: Determinant of the Tate representation of a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f of level N and nebentypusχ, V_(f,λ) has dimension two over F_λ and detρ_(f,λ)=χ·χ_ℓ as characters of G_Q, whereχ is viewed as a Galois character andχ_ℓ is the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character. This character identity applies on every decomposition group, including primes dividing N.

title: Full Atkin–Lehner quotient of a modular curve
description: For squarefree N, let W(N) be the finite group generated by all Atkin–Lehner involutions w_Q on X₀(N). The quotient X*(N)=X₀(N)/W(N) is the smooth projective curve overQ whose function field isQ(X₀(N))^W(N); its noncuspidal open is denotedY*(N).

title: Geometric fibers of a finite group quotient of a curve
description: For a finite group G acting by automorphisms on a smooth projective curve C over a characteristic-zero field k, the smooth projective curve with function field k(C)^G is its finite quotient C/G; each geometric fiber of C→C/G is exactly one G-orbit.

title: Q-curves from rational Atkin–Lehner quotient points
description: For squarefree N and P∈Y*(N)(Q), every geometric lift of P toY₀(N) represents an elliptic curve geometrically isogenous to all its Galois conjugates, hence aQ-curve. All curves represented by this fiber are geometrically isogenous. This asserts the forward construction, not the converse classification of allQ-curves.

title: Twisting criterion for a completely defined quadratic Q-curve
description: LetK/Q be quadratic with a fixed liftν∈G_Q, letE/K be geometrically non-CM, and letµ:E→νE be a geometric isogeny. Writeσµ=c_σµ withc_σ∈{±1} forσ∈G_K. Forb∈K×, the twistE^b admits aK-defined isogeny toν(E^b) iff c_σ=κ_(N_K/Q b)(σ) for allσ∈G_K, whereκ_a(σ)=σ√a/√a.

title: Normalizer of a subgroup
description: For a subgroup H of a group G, its normalizer is N_G(H)={g∈G:gHg⁻¹=H}. It is a subgroup of G containing H, and H is normal in N_G(H).

title: Split Cartan subgroup of GL₂ over a finite field
description: For a finite field k, a split Cartan subgroup of GL₂(k) is the stabilizer of each of two distinct lines in k². In a basis on these lines it is the full group of invertible diagonal matrices, isomorphic to k××k×.

title: Nonsplit Cartan subgroup of GL₂ over a finite field
description: Let k₂/k be a quadratic extension of finite fields. Multiplication by k₂× on the two-dimensional k-vector space k₂ embeds it in GL₂(k). A conjugate of this subgroup is a nonsplit Cartan subgroup; it is cyclic of order |k|²−1.

title: Projective general linear group PGL₂ over a finite field
description: For a finite field k, PGL₂(k)=GL₂(k)/{aI:a∈k×}. It acts faithfully on the projective line P¹(k), by the action of matrices on one-dimensional subspaces of k².

title: Alternating group of a finite set
description: For an n-element set, the alternating group A_n is the subgroup of its symmetric group consisting of the permutations expressible as a product of an even number of transpositions. The parity of such an expression is independent of the expression.

title: Dihedral group
description: For an integer n≥2, the dihedral group D_(2n) is C_n⋊C₂, where the nonidentity element of C₂ acts on C_n by inversion. Equivalently it has generators r,s with r^n=s²=1 and srs⁻¹=r⁻¹; its order is 2n.

title: Normalizers of Cartan subgroups of GL₂ over an odd prime field
description: Let p be odd and C a split or nonsplit Cartan subgroup of GL₂(𝔽_p). Its normalizer N has [N:C]=2. In the split case N consists of diagonal and antidiagonal invertible matrices; in the nonsplit case its elements are x↦ax or x↦ax^p on 𝔽_(p²). Its image in PGL₂(𝔽_p) is dihedral of order 2(p−1) or 2(p+1), respectively.

title: Prime-to-p finite subgroups of PGL₂ over a prime field
description: Let p be prime and H⊆PGL₂(𝔽_p) have order coprime to p. Then H is cyclic, dihedral, or isomorphic to A₄, S₄ or A₅. The alternatives need not all occur over a given prime field.

title: Subgroup classification of GL₂ over a prime field
description: For a prime p>3 and G⊆GL₂(𝔽_p), at least one holds: G contains SL₂(𝔽_p); G stabilizes a line in 𝔽_p²; G is contained in the normalizer of a split or nonsplit Cartan subgroup; or its projective image is isomorphic to A₄, S₄ or A₅.

title: Direct product of groups
description: For groups G and H, the direct product G×H has underlying Cartesian product and multiplication (g,h)(g′,h′)=(gg′,hh′). Its identity and inverse are taken componentwise.

title: Mazur’s theorem on rational isogenies of prime degree
description: If an elliptic curve over ℚ admits an isogeny over ℚ of prime degree p, then p∈{2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,43,67,163}. Conversely each listed prime occurs for some elliptic curve over ℚ.

title: Mazur’s theorem on rational elliptic torsion
description: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ, its torsion subgroup E(ℚ)_tors is isomorphic either to ℤ/nℤ with 1≤n≤10 or n=12, or to ℤ/2ℤ×ℤ/(2m)ℤ with 1≤m≤4. Each of these fifteen groups occurs.

title: Manin constant of an X₀ modular parametrization
description: For E/Q of conductor N, let f be its normalized weight-two newform andπ:X₀(N)→E a modular parametrization. For a global minimal invariant differentialω_E, the nonzero rational number c(π) is defined byπ*ω_E=c(π)f(q)dq/q. Changing the sign ofω_E changes the sign ofc(π); its absolute value is the unsigned Manin constant.

title: Integral q-expansions of Néron differentials on a modular Jacobian
description: For the Néron model overZ of J₁(N), the q-expansion map at its rational Tate cusp sends invariant integral differentials intoZ[[q]]dq/q. Pullbacks of integral Néron differentials along homomorphisms J₁(N)→J₀(N)→A have integral q-expansions as well.

title: Integrality of the X₀ Manin constant
description: For a modular parametrizationπ:X₀(N)→E/Q at the conductor level and a global minimal differentialω_E, the signed Manin constant c(π) is a nonzero integer. In particular the unsigned constant of the optimal quotient is a positive integer.

title: Manin conjecture for an optimal X₀ elliptic quotient
description: For an optimal modular parametrizationX₀(N)→E/Q at the conductor level, the unsigned Manin constant is1, or equivalently the signed constant attached to a chosen minimal differential is±1. This is a conjecture, not asserted by its definition or by integrality.

title: Kato critical-value Selmer finiteness for a weight-two newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f with L(f,1)≠0 and each finite prime λ of its coefficient field, the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of every G_ℚ-stable O_λ-lattice T in the Tate component V_(f,λ) is finite. In Kato’s normalization V_(f,λ) is the critical Tate twist V(f)(1) of his cohomological realization, up to replacing f by its complex-conjugate newform; the local condition above λ is the Bloch–Kato crystalline condition, not an unrestricted H¹ condition.

title: Kummer exact sequence for the primary Selmer group of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K and a primeℓ, define Sel_(ℓ∞)(A/K)=ker[H¹(K,A[ℓ∞])→∏_vH¹(K_v,A)]. There is an exact sequence0→A(K)⊗(Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)→Sel_(ℓ∞)(A/K)→Sha(A/K)[ℓ∞]→0.

title: Bloch–Kato comparison for abelian-variety Selmer groups
description: For an abelian variety over a number field, the Bloch–Kato finite local conditions on its rational Tate realization agree with the rationalized local Kummer conditions. In particular decomposing a modular abelian Tate realization into newform critical realizations decomposes its rational Selmer group; finite lattice discrepancies do not affect finiteness of the primary Selmer group.

title: Mordell–Weil finite generation for an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K, the abelian group A(K) is finitely generated. This is the arbitrary-dimensional theorem, extending the elliptic-curve case.

title: Kato rank-zero criterion for a modular abelian quotient
description: Let A/Q be an abelian variety admitting a surjective homomorphism J₁(N)→A for some N. If L(A/Q,1)≠0, then A(Q) is finite. The assertion is a theorem and does not assume the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture.

title: Perron splitting of a uniformly positive matrix cocycle
description: Let θ be a homeomorphism of compact metric Ω and A:Ω→M_d(ℝ) continuous and nonnegative. Suppose some s≥1 makes A^(s)(ω)=A(θ^(s−1)ω)⋯A(ω) strictly positive for every ω. There are continuous positive unit vectors u(ω),v(ω) such that A(ω)u(ω) is a positive multiple of u(θω), A(ω)ker(v(ω)ᵀ)⊆ker(v(θω)ᵀ), and ℝᵈ=ℝu(ω)⊕ker(v(ω)ᵀ). Some C>0,0<α<1 give ‖A^(n)(ω)b‖≤Cαⁿ‖A^(n)(ω)u(ω)‖ for every unit b⊥v(ω), uniformly in ω and n≥0.

title: Schauder–Tychonoff fixed-point theorem
description: Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a Hausdorff locally convex real topological vector space has a fixed point.

title: Continuity of a uniform limit
description: A uniform limit of continuous maps from a topological space to a metric space is continuous.

title: Common growth exponent for a stationary uniformly positive matrix product
description: Let (Ω,θ,Q) be an ergodic probability-preserving compact metric system with θ a homeomorphism. Let A:Ω→M_d(ℝ) be continuous and nonnegative, with one fixed-length product A^(s)(ω)=A(θ^(s−1)ω)⋯A(ω) strictly positive for every ω. There is a finite deterministic r such that n⁻¹log‖A^(n)(ω)‖→r and n⁻¹log‖A^(n)(ω)z‖→r for Q-almost every ω and every nonzero z∈ℝ_+ᵈ.

title: Shafarevich finiteness for elliptic curves
description: For a number field K and a finite set S of its finite places, only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves have good reduction at every place outsideS.

title: Finiteness of an elliptic isogeny class over a number field
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves are K-isogenous toE.

title: Billerey effective bound for prime isogenies
