description: For a geometrically non-CM elliptic curve E over a number field K, Billerey’s explicit resultant criterion computes a finite set S of rational primes containing everyp for which E admits aK-defined cyclicp-isogeny. Searching the good-prime-ideal resultants terminates because infinitely many of them are nonzero; exceptional primes dividing6disc(K)Norm(Δ) are included separately.

title: Division polynomials of an elliptic curve
description: Fix a characteristic-zero Weierstrass equation y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆. Its division polynomials have ψ₀=0; for odd n≥1, ψ_n=n∏_(P∈(E[n]∖{O})/{±1})(x−x(P)); for even n≥2, ψ_n=(n/2)(2y+a₁x+a₃)∏_(P∈(E[n]∖E[2])/{±1})(x−x(P)). The products give polynomials over the base field; their zeros encode the indicated torsion points in these fixed coordinates.

title: Vélu quotient by a finite elliptic subgroup
description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field K and a finite G_K-stable subgroup C⊂E(K̄), the quotient isogeny E→E/C is defined overK. Vélu’s finite-sum formulas compute a Weierstrass equation and the isogeny rational functions from the coordinates ofC.

title: Effective prime-isogeny enumeration over a number field
description: For a geometrically non-CM elliptic curve E/K over a number field, an algorithm determines every rational primep admitting aK-defined cyclicp-isogeny fromE and computes all such isogenies up to targetK-isomorphism.

title: Isogeny graph of a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field
description: For a geometrically non-CM elliptic curve E/K, its K-isogeny graph has vertices the K-isomorphism classes K-isogenous toE and an edge labeledp between two vertices when there is aK-defined cyclic isogeny of prime degreep between them. Dual isogenies make the edges undirected; the graph is finite and connected, and traversing prime-degree isogenies enumerates its vertices.

title: Dirichlet density of a set of prime ideals
description: For a set T of nonzero prime ideals in a number field K, its Dirichlet density is lim_(s→1+) (∑_(p∈T)N(p)^(−s))/log(1/(s−1)), when this limit exists. Changing finitely many primes does not change this density.

title: Conjugacy class in a group
description: For an element g of a group G, its conjugacy class is {hgh⁻¹:h∈G}. The conjugacy classes partition G.

title: Centralizer of a group element
description: For g∈G, its centralizer is C_G(g)={h∈G:hg=gh}, a subgroup. Conjugation identifies the cosets G/C_G(g) as a set with the conjugacy class of g.

title: Frobenius Dirichlet density in abelian extensions
description: For a finite abelian extension L/K of number fields with Galois group G and σ∈G, the unramified prime ideals of K whose Frobenius equals σ have Dirichlet density 1/|G|.

title: Zero Dirichlet density of primes of higher relative residue degree
description: For a finite extension M/K of number fields, the prime ideals q of M with residue degree [O_M/q:O_K/(q∩O_K)]>1 have Dirichlet density zero as primes of M.

title: Signature of a number field
description: The signature (r₁,r₂) of a number field K consists of the number r₁ of embeddings K→ℝ and half the number of nonreal embeddings K→ℂ, counted in complex-conjugate pairs. Thus [K:ℚ]=r₁+2r₂.

title: Unit group of the ring of integers of a number field
description: For a number field K, its unit group O_K× consists of the u∈O_K for which u⁻¹ also lies in O_K, with multiplication. Its torsion elements are exactly the roots of unity in K.

title: Logarithmic embedding of number-field units
description: Choose the real embeddings σ₁,…,σ_(r₁) and one from each conjugate pair σ_(r₁+1),…,σ_(r₁+r₂) of K. The logarithmic map sends u∈O_K× to (log|σ_i(u)|)_i∈ℝ^(r₁+r₂); its image lies in ∑_(i≤r₁)x_i+2∑_(i>r₁)x_i=0. Complex coordinates here have unweighted logarithms, with weight2 in the hyperplane.

title: Minkowski’s convex-body theorem
description: Let Λ⊂ℝⁿ be a full lattice with covolume d. Any convex body symmetric about the origin and of volume greater than 2ⁿd contains a nonzero point of Λ.

title: Minkowski embedding of the ring of integers as a lattice
description: For a number field K of signature (r₁,r₂), its embedding into ℝ^(r₁)×ℂ^(r₂), using all real and one of each conjugate pair of complex embeddings, identifies O_K with a full lattice in this real vector space. In real/imaginary coordinates its covolume is 2^(−r₂)√N(d_(K/ℚ)), using the norm of the relative discriminant ideal.

title: Finiteness of integral ideals of bounded norm
description: For a number field K and a real bound B, only finitely many nonzero integral ideals a⊂O_K have absolute norm N(a)≤B.

title: Finiteness of algebraic integers with bounded degree and conjugates
description: Given an integer d≥1 and a real B>0, only finitely many algebraic integers α have degree at most d over ℚ and every complex conjugate of absolute value at most B.

title: Structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups
description: A finitely generated abelian group A is isomorphic to A_tors×ℤʳ for a unique nonnegative integer r, where A_tors={a∈A:na=0 for some nonzero integer n} is finite. The integer r is its rank.

title: Skew product of a discrete random dynamical system
description: For a discrete random dynamical system φ over a measure-preserving map θ on Ω, the skew product is Φ(ω,x)=(θω,φ(1,ω,x)); its iterates are Φⁿ(ω,x)=(θⁿω,φ(n,ω,x)). A probability on Ω×X invariant under Φ and having environmental marginal Q is an invariant joint law; in standard Borel spaces it is equivalently Q(dω)π_ω(dx) for an invariant random probability kernel.

title: Poincaré recurrence for a probability-preserving map
description: If T preserves a probability measure μ and A is measurable, then μ-almost every point of A returns to A infinitely often.

title: Ergodic decomposition for a continuous map of a compact metric space
description: For a continuous self-map T of a compact metric space, every invariant Borel probability μ is a mixture of ergodic invariant Borel probabilities: μ=∫ν dη(ν), with ∫f dμ=∫(∫f dν)dη(ν) for every bounded Borel f. The component law is unique modulo the usual almost-everywhere convention.

title: Weighted invasion criterion for structured-population persistence
description: For a structured stochastic population map over an ergodic compact metric environmental system (Ω,θ,Q) with θ a homeomorphism, assume a compact forward-invariant population set K and continuous Aᵢ(ω,x) with fixed primitive zero patterns. Put K₀={x:some xᵢ=0}, Φ(ω,x)=(θω,(Aᵢ(ω,x)xᵢ)ᵢ), and rᵢ(μ)=∫limsup_n n⁻¹log‖Aᵢ^(n)(ω,x)‖dμ for Φ-invariant laws with marginal Q. If some pᵢ>0 give ∑ᵢpᵢrᵢ(μ)>0 at every such ergodic law supported on Ω×K₀, empirical stochastic persistence holds from every x∈K∖K₀ for Q-almost every environmental path.

title: Growth criterion for one structured population
description: Consider one structured stochastic population on a compact forward-invariant K containing0, over an ergodic compact metric environmental homeomorphism, with continuous nonnegative matrices of a fixed primitive zero pattern. Let r be the common top exponent of A(ω,0). If r>0, the population is stochastically persistent. If r<0 and A(ω,x)≤A(ω,0) entrywise for all ω,x, every positive population trajectory tends to0 for almost every environmental path.

title: Minimal polynomial criterion for an algebraic integer
description: An algebraic number is integral overZ if and only if its monic minimal polynomial overQ has integer coefficients. In degree two this is equivalent to its field trace and norm being integers.

title: Integral basis of a quadratic number field
description: Letd≠1 be a nonzero squarefree integer andF=Q(√d). ThenO_F=Z[√d] ifd≡2 or3 mod4, andO_F=Z[(1+√d)/2] ifd≡1 mod4. The squarefree assumption on the chosen radicand is essential; the same formulas with an arbitrary merely nonsquarem are not valid.

title: Denominator ideal of an element of a number field
description: Forα in a number field K, the denominator ideal isD_α={a∈O_K:aα∈O_K}. It is a nonzero integral ideal ofO_K and is the largest integral ideal whose product withα lies inO_K. This definition uses the full ring of integers rather than a chosen possibly nonmaximal order.

title: Real periods and components of a real elliptic curve
description: For E/R and a nonzero real invariant differentialω, its complex period lattice has a unique primitive positive real periodω₁ and a basisω₁,ω₂ withImω₂>0 andReω₂ either0 orω₁/2. In the first caseE(R) has two connected components and all ofE[2] is real; in the second it is connected and only one nonzero2-torsion point is real.

title: Finiteness of a nonconstant morphism of smooth projective curves
description: A nonconstant morphism between smooth projective geometrically integral curves over a field is finite and surjective.

title: Gradient approximation for a finite differentiable convex conjugate
description: Let Λ:ℝᵈ→ℝ be convex and differentiable and I=Λ*. Every x with I(x)<∞ has a sequence x_j∈∇Λ(ℝᵈ) with x_j→x and I(x_j)→I(x); for x_j=∇Λ(λ_j), I(x_j)=⟨λ_j,x_j⟩−Λ(λ_j), and x_j uniquely minimizes I(z)−⟨λ_j,z⟩.

title: Gärtner–Ellis theorem with finite differentiable limiting cumulant
description: Let μ_ε be probability laws on ℝᵈ such that Λ(λ)=lim_(ε↓0)εlog∫exp(⟨λ,z⟩/ε)dμ_ε(z) exists and is finite for every λ∈ℝᵈ. If Λ is differentiable on all ℝᵈ, then μ_ε satisfies a large-deviation principle at speed1/ε with good convex rate Λ*(z)=sup_λ(⟨λ,z⟩−Λ(λ)); good means each finite sublevel set is compact.

title: Large deviations of a scaled independent Poisson vector
description: Fix a∈ℝ_+ᵈ and let Y_ε=ε(N₁,…,N_d), with independent Nᵢ∼Poisson(aᵢ/ε). Then Y_ε satisfies a large-deviation principle at speed1/ε with good rate I_a(y)=∑ᵢ[yᵢlog(yᵢ/aᵢ)−yᵢ+aᵢ] for y∈ℝ_+ᵈ and +∞ otherwise. The conventions are 0log(0/a)=0, a=0<y gives +∞, and the a=y=0 summand is0.

title: Inner twists and the Tate centralizer of a non-CM newform
description: For a non-CM weight-two newform f with coefficient field F and a number field L, letΓ_L be the coefficient-field automorphismsσ with an inner-twist characterχ_σ trivial onG_L. Then dim_(Qℓ)End_(G_L)(V_ℓ(A_f))=[F:Q]·|Γ_L|.

title: Complex conjugation of newform coefficients
description: For a normalized newform f=∑a_nqⁿ of weight k with nebentypus ε, at every prime p not dividing the level one has ā_p=ε(p)⁻¹a_p. For a weight-two newform without complex multiplication this says that complex conjugation on the coefficient field is an inner twist with character ε⁻¹.

title: Faithfulness of the rational Tate module on abelian homomorphisms
description: For abelian varieties A,B over a characteristic-zero field k and a primeℓ, the natural map Hom_k(A,B)⊗Q_ℓ→Hom_(G_k)(V_ℓA,V_ℓB) is injective.

title: Strong multiplicity one for classical newforms
description: Two normalized primitive cuspidal newforms whose Hecke eigenvalues agree at all but finitely many primes are equal, with equal weight, level and nebentypus.

title: Inner twist and nebentypus of a quadratic Q-curve newform
description: Let E/K be a geometrically non-CM completely defined quadraticQ-curve with conjugate isogenyµ andνµµ=[m], where m is nonsquare, and let f be the associated newform with coefficient fieldF=Q(√m). Its nontrivial coefficient conjugationσ satisfiesσ(a_p)=χ_K(p)a_p atp outside the level, whereχ_K is the primitive quadratic character ofK. The nebentypus of f is trivial when m>0 and isχ_K, viewed modulo the level, when m<0.

title: The Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for the elliptic curve 121c2
description: For the elliptic curve E/ℚ given by y²+xy=x³+x²−3632x+82757, labeled 121c2 in Cremona’s tables, Sha(E/ℚ)[11]=0 and the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer rank and leading-term assertions hold.

title: Integral weight-two modular symbols
description: For a congruence subgroupΓ⊂SL₂(Z), the groupM₂(Γ) of weight-two modular symbols is generated overZ by{a,b} witha,b∈P¹(Q), modulo{a,b}+{b,c}+{c,a}=0, the relations{γa,γb}={a,b} forγ∈Γ, and torsion. The notation records oriented paths between cusps; closed-symbol combinations give integral cycles on the compact modular curve.

title: Integration pairing for weight-two modular symbols
description: For f∈S₂(Γ₁(N)), the assignment{a,b}↦∫_a^b f(z)dz defines a well-defined complex-linear integration pairing withM₂(Γ₁(N))⊗C. The integrals at cusps converge, depend only on the modular-symbol class, and are additive in both the cusp form and the symbol.

title: Compact-uniform one-step large-deviation lower bound
description: For kernels P_ε on a metric space and a finite action ρ(x,y) on an open set of starting states, the one-step lower LDP bound is compact-uniform if, for every compact K in that open set and every nonempty open ball B, liminf_(ε↓0)inf_(x∈K)[εlog P_ε(x,B)+inf_(y∈B)ρ(x,y)]≥0, with log0=−∞.

title: Transitive compact invariant set
description: A compact invariant set K of a continuous map F is transitive in the dense-orbit sense if some x∈K has {Fⁿ(x):n≥0} dense in K.

title: Localization of chain recurrence by a Morse decomposition
description: For a continuous self-map of a compact metric space with a finite Morse decomposition, every chain-recurrent point belongs to the union of the Morse sets; a δ-chain is a finite sequence with d(x_(j+1),F(x_j))<δ, and chain recurrence means having a nontrivial δ-chain from the point to itself for every δ>0.

title: Morse-attractor concentration of small-noise quasi-stationary laws
description: Let F:S→S be continuous with bounded image on closed Euclidean S, with closed absorbing S₀ and invariant S₊=S∖S₀. Let QSDs μ_ε have kernels P_ε and survivals λ_ε. Suppose a finite continuous action ρ on S₊×S vanishes exactly at y=F(x), is uniformly positive off each fixed tracking tube, and satisfies compact-uniform lower LDP bounds. Require β_δ(ε)=sup_xP_ε(x,{y:d(y,F(x))≥δ})≤e^(−c_δ/ε) eventually, and, for every c>0, some neighborhood V of S₀ satisfies inf_(x∈V∩S₊)P_ε(x,S₀)≥e^(−c/ε) eventually. If a finite Morse decomposition separates S₀ from S₊, its non-attractor Morse sets in S₊ are transitive, and μ_ε charges every neighborhood of some positive attractor, every weak QSD limit is F-invariant and supported on the positive Morse attractors; λ_ε≥1−e^(−c/ε) eventually for some c>0.

title: QSD concentration under global attraction to an absorbing boundary
description: Let F:S→S be continuous with bounded image on closed Euclidean S, preserving both closed S₀ and S₊=S∖S₀. Let P_ε be small random perturbations absorbed in S₀, with QSDs μ_ε. If dist(Fⁿ(x),S₀)→0 for every x∈S, every weak limit of μ_ε as ε↓0 is supported on S₀. No assumption λ_ε→1 or strict trapping neighborhood of the whole boundary is required.

title: Integer sublevel bound for a univariate polynomial
description: For a polynomialP∈Q[x] of degree d≥1 with leading coefficienta≠0, andM≥1, #{x∈Z:|P(x)|≤M}≤d(2(M/|a|)^(1/d)+1). In particular it isO_(a,d)(M^(1/d)), uniformly in all the other coefficients.

title: Prime-power root count with fixed leading coefficient
description: ForP∈Z[x] of degree d≥1 and leading coefficienta≠0, every primep and integerf≥0 satisfy #{x modp^f:P(x)≡0modp^f}≤d·p^(f−f/d+v_p(a)/d)≤d|a|^(1/d)p^(f−f/d). Thus the constant depends only on a,d, uniformly in p,f and the other coefficients.

title: Ideal class group of a number field
description: For a number field K, its ideal class group Cl(K) is the group of nonzero fractional ideals of O_K modulo principal fractional ideals (a), a∈K×. Its cardinality h_K is called the class number.

title: S-ideal class group of a number field
description: For a number field K and a finite set S of places containing all infinite places, Cl_S(K) is Cl(K) modulo the subgroup generated by the classes of its finite prime ideals in S. Equivalently it is the ideal class group of the ring of S-integers.

title: Maximal extension unramified outside a finite set of places
description: Fix a separable closure of a number field K and a finite set S of places containing the infinite places. The field K_S is the compositum in that closure of all finite extensions of K unramified at each finite place outside S. It is Galois over K, and G_(K,S)=Gal(K_S/K) has its profinite topology.

title: Galois cohomology unramified outside a finite set
description: For K_S/K as above and a discrete continuous G_(K,S)-module M, write Hⁱ_S(K,M)=Hⁱ(G_(K,S),M). The coefficient action factors through this quotient; for H¹ this describes global classes unramified outside S when M itself is unramified there.

title: Mod-p cyclotomic character module
description: Let p be prime and ω:G_ℚ→𝔽_p× the mod-p cyclotomic character. For an integer k, 𝔽_p(k) is the one-dimensional 𝔽_p-vector space with σ acting by ω(σ)^k. The same notation denotes its restriction to a subgroup or its induced action through Gal(ℚ(μ_p)/ℚ); exponents are taken modulo p−1.

title: Multiplicative Kummer isomorphism in Galois cohomology
description: For a number field K and an integer n≥1, the connecting map gives K×/(K×)^n≅H¹(G_K,μ_n), where μ_n is the group of nth roots of unity in a separable closure. The class of a maps to the cocycle σ↦σ(α)/α for any α with α^n=a.

title: Prime-to-residue-characteristic Kummer ramification criterion
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with normalized valuation v and let n≥1 be prime to its residue characteristic. For a∈K× and α^n=a, K(α)/K is unramified if and only if n divides v(a).

title: S-unit Kummer exact sequence
description: Let K be a number field, p an odd prime, and S a finite set of places containing the infinite places and every place above p. There is an exact sequence 0→O_(K,S)×/(O_(K,S)×)^p→H¹_S(K,μ_p)→Cl_S(K)[p]→0. Under Kummer theory the middle term consists of a∈K×/(K×)^p with v_q(a) divisible by p for every q outside S; the last map sends a to the class of the S-ideal with valuations v_q(a)/p.

title: Minkowski bound for representatives of ideal classes
description: For a number field K of degree n and signature (r₁,r₂), each ideal class contains a nonzero integral ideal a with N(a)≤(4/π)^(r₂)(n!/n^n)√N(d_(K/ℚ)), where d_(K/ℚ) is the relative discriminant ideal.

title: Permanence of a discrete population map
description: A continuous map of the nonnegative orthant is permanent if it has a compact forward-invariant absorbing set contained in the strictly positive orthant: every strictly positive initial state eventually enters that set. In particular all species eventually have one common positive lower bound independent of the initial state.

title: Compact return criterion for an absorbing set
description: Let T be a continuous self-map of a compact metric space X, V an open forward-invariant subset, and U an open set with closure U⊂V. If every forward orbit starting in V meets U, then the closure of ⋃_(n≥0)Tⁿ(closure U) is a compact subset of V absorbing every orbit in V.

title: Weighted boundary-equilibrium criterion for Lotka–Volterra permanence
description: For Fᵢ(x)=xᵢexp(bᵢ+∑ⱼAᵢⱼxⱼ), suppose there is a compact forward-invariant set absorbing all nonnegative states. If some pᵢ>0 satisfy ∑ᵢpᵢ(bᵢ+∑ⱼAᵢⱼxⱼ*)>0 at every boundary fixed point x*, then F is permanent.

title: Alternative for strict positive linear feasibility
description: For a real matrix A and real column b, exactly one holds: Ax=b for some column x with every coordinate strictly positive; or there is a real column p with Aᵀp≥0, pᵀb≤0, and at least one strict inequality among these scalar inequalities.

title: Boundary attraction without a positive Lotka–Volterra equilibrium
description: Let Fᵢ(x)=xᵢexp(bᵢ+∑ⱼAᵢⱼxⱼ) on the nonnegative orthant, with every positive forward orbit bounded. If Ax=−b has no strictly positive solution, then dist(Fⁿ(x),∂ℝ_+ᵈ)→0 for every strictly positive x.

title: Invasion rates from stationary Lotka–Volterra means
description: For a stationary ergodic compactly bounded solution of Xᵢ,t+1=Xᵢ,t exp(bᵢ+∑ⱼAᵢⱼXⱼ,t+Eᵢ,t), assume Eᵢ,t is integrable and let I be exactly its resident species. Put βᵢ=bᵢ+E[Eᵢ,t]. If A_(I,I)x̂_I=−β_I has a unique solution, with x̂ᵢ=0 off I, then the invasion growth rates are rᵢ=0 on I and rᵢ=∑_(j∈I)Aᵢⱼx̂ⱼ+βᵢ off I.

title: Persistence from a symmetric iid storage effect
description: Let Xᵢ,t+1=Xᵢ,t[Eᵢ,t+1 f(E₁,t+1X₁,t+E₂,t+1X₂,t)+s], i=1,2, with0<s<1, f positive C¹, f′<0 and f(x)→0. Let the environmental pairs be iid, exchangeable, in[e_min,M]² with e_min>0, and P(E₁≠E₂)>0. If Elog(Eᵢf(0)+s)>0, the two-species system is stochastically persistent.

title: Representation number of a positive quadratic lattice
description: For a positive definite quadratic ℤ-lattice L and an integer n, r_L(n)=|{x∈L:Q(x)=n}| counts its integral representing vectors. This count includes imprimitive vectors and is finite by positive definiteness.

title: Weighted spinor-genus representation average
description: For a positive definite quadratic ℤ-lattice L, choose representatives M of the finitely many isometry classes in its proper spinor genus. Its weighted representation average is r_spn(L)(n)=(∑_M r_M(n)/|Aut(M)|)/(∑_M 1/|Aut(M)|), where Aut(M) consists of integral isometries preserving M.

title: Ternary spinor-genus representation error bound
description: For a positive definite integral ternary quadratic lattice L and every ε>0, r_L(n)=r_spn(L)(n)+O_(L,ε)(n^(1/2−1/28+ε)) as positive integers n tend to infinity, with no congruence conditions on representing vectors.

title: Lower bound for a primitive ternary spinor-genus average
description: For a positive definite integral ternary quadratic lattice L and every ε>0, r_spn(L)(n)≥c_(L,ε)n^(1/2−ε) for sufficiently large positive integers n primitively represented by some lattice in the spinor genus of L, with c_(L,ε)>0. The constant is not claimed effective.

title: Duke–Schulze-Pillot ternary spinor-genus representation theorem
description: For a positive definite integral ternary quadratic ℤ-lattice L, every sufficiently large positive integer n that is primitively represented by some lattice in its proper spinor genus is represented by L itself. The conclusion asserts integral representation and does not require that L’s representing vector be primitive.

title: Adjugate identity and matrix inverse
description: For a square matrix A over a commutative ring, its adjugate is the transpose of its cofactor matrix and satisfies A adj(A)=adj(A)A=(det A)I. Over a field, det A≠0 therefore gives A⁻¹=adj(A)/det A.

title: Nonstationary phase with a smooth compact amplitude
description: Let w∈C_c^∞(Rⁿ) and let real smooth phases φ_Λ on a neighborhood of its support satisfy |∇φ_Λ|≥cΛ and |∂^αφ_Λ|≤C_αΛ for all |α|≥1, with fixed positive c and fixed constants C_α. For Λ≥1 and every M≥1, ∫w(x)exp(iφ_Λ(x))dx=O_M(Λ^(−M)).

title: Van der Corput second derivative integral test
description: If f is real C² on a bounded interval [a,b] and |f″(x)|≥Λ>0 throughout it, then |∫_a^b exp(if(x))dx|≤CΛ^(−1/2) for an absolute constant C. No monotonicity of f′ is an additional hypothesis.

title: Quadratic oscillatory integral bounds
description: Let A be a real symmetric n×n matrix with eigenvalues ρ_j, w∈C_c^∞(Rⁿ) supported in [−1,1]ⁿ, and I(A,λ)=∫exp(2πi(xᵀAx−λ·x))w(x)dx. Uniformly in A and λ, |I(A,λ)|≤C_w∏_j min(1,|ρ_j|^(−1/2)), with a zero-eigenvalue factor interpreted as one. If |λ|≥max(1,4√n‖A‖op), then |I(A,λ)|≤C_(M,w)|λ|^(−M) for every M≥1.

title: Unimodular integer matrix
description: A square matrix with integer entries is unimodular if its determinant is 1 or −1; equivalently it has an inverse with integer entries.

title: Smith diagonalization of an integer matrix
description: For every m×n integer matrix A there are unimodular integer matrices U,V such that UAV is rectangular diagonal, with positive nonzero entries d₁,…,d_r satisfying d₁|d₂|⋯|d_r, followed by zeros. The number r is the rank of A over Q.

title: Prime-power solution bound for integer linear congruences
description: Let A be an m×n integer matrix of rank r≥1 over Q, b∈Z^m, p a prime and e≥1. If δ is the least p-adic valuation among the nonzero r×r minors of A, then #{x mod p^e:Ax≡b mod p^e}≤p^min(ne,(n−r)e+δ).

title: Thompson metric on the strictly positive orthant
description: For x,y∈(0,∞)ᵈ, the Thompson part metric is d_T(x,y)=max_i|log(x_i/y_i)|, equivalently inf{log a:a≥1,a⁻¹y≤x≤ay} with coordinatewise inequalities.

title: Nonuniform strong unstable manifold for random smooth maps
description: Let an invertible ergodic base drive C² maps fixing0, with tempered local C² bounds. Suppose the derivative cocycle has an Oseledets splitting with tempered projections, a simple top exponent λ₁>max(0,λ₂), and tempered inverses on its top line. For max(0,λ₂)<a<λ₁ there is a measurable local strong unstable curve tangent to the top line; its points have unique local backward orbits bounded by C(ω)e^(−an), within the tempered local neighborhoods.

title: Positive stationary statistics for spatial Beverton–Holt dynamics
description: Let D be a fixed primitive nonnegative d×d matrix with Dᵀ stochastic (so D is column-stochastic), c_j>0, and E_t a stationary ergodic sequence in[a,b]ᵈ with0<a≤b<∞. For X_i,t+1=∑_jD_ijE_j,t+1X_j,t/(1+c_jX_j,t), let r be the top exponent of D diag(E_t). If r>0, on the full two-sided environmental path space there is a unique strictly positive random equilibrium X*, and every nonzero nonnegative deterministic initial state has laws converging weakly to m=law(X*) and empirical state measures converging weakly to m almost surely.

title: Lyapunov continuity at uniformly supported nonnegative cocycles
description: Let an ergodic homeomorphism of compact metric Ω preserve Q. Let A:Ω→M_d(ℝ) be continuous and nonnegative, with a fixed zero pattern and no zero rows. Then the top exponent γ(B) of continuous nonnegative cocycles is continuous at A in uniform matrix norm, even when A is reducible. In particular, this applies at a positive diagonal cocycle and to primitive cocycles with fixed positive entry pattern.

title: Nakayama determinant trick
description: If M is a finitely generated module over a commutative ring R and I is an ideal with IM=M, then some a∈I satisfies (1−a)M=0. In particular M=0 when I is contained in the Jacobson radical of R.

title: Projective elimination and closed projection
description: Let k be algebraically closed. For finitely many polynomials f_i(t₁,…,t_m;x₀,…,x_N) homogeneous in x, the set of parameters t for which the f_i(t;x) have a common nonzero x is Zariski closed in A^m_k. Equivalently the projection A^m_k×P^N_k→A^m_k takes closed algebraic subsets to closed subsets.

title: Toric dual discriminant character formula
description: For a smooth projective toric embedding X_A over an algebraically closed field, with lattice polytope Q and dual hypersurface equation Δ_A, let µ be the generic degree of its conormal projection. The torus character of Δ_A is (1/µ)Σ_(facesΓ⊆Q)(−1)^codimΓ(dimΓ+1)∫_Γu dµ_Γ(u), where each face measure assigns volume one to a lattice unit simplex. In characteristic zero µ=1.

title: Generic singular complete intersection has one ordinary double point
description: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, for1≤c≤N and homogeneous degrees d_i≥2, a general tuple in the discriminant locus of c equations in P^N cuts out a codimension-c intersection with exactly one singular point, an ordinary double point; its gradients have exactly one relation there.

title: Discriminant of equal-degree complete intersections
description: For1≤c≤N and d≥2, there is a primitive integer polynomial Δ in the coefficients of c degree-d forms in N+1 variables, unique up to sign, whose specialization over every field of characteristic different from two is absolutely irreducible and vanishes exactly when the forms fail to cut out a smooth codimension-c projective intersection geometrically. Its degree in each form’s coefficients is binom(N+1,c)d^(c−1)(d−1)^(N−c+1), hence its total degree is c times this number.

title: Degree formula for factorization of a number-field prime
description: If L/K is a finite extension of number fields and pO_L=∏_i P_i^(e_i) for a nonzero prime ideal p⊂O_K, put f_i=[O_L/P_i:O_K/p]. Then ∑_i e_i f_i=[L:K].

title: Discriminant index formula for number-field orders
description: For a number field K and a subring A⊂O_K containing1 and of finite index, the trace discriminants satisfy disc(A/ℤ)=[O_K:A]² d_K, where d_K is the integral-basis field discriminant. The discriminant of A is computed using any ℤ-basis of A.

title: Ramification criterion from the relative discriminant
description: For a finite extension L/K of number fields, a nonzero prime ideal p of O_K divides the relative discriminant d_(L/K) if and only if at least one prime of L above p has ramification index greater than1.

title: Integers and ramification in a prime-power cyclotomic field
description: Let p be prime, r≥1 and ζ a primitive p^rth root of unity. For K=ℚ(ζ), [K:ℚ]=p^(r−1)(p−1), O_K=ℤ[ζ], and λ=1−ζ generates the unique prime above p, with (p)=(λ)^(p^(r−1)(p−1)) and O_K/(λ)≅𝔽_p. Every prime other than p is unramified in K.

title: Kummer’s Bernoulli criterion for a regular prime
description: For an odd prime p, p does not divide the class number of ℚ(ζ_p) if and only if p divides none of the numerators of B₂,B₄,…,B_(p−3), written in lowest terms. Such a prime is called regular.

title: Cyclotomic unramified Kummer cohomology at a regular prime
description: Let p be odd, K=ℚ(ζ_p), Γ=Gal(K/ℚ), and S the infinite places and the unique prime above p. If p∤h_K, then, for the natural Γ-action, H¹_S(K,μ_p)≅𝔽_p(1)⊕⊕_(i=0)^((p−3)/2)𝔽_p(2i), where Γ acts on 𝔽_p(k) by its cyclotomic character to the kth power.

title: Periodic orbit of a discrete map
description: A point x of a self-map F is periodic of least period p≥1 if Fᵖ(x)=x and Fʲ(x)≠x for1≤j<p; its periodic orbit is {x,F(x),…,F^(p−1)(x)}.

title: Hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit of an interval map
description: For a C¹ interval map F, a periodic orbit of least period p is hyperbolic attracting if |(Fᵖ)′(x)|<1 at one, equivalently every, point x of that orbit.

title: Uniformly expanding invariant set of an interval map
description: For a C¹ interval map F, a compact invariant set K is uniformly expanding if some C>0 and λ>1 satisfy |(Fⁿ)′(x)|≥Cλⁿ for every x∈K and n≥1.

title: Density of hyperbolicity in a regular analytic unimodal family
description: Let f_λ be a nontrivial real-analytic family of analytic interval maps with one nondegenerate turning critical point. Assume regularity: the critical omega-limit contains no neutral periodic orbit unless it equals that orbit. Nontrivial means some two members have different ordered critical-orbit itineraries. Then parameters whose maps have finitely many hyperbolic periodic attractors and uniformly expanding complement of their basins are dense in the parameter domain.

title: Singer’s attracting-cycle theorem for negative Schwarzian maps
description: For a C³ interval map with negative Schwarzian derivative wherever its derivative is nonzero, the immediate basin of each attracting periodic orbit contains a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

title: Finite Morse decomposition of a hyperbolic interval map
description: For a C³ interval map with finitely many nonflat critical points whose nonwandering dynamics is hyperbolic, the attracting periodic orbits and the transitive expanding basic components of the remaining nonwandering set form a finite Morse decomposition.

title: Openness of hyperbolicity for interval maps
description: If a smooth interval map has finitely many hyperbolic periodic attractors and a uniformly expanding complement of their basins, every sufficiently close smooth map in the C1 topology has the same hyperbolicity property.

title: Open dense Ricker parameters with a hyperbolic Morse decomposition
description: For an open dense set of r>0, F_r(x)=x exp(r(1−x)) has a unique hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit in(0,∞), and on its compact global invariant set it admits a finite Morse decomposition consisting of that orbit, {0}, and transitive uniformly expanding invariant sets in(0,∞).

title: Grothendieck–Lefschetz finite-field trace formula
description: For a separated finite-type scheme X over F_q and a prime ℓ∤q, #X(F_(q^a))=Σ_i(−1)^i Tr(Frob_q^a|H_c^i(X_overlineFq,Q_ℓ)) for every a≥1, where Frob_q is geometric Frobenius and the finite-dimensional compactly supported cohomology vanishes outside0≤i≤2dimX.

title: Deligne weight bound for compactly supported cohomology
description: For a separated finite-type scheme X over F_q and ℓ∤q, every geometric-Frobenius eigenvalue α on H_c^i(X_overlineFq,Q_ℓ) is algebraic and all its complex conjugates have absolute value at most q^(i/2).

title: Cohomology outside the singular band of a complete intersection
description: Let X⊂Pᴺ over F_q be a geometrically integral projective complete intersection of dimension n≥1 whose geometric singular locus has dimension s (s=−1 if X is smooth), and let ℓ∤q. For 0≤i<n and for n+s+1<i≤2n, H^i(X_F̄q,Q_ℓ) is 0 for odd i and is isomorphic, compatibly with the Galois action, to the Tate twist Q_ℓ(−i/2) for even i; for i<n this isomorphism is restriction from Pᴺ.

title: Katz uniform bound on projective Betti numbers
description: If X⊂P^N over an algebraically closed field is defined scheme-theoretically by m homogeneous equations of degrees at most D≥1, then for ℓ different from the characteristic, Σ_i dimH^i(X,Q_ℓ)≤8·2^m(mD+3)^(N+1). In particular these dimensions are uniformly bounded by the ambient dimension, number and degrees of equations.

title: Geometric integrality of a complete intersection regular in codimension one
description: Over an algebraically closed field, a projective complete intersection X of dimension n≥1 whose singular locus has dimension at most n−2, so that X is regular in codimension one, is integral.

title: Primary decomposition in a Noetherian ring
description: Every proper ideal in a commutative Noetherian ring is a finite intersection of primary ideals. An ideal Q is primary if ab∈Q and a∉Q imply b^m∈Q for some m≥1; its radical is prime. The radicals in a minimal primary decomposition are the associated primes of the quotient.

title: Local cohomology with support
description: For an ideal I in a Noetherian ring R, H_I^i(M) is the ith right derived functor of Γ_I(M)={m∈M:I^a m=0 for some a}. Short exact sequences of modules induce the natural long exact sequence of these groups; H_I^i(M)=0 below the I-depth of M.

title: Bézout degree of a projective complete intersection
description: A projective complete intersection cut out scheme-theoretically by a regular sequence of homogeneous degrees d₁,…,d_c has degree d₁⋯d_c, with its components counted with scheme multiplicities. In dimensionzero this is the scheme’s length over an algebraically closed ground field.

title: Macaulay regularity of a zero-dimensional complete intersection
description: If T⊂P^n over a field is a zero-dimensional complete intersection of n hypersurfaces of degrees d₁,…,d_n, then H⁰(P^n,O(k))→H⁰(T,O_T(k)) is surjective for every k≥Σ_i(d_i−1).

title: Refined Gysin intersection product
description: For a regular closed embedding i:Y→X of codimension c and a morphism X′→X, the refined Gysin map i^!:A_*(X′)→A_(*−c)(Y×_X X′) on Chow groups is defined by deformation to the normal cone followed by the zero-section pullback in the pulled-back normal bundle. It retains excess-intersection contributions even when the fiber product has larger than the expected dimension.

title: Kollár effective Nullstellensatz degree bound
description: Let n≥2,D≥3 and K be a field. If homogeneous forms f_i of common degree D in K[x₀,…,x_n] generate I, then (√I)^(D^n)⊆I. Consequently, if affine polynomials g_i in n variables have degrees at most D and h vanishes on their common zeros over an algebraic closure, then h^s=Σ_i a_i g_i for some1≤s≤D^n and a_i∈K[x₁,…,x_n].

title: Jentzsch theorem for a strictly positive compact countable kernel
description: Let q(x,y)>0 on a nonempty countable set, with its row action defining a compact positive operator Q on ℓ¹. Then r(Q)>0 is an eigenvalue with a strictly positive ℓ¹ eigenvector; that eigenvector is unique up to scaling among nonnegative eigenvectors, and no other eigenvalue has modulus r(Q).

title: Equisummability criterion for relative compactness in ℓ¹
description: A bounded family B⊂ℓ¹(X) on a countable set is relatively compact exactly when for every η>0 there is a finite K⊂X with sup_(u∈B)∑_(x∉K)|u(x)|<η.

title: Existence of a QSD for a bounded nonlinear Poisson population
description: Let X_(t+1)=ε(N₁,…,N_d) conditionally on X_t=x, with independent Nᵢ∼Poisson(Fᵢ(x)/ε). Suppose F is continuous and bounded, Fᵢ(x)>0 for strictly positive x, and the boundary of the nonnegative orthant is absorbing. For each ε>0 this chain has a quasi-stationary distribution supported on ε{1,2,…}ᵈ, with survival eigenvalue0<λ_ε<1.

title: Uniform deviation bounds for bounded nonlinear Poisson kernels
description: Let F:ℝ_+ᵈ→ℝ_+ᵈ be continuous and bounded, preserving the boundary and its complement, and let P_ε be its independent-coordinate scaled Poisson kernel. The action ρ(x,y)=∑ᵢ[yᵢlog(yᵢ/Fᵢ(x))−yᵢ+Fᵢ(x)] has compact-uniform one-step lower LDP bounds for positive starting states. For every δ>0 some c_δ>0 gives sup_xP_ε(x,{y:‖y−F(x)‖∞≥δ})≤2d e^(−c_δ/ε). For every c>0 an open boundary neighborhood V has inf_(x∈V)P_ε(x,∂ℝ_+ᵈ)≥e^(−c/ε).

title: Dominant scheme morphism
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→Y is dominant if its image is dense in the underlying topological space of Y. For a morphism between integral affine schemes SpecB→SpecA, dominance is equivalent to injectivity of the ring map A→B.

title: Dimension of a finite-type scheme
description: The dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets of its underlying space. On an affine chart SpecA it equals the Krull dimension of A; for a finite-type scheme over a field it is the maximum of these dimensions over any finite affine open cover.

title: Fiber of a scheme morphism
description: For a scheme morphism f:X→Y and a point y∈Y with residue field κ(y), its fiber over y is X_y=X×_Y Specκ(y), regarded as a κ(y)-scheme. For finite-type varieties over an algebraically closed field at closed points this recovers the subvariety obtained by specializing the target coordinates.

title: Dimension and transcendence degree of an affine domain
description: If A is a finitely generated integral algebra over a field k, then dimA equals trdeg_k FracA, the cardinality of a maximal algebraically independent subset of its fraction field over k. For a tower of finitely generated field extensions K⊂L⊂M, trdeg_KM=trdeg_KL+trdeg_LM.

title: Chevalley constructible image theorem
description: The image of a constructible subset under a finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes is constructible. In an irreducible Noetherian target a constructible set containing the generic point contains a nonempty open subset; if it omits the generic point its closure is proper.

title: Upper semicontinuity of local fiber dimension
description: For a locally finite-type morphism f:X→Y, the function x↦dim_x(X_(f(x))) is upper semicontinuous on X: for every integer d the set where this local fiber dimension is at most d is open. This concerns points of the source; it does not assert upper semicontinuity of total fiber dimension on an arbitrary target.

title: Linearly disjoint finite field extensions
description: Finite extensions L/K and M/K in a common overfield are linearly disjoint over K when [LM:K]=[L:K][M:K], where LM is their compositum. Equivalently a K-basis of L remains linearly independent over M.

title: Absence of nontrivial everywhere finitely unramified extensions of the rationals
description: If a number field K is unramified at every finite prime of ℚ, then K=ℚ. No condition at the infinite place is needed.

title: Linear disjointness of rational Galois extensions with disjoint ramification
description: Let L/ℚ and M/ℚ be finite Galois extensions in a common algebraic closure. If no finite rational prime ramifies in both extensions, then L∩M=ℚ, L and M are linearly disjoint over ℚ, and restriction identifies Gal(LM/M) with Gal(L/ℚ).

title: Unramified elliptic division fields at good primes
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K, p a prime and r≥1. At a finite place v of residue characteristic different from p where E has good reduction, K(E[p^r])/K is unramified.

title: Kolyvagin bound from a Heegner point and surjective torsion image
description: Let E/ℚ be geometrically non-CM and let K be an imaginary quadratic field distinct from ℚ(i) and ℚ(√−3), satisfying the Heegner hypothesis for E. Let y_K∈E(K) be a nontorsion Heegner point with finite index I_K=[E(K):ℤy_K]. If p≥5 and ρ_(E,p):G_ℚ→GL₂(𝔽_p) is surjective, then Sha(E/K)[p^∞] is finite and v_p(#Sha(E/K)[p^∞])≤2v_p(I_K).

title: Orthogonality of finite abelian characters
description: For a finite abelian group G and its complex character group Ghat, |Ghat|=|G| and Σ_(χ∈Ghat)χ(g)conjugate(χ(h)) equals|G| ifg=h and0 otherwise. Dually Σ_(g∈G)χ(g)conjugate(ψ(g)) equals|G| ifχ=ψ and0 otherwise.

title: Dirichlet L-functions on the line Re(s)=1
description: For a nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ, L(s,χ) is holomorphic and nonzero on Re(s)≥1. For the principal character moduloq, L(s,χ₀)=ζ(s)∏_(p|q)(1−p^(−s)) has a simple pole of residueφ(q)/q at1 and no zeros on Re(s)=1.

title: Newman–Zagier Laplace Tauberian theorem
description: Let f:[0,∞)→R be bounded and locally integrable. If its Laplace transform g(z)=∫₀∞f(t)e^(−zt)dt, initially defined forRe(z)>0, extends holomorphically to an open neighborhood of the closed right half-plane, then the improper integral∫₀∞f(t)dt converges and equalsg(0).

title: Prime number theorem in a fixed arithmetic progression
description: For fixed integers q≥1 and a with gcd(a,q)=1, π(x;q,a)=#{primesp≤x:p≡a modq} satisfies π(x;q,a)∼x/(φ(q)logx) asx→∞. The modulus is fixed; this statement asserts no uniform error bound asq varies.

title: Grassmannian of vector subspaces
description: For0≤r≤n over a field k, Gr(r,n) is the projective algebraic variety parametrizing r-dimensional linear subspaces of k^n. Its standard open charts consist of graphs of linear maps between complementary coordinate subspaces and are affine spaces of r×(n−r) matrices, glued by change of graph coordinates.

title: Codimension of a linear-subspace intersection condition
description: Let A,B be fixed subspaces of a c-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field, of dimensions a,b. For max(0,a+b−c)≤p≤min(a,b), the closed locus {g∈GL_c:dim(gA∩B)≥p} has codimension p(c−a−b+p).

title: Smoothness of a transverse intersection
description: If smooth locally closed subvarieties Y,Z of a smooth variety X over a field meet at a geometric point x with T_xY+T_xZ=T_xX, their scheme intersection is smooth at x of dimension dimY+dimZ−dimX.

title: Upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension for proper morphisms
description: For a proper morphism of finite-type schemes f:X→Y over a field and every integer d, the subset {y∈Y:dimX_y≥d} is closed inY. Empty fibers have dimension−1.

title: Bertini smoothness for general linear sections
description: Let Y⊂P^N_k be a smooth locally closed subvariety over an algebraically closed field, and0≤c≤N. A nonempty Zariski open set of codimension-c projective linear subspaces L has Y∩L empty or smooth of pure dimension dimY−c, with the intersection transverse. This holds in every characteristic.

title: Diagonalization of a symmetric bilinear form by congruence
description: Over a field of characteristic different from two, every symmetric matrix A admits an invertible matrix P with PᵀAP diagonal. Over an algebraically closed field, it is congruent to diag(I_r,0), where r=rankA.

title: Geometry of the symmetric determinant hypersurface
description: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two and for n≥2, the locus of singular symmetric n×n matrices is an irreducible reduced determinant hypersurface in the affine space Sym_n. Its singular locus is exactly the matrices of rank at most n−2, which has codimension three in Sym_n.

title: Proper metric space
description: A metric space is proper if every closed bounded ball is compact.

title: Left-invariant metric on a group
description: A metric d on a group G is left invariant if d(gx,gy)=d(x,y) for all g,x,y∈G. On a topological group it is compatible if its metric topology equals the given topology.

title: Existence and uniqueness of Haar measure on a locally compact group
description: Every locally compact Hausdorff group admits a left Haar measure, a nonzero left-invariant Radon measure (finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets, inner regular on open sets), and any two left Haar measures differ by a positive constant factor.

title: Continuity of left translations in Haar L¹
description: For a left Haar measure on a locally compact group and f∈L¹(G), ‖f(g⁻¹·)−f‖₁→0 as g→e.

title: Struble’s proper left-invariant metrization theorem
description: Every second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group has a compatible proper left-invariant metric.

title: Proper metrization of a discrete–compact double quotient
description: Let G be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, Γ a closed discrete subgroup, and K a compact subgroup. The double quotient Γ∖G/K is second countable and has a compatible proper metric; this applies in particular to Γ∖G for a lattice Γ.

title: Nonemptiness of inverse limits of finite sets
description: For a sequence of nonempty finite sets X_n and maps f_n:X_(n+1)→X_n, there exists a coherent tuple (x_n) with f_n(x_(n+1))=x_n for every n. Equivalently the countable inverse limit is nonempty; the maps need not be surjective.

title: Primitive prime-power root count for a smooth homogeneous equation
description: Fix a homogeneous f∈Z[x₁,…,x_r] of positive degree with r≥2 whose projective hypersurface overQ is smooth. For every primep there is C_(f,p)>0 such that #{x modp^e:p∤(x₁,…,x_r), f(x)≡0 modp^e}≤C_(f,p)p^(e(r−1)) for all e≥1. The constants C_(f,p) can be chosen bounded outside a finite set of primes depending onf.

title: Orthogonality of finite cyclic exponential sums
description: For integers q≥1 and m, Σ_(a modq) exp(2πiam/q) equalsq ifq dividesm and0 otherwise. On (Z/qZ)^k, the product character sum similarly vanishes unless every frequency is divisible byq, in which case it equalsq^k.

title: Quadratic Gauss sum kernel bound
description: For a symmetric integer k×k matrixA and q≥1, define S(A;q)=Σ_(x∈(Z/qZ)^k) exp(2πixᵀAx/q) and K(A;q)={z modq:2Az≡0modq}. Then |S(A;q)|²≤q^k|K(A;q)|.

title: Prime-power mean bound for quadratic Gauss sums in a net
description: Let Q=(Q₁,Q₂,Q₃) be integral-matrix quadratic forms in k≥4 variables whose determinant equation is nonsingular overQ. For q=p^e, put S_q(a)=Σ_(x modq)exp(2πiΣ_ja_jQ_j(x)/q). Then Σ_(a modq,gcd(a₁,a₂,a₃,p)=1)|S_q(a)|≤A_p p^(e(3+k/2)) for some A_p independent ofe. The A_p are bounded outside the finite set of primes dividing2Disc(det(Σ_ja_jQ_j)).

title: Uniform solubility of a smooth quadratic net at large primes
description: For an integral-matrix quadratic net Q in k>6 variables whose determinant equation is nonsingular overQ, there exists p₀(Q) such that for every primep>p₀ and every n∈Z_p³ the system Q(x)=n has a solution x∈Z_p^k.

title: Independence of eigenvectors with distinct eigenvalues
description: For a linear endomorphism over a field, nonzero eigenvectors belonging to pairwise distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent.

title: Diagonalization of a smooth pencil of quadrics
description: Let A,B be symmetric k×k matrices over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, with k≥3. If their two projective quadratic equations define a smooth codimension-two intersection, then an invertible change of variables makes both matrices diagonal, diag(a_i),diag(b_i), with every pair(a_i,b_i) nonzero and all ratios[a_i:b_i] distinct. Equivalently det(sA+tB) has k distinct projective roots; in particular every nonzero pencil member has rank at least k−1.

title: Elliptic curve over a finite field
description: An elliptic curve over a finite field k is a one-dimensional abelian variety over k, with its identity as distinguished point. Its k-rational points form the finite abelian group E(k).

title: Frobenius characteristic polynomial of a finite-field elliptic curve
description: Let E/𝔽_q be elliptic and ℓ∤q prime. The q-power Frobenius endomorphism, acting by qth powers on coordinates, acts on T_ℓE with characteristic polynomial T²−a_qT+q, where a_q=q+1−#E(𝔽_q).

title: Frobenius traces on elliptic torsion at a good prime
description: Let E/ℚ have good reduction at a rational prime ℓ and write a_ℓ=ℓ+1−#Ẽ(𝔽_ℓ). For any prime p≠ℓ and r≥1, the characteristic polynomial of arithmetic Frobenius at ℓ acting on E[p^r] is T²−a_ℓT+ℓ modulo p^r. The corresponding polynomial on T_pE is T²−a_ℓT+ℓ.

title: Filtration of an elliptic good-reduction kernel
description: For an elliptic curve with good reduction over a nonarchimedean local field K with valuation ring R, maximal ideal 𝔪 and residue field k, the kernel E₁(K) of reduction has the complete separated filtration E_n(K) given in a local parameter at the identity by valuation at least n. Its quotients E_n(K)/E_(n+1)(K) are the additive groups 𝔪^n/𝔪^(n+1), and addition induces their additive law.

title: Prime-to-residue-characteristic divisibility under elliptic good reduction
description: Let K be a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of characteristic ℓ, and let E/K have good reduction, and let n≥1 be coprime to ℓ. Multiplication by n is an automorphism of the reduction kernel E₁(K), and reduction induces E(K)[n]≅Ẽ(k)[n] and E(K)/nE(K)≅Ẽ(k)/nẼ(k).

title: Lutz–Nagell integrality of rational elliptic torsion
description: If E/ℚ is given by y²=x³+Ax+B with A,B∈ℤ and 4A³+27B²≠0, then every nonidentity rational torsion point has integral x- and y-coordinates.

title: Dvornicich–Zannier counterexample to local-global divisibility by four
description: There exist an elliptic curve E/ℚ and an infinite-order P∈E(ℚ) which lies in4E(ℚ_v) at every finite place except possibly2, but does not lie in4E(ℚ).

title: Local-global divisibility by a prime on a rational elliptic curve
description: For every elliptic curve E/ℚ and prime p, a rational point P∈E(ℚ) which belongs to pE(ℚ_ℓ) for all but finitely many rational primes ℓ already belongs to pE(ℚ).

title: Abstract simplicial complex
description: An abstract simplicial complex on a vertex set V is a family of finite subsets of V closed under taking subsets and containing every singleton. Members are simplices, their subsets are faces, and a simplex with n+1 vertices has dimension n. An isomorphism is a vertex bijection preserving simplices in both directions.

title: Coxeter system
description: A Coxeter system (W,S) is a group generated by involutions S with only relations (st)^(m_st)=1, where m_ss=1 and m_st=m_ts∈{2,3,…,∞} for s≠t, with∞ imposing no relation. Equivalently any assignment of S to involutions in another group satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a homomorphism from W.

title: Word length in a Coxeter system
description: For a Coxeter system (W,S), ℓ(w) is the minimum length of a word in S representing w; a word of length ℓ(w) is reduced.

title: Reflection in an affine Euclidean hyperplane
description: For a unit vector u and c∈ℝ, reflection in {x:⟨x,u⟩=c} is x↦x−2(⟨x,u⟩−c)u. It is the affine isometry fixing that hyperplane pointwise and reversing its normal direction.

title: Weyl group of a finite root system
description: For a finite crystallographic root system Φ in a real inner-product space, its Weyl group is the group generated by the linear reflections s_α in α⊥ for α∈Φ. It acts on Φ; since Φ spans, this action is faithful and the group is finite.

title: Affine Weyl group of a reduced crystallographic root system
description: For a reduced finite crystallographic root system Φ in E, its affine Weyl group is generated by s_(α,k)(x)=x−(⟨x,α⟩−k)α∨, α∈Φ,k∈ℤ. Here α∨=2α/⟨α,α⟩; equivalently W_aff=Q∨⋊W with coroot lattice Q∨ and finite Weyl group W.

title: Weyl chamber of a finite root system
description: For a finite root system Φ in E, an open Weyl chamber is a connected component of E∖⋃_(α∈Φ)α⊥; its closure is a closed Weyl chamber, a simplicial cone after choosing simple roots. Opposite chambers are negatives of one another.

title: Affine Coxeter complex of a crystallographic root system
description: For an irreducible reduced finite crystallographic root system Φ, the affine Coxeter complex is the Euclidean simplicial tessellation cut out by hyperplanes ⟨x,α⟩=k for α∈Φ,k∈ℤ. Its maximal cells are alcoves, and its walls are the reflecting hyperplanes. The affine Weyl group acts simply transitively on alcoves; labeling one alcove’s vertices by opposite walls and propagating by this action gives its vertex types.

title: Affine building
description: An affine building is a typed simplicial complex equipped with apartments isomorphic to one affine Coxeter complex, such that any two simplices lie in an apartment and any two apartments have a type-preserving simplicial isomorphism fixing their intersection pointwise. Apartment intersections are convex in their Euclidean realizations. It is thick if each codimension-one chamber face lies in at least three chambers, and locally finite if each vertex belongs to finitely many simplices.

title: Apartment of an affine building
description: An apartment is one of the distinguished subcomplexes in an affine building’s apartment system, with its Euclidean affine-Coxeter realization. The maximal apartment system consists of every subcomplex isomorphic to the model apartment in the building-theoretic sense.

title: Chamber of an affine building
description: A chamber of an affine building is a maximal simplex; an alcove of an apartment is a chamber in that apartment.

title: Panel of an affine building
description: A panel is a codimension-one face of a chamber. Two distinct chambers are adjacent if they share a panel; its type is the vertex label omitted by that panel.

title: Gallery in an affine building
description: A gallery is a finite sequence of chambers with consecutive distinct chambers sharing a panel; its length is the number of steps. It is minimal between its endpoints if no shorter gallery connects them. Its type is the sequence of omitted panel labels.

title: Wall of an affine building apartment
description: A wall in an apartment is a reflecting affine hyperplane of its affine Coxeter complex, regarded with its induced subcomplex. Its two closed half-spaces are half-apartments.

title: Sector of an affine building
description: A sector in an apartment is a translate v+C of a closed Weyl chamber C of its finite root system; v is its vertex. Sectors have opposite direction when their chamber cones are C and−C.

title: Special vertex of an affine building
description: A vertex v in an apartment is special if its stabilizer in the affine Weyl group maps onto the full finite Weyl group under the linear-part homomorphism. Equivalently every apartment wall direction has a parallel wall through v; the condition is independent of the chosen apartment.

title: Type-preserving automorphism of an affine building
description: A simplicial automorphism of a typed affine building is type preserving if it fixes every vertex label. Such an automorphism stabilizing a chamber fixes each of its vertices, hence the chamber pointwise.

title: Strongly transitive action on an affine building
description: A group action by simplicial automorphisms of an affine building is strongly transitive relative to an apartment system if it is transitive on pairs (C,A) of a chamber and an apartment containing it.

title: Weyl distance between chambers of an affine building
description: Fix the model affine Coxeter system (W,S) and vertex types. For chambers C,D choose an apartment and a type-preserving identification with its Coxeter complex sending C to the fundamental alcove; if D maps to w times that alcove, put δ(C,D)=w. This is independent of the choices and ℓ(δ(C,D)) is the minimal gallery length. Type-preserving automorphisms preserve δ.

title: Hilbert polynomial and degree of a projective scheme
description: For a finitely generated standard graded algebra A over a field with nonempty projective scheme of dimensionr, dim_kA_m agrees for large m with a polynomial of degree r whose leading coefficient is deg(ProjA)/r!. Hilbert polynomials are additive in short exact sequences of finitely generated graded modules, and a degree shift byD replaces P(m) byP(m−D).

title: Component multiplicities in projective degree
description: The degree of a pure-dimensional projective scheme is the sum of the degrees of its top-dimensional irreducible reduced components weighted by their positive generic scheme lengths. Thus its reduced support has degree no greater than the scheme, and deleting some components can only decrease that total.

title: Dimension of an affine hypersurface section
description: If A is a finitely generated integral algebra over a field and f∈A is nonzero and not a unit, every irreducible component of Spec(A/(f)) has dimension dimA−1. Equivalently a nonempty hypersurface section of an irreducible affine variety that is not the entire variety is pure of codimensionone.

title: Zero divisors in a reduced Noetherian ring
description: In a reduced commutative Noetherian ring, the zero divisors are exactly the union of its minimal prime ideals. Hence an element nonzero on every irreducible component of its spectrum acts injectively by multiplication.

title: Unique factorization for polynomial rings over a field
description: For a field k and finitely many variables, every nonzero nonunit polynomial in k[x₁,…,x_n] factors into irreducibles, uniquely up to nonzero scalar factors and reordering. In particular an irreducible polynomial generates a prime ideal.

title: Irreducibility of a smooth projective plane equation
description: A nonzero homogeneous polynomial F∈k[x,y,z] of positive degree whose projective plane equation is Jacobian-nonsingular over an algebraic closure is irreducible over that algebraic closure. Thus its projective curve is geometrically integral.

title: Bilinearity of the quadratic Hilbert symbol over rational completions
description: For v a rational prime or the real place, the quadratic Hilbert symbol is multiplicative in each variable: (ab,c)_v=(a,c)_v(b,c)_v and (a,bc)_v=(a,b)_v(a,c)_v for a,b,c∈ℚ_v×.

title: Explicit quadratic Hilbert symbols over the rational completions
description: At an odd prime p write a=p^αu,b=p^βv with u,v units; then (a,b)_p=(−1)^(αβ(p−1)/2)(u/p)^β(v/p)^α. At2, writing a=2^αu,b=2^βv, the symbol is (−1)^(ε(u)ε(v)+αω(v)+βω(u)), with ε(u)=(u−1)/2 mod2 and ω(u)=(u²−1)/8 mod2. At the real place the symbol is−1 exactly when both arguments are negative.

title: Hilbert reciprocity over the rational numbers
description: For any a,b∈ℚ×, (a,b)_v=1 for all but finitely many rational places v, and ∏_v(a,b)_v=1, where v ranges over the finite primes and the real place with ℚ_∞=ℝ.

title: Hasse invariant of a diagonal local quadratic form
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic form over a local field of characteristic different from2, diagonalized as ∑_(i=1)^n a_i x_i², its Hasse invariant is ε(Q)=∏_(i<j)(a_i,a_j), using the local quadratic Hilbert symbol. This convention uses i<j, and the value is independent of the diagonalization.

title: Hasse-invariant criterion for local ternary isotropy
description: For a nondegenerate ternary quadratic form Q over a local field F of characteristic different from2, write d for its Gram determinant modulo squares and ε(Q)=∏_(i<j)(a_i,a_j) for a diagonalization. Then Q is isotropic if and only if ε(Q)=(−1,−d)_F.

title: Parity of anisotropic places of a rational ternary quadratic form
description: For a nondegenerate ternary quadratic form over ℚ, the set of places v at which the same form over ℚ_v is anisotropic is finite and has even cardinality, including the real place among the places. Consequently a positive definite ternary form isotropic at every odd prime is anisotropic at2.

title: Subpower bounds for the divisor function
description: For every ε>0, the numberτ(n) of positive divisors satisfies τ(n)≤C_ε n^ε for all n≥1. More generally, for every fixed C≥1 and ε>0, C^ω(n)≤C_(C,ε)n^ε, whereω(n) is the number of distinct prime divisors.

title: Averaged doubled exponential sums for a smooth quadratic net
description: Let Q be an integral-matrix quadratic net in k≥4 variables with nonsingular determinant equation. For ℓ=(u,v)∈Z^(2k), set S(ℓ;q)=Σ_(a modq,gcd(a₁,a₂,a₃,q)=1)Σ_(x,y modq)exp(2πi[a·(Q(x)−Q(y))+u·x+v·y]/q). For X,L≥1 and ε>0, Σ_(q≤X)Σ_(max|ℓ_i|≤L)|S(ℓ;q)|≪_(Q,ε)X^(k+3+ε)L^(2k+ε)+X^(k+4+ε)L^k.

title: Folding an affine apartment onto a half-apartment
description: For a wall H in an affine Coxeter apartment and a chosen closed half-apartment H⁺, its folding fixes H⁺ and reflects the other half across H. It preserves chamber incidence, does not increase gallery distances, and a gallery crossing H maps to one with a repeated consecutive chamber at that crossing.

title: Canonical retraction to a building apartment
description: For a thick affine building, apartment A and chamber C⊂A, there is a canonical type-preserving retraction ρ_(A,C):Δ→A. On every apartment containing C it is the unique isomorphism to A fixing the overlap pointwise. It preserves gallery distances from faces of C and does not increase gallery distance between chambers.

title: Comparison of adjacent-center apartment retractions
description: Let adjacent C,C′ lie in an apartment A, let H,H′ be the half-apartments containing them and r their common-wall reflection. For another chamber D, the retractions centered at C,C′ agree in H if d(C′,D)>d(C,D), and agree in H′ if the inequality reverses. If the distances are equal, ρ_C(D)∈H′, ρ_C′(D)∈H, and rρ_C(D)=ρ_C′(D).

title: Coxeter subcomplex characterization of maximal apartments
description: A chamber subcomplex of a thick affine building is an apartment in the maximal apartment system if it is type-preservingly isomorphic to the model affine Coxeter complex.

title: Wall criterion for minimal galleries in an affine Coxeter complex
description: In an affine Coxeter complex, gallery distance between chambers equals the number of walls separating them. A gallery is minimal exactly when it crosses each separating wall once and no other wall. A chamber E lies on some minimal gallery from C to D exactly when no wall separates E from both C and D.

title: Gallery convexity of a building apartment
description: If chambers C,D of a thick affine building lie in an apartment A, every minimal gallery in the building from C to D is contained in A.

title: Reduced-word criterion for building galleries
description: A non-stuttering gallery in a thick affine building is minimal if and only if its panel-type word is reduced in the model Coxeter system. Consequently its endpoint Weyl distance is the product of that reduced word.

title: Weyl isometry between chamber sets
description: A Weyl isometry (strong isometry) between sets of chambers in buildings with the same typed Coxeter model is a bijection f satisfying δ(fC,fD)=δ(C,D) for every pair of chambers in its domain.

title: Apartment containment from a Weyl-isometric chamber set
description: In a thick affine building with its maximal apartment system, any set of chambers Weyl-isometric to a subset of a model apartment is contained in an apartment.

title: C¹ diffeomorphism between Euclidean open sets
description: A C¹ diffeomorphism Φ:U→V between open subsets of R^n is a bijection such that both Φ and Φ⁻¹ are continuously differentiable.

title: Riemann change of variables on a compact Jordan set
description: Let S⊂U⊂R^n be compact and Jordan measurable, with U open. If g:U→R^n is injective and C¹ and detDg is nonzero onS, then for every Riemann-integrable f on g(S), ∫_(g(S))f(y)dy=∫_S f(g(x))|detDg(x)|dx.

title: Uniqueness of Radon measures from continuous tests
description: Two nonnegative Radon Borel measures on a locally compact Hausdorff space are equal if they give the same integral to every real continuous compactly supported function.

title: Null-set preservation by locally Lipschitz maps
description: A locally Lipschitz map between open subsets of the same Euclidean space R^n sends Lebesgue-null sets to Lebesgue-null sets. On a region with Lipschitz constantL, image outer measure is bounded by a dimensional constant times L^n times domain outer measure.

title: Pointwise stabilizer of a set under a group action
description: For a group action G on X and A⊆X, its pointwise stabilizer is {g∈G:ga=a for every a∈A}, a subgroup of G. This is distinct from merely preserving A as a set.

title: Density of compactly supported continuous functions in Radon Lᵖ
description: If μ is a Radon measure on a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space and1≤p<∞, then compactly supported continuous functions are dense in Lᵖ(μ).

title: Conditional expectation for a compact-group quotient
description: Let a compact group K act continuously on a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff space Y preserving a Radon probability m. With π:Y→X=Y/K and π_*m, pullback identifies L²(X) isometrically with the K-invariant subspace of L²(Y), and P_Kf(y)=∫_Kf(k⁻¹y)dk is both conditional expectation onto π⁻¹B(X) and the orthogonal projection onto that subspace, for normalized Haar dk.

title: Stable-past finite-coset criterion for a Markov state space
description: Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact group G, K a compact subgroup and a∈G. Put Y=Γ∖G, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹. If K=⊔_(j=1)^rω_j(K∩a⁻¹Ka), where every ω_j belongs to ⋂_(n≥0)aⁿKa⁻ⁿ, then Y→X has the Markov module property for S.

title: Arrow chamber-fixing subgroup
description: Let G act on an affine building, and let v₀,v₁ be special vertices of one apartment sharing no wall. Let C₀ be the apartment chamber at v₀ directed toward v₁, and C₁ the chamber at v₁ directed toward v₀. The arrow subgroup is Fix_G(C₀)∩Fix_G(C₁), where fixers are pointwise; it is unchanged when the two corners are reversed.

title: Dyadic oscillatory integrals for a smooth quadratic net
description: Let Q be a k-variable integral quadratic net with nonsingular determinant equation, m∈{1,2}, F^(1)(x)=Q(x), F^(2)(x,y)=Q(x)−Q(y), and w∈C_c^∞(R^(mk)). Put I_m(ν,λ)=∫w(z)exp(2πi[ν·F^(m)(z)−λ·z])dz. Forφ_j>0, D_φ=∏_j([φ_j,2φ_j]∪[−2φ_j,−φ_j]) and Φ=maxφ_j, one has ∫_(D_φ)|I_m(ν,λ)|dν≪_(Q,w)∏φ_j. IfΦ≥1 it is also ≪_(Q,w)Φ^(3−mk/2)(1+logΦ)^(m−1), uniformly inλ.

title: Equivalence of norms in finite dimensions
description: Any two norms on the same finite-dimensional real vector space bound one another by positive constant multiples. They therefore induce the same topology and the same notions of boundedness and convergence.

title: Integral reflection criterion for a primitive local lattice vector
description: Let L be a quadratic ℤ_p-lattice in V and let v∈L be primitive with Q(v)≠0. The reflection τ_v(x)=x−2B(x,v)v/Q(v) preserves L if and only if2B(v,L)⊆Q(v)ℤ_p.

title: Unit representation and integral rotation spinor norms
description: Let L be a quadratic ℤ_p-lattice of rank at least2 with Q(L)⊆ℤ_p. If L represents every unit of ℤ_p, then θ(SO(L)) contains the square class of every unit of ℤ_p.

title: Normal form of an odd-prime universal ternary lattice
description: Let p be odd and L a nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice of rank3 with Q(L)⊆ℤ_p. If Q(L)=ℤ_p, then L is isometric to⟨1,−1,−d⟩, where d is its Gram determinant up to a unit square. In particular its underlying ℚ_p-space is isotropic and θ(SO(L)) contains every unit square class.

title: Unit local spinor norms imply one proper ternary spinor genus
description: Let L be a positive definite ternary quadratic ℤ-lattice. If for every finite prime p the group θ(SO(L_p)) contains the square class of every unit of ℤ_p, then the genus of L contains exactly one proper spinor genus.

title: Prime-square transfer for a squarefree ternary spinor exception
description: Let L be positive definite integral ternary, t>0 squarefree and a primitive spinor exception of its genus, and E=ℚ(√(−dt)) for Gram determinant d. For all sufficiently large primes q: if the proper spinor genus of L does not represent t and q splits in E, L does not represent tq²; if it represents t and q is inert in E, L represents tq² exactly when it represents t.

title: Infinitely many prime-square nonrepresentations from a squarefree spinor exception
description: Let L be a positive definite integral ternary quadratic ℤ-lattice, and let t>0 be squarefree and a primitive spinor exception of its genus. If L does not represent t, then L fails to represent tq² for infinitely many rational primes q.

title: Integral spinor norms of separated diagonal binary two-adic lattices
description: Put F=ℚ₂, S=(F×)², U=ℤ₂× and H_d={γ∈F×:(γ,d)₂=1}. For L=⟨1,2^rα⟩ with r≥1 and α∈U, identify θ(SO(L)) with its inverse image in F×. This image equals H_(−2α) for r=1 or3; H_(−α)∩US for r=2; S∪αS∪5S∪5αS for r=4; and S∪2^rαS for r≥5.

title: Bounded representatives of real quadratic fibers
description: Let Q:R^k→R^r be a tuple of homogeneous quadratic polynomials such that DQ has rank r at every nonzero common zero. For any 0<A₂≤A₁ there is Λ depending only on Q,A₁,A₂ such that every soluble fiber Q(x)=ν with A₂≤|ν|≤A₁ has a real solution with |x|≤Λ.

title: Fourier transform of the triangular kernel
description: For ε>0 and sinc(t)=sin(πt)/(πt), with sinc(0)=1, one has ∫_R sinc²(εt) exp(2πitu)dt=ε^(−1)(1−|u|/ε)_+ for every real u. The d-dimensional product identity follows by integrating one coordinate at a time.

title: Effective equidistribution from average Bowen-ball separation
description: Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact group G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact, X=Y/K, and S(y)=ya⁻¹. Assume the Markov module property and0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1. Let μ be S-invariant, Ω compact, s≤0≤t, n=t−s+1≥2, and α=−n⁻¹log∫_Ωμ(yB^(s,t))dμ(y). Choose a symmetric relatively compact open identity neighborhood B₀⊂N_G(K) with B₀²⊂B, injective quotient maps gB₀→Y for Γg∈Ω, and vol(B₀^(s,t))≥Ce^(−nh), C,h>0, using covolume-one Haar measure. For X-measurable0≤φ≤1 put u=μφ. In the lower-semicontinuous case put p=m(esssup_(b∈B₀)φ(·b)), η=(u−1+κ)/κ, q=θ+(1−θ)p; in the upper-semicontinuous case put p=m(essinf_(b∈B₀)φ(·b)), η=u/κ, q=(1−θ)p. If p,u∈(0,1),0<κ<μΩ, k≥1 and θ=λᵏ, with p≤η and θ≤(η−p)/(1−p) in the first case, or η≤p and θ≤(p−η)/p in the second, then C(μΩ−κ)²e^(−n(h−α))/4≤k e^(D(u‖p))e^(−nD(η‖q)/k).

title: Conditional information and entropy of a finite partition
description: For a finite measurable partition ξ of a probability space and sub-σ-algebra A, set I_μ(ξ|A)(x)=−∑_(C∈ξ)1_C(x)log E_μ[1_C|A](x), with the almost-everywhere conditional-probability convention; its integral H_μ(ξ|A) is the conditional entropy.

title: Chain rule for finite-partition conditional information
description: For finite measurable partitions ξ,η and a sub-σ-algebra A of a probability space, I_μ(ξ∨η|A)=I_μ(η|A)+I_μ(ξ|σ(η)∨A) almost everywhere. Conditional information also commutes with pullback by a measure-preserving map when both partition and conditioning σ-algebra are pulled back.

title: Domination and convergence of finite-partition conditional information
description: If ξ is a finite measurable partition of a probability space and A_n increases to A_∞=σ(⋃A_n), then I_μ(ξ|A_n)→I_μ(ξ|A_∞) almost surely and in L¹, and ∫sup_n I_μ(ξ|A_n)dμ≤H_μ(ξ)+1.

title: Future conditional formula for finite-partition entropy rate
description: For a probability-preserving transformation T and finite partition ξ, h_μ(T,ξ)=H_μ(ξ|∨_(j≥1)T^(−j)ξ). This is the entropy rate for the ξ-name process; no generating-partition hypothesis is required.

title: Maximal ergodic inequality for a nonnegative function
description: If T preserves probability μ, g≥0 belongs to L¹(μ), and r>0, then μ{sup_(n≥1)n⁻¹∑_(j=0)^(n−1)g(T^jx)>r}≤‖g‖₁/r.

title: Cyclic cohomology criterion for elliptic local-global divisibility
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F, m>1 and G=Gal(F(E[m])/F). If the cyclic restriction kernel H¹_loc(G,E[m]) is zero, every P∈E(F) divisible by m in E(F_v) at all but finitely many finite places is divisible by m in E(F).

title: Standard Borel measurable space
description: A measurable space is standard Borel if it is measurably isomorphic to a Borel subset of a Polish space, with the induced Borel σ-algebra. Only the measurable structure, rather than a chosen compatible topology, is part of this definition.

title: Ergodic decomposition on a standard Borel probability space
description: If T is a probability-preserving measurable self-map of a standard Borel space (X,B,μ), there is a probability kernel x↦μ_x with μ=∫μ_xdμ(x), and μ_x is T-invariant and ergodic for μ-almost every x. It can be chosen as a regular conditional distribution of the identity given the invariant σ-algebra I, so ∫f dμ_x=E_μ[f|I](x) almost surely for every bounded Borel f; the kernel is unique up to a common μ-null set.

title: Future conditional formula for relative entropy rate
description: For a probability-preserving T, finite partition ξ and strictly T-invariant sub-σ-algebra A, the relative rate lim_(n→∞)n⁻¹H_μ(∨_(j=0)^(n−1)T^(−j)ξ|A) equals H_μ(ξ|A∨∨_(j≥1)T^(−j)ξ).

title: Countable generation modulo a standard Borel probability
description: For a probability μ on a standard Borel space and any sub-σ-algebra A, there exists a countably generated sub-σ-algebra C⊆A such that every A-set agrees μ-almost everywhere with some C-set. Thus C and A have the same μ-completion within the ambient completed probability space.

title: Entropy is affine under ergodic decomposition
description: For a probability-preserving measurable T on a standard Borel probability space, let μ=∫μ_xdμ(x) be its ergodic decomposition. Then h_μ(T)=∫h_(μ_x)(T)dμ(x), allowing +∞. For every finite measurable partition ξ one likewise has h_μ(T,ξ)=∫h_(μ_x)(T,ξ)dμ(x).

title: Gelfand–Mazur theorem
description: Every nonzero complex unital Banach algebra in which every nonzero element is invertible consists precisely of the scalar multiples of its identity, so the scalar map C→A, λ↦λ1, is an algebra isomorphism. It is isometric when ||1||=1.

title: Spectral radius of a normal C*-algebra element
description: For every normal element a of a complex C*-algebra, its norm equals the spectral radius sup{|λ|:λ∈σ(a)}, with spectrum computed in a unitization if necessary.

title: Neumann series in a unital Banach algebra
description: If a lies in a unital Banach algebra and ||a||<1, then1−a is invertible and (1−a)^(−1)=Σ_(n≥0)a^n in norm.

title: Uniform local injectivity of a discrete quotient on compact sets
description: Let Γ be a discrete subgroup of a locally compact Hausdorff group G and q:G→Γ∖G. For every compact Ω⊆Γ∖G there is an open identity neighborhood V⊆G such that q is injective on gV whenever q(g)∈Ω.

title: Entropy scaling under iterates and inversion
description: For a probability-preserving transformation T, h_μ(Tᵏ)=k h_μ(T) for every integer k≥1. If T is invertible with measurable inverse, h_μ(T⁻¹)=h_μ(T), and therefore h_μ(Tᵏ)=|k|h_μ(T) for every nonzero integer k, allowing infinite entropy.

title: One-point compactification of a locally compact space
description: For a noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space Y, its one-point compactification is Y∪{∞}, whose opens are the open subsets of Y together with complements of compact closed subsets of Y. It is compact Hausdorff; if Y is second countable it is metrizable.

title: Properness of a compact-group quotient
description: If a compact topological group K acts continuously on a Hausdorff space Y, the orbit quotient map q:Y→Y/K is closed and has compact fibers; in particular q⁻¹(C) is compact for every compact C⊆Y/K.

title: State-space entropy bound for limits with Bowen-ball separation
description: Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact with open normalizer, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹. Assume the Markov module property,0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1, Haar a-homogeneity and finite h_m(S). Let S-invariant Radon probabilities μ_i converge weakly to a probability μ. Suppose a compact-set family F satisfies sup_(Ω∈F)limsup_iμ_i(Ω)=1, and for every Ω∈F there are an open identity neighborhood B, t_i→∞ and C_Ω>0 with ∫_Ωμ_i(yB^(−t_i,t_i))dμ_i(y)≤C_Ωe^(−2ht_i), h>0. For continuous X-measurable0≤φ≤1, or an open/closed X-indicator, put u=μφ,p=mφ∈(0,1). If θ=λᵏ, k≥1, then D(u‖θ+(1−θ)p)/(−logθ)≤(h_m(S)−h)/(−logλ) when p

title: State expectations controlled by an entropy deficit
description: Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact with open normalizer, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹. Assume the Markov module property,0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1, Haar a-homogeneity and finite Haar entropy h_m(S) maximal among S-invariant probabilities. Every S-invariant Radon probability μ and continuous X-measurable0≤φ≤1 satisfy |μφ−mφ|≤sqrt((h_m(S)−h_μ(S))/(−2logλ))sqrt(−logθ)+θ for every θ=λᵏ, k≥1.

title: Non-escape of mass from a state-space norm gap and entropy
description: Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact with open normalizer, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹. Assume the Markov module property,0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1, Haar a-homogeneity and finite Haar entropy h_m(S) maximal among S-invariant probabilities. If S-invariant Radon probabilities μ_i converge vaguely to a Radon measure μ and h=liminf_i h_(μ_i)(S), then μ(Y)≥1−(h_m(S)−h)/(−logλ).

title: Local Artin norm quotient and inertia image
description: Let K be a finite extension ofℚ_p and L/K a finite abelian extension. The local Artin map induces K×/N_(L/K)(L×)≅Gal(L/K). Under this map, the image of O_K× is precisely the inertia subgroup of Gal(L/K). The normalization sends a uniformizer to arithmetic Frobenius on every unramified subextension.

title: Unit norm criterion for unramified local abelian extensions
description: Let K be a finite extension ofℚ_p and L/K a finite abelian extension. Then O_K×⊆N_(L/K)(L×) if and only if L/K is unramified. The trivial extension is included.

title: Imaginary quadratic fields unramified outside two
description: An imaginary quadratic extension E/ℚ is unramified at every odd finite prime if and only if E=ℚ(i) or E=ℚ(√−2).

title: Jacobs–de Leeuw–Glicksberg minimal group for Hilbert contractions
description: Let S be a nonempty weak-operator-closed semigroup of contractions on a Hilbert space. Then S is weakly compact and has a unique minimal idempotent Q, an orthogonal projection commuting with S. The minimal ideal QS=SQ is a compact topological group with identity Q, on which strong and weak operator topologies coincide.

title: Hilbert tensor products as Hilbert–Schmidt operators
description: There is a canonical unitary identification H⊗K≅HS(K̄,H) for complex Hilbert spaces: x⊗y corresponds to the rank-one map z̄↦⟨y,z⟩x when inner products are linear in their first argument. Under this identification U⊗V acts by A↦U A V̄*, for unitary U,V.

title: Hilbert–Schmidt operators are compact
description: Every Hilbert–Schmidt operator between Hilbert spaces is compact, and is the limit of finite-rank operators in Hilbert–Schmidt norm and hence in operator norm.

title: Connected semisimple algebraic group
