F is mixed of weights ≤n if it is an iterated extension of pointwise pure sheaves of weights ≤n. The constant sheaf Q_ℓ is pure of weight 0.

title: Deligne’s purity theorem for lisse sheaves on curves
description: Let X₀ be a projective smooth curve over F_q, j:U₀→X₀ a dense open immersion and F a lisse Q_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ that is pointwise ι-pure of weight β. Then every eigenvalue of Frobenius on H¹(X,j_*F) is ι-pure of weight β+1 (Weil II, Theorem 3.2.3).

title: Higher direct images with proper support
description: For a separated morphism of finite type f:X→S, factored as an open immersion j:X→X̄ followed by a proper f̄:X̄→S, and a torsion étale sheaf F on X, R^if_!F=R^if̄_*(j_!F), independent of the factorization. When S is the spectrum of a separably closed field these are the compactly supported cohomology groups.

title: Proper base change theorem in étale cohomology
description: For a proper morphism f:X→S, a torsion étale sheaf F on X and a morphism g:S′→S with base change f′, the base change maps g^(−1)R^if_*F→R^if′_*(g′^(−1)F) are isomorphisms; in particular the stalk of R^if_*F at a geometric point s̄ is H^i(X_s̄,F). Consequently R^if_! commutes with arbitrary base change for separated finite-type f.

title: Leray spectral sequence for proper-support direct images
description: For separated finite-type morphisms g:X→Y and h:Y→Z and a torsion or ℓ-adic étale sheaf F on X, there is a spectral sequence E₂^(p,q)=R^ph_!(R^qg_!F)⇒R^(p+q)(h∘g)_!F.

title: Deligne’s weight theorem for the local monodromy filtration
description: Let F be a lisse Q_ℓ-sheaf on a dense open of a smooth curve over F_q, pointwise ι-pure of weight β, and s a point of the complement. Then the graded pieces Gr_i^M of the local monodromy filtration on the geometric generic stalk at s are ι-pure of weight β+i as representations of the local Weil group (Weil II, Theorem 1.8.4).

title: Topological invariance of the étale site
description: A universal homeomorphism of schemes Y→X, for example a nilpotent thickening or a purely inseparable base field extension, induces an equivalence between the small étale sites of X and Y; hence étale cohomology does not change under such a base change.

title: Katz bound on compact Betti numbers of affine schemes
description: Over an algebraically closed field, let V⊂Aᴺ be defined by r polynomials of degree ≤d, and suppose E(N,r,d) bounds |χ_c| for all such affine schemes. Put A(N,r,d)=E(N,r,d)+2+2Σ_(n<N)E(n,r,d) and B(N,r,d)=1+Σ_(∅≠S⊆{1..r})A(N+1,1,1+d|S|). Then Σ_i dim H^i_c(V,Q_ℓ)≤B(N,r,d) for every ℓ invertible in k (Katz, Theorem 1).

title: Adolphson–Sperber bound for the ℓ-adic Euler characteristic
description: If V⊂Aᴺ over an algebraically closed field is defined by r polynomials of degree at most d and ℓ is invertible, then |χ_c(V,Q_ℓ)|≤2^r·D_(N,r)(1,1+d,…,1+d)≤2^r(r+1+rd)^N, where D_(N,r) is the sum of all monomials of degree N in r+1 variables.

title: Excision sequence for compactly supported cohomology
description: For a separated scheme X of finite type over a separably closed field, an open U⊆X with closed complement Z, and a torsion or ℓ-adic sheaf F, there is a functorial long exact sequence ⋯→H^i_c(U,F)→H^i_c(X,F)→H^i_c(Z,F)→H^(i+1)_c(U,F)→⋯, Galois-equivariant when everything is defined over a subfield.

title: Bertini theorem for general linear sections
description: Let X⊂Pᴺ be a closed subvariety over an algebraically closed field and r≤dim X. For E in a nonempty Zariski-open set of codimension-r linear subspaces, X∩E is a proper linear section of dimension dim X−r that is reduced, irreducible if dim X>r, of degree deg X, and whose singular locus has dimension dim Sing X−r (empty if dim Sing X<r).

title: Weak Lefschetz theorem in high degrees via the Gysin map
description: Let X be an irreducible projective scheme of dimension n over a perfect field and Y⊂X a proper linear section of codimension r that is a nonsingular variety. Then the Gysin map H^(i−2r)(Ȳ,Q_ℓ(−r))→H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ) is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism for i≥n+r+1 and surjective for i=n+r.

title: Cohomology of nonsingular projective complete intersections
description: If X⊂Pᴺ is a nonsingular complete intersection of dimension n over a separably closed field and ℓ is invertible, then the restriction H^i(Pᴺ,Q_ℓ)→H^i(X,Q_ℓ) is an isomorphism for all i≠n with 0≤i≤2n, so only H^n can have primitive part; its dimension depends only on N and the multidegree.

title: Artin vanishing theorem for affine schemes
description: For an affine scheme X of finite type over a separably closed field and a torsion étale sheaf F, H^i(X_et,F)=0 for i>dim X. Consequently, by the Mayer–Vietoris spectral sequence, a separated scheme of finite type over such a field, of dimension n and covered by r affine opens, has H^i(X_et,F)=0 for i≥n+r.

title: Poincaré duality for ℓ-adic cohomology of smooth varieties
description: For a smooth separated scheme X of pure dimension d over a separably closed field and ℓ invertible, cup product and the trace map give a perfect pairing H^i_c(X,Q_ℓ)×H^(2d−i)(X,Q_ℓ(d))→Q_ℓ, compatible with Galois actions when X is defined over a subfield.

title: ℓ-adic cohomology of projective space
description: For projective space Pᴺ over a field k with separable closure k̄ and ℓ invertible in k, H^i(Pᴺ_k̄,Q_ℓ) is isomorphic as a Galois module to Q_ℓ(−i/2) for even 0≤i≤2N and is zero otherwise.

title: Complete intersections are Cohen–Macaulay
description: A Noetherian local ring that is the quotient of a regular local ring by an ideal generated by a regular sequence is Cohen–Macaulay. Hence every projective complete intersection over a field is a Cohen–Macaulay scheme.

title: Connectedness of positive-dimensional projective complete intersections
description: A projective complete intersection of dimension at least one over a field is connected; indeed H⁰(X,O_X)=k (Hartshorne, Exercise III.5.5).

title: Serre’s criterion for normality
description: A Noetherian ring or scheme is normal if and only if it satisfies Serre’s conditions (R₁), regularity of the local rings of dimension at most one, and (S₂), depth of each local ring at least min(2, its dimension). In particular a Cohen–Macaulay scheme regular in codimension one is normal.

title: Normal Noetherian schemes are disjoint unions of integral schemes
description: A Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes. In particular a connected normal Noetherian scheme is integral.

title: Bounded denominators of rational Siegel modular forms
description: If a scalar-valued Siegel modular form of degree g and weight k for Sp_2g(ℤ) has all Fourier coefficients c(T) rational, then it has bounded denominators: some positive integer l makes every l·c(T) an integer. This is a consequence of the arithmetic theory of Chai–Faltings (q-expansion principle).

title: Chain in a partially ordered set
description: A chain in a partially ordered set P is a subset C⊆P that is totally ordered by the restricted order, so any two elements of C are comparable. The empty set is a chain.

title: Upper bound of a subset of a partially ordered set
description: An upper bound of a subset A of a partially ordered set P is an element b∈P with a≤b for every a∈A; b need not belong to A.

title: Maximal element of a partially ordered set
description: An element m of a partially ordered set P is maximal if no x∈P satisfies m<x, that is, m≤x implies x=m. Unlike a greatest element, a maximal element need not be comparable with every element and need not be unique.

title: Axiom of choice
description: The set-theoretic axiom that every family of nonempty sets indexed by a set has a choice function, assigning to each index an element of the corresponding set; equivalently, a Cartesian product of nonempty sets is nonempty.

title: Hartogs’ lemma on ordinals not injecting into a set
description: For every set X there is an ordinal α admitting no injection into X, equivalently not in bijection with any subset of X. The proof uses the replacement axiom but not the axiom of choice.

title: Well-founded recursion theorem
description: Let X be a partially ordered set in which every nonempty subset has a minimal element, T a set, and r a rule assigning an element of T to each x∈X and function {y:y<x}→T. Then there is a unique f:X→T with f(x)=r(x,f|{y:y<x}) for all x. For ordinals this is transfinite recursion.

title: Order-preserving map between partially ordered sets
description: A function f:P→Q between partially ordered sets is order-preserving (isotone, monotone) if x≤y implies f(x)≤f(y); it is strictly order-preserving if x<y implies f(x)<f(y).

title: Direct product of associative algebras over a field
description: For associative algebras A₁,…,A_n over a field k, the direct product A₁×⋯×A_n is their Cartesian product with componentwise addition, scalar multiplication and multiplication. It is an associative k-algebra with identity (1,…,1), also written A₁⊕⋯⊕A_n.

title: Homomorphism of Lie algebras
description: A linear map f:𝔤→𝔥 between Lie algebras over the same field satisfying f([x,y])=[f(x),f(y)] for all x,y∈𝔤. An isomorphism is a bijective homomorphism.

title: Nilpotent Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra 𝔤 is nilpotent if its lower central series 𝔤₁=𝔤, 𝔤ₖ₊₁=[𝔤,𝔤ₖ] (the linear span of all brackets [x,y] with x∈𝔤, y∈𝔤ₖ) reaches 0. It is m-step nilpotent if 𝔤ₘ₊₁=0, equivalently every iterated bracket [x₁,[x₂,…,[xₘ,xₘ₊₁]…]] vanishes.

title: Differential of a Lie group homomorphism
description: For a smooth group homomorphism φ:G→H of real Lie groups, its differential φ_*:Lie(G)→Lie(H) is the derivative of φ at the identity; equivalently it is the unique linear map with φ(exp_G(tX))=exp_H(tφ_*X) for all X∈Lie(G) and real t. It is a homomorphism of Lie algebras, and (ψ∘φ)_*=ψ_*∘φ_*.

title: Exponential coordinates on a real Lie group
description: For a real Lie group G, the exponential map exp_G:Lie(G)→G is smooth with derivative the identity at 0, and it restricts to a diffeomorphism from an open neighbourhood of 0 in Lie(G) onto an open neighbourhood of the identity in G.

title: Adjoint representation of a real Lie group
description: For a real Lie group G and g∈G, Ad_g:Lie(G)→Lie(G) is the differential of the conjugation h↦ghg⁻¹. Then g↦Ad_g is a smooth homomorphism G→GL(Lie(G)) with g·exp(X)·g⁻¹=exp(Ad_g X), and its differential is ad: X↦[X,·].

title: Adjoint exponential formula for a Lie group
description: For X in the Lie algebra of a real Lie group, Ad(exp X)=e^{ad X}=∑_{n≥0}(ad X)ⁿ/n!, where ad X=[X,·] is the adjoint endomorphism of the Lie algebra; equivalently exp(X)exp(Y)exp(−X)=exp(e^{ad X}Y).

title: Matrix logarithm near the identity
description: For a real or complex square matrix A with ∥A−I∥<1 in an operator norm, log A=∑_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}(A−I)ⁿ/n. The series converges absolutely and exp(log A)=A; on matrices near 0, log(exp B)=B.

title: Lie subgroup–subalgebra correspondence
description: For a real Lie group G, sending a connected Lie subgroup H (a subgroup carrying a Lie group structure for which the inclusion is an injective immersion, not necessarily closed) to its Lie algebra is a bijection onto the Lie subalgebras of Lie(G). Existence comes from integrating the left-invariant distribution of the subalgebra (Frobenius theorem).

title: Lie group homomorphisms with bijective differential are coverings
description: If φ:H→G is a smooth homomorphism of connected real Lie groups whose differential Lie(H)→Lie(G) is a linear isomorphism, then φ is surjective, its kernel is a discrete normal subgroup, and φ is a covering map.

title: Connected topological groups are generated by identity neighbourhoods
description: If G is a connected topological group and U is a neighbourhood of the identity, then the subgroup generated by U is all of G, since that subgroup is open and hence also closed.

title: Linearity and monotonicity of conditional expectation
description: For integrable real random variables X,Y, a real number a and a sub-σ-algebra G, E[aX+Y|G]=aE[X|G]+E[Y|G] almost surely, and X≤Y almost surely implies E[X|G]≤E[Y|G] almost surely.

title: Local time of a continuous semimartingale
description: For a real continuous semimartingale X and a level a∈ℝ, the local time L^a of X at a is the continuous nondecreasing adapted process with L^a_0=0 appearing in Tanaka's formula |X_t−a|=|X_0−a|+∫_0^t sgn(X_s−a)dX_s+L^a_t; it increases only on {t:X_t=a}. With sgn(0)=0 this is the symmetric local time; the convention sgn(0)=−1 gives the right local time.

title: Itô–Tanaka formula for a continuous semimartingale
description: If X is a real continuous semimartingale and f:ℝ→ℝ is a difference of two convex functions, with left derivative f′₋ and second-derivative measure f″(da), then f(X_t)=f(X_0)+∫_0^t f′₋(X_s)dX_s+½∫_ℝ L^a_t f″(da), where L^a are the right local times of X. In particular f(X) is a continuous semimartingale.

title: Logarithm of a positive definite complex matrix
description: For a positive definite matrix A=U diag(λ₁,…,λₙ)U* with U unitary, log A=U diag(log λ₁,…,log λₙ)U*; this Hermitian matrix does not depend on the chosen unitary diagonalization.

title: Relative entropy of positive definite matrices
description: For positive definite complex matrices A and H of the same size, the entropy of A relative to H is D(A;H)=tr[A(log A−log H)−(A−H)], with matrix logarithms defined by spectral calculus.

title: Nonnegativity of matrix relative entropy
description: For positive definite complex matrices A and H of the same size, tr[A(log A−log H)−(A−H)]≥0, with equality when A=H. Equivalently tr M=sup_{T≻0}tr[T log M−T log T+T] for every positive definite M.

title: Joint convexity of matrix relative entropy
description: The map (A,H)↦tr[A(log A−log H)−(A−H)] is jointly convex on pairs of positive definite complex matrices of the same size.

title: Tree (graph theory)
description: An undirected graph that is connected, meaning any two vertices are joined by a path, and acyclic, meaning it has no cycle: no closed path of positive length repeating no edge and no vertex other than its common endpoints. Equivalently, any two vertices are joined by exactly one simple path; in particular a tree has no loops or parallel edges.

title: Linear form over a field
description: For a field K, a linear form in n variables is a K-linear map L:Kⁿ→K, written L(x)=a₁x₁+⋯+a_nx_n with coefficients a_i∈K, or formally a₁X₁+⋯+a_nX_n. Linear forms are linearly independent when their coefficient vectors are.

title: Fully faithful functor
description: A functor F:C→D is fully faithful if for all objects X,Y of C the map Hom_C(X,Y)→Hom_D(FX,FY), f↦F(f), is bijective. For linear functors this means F induces isomorphisms of morphism spaces.

title: Dominant functor between additive categories
description: A functor F:C→D between additive categories is dominant if every object of D is isomorphic to a direct summand of F(X) for some object X of C. For semisimple categories this is the notion EGNO call a surjective functor.

title: Module functor between module categories
description: For module categories M,N over a monoidal category C, a module functor is a functor F:M→N with natural isomorphisms F(X⊗M)≅X⊗F(M) compatible with the associativity and unit constraints. Morphisms of module functors are natural transformations commuting with these isomorphisms; a module equivalence is a module functor that is an equivalence of categories.

title: Rational form of a module category
description: Let k⊂K be fields, D_K a fusion category over K with rational form D_k, and M_K a semisimple K-linear module category over D_K. A rational form of M_K over k is a semisimple k-linear module category M_k over D_k with an equivalence Kar(M_k⊗_kK)≃M_K of module categories, compatible with the given tensor equivalence Kar(D_k⊗_kK)≃D_K.

title: Algebra in a monoidal category
description: An object A of a monoidal category with a multiplication m:A⊗A→A and unit u:1→A such that m is associative, using the associativity constraint, and u is a two-sided unit for m. Morphisms of algebras preserve m and u.

title: Right module over an algebra in a monoidal category
description: For an algebra (A,m,u) in a monoidal category C, a right A-module is an object M of C with an action p:M⊗A→M that is associative with respect to m and unital with respect to u. Morphisms commute with the actions; the category Mod_C(A) is a left C-module category via X⊗M.

title: Bimodule over algebras in a monoidal category
description: For algebras A,B in a monoidal category C, an A–B bimodule is an object M of C with a left A-module action A⊗M→M and a right B-module action M⊗B→M that commute up to the associativity constraint. Bimodule morphisms commute with both actions.

title: Ostrik’s internal-End theorem for module categories
description: Let M be an indecomposable semisimple module category over a fusion category C and M a nonzero object of M. Then A=Hom̲(M,M), the internal endomorphism object, is an algebra in C, and N↦Hom̲(M,N) is an equivalence of C-module categories from M to the category Mod_C(A) of right A-modules in C.

title: Module functors between module-object categories as bimodules
description: For algebras A,B in a tensor category C, P↦(−)⊗_AP is an equivalence from the category of A–B bimodules in C to the category Fun_C(Mod_C(A),Mod_C(B)) of right exact C-module functors between the categories of right modules, with module natural transformations as morphisms.

title: Yoneda lemma
description: For an object U of a category C and a functor F:C^op→Set, natural transformations Hom(−,U)→F correspond bijectively to elements of F(U), via s↦s_U(id_U); dually for covariant functors. Hence the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful and a representing object of a representable functor is unique up to unique isomorphism.

title: Simplicial map between simplicial complexes
description: A simplicial map f:X→Y between abstract simplicial complexes is a function on vertices sending the vertex set of every simplex of X onto a simplex of Y, possibly of lower dimension. A retraction of X onto a subcomplex Y is a simplicial map X→Y restricting to the identity on Y.

title: Chamber complex
description: A chamber complex is an abstract simplicial complex in which every simplex lies in a maximal simplex, called a chamber, and any two chambers are joined by a gallery of chambers whose consecutive members share a codimension-one face. A chamber subcomplex is a subcomplex that is itself a chamber complex whose chambers are chambers of the ambient complex. It is thin, or thick, if every codimension-one face of a chamber lies in exactly two, or at least three, chambers.

title: Standard uniqueness lemma for chamber complex maps
description: Let X,Y be chamber complexes with every codimension-one face in Y contained in at most two chambers. If two chamber maps X→Y (simplicial maps sending chambers to chambers) agree pointwise on a chamber C and both send non-stuttering galleries starting at C to non-stuttering galleries, then they are equal.

title: Gate property for panels in a building
description: For a panel P of a building and a chamber D there is a unique chamber proj_P D containing P nearest to D, and d(C,D)=d(C,proj_P D)+d(proj_P D,D) for every chamber C⊇P. Thus for distinct chambers C,C′⊇P either one lies on a minimal gallery from the other to D, or d(C,D)=d(C′,D) and a third chamber of P begins minimal galleries to D from both.

title: Accumulation point of a subset of a topological space
description: A point x is an accumulation point of a subset A if every open set containing x contains a point of A different from x.

title: Multiplicativity of the determinant
description: For square matrices A and B of the same size over a commutative ring, det(AB)=det(A)det(B).

title: Transpose invariance of the determinant
description: A square matrix over a commutative ring and its transpose have the same determinant.

title: Fekete’s subadditive lemma
description: If a real sequence satisfies a_{m+n}≤a_m+a_n for all m,n≥1, then a_n/n converges to inf_{n≥1}a_n/n, which may be −∞.

title: Real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors of a self-adjoint operator
description: Every eigenvalue of a bounded self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space is real, and eigenvectors belonging to distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.

title: Existence of orthonormal bases in Hilbert spaces
description: Every orthonormal family in a Hilbert space extends to an orthonormal basis; in particular every Hilbert space, and every closed subspace of one, has an orthonormal basis.

title: Inclusion–exclusion formula for mixed volumes
description: For convex bodies K₁,…,K_d⊂ℝᵈ, d!V(K₁,…,K_d)=∑_{k=1}^d(−1)^{d+k}∑_{i₁<⋯<i_k}|K_{i₁}+⋯+K_{i_k}|, where |·| is Euclidean volume.

title: Hausdorff continuity of Minkowski addition
description: For nonempty compact sets A,A′,B,B′⊂ℝᵈ, the Hausdorff distance satisfies d_H(A+B,A′+B′)≤d_H(A,A′)+d_H(B,B′); hence Minkowski addition is continuous for Hausdorff convergence.

title: Finite Borel measures are determined by bounded continuous functions
description: Two finite Borel measures on a metric space are equal if they give the same integral to every bounded continuous real function.

title: Kolmogorov–Riesz compactness criterion in Lᵖ(ℝᵈ)
description: For 1≤p<∞, a subset F of Lᵖ(ℝᵈ) is relatively compact exactly when it is bounded, ∫_{|x|>R}|f|ᵖ→0 as R→∞ uniformly in f∈F, and ‖f(·−h)−f‖_p→0 as h→0 uniformly in f∈F.

title: Zero extension of H₀¹ functions
description: For an open Ω⊆ℝᵈ, extending u∈H₀¹(Ω) by zero outside Ω gives a function in H¹(ℝᵈ) whose weak gradient is the zero extension of ∇u; the extension map is an isometry H₀¹(Ω)→H¹(ℝᵈ).

title: Translation difference bound for first-order Sobolev functions
description: For 1≤p<∞, f∈W¹,ᵖ(ℝᵈ) and h∈ℝᵈ, ‖f(·−h)−f‖_{Lᵖ}≤|h|‖∇f‖_{Lᵖ}.

title: Completeness of L∞
description: For a measure space, L∞ with the essential-supremum norm is a Banach space.

title: Principal logarithm and principal powers on the slit plane
description: The principal logarithm Log is the holomorphic logarithm of z on ℂ∖(−∞,0] with Log 1=0, so Log z=ln|z|+i arg z with |arg z|<π. Principal powers are z^a=exp(a Log z) for complex a.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Analytic continuation along a path
description: Given a path γ:[0,1]→ℂ, an analytic continuation along γ is a family of holomorphic functions f_t on open disks containing γ(t) such that f_t and f_s agree on the overlap of their disks whenever s is close to t; f_1 continues f_0 along γ.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Orthonormal polynomials of a complex weight on the real line
description: For a complex-valued weight w on ℝ with ∫|x|^k|w(x)|dx<∞, orthonormal polynomials are complex polynomials p_j(x)=κ_jx^j+⋯ with κ_j≠0 and ∫p_j(x)p_k(x)w(x)dx=δ_jk. The pairing is bilinear, without complex conjugation; for w≥0 this is the usual orthonormal sequence.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Complex sine function
description: The entire function sin z=(e^{iz}−e^{−iz})/(2i), which restricts to the real sine function on ℝ.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Fundamental pair of solutions of a second-order linear complex ODE
description: For y″+p(z)y′+q(z)y=0 with p,q holomorphic on a complex domain U, a fundamental pair is two holomorphic solutions y₁,y₂ on U whose Wronskian y₁y₂′−y₁′y₂ vanishes nowhere.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Oriented contour in the complex plane
description: A finite union of oriented arcs in ℂ, each the image of an injective C¹ map with nonvanishing derivative from a compact interval or a half-line, meeting only at endpoints. The left side of each arc is its + side and the right side its − side; the contour carries arc-length measure |dz|.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Nontangential boundary values on an oriented contour
description: For f holomorphic on ℂ∖Σ, with Σ an oriented contour, f_±(s) is the limit of f(z) as z→s within a sector of opening less than π on the + (left) or − (right) side of Σ at a non-endpoint s, when it exists.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Cauchy integral on an oriented contour
description: For an oriented contour Σ and h on Σ with ∫_Σ|h(s)||ds|/(1+|s|)<∞, the Cauchy integral is (Ch)(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_Σh(s)/(s−z)ds for z∉Σ.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Weierstrass product for the gamma function
description: 1/Γ(z)=z e^{γz}∏_{n≥1}(1+z/n)e^{−z/n} for all z∈ℂ, with γ the Euler–Mascheroni constant; the product converges locally uniformly. Logarithmic differentiation gives Γ′(z+1)/Γ(z+1)=−γ+∑_{k≥1}[1/k−1/(z+k)].
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Fundamental theorem for complex line integrals
description: If F is holomorphic on an open set G with F′=f continuous and γ⊂G is a piecewise C¹ path from a to b, then ∫_γf(z)dz=F(b)−F(a).
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Andréief integration formula
description: For a measure space (I,μ) and functions f_0,…,f_{N−1},φ_0,…,φ_{N−1} with every f_jφ_k integrable, ∫_{I^N}det[f_j(x_k)]det[φ_j(x_k)]dμ(x_1)⋯dμ(x_N)=N!det[∫_If_jφ_kdμ]_{j,k=0}^{N−1}.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Length–maximum estimate for complex line integrals
description: For a piecewise C¹ path γ and f continuous on γ, |∫_γf(z)dz|≤max_{z∈γ}|f(z)|·length(γ).
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Holomorphic functions with zero derivative on a region are constant
description: If f is complex differentiable with f′=0 everywhere on a connected open subset of ℂ, then f is constant there.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Bessel function of the first kind
description: J_ν(z)=∑_{k≥0}(−1)^k(z/2)^{ν+2k}/(k!Γ(k+ν+1)) on the slit plane with principal powers, a solution of Bessel’s equation z²y″+zy′+(z²−ν²)y=0.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Hankel functions (Bessel functions of the third kind)
description: H_ν^{(1)}=J_ν+iY_ν and H_ν^{(2)}=J_ν−iY_ν, where for nonintegral ν Y_ν=[J_ν cos νπ−J_{−ν}]/sin νπ, with integer orders by continuity in ν.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Hankel’s large-argument expansions of Bessel and Hankel functions
description: As |z|→∞, H_ν^{(1)}(z)∼(2/(πz))^{1/2}e^{i(z−νπ/2−π/4)}∑_m i^m(ν,m)(2z)^{−m} for −π+δ≤arg z≤2π−δ, with the conjugate expansion for H_ν^{(2)} on −2π+δ≤arg z≤π−δ, where (ν,m)=Γ(ν+m+1/2)/(m!Γ(ν−m+1/2)); the corresponding expansions of J_ν follow.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Connection formulas for modified Bessel functions
description: I_ν(z)=e^{∓νπi/2}J_ν(ze^{±πi/2}) for the appropriate ranges of arg z, and K_ν(z)=(πi/2)e^{νπi/2}H_ν^{(1)}(iz)=−(πi/2)e^{−νπi/2}H_ν^{(2)}(−iz).
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Zero set of a nonzero polynomial is Lebesgue-null
description: The set of zeros in ℝⁿ of a polynomial in n real variables that is not identically zero is closed and has Lebesgue measure zero.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Resultant of two univariate polynomials
description: The resultant of f=a_mx^m+⋯ and g=b_nx^n+⋯ is the determinant of their (m+n)×(m+n) Sylvester coefficient matrix. Over an algebraically closed field with a_mb_n≠0 it vanishes exactly when f and g have a common root.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Discriminant of a univariate polynomial
description: For f=a_n∏(x−r_i) of degree n, disc f=a_n^{2n−2}∏_{i<j}(r_i−r_j)², a polynomial in the coefficients of f; it vanishes exactly when f has a repeated root.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Cauchy–Binet formula
description: For an n×m matrix A and an m×n matrix B over a commutative ring with m≥n, det(AB)=∑_S det(A_{·S})det(B_{S·}), summing over n-element subsets S of the m indices.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Floor of a real number
description: For a real number x, its floor ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer n with n≤x.

title: Orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of a Hilbert space
description: A real or complex Hilbert space H is the orthogonal direct sum ⊕_m H_m of a sequence of closed subspaces when the H_m are pairwise orthogonal and every x∈H is a norm-convergent sum ∑_m x_m with x_m∈H_m; the expansion is then unique. For pairwise orthogonal closed subspaces this holds exactly when their linear span is dense.

title: Sequential characterization of continuity in metric spaces
description: A map f:X→Y between metric spaces is continuous at x, in the ε–δ sense, exactly when f(x_n)→f(x) for every sequence x_n→x in X. Consequently f is continuous for the metric topologies exactly when it is sequentially continuous at every point.

title: Lower and upper Darboux integrals
description: For bounded f:[a,b]→ℝ and a partition a=x₀<⋯<x_n=b, the lower and upper Darboux sums are ∑m_i(x_i−x_{i−1}) and ∑M_i(x_i−x_{i−1}), where m_i and M_i are the infimum and supremum of f on [x_{i−1},x_i]. The lower (upper) Darboux integral is the supremum of all lower sums (infimum of all upper sums).

title: Equivalence of the Riemann and Darboux integrals
description: A bounded f:[a,b]→ℝ is Riemann integrable, in the sense that its tagged Riemann sums converge as the mesh tends to zero, exactly when its lower and upper Darboux integrals are equal; the common value is then the Riemann integral.

title: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for real inner-product spaces
description: In a real inner-product space, ⟨u,v⟩²≤⟨u,u⟩⟨v,v⟩ for all vectors u,v.

title: Extension of bounded linear maps from dense subspaces
description: If D is a dense linear subspace of a normed space X and T:D→Y is a bounded linear map into a Banach space Y, then T has a unique bounded linear extension X→Y, and the extension has the same operator norm. In particular a linear isometry from D extends to a linear isometry on X.

title: Green’s second identity
description: For a bounded open set Ω⊂ℝⁿ with C¹ boundary and functions u,v that are C² on a neighbourhood of its closure, ∫_Ω(uΔv−vΔu)dx=∫_{∂Ω}(u∂_νv−v∂_νu)dS, where ∂_ν is the derivative along the outward unit normal and dS is surface measure.

title: Gibbs’ inequality for relative entropy
description: For probability distributions p and q on the same finite set, the relative entropy satisfies D(p∥q)≥0, with equality exactly when p=q.

title: Tate–Shafarevich group of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K, Sha(A/K)=ker[H¹(K,A)→∏_vH¹(K_v,A)], where H¹(K,A)=H¹(Gal(K̄/K),A(K̄)) with the discrete Galois module of geometric points and v runs over all finite and infinite places. Localization restricts cocycles along compatible embeddings K̄→K̄_v. Finiteness is not part of the definition.

title: Continuous cohomology of a profinite group with topological coefficients
description: For a profinite group G acting continuously on a topological abelian group M, Hⁿ_cont(G,M) is the cohomology of the complex of continuous maps Gⁿ→M with the inhomogeneous coboundary. For discrete M it is ordinary profinite cohomology; for ℚ_p-vector spaces with p-adic topology it gives the Galois cohomology used for p-adic representations.

title: Fontaine's crystalline period ring
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, B_cris=A_cris[1/p][1/t], where A_cris is the p-adic completion of the divided-power envelope of the Witt-vector ring W(O_(ℂ_p)^♭) along the kernel of Fontaine's map θ:W(O_(ℂ_p)^♭)→O_(ℂ_p), and t=log[ε] for a compatible system ε of p-power roots of unity. It is a ℚ_p-algebra with continuous G_K-action and Frobenius.

title: Bloch–Kato Selmer group of a p-adic Galois representation
description: For a number field K and a G_K-stable ℤ_p-lattice T in a continuous p-adic representation V, Sel(K,T)⊂H¹(K,V/T) is the set of classes whose localization at each place v lies in the image of H¹_f(K_v,V). Here H¹_f is 0 at archimedean v, the unramified classes ker[H¹(K_v,V)→H¹(K_v^ur,V)] at v∤p, and ker[H¹(K_v,V)→H¹(K_v,B_cris⊗V)] at v|p, using continuous cohomology.

title: Ample invertible sheaf
description: An invertible sheaf L on a scheme X of finite type over a field is ample if for every coherent sheaf F the sheaves F⊗L^(⊗n) are generated by global sections for all large n. For proper X this holds exactly when some tensor power L^(⊗n), n≥1, is very ample.

title: Projectivity of abelian varieties
description: Every abelian variety over a field has an ample invertible sheaf, and hence is projective; the sheaf can be chosen symmetric, L≅[−1]*L.

title: Dual abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a field k, the dual A^∨ is the abelian variety representing the identity component Pic⁰ of the Picard functor, with the Poincaré sheaf on A×A^∨ as universal family. A homomorphism f:A→B induces f^∨:B^∨→A^∨ by pulling back invertible sheaves.

title: Mumford homomorphism of an invertible sheaf on an abelian variety
description: For an invertible sheaf L on an abelian variety A, φ_L:A→A^∨ sends a point a to the class of t_a*L⊗L⁻¹. By the theorem of the square it is a homomorphism, and f^∨∘φ_L∘f=φ_(f*L) for every homomorphism f:B→A.

title: Mumford homomorphism of an ample sheaf is an isogeny
description: If L is an ample invertible sheaf on an abelian variety A, then φ_L:A→A^∨ has finite kernel and is an isogeny. In particular, for an abelian subvariety B⊆A the restriction L|_B is ample and φ_(L|B) is an isogeny.

title: Identity component of a group scheme over a field
description: For a group scheme G of finite type over a field k, G⁰ is the connected component of G containing the identity. It is an open and closed geometrically connected subgroup scheme of finite index; over a perfect field its reduced subscheme is a smooth subgroup scheme.

title: Weak Mordell–Weil theorem for an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K and an integer n≥2, the quotient A(K)/nA(K) is finite.

title: Néron–Tate height pairing on an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K and a symmetric ample invertible sheaf L, the limit ĥ_L(P)=lim 4^(−n)h_L(2ⁿP) of Weil heights is a quadratic form on A(K). Its bilinear pairing is symmetric and positive semidefinite, and {P∈A(K):ĥ_L(P)≤C} is finite for every real C.

title: Multiplication by n on an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A of dimension g over a field k and an integer n≥1, multiplication by n is an isogeny of degree n^(2g), étale exactly when char k does not divide n. In particular it is surjective on points over a separable closure when char k∤n.

title: Profinite group cohomology commutes with direct limits
description: For a profinite group G and a direct system of discrete G-modules M_i indexed by a directed set, the natural map lim→Hⁿ(G,M_i)→Hⁿ(G,lim→M_i) is an isomorphism for every n≥0.

title: Exactness of direct limits of abelian groups
description: Direct limits over a directed set carry exact sequences of directed systems of modules over a commutative ring, in particular of abelian groups, to exact sequences: if L_i→M_i→N_i is exact for every i, compatibly with the transition maps, then lim→L_i→lim→M_i→lim→N_i is exact.

title: Splitting of the tensor square of a finite Galois extension
description: For a finite Galois extension L/k with group G, the map L⊗_kL→∏_(σ∈G)L, a⊗b↦(aσ(b))_σ, is an isomorphism of L-algebras. Equivalently, Spec L×_(Spec k)Spec L is a disjoint union of copies of Spec L indexed by G.

title: Descent of morphisms along fpqc coverings
description: For an fpqc covering {T_i→T} of schemes and any scheme S, morphisms T_i→S whose restrictions agree on every T_i×_TT_j glue to a unique morphism T→S. Equivalently every representable functor is a sheaf for the fpqc topology.

title: Eichler–Shimura congruence relation
description: For a prime p not dividing N, on the reduction of the Jacobian J₁(N) modulo p the Hecke operator T_p equals F+⟨p⟩F^∨, where F is the Frobenius endomorphism, F^∨ its dual (Verschiebung) and ⟨p⟩ the diamond operator. For J₀(N) this reads T_p=F+F^∨.

title: Good reduction of X₁(N) away from the level
description: For N≥5 the modular curve X₁(N) has a smooth proper model over ℤ[1/N]; hence X₁(N) and its Jacobian J₁(N) have good reduction at every prime not dividing N.

title: Weil pairing on an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over k and n prime to char k, there is a nondegenerate bilinear Galois-equivariant pairing e_n:A[n]×A^∨[n]→μ_n, compatible as n varies. Composition with a polarization gives pairings on A[n] and on Tate modules with values in roots of unity or ℤ_ℓ(1).

title: Carayol local–global compatibility for modular forms
description: Let F be totally real and π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F) whose archimedean components are discrete series D_(k_τ,w) with all k_τ≥2 of the parity of w, as for a Hilbert newform, in particular a classical newform of weight ≥2 over ℚ; if [F:ℚ] is even, assume π_v essentially square-integrable at some finite v. Then π has a strictly compatible system of two-dimensional λ-adic Galois representations whose restriction to the Weil group at each finite place 𝔭 of residue characteristic different from λ's is the λ-adic realization of the Weil–Deligne representation attached to π_𝔭 by the Hecke-normalized local Langlands correspondence. Hence its local L-factor and conductor at 𝔭 are those of π_𝔭.

title: Serre's modularity conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger theorem)
description: Every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible representation ρ̄:Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)→GL₂(F̄_p) arises from a normalized cuspidal eigenform of Serre's weight k(ρ̄) and prime-to-p Artin conductor level N(ρ̄).

title: Faltings's isogeny theorem for abelian varieties over number fields
description: For abelian varieties A,B over a number field K and a prime ℓ, the map Hom_K(A,B)⊗ℤ_ℓ→Hom_(G_K)(T_ℓA,T_ℓB) is an isomorphism and V_ℓA is a semisimple G_K-module. For all but finitely many ℓ the mod-ℓ analogue Hom_K(A,B)⊗F_ℓ≅Hom_(G_K)(A[ℓ],B[ℓ]) holds and A[ℓ] is semisimple.

title: λ-adic representations of an abelian variety of GL₂-type
description: For an abelian variety A/ℚ whose endomorphism algebra contains a number field E with [E:ℚ]=dim A, V_ℓ(A) is free of rank two over E⊗ℚ_ℓ. For each prime λ|ℓ of E, V_λ(A)=V_ℓ(A)⊗_(E⊗ℚ_ℓ)E_λ is a two-dimensional E_λ-linear G_ℚ-representation ρ_λ, and an O_E-stable model gives mod-λ reductions on A[λ].

title: Finite dimensionality of weight-two cusp forms
description: For every N≥1 the space S₂(Γ₁(N)) of weight-two cusp forms is finite-dimensional; its dimension is the genus of X₁(N). Consequently there are only finitely many normalized newforms of weight two and level dividing a given integer.

title: Endomorphism algebra of the modular abelian variety of a newform
description: For a normalized weight-two newform f with coefficient field K_f, the modular abelian variety A_f has dimension [K_f:ℚ], and End⁰_ℚ(A_f) is the image of the Hecke algebra, isomorphic to K_f. In particular A_f is ℚ-simple of GL₂-type.

title: Isogeny decomposition of J₁(N) into modular abelian varieties
description: The Jacobian J₁(N) is ℚ-isogenous to a product of modular abelian varieties A_f, with f ranging over Galois-conjugacy classes of normalized weight-two newforms of level M dividing N, each A_f occurring with multiplicity the number of divisors of N/M.

title: Poitou–Tate exact sequence
description: For a number field K, a finite set S of places containing the archimedean places and those above p, and a finite G_(K,S)-module M of p-power order, there is a nine-term exact sequence linking Hⁱ(G_(K,S),M), ∏_(v∈S)Hⁱ(K_v,M) and the Pontryagin duals H^(2−i)(G_(K,S),M′)^∨, where M′=Hom(M,μ). Kato uses its versions for lattices and divisible modules.

title: Local Tate duality
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a finite discrete G_K-module M, cup product followed by the invariant H²(K,μ)≅ℚ/ℤ gives perfect pairings Hⁱ(K,M)×H^(2−i)(K,Hom(M,μ))→ℚ/ℤ for 0≤i≤2.

title: Kato's explicit reciprocity law for zeta elements
description: For a newform f of weight k≥2 and a λ-adic lattice in its Galois realization, Kato's zeta elements in Iwasawa cohomology over the cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower are related by the Bloch–Kato dual exponential at p to period-normalized critical L-values L(f,χ,r), 1≤r≤k−1, for finite-order characters χ.

title: Kato's Euler-system bound
description: For a lattice T in a two-dimensional odd p-adic representation of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) satisfying irreducibility, purity and big-image hypotheses, an Euler system over cyclotomic fields with nonzero Iwasawa-theoretic bottom class bounds the length of the second Iwasawa cohomology by the index of the module generated by the Euler system (Kato, Theorem 13.4).

title: Discriminant locus of projective complete intersections
description: For a field K, integers N≥1 and 1≤c≤N+1, and degrees d₁,…,d_c≥1, let V be the affine space of c-tuples (F₁,…,F_c) of homogeneous polynomials in N+1 variables with deg F_i=d_i. The discriminant locus D⊂V is the Zariski-closed set of tuples for which {F₁=⋯=F_c=0}⊂P^N over an algebraic closure is not a smooth complete intersection of codimension c: either the codimension is smaller or the Jacobian matrix (∂F_i/∂x_j) has rank <c at a common zero. It carries its reduced structure; when D is a hypersurface its equation is the discriminant.

title: General point of an algebraic variety
description: A property holds at a general point of an algebraic variety X, or for a general member of a family parametrized by X, if it holds at every point of some dense Zariski-open subset of X. If X is irreducible, every nonempty open subset is dense and finitely many such conditions can be imposed simultaneously.

title: Completed local ring at a point of a scheme
description: For a point x of a scheme X with local ring (O_{X,x},𝔪_x), the completed local ring is Ô_{X,x}=lim←O_{X,x}/𝔪_xⁿ, the inverse limit of the quotient rings under the reduction maps. At a k-rational point of a scheme smooth of dimension n over a field k it is isomorphic to the formal power series ring k[[t₁,…,tₙ]].

title: Ordinary double point
description: Let X be a scheme of finite type over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic different from two, and x a closed point at which X has dimension d. Then x is an ordinary double point of X if its completed local ring is isomorphic to k[[T₁,…,T_{d+1}]]/(Q) for a nondegenerate quadratic form Q in d+1 variables. Such a point is singular.

title: Lattice polytope
description: A lattice polytope in a real vector space (or affine space) equipped with a lattice is the convex hull of finitely many lattice points; it is a convex polytope whose vertices are lattice points.

title: Face of a convex polytope
description: For a convex polytope Q, the convex hull of finitely many points of a real affine space, a face is Q itself or a nonempty subset Q∩{ℓ=c} where ℓ is an affine function with ℓ≤c on Q. Faces are polytopes; dim Γ is the dimension of the affine span of Γ, and codim Γ=dim Q−dim Γ. Vertices are the zero-dimensional faces.

title: Projective toric variety of a lattice point configuration
description: Let T̃ be a split algebraic torus over a field K with character lattice X(T̃), let h:X(T̃)→ℤ be surjective, and let A⊂h⁻¹(1) be a finite set affinely generating the lattice h⁻¹(1). The affine toric variety X̃_A is the Zariski closure in K^A of {(χ(t))_{χ∈A}: t∈T̃}; it is a cone, and its projectivization X_A⊂P^{|A|−1} is the projective toric variety of A, with dense torus T=T̃/G_m and lattice polytope Q=conv(A)⊂h⁻¹(1)⊗ℝ. The torus T̃ acts on the dual coordinates (c_χ) by c_χ↦χ(t)⁻¹c_χ.

title: Projective dual variety and its discriminant
description: Let X⊂P^m be a closed irreducible subvariety over an algebraically closed field. Its conormal (incidence) variety W_X⊂P^m×P̌^m is the closure of the set of pairs (x,H) with x a smooth point of X and H a hyperplane containing the tangent space T_xX. The dual variety X^∨⊂P̌^m is the image of W_X under the second projection p₂. X is defective if X^∨ is not a hypersurface; otherwise the reduced homogeneous equation of X^∨, unique up to a scalar, is the discriminant of X (for a toric X_A, the A-discriminant Δ_A).

title: Degree of a generically finite dominant morphism
description: For a dominant morphism f:X→Y of integral schemes of finite type over a field with dim X=dim Y, the function field K(X) (the fraction field of the coordinate ring of any nonempty affine open) is a finite extension of K(Y) via f, and deg f=[K(X):K(Y)]. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a general point of Y has exactly deg f preimages.

title: Irreducibility of the complete-intersection discriminant locus
description: Over an algebraically closed field, the discriminant locus of c-tuples of homogeneous forms of degrees d₁,…,d_c in N+1 variables (those not cutting out a smooth codimension-c complete intersection of P^N) is irreducible. Benoist’s proof projects the incidence variety of pairs (tuple, common zero P at which the Jacobian matrix has rank <c), whose fibres over P^N are irreducible loci of rank-deficient matrices.

title: Versal deformation of an ordinary double point
description: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, the hypersurface Q(x₀,…,x_d)=t over the t-line, with Q a nondegenerate quadratic form, is a versal deformation of the ordinary double point Q=0 (SGA 7, Exposé XV). Consequently, in a flat family whose special fibre has an ordinary double point at x, the fibres near the special one have near x at most one singular point, and any such point is again an ordinary double point.

title: Bertini theorem for linear systems
description: Let X be a smooth quasi-projective variety over an algebraically closed field and L a finite-dimensional linear system of divisors on X with base locus B. In characteristic zero, a general member of L is smooth away from B. In arbitrary characteristic the same holds when the morphism X∖B→P(L^∨) defined by L is unramified.

title: Gelfand–Kapranov–Zelevinsky determinantal formula for the A-discriminant
description: Let X_A be a smooth projective toric variety with torus of dimension k−1, S⊂X(T̃) the semigroup generated by A, and for l≫0 let C^i(A,l)=⊕_{u∈S_{i+l}}Λ^i(Γ̃(u)_ℤ⊗K), Γ̃(u) the smallest face of the cone over Q containing u, with the differential ∂_f determined by f∈K^A. If X_A is not defective, Δ_A(f)^µ=det(C^•(A,l),∂_f)^{(−1)^k} up to a nonzero constant, where µ is the degree of the conormal projection W_{X_A}→X_A^∨ (µ=1 in characteristic zero); if X_A is defective the determinant is a nonzero constant.

title: Determinant of a based exact complex
description: For a bounded exact complex (W^•,d) of finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field with chosen bases e(i) of each W^i, its determinant (Cayley torsion) det(W^•,d,e)∈K^× is the alternating product of determinants of the isomorphisms induced by d between complements of the images, computed in the chosen bases. Changing bases by transition matrices M(i) multiplies it by ∏_i det M(i)^{(−1)^i}.

title: Ehrhart’s theorem on lattice-point counts
description: For a lattice polytope P of dimension d, the number of lattice points of its dilate lP is a polynomial in the integer l≥0 of degree d, whose leading coefficient is the volume of P normalized by the lattice (Euclidean volume relative to a fundamental domain of the lattice in the affine span).

title: Serre vanishing theorem
description: If X is a projective scheme over a Noetherian ring with very ample invertible sheaf O(1) and F is a coherent sheaf on X, then H^i(X,F⊗O(l))=0 for all i>0 and all sufficiently large l. In particular, for a closed subscheme X⊂P^m the restriction maps H⁰(P^m,O(l))→H⁰(X,O(l)) are surjective for l≫0.

title: Sections of O(l) on a normal projective toric variety
description: If the projective toric variety X_A of a lattice point configuration A is normal, then for every l≥0 the torus-eigenvectors of H⁰(X_A,O(l)) are the characters u lying in the lattice points of the dilate lQ of its polytope, and these form a basis of H⁰(X_A,O(l)).

title: Reflexivity of projective duality in characteristic zero
description: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, for a closed irreducible subvariety X⊂P^m the conormal variety of X^∨ is the conormal variety of X with the factors exchanged. Hence (X^∨)^∨=X, and when X^∨ is a hypersurface the projection from the conormal variety W_X onto X^∨ is birational, of degree one. In positive characteristic reflexivity can fail.

title: Noetherian commutative ring
description: A commutative ring in which every ideal is finitely generated; equivalently every ascending chain of ideals is eventually constant.

title: Integrally closed integral domain
description: An integral domain A is integrally closed if every element of its fraction field that is integral over A already lies in A.

title: Dedekind domain
description: A Noetherian integrally closed integral domain of Krull dimension one: it is not a field and every nonzero prime ideal is maximal. Some authors, for example Milne, also admit fields.

title: Integral closure of a Dedekind domain in a finite separable extension
description: If A is a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and L/K is a finite separable field extension, the integral closure of A in L is a Dedekind domain, finitely generated as an A-module.

title: Localization of a Dedekind domain
description: For a Dedekind domain A and a multiplicative subset S not containing0, the localization S⁻¹A is again Noetherian, integrally closed and has every nonzero prime maximal; it is a Dedekind domain unless it is the fraction field.

title: Convex cone in ℝᵈ
description: A nonempty subset C⊆ℝᵈ is a convex cone if λx+μy∈C for all x,y∈C and real λ,μ≥0; equivalently it is convex, contains0 and is closed under nonnegative scaling, so it contains every nonnegative linear combination of its elements.

title: Strict separation of a compact convex set from a disjoint closed convex set
description: If A and B are disjoint nonempty closed convex subsets of ℝᵈ and A is compact, there are a nonzero linear functional φ and c∈ℝ with φ(a)<c<φ(b) for all a∈A and b∈B: some affine hyperplane strictly separates them.

title: Space of compactly supported continuous functions with the inductive-limit topology
description: For a locally compact Hausdorff space X, C_c(X) consists of the continuous complex functions with compact support. It carries the locally convex inductive-limit topology of the subspaces C_K(X) of functions supported in compact K, each with the supremum norm; a seminorm on C_c(X) is continuous exactly when on every C_K(X) it is bounded by a multiple of the supremum norm.

title: Polynomial count of rational points of bounded adelic height
description: For a linear algebraic group G over a number field F with a matrix height ‖·‖ on G(A_F) defined by a faithful representation, there are constants C,N with #{γ∈G(F):‖γ‖≤t}≤Ct^N for all t≥1.

title: Hilbert–Schmidt property of square-integrable integral kernels
description: For a σ-finite measure space (Y,μ), an integral operator on L²(Y) with kernel K∈L²(Y×Y) is Hilbert–Schmidt with Hilbert–Schmidt norm ‖K‖₂; conversely every Hilbert–Schmidt operator on L²(Y) has such a kernel.

title: Products of Hilbert–Schmidt operators are trace class
description: If A and B are Hilbert–Schmidt operators on a Hilbert space, then AB is trace class and ‖AB‖₁≤‖A‖₂‖B‖₂.

title: Compactness of adelic quotients of unipotent groups
description: For a unipotent linear algebraic group N over a number field F, N(F) is a discrete cocompact subgroup of N(A_F): the quotient N(F)∖N(A_F) is compact.

title: Td-group
description: A Hausdorff topological group in which every neighbourhood of the identity contains a compact open subgroup. Such a group is locally compact and totally disconnected; examples are G(F_v) at a nonarchimedean place and finite-adelic points G(A_F^∞).

title: Smooth compactly supported test function on a Lie group times a td-group
description: For G=L×D with L a real Lie group and D a td-group, C_c^∞(G) is the space of finite sums of products f_L(l)f_D(d), with f_L a compactly supported smooth complex function on L and f_D a compactly supported locally constant complex function on D.

title: Dirac sequence on a locally compact group
description: A sequence of nonnegative compactly supported smooth functions f_n with f_n(x⁻¹)=f_n(x) and ∫f_n=1 whose supports eventually lie in every neighbourhood of the identity. For every strongly continuous unitary representation π one then has π(f_n)v→v.

title: Trace-class operators are Hilbert–Schmidt
description: Every trace-class operator T on a Hilbert space is Hilbert–Schmidt, with ‖T‖₂≤‖T‖₁.

title: Affine morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is affine if f⁻¹(V) is an affine scheme for every affine open subscheme V⊆S; it suffices to check this on one affine open cover of S. An S-affine group scheme is a group scheme whose structure map is affine.

title: Generic point of an irreducible scheme
description: A point of an irreducible scheme whose closure is the whole underlying space; every irreducible scheme has exactly one. For a morphism X→S with S irreducible, the generic fiber is the fiber over this point.

title: Étale-local lifting of multiplicative-type subgroups of smooth affine group schemes
description: Let G→S be a smooth affine group scheme, s∈S and H₀⊂G_s a subgroup of multiplicative type. Some étale neighbourhood (S′,s′) of (S,s) with k(s′)=k(s) carries a multiplicative-type subgroup H′⊂G_(S′) whose s′-fiber is H₀ (SGA3 XI 5.8).

title: Smoothness of torus centralizers in smooth affine group schemes
description: If T is a torus in a smooth affine group scheme G over a scheme S, the functorial centralizer Z_G(T) is represented by a smooth closed S-subgroup scheme of G.

title: Fibral isomorphism criterion
description: Let X and Y be finitely presented S-schemes with X flat over S. An S-morphism X→Y that induces an isomorphism X_s→Y_s on every fiber is an isomorphism (EGA IV₄ 17.9.5).

title: Connectedness of torus centralizers in connected algebraic groups
description: In a smooth connected affine algebraic group over an algebraically closed field, the centralizer of a torus is connected; in a connected reductive group it is connected reductive.

title: Smoothness and connectedness of torus-fixed subgroups
description: If a torus acts on a smooth connected affine algebraic group H over a field, the fixed-point subgroup scheme H^T is smooth and connected.

title: Étaleness of the Weyl group scheme of a torus
description: For a torus T in a smooth affine group scheme G over S, the normalizer N_G(T) is a smooth closed subgroup and W_G(T)=N_G(T)/Z_G(T) is a separated étale S-group scheme of finite presentation, quasi-finite over S.

title: Constructibility of the geometrically connected fiber locus
description: For a finitely presented morphism of schemes X→S, the set of points s∈S whose fiber X_s is geometrically connected is locally constructible in S (EGA IV₃ 9.7.7).

title: Specialization criterion for closedness of constructible sets
description: A constructible subset Y of a Noetherian scheme S is closed if and only if it is stable under specialization; equivalently, for every morphism Spec R→S from a discrete valuation ring, if the generic point maps into Y then so does the closed point.

title: Local constancy of root systems along a split maximal torus
description: Let G→S be a smooth affine group scheme whose geometric fibers have connected reductive identity components, and T⊂G a split torus maximal on geometric fibers. Then the root systems Φ(G⁰_s,T_s) are locally constant on S: for s near s₀ they identify with Φ(G⁰_(s₀),T_(s₀)) through the character group of T.

title: Zariski's Main Theorem for quasi-finite morphisms
description: Let S be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and f:X→S a separated quasi-finite morphism of finite presentation. Then f factors as a quasi-compact open immersion X→T followed by a finite morphism T→S of finite presentation (Grothendieck’s form of Zariski’s Main Theorem, EGA IV₃ 8.12.6, 18.12.13).

title: Linear differential operator with smooth coefficients
description: On an open set U⊆ℝⁿ, an operator P=∑_(|α|≤m)a_α(x)∂^α with smooth complex coefficients a_α; its order is the largest |α| with a_α≠0. It acts on smooth functions and, through its formal transpose, on distributions. The notion is local and passes through charts to smooth manifolds, e.g. to left-invariant operators on Lie groups.

title: Elliptic linear differential operator
description: A linear differential operator P=∑_(|α|≤m)a_α∂^α of order m with smooth coefficients on U is elliptic if its principal symbol ∑_(|α|=m)a_α(x)ξ^α is nonzero for every x∈U and every nonzero ξ∈ℝⁿ.

title: Fundamental solution of a linear differential operator at a point
description: For a linear differential operator P with smooth coefficients on an open set U∋x₀, a fundamental solution at x₀ is a distribution E on U with PE=δ_(x₀), the Dirac distribution φ↦φ(x₀). It is local when U is only some neighbourhood of x₀.

title: Meromorphic function of several complex variables
description: A function on a connected open subset of ℂⁿ that is locally a quotient g/h of holomorphic functions, with h not identically zero; it is holomorphic off the zero set of the denominators.

title: Normalized parabolic induction for adelic reductive groups
description: For an F-parabolic P=MN of a connected reductive number-field group G, compatible maximal compact K, a unitary representation σ of M(A_F) and λ∈a*_(P,C), I_P(σ,λ) is right translation on functions φ:G(A_F)→V_σ with φ(nmg)=σ(m)e^((λ+ρ_P)(H_P(m)))φ(g), square-integrable on K. The factor e^(ρ_P(H_P))=δ_P^(1/2) makes it unitary for λ∈ia*_P.

title: Cuspidal datum of a reductive number-field group
description: An equivalence class of pairs (M,σ) with M a Levi subgroup of an F-parabolic subgroup of G and σ a cuspidal automorphic representation of M(A_F)¹; (M,σ) and (M′,σ′) are equivalent if some element of G(F) conjugates M to M′ and carries σ to a representation unitarily equivalent to σ′.

title: Direct integral of unitary representations
description: For a σ-finite measure space (X,μ), a separable Hilbert space H and a family x↦π_x of unitary representations of G on H with measurable matrix coefficients, the direct integral acts on L²(X,μ;H), the square-integrable measurable H-valued functions modulo null functions, by (πF)(x)=π_x(g)F(x). Measurable fields of varying Hilbert spaces are treated likewise.

title: Eisenstein series on a reductive number-field group
description: For an F-parabolic P of a connected reductive group G, a K-finite automorphic vector φ in the space of the induced representation I_P(λ) and λ∈a*_(P,C), E(x,φ,λ)=∑_(δ∈P(F)∖G(F))φ(δx)e^((λ+ρ_P)(H_P(δx))). It converges absolutely for Re λ∈ρ_P+(a*_P)⁺ and, by Langlands, continues meromorphically to a*_(P,C).

title: Monomorphism in a category
description: A morphism f:X→Y of a category is a monomorphism if it is left cancellable: f∘a=f∘b implies a=b for every object W and all morphisms a,b:W→X.

title: Epimorphism in a category
description: A morphism f:X→Y of a category is an epimorphism if it is right cancellable: a∘f=b∘f implies a=b for every object W and all morphisms a,b:Y→W.

title: Zero morphism in a category with a zero object
description: In a category with a zero object 0, the zero morphism X→Y is the composite X→0→Y of the unique morphisms through 0. Any composite of a zero morphism with another morphism is again a zero morphism.

title: Kernel of a morphism in a category with a zero object
description: For a morphism f:X→Y in a category with a zero object, a kernel of f is a morphism k:K→X with f∘k=0 such that every g:W→X with f∘g=0 factors as g=k∘h for a unique h:W→K.

title: Cokernel of a morphism in a category with a zero object
description: For a morphism f:X→Y in a category with a zero object, a cokernel of f is a morphism c:Y→C with c∘f=0 such that every g:Y→W with g∘f=0 factors as g=h∘c for a unique h:C→W.

title: Product of a family of objects in a category
description: For a family (X_i)_{i∈I} of objects of a category, a product is an object P with morphisms p_i:P→X_i such that for every object W and morphisms f_i:W→X_i there is a unique f:W→P with p_i∘f=f_i for all i.

title: Coproduct of a family of objects in a category
description: For a family (X_i)_{i∈I} of objects of a category, a coproduct is an object Q with morphisms q_i:X_i→Q such that for every object W and morphisms f_i:X_i→W there is a unique f:Q→W with f∘q_i=f_i for all i.

title: Object of finite length in an abelian category
description: An object X of an abelian category has finite length if it has a finite chain of subobjects 0=X_0⊂X_1⊂⋯⊂X_n=X whose successive quotients X_i/X_{i−1}, the cokernels of the inclusions, are simple objects. Such a chain is a Jordan–Hölder (composition) series of X.

title: Braided monoidal functor
description: A strong monoidal functor (F,J) between braided monoidal categories is braided if J_{Y,X}∘c_{F(X),F(Y)}=F(c_{X,Y})∘J_{X,Y} for all objects X,Y. A braided monoidal equivalence is a braided monoidal functor whose underlying functor is an equivalence of categories.

title: Deligne tensor product of locally finite abelian categories
description: For locally finite k-linear abelian categories C and D, the Deligne tensor product C⊠D is a k-linear abelian category with a bilinear bifunctor ⊠:C×D→C⊠D, right exact in each variable, such that every bilinear bifunctor C×D→A right exact in each variable factors as F̄∘⊠ for a unique right exact functor F̄:C⊠D→A.

title: Opposite monoidal category
description: For a monoidal category (C,⊗,a,1), the opposite monoidal category C^op (also written C^{⊗op} or C^rev) has the same underlying category, tensor product X⊗^op Y=Y⊗X and associativity constraint a^op_{X,Y,Z}=a^{-1}_{Z,Y,X}. It differs from the dual category with reversed morphisms.

title: Drinfeld center as the dual category of C⊠C^op
description: Let C be a finite multitensor category, regarded as a module category over C⊠C^op by (X⊠Y)⊗M=X⊗M⊗Y. The dual category Fun_{C⊠C^op}(C,C) of module endofunctors is canonically tensor equivalent to the Drinfeld center Z(C): a bimodule endofunctor −⊗Z corresponds to Z with the half-braiding given by its right module structure.

title: Coset of a subgroup
description: For a subgroup H of a group G and g∈G, the left coset gH={gh:h∈H}, written g+H in additive notation. The left cosets of H partition G and each is in bijection with H.

title: Order of an element of a group
description: The order of g in a group G is the least positive integer n with gⁿ=e, or infinite if no such n exists.

title: Exponent of a finite group
description: The exponent of a finite group G is the least common multiple of the orders of its elements, equivalently the least positive integer n with gⁿ=e for every g∈G.

title: Irreducible linear representation of a group
description: A linear representation ρ:G→GL(V) is irreducible if V≠0 and the only subspaces W⊆V with ρ(g)W⊆W for every g∈G are 0 and V.

title: Fenchel–Moreau biconjugation theorem
description: A proper function f:E→(−∞,∞] on a real Banach space, for example ℝᵈ, equals its biconjugate f** on E, where f**(x)=sup_{x*∈E*}(⟨x*,x⟩−f*(x*)), if and only if f is convex and lower semicontinuous.

title: Brøndsted–Rockafellar theorem
description: Let f be a proper lower semicontinuous convex function on a real Banach space, x₀∈dom f, ε>0 and x₀* an ε-subgradient at x₀. For every λ>0 there are x and x*∈∂f(x) with ‖x−x₀‖≤ε/λ and ‖x*−x₀*‖≤λ. Consequently every x∈dom f is a limit of points x_k∈dom ∂f with f(x_k)→f(x).

title: Frobenius–Perron dimension is a ring homomorphism
description: For a fusion category C, the assignment X↦FPdim(X) extends to a ring homomorphism from the Grothendieck ring K(C) to ℝ. It is the unique ring homomorphism K(C)→ℝ taking positive values on all classes of simple objects.

title: Cyclotomicity of characters of the Grothendieck ring of a fusion category
description: For a fusion category C over ℂ and an irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation L of its Grothendieck ring K(C), there is a root of unity ξ with Tr([X],L)∈ℤ[ξ] for every object X. In particular every ring homomorphism K(C)→ℂ takes values in ℤ[ξ] for some root of unity ξ.

title: Unique factorization of ideals in a Dedekind domain
description: In a Dedekind domain every nonzero proper ideal is a product of nonzero prime ideals, uniquely up to order. Consequently the nonzero fractional ideals form a group, free abelian on the nonzero prime ideals, and for nonzero integral ideals a⊇b holds exactly when a divides b.

title: Multiplicativity of the absolute ideal norm
description: For a number field K the absolute norm N(a)=|O_K/a| of nonzero ideals of O_K is multiplicative: N(ab)=N(a)N(b). If p is a nonzero prime of O_K with p∩ℤ=pℤ, then N(p)=p^f with f=[O_K/p:𝔽_p]; hence N(a)ℤ is the relative ideal norm of a from K to ℚ.

title: Inequality of arithmetic and geometric means
description: For nonnegative reals x₁,…,x_n, (x₁x₂⋯x_n)^{1/n}≤(x₁+⋯+x_n)/n, with equality exactly when all x_i are equal.

title: Determinant square class of a quadratic space
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space V over a field F of characteristic different from two, its determinant (or discriminant) d(V) is det(B(e_i,e_j)) for a basis e₁,…,e_n, regarded in F×/(F×)²; a change of basis multiplies the determinant by a nonzero square. For a diagonalization ∑a_ix_i², d(V)=a₁⋯a_n.

title: Characterization of the hyperbolic plane
description: For a nondegenerate two-dimensional quadratic space V over a field of characteristic different from two, the following are equivalent: V is isotropic; V≅⟨1,−1⟩, the hyperbolic plane; V≅⟨a,−a⟩ for every nonzero a; −d(V) is a square. Hence all isotropic nondegenerate binary spaces are isometric.

title: Representation criterion via isotropy of an orthogonal sum
description: Let V be a nondegenerate quadratic space over a field of characteristic different from two and a a nonzero scalar. Then V represents a, meaning Q(x)=a for some x∈V, if and only if the orthogonal sum V⊥⟨−a⟩ is isotropic.

title: Orthogonal splitting off a nondegenerate subspace
description: If W is a nondegenerate subspace of a quadratic space V over a field of characteristic different from two, then V=W⊥W^⊥. In particular, if Q(x)=a≠0 then V=⟨a⟩⊥(Fx)^⊥.

title: Isotropy criterion for quaternary quadratic spaces over ℚ_p
description: A nondegenerate four-dimensional quadratic space V over ℚ_p is isotropic if and only if either its determinant d(V) is not a square, or d(V) is a square and its Hasse invariant equals the Hilbert symbol (−1,−1)_p. When d(V) is a square the i<j and i≤j Hasse-invariant conventions agree.

title: Isotropy of quadratic spaces of dimension at least five over ℚ_p
description: Every nondegenerate quadratic space of dimension at least five over ℚ_p is isotropic. Consequently every nondegenerate quaternary quadratic space over ℚ_p represents every nonzero p-adic number.

title: Riemann–Roch theorem for smooth projective curves
description: Let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over a field k, K a canonical divisor (of a nonzero rational differential) and ℓ(D)=dim_k{f∈k(C)×:div f+D≥0}∪{0}. Then ℓ(D)−ℓ(K−D)=deg D+1−g for every divisor D. Cohomologically χ(O(D))=deg D+1−g and H¹(C,O(D)) is dual to H⁰(C,Ω¹(−D)), so g=dim H¹(C,O_C).

title: Global regular functions on a proper geometrically integral scheme
description: If X is a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field k, then H⁰(X,O_X)=k, so every global regular function is constant. If X is merely a proper integral scheme over k, then H⁰(X,O_X) is a field finite over k.

title: Projective embeddings of a genus-zero curve by positive-degree line bundles
description: Let X be a proper curve over a field k with H⁰(X,O_X)=k and H¹(X,O_X)=0. For an invertible O_X-module L of degree d>0, dim H⁰(X,L)=d+1, H¹(X,L)=0 and a basis of H⁰(X,L) defines a closed immersion X→ℙ^d_k. For d=1 this gives an isomorphism X≅ℙ¹_k.

title: Holomorphic map between complex manifolds
description: A continuous map f:M→N between complex analytic manifolds is holomorphic if its expressions in holomorphic charts are holomorphic functions of several complex variables, equivalently if h∘f is holomorphic for every holomorphic function h on an open subset of N. A biholomorphism is a holomorphic bijection with holomorphic inverse.

title: Complex tangent space of a complex manifold
description: For a point p of a complex manifold M of dimension n, T_pM is the complex vector space of ℂ-linear derivations D of germs of holomorphic functions at p, D(fg)=D(f)g(p)+f(p)D(g). In local coordinates it has basis ∂/∂z_i. A holomorphic map F has ℂ-linear differential d_pF(v)(f)=v(f∘F); a holomorphic curve γ has velocity γ′(z)=d_zγ(1).

title: Complex Lie group
description: A group G with a structure of complex analytic manifold for which multiplication G×G→G and inversion are holomorphic. Forgetting the complex structure, G is a real Lie group of twice its complex dimension; its Lie algebra is the complex tangent space at the identity. Morphisms are holomorphic group homomorphisms.

title: Holomorphic existence, uniqueness and parameter dependence for ODEs
description: Let F(t,w,λ) be holomorphic on an open subset of ℂ×ℂⁿ×ℂᵐ. Near each point (t₀,w₀,λ₀) the initial-value problem w′=F(t,w,λ), w(t₀)=w₀ has a unique holomorphic solution on a disk around t₀, and the solution depends holomorphically on (t,w₀,λ).

title: Topology induced by a metric
description: For a metric space (X,d), the topology whose open sets are the subsets U⊆X such that every x∈U has some r>0 with open ball B(x,r)={y:d(x,y)<r}⊆U.

title: Basin of attraction of a periodic orbit
description: For a self-map F of a metric space and a periodic orbit O of least period p, the basin of O is the set of points x for which the iterates F^{np}(x) converge, as n→∞, to some point of O.

title: C¹ topology on maps of a compact interval
description: On C¹ maps of a compact interval I into ℝ, the topology induced by the metric d(f,g)=sup_I|f−g|+sup_I|f′−g′|, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints; g is C¹-close to f when d(f,g) is small.

title: Rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol)
description: For a real number a and an integer m≥0, (a)₀=1 and (a)_m=a(a+1)⋯(a+m−1).

title: Gegenbauer polynomial
description: For λ>0 and an integer k≥0, the Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomial is C_k^λ(x)=∑_{j=0}^{⌊k/2⌋}(−1)^j(λ)_{k−j}(2x)^{k−2j}/(j!(k−2j)!), with (a)_m the rising factorial. Equivalently, (1−2xt+t²)^{−λ}=∑_{k≥0}C_k^λ(x)t^k for |x|≤1 and |t|<1.

title: Distance from a point to a subset of a metric space
description: For a nonempty subset A of a metric space (X,d) and x∈X, d(x,A)=inf{d(x,a):a∈A}.

title: Set of finite perimeter in Euclidean space
description: A Lebesgue measurable E⊆ℝⁿ whose indicator has distributional gradient D1_E given by an ℝⁿ-valued Radon measure of finite total variation; its perimeter is |D1_E|(ℝⁿ).

title: Brenier–McCann theorem
description: If μ and ν are Borel probability measures on ℝⁿ and μ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, there is a convex function φ whose gradient, defined μ-almost everywhere, pushes μ forward to ν; this gradient map is unique μ-almost everywhere.

title: Gradients of convex functions are locally of bounded variation
description: If φ:ℝⁿ→ℝ is convex, then ∇φ is locally of bounded variation and its distributional derivative D∇φ is a Radon measure with values in symmetric positive semidefinite n×n matrices.

title: McCann’s almost-everywhere Monge–Ampère equation for Brenier maps
description: If T=∇φ is the Brenier map pushing f(x)dx to g(y)dy, with probability densities f and g, then g(T(x))det∇²φ(x)=f(x) for almost every x with f(x)>0, where ∇²φ is the absolutely continuous part (Aleksandrov Hessian) of D∇φ.

title: Divergence theorem for BV vector fields on sets of finite perimeter
description: If E⊆ℝⁿ has finite perimeter and T∈BV(ℝⁿ;ℝⁿ) is bounded, then the distributional divergence satisfies Div T(E^{(1)})=∫_{∂*E}tr_E(T)·ν_E dH^{n−1}, where E^{(1)} is the set of density-one points, ∂*E the reduced boundary with outer normal ν_E, and tr_E(T) the inner trace.

title: Bounded Lipschitz domains have finite perimeter
description: A bounded Lipschitz domain E⊂ℝⁿ is a set of finite perimeter; H^{n−1}-almost all of ∂E lies in its reduced boundary, where the measure-theoretic outer normal equals the classical outer unit normal, and D1_E=−ν_E H^{n−1}⌊∂E.

title: Muckenhoupt’s weighted maximal inequality
description: For 1<p<∞ and a weight w in the Muckenhoupt class A_p on ℝⁿ, the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator satisfies ∫(Mf)^p w≤C∫|f|^p w, with C depending only on n, p and the A_p constant of w.

title: Aₚ extrapolation into variable Lebesgue spaces
description: Suppose nonnegative pairs (f,g) satisfy ∫f^{p₀}w≤C∫g^{p₀}w for some 1<p₀<∞ and every A_{p₀} weight w, with C depending on the A_{p₀} constant. If 1<p₁<p⁻ and the maximal operator is bounded on L^{(p(·)/p₁)′}, then ∥f∥_{p(·)}≤C∥g∥_{p(·)} when the left side is finite, and ∥(∑_j f_j^q)^{1/q}∥_{p(·)}≤C∥(∑_j g_j^q)^{1/q}∥_{p(·)} for 1<q<∞.

title: Boundedness of the maximal operator on log-Hölder variable Lebesgue spaces
description: If p is globally log-Hölder continuous with 1<p⁻≤p⁺<∞, then the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator is bounded on L^{p(·)}(ℝⁿ): ∥Mf∥_{p(·)}≤C∥f∥_{p(·)}.

title: Radial boundary function of a function on the unit disk
description: For a function f on the unit disk 𝔻 and ζ on the unit circle, the radial limit f*(ζ)=lim_{r→1⁻} f(rζ) is taken along the radius ending at ζ. The radial boundary function f* is defined at those ζ where this limit exists; Hardy-space results assert existence almost everywhere for arc-length measure.

title: Strictly convex body
description: A convex body K⊂ℝᵈ is strictly convex if its boundary contains no line segment of positive length; equivalently, every supporting hyperplane of K meets K in exactly one point.

title: Fatou’s nontangential limit theorem for bounded holomorphic functions
description: If f is bounded and holomorphic on the unit disk, then for almost every ζ on the unit circle f(z) converges as z→ζ inside every Stolz angle {z∈𝔻:|z−ζ|<α(1−|z|)}, α>1. In particular its radial limits exist almost everywhere and equal these nontangential limits.

title: Beurling’s characterization of cyclic functions in Hardy H²
description: A nonzero f∈H² of the unit disk has polynomial multiples dense in H² exactly when log|f*| is integrable on the circle and f(z)=c·exp∫(ζ+z)/(ζ−z)·log|f*(ζ)|dm(ζ) with |c|=1, where m is normalized arc measure. Thus the cyclic and the exponential definitions of outer functions agree in H².

title: Differentiability criterion for support functions
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ and u≠0, the support function h_K is differentiable at u exactly when the support set {x∈K:⟨x,u⟩=h_K(u)} is a single point x; then ∇h_K(u)=x.

title: Area formula for a C¹ parametrized hypersurface
description: If M⊂ℝⁿ⁻¹ is open and X:M→ℝⁿ is an injective C¹ map whose differential has rank n−1 everywhere, then H^{n−1}(X(A))=∫_A √det(DX(y)ᵀDX(y)) dy for every Borel set A⊆M, where H^{n−1} is (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

title: Local Steiner formula for convex bodies
description: For every convex body K⊂ℝⁿ of any dimension there are finite positive Borel measures Θ₀(K,·),…,Θ_{n−1}(K,·) on ℝⁿ×S^{n−1} such that, for each Borel η and ρ>0, the points x with 0<d(K,x)≤ρ whose nearest point and normal direction (p(K,x),u(K,x)) lie in η have volume n⁻¹∑_m C(n,m)ρ^{n−m}Θ_m(K,η). Each Θ_m(K,·) depends weakly continuously on K in Hausdorff distance.

title: Hausdorff-measure description of the top area measure of a convex body
description: For an n-dimensional convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, the area measure S_{n−1}(K,ω)=Θ_{n−1}(K,ℝⁿ×ω) given by the local Steiner formula equals the (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the set of boundary points of K having an outer unit normal in ω. For bodies of dimension n−1 it is concentrated on the two unit normals of their affine hull, and it vanishes in lower dimensions.

title: Minkowski’s existence theorem for polytopes
description: If u₁,…,u_N are pairwise distinct unit vectors spanning ℝⁿ and f₁,…,f_N>0 satisfy ∑f_iu_i=0, there is an n-dimensional convex polytope whose facet outer unit normals are exactly u₁,…,u_N and whose facet with normal u_i has (n−1)-dimensional volume f_i.

title: Blaschke selection theorem
description: Every sequence of nonempty compact convex subsets of ℝⁿ contained in a fixed ball has a subsequence converging in Hausdorff distance to a nonempty compact convex set.

title: Kummer map of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a characteristic-zero field K and n≥1, the connecting map of 0→A[n](K̄)→A(K̄)→A(K̄)→0 (multiplication by n) is the injective map A(K)/nA(K)→H¹(K,A[n](K̄)), sending P to the class of σ↦σ(Q)−Q for any Q with nQ=P. For K a finite extension of some ℚ_ℓ and a prime p, the maps for n=p^m pass to the limit and, after ⊗ℚ_p, give the local Kummer map κ:A(K)^∧⊗_(ℤ_p)ℚ_p→H¹(K,V_pA) in continuous cohomology, where A(K)^∧ is the p-adic completion.

title: Scalar extension of a finite separable field extension
description: For a finite separable extension K/k and any field extension Ω/k, K⊗_kΩ is a finite product of finite separable field extensions of Ω, one for each irreducible factor over Ω of the minimal polynomial of a primitive element. If Ω contains a normal closure of K/k, for example if Ω is algebraically closed, then a⊗b↦(σ(a)b)_σ gives K⊗_kΩ≅∏_(σ∈Hom_k(K,Ω))Ω.

title: Completion decomposition of a finite separable extension
description: Let L/K be a finite separable extension and |·| an archimedean or discrete nonarchimedean absolute value on K with completion K̂. Then |·| has finitely many extensions |·|₁,…,|·|_g to L, and a⊗b↦(ab)_i gives L⊗_KK̂≅∏_iL_i, where L_i is the completion of L at |·|_i. For a number field F and a prime ℓ this is F⊗_ℚℚ_ℓ≅∏_(λ|ℓ)F_λ.

title: Casselman’s newform theorem for local components of GL₂
description: For an irreducible infinite-dimensional admissible representation π of GL₂(F), F a nonarchimedean local field, the vectors fixed by K₁(𝔭^c)={(a b;c d)∈GL₂(O):c≡0, d≡1 mod 𝔭^c} vanish for c<a(π) and form a line for c=a(π), the conductor exponent. For the automorphic representation of a normalized newform of level N, the local component at p therefore has a(π_p)=v_p(N).

title: Mackey restriction formula for induced representations
description: Let H and K be subgroups of a group G with H of finite index (open, for profinite G and continuous actions). For an H-module W, Res^G_K Ind^G_H W≅⊕_(s∈K\G/H) Ind^K_(K∩sHs⁻¹)(ˢW), where ˢW is W with action k·w=(s⁻¹ks)w of K∩sHs⁻¹.

title: Artin formalism for L-functions of ℓ-adic Galois representations
description: For compatible systems of ℓ-adic representations of absolute Galois groups of number fields, with Euler factors det(1−Frob_v⁻¹(Nv)^(−s)|(V^∨)^(I_v))^(−1) at every finite place, L(ρ⊕ρ′,s)=L(ρ,s)L(ρ′,s), and for a finite extension K/F, L(Ind_(G_K)^(G_F)ρ,s)=L(ρ,s), with equality of all local factors including ramified places.

title: Tate module of a quadratic twist of an elliptic curve
