description: For an elliptic curve E over a characteristic-zero field F, D∈F×∖(F×)² and a prime ℓ, an F(√D)-isomorphism E→E^D identifies T_ℓ(E^D)≅T_ℓ(E)⊗κ_D as G_F-modules, where κ_D(σ)=σ(√D)/√D∈{±1} is the quadratic character of F(√D)/F.

title: Tate-module description of elliptic-curve Euler factors
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, a finite prime 𝔭 and ℓ prime to 𝔭, det(1−Frob_𝔭⁻¹T|(V_ℓE^∨)^(I_𝔭)) is 1−a_𝔭T+N𝔭T² at good reduction, 1−T at split multiplicative, 1+T at nonsplit multiplicative and 1 at additive reduction. Hence the Hasse–Weil L-function defined by reduction types is the L-function of the ℓ-adic representation V_ℓE^∨.

title: Pullback of a line bundle by multiplication on an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A, an integer n and an invertible sheaf L on A, n_A^*L≅L^((n²+n)/2)⊗((−1)_A^*L)^((n²−n)/2). In particular n_A^*L≅L^(n²) when L is symmetric. This is a consequence of the theorem of the cube.

title: Intersection number of divisors on a smooth projective variety
description: For divisors D₁,…,D_g on a smooth projective variety V of dimension g over an algebraically closed field, (D₁,…,D_g) is the sum over points v of the common support of dim_k O_(V,v)/(f₁,…,f_g), f_i local equations, when the D_i are effective and meet in finitely many points; it is extended by linearity and invariance under linear equivalence to all g-tuples.

title: Multidimensional time-dependent Itô formula for càdlàg semimartingales
description: Let Y be an ℝᵈ-valued càdlàg semimartingale, T<∞, D⊆ℝᵈ open and f∈C^{1,2}([0,T]×D) (∂_tf, ∂_jf, ∂_j∂_kf continuous and extending continuously to [0,T]×D), and suppose almost surely the closure of the path Y[0,T] lies in D, i.e. Y_t and Y_(t−) lie in D for t≤T. Then for t≤T, f(t,Y_t)=f(0,Y_0)+∫₀ᵗ∂_sf(s,Y_s)ds+Σ_j∫_(0,t]∂_jf(s,Y_(s−))dY^j_s+½Σ_(j,k)∫_(0,t]∂_j∂_kf(s,Y_(s−))d[Y^j,Y^k]_s+Σ_(0<s≤t)[f(s,Y_s)−f(s,Y_(s−))−∇f(s,Y_(s−))·ΔY_s−½ΔY_sᵀD²f(s,Y_(s−))ΔY_s], the jump sum converging absolutely; for continuous Y it vanishes.

title: Local martingale with integrable running maximum is a martingale
description: A right-continuous local martingale M with sup_(0≤s≤t)|M_s| integrable for every t≥0 is a martingale. In particular a local martingale bounded on every bounded time interval is a martingale.

title: Nonnegative local martingales are supermartingales
description: A nonnegative local martingale X with EX₀<∞ is a supermartingale. It is a martingale if and only if EX_t=EX₀ for every time t; the same holds on a finite horizon [0,T].

title: Existence of countable product probability measures
description: For probability spaces (Ω_i,𝔽_i,P_i), i∈ℕ, there is a unique probability measure P on the product σ-algebra of ∏_iΩ_i with P(A₁×⋯×A_n×∏_(i>n)Ω_i)=∏_(i≤n)P_i(A_i) for all n and A_i∈𝔽_i. Under P the coordinate maps are independent random elements with laws P_i.

title: Lindelöf property of separable metric spaces
description: Every cover of a subset of a separable metric space by open sets has a countable subcover.

title: Noetherian topological space
description: A topological space satisfying the descending chain condition on closed subsets: every decreasing sequence Z₁⊇Z₂⊇⋯ of closed subsets is eventually constant. Equivalently every nonempty family of closed subsets has a minimal member, which is what Noetherian induction uses.

title: Locally closed subset of a topological space
description: A subset of a topological space that is the intersection U∩Z of an open subset U and a closed subset Z.

title: Constructible subset of a Noetherian topological space
description: A subset of a Noetherian topological space that is a finite union of locally closed subsets. Equivalently it belongs to the smallest family of subsets containing every open subset and closed under finite intersections and complements; finite unions, intersections, complements and continuous preimages of constructible sets are constructible.

title: Noetherian scheme
description: A scheme is locally Noetherian if it is covered by open affine subschemes Spec A with each A a Noetherian ring, and Noetherian if moreover it is quasi-compact, equivalently covered by finitely many such affine opens. The underlying topological space of a Noetherian scheme is a Noetherian topological space.

title: Local dimension of a topological space at a point
description: For a point x of a topological space X, dim_x X is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of the open neighbourhoods of x, each with the subspace topology. For a scheme the local dimension is that of its underlying space.

title: Algebraically independent subset of a field extension
description: A subset S of a field extension L/K is algebraically independent over K if no nonzero polynomial with coefficients in K vanishes when evaluated at finitely many distinct elements of S; otherwise S is algebraically dependent over K.

title: Transcendence degree of a field extension
description: A transcendence basis of L/K is an algebraically independent subset S over K such that L is algebraic over K(S). Transcendence bases exist and all have the same cardinality, the transcendence degree trdeg_K L; equivalently it is the cardinality of a maximal algebraically independent subset.

title: Character group of a finite abelian group
description: For a finite abelian group G, its character group or dual group Ĝ is the set of group homomorphisms G→ℂ^×, a group under pointwise multiplication. Every character takes values in roots of unity, so Ĝ equals the group of homomorphisms from G to the unit circle.

title: Laplace transform of a function on the half-line
description: For a locally integrable f:[0,∞)→ℂ, its Laplace transform is g(z)=∫₀^∞f(t)e^(−zt)dt at those complex z for which the Lebesgue integral converges absolutely. If f is bounded the integral converges absolutely and locally uniformly on Re z>0, where g is holomorphic.

title: Finite morphisms of schemes are closed
description: A finite morphism of schemes, and more generally an integral morphism, is a closed map: the image of every closed subset of the source is closed in the target. Affinely this is the lying-over theorem for the integral ring map B/J→A/I.

title: Noether normalization lemma
description: If A is a finitely generated algebra over a field k, there are elements x₁,…,x_d of A, algebraically independent over k, such that A is a finitely generated module over the polynomial subalgebra k[x₁,…,x_d].

title: Lying-over and going-up theorems for integral extensions
description: Let A⊆B be commutative rings with B integral over A. Every prime ideal of A is the contraction of a prime ideal of B (lying over), and if 𝔭⊆𝔭′ are primes of A and 𝔮 is a prime of B over 𝔭, there is a prime 𝔮′⊇𝔮 of B over 𝔭′ (going up).

title: Prime ideals of a localization
description: For a multiplicative subset S of a commutative ring A, the map 𝔭↦S⁻¹𝔭 is an inclusion-preserving bijection from the prime ideals of A disjoint from S onto the prime ideals of S⁻¹A, with inverse given by contraction along A→S⁻¹A.

title: Transitivity of algebraic field extensions
description: If K⊆L⊆M are fields with M algebraic over L and L algebraic over K, then M is algebraic over K.

title: Quasi-finite ring map
description: A finite-type homomorphism R→S of commutative rings is quasi-finite at a prime 𝔮 of S, lying over 𝔭⊂R, if 𝔮 is an isolated point of its fibre Spec(S⊗_Rκ(𝔭)); it is quasi-finite if this holds at every prime, equivalently if every fibre ring S⊗_Rκ(𝔭) is finite-dimensional over κ(𝔭).

title: Dimension inequality for a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings
description: If (A,𝔪)→(B,𝔫) is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, then dim B≤dim A+dim(B/𝔪B), with equality when B is flat over A.

title: Functional equation of the Riemann zeta function
description: The completed function Λ(s)=π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2)ζ(s) extends meromorphically to ℂ with simple poles only at s=0 and s=1 and satisfies Λ(s)=Λ(1−s). Consequently, outside the strip 0≤Re s≤1 the zeros of ζ are exactly the simple zeros at the negative even integers.

title: Hadamard product for the Riemann xi function
description: The entire function ξ(s)=s(s−1)π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2)ζ(s) has order one and ξ(s)=e^(A+Bs)∏_ρ(1−s/ρ)e^(s/ρ), the product running over the nontrivial zeros of ζ with multiplicity and converging absolutely and locally uniformly. Hence ξ′(s)/ξ(s)=B+∑_ρ(1/(s−ρ)+1/ρ).

title: Polynomial growth of the Riemann zeta function in vertical strips
description: For every real σ₀ there is A=A(σ₀) such that ζ(σ+it)=O(|t|^A) uniformly for σ≥σ₀ and |t|≥2.

title: Local partial-fraction formula for the logarithmic derivative of zeta
description: Uniformly for −1≤σ≤2 and |t|≥2, at points s=σ+it which are not zeros of ζ, ζ′(s)/ζ(s)=∑_(ρ:|t−Im ρ|<1)1/(s−ρ)+O(log|t|), the sum running over nontrivial zeros with multiplicity.

title: Von Mangoldt series for the logarithmic derivative of zeta
description: For Re s>1, −ζ′(s)/ζ(s)=∑_(n≥1)Λ(n)n^(−s), where Λ is the von Mangoldt function; the series converges absolutely and arises by logarithmic differentiation of the Euler product.

title: Truncated Perron formula
description: Let ∑a_n n^(−s) converge absolutely at real c>0. For x,T≥2, ∑′_(n≤x)a_n=(2πi)⁻¹∫_(c−iT)^(c+iT)(∑a_n n^(−s))x^s ds/s+O(x^c∑_n|a_n|n^(−c)min(1,(T|log(x/n)|)⁻¹)), where ∑′ counts a term with n=x with weight 1/2 and the n=x error term is replaced by c/T.

title: Nonvanishing of the Riemann zeta function on the line Re s=1
description: The Riemann zeta function has no zeros on the line Re s=1 (Hadamard and de la Vallée Poussin).

title: Landau theorem on Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients
description: If a Dirichlet series ∑a_n n^(−s) with nonnegative real coefficients has finite real abscissa of absolute convergence L, then its sum does not extend to a holomorphic function on any neighbourhood of s=L.

title: Minimal topological dynamical system
description: A compact topological dynamical system (X,T), with T a homeomorphism, is minimal if ∅ and X are its only closed subsets A with T(A)=A; equivalently every orbit {Tⁿx:n∈ℤ} is dense in X.

title: Topologically transitive dynamical system
description: A compact topological dynamical system (X,T), with T a homeomorphism, is transitive if some point x has dense two-sided orbit {Tⁿx:n∈ℤ}; such an x is a transitive point.

title: Factor map of topological dynamical systems
description: For compact topological dynamical systems (X,T) and (Y,S), a factor map is a continuous surjection p:X→Y with S∘p=p∘T; then (Y,S) is a factor of (X,T). A bijective factor map is a conjugacy.

title: Inverse limit of topological dynamical systems
description: For compact metric systems (X_i,T_i), i∈ℕ, and factor maps π_i:X_(i+1)→X_i, the inverse limit is the subspace {(x_i):π_i(x_(i+1))=x_i for all i} of the product ∏X_i with the map (x_i)↦(T_ix_i). A system is an inverse limit of systems of a class when it is conjugate to such a limit with all (X_i,T_i) in the class.

title: Maximal compact subgroup of a topological group
description: A subgroup K of a topological group G that is compact in the subspace topology and is not properly contained in any other compact subgroup of G.

title: Reductive group scheme
description: Over a ring k, a reductive group scheme is a smooth affine k-group scheme G whose geometric fibers G_s̄, for all geometric points s̄ of Spec k, are connected reductive algebraic groups. Over a field this is a connected reductive group.

title: Parabolic subgroup scheme of a reductive group scheme
description: For a reductive group scheme G over a ring k, a parabolic subgroup scheme is a smooth closed k-subgroup scheme P⊂G such that for every geometric point s̄ of Spec k the fiber P_s̄ is a parabolic subgroup of G_s̄.

title: Finite-intersection characterization of compactness
description: A topological space is compact if and only if every family of closed subsets with the finite intersection property, meaning every finite subfamily has nonempty intersection, has nonempty total intersection.

title: Subnet characterization of compactness
description: A subset K of a topological space is compact if and only if every net in K has a subnet converging to a point of K.

title: Minkowski functional of a convex absorbing set
description: For a convex absorbing subset B of a real vector space, p_B(x)=inf{λ>0:x∈λB}. If B is symmetric, p_B is a seminorm; for an open convex symmetric neighbourhood of 0 in a topological vector space it is continuous and B={x:p_B(x)<1}.

title: Euclidean structure of finite-dimensional Hausdorff topological vector spaces
description: Every m-dimensional Hausdorff real topological vector space is linearly homeomorphic to ℝᵐ with its Euclidean topology; in particular any linear bijection from ℝᵐ onto it is a homeomorphism.

title: Closed graph criterion for maps into a compact Hausdorff space
description: A map f:X→Y from a topological space to a compact Hausdorff space is continuous if and only if its graph {(x,f(x)):x∈X} is closed in X×Y.

title: Algebra homomorphisms between continuous-function algebras are compositions
description: For compact Hausdorff spaces X and Y, every unital algebra homomorphism κ:C(Y)→C(X) of real or complex continuous-function algebras has the form κf=f∘φ for a unique continuous map φ:X→Y.

title: Openness of factor maps between minimal distal systems
description: If p:X→Y is a factor map between minimal distal compact metric systems, for one homeomorphism or a countable abelian group of commuting homeomorphisms, then p is an open map.

title: Krylov–Bogolyubov theorem for a continuous map of a compact metric space
description: Every continuous self-map T of a nonempty compact metric space X has a T-invariant Borel probability measure; any weak* limit point of the empirical averages n⁻¹∑_(j<n)δ_(T^jx) is one.

title: Factor map of measure-preserving systems
description: For probability-preserving systems (X,μ,T) and (Y,ν,S), a factor map is a measurable map π:X→Y, defined μ-almost everywhere, with π_*μ=ν and π∘T=S∘π almost everywhere. An almost-everywhere invertible factor map with measurable inverse is an isomorphism.

title: Ergodicity, minimality and unique ergodicity of nilsystems
description: For a nilsystem (G/Γ, x↦τx) with its Haar probability measure, ergodicity, minimality and unique ergodicity are equivalent.

title: Orbit closures in nilsystems are nilsystems
description: In a d-step nilsystem (G/Γ, x↦τx), the closed orbit of any point, with the restricted translation, is topologically conjugate to a d-step nilsystem.

title: Host–Kra cube measure
description: For an ergodic system (X,μ,T), μ^[1]=μ×μ on X^[1]=X², and μ^[d+1] on X^[d+1]=X^[d]×X^[d] is the relatively independent self-joining of μ^[d] over the σ-algebra of T^[d]-invariant sets. It is invariant and ergodic for the cube group, its one-dimensional marginals equal μ, and factor maps carry cube measures to cube measures.

title: Gowers–Host–Kra uniformity seminorm
description: For an ergodic system (X,μ,T), d≥1 and f∈L^∞(μ), |||f|||_d=(∫∏_(ε⊂[d]) C^(|ε|)f(x_ε) dμ^[d](x))^(1/2^d), where μ^[d] is the Host–Kra cube measure and C is complex conjugation. It is a seminorm.

title: Host–Kra structure theorem for uniformity seminorms
description: For an ergodic system (X,μ,T) and d≥1 the following are equivalent: (X,μ,T) is measure-theoretically isomorphic to an inverse limit of (d−1)-step ergodic nilsystems; |||·|||_d is a norm on L^∞(μ); the coordinate x_∅ is μ^[d]-almost everywhere a measurable function of the other coordinates.

title: Host–Kra L² convergence of cubic averages
description: For an ergodic system (X,μ,T), d≥1 and f_ε∈L^∞(μ), ∅≠ε⊂[d], the averages N^(−d)∑_(0≤n_1,…,n_d<N)∏_ε f_ε(T^(n·ε)x) converge in L²(μ), and the limit F satisfies ∫gF dμ=∫g(x_∅)∏_ε f_ε(x_ε)dμ^[d](x) for every g∈L^∞(μ).

title: Everywhere uniform convergence of cubic averages on nilsystems
description: On a minimal (d−1)-step nilsystem, for continuous functions f_ε, ∅≠ε⊂[d], the cubic averages N^(−d)∑_(0≤n_i<N)∏_ε f_ε(T^(n·ε)x) converge at every point and uniformly in x.

title: Minimal nilsystems close dynamical cubes uniquely
description: For d≥1, a minimal d-step nilsystem (X,T) satisfies: if (x,y,…,y)∈Q^[d+1](X), the closure of the cubes (T^(n·ε)z)_(ε∈{0,1}^(d+1)), then x=y.

title: Regionally proximal relation of order d
description: For a compact metric system (X,T) and d≥1, (x,y)∈RP^[d] if for every δ>0 there are x′,y′∈X and n∈ℤᵈ with d(x,x′)<δ, d(y,y′)<δ and d(T^(n·ε)x′,T^(n·ε)y′)<δ for every nonempty ε⊂{1,…,d}. RP^[1] is the classical regionally proximal relation.

title: Cube criterion for the regionally proximal relation of order d
description: For a minimal system (X,T) and d≥1, (x,y)∈RP^[d] exactly when (x,y,y,…,y)∈Q^[d+1](X); RP^[d] is a closed invariant equivalence relation.

title: Lifting of higher-order regionally proximal pairs through factor maps
description: If π:X→Y is a factor map between minimal systems and d≥1, then (π×π)(RP^[d](X))=RP^[d](Y).

title: Iwasawa decomposition of the real points of a reductive group
description: For a connected reductive group G over ℝ and a minimal ℝ-parabolic subgroup P₀, some maximal compact subgroup K of G(ℝ) satisfies G(ℝ)=P₀(ℝ)K, refining to G(ℝ)=KAN. Applied to the restriction of scalars of a complex group it gives G(ℂ)=B(ℂ)K for a Borel B.

title: Bruhat–Tits Iwasawa decomposition at a special point
description: Let G be connected reductive over a nonarchimedean local field F, P₀ a minimal F-parabolic and S⊂P₀ a maximal F-split torus. The stabilizer K of a special point of the apartment of S in the extended Bruhat–Tits building is a maximal compact subgroup of G(F) and G(F)=P₀(F)K.

title: Maximality of hyperspecial subgroups
description: If G is connected reductive over a nonarchimedean local field F and 𝒢 is an affine O_F-model of G with connected reductive special fiber, then 𝒢(O_F) is a maximal compact subgroup of G(F).

title: Smooth projective scheme of parabolic subgroups of a reductive group scheme
description: For a reductive group scheme G over a ring k and a parabolic subgroup scheme P, the functor of closed subgroup schemes étale-locally conjugate to P is represented by a smooth projective k-scheme G/P, and g↦gPg⁻¹ defines G→G/P.

title: Valuative criterion of properness over a discrete valuation ring
description: If R is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and X is a proper R-scheme, the restriction map X(R)→X(K) is a bijection.

title: Rational conjugacy of geometrically conjugate parabolic subgroups
description: For a connected reductive group G over a field k, two parabolic k-subgroups conjugate under G(k̄) are conjugate under G(k). Consequently, for a parabolic P, G(k)/P(k)→(G/P)(k) is bijective.

title: Torsor under a group scheme
description: For a group scheme G over S, a right G-torsor is an S-scheme X with a right G-action such that X→S is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation and (x,g)↦(x,xg) is an isomorphism X×_SG→X×_SX.

title: Smoothness of torsors under smooth group schemes
description: A torsor under a smooth group scheme over S is smooth over S.

title: Dynamic description of parabolic subgroups over a field
description: Let G be connected reductive over a field k, P a parabolic k-subgroup and T⊂P a maximal k-torus. Some cocharacter λ:G_m→T gives P=P_G(λ), the subgroup of g for which t↦λ(t)gλ(t)⁻¹ extends over t=0; the centralizer of λ is a Levi subgroup and the points with limit 1 form the unipotent radical.

title: Dynamic parabolic subgroup schemes
description: For a smooth affine group scheme G over a ring k and a cocharacter λ:G_m→G, the functor P_G(λ) of points whose λ-conjugates have a limit at t=0 is a smooth closed subgroup scheme, with connected fibers if G has them. If G is reductive and λ factors through a maximal torus, P_G(λ) is a parabolic subgroup scheme.

title: Spreading out a maximal torus of a reductive group scheme
description: For a reductive group scheme 𝒢 over O_(F,S) with generic fiber G and a maximal F-torus T⊂G, after enlarging S by finitely many primes the schematic closure of T in 𝒢 is a maximal torus of 𝒢.

title: Existence of affine integral models of algebraic groups
description: Every affine algebraic group G over a number field F, and every finite set S of places containing the infinite ones, admits an affine integral group model over O_(F,S), for example the schematic closure of G in GL_n for a faithful representation G→GL_n.

title: Principal ideal domain
description: An integral domain R in which every ideal is principal, that is, equal to aR={ar:r∈R} for some a∈R. Examples are ℤ, ℤ_p and the polynomial ring in one variable over a field.

title: Rank of a finite free module over a commutative ring
description: If R is a nonzero commutative ring and a free R-module has a finite basis, all its bases have the same number of elements; this number is its rank. The module Rⁿ of n-tuples, with its coordinate basis, is free of rank n, and every free module of rank n is isomorphic to Rⁿ.

title: Kuz′min–Tate module of a number field
description: For a number field K, a prime ℓ and the cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞/K, the Kuz′min–Tate module is T_K=Gal(K∞^cd/K∞), where K∞^cd is the maximal abelian pro-ℓ extension of K∞ in which every place of K∞ splits completely. Γ=Gal(K∞/K) acts on it by conjugation, making it a module over the Iwasawa algebra of Γ.

title: Logarithmic class groups as Kuz′min–Tate coinvariants
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), with cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞=⋃K_n and Γ=Gal(K∞/K) topologically generated by γ. The Kuz′min–Tate module T_K is a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra of Γ, and for every n the ℓ-primary logarithmic class group of K_n is isomorphic to the coinvariant quotient T_K/(γ^(ℓⁿ)−1)T_K.

title: Local roots-of-unity criterion for the Leopoldt conjecture
description: A number field K satisfies the Leopoldt conjecture for a prime ℓ (the compositum of its ℤ_ℓ-extensions has Galois group ℤ_ℓ^(r₂+1)) if and only if every element of ℤ_ℓ⊗K× whose image in each local ℓ-primary completion of a finite place is a root of unity is a global root of unity: (ℤ_ℓ⊗K×)∩∏_pμ(K_p)=μ_(ℓ∞)(K).

title: Logarithmic class group as degree-zero logarithmic divisor classes
description: For a number field K containing μ_(2ℓ), ℓ-adic class field theory identifies its ℓ-primary logarithmic class group Gal(K^lc/K∞) with D̃ℓ_K/P̃ℓ_K. Here D̃ℓ_K is the ℤ_ℓ-module of degree-zero logarithmic divisors ∑a_p p over finite places (a_p∈ℤ_ℓ, almost all zero, ∑a_p deg p=0), and P̃ℓ_K is the image of ℤ_ℓ⊗K× under x↦∑ν̃_p(x)p, where the logarithmic valuation is ν̃_p(x)=−Log_ℓ N_(K_p/ℚ_ℓ)(x)/deg p, Log_ℓ being Iwasawa’s ℓ-adic logarithm of the ℓ-adic absolute value.

title: Exact sequence of logarithmic units and ℓ-units
description: For a number field K containing μ_(2ℓ), let E′_K=ℤ_ℓ⊗(ℓ-units of K) and Cℓ′_K the ℓ-part of its class group modulo classes of primes above ℓ. The logarithmic divisor map gives an exact sequence 1→Ẽ_K→E′_K→⊕̃_(p|ℓ)ℤ_ℓp→C̃ℓ_K→Cℓ′_K, where Ẽ_K is the global logarithmic unit group, ⊕̃ denotes degree-zero logarithmic divisors supported above ℓ, and C̃ℓ_K is the ℓ-primary logarithmic class group.

title: Dirichlet’s S-unit theorem
description: For a number field K and a finite set S of its places containing all archimedean places, the S-unit group is isomorphic to μ(K)×ℤ^(|S|−1), where μ(K) is the finite group of roots of unity in K.

title: Structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID
description: Every finitely generated module M over a principal ideal domain R is isomorphic to Rʳ⊕R/(d₁)⊕⋯⊕R/(d_k) with nonzero nonunits d₁|d₂|⋯|d_k. The rank r and the ideals (d_i) are uniquely determined; in particular M is the direct sum of its torsion submodule and a free module of rank r.

title: Dedekind’s theorem on independence of characters
description: For a group G and a field F, every finite set of distinct group homomorphisms χ₁,…,χ_m:G→F× is linearly independent over F as F-valued functions on G: if ∑a_iχ_i(g)=0 for every g∈G, with a_i∈F, then all a_i=0.

title: Strong Feller Markov kernel
description: A Markov kernel P on a topological space with its Borel σ-algebra is strong Feller if Pf(x)=∫f(y)P(x,dy) is a continuous function of x for every bounded Borel measurable f.

title: Comparison theorem for Markov chain drift inequalities
description: Let (X_k) be a Markov chain with natural filtration (F_k), let Z_k≥0 be adapted, and let f_k,s_k≥0 be measurable functions with E[Z_{k+1}|F_k]≤Z_k−f_k(X_k)+s_k(X_k) for every k. Then for every stopping time τ and initial state x, E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ−1}f_k(X_k)]≤Z_0(x)+E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ−1}s_k(X_k)].

title: Existence of small sets for a ψ-irreducible kernel
description: If a Markov kernel P on a countably generated measurable space is ψ-irreducible, then every measurable set A with ψ(A)>0 contains a small set C with ψ(C)>0: for some m≥1 and nonzero measure ν with ν(C)>0, P^m(x,B)≥ν(B) for all x∈C and measurable B. The result goes back to Jain and Jamison and to Orey.

title: Regularity of finite Borel measures on Polish spaces
description: Every finite Borel measure μ on a Polish space is regular: for every Borel set A, μ(A)=sup{μ(K):K⊆A compact}=inf{μ(O):O⊇A open}.

title: Semicontinuity characterization of weak Feller kernels
description: A Markov kernel P on a locally compact separable metric space is weak Feller if and only if x↦P(x,O) is lower semicontinuous for every open set O. Then for every probability (a_n) on the nonnegative integers, x↦∑_n a_nP^n(x,O) is lower semicontinuous for open O, and x↦∑_n a_nP^n(x,F) is upper semicontinuous for closed F.

title: Fenchel–Rockafellar duality theorem
description: Let Θ,Ξ:E→(−∞,+∞] be convex functions on a normed space E with continuous dual E*. If some z₀ has Θ(z₀)<∞, Ξ(z₀)<∞ and Θ is continuous at z₀, then inf_E(Θ+Ξ)=max_{z*∈E*}[−Θ*(−z*)−Ξ*(z*)], where * denotes the Fenchel conjugate; the maximum is attained.

title: Lipschitz approximation of lower semicontinuous functions by inf-convolution
description: On a metric space (X,d), let F:X→[0,∞] be lower semicontinuous and not identically ∞. Then F_n(x)=inf_y[F(y)+n·d(x,y)] are finite nonnegative n-Lipschitz functions, nondecreasing in n, and F_n(x)↑F(x) for every x; thus F is the supremum of an increasing sequence of uniformly continuous nonnegative functions.

title: Nummelin splitting of a Markov chain
description: Given a one-step minorization P(x,·)≥δ1_C(x)ν(·) with δ∈(0,1] and a probability ν, the split chain lives on X×{0,1}: at a visit to x∈C an independent coin with success probability δ is tossed; on success the next state is drawn from ν, otherwise from (P(x,·)−δν)/(1−δ), and outside C from P(x,·). Its first coordinate is a copy of the original chain, and C×{1} is an atom of the split chain, accessible when the original chain is ψ-irreducible and ψ(C)>0.

title: Geometric ergodic theorem for a Kendall atom
description: Let an aperiodic ψ-irreducible Markov chain with invariant probability π have an accessible atom α (all states of α have the same transition law) that is f-Kendall of rate κ>1 for a measurable f≥1, i.e. E_α[∑_{k=0}^{τ_α−1}f(X_k)κ^k]<∞ with τ_α the first return time. Then the set S where U(x)=E_x[∑_{k=1}^{τ_α}f(X_k)κ^k] is finite is absorbing and full, and there are r>1 and R<∞ with ∑_n r^n‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_f≤R·U(x) for every x∈S. The proof uses Kendall's renewal theorem and the regenerative decomposition.

title: Geometric regularity of petite Kendall sets
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain and measurable f≥1, a set C is petite and f-Kendall, meaning sup_{x∈C}E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_C−1}f(X_k)κ^k]<∞ for some κ>1, if and only if ψ(C)>0 and C is f-geometrically regular: for every B with ψ(B)>0 there is r>1 with sup_{x∈C}E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_B−1}f(X_k)r^k]<∞. Here τ denotes first return times.

title: Drift characterization of geometric regularity of a Markov chain
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain: if an everywhere finite V≥1, a petite set C, β>0 and b<∞ satisfy PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C, then for every B with ψ(B)>0 there are r>1 and c(B)<∞ with E_x[∑_{k=1}^{τ_B}V(X_k)r^k]≤c(B)V(x) for all x. Conversely, if for some petite C and κ>1 the quantity E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_C−1}f(X_k)κ^k] is finite for every x and bounded on C, with f≥1, then such a drift inequality holds for some everywhere finite V≥f.

title: Skeleton inheritance of geometric drift
description: For a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain, if V≥1, a petite set C, β>0 and b<∞ satisfy PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C, then for every m≥1 the m-skeleton P^m satisfies P^mV≤ρV+b′1_{C′} with ρ<1, b′<∞ and a set C′ petite for P^m. Consequently a set that is f-geometrically regular for the chain is f-geometrically regular for every skeleton.

title: Petite sets are small for aperiodic chains
description: For a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov kernel P, every petite set C is small: there are m≥1, ε>0 and a probability ν with P^m(x,·)≥εν for every x∈C.

title: f-norm ergodic theorem for Markov chains
description: For a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain and measurable f≥1, the following are equivalent: (i) the chain is positive recurrent with invariant probability π and π(f)<∞; (ii) some petite set C has sup_{x∈C}E_x[∑_{n=0}^{τ_C−1}f(X_n)]<∞; (iii) some petite C, b<∞ and nonnegative V, finite at some point, satisfy PV≤V−f+b1_C. Then {V<∞} is absorbing and full, and ‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_f→0 for every x in it.

title: Harris recurrence from almost sure return to a petite set
description: A ψ-irreducible Markov chain is Harris recurrent if some petite set C is reached almost surely from every initial state, that is P_x(τ_C<∞)=1 for every x.

title: Essential spectral radius of a bounded operator
description: For a bounded operator L on a complex Banach space, r_ess(L)=lim_n(inf_K‖L^n−K‖)^{1/n}, the infimum being over compact operators K. Equivalently it is the infimum of r₀ such that the spectrum of L outside the closed disc of radius r₀ consists of finitely many isolated eigenvalues with finite-dimensional generalized eigenspaces.

title: Quasi-compact operator
description: A bounded operator L on a complex Banach space is quasi-compact if its essential spectral radius is strictly smaller than its spectral radius r(L). Then for r_ess(L)<r₀<r(L) the space splits into finitely many generalized eigenspaces for eigenvalues of modulus at least r₀ and a closed invariant subspace on which ‖L^n‖=O(r₀^n).

title: Guibourg–Hervé–Ledoux quasi-compactness theorem on weighted-supremum spaces
description: Let P be a Markov kernel and V≥1 a weight with PV/V bounded. Suppose the weak drift condition P^NV≤δ^NV+d holds for some N≥1, δ<1 and d<∞, and that some power P^ℓ maps the bounded measurable functions compactly into B_V. Then P is power-bounded and quasi-compact on B_V, and its essential spectral radius there is at most δ_V(P), the infimum of such δ.

title: Spectral characterization of V-geometric ergodicity
description: Let a Markov kernel P have an invariant probability π with π(V)<∞. P is V-uniformly ergodic if and only if P is power-bounded and quasi-compact on B_V with 1 a simple eigenvalue and the only eigenvalue of modulus one. Then the optimal rate ρ_V(P) is at least r_ess(P); for r_ess(P)<r₀<1, ρ_V(P)≤r₀ if no eigenvalue satisfies r₀≤|λ|<1, and otherwise ρ_V(P) is the largest modulus of these eigenvalues.

title: Unique invariant law of a contractive iterated function system
description: Let X_n=F(θ_n,X_{n−1}) with iid θ_n and maps F(θ,·) Lipschitz on a Polish space (X,d). If for some a≥1 and x₀ one has E[d(F(θ₁,x₀),x₀)^a]<∞ and κ̂_a=lim_n(E[Lip(F_{θ_n}∘⋯∘F_{θ₁})^a])^{1/(na)}<1, then the transition kernel has a unique invariant probability π, and ∫d(x₀,y)^aπ(dy)<∞.

title: Geometric convergence of contractive iterated function systems on weighted Lipschitz functions
description: Let X_n=F(θ_n,X_{n−1}) with iid θ_n and maps F(θ,·) Lipschitz on a Polish space (X,d), and suppose for some a≥1 and x₀ that E[d(F(θ₁,x₀),x₀)^a]<∞ and κ₁=(E[Lip(F(θ₁,·))^a])^{1/a}<1; let π be the invariant law. Put p(x)=1+d(x,x₀) and let L_a be the functions with m_a(f)=sup_{x≠y}|f(x)−f(y)|/(d(x,y)(p(x)+p(y))^{a−1})<∞, normed by m_a(f)+sup|f|/p^a. Then P acts boundedly on L_a, and there are c,c′ with sup_x|P^nf(x)−π(f)|/p(x)^a≤cκ₁^n m_a(f) and ‖P^nf−π(f)‖_{L_a}≤c′κ₁^n‖f‖_{L_a} for all n≥1 and f∈L_a.

title: Structure of the invariant eigenprojection of a quasi-compact Markov kernel
description: If a Markov kernel P is power-bounded and quasi-compact on a weighted-supremum space B_V and 1 is its only eigenvalue of modulus one, then P^n converges in operator norm to a finite-rank projection Π onto Ker(P−I), and Πf=∑_{k=1}^mμ_k(f)f_k for linearly independent nonnegative P-harmonic f_k∈B_V and P-invariant probabilities μ_k with μ_k(V)<∞.

title: Spectrum of the Banach-space adjoint
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Banach space X, its adjoint T′ on the dual space X*, defined by (T′φ)(x)=φ(Tx), has the same operator norm and the same spectrum as T.

title: Locally integrable function on an open Euclidean set
description: A Lebesgue measurable function f on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ is locally integrable if ∫_K|f|dx<∞ for every compact K⊂Ω. The space L¹_loc(Ω) consists of such functions, identified when they agree almost everywhere.

title: Harmonic function on an open Euclidean set
description: A twice continuously differentiable real or complex function u on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ satisfying Laplace’s equation Δu=∑ᵢ∂ᵢ²u=0 throughout Ω. For n=2 this is a harmonic function on a plane domain.

title: Superharmonic function on an open Euclidean set
description: A lower semicontinuous u:Ω→(−∞,∞] on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ, not identically ∞ on any connected component, is superharmonic if u(x) is at least the surface-measure average of u over the sphere S(x,r) whenever the closed ball of radius r about x lies in Ω. For n=2 this is the superharmonic function on a planar domain.

title: Subharmonic function on a planar domain
description: A function v:Ω→[−∞,∞) on an open Ω⊆ℝ² is subharmonic if −v is superharmonic: v is upper semicontinuous, not identically −∞ on any component, and its value at each center is at most its circle average whenever the closed disk lies in Ω.

title: Positive distribution on an open Euclidean set
description: A distribution T on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ is positive (nonnegative), written T≥0, if T(φ)≥0 for every real test function φ∈C_c^∞(Ω) with φ≥0; T≤S means S−T≥0.

title: Convolution of a distribution with a test function
description: For a distribution T on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and φ∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ) supported in B(0,δ), (T*φ)(x)=T(φ(x−·)) for points of Ω at distance more than δ from its boundary. It is a smooth function with ∂^α(T*φ)=T*∂^αφ=(∂^αT)*φ, and T*j_ε→T as distributions for scaled mollifiers j_ε.

title: Mean-value property of harmonic functions
description: If u is harmonic on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and the closed ball of radius r about x lies in Ω, then u(x) equals both the surface-measure average of u over the sphere S(x,r) and the volume average of u over the ball B(x,r).

title: Harnack inequality for positive harmonic functions
description: For a connected open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and a compact K⊂Ω there is a constant C depending only on n, K and Ω such that every positive harmonic function u on Ω satisfies sup_K u≤C inf_K u. On a ball, explicit constants follow from the Poisson integral formula.

title: Locally uniform limits of harmonic functions are harmonic
description: If harmonic functions on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ converge uniformly on compact subsets of Ω, then the limit is harmonic on Ω, and every partial derivative of the sequence converges uniformly on compact subsets to the corresponding derivative of the limit.

title: Maximum principle for harmonic functions
description: A real harmonic function u on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ that attains its maximum or minimum at a point is constant on the connected component of Ω containing that point. If limsup u(a_k)≤M for every sequence (a_k) in Ω tending to a point of ∂Ω or to ∞, then u≤M on Ω; dually for liminf and lower bounds.

title: Superharmonicity and Laplacian of the potential of a positive measure
description: For a compactly supported positive Borel measure μ on ℝⁿ, let U_μ(x)=∫Γ(x−y)dμ(y), where Γ is the fundamental solution of −Δ: (2π)⁻¹log(1/|x|) for n=2 and |x|^{2−n}/((n−2)|S^{n−1}|) for n≥3. Then U_μ is superharmonic on ℝⁿ, harmonic off the support of μ, and −ΔU_μ=μ as distributions.

title: Local integrability of superharmonic functions
description: A superharmonic function on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ is finite almost everywhere and locally integrable on Ω; its sphere and ball averages over closed balls contained in Ω are finite.

title: Smooth approximation of superharmonic functions by mollification
description: If u is superharmonic on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and j_ε are scaled radial mollifiers, then u*j_ε is smooth and superharmonic on the points of Ω at distance more than ε from the boundary, and u*j_ε increases pointwise to u as ε decreases to zero.

title: Laplacian criterion for C² superharmonic functions
description: A twice continuously differentiable real function u on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ is superharmonic exactly when Δu≤0 at every point of Ω.

title: Monotone means of a superharmonic function
description: If u is superharmonic on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and x∈Ω, then its sphere and ball averages over radius r about x decrease as r increases and tend to u(x) as r→0. Consequently two superharmonic functions that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere.

title: Poisson modification of a superharmonic function
description: If u is superharmonic on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and a closed ball B̄ lies in Ω, replacing u inside the open ball B by the Poisson integral of its boundary values gives a function u_B≤u that is superharmonic on Ω and harmonic in B.

title: Perron envelope theorem for subharmonic families
description: Let V be a nonempty family of subharmonic functions on a connected open Ω⊆ℝⁿ that is closed under pairwise maxima and under Poisson modification in closed balls contained in Ω. Then the pointwise supremum of V is either identically +∞ or harmonic on Ω.

title: Poisson integral solution of the Dirichlet problem on the disk
description: For a continuous function g on the unit circle, P[g](z)=(2π)⁻¹∫₀²π(1−|z|²)/|e^{it}−z|²·g(e^{it})dt is harmonic in the open unit disk and extends continuously to g on the circle. Conversely, a function continuous on the closed disk and harmonic inside equals the Poisson integral of its boundary values.

title: Irreducible decomposition of a noetherian topological space
description: A nonempty noetherian topological space is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets. An irredundant such decomposition is unique up to order, and its members are exactly the irreducible components of the space.

title: Orbit–stabilizer theorem for a group action
description: For a group G acting on a set X and x∈X, the map gG_x↦gx is a bijection from the left cosets of the stabilizer G_x onto the orbit Gx. In particular a transitive action identifies X with G/G_x, and |Gx|=[G:G_x].

title: First isomorphism theorem for groups
description: For a group homomorphism φ:G→H, the kernel of φ is a normal subgroup of G and φ induces an isomorphism G/ker φ≅φ(G). In particular a surjective homomorphism with kernel N gives [G:N]=|H|.

title: Local–global correspondence for lattices on a rational vector space
description: Let V be a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space and L a ℤ-lattice on V. A lattice M on V is determined by its localizations, M=⋂_p(V∩M_p). Conversely, any family of ℤ_p-lattices N_p on V_p=ℚ_p⊗V with N_p=L_p for almost all primes p is the family of localizations of a unique lattice on V.

title: Surjectivity of the local spinor norm in dimension at least three
description: For a prime p and a nondegenerate quadratic space V over ℚ_p of dimension at least 3, the spinor norm maps the special orthogonal group SO(V) onto the full square-class group ℚ_p×/(ℚ_p×)².

title: Spinor norms of a unimodular lattice at an odd prime
description: For an odd prime p and a unimodular quadratic ℤ_p-lattice L of rank at least 2, the spinor norms of the rotations of L are exactly the unit square classes: θ(SO(L))=ℤ_p×(ℚ_p×)²/(ℚ_p×)².

title: Spinor norm image of a rational rotation group
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space V over ℚ of dimension at least 3, the spinor norm of SO(V) is all of ℚ×/(ℚ×)² when V⊗ℝ is isotropic, and is the group of positive square classes when V⊗ℝ is anisotropic (definite).

title: Degree equality ef=[L:K] for a complete discretely valued field
description: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation and L/K a finite extension, with the unique extension of the valuation to L. Then its ramification index e and residue degree f satisfy ef=[L:K].

title: k-pseudorandom measure on ℤ/Nℤ (Green–Tao)
description: For fixed k≥3, a family of functions ν=ν_N:ℤ/Nℤ→[0,∞) with average 1+o(1) as N→∞ is k-pseudorandom if it satisfies Green–Tao's (k·2^(k−1),3k−4,k)-linear forms condition, that averages of products of ν along systems of pairwise non-parallel affine-linear forms are 1+o(1), and their 2^(k−1)-correlation condition, bounding correlations of shifts of ν by a weight with bounded moments.

title: Green–Tao relative Szemerédi theorem
description: For k≥3 and 0<δ≤1, if ν is a k-pseudorandom measure on ℤ/Nℤ and 0≤f≤ν with average at least δ, then the average of f(x)f(x+r)⋯f(x+(k−1)r) over x,r∈ℤ/Nℤ is at least c(k,δ)−o(1), where c(k,δ)>0 is the constant in the Varnavides form of Szemerédi's theorem.

title: Green–Tao pseudorandom majorant of the W-tricked primes
description: With W the product of the primes up to a slowly growing w(N) and the W-tricked von Mangoldt function Λ̃(n)=(φ(W)/W)log(Wn+1) when Wn+1 is prime and 0 otherwise, for every k≥3 and every large prime N there is a k-pseudorandom measure ν on ℤ/Nℤ, built from Goldston–Yıldırım truncated divisor sums, with ν(n)≥k^(−1)2^(−k−5)Λ̃(n) for ε_kN≤n≤2ε_kN, where ε_k=1/(2^k(k+4)!).

title: Tate’s theorem relating K2 of a global field to Galois cohomology
description: For a global field F and a prime ℓ different from its characteristic, Tate's Galois symbol map identifies the ℓ-primary part of K₂F with the torsion subgroup of H²(F,ℤ_ℓ(2)); equivalently H¹(F,(ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ)(2)) modulo its maximal divisible subgroup is canonically isomorphic to the ℓ-primary part of K₂F.

title: Left-exact cotangent sequence for a generically separable morphism
description: Let π:X→Y be a dominant morphism of irreducible varieties of the same dimension over a field k, with Y smooth and K(X)/K(Y) finite separable. Then the cotangent sequence 0→π*Ω_(Y/k)→Ω_(X/k)→Ω_(X/Y)→0 of sheaves of Kähler differentials is exact; that is, π*Ω_(Y/k)→Ω_(X/k) is injective.

title: Degree of a coherent sheaf on a projective curve
description: For a coherent sheaf F on an irreducible reduced projective curve C over a field k, deg F=χ(C,F)−(rank F)·χ(C,O_C), where rank F is the rank at the generic point and χ is the Euler characteristic of sheaf cohomology.

title: Discreteness of rational points in adelic points of an affine variety
description: For an affine variety X over a number field F, the set X(F) is discrete in X(A_F) for the adelic topology. Consequently X(F) meets each compact subset of X(A_F) in a finite set.

title: Algebraic variety over a field
description: An algebraic variety over a field k is a scheme X with a separated morphism of finite type X→Spec k that is geometrically reduced: its base change to an algebraic closure of k is reduced, i.e. its rings of sections have no nonzero nilpotent elements. Varieties need not be irreducible, connected or affine. Over an algebraically closed field this means a reduced separated k-scheme of finite type.

title: Algebraic group over a field
description: An algebraic group over a field k is a group scheme G over Spec k whose structure morphism G→Spec k is of finite type; equivalently a finite-type k-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the group axioms. It need not be smooth, connected or affine.

title: Action of an algebraic group on an algebraic variety
description: An action of an algebraic group G on an algebraic variety X over k is a morphism μ:G×_k X→X with μ∘(e×id_X)=id_X and μ∘(m×id_X)=μ∘(id_G×μ) as morphisms G×G×X→X; on R-points it gives actions of the groups G(R) on X(R). For a k-point x the orbit map G→X is g↦μ(g,x), and the orbit of x is its image in X.

title: Procyclic group
description: A profinite group G is procyclic if it has a topological generator: an element g whose cyclic subgroup {gⁿ:n∈ℤ} is dense in G. Finite cyclic groups with the discrete topology are procyclic.

title: Rational representation of an affine algebraic group
description: A rational representation of an affine algebraic group G with coordinate Hopf algebra A over a field k is a k-vector space V with a linear coaction ρ:V→V⊗A satisfying (id⊗Δ)ρ=(ρ⊗id)ρ and (id⊗ε)ρ=id; V may be infinite-dimensional. Every vector lies in a finite-dimensional subrepresentation, which is an algebraic representation, and v is invariant when ρ(v)=v⊗1.

title: Linearly reductive affine algebraic group
description: An affine algebraic group over a field is linearly reductive if every finite-dimensional algebraic representation is semisimple: each subrepresentation has an invariant complement, equivalently the representation is a direct sum of irreducible subrepresentations.

title: Centre–derived decomposition of a connected reductive group
description: For a connected reductive algebraic group G over a field, the centre Z(G) is of multiplicative type, the derived group G^der is semisimple, and the multiplication map Z(G)×G^der→G is surjective with finite central kernel, so G=Z(G)·G^der.

title: Semisimplicity of representations of groups of multiplicative type
description: Every finite-dimensional representation of an algebraic group of multiplicative type over a field is semisimple. Over an algebraically closed field, where such a group is diagonalizable, every representation is the direct sum of its weight spaces V_χ={v:gv=χ(g)v} for the characters χ.

title: Complete reducibility for semisimple algebraic groups in characteristic zero
description: Over a field of characteristic zero, every finite-dimensional representation of a semisimple algebraic group is semisimple: each subrepresentation has an invariant complement.

title: Dimension drop for proper closed subsets of irreducible finite-type schemes
description: If X is an irreducible scheme of finite type over a field and Z⊊X is a proper closed subset, then dim Z<dim X.

title: Profiniteness of Galois groups
description: For a Galois extension Ω/F, possibly infinite, the Galois group Gal(Ω/F) with its Krull topology is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected, hence a profinite group; it is the inverse limit of the finite groups Gal(E/F) over finite Galois subextensions E.

title: Cyclic Galois groups of extensions of finite fields
description: If E/F is an extension of degree n of finite fields with |F|=q, then E/F is Galois and Gal(E/F) is cyclic of order n, generated by the q-Frobenius x↦x^q.

title: Steinitz exchange lemma
description: If v₁,…,v_m are linearly independent and w₁,…,w_n span a vector space V, then m≤n and, after renumbering, v₁,…,v_m,w_(m+1),…,w_n spans V. In particular a linearly independent family in an n-dimensional space has at most n members.

title: Formal partial derivative of a multivariable polynomial
description: For f in R[x₁,…,x_n] over a commutative ring R, ∂f/∂x_i is the formal derivative of f regarded as a polynomial in x_i with coefficients in the polynomial ring in the other variables; it is R-linear and sends x^α to α_i x^(α−e_i).

title: Standard smooth algebra over a commutative ring
description: An R-algebra isomorphic to R[x₁,…,x_n]/(f₁,…,f_c) with c≤n such that the determinant of the c×c matrix (∂f_j/∂x_i) for 1≤i,j≤c maps to a unit of the quotient.

title: Naive cotangent complex of a ring map
description: For a presentation P=R[x_i]→S with kernel I, the two-term complex NL=(I/I²→Ω_(P/R)⊗_P S), f↦df⊗1, in degrees 1 and 0; it is independent of the presentation up to homotopy and its degree-0 homology is Ω_(S/R).

title: Naive cotangent complex criterion for smoothness
description: A finitely presented R-algebra S has the infinitesimal lifting property for square-zero (equivalently nilpotent) ideals if and only if H₁ of its naive cotangent complex vanishes and Ω_(S/R) is a finite projective S-module.

title: Local freeness of finite projective modules
description: A finitely generated projective module M over a commutative ring R is Zariski-locally free: Spec R is covered by standard opens D(g) such that each localization M_g is a free R_g-module of finite rank.

title: Morphism of schemes locally of finite presentation
description: A morphism f:X→S such that every point of X has an affine open neighbourhood U=Spec A mapping into an affine open V=Spec R of S with A a finitely presented R-algebra; equivalently this holds for all such affine pairs U,V.

title: Smoothness of a morphism of schemes at a point
description: A morphism f:X→S is smooth at x∈X if there are affine opens x∈U=Spec A⊂X and V=Spec R⊂S with f(U)⊂V such that A is a smooth finitely presented R-algebra (Stacks convention); f is smooth when it is smooth at every point.

title: Closed conjugacy classes are the semisimple classes in a reductive group
description: In a connected reductive algebraic group G over an algebraically closed field, the conjugacy class of an element x is Zariski closed in G if and only if x is semisimple.

title: Richardson’s comparison of involution orbits with conjugacy classes
description: Let G be reductive over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not two, θ an involution, K=G^θ and Q={g∈G:θ(g)=g⁻¹}. For x∈Q, the conjugation orbit of x under the identity component K⁰ is closed in Q if and only if the G-conjugacy class of x is closed in G.

title: Closed graph theorem for Banach spaces
description: A linear map T:X→Y between Banach spaces is bounded exactly when its graph {(x,Tx):x∈X} is closed in X×Y.

title: Elliptical range theorem for 2×2 complex matrices
description: The numerical range of a linear operator on a two-dimensional complex inner-product space is a closed elliptical disc, possibly degenerate to a segment or point, whose foci are the eigenvalues; in particular it is convex.

title: Pettis measurability theorem
description: For a measure space (S,𝒜,µ) and a Banach space X, a function f:S→X is strongly µ-measurable (a µ-a.e. limit of µ-simple functions) exactly when it is µ-essentially separably valued and weakly µ-measurable: x*∘f is µ-measurable for every x*∈X*. Pointwise version: on a measurable space, f is a pointwise limit of simple functions exactly when it is separably valued and every x*∘f is measurable.

title: Minkowski’s inequality for integrals
description: For σ-finite measure spaces X,Y, 1≤p<∞ and measurable F≥0 on X×Y, (∫_X(∫_Y F(x,y)dν(y))^p dμ(x))^{1/p}≤∫_Y(∫_X F(x,y)^p dμ(x))^{1/p}dν(y).

title: Product rule for derivatives of real functions
description: If real functions f and g are differentiable at x, then fg is differentiable at x and (fg)′(x)=f′(x)g(x)+f(x)g′(x).

title: Derivative of the real exponential function
description: The real exponential function is differentiable on ℝ and is its own derivative: exp′(x)=exp(x) for every real x.

title: Legendre’s criterion for continued-fraction convergents
description: If α is an irrational real number and p,q are integers with q>0 and |α−p/q|<1/(2q²), then p/q is a convergent of the simple continued fraction of α.

title: Approximation bounds for continued-fraction convergents
description: If α is irrational with simple continued-fraction convergents p_n/q_n in lowest terms, then 1/(q_n(q_n+q_(n+1)))<|α−p_n/q_n|<1/(q_n q_(n+1)) for every n≥0; in particular |α−p_n/q_n|>1/(2q_n q_(n+1)).

title: Path component of a topological space
description: For a point x of a topological space X, its path component is the set of points joined to x by a continuous path [0,1]→X; equivalently the largest path-connected subset containing x. The path components partition X.

title: Path-connected spaces are connected
description: Every path-connected topological space is connected.

title: Poisson-integral solution of the Dirichlet problem for the ball
description: For continuous f on the unit sphere S⊂ℝⁿ, the function equal on the open unit ball to P[f](x)=∫_S f(ζ)(1−|x|²)/|x−ζ|ⁿ dσ(ζ), with σ normalized surface measure, and equal to f on S is continuous on the closed ball and harmonic in the open ball.

title: Rank–nullity theorem
description: For a linear map T:V→W with V finite dimensional, dim V=dim ker T+dim im T. In particular an injective linear map from a finite-dimensional vector space to itself is surjective.

title: Boundedness of continuous functions on compact spaces
description: Every continuous real-valued function on a compact topological space is bounded above and below.

title: Urysohn lemma for locally compact Hausdorff spaces
description: If K is a compact subset of an open set U in a locally compact Hausdorff space X, there is a continuous f:X→[0,1] with f=1 on K whose support is compact and contained in U.

title: Regularity of locally finite Borel measures on σ-compact locally compact spaces
description: On a locally compact Hausdorff space in which every open set is σ-compact, in particular a second-countable one, every Borel measure finite on compact sets is outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on every Borel set.

title: σ-algebra of a stopping time
description: For a stopping time T of a filtration (F_t) on a probability space (Ω,F,P), F_T consists of the events A∈F with A∩{T≤t}∈F_t for every time t: the information available up to time T.

title: John ellipsoid of a convex body
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, the unique ellipsoid of maximal volume contained in K, an ellipsoid being the image of the closed Euclidean unit ball under an invertible affine map.

title: John’s characterization of the maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoid
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ containing the closed unit ball B, B is the maximal-volume ellipsoid in K if and only if there are points u₁,…,u_m on the boundaries of both B and K and weights c_i>0 with ∑c_iu_i=0 and ∑c_i⟨x,u_i⟩²=|x|² for every x∈ℝⁿ.

title: Supporting hyperplane theorem
description: Through every boundary point x of a closed convex set C⊂ℝⁿ passes a supporting hyperplane: some nonzero u satisfies ⟨y,u⟩≤⟨x,u⟩ for every y∈C.

title: Modification (version) of a stochastic process
description: Two stochastic processes X and Y on the same probability space with the same time index set are modifications, or versions, of each other if P(X_t=Y_t)=1 for every time t; the exceptional null set may depend on t.

title: Indistinguishable stochastic processes
description: Two stochastic processes X and Y on the same probability space with the same time index set are indistinguishable if there is a null set N such that X_t(ω)=Y_t(ω) for every time t and every ω outside N.

title: Uniform integrability of the conditional expectations of an integrable variable
description: If X is an integrable random variable on (Ω,F,P), the family {E[X|G] : G a sub-σ-algebra of F} is uniformly integrable.

title: Càdlàg modification of a submartingale under the usual conditions
description: If the filtration satisfies the usual conditions and X is a submartingale with t↦E[X_t] right-continuous, then X has a càdlàg modification that is again a submartingale; in particular every martingale has a càdlàg modification.

title: Gordon’s Gaussian min–max comparison inequality
description: Let (X_{t,u}) and (Y_{t,u}), (t,u)∈T×U with T,U compact, be almost surely bounded centered Gaussian processes with E(X_{t,u}−X_{t,u′})²≤E(Y_{t,u}−Y_{t,u′})² for all t,u,u′ and E(X_{t,u}−X_{t′,u′})²≥E(Y_{t,u}−Y_{t′,u′})² whenever t≠t′. Then E min_t max_u X_{t,u}≤E min_t max_u Y_{t,u}.

title: Monotonicity of the mean-norm deficit of standard Gaussian vectors
description: Let g_k be a standard Gaussian vector in ℝ^k. For integers 1≤n≤m, E‖g_m‖₂−E‖g_n‖₂≥√m−√n; equivalently k↦√k−E‖g_k‖₂ is nonincreasing.

title: Helly selection theorem for monotone functions
description: Every uniformly bounded sequence of nondecreasing real functions on a real interval has a subsequence converging pointwise at every point of the interval; the limit is nondecreasing.

title: Supporting hyperplane theorem in ℝᵈ
description: If C⊆ℝᵈ is convex and x∈ℝᵈ is not an interior point of C, there is a nonzero linear functional ξ on ℝᵈ with ξ(c)≤ξ(x) for every c∈C.

title: Relative interior of a convex set
description: The relative interior ri C of a convex set C⊆ℝᵈ is its interior relative to its affine hull aff C, the smallest affine subspace containing C, equivalently the set of all affine combinations of points of C.

title: Nonemptiness of the relative interior of a convex set
description: Every nonempty convex subset of ℝᵈ has nonempty relative interior.

title: Continuity of finite convex functions on the relative interior
description: A real-valued convex function on a convex set C⊆ℝᵈ is continuous on the relative interior of C, for the topology of the affine hull of C.

title: Weyl monotonicity of Hermitian eigenvalues
description: If A and H are n×n Hermitian matrices with A≼H in the Löwner order, then λ_i(A)≤λ_i(H) for every i, where λ_1≥⋯≥λ_n lists eigenvalues in decreasing order with multiplicity.

title: Integral representation of the positive definite matrix logarithm
description: For a positive definite complex matrix A, log A=∫_0^∞[(1+u)⁻¹I−(A+uI)⁻¹]du as an entrywise improper integral; the scalar case is log a=∫_0^∞[1/(1+u)−1/(a+u)]du for a>0.

title: Order reversal of inversion on positive definite matrices
description: If A and H are positive definite complex matrices with A≼H in the Löwner order, then H⁻¹≼A⁻¹; equivalently t↦−(t+u)⁻¹ is operator monotone on (0,∞) for every u≥0.

title: Predictable local martingales are continuous
description: On a complete filtered probability space, every real predictable càdlàg local martingale has continuous paths, up to indistinguishability.

title: Continuous finite-variation local martingales are constant
description: A real continuous local martingale whose paths have locally finite variation is indistinguishable from its initial value M_0.

title: Lower central series of a group
description: For a group G, the lower central series is G=γ₁(G)⊇γ₂(G)⊇⋯ with γ_(j+1)(G)=[γ_j(G),G], the subgroup generated by all commutators xyx⁻¹y⁻¹ with x∈γ_j(G) and y∈G. Each γ_j(G) is a normal subgroup of G, and γ₂(G) is the commutator subgroup.

title: Finite locally free morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes S′→S is finite locally free if S is covered by affine opens Spec R whose inverse images are affine, Spec A, with A a finitely generated free R-module. Its rank may vary on connected components of S.

title: Commutator grading of the lower central series
description: For every group G and all i,j≥1, the commutator subgroup of the i-th and j-th terms of the lower central series satisfies [γ_i(G),γ_j(G)]⊆γ_(i+j)(G).

title: Leibman’s primitive decomposition of a nilpotent unitary action
description: Let a finitely generated nilpotent group G act by unitary operators on a Hilbert space H. Then H is the closed orthogonal sum of G-invariant subspaces, each of which is the closed orthogonal sum of subspaces L_α permuted transitively by G, such that every element of G mapping some L_α onto itself acts on L_α either as a scalar or weakly mixingly.

title: Weakly mixing vector of a unitary operator
description: A unitary operator T on a Hilbert space H is weakly mixing on u∈H if (1/N)∑_(n=1)^N|⟨Tⁿu,v⟩|→0 for every v∈H. Equivalently, u is orthogonal to every eigenvector of T; such u form the closed invariant subspace complementary to the span of eigenvectors.

title: Isolator of a subgroup of a nilpotent group
description: If H is a subgroup of a nilpotent group G, then its isolator {x∈G: xⁿ∈H for some n≥1} is an isolated subgroup of G. If G is finitely generated, H has finite index in its isolator.

title: Compactness of complete totally bounded metric spaces
description: A metric space is compact if and only if it is complete and totally bounded. Consequently, a subset of a complete metric space is relatively compact exactly when it is totally bounded.

title: Northcott finiteness for projective heights
description: For constants C and d, only finitely many points P of projective space ℙᴺ over an algebraic closure of ℚ have absolute height H(P)≤C and field of definition of degree at most d over ℚ. In particular, for a number field K only finitely many points of ℙᴺ(K) have bounded height.

title: Quasi-parallelogram law for heights on an elliptic curve
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K and f a nonconstant even function on E, with h_f(P) the logarithmic height of f(P)∈ℙ¹. Then h_f(P+Q)+h_f(P−Q)=2h_f(P)+2h_f(Q)+O(1) for all P,Q∈E(K̄), the constant depending only on E and f. Consequently h_f([m]P)=m²h_f(P)+O(1) for each integer m.

title: Janossy densities of a point process
description: For a point process ξ on a space with reference measure λ and a bounded region A, the k-th Janossy density j_{A,k} is the symmetric density on Aᵏ, with respect to λᵏ, of the positions of the points of ξ in A on the event that ξ(A)=k. Normalizations differ by a factor k!.

title: Infinite-particle jump form on configuration space
description: For a point-process law μ on locally finite configurations in S⊆ℝᵈ and a nonnegative measurable jump-rate density ν(ξ,x;y), the bilinear form E(f,g)=½∫μ(dξ)∫ξ(dx)∫ν(ξ,x;y)[f(ξ−δ_x+δ_y)−f(ξ)][g(ξ−δ_x+δ_y)−g(ξ)]dy on local smooth functions f∈L²(μ) with E(f,f)<∞. A local smooth function depends only on the points in a bounded ball and is smooth and symmetric in their coordinates for each particle count.

title: Hölder continuous function
description: For 0<α≤1, a map f between metric spaces is α-Hölder continuous if its α-Hölder constant sup_{s≠t} d(f(s),f(t))/d(s,t)^α is finite. For functions on a bounded interval, an α-Hölder norm adds the supremum norm to this constant.

title: Sobolev space W₀¹,ᵖ of an open Euclidean set
description: For an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and 1≤p<∞, W₀¹,ᵖ(Ω) consists of the u∈W¹,ᵖ(Ω) that are limits in the W¹,ᵖ norm of compactly supported smooth functions on Ω; these are the W¹,ᵖ functions with zero boundary values in the Sobolev sense. For p=2 it is H₀¹(Ω).

title: Closability of an increasing limit of closable forms
description: If nonnegative symmetric forms E_n on a common dense domain D of a Hilbert space are closable and increase pointwise to a form E that is finite on D, then E is closable.

title: Closability of a superposition of closable forms
description: Let μ=∫μ_s λ(ds) be a mixture of measures and E(f,g)=∫E_s(f,g)λ(ds) for nonnegative symmetric forms E_s on a common domain D. If E_s is closable on L²(μ_s) for λ-almost every s, then E is closable on L²(μ).

title: Finite-volume reduction of closability for configuration-space jump forms
description: For an infinite-particle jump form E on local smooth functions in L²(μ), let E_r^n integrate, over configurations with exactly n points in the ball U_r, the energy of jumps of those n points and of jumps into U_r. If every E_r^n is closable on L²(μ), then E is closable. This is Esaki’s jump-form version of Osada’s Theorem 2 (1996) for diffusion forms.

title: Compactness of configuration sets with bounded local counts
description: For a nondecreasing sequence of natural numbers (a_r)_(r≥1), the set of locally finite configurations ξ on a closed S⊆ℝᵈ with ξ({x∈S:|x|<2^r})≤a_r for every r is compact in the vague topology.

title: Closure of a Markovian closable form is a Dirichlet form
description: Let E be a densely defined closable nonnegative symmetric form on real L²(X,m). If for every ε>0 there is φ_ε:ℝ→ℝ with φ_ε(t)=t on [0,1], −ε≤φ_ε≤1+ε and 0≤φ_ε(t′)−φ_ε(t)≤t′−t for t<t′, such that φ_ε∘u lies in the domain and E(φ_ε∘u,φ_ε∘u)≤E(u,u) for every u in the domain, then the closure of E is a symmetric Dirichlet form.

title: Exponential martingale inequality for Itô integrals
description: If M_t=∫₀ᵗu_s dW_s for an adapted process u that is locally square integrable and W is a Wiener process, then for all x,y>0, P(sup_t M_t≥x and ∫₀^∞|u_s|²ds≤y)≤exp(−x²/(2y)).

title: Unitary equivalence of unitary representations
description: Unitary representations (π₁,V₁) and (π₂,V₂) of a topological group G are unitarily equivalent if some unitary isomorphism U:V₁→V₂ of Hilbert spaces satisfies Uπ₁(g)=π₂(g)U for every g∈G.

title: Outer tensor product of unitary representations
description: For unitary representations π₁ of G₁ on V₁ and π₂ of G₂ on V₂, the outer tensor product π₁⊗π₂ is the unitary representation of G₁×G₂ on the Hilbert tensor product V₁⊗̂V₂ given on elementary tensors by (g₁,g₂)(v₁⊗v₂)=π₁(g₁)v₁⊗π₂(g₂)v₂ and extended by continuity.

title: Tempered random variable
description: For an invertible measure-preserving transformation θ of a probability space Ω, a measurable R:Ω→(0,∞) is tempered if |n|⁻¹log R(θⁿω)→0 as n→±∞ for almost every ω; that is, R grows and decays subexponentially along almost every orbit.

title: Oseledets splitting of an invertible linear cocycle
description: Let θ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of Ω and A:Ω→GL_d(ℝ) measurable, with A⁽ⁿ⁾(ω)=A(θⁿ⁻¹ω)⋯A(ω) and A⁽⁻ⁿ⁾(ω)=A⁽ⁿ⁾(θ⁻ⁿω)⁻¹. An Oseledets splitting is an almost everywhere defined measurable decomposition ℝᵈ=E₁(ω)⊕⋯⊕E_k(ω) with A(ω)E_i(ω)=E_i(θω), together with Lyapunov exponents λ₁>⋯>λ_k such that n⁻¹log‖A⁽ⁿ⁾(ω)v‖→λ_i as n→±∞ for every nonzero v∈E_i(ω). The multiplicity of λ_i is dim E_i(ω); λ_i is simple when this is one.

title: Twice continuously differentiable Euclidean map
description: A map on an open subset of ℝⁿ is C² if all its component partial derivatives of first and second order exist and are continuous.

title: Type I locally compact group
description: A locally compact group is type I if every unitary representation generates a type I von Neumann algebra. For second countable groups this is equivalent (Glimm) to the Fell topology on the unitary dual being T₀, or to injectivity of the map from the unitary dual to primitive ideals of the group C*-algebra.

title: Irreducible unitary representations of a product with a type I factor
description: Let G₁,G₂ be locally compact groups. Outer tensor products of irreducible unitary representations of G₁ and G₂ are irreducible representations of G₁×G₂. If G₁ or G₂ is type I, every irreducible unitary representation of G₁×G₂ is unitarily equivalent to such an outer tensor product, with both factors determined up to unitary equivalence.

title: Type I property of real algebraic groups
description: If G is an affine algebraic group over ℝ, the locally compact group G(ℝ) of real points is of type I.

title: Completeness of the space of bounded linear operators
description: If X is a normed space and Y a Banach space, the space of bounded linear operators X→Y with the operator norm is a Banach space.

title: Absolute-convergence criterion for Banach spaces
description: A normed vector space is complete exactly when every series ∑xₙ with ∑‖xₙ‖<∞ converges in norm.

title: Energy measure of a regular Dirichlet form
description: For a regular symmetric Dirichlet form (E,F) on L²(X,m) and a bounded u∈F, the energy measure μ⟨u⟩ is the unique positive finite Radon measure on X with ∫φ dμ⟨u⟩=2E(uφ,u)−E(u²,φ) for every φ∈F∩C_c(X). Strong locality is not assumed.

title: Equicontinuous family of functions
description: A family F of functions from a topological space X to a metric space (Y,d) is equicontinuous at x∈X if for every ε>0 there is a neighbourhood U of x with d(f(y),f(x))<ε for all y∈U and all f∈F; it is equicontinuous if this holds at every point of X.

title: Dirichlet’s integral over the standard simplex
description: For real s₁,…,s_{n+1}>0, the integral over {x∈ℝⁿ: x_i>0, x₁+⋯+x_n<1} of (1−x₁−⋯−x_n)^{s_{n+1}−1}∏_{i=1}^n x_i^{s_i−1} dx equals Γ(s₁)⋯Γ(s_{n+1})/Γ(s₁+⋯+s_{n+1}). For n=1 this is Euler’s beta integral.

title: Volume of a Euclidean simplex by a determinant
description: The n-dimensional Lebesgue measure of the n-simplex in ℝⁿ with vertices v₀,…,v_n is |det(v₁−v₀,…,v_n−v₀)|/n!.

title: Orthogonality relations for the short-time Fourier transform
description: Moyal’s formula: for f₁,f₂,g₁,g₂∈L²(ℝᵈ), the short-time Fourier transforms V_{g₁}f₁ and V_{g₂}f₂ lie in L²(ℝ²ᵈ) and ⟨V_{g₁}f₁,V_{g₂}f₂⟩=⟨f₁,f₂⟩·conj(⟨g₁,g₂⟩). In particular ‖V_gf‖₂=‖f‖₂‖g‖₂.

title: Agreement of Riemann and Lebesgue integrals
description: If f is Riemann integrable on a compact interval [a,b], then f is Lebesgue measurable and integrable on [a,b] with respect to Lebesgue measure, and its Lebesgue integral equals its Riemann integral.

title: Smoothness of convolution with a compactly supported smooth function
description: If f is locally integrable on ℝᵈ and φ∈C_c^∞(ℝᵈ), then f∗φ is smooth and ∂^α(f∗φ)=f∗∂^αφ for every multi-index α; for φ∈C_c¹ the same holds for first derivatives.

title: Pascal’s rule for binomial coefficients
description: For integers n≥0 and 1≤k≤n, binom(n+1,k)=binom(n,k)+binom(n,k−1).

title: Strongly continuous semigroup of bounded operators
description: A family (T_t)_{t≥0} of bounded linear operators on a Banach space X with T₀=I, T_{s+t}=T_sT_t for all s,t≥0, and ‖T_tx−x‖→0 as t↓0 for every x∈X; also called a C₀-semigroup.

title: Generator of a strongly continuous semigroup
description: For a strongly continuous semigroup (T_t) on a Banach space X, the generator is the linear operator Ax=lim_{t↓0}(T_tx−x)/t, defined on the subspace D(A) of those x∈X for which this norm limit exists.

title: Resolvent set and resolvent of a closed operator
description: For a closed linear operator A:D(A)⊆X→X on a Banach space X, the resolvent set ρ(A) consists of the scalars λ for which λI−A:D(A)→X is bijective; its inverse, the resolvent R(λ,A)=(λI−A)^{-1}, is then a bounded operator on X.

title: Exponential of a bounded operator
description: For a bounded linear operator B on a Banach space, e^{tB}=∑_{k≥0}t^kB^k/k! converges in operator norm for every real t and gives a norm-continuous one-parameter group of bounded operators with e^{(s+t)B}=e^{sB}e^{tB}.

title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for Banach-valued C¹ functions
description: If f:[a,b]→X is continuously differentiable into a Banach space X, then f(b)−f(a)=∫_a^b f′(t)dt as a Banach-valued Riemann integral.

title: Hitting times of open sets are stopping times for the right-continuous filtration
description: If X is an adapted process with left- or right-continuous paths in a metric space and G is open, then τ_G=inf{t≥0:X_t∈G} is a stopping time for the filtration (F_{t+}); if (F_t) is right-continuous it is an (F_t)-stopping time.

title: Right-continuous submartingales remain submartingales for F_{t+}
description: A submartingale with right-continuous paths with respect to a filtration (F_t) is also a submartingale with respect to the right-continuous filtration F_{t+}=∩_{u>t}F_u.

title: Optional stopping for a right-continuous submartingale at truncated stopping times
description: If M is a submartingale with right-continuous paths and σ,τ are stopping times, then for every finite T the variable M_{τ∧T} is integrable and E[M_{τ∧T}|F_σ]≥M_{σ∧τ∧T} almost surely.

title: L¹ convergence of partition sums to the quadratic variation of a square-integrable martingale
description: For a real càdlàg square-integrable martingale M and t≥0, the sums ∑_i(M_(t_(i+1))−M_(t_i))² over partitions of [0,t] whose mesh tends to0 converge in L¹ to the quadratic variation [M]_t.

title: Vitali convergence theorem for random variables
description: If real random variables X_n converge to X in probability, then X_n→X in L¹ if and only if the family (X_n) is uniformly integrable; in particular, almost sure convergence plus uniform integrability gives convergence of expectations.

title: Almost surely convergent subsequence of a sequence converging in probability
description: If random variables X_n converge to X in probability, in particular if they converge in L¹, then some subsequence X_(n_k) converges to X almost surely.

title: Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations
description: If X_n→X almost surely and |X_n|≤Y for an integrable Y, then E[X_n|G]→E[X|G] almost surely for every sub-σ-algebra G.

title: Progressive measurability of adapted right- or left-continuous processes
description: An adapted process indexed by [0,∞) with values in a metric space whose paths are all right-continuous, or all left-continuous, is progressively measurable.

title: Measurability of a progressive process at a stopping time
description: If X is progressively measurable and τ is a stopping time, then the value X_τ on the event {τ<∞} is F_τ-measurable there.

title: Outer probability of a subset
description: For a probability space (Ω,F,P) and any A⊆Ω, the outer probability is P*(A)=inf{P(B): B∈F, A⊆B}; it agrees with P on F and is attained by some measurable cover B⊇A.

title: Monotone class theorem for an algebra of sets
description: If an algebra of subsets of a set is contained in a monotone class, a family closed under increasing countable unions and decreasing countable intersections, then the σ-algebra generated by the algebra is contained in that monotone class.

title: Predictable-graph criterion for predictable stopping times
description: On a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, a stopping time T is predictable if and only if its graph {(t,ω): t=T(ω)<∞} is a predictable subset of [0,∞)×Ω.

title: Compensator of an adapted process of integrable variation
description: For a real adapted càdlàg process K with K₀=0 and integrable total variation on a usual filtration, its compensator, or dual predictable projection, is the unique predictable càdlàg process K^p with K^p₀=0 and integrable total variation such that K−K^p is a martingale; E Var(K^p)_∞≤E Var(K)_∞.

title: Totally inaccessible stopping time
description: A stopping time T is totally inaccessible if P(T=S<∞)=0 for every predictable stopping time S: no predictable time can charge its graph.

title: σ-algebra strictly before a stopping time
description: For a stopping time T of a filtration (F_t), F_(T−) is the σ-algebra generated by F₀ and the events A∩{t<T} with t≥0 and A∈F_t: the information available strictly before T.

title: Measurability of a predictable process at a stopping time
description: If H is a predictable process and T is a stopping time, then H_T1_(T<∞) is F_(T−)-measurable.

title: Predictable càdlàg processes do not jump at totally inaccessible times
description: If A is a predictable càdlàg process on a usual filtration and T is a totally inaccessible stopping time, then ΔA_T=0 almost surely on {T<∞}.

title: Zero conditional mean of a martingale jump at a predictable time
description: If M is a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale on a usual filtration and T is a predictable stopping time, then E[ΔM_T1_(T<∞)|F_(T−)]=0 almost surely.

title: Accessible and totally inaccessible parts of a stopping time
description: For every stopping time T on a usual filtration there is A∈F_T such that T_A (equal to T on A, ∞ off A) is accessible, its graph lying up to an evanescent set in a countable union of graphs of predictable stopping times, while T_(A^c) is totally inaccessible.

title: Weighted Bergman space of the unit disk
description: For a nonnegative measurable weight ω on the unit disk 𝔻, A²(ω) is the space of holomorphic f on 𝔻 with ∫_𝔻|f|²ω dA<∞, carrying the inner product of L²(ω dA); dA is area measure, often normalized to total mass 1.

title: Fatou's characterization of finite Blaschke products
description: A holomorphic function f on the unit disk with |f(z)|→1 as |z|→1 is a finite Blaschke product. In particular, a disk-algebra function that is unimodular on the unit circle is a finite Blaschke product.

title: Valence of a finite Blaschke product
description: A finite Blaschke product of degree n≥1 takes every value w of the extended complex plane exactly n times counting multiplicity; the solutions lie in the open disk, on the unit circle, or outside the closed disk according as w does.

title: Orthonormal-basis expansion of a reproducing kernel
description: If (e_s) is an orthonormal basis of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space on a set X with kernel K, then K(x,y)=∑_s e_s(x)·conj(e_s(y)) for all x,y∈X, the sum converging pointwise.

title: Expectation of a product of independent random variables
description: If X and Y are independent integrable real random variables, then XY is integrable and E[XY]=E[X]E[Y]. By induction the same holds for finitely many independent integrable variables.

title: Fermat’s interior extremum theorem
description: If f:(a,b)→ℝ has a relative maximum or relative minimum at an interior point c∈(a,b) and f is differentiable at c, then f′(c)=0.

title: Funk–Hecke formula
description: Let d≥3, φ a bounded measurable function on [−1,1] and H a spherical harmonic of degree n on S^{d−1}. Then ∫φ(u·v)H(v)dσ(v)=λ_n(φ)H(u) for every u∈S^{d−1}, where σ is spherical area and λ_n(φ)=|S^{d−2}|∫_{−1}^{1}φ(t)P_n(t)(1−t²)^{(d−3)/2}dt with P_n=C_n^{(d−2)/2}/C_n^{(d−2)/2}(1).

title: Rodrigues formula for Gegenbauer polynomials
description: For λ>0 and n≥0, C_n^λ(x)=(−1)ⁿ(2λ)_n/(2ⁿn!(λ+1/2)_n)·(1−x²)^{1/2−λ}dⁿ/dxⁿ(1−x²)^{n+λ−1/2} on (−1,1), where (a)_n is the rising factorial.

title: Matrix coefficient of a unitary representation
description: For a unitary representation π of a topological group G on a Hilbert space H and vectors v,w∈H, the continuous function g↦⟨π(g)v,w⟩ on G. For finite-dimensional π with an orthonormal basis (e_i), the matrix entries π_ij(g)=⟨π(g)e_j,e_i⟩ span the space of matrix coefficients of π.

title: Hessian matrix of a C² function on Euclidean space
description: For a C² real function f on an open subset of ℝⁿ, the n×n matrix ∇²f(x)=(∂_i∂_jf(x)) of second partial derivatives at x; it is the Jacobian matrix of the gradient ∇f and defines the quadratic form v↦vᵀ∇²f(x)v.

title: Spherical Hessian of a function on the Euclidean unit sphere
description: For a C² function f on S^{n−1}⊂ℝⁿ (the restriction of a C² function on a neighbourhood) and u∈S^{n−1}, ∇²_Sf(u) is the symmetric bilinear form on the tangent space u⊥ whose quadratic form sends a unit vector v⊥u to (f∘γ_v)″(0), where γ_v(t)=u cos t+v sin t is the great circle through u in direction v, extended to all v⊥u by quadratic homogeneity.

title: Characteristic function of a random vector in ℝᵈ
description: For a Borel probability measure μ on ℝᵈ, φ_μ(u)=∫exp(iu·x)μ(dx) for u∈ℝᵈ, where u·x is the dot product. For a random vector X in ℝᵈ, φ_X(u)=Eexp(iu·X) is the characteristic function of its law.

title: Fréchet space
description: A real or complex locally convex topological vector space whose topology is induced by a translation-invariant metric for which it is complete; equivalently, a complete locally convex space whose topology is generated by a countable separating family of seminorms.

title: Continuous representation of a topological group on a topological vector space
description: A group homomorphism π from a topological group G to the invertible continuous linear maps of a real or complex topological vector space V such that the action map G×V→V, (g,v)↦π(g)v, is continuous.

title: Smooth vector of a Lie group representation
description: For a continuous representation π of a real Lie group G on a locally convex space V and X in the Lie algebra of G, set dπ(X)v=lim_{t→0}(π(exp tX)v−v)/t when the limit exists.
