An abstract operator space is a vector space with matrix norms that admits a linear complete isometry onto such a subspace.

title: Completely bounded map between operator spaces
description: A linear map u:X→Y between operator spaces is completely bounded if its amplifications u_n:M_n(X)→M_n(Y), [x_ij]↦[u(x_ij)], satisfy ‖u‖_cb=sup_n‖u_n‖<∞. It is completely contractive if every u_n is a contraction (‖u‖_cb≤1) and completely isometric if every u_n is an isometry.

title: Matrix C*-algebra M_n(A) over a C*-algebra
description: For a C*-algebra A and n≥1, M_n(A) is the *-algebra of n×n matrices over A with matrix multiplication and involution [a_ij]*=[a_ji*]. It has a unique C*-norm, computed by viewing M_n(A)⊆B(Hⁿ) for any faithful star representation A⊆B(H); these matrix norms make every C*-algebra an operator space.

title: Gelfand–Naimark representation theorem for C*-algebras
description: Every C*-algebra A admits a faithful star representation π:A→B(H) on a complex Hilbert space; π is then isometric, so A is isometrically star-isomorphic to a norm-closed star subalgebra of B(H).

title: Commutative Gelfand–Naimark theorem (nonunital)
description: For a commutative C*-algebra A, its character space Â with the weak-star topology is locally compact Hausdorff, and the Gelfand transform Γ(a)(χ)=χ(a) is an isometric star isomorphism of A onto C₀(Â), the complex continuous functions on Â vanishing at infinity. For unital A this is C(Â) with Â compact.

title: C*-subalgebra
description: A C*-subalgebra of a C*-algebra A is a complex linear subspace B⊆A closed under multiplication and the involution and closed in the norm topology; with the restricted operations and norm it is itself a C*-algebra.

title: Exactness passes to C*-subalgebras
description: Every C*-subalgebra of an exact C*-algebra is exact.

title: Commutative C*-algebras are exact
description: Every commutative C*-algebra is exact: tensoring with it preserves short exact sequences of C*-algebras for the minimal C*-tensor product.

title: Metrizable topological space
description: A topological space whose topology is the metric topology of some metric on its underlying set.

title: Compact Hausdorff spaces are normal
description: Every compact Hausdorff space is normal: any two disjoint closed subsets have disjoint open neighbourhoods.

title: Stinespring dilation theorem
description: For a unital C*-algebra A and a completely positive map φ:A→B(H), there are a Hilbert space K, a star representation π:A→B(K) and a bounded V:H→K with φ(a)=V*π(a)V for all a∈A; moreover ‖φ‖=‖φ‖_cb=‖V‖²=‖φ(1)‖.

title: Haagerup–Paulsen–Wittstock factorization of completely bounded maps
description: For a C*-algebra A and a completely bounded map φ:A→B(H), there are a star representation π:A→B(K) and bounded operators V₁,V₂:H→K with φ(a)=V₁*π(a)V₂ for all a∈A and ‖V₁‖‖V₂‖=‖φ‖_cb.

title: Wittstock extension theorem
description: If X⊆Y are operator spaces and φ:X→B(H) is completely bounded, then φ extends to a completely bounded map Y→B(H) with the same cb norm. In particular B(H), and each matrix algebra M_n(ℂ), is injective for completely contractive maps.

title: Exactness passes to the unitization
description: If A is an exact nonunital C*-algebra, its minimal unitization Ã is exact.

title: Reduced crossed product of a C*-dynamical system
description: For a C*-dynamical system (A,G,α) with G locally compact and A⊆B(H) faithfully represented, let (π̃(a)ξ)(t)=α_(t⁻¹)(a)ξ(t) and (λ_sξ)(t)=ξ(s⁻¹t) on L²(G,H). The reduced crossed product is the norm closure of the operators ∫f(s)π̃(a)λ_s ds with a∈A, f∈C_c(G); it does not depend on the faithful representation, and λ_sπ̃(a)λ_s*=π̃(α_s(a)) implements α by unitaries.

title: Upward directedness of the positive open unit ball of a C*-algebra
description: In a C*-algebra A, the positive elements of norm strictly less than one form an upward directed set: for any two such a,b there is such a c with a≤c and b≤c. This yields the canonical positive contractive approximate identity.

title: Witt decomposition of a quadratic space
description: Every nondegenerate quadratic space V over a field of characteristic different from two decomposes as V≅H^m⊥V₀, with H the hyperbolic plane and V₀ anisotropic. The Witt index m, the dimension of a maximal totally isotropic subspace, and the isometry class of V₀ are uniquely determined by V; uniqueness follows from Witt cancellation.

title: Splitting off a modular sublattice of maximal scale
description: Let L be a nondegenerate quadratic ℤ_p-lattice and K⊆L an (a)-modular sublattice, meaning aK#=K. If the scale ideal s(L) equals (a), then K is an orthogonal summand of L: L=K⊥(L∩W), where W is the orthogonal complement of ℚ_pK in ℚ_pL.

title: Galois group and Frobenius elements of a cyclotomic field
description: For n≥1 and a primitive nth root of unity ζ_n, ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ is Galois and a↦σ_a with σ_a(ζ_n)=ζ_n^a is an isomorphism (ℤ/nℤ)×≅Gal(ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ). Every prime ℓ∤n is unramified in ℚ(ζ_n) with Frobenius σ_ℓ; hence ℓ splits completely in the fixed field of a subgroup H exactly when ℓ mod n lies in H.

title: q-power Frobenius endomorphism of an elliptic curve over 𝔽_q
description: For an elliptic curve E over 𝔽_q given by a Weierstrass equation, φ_q(x,y)=(x^q,y^q), fixing O, is an endomorphism of E defined over 𝔽_q. It is purely inseparable of degree q, and its fixed points in E(𝔽̄_q) are exactly the points of E(𝔽_q).

title: Kernel order of a separable elliptic isogeny
description: Let φ:E₁→E₂ be a nonconstant isogeny of elliptic curves over a field K, of degree [K̄(E₁):φ*K̄(E₂)]. Each fibre of φ on K̄-points has as many points as the separable degree of φ. In particular, if φ is separable then it is unramified and #ker φ=deg φ.

title: Separability of m+nφ for the Frobenius endomorphism
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over 𝔽_q, where q is a power of the prime p, with q-power Frobenius endomorphism φ, and let m,n∈ℤ. The endomorphism m+nφ of E is separable if and only if p∤m. In particular 1−φ is separable.

title: Degree as a positive definite quadratic form on elliptic homomorphisms
description: For elliptic curves E₁,E₂ over a field, set deg 0=0. Then deg:Hom(E₁,E₂)→ℤ is a positive definite quadratic form: deg(nφ)=n²deg φ, deg φ>0 for φ≠0, and (φ,ψ)↦deg(φ+ψ)−deg φ−deg ψ is ℤ-bilinear. Bilinearity comes from the dual isogeny, with φ̂φ=[deg φ].

title: Shimura covering of X₀(N) at prime level
description: Let N≥5 be prime and n the numerator of (N−1)/12. Over ℤ[1/N], X₁(N)→X₀(N) is a Galois cover with cyclic group (ℤ/Nℤ)×/{±1}, and its unique intermediate cover X₂(N)→X₀(N) that is cyclic of degree n is finite étale. Mazur calls it the Shimura covering.

title: Level-one fundamental character of tame inertia
description: Let L be a finite extension of ℚ_p with uniformizer π and inertia group I. The level-one fundamental character θ:I→𝔽_p× sends σ to the residue of σ(ϖ)/ϖ for a (p−1)st root ϖ of π; it factors through tame inertia and does not depend on the choices. If e is the absolute ramification index of L, the mod-p cyclotomic character restricted to I equals θ^e.

title: Raynaud’s bound on inertia exponents of order-p group schemes
description: Let L be a finite extension of ℚ_p with absolute ramification index e and level-one fundamental character θ. If G is a finite flat group scheme of order p over the ring of integers of L, inertia acts on G(L̄)≅𝔽_p through θ^a for an integer a whose residue ⟨a⟩ in [0,p−1) satisfies 0≤⟨a⟩≤e.

title: Tangent space of a smooth manifold
description: For a point x of a smooth manifold M, T_xM is the real vector space of derivations at x: linear maps v:C^∞(M)→ℝ with v(fg)=v(f)g(x)+f(x)v(g). In a chart with coordinates x¹,…,xⁿ the partial derivatives ∂/∂x^i at x form a basis. A smooth map F induces dF_x:T_xM→T_(F(x))N, v↦(f↦v(f∘F)); a smooth path γ has velocity γ′(t)=dγ_t(d/dt).

title: Differential one-form on a smooth manifold
description: A smooth one-form ω on a smooth manifold M assigns to each x a linear functional ω_x on T_xM, written ∑f_i dx^i with smooth f_i in each chart. A smooth function h has differential dh with dh_x(v)=v(h). The pullback along a smooth map F is (F*ω)_y(v)=ω_(F(y))(dF_y v). ω is closed if ∂f_i/∂x^j=∂f_j/∂x^i in every chart; every dh is closed.

title: Singular homology of a topological space
description: For a topological space X, the singular n-chains C_n(X) form the free abelian group on continuous maps σ:Δⁿ→X from the standard n-simplex. The boundary ∂σ=∑_(i=0)^n(−1)^iσ∘δ_i, with δ_i the ith face inclusion, satisfies ∂∘∂=0, and H_n(X;ℤ)=ker∂_n/im∂_(n+1). Elements of ker∂_n are integral n-cycles; a closed path is an integral one-cycle.

title: Dirichlet density of prime ideals in classes modulo a congruence subgroup
description: Let K be a number field, 𝔪 a modulus, I^𝔪 the group of fractional ideals prime to 𝔪 and H a congruence subgroup with i(K_(𝔪,1))⊆H⊆I^𝔪. For every class k∈I^𝔪/H, the prime ideals of K lying in k have Dirichlet density 1/(I^𝔪:H). For H=i(K_(𝔪,1)) the prime ideals are equidistributed among the ray classes modulo 𝔪.

title: Polar density of a set of prime ideals
description: For a set T of nonzero prime ideals of a number field K put ζ_(K,T)(s)=∏_(𝔭∈T)(1−N𝔭^(−s))^(−1) for Re(s)>1. T has polar density m/n if ζ_(K,T)(s)^n extends to a meromorphic function near s=1 with a pole of order m there. A set with polar density δ also has Dirichlet density δ.

title: Dense affine representation of a simple noncyclic dimension group
description: If (G,u) is a simple dimension group not isomorphic to ℤ, the image of its affine representation g↦ĝ is norm dense in Aff S(G,u), and G⁺ consists of 0 and the g with ĝ strictly positive. Conversely, a torsion-free abelian group with a dense-range homomorphism φ into Aff K, K a Choquet simplex, is a simple dimension group for the positive cone {0}∪{g:φ(g)≫0}.

title: Choquet simplex of normalized traces of a dimension group
description: For a dimension group G with order unit u, the normalized trace space S(G,u) is a Choquet simplex. If G has exactly n pure (extreme) normalized traces, S(G,u) is an (n−1)-simplex and Aff S(G,u) is isomorphic to ℝⁿ with the coordinatewise order, the pure traces becoming the coordinate projections.

title: Structure of closed subgroups of a finite-dimensional real vector space
description: Every closed subgroup J of a finite-dimensional real vector space V is the direct sum of the largest real vector subspace contained in J and a discrete subgroup. Equivalently, in a suitable basis e₁,…,e_n of V, J=ℝe₁⊕⋯⊕ℝe_a⊕ℤe_(a+1)⊕⋯⊕ℤe_(a+b) with a+b≤n.

title: Van der Corput’s lattice-point theorem for symmetric convex sets
description: Let Λ be a full lattice in ℝⁿ and C a convex set symmetric about the origin. If vol(C)>k·2ⁿ·covol(Λ) for a positive integer k, then C contains at least k pairs ±x of nonzero points of Λ. In particular a symmetric convex set of infinite volume contains infinitely many lattice points. For k=1 this is Minkowski’s convex body theorem.

title: Euler’s q-exponential identities
description: For |q|<1, with (a;q)_n=∏_(0≤j<n)(1−aqʲ), one has (−z;q)_∞=∑_(n≥0)q^(n(n−1)/2)zⁿ/(q;q)_n for every complex z, and 1/(z;q)_∞=∑_(n≥0)zⁿ/(q;q)_n for |z|<1.

title: Symplectic vector space
description: A symplectic vector space (V,ω) over a field F is a vector space V with a bilinear form ω:V×V→F that is alternating, ω(v,v)=0 for every v (so ω(u,v)=−ω(v,u)), and nondegenerate.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: First-order sentence in the language of rings
description: A first-order formula in the language of rings is built from variables, the constants 0 and 1, the operations +, − and ·, equality, the connectives ¬, ∧, ∨ and quantifiers ∀, ∃ over elements; a sentence is a formula without free variables. Interpreting the symbols in a ring R makes each sentence true or false in R.

title: Real form of a complex vector space
description: A real form of a complex vector space V is a real vector subspace W⊆V with V=W⊕iW as real vector spaces; equivalently the complex-linear map C⊗_R W→V, z⊗w↦zw, is an isomorphism. Then V is the complexification of W.
field: Linear algebra and additive number theory

title: Finitely generated field extension
description: A field extension L/K is finitely generated if L=K(a₁,…,aₙ) for finitely many elements aᵢ∈L, that is, L is the smallest subfield of L containing K and all the aᵢ.

title: Cartan’s closed subgroup theorem
description: Every closed subgroup H of a real Lie group G, with its subspace topology, carries a unique smooth manifold structure making it a real Lie group embedded in G as a submanifold; its Lie algebra is identified with {X∈Lie(G): exp(tX)∈H for every real t}.

title: Conjugacy of Borel subgroups
description: In a smooth connected affine algebraic group G over an algebraically closed field k, any two Borel subgroups are conjugate by an element of G(k), and G/B is a complete variety for every Borel subgroup B.

title: Borel subgroups cover a connected algebraic group
description: For a smooth connected affine algebraic group G over an algebraically closed field k and a Borel subgroup B, every element of G(k) lies in some conjugate gBg⁻¹; that is, G(k) is the union of the groups of points of its Borel subgroups.

title: Torus decomposition of a connected solvable algebraic group
description: Let G be a smooth connected solvable affine algebraic group over an algebraically closed field k and T a maximal torus of G. Then G is the semidirect product G_u⋊T of its unipotent part and T, and every diagonalizable algebraic subgroup of G is conjugate by an element of G_u(k) to a subgroup of T.

title: Diagonalizable affine algebraic group
description: An affine algebraic group over a field k is diagonalizable if it is isomorphic to a closed subgroup of the group of invertible diagonal n×n matrices for some n; equivalently its coordinate algebra is spanned by its characters.

title: A connected group variety without tori is unipotent
description: A smooth connected affine algebraic group over a field that contains no nontrivial algebraic torus is unipotent.

title: Unipotence is invariant under base field extension
description: For an affine algebraic group G over a field k and an extension field k′/k, G is unipotent if and only if its base change G_(k′) is unipotent.

title: Density of separable points on a geometrically reduced scheme
description: On a geometrically reduced algebraic scheme X over a field k, the closed points with residue field separable over k are dense; in particular a nonempty such X, for instance a nonempty smooth k-scheme, has a point over some finite separable extension of k.

title: Tangent-space criterion for smoothness of an algebraic group
description: For an algebraic group G over a field, the Zariski tangent space at the identity satisfies dim Tgt_e(G)≥dim G, with equality if and only if G is smooth.

title: Geometrically reduced algebraic groups are smooth
description: An algebraic group over a field is smooth if and only if it is geometrically reduced; in particular a reduced algebraic group over an algebraically closed (or perfect) field is smooth.

title: Vaught’s test for completeness of a first-order theory
description: If a first-order theory T in a language L has no finite models and is κ-categorical for some infinite cardinal κ≥|L|, meaning any two models of cardinality κ are isomorphic, then T is complete: every sentence or its negation is a consequence of T.

title: Steinitz classification of algebraically closed fields
description: Two algebraically closed fields are isomorphic if and only if they have the same characteristic and the same transcendence degree over their prime field.

title: Quotient of an algebraic group by a normal subgroup over an arbitrary field
description: For a normal algebraic subgroup N of an algebraic group G over any field k, the quotient G/N is an algebraic group with a faithfully flat homomorphism G→G/N whose kernel is N, universal among homomorphisms from G whose kernel contains N.

title: Simple Lie algebra
description: A Lie algebra 𝔤 is simple if it is not abelian (some bracket [x,y] is nonzero) and its only ideals are 0 and 𝔤.

title: Cartan matrix of a root system
description: For a reduced finite crystallographic root system with an ordered simple system α₁,…,α_r, the Cartan matrix is the r×r integer matrix a_ij=⟨α_i∨,α_j⟩=2(α_i,α_j)/(α_i,α_i). It has a_ii=2 and a_ij≤0 for i≠j, d_i·a_ij is symmetric for d_i=(α_i,α_i)/2, and it determines the root system up to isomorphism. For G₂ it is (2 −3; −1 2) in this ordering; some authors use the transpose.

title: Free Lie algebra on a set
description: For a set X and a field k, the free Lie algebra FL(X) is a Lie algebra with a map X→FL(X) such that every map from X to a Lie algebra 𝔤 extends uniquely to a Lie algebra homomorphism FL(X)→𝔤; it is spanned by iterated brackets of elements of X. The Lie algebra presented by generators X and relations R is the quotient of FL(X) by the ideal generated by R.

title: Serre presentation of a semisimple Lie algebra from its Cartan matrix
description: For the Cartan matrix (a_ij) of a reduced root system R of rank r, 𝔤(R) is the complex Lie algebra generated by e_i,f_i,h_i (1≤i≤r) with relations [h_i,h_j]=0, [h_i,e_j]=a_ij e_j, [h_i,f_j]=−a_ij f_j, [e_i,f_j]=δ_ij h_i and the Serre relations (ad e_i)^(1−a_ij)e_j=0=(ad f_i)^(1−a_ij)f_j for i≠j, where (ad x)(y)=[x,y]. By Serre’s theorem 𝔤(R) is finite-dimensional with root system R, and it is simple when R is irreducible.

title: Free associative algebra on a set
description: For a set X and a field k, the free algebra k⟨X⟩ has the finite words in X as a basis, with concatenation as multiplication and the empty word as identity; every map from X to a unital associative k-algebra extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism. The algebra presented by generators X and relations R is k⟨X⟩ modulo the two-sided ideal generated by R, the smallest subspace containing R and closed under multiplication on both sides.

title: Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group U_q(𝔤)
description: For the Cartan matrix (a_ij) of a reduced root system, with d_i=(α_i,α_i)/2 and q_i=q^(d_i), U_q(𝔤) is the associative algebra over the rational-function field ℚ(q) (or ℂ(q)) generated by E_i,F_i,K_i^(±1) with K_iK_j=K_jK_i, K_iK_i^(−1)=1, K_iE_jK_i^(−1)=q_i^(a_ij)E_j, K_iF_jK_i^(−1)=q_i^(−a_ij)F_j, E_iF_j−F_jE_i=δ_ij(K_i−K_i^(−1))/(q_i−q_i^(−1)), and the quantum Serre relations ∑_(r=0)^(1−a_ij)(−1)^r[1−a_ij choose r]_(q_i)E_i^(1−a_ij−r)E_jE_i^r=0 and likewise for F, for i≠j, with Gaussian binomials built from quantum integers. It is a Hopf algebra with Δ(K_i)=K_i⊗K_i, Δ(E_i)=E_i⊗K_i+1⊗E_i, Δ(F_i)=F_i⊗1+K_i^(−1)⊗F_i. It deforms the universal enveloping algebra of the corresponding semisimple Lie algebra; normalizations of q and of the coproduct vary between authors.

title: Representation of a Lie algebra
description: A representation of a Lie algebra 𝔤 over k on a vector space V is a Lie algebra homomorphism 𝔤→𝔤𝔩(V), where 𝔤𝔩(V) is the space of linear endomorphisms of V with bracket [A,B]=AB−BA. Equivalently V is a module over the universal enveloping algebra U(𝔤).

title: Simple module over an associative algebra
description: A module V over an associative algebra A is simple, or irreducible, if V≠0 and its only A-invariant subspaces are 0 and V.

title: Type-1 highest-weight module of a Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group
description: A U_q(𝔤)-module M is of type 1 if it is the direct sum of its weight spaces M_λ={m: K_i m=q_i^(⟨λ,α_i∨⟩)m for all i} over integral weights λ, the integer combinations of fundamental weights. A highest-weight vector is a nonzero weight vector annihilated by every E_i, and a highest-weight module is generated by one. For generic q and each dominant integral λ there is a unique finite-dimensional simple type-1 module L(λ) of highest weight λ, and these exhaust the finite-dimensional simple type-1 modules.

title: Laurent polynomial ring
description: For a commutative ring R, R[q,q^(−1)] consists of finite sums ∑_(n∈ℤ) a_n qⁿ with a_n∈R, added coefficientwise and multiplied using qᵐqⁿ=q^(m+n); it is the polynomial ring R[q] with q made invertible.

title: Lusztig’s divided-power integral form of a quantum group
description: For the Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group U_q(𝔤) over ℚ(q) and A=ℤ[q,q^(−1)], U_A^res is the A-subalgebra generated by K_i^(±1) and the divided powers E_i^((r))=E_i^r/[r]_(q_i)! and F_i^((r))=F_i^r/[r]_(q_i)! for r≥1. It is a Hopf algebra over A, free as an A-module, with U_A^res⊗_Aℚ(q)=U_q(𝔤). Base change along A→k, q↦ζ, for a field k and typically a root of unity ζ, gives the restricted quantum group U_ζ^res=U_A^res⊗_A k.

title: Weyl module of a quantum group
description: For a dominant integral weight λ, let v be a highest-weight vector of the simple type-1 U_q(𝔤)-module L(λ) over ℚ(q). The A-form W_A^λ=U_A^res·v is a U_A^res-module, free of finite rank over A=ℤ[q,q^(−1)], and for a specialization q↦ζ in a field k the Weyl module is W_ζ^λ=W_A^λ⊗_A k; at roots of unity it need not be simple. The dual Weyl module is the linear dual (W^λ)*, made a left module through the antipode.

title: Compact surface with boundary
description: A compact Hausdorff space in which every point has an open neighbourhood homeomorphic to an open subset of the closed half-plane {(x,y)∈ℝ²: y≥0}; points sent to the line y=0 form the boundary. Examples are the closed disc, the annulus and closed surfaces, whose boundary is empty.

title: Euler characteristic of a finite triangulated space
description: For a finite simplicial complex K, χ(K)=∑_n(−1)ⁿs_n, where s_n is the number of n-simplices; in dimension two this is vertices − edges + triangles. A space homeomorphic to the geometric realization of K has Euler characteristic χ(K), independent of the chosen triangulation because it equals the alternating sum of the ranks of homology. For example, a closed disc has χ=1.

title: Kuperberg’s G₂ equinumeration theorem
description: For every sequence of G₂ clasps, the clasped G₂ web space and the space of U_q(𝔤₂)-invariants in the tensor product of the corresponding irreducible representations have the same dimension. In particular the number of non-elliptic G₂ webs with n boundary points equals dim Inv(V⊗n) for the seven-dimensional module V.

title: Spanning of G₂ invariant tensors by webs
description: For the seven-dimensional U_q(𝔤₂)-module V, Kuperberg’s evaluation of G₂ webs, which places a fixed nonzero invariant of V⊗3 at each trivalent vertex and the invariant symmetric form along edges, sends the G₂ webs with n boundary points to a spanning set of the invariant space Inv(V⊗n) for every n. Surjectivity holds at q=1, for the classical 𝔤₂-module, and hence for generic q.

title: Kuperberg’s quantum G₂ link invariant
description: Kuperberg’s recursive rules for loops, monogons, small faces and crossings define a regular-isotopy invariant ⟨·⟩_G₂ of links and tangled trivalent graphs. It coincides with the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant of U_q(𝔤₂) with edges coloured by the seven-dimensional module and vertices by an invariant trilinear form, so the G₂ spider relations and crossing formula hold for the corresponding intertwiners.

title: Radon measure on a locally compact Hausdorff space
description: A Borel measure on a locally compact Hausdorff space that is finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets (each has measure equal to the infimum over open supersets) and inner regular on open sets (each has measure equal to the supremum over compact subsets). This is the Folland–Cohn convention; on σ-compact spaces it coincides with compact inner regularity on all Borel sets.

title: Compact-inner-regular Radon measure on a Hausdorff space
description: A Borel measure on a Hausdorff topological space that is finite on compact sets and inner regular: the measure of every Borel set is the supremum of the measures of its compact subsets.

title: Disjoint compact sets in a Hausdorff space have disjoint neighbourhoods
description: In a Hausdorff topological space, any two disjoint compact subsets K and L are contained in disjoint open sets U⊇K and V⊇L.

title: Approximation of finite-measure Lebesgue sets by elementary sets
description: For every Lebesgue measurable E⊆ℝⁿ of finite measure and every ε>0 there is an elementary set A, a finite union of boxes, with m(E△A)≤ε (Littlewood’s first principle).

title: Nonwandering set of a continuous map
description: For a continuous self-map f of a topological space X, a point x is nonwandering if every neighbourhood U of x meets fⁿ(U) for some n≥1. The nonwandering set Ω(f) is the closed forward-invariant set of nonwandering points.

title: Nonflat critical point of an interval map
description: A critical point c (f′(c)=0) of a C^r interval map f, r≥2, is nonflat if near c one can write f(x)=f(c)±|φ(x)|^α for some real α>1 and some C^r map φ with C^r inverse defined near c and φ(c)=0.

title: Finite-rank approximation of compact Hilbert-space operators
description: A bounded operator between Hilbert spaces is compact exactly when it is an operator-norm limit of finite-rank operators.

title: Orthonormal-family criterion for trace-class operators
description: A bounded operator T on a separable complex Hilbert space is trace class exactly when sup∑_j|⟨Tg_j,h_j⟩| is finite, the supremum over pairs of finite orthonormal families of equal length; this supremum equals the trace norm ‖T‖₁. In particular |tr T|≤‖T‖₁.

title: Ideal property of trace-class operators
description: If T:H→K is a trace-class operator between Hilbert spaces and S:K→L, U:G→H are bounded operators, then STU:G→L is trace class and ‖STU‖₁≤‖S‖‖T‖₁‖U‖.

title: Operator representation of a bounded sesquilinear form
description: If a is a sesquilinear (in the real case bilinear) form on a Hilbert space H with |a(x,y)|≤C‖x‖‖y‖, there is a unique bounded operator A on H with a(x,y)=⟨Ax,y⟩ for all x,y, and ‖A‖≤C.

title: Zonal harmonic with a given pole
description: For η on the unit sphere S⊂ℝⁿ and m≥0, the zonal harmonic Z_m(·,η) is the unique degree-m spherical harmonic with p(η)=∫_S p(ζ)Z_m(ζ,η)dσ(ζ) for every degree-m spherical harmonic p, σ being normalized surface measure.

title: Zonal-harmonic expansion of the Poisson kernel of the ball
description: For n≥2, x in the open unit ball B⊂ℝⁿ and ζ in its boundary sphere, the Poisson kernel P(x,ζ)=(1−|x|²)/|x−ζ|ⁿ equals ∑_{m≥0}Z_m(x,ζ), with Z_m extended to x∈ℝⁿ as homogeneous harmonic polynomials; the series converges absolutely and uniformly on K×S for compact K⊂B.

title: Lebesgue number lemma
description: For every open cover of a compact metric space there is δ>0, a Lebesgue number of the cover, such that every subset of diameter less than δ lies in one member of the cover.

title: Triebel–Lizorkin-type sequence space with variable exponents and cube weight
description: For bounded positive exponents p,q with globally log-Hölder reciprocals, bounded locally log-Hölder s, and a doubling, locally comparable cube weight φ, f^{s(·),φ}_{p(·),q(·)} consists of complex sequences t=(t_Q) indexed by dyadic cubes of side at most 1 with finite sup_P φ(P)⁻¹∥(∑_{Q⊂P}(|Q|^{−s(·)/n−1/2}|t_Q|χ_Q)^{q(·)})^{1/q(·)}∥_{L^{p(·)}(P)}, the supremum over all dyadic cubes P; for q≡∞ the sum is replaced by a supremum.

title: Vybíral’s Sobolev embedding for variable-exponent Triebel–Lizorkin sequence spaces
description: Let s₁≤s₀ and 0<p₀≤p₁ be measurable with 0<p₀⁻≤p₁⁻≤p₁⁺<∞, s₀−n/p₀=s₁−n/p₁ pointwise, and s₀, 1/p₀ satisfying the log-Hölder condition for ∥x−y∥_∞≤1. For q≡∞ or 0<q⁻≤q<∞, f^{s₀(·)}_{p₀(·),q(·)} embeds continuously in f^{s₁(·)}_{p₁(·),q(·)}, where ∥γ∥=∥(∑_{j≥0,m∈ℤⁿ}(2^{js(·)}|γ_{jm}|χ_{Q_{jm}})^{q(·)})^{1/q(·)}∥_{L^{p(·)}} with Q_{jm} the cubes of side 2^{−j}. If inf(s₀−s₁)>0, then f^{s₀(·)}_{p₀(·),∞} embeds in f^{s₁(·)}_{p₁(·),q} for every constant 0<q≤∞.

title: Convolution estimate trading vanishing moments for smoothness at dyadic scales
description: Write η_{ν,m}(x)=2^{νn}(1+2^ν|x|)^{−m}. Let k≥0, m₀>n and m₁>n+k, and let g,h be locally integrable on ℝⁿ with D^γg∈L¹(ℝⁿ) for all |γ|≤k. If |D^γg|≤2^{νk}η_{ν,m₀} for |γ|=k, |h|≤η_{μ,m₁}, and h has vanishing moments of all orders below k, then |g*h|≤C2^{k(ν−μ)}η_{ν,m₀}*η_{μ,m₁−k}, with C independent of g,h,ν,μ. It gives the scale-decay of φ_j*m_Q for dyadic kernels φ_j and smooth molecules m_Q.

title: Generation of lower central terms by simple commutators of generators
description: If a group G is generated by a set A, then for every n≥1 the term γ_n(G) of its lower central series is generated by γ_(n+1)(G) together with the simple commutators [a₁,…,a_n]=[[a₁,…,a_(n−1)],a_n] with all a_i∈A.

title: Multilinearity of iterated commutators modulo the lower central series
description: Let γ_i be the lower central series of a group G and let g_k,h_k∈γ_(l_k)(G) for k=1,…,n. Modulo γ_(l₁+⋯+l_n+1)(G), the simple commutator [g₁,…,g_n] is multiplicative in each argument: replacing g_k by g_kh_k multiplies it by the commutator with h_k in place k. In particular [g₁^(m₁),…,g_n^(m_n)]≡[g₁,…,g_n]^(m₁⋯m_n) for positive integers m_k.

title: Upper central series of a group
description: For a group G, the upper central series 1=ζ₀(G)≤ζ₁(G)≤ζ₂(G)≤⋯ is defined by letting ζ_(i+1)(G)/ζ_i(G) be the centre of G/ζ_i(G); equivalently ζ_(i+1)(G)={x∈G:[x,y]∈ζ_i(G) for every y∈G}. Thus ζ₁(G) is the centre of G, and each ζ_i(G) is normal in G.

title: Nilpotency class via the upper and lower central series
description: For a group G and c≥0, the upper central series reaches G at step c, ζ_c(G)=G, exactly when the lower central series satisfies γ_(c+1)(G)=1. Hence a nilpotent group has class c precisely when ζ_c(G)=G with ζ_(c−1)(G)≠G, and no central series of G is shorter than c.

title: Infinite cyclic subnormal series characterizing isolated subgroups
description: A subgroup H of a finitely generated nilpotent group G is isolated, meaning x^m∈H with m≥1 implies x∈H, if and only if there is a chain H=H₀⊂H₁⊂⋯⊂H_t=G in which each H_(j−1) is normal in H_j and every quotient H_j/H_(j−1) is infinite cyclic.

title: Kirszbraun extension theorem for Euclidean spaces
description: Every L-Lipschitz map from a subset of ℝᵐ to ℝⁿ, both with Euclidean norms, extends to an L-Lipschitz map on all of ℝᵐ. Equivalently (Kirszbraun’s intersection property), if uᵢ∈ℝᵐ and vᵢ∈ℝⁿ (i≤k) satisfy ‖vᵢ−vⱼ‖≤‖uᵢ−uⱼ‖, then every x∈ℝᵐ has some y∈ℝⁿ with ‖y−vᵢ‖≤‖x−uᵢ‖ for all i.

title: Finite intersection property for closed bounded convex sets in a Hilbert space
description: If a nonempty family of closed bounded convex subsets of a Hilbert space has the finite intersection property, meaning every finite subfamily has nonempty intersection, then the whole family has nonempty intersection.

title: Contractivity of the Cauchy transform of boundary conjugates on a convex domain
description: Let Ω⊂ℂ be a bounded open convex set with smooth boundary and f continuous on the closure of Ω and holomorphic in Ω. Then g(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_∂Ω conj(f(σ))(σ−z)⁻¹dσ extends continuously to the closure of Ω, is holomorphic in Ω, satisfies sup|g|≤sup|f|, and maps ∂Ω into the convex hull of f(∂Ω).

title: C*-identity for bounded Hilbert-space operators
description: For every bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space, ‖T*‖=‖T‖ and ‖T*T‖=‖TT*‖=‖T‖² in the operator norm; thus the bounded operators form a C*-algebra.

title: Mergelyan’s approximation theorem
description: If K⊂ℂ is compact and ℂ∖K is connected, every continuous function on K that is holomorphic on the interior of K is a uniform limit on K of polynomials.

title: Number of upcrossings of an interval by a real sequence
description: For real a<b and real numbers x₀,…,x_n, the number U_n(a,b) of completed upcrossings of [a,b] is the largest k for which there are indices s₁<t₁<s₂<t₂<⋯<s_k<t_k≤n with x_(s_i)≤a and x_(t_i)≥b, and 0 if there is none.

title: Nonemptiness of the spectrum in a complex Banach algebra
description: Every element of a nonzero complex Banach algebra with identity has nonempty spectrum. The usual proof applies Liouville’s theorem to φ((a−λ1)⁻¹) for continuous linear functionals φ.

title: Norm criterion for positivity of a self-adjoint C*-algebra element
description: Let a be a self-adjoint element of a unital C*-algebra and t≥‖a‖. Then the spectrum of a lies in [0,∞) exactly when ‖t1−a‖≤t; if this inequality holds for one t≥‖a‖ it holds for all.

title: Increasing convex functions of a submartingale
description: If (X_n) is a discrete-time submartingale and φ:ℝ→ℝ is increasing and convex with φ(X_n) integrable for every n, then (φ(X_n)) is a submartingale for the same filtration; in particular ((X_n−a)⁺) is a submartingale for every real a.

title: Martingale transform of a submartingale by a bounded nonnegative predictable sequence
description: Let (X_n)_(n≥0) be a submartingale for (F_n) and (H_n)_(n≥1) bounded, nonnegative and predictable, that is H_n is F_(n−1)-measurable. Then (H·X)_n=∑_(m=1)^n H_m(X_m−X_(m−1)) is a submartingale; the same holds for supermartingales, and for martingales without the sign condition.

title: Compact metric spaces are separable
description: Every compact metric space has a countable dense subset: for each n finitely many open balls of radius 1/n cover it, and the centres of all these balls form a countable dense set.

title: Division with remainder for integers
description: For integers a and b with b>0 there are unique integers q and r with a=bq+r and 0≤r<b.

title: Determinant and trace of an elliptic endomorphism on the Tate module
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a field K and ℓ a prime different from char K. For every endomorphism ψ of E, the induced ℤ_ℓ-linear map ψ_ℓ on the rank-two Tate module T_ℓE satisfies det ψ_ℓ=deg ψ and tr ψ_ℓ=1+deg ψ−deg(1−ψ), with deg 0=0. In particular both are integers independent of ℓ.

title: Integral µ_N-level modular curve with its Tate-curve cusp
description: For N≥1, the coarse moduli scheme X_µ(N) over ℤ of generalized elliptic curves with irreducible geometric fibres and a closed embedding µ_N↪E^sm is a smooth non-proper ℤ-curve. The standard 1-gon with µ_N⊂𝔾_m gives a ℤ-point ∞, and the Tate curve identifies the formal completion along ∞ with Spf ℤ[[q]], q being the analytic parameter exp(2πiτ) on X₁(N).

title: Pontryagin duality for locally compact abelian groups
description: For a Hausdorff locally compact abelian group A, its dual A∨=Hom_cont(A,ℝ/ℤ) with the compact-open topology is again locally compact abelian, and evaluation A→(A∨)∨ is an isomorphism of topological groups. Duality exchanges compact and discrete groups, and abelian profinite groups and discrete abelian torsion groups.

title: Euler–Maclaurin summation formula
description: For integers a<b, m≥1 and f∈C^{2m}[a,b], ∑_{j=a}^{b}f(j)=∫_a^bf+½(f(a)+f(b))+∑_{s=1}^{m}B_{2s}(f^{(2s−1)}(b)−f^{(2s−1)}(a))/(2s)!−∫_a^bB_{2m}(x−⌊x⌋)f^{(2m)}(x)dx/(2m)!, where B_n are the Bernoulli numbers and B_n(x) the Bernoulli polynomials.

title: Euler–Gauss limit formula for the gamma function
description: For every complex z other than 0,−1,−2,…, Γ(z)=lim_{n→∞} n!·n^z/(z(z+1)⋯(z+n)), where n^z=exp(z log n).

title: Reflection formula for the gamma function
description: For every z∈ℂ∖ℤ, Γ(z)Γ(1−z)=π/sin(πz); equivalently Γ(z)Γ(−z)=−π/(z sin(πz)).

title: Pointwise convergence of Fourier series of piecewise C¹ periodic functions
description: If φ:ℝ→ℂ has period 1 and is piecewise C¹, with one-sided limits of φ and φ′ at its finitely many breakpoints in each period, then for every real x the symmetric partial sums ∑_{|m|≤M}φ̂(m)e^{2πimx}, with φ̂(m)=∫₀¹φ(t)e^{−2πimt}dt, converge to (φ(x−)+φ(x+))/2.

title: Purely inseparable field extension
description: An algebraic extension L/K of fields of characteristic p>0 is purely inseparable if every α∈L satisfies α^(pⁿ)∈K for some n≥0; equivalently each α∈L has only one root of its minimal polynomial over K in an algebraic closure. In characteristic zero only K/K itself is purely inseparable.

title: Separable real stochastic process
description: A real process (X_t)_{t∈T} indexed by a metric space T is separable if there are a countable T₀⊆T and an almost sure event on which, for every t∈T, some sequence s_n∈T₀ with s_n→t has X_{s_n}→X_t. On that event sup_{t∈T}X_t=sup_{t∈T₀}X_t.

title: Pointwise measurable class of real functions
description: A class G of real measurable functions on a measurable space S is pointwise measurable if it has a countable subclass G₀ such that every g∈G is the pointwise limit of a sequence in G₀. Then suprema over G agree pointwise with suprema over G₀.

title: Density of the chi distribution
description: For a positive integer d, the chi distribution with d degrees of freedom has Lebesgue density 2^(1−d/2)x^(d−1)e^(−x²/2)/Γ(d/2) for x>0 and 0 for x≤0.

title: Independence of functions of disjoint groups of independent random variables
description: If real random variables X_{i,j}, 1≤i≤n, 1≤j≤m(i), are independent and f_i:ℝ^{m(i)}→ℝ are Borel measurable, then the random variables f_i(X_{i,1},…,X_{i,m(i)}), 1≤i≤n, are independent.

title: Joint law of independent random elements is the product law
description: If X₁,…,X_n are independent random elements of measurable spaces S₁,…,S_n with laws μ₁,…,μ_n, then the law of (X₁,…,X_n) on the product σ-algebra of S₁×⋯×S_n is the product measure μ₁×⋯×μ_n.

title: Gaussian integration by parts for a centered Gaussian vector
description: If X∼N(0,Σ) in ℝⁿ and f:ℝⁿ→ℝ is continuously differentiable with f and its partial derivatives of at most polynomial growth, then E[X_i f(X)]=∑_jΣ_ij E[∂_jf(X)] for every i.

title: Lebesgue outer measure on ℝⁿ
description: For S⊆ℝⁿ, the Lebesgue outer measure m*(S)∈[0,∞] is the infimum of ∑_j V(R_j) over all sequences of open boxes R_j covering S, where V(R_j) is the product of the side lengths of R_j. A set S with m*(S)=0 is a Lebesgue-null set, or has measure zero.

title: Jordan measurable set in ℝⁿ
description: A bounded set S⊆ℝⁿ is Jordan measurable if its indicator function χ_S is Riemann integrable on a closed box R containing S; this does not depend on R, and the Jordan content (volume) of S is V(S)=∫_R χ_S.

title: Riemann integral over a Jordan measurable set
description: For a bounded Jordan measurable S⊆ℝⁿ, a bounded f:S→ℝ is Riemann integrable on S if its extension by zero to a closed box R containing S is Riemann integrable on R; then ∫_S f is the integral of that extension, independent of R.

title: Jordan measurability of injective C¹ images
description: If U⊆ℝⁿ is open, S⊆U is compact and Jordan measurable, and g:U→ℝⁿ is an injective C¹ map whose Jacobian determinant never vanishes on S, then g(S) is compact and Jordan measurable.

title: Volume of the linear image of a box
description: If R⊆ℝⁿ is a closed box and A:ℝⁿ→ℝⁿ is linear, then A(R) is Jordan measurable and its volume is |det A|·V(R).

title: Linearity and almost-everywhere monotonicity of the Riemann integral over a Jordan set
description: Let S⊆ℝⁿ be bounded and Jordan measurable and f,g Riemann integrable on S. Then f+g and αf (α∈ℝ) are Riemann integrable with ∫_S(f+g)=∫_Sf+∫_Sg and ∫_Sαf=α∫_Sf, and f≤g outside a Lebesgue-null set implies ∫_Sf≤∫_Sg; in particular functions equal almost everywhere have equal integrals.

title: Additivity of the Riemann integral over disjoint Jordan sets
description: If A,B⊆ℝⁿ are disjoint bounded Jordan measurable sets and f:A∪B→ℝ is Riemann integrable on A and on B, then f is Riemann integrable on A∪B and ∫_(A∪B)f=∫_Af+∫_Bf.

title: Opposite C*-algebra
description: For a C*-algebra A, the opposite C*-algebra Aᵒᵖ has the same Banach space, involution and norm as A with reversed multiplication a·b:=ba; it is again a C*-algebra. A linear map φ:A→B induces the same linear map φᵒᵖ:Aᵒᵖ→Bᵒᵖ.

title: Exactness of minimal tensor products of exact C*-algebras
description: If A and B are exact C*-algebras, then their minimal C*-tensor product A⊗_min B is exact.

title: Finiteness of the class number of a genus of quadratic ℤ-lattices
description: A genus of nondegenerate quadratic ℤ-lattices contains only finitely many isometry classes; their number is the class number of the genus.

title: Finiteness of isometry classes of ℤ-lattices with given rank and discriminant
description: For each n≥1 and nonzero rational d there are only finitely many isometry classes of nondegenerate quadratic ℤ-lattices of rank n and discriminant d.

title: Theta series of a positive definite quadratic lattice
description: For a positive definite integral quadratic ℤ-lattice L, θ_L(z)=∑_(x∈L)e^(2πiQ(x)z)=∑_(n≥0)r_L(n)e^(2πinz) on the upper half-plane. It is a holomorphic modular form of weight rank(L)/2 for a congruence subgroup, with a character.

title: Siegel’s theorem that lattice and genus theta series differ by a cusp form
description: For a positive definite integral quadratic ℤ-lattice L, let θ(gen L) be the average of θ_M over representatives M of the classes in the genus of L, weighted by 1/|O(M)|. Then θ(gen L)−θ_L is a cusp form of weight rank(L)/2.

title: Schulze-Pillot’s theorem on theta series of ternary spinor genera
description: For a positive definite integral ternary quadratic ℤ-lattice L, let θ(spn L), θ(gen L) be the 1/|O(M)|-weighted averages of theta series over the classes in the spinor genus and in the genus of L. Then θ_L−θ(spn L) is Petersson-orthogonal to the space U of weight-3/2 cusp forms spanned by unary theta series ∑_m ψ(m)m e^(2πitm²z), while θ(spn L)−θ(gen L) lies in U.

title: Iwaniec–Duke bound for Fourier coefficients of weight-3/2 cusp forms
description: Let f(z)=∑a(n)e^(2πinz) be a weight-3/2 cusp form on Γ₁(N) whose Shimura lift is a cusp form (equivalently, f is orthogonal to the unary theta series). For ε>0, a(n)≪_(f,ε)n^(1/2−1/28+ε) as n→∞ through n=t n₀² with (n₀,N)=1 and t a squarefree number times an element of a fixed finite set.

title: Analytic hypersurface in a complex manifold
description: A closed subset V of a complex manifold M such that each point of V has a connected open coordinate neighbourhood U on which V∩U is the zero set of a single holomorphic function U→ℂ that is not identically zero. V is irreducible if it is not the union of two analytic hypersurfaces each properly contained in V. Its smooth points are those near which such a local equation can be chosen with nonzero differential.

title: Siegel modular variety Sp₂g(ℤ)∖ℍ_g
description: The orbit space A_g=Sp₂g(ℤ)∖ℍ_g of the Siegel upper half-space under the action M⟨Z⟩=(AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹ of M=[[A,B],[C,D]]∈Sp₂g(ℤ), with the quotient topology and projection π:ℍ_g→A_g. Subsets and functions on A_g correspond to Sp₂g(ℤ)-invariant ones on ℍ_g. For g=1 it is the modular curve SL₂(ℤ)∖ℍ; for g=2 it has complex dimension three.

title: Siegel modular form with a character
description: For a group homomorphism v:Sp₂g(ℤ)→ℂ^× and an integer k, a holomorphic F:ℍ_g→ℂ with F((AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹)=v(M)det(CZ+D)^kF(Z) for all M=[[A,B],[C,D]]∈Sp₂g(ℤ), with the usual cusp condition when g=1. Trivial v gives ordinary Siegel modular forms. For g=2 the abelianization of Sp₄(ℤ) has order two, so there is exactly one nontrivial character, with values ±1.

title: Theta constant with half-integral characteristic
description: For ε=(ε′,ε″) with ε′,ε″∈{0,1}^g and Z∈ℍ_g, θ[ε](Z)=∑_{m∈ℤ^g}exp(2πi(½(m+ε′/2)ᵗZ(m+ε′/2)+(m+ε′/2)ᵗε″/2)), a locally uniformly convergent series defining a holomorphic function on ℍ_g. The characteristic is even if ε′·ε″ is even and odd otherwise; odd theta constants vanish identically, and there are 2^(g−1)(2^g+1) even ones, ten for g=2.

title: Genus-two even theta product Δ₅
description: Δ₅(Z)=2⁻⁶∏θ[ε](Z), the product over the ten even half-integral characteristics of genus two, Z∈ℍ₂. It is a Siegel modular form of weight 5 for Sp₄(ℤ) with the nontrivial ±1 character, has integral Fourier coefficients and satisfies Δ₅(z₁,−z₂,z₃)=−Δ₅(z₁,z₂,z₃) for Z=[[z₁,z₂],[z₂,z₃]]; its square is a weight-10 Siegel modular form with trivial character.

title: Integral symplectic similitude matrices
description: The monoid GSp₂g⁺(ℤ) of integral 2g×2g matrices M with MᵗJM=μ(M)J for J=[[0,I_g],[−I_g,0]] and a positive integer μ(M), the multiplier. It contains Sp₂g(ℤ) as the elements of multiplier 1, is stable under multiplication by Sp₂g(ℤ) on both sides, and acts on ℍ_g by M⟨Z⟩=(AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹ for M=[[A,B],[C,D]]; for example diag(1,…,1,p,…,p) has multiplier p.

title: Weight-k slash operator on functions on the Siegel upper half-space
description: For an integer k, a function F on ℍ_g and a symplectic similitude M=[[A,B],[C,D]] of positive multiplier, (F|_kM)(Z)=det(CZ+D)^(−k)F((AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹). Some authors include a power of the multiplier as normalization. On Sp₂g(ℤ) it is a right action, (F|_kM)|_kN=F|_k(MN).

title: Siegel Eisenstein series of even weight
description: For g≥1 and even k>g+1, E_k^(g)(Z)=∑det(CZ+D)^(−k), summed over the bottom block rows (C,D) of the matrices in Sp₂g(ℤ) taken modulo left multiplication by GL_g(ℤ). The series converges absolutely to a Siegel modular form of weight k for Sp₂g(ℤ) with constant Fourier coefficient 1; for g=1 it is the normalized elliptic Eisenstein series E_k.

title: Eichler–Zagier index-raising operator V_l on Jacobi forms
description: For an integer l≥1 and a Jacobi form φ of weight k and index m, (φ|_kV_l)(τ,z)=l^(k−1)∑d^(−k)φ((aτ+b)/d,az), summed over ad=l and b mod d. It maps Jacobi forms of weight k and index m to Jacobi forms of index lm. Gritsenko–Nikulin’s T₋(l) is the same operator written on functions φ(τ,z)e(mω) on ℍ₂, with a different power of l as normalization.

title: Theta decomposition of a Jacobi form
description: A holomorphic Jacobi form of weight k and positive integral index m has a unique expansion φ(τ,z)=∑_{μ mod 2m}h_μ(τ)θ_{m,μ}(τ,z) with θ_{m,μ}=∑_{r≡μ (2m)}q^(r²/4m)ζ^r, where (h_μ) is a vector-valued modular form of weight k−½; its Fourier coefficients c(n,r) depend only on 4mn−r² and r mod 2m.

title: Generation of Sp₄(ℤ) by the Jacobi group and the coordinate swap
description: Modulo ±1, the Siegel modular group Sp₄(ℤ) is generated by its integral Jacobi subgroup Γ^J, which acts on Z=[[z₁,z₂],[z₂,z₃]] through SL₂(ℤ) on z₁ and integral Heisenberg translations of z₂ while fixing the Fourier–Jacobi variable z₃ up to shifts, together with the element exchanging z₁ and z₃.

title: Uniqueness of the weight-five genus-two form with the sign character
description: Every Siegel modular form of weight5 for Sp₄(ℤ) with the nontrivial ±1 character is a constant multiple of the even theta product Δ₅.

title: Nagaoka’s p-integral divisibility by X₁₀
description: Let p be a prime and k even. If a full-group genus-two Siegel modular form f of weight k has p-integral rational Fourier coefficients and its Witt restriction W(f) to the diagonal vanishes, then f=X₁₀h for a form h of weight k−10 with p-integral coefficients, where X₁₀ is Igusa’s integrally normalized weight-10 cusp form.

title: Igusa’s Witt images of the integral genus-two generators
description: With x_k=e_k⊗e_k (k=2,4,6), x₁₂=Δ⊗Δ, y₁₂=e₄³⊗Δ+Δ⊗e₄³: W(X₄)=x₄, W(X₆)=x₆, W(X₁₀)=0, W(X₁₂)=12x₁₂, W(Y₁₂)=y₁₂, W(X₁₆)=x₄x₁₂, W(X_{12i})=(12/gcd(12,i))x₁₂^i (i≤4), W″(X₁₀)=x₁₂, W″(X₁₂)=x₂x₁₂. Hence W maps integral weight-k forms onto Sym²(M_k(SL₂(ℤ)))_ℤ when 12∤k, and for k=12n its integral image is spanned by the corresponding monomial images.

title: p-adic exponential series
description: For a field K complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value extending |·|_p on ℚ_p, the p-adic exponential is exp(x)=∑_(n≥0)xⁿ/n!, defined on the open disc D_p={x∈K:|x|<p^(−1/(p−1))} where this series converges.

title: p-adic logarithm series
description: For a field K complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value extending |·|_p on ℚ_p, the p-adic logarithm of y∈K with |y−1|<1 is log y=∑_(n≥1)(−1)^(n−1)(y−1)ⁿ/n, a series converging on that disc.

title: Inverse isometric isomorphisms of the p-adic exponential and logarithm
description: For a field K complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value extending |·|_p and D_p={x∈K:|x|<p^(−1/(p−1))}, the p-adic exponential and logarithm are mutually inverse isometric group isomorphisms between the additive group D_p and the multiplicative group 1+D_p.

title: Frobenius reciprocity for coinduced group modules
description: For a subgroup H of a group G, an H-module N and a G-module M, let Ind_H^G N be the G-module of maps φ:G→N with φ(hg)=hφ(g) and (gφ)(x)=φ(xg). Composing with evaluation at 1 gives a natural isomorphism Hom_G(M,Ind_H^G N)≅Hom_H(M,N).

title: Positive real part of a split torus over a number field
description: For a torus S split over a number field F, its positive real part A_S≅Hom(X*(S),ℝ_(>0)) is the subgroup of S(F_∞)=∏_(v|∞)S(F_v) which, under a splitting S≅G_m^r, is (ℝ_(>0))^r embedded diagonally at every archimedean place. It is a connected real vector group of dimension r.

title: Relative Weyl group of a maximal split torus
description: For a maximal F-split torus S of a connected reductive F-group G, the relative Weyl group is W(G,S)=N_G(S)(F)/Z_G(S)(F), the F-points of the normalizer of S modulo those of its centralizer. It is finite and acts on S, on X*(S) and on the relative roots.

title: Adelic height of a primitive vector
description: For a number field F, x∈A_F^n is primitive if x=g(ξ) for some g∈GL_n(A_F) and nonzero ξ∈F^n. Its height is ‖x‖=∏_v‖x_v‖_v, with ‖·‖_v the maximum normalized absolute value of the coordinates at finite v and a normalized Euclidean or Hermitian norm at archimedean v; almost all factors are 1, and other compatible norms change ‖·‖ by a bounded factor.

title: Relative root system of a connected reductive group
description: For a maximal F-split torus S of a connected reductive F-group G, the relative roots Φ(G,S) form a possibly nonreduced root system in the subspace of X*(S)⊗ℝ they span, and the relative Weyl group N_G(S)(F)/Z_G(S)(F) acts on it as its Weyl group.

title: Simple transitivity of the Weyl group on Weyl chambers
description: For a finite root system Φ in a Euclidean space E, its Weyl group permutes the open Weyl chambers simply transitively, and the closure of any one chamber meets every W-orbit in E, so E is the union of the W-translates of a closed chamber.

title: Haar measure decomposition along a product of closed subgroups
description: Let S and T be closed subgroups of a locally compact group G with compact intersection such that the product map S×T→G is open with image of full Haar measure. Then Haar measures can be normalized so that ∫_G f(g)d_ℓg=∫_(S×T)f(st)Δ_T(t)Δ_G(t)⁻¹d_ℓs d_ℓt for f∈C_c(G), Δ denoting modular quasi-characters.

title: Modular quasi-character of a locally compact group
description: For a locally compact group G with right Haar measure d_rg, the modular quasi-character Δ_G:G→ℝ_(>0) is the continuous homomorphism with d_r(hg)=Δ_G(h)d_rg; G is unimodular exactly when Δ_G is trivial. Some references use the reciprocal convention.

title: Modular quasi-character of the points of an algebraic group
description: For a smooth affine algebraic group G over a number field F, the modular quasi-character of G(F_v) is g↦|det(Ad(g)|Lie(G)⊗F_v)|_v, and that of G(A_F) is g↦|det(Ad(g)|Lie(G)⊗A_F)|_A, the product of the local ones.

title: Unimodularity of adelic points of a reductive group
description: For a reductive group G over a number field F, each G(F_v) and G(A_F) is unimodular; for any affine algebraic group G over F, the subgroup G(A_F)¹ is unimodular.

title: Minkowski reduction for adelic GL_n
description: Let K=O(n)∏_pGL_n(ℤ_p)⊂GL_n(A_ℚ). Every g∈GL_n(A_ℚ) has γ∈GL_n(ℚ) with gγ=kt, k∈K and t upper triangular whose diagonal ideles satisfy |t_i/t_(i+1)|≤2/√3 for 1≤i<n.

title: Closed embedding of adelic quotients of a closed subgroup
description: For a closed ℚ-subgroup H of a linear algebraic group G over ℚ, the natural injection H(A)¹/H(ℚ)→G(A)/G(ℚ) is proper, hence a homeomorphism onto a closed subset; here H(A)¹ is the subgroup where all ℚ-rational characters of H have idelic norm 1.

title: Lie product formula in a real Lie group
description: For a real Lie group G with exponential map exp and X,Y in its Lie algebra, exp(X+Y)=lim_(n→∞)(exp(X/n)exp(Y/n))ⁿ. For matrix groups this is the Lie–Trotter product formula.

title: Unique shortest paths in a closed simple polygon
description: In the closed region bounded by a simple polygon in the plane, any two points are joined by a shortest path lying in the region. It is unique, and it is a polygonal path whose bends occur only at vertices of the boundary.

title: Absolute continuity of the Lebesgue integral
description: If f is integrable on a measure space (X,μ), then for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that ∫_A|f|dμ<ε for every measurable A with μ(A)<δ.

title: Two-component boundary model of a de Branges–Rovnyak space
description: Let b be in the closed unit ball of H∞, with boundary function b* and Δ=(1−|b*|²)^{1/2} on the unit circle. A function f∈H² lies in H(b) exactly when some g in the L²-closure of ΔH² makes conj(b*)f*+Δg orthogonal to H² in L². Such g is unique and ‖f‖²_{H(b)}=‖f‖²₂+‖g‖²₂, so f↦(f,g) embeds H(b) isometrically into H²⊕clos(ΔH²). Aleman–Malman extend this model to all spaces with a contractive backward shift.

title: Wiener–Helson classification of shift-invariant subspaces of L² of the circle
description: Let M be a closed subspace of L² of the unit circle with ζM⊆M, ζ the coordinate function. If ζM=M, then M={f∈L²: f=0 a.e. off E} for a measurable set E (Wiener). If ζM≠M, then M=θH² for a measurable θ with |θ|=1 a.e. (Helson). In general M is the orthogonal sum of a doubly invariant and a simply invariant part.

title: Analytic map between analytic manifolds over a local field
description: For analytic manifolds X,Y over a local field K, a map f:X→Y is analytic if it is continuous and its expressions in charts are given near every point by convergent K-power series. Its derivative T_xf at x is the K-linear map whose matrix in charts is the Jacobian of first-order coefficients; f is an analytic isomorphism if it is bijective with analytic inverse.

title: Stable horospherical subgroup of a group element
description: For an element a of a topological group G, the stable horospherical subgroup is G⁻_a={g∈G: aⁿga⁻ⁿ→e as n→∞}; it is a subgroup normalized by a. The unstable horospherical subgroup is G⁺_a=G⁻_(a⁻¹).

title: Existence of the quotient of an algebraic group by an algebraic subgroup
description: For an algebraic subgroup H of an algebraic group G over a field k there is a separated algebraic k-scheme G/H with a G-action and a point o∈(G/H)(k) with stabilizer H whose orbit map G→G/H is faithfully flat; it is unique up to unique isomorphism.

title: Orbit of a reduced algebraic group as the quotient by its stabilizer
description: Let a reduced algebraic group G act on a separated algebraic scheme X over k and let x∈X(k). The orbit map g↦gx is faithfully flat onto the orbit O_x with its reduced structure and induces an isomorphism G/G_x→O_x.

title: Smoothness of the quotient map by a smooth algebraic subgroup
description: For algebraic subgroups H⊂H′ of an algebraic group G, the canonical map G/H→G/H′ is faithfully flat, and it is smooth when H′/H is smooth. In particular G→G/H is smooth whenever H is smooth.

title: Complex semisimple Lie algebra
description: A finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra is semisimple if 0 is its only abelian ideal; equivalently, it is a direct sum of simple Lie algebras, namely its simple ideals.

title: Highest-weight module of a complex semisimple Lie algebra
description: Present a complex semisimple Lie algebra as the Serre algebra 𝔤(R) of its root system, with Cartan subalgebra spanned by the h_i. For a 𝔤-module M and an integral weight λ (an integer combination of fundamental weights), the weight space is M_λ={m: h_i m=⟨λ,α_i∨⟩m for all i}. A highest-weight vector is a nonzero weight vector killed by every e_i, and a highest-weight module is generated by one. Every finite-dimensional module is the direct sum of its integral weight spaces; for each dominant integral λ there is a unique finite-dimensional simple module L(λ) of highest weight λ, and these exhaust the finite-dimensional simple modules.

title: Bounded subset of a metric space
description: A subset B of a metric space (X,d) is bounded if sup{d(x,y): x,y∈B}<∞, equivalently B lies in some ball. In a normed space with its norm metric this means sup_(b∈B)‖b‖<∞.

title: Jimbo’s quantum Schur–Weyl duality
description: Let V be the natural k-dimensional module of U_q(𝔤𝔩_k) over ℂ(q). The R-matrix operators on adjacent factors of V^⊗r satisfy (Ř−q)(Ř+q⁻¹)=0 and give an action of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_r(q) whose image is exactly End_(U_q(𝔤𝔩_k))(V^⊗r); the image of U_q(𝔤𝔩_k) is in turn the commutant of H_r(q).

title: Lusztig’s classical limit of simple quantum-group modules
description: For q an indeterminate and a dominant integral weight λ, let L_q(λ) be the simple type-1 U_q(𝔤)-module with highest-weight vector v. The lattice spanned by the vectors F_(i₁)⋯F_(i_k)v over the ring of rational functions regular at q=1 is stable under E_i, F_i, K_i^(±1) and (K_i−K_i⁻¹)/(q_i−q_i⁻¹), and its specialization at q=1 is the simple 𝔤-module L(λ). In particular L_q(λ) and L(λ) have the same weight multiplicities.

title: Lehrer–Zhang Casimir generation theorem for strongly multiplicity-free modules
description: If V is a strongly multiplicity-free module of a complex simple Lie algebra 𝔤, then for every r≥2 the commutant End_𝔤(V^⊗r) is generated by the operators through which the two-factor components C_ij of the quadratic Casimir act on V^⊗r, so it is a quotient of Kohno’s infinitesimal braid algebra. The same generation holds for End_G(V^⊗r) for the natural modules of SL_k(ℂ), O_k(ℂ) (including even k) and Sp_2k(ℂ), the symmetric powers of ℂ² for SL₂(ℂ), and the seven-dimensional G₂-module.

title: Classification of strongly multiplicity-free modules
description: The strongly multiplicity-free irreducible modules of a complex simple Lie algebra are exactly the natural 𝔰𝔩_k-module and its dual (k>2), the natural 𝔰𝔬_(2k+1)-module (k≥2), the natural 𝔰𝔭_2k-module (k>1), the seven-dimensional G₂-module, and every irreducible 𝔰𝔩₂-module of dimension greater than one. For generic q, a simple type-1 U_q(𝔤)-module is strongly multiplicity-free exactly when the 𝔤-module of the same highest weight is.

title: Universal R-matrix of a Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group
description: For q an indeterminate, U_q(𝔤) has a universal R-matrix in a completion of U_q(𝔤)⊗U_q(𝔤) that acts on tensor products of finite-dimensional type-1 modules. Hence Ř=flip∘R gives module isomorphisms V⊗W→W⊗V satisfying the hexagon identities and the Yang–Baxter equation, so these modules form a braided monoidal category.

title: Ribbon element of a Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group
description: For q an indeterminate, a completion of U_q(𝔤) contains an invertible central element v such that, in Lehrer–Zhang’s normalization, v⁻¹ acts on the simple type-1 module L(λ) by q^((λ+2ρ,λ)), with ρ half the sum of the positive roots, and Δ(v⁻¹)=(v⁻¹⊗v⁻¹)R₂₁R for the universal R-matrix R. It makes the finite-dimensional type-1 modules a ribbon category.

title: Quadratic Casimir element of a semisimple Lie algebra
description: For a complex semisimple Lie algebra 𝔤 with a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form and dual bases x_a, x^a, the element C=∑_a x_a x^a of U(𝔤) is independent of the basis and central. It acts on the simple module L(λ) by the scalar (λ+2ρ,λ) for the induced form, where ρ is half the sum of the positive roots.

title: Weyl’s complete reducibility theorem for semisimple Lie algebras
description: Every finite-dimensional representation of a complex semisimple Lie algebra is a direct sum of irreducible representations.

title: Complete reducibility for a generic Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group
description: For q an indeterminate, every finite-dimensional type-1 U_q(𝔤)-module over ℚ(q) or ℂ(q) is a direct sum of simple modules L(λ) with λ dominant integral.

title: Dual of a module over a Hopf algebra
description: For a finite-dimensional module V over a Hopf algebra H with antipode S, the dual space V*=Hom_k(V,k) is an H-module by (h·f)(v)=f(S(h)v), and evaluation V*⊗V→k is H-linear. For finite-dimensional modules U and W, the canonical isomorphism Hom_k(U,W)≅W⊗U* identifies H-module maps with H-invariant vectors of W⊗U*.

title: Jentzsch theorem for irreducible kernel operators on Lᵖ
description: Let (X,μ) be σ-finite, 1≤p≤∞, and Q a bounded operator on Lᵖ(μ) given by a measurable kernel q≥0. Suppose some power of Q is compact and q gives positive mass to (X∖Y)×Y whenever μ(Y)>0 and μ(X∖Y)>0. Then the spectral radius r(Q) is positive and a simple eigenvalue with an eigenvector positive μ-almost everywhere, and no other eigenvalue has a positive eigenvector. If q>0 almost everywhere, every other eigenvalue has modulus less than r(Q).

title: Conley’s trapping-neighborhood characterization of attractors
description: For a continuous map F on a closed subset of ℝᵈ, a compact set A is an attractor of F exactly when some open set V containing A satisfies F(cl V)⊆V and ⋂_(n∈ℕ)Fⁿ(V)=A.

title: Positive distance between a compact set and a disjoint closed set
description: In a metric space, if K is a nonempty compact set and C a nonempty closed set disjoint from K, then inf{d(x,y): x∈K, y∈C}>0. Hence some δ-neighborhood of K is disjoint from C.

title: Duality for a nondegenerate pairing with a finite-dimensional factor
description: Let b:V×W→F be a bilinear pairing of vector spaces over a field F such that only v=0 pairs to zero with all of W and only w=0 pairs to zero with all of V. If V is finite-dimensional, then w↦b(·,w) is an isomorphism of W onto the dual space of V, so dim W=dim V. Consequently, for a nondegenerate bilinear form on any vector space and a finite-dimensional subspace A, the vectors orthogonal to all of A^⊥ form exactly A.

title: Extension of a linearly independent set to a basis of any vector space
description: Every linearly independent subset of a vector space, possibly infinite-dimensional, is contained in a basis; the standard proof applies Zorn’s lemma to linearly independent supersets. In particular every vector space has a basis, every subspace has a complementary subspace, and every linear form on a subspace extends to the whole space.

title: Field of formal Laurent series
description: For a field k, k((t)) consists of formal series ∑_(n≥n₀) a_n tⁿ with a_n∈k and n₀∈ℤ, added coefficientwise and multiplied by Cauchy products; it is the fraction field of the formal power series ring k[[t]]. The exponent of the lowest nonzero term is a discrete valuation for which k((t)) is complete with residue field k.

title: Primitive element theorem
description: A finite field extension K/F is simple, K=F(α) for some α∈K, if and only if it has only finitely many intermediate fields. Every finite separable extension is simple, and therefore has only finitely many intermediate fields.

title: Finite field extensions are the finitely generated algebraic extensions
description: A field extension L/F is finite, [L:F]<∞, if and only if L is generated over F by finitely many elements algebraic over F. In particular every element of a finite extension is algebraic, and [F(α):F] is the degree of the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element α.

title: Algebraic closure of a field in an extension
description: For a field extension L/F, the elements of L algebraic over F form a subfield of L containing F, the relative algebraic closure of F in L. Unlike an algebraic closure of F, it need not be algebraically closed.

title: Laurent-series structure of complete discretely valued fields of characteristic p
description: Let K be a field of characteristic p>0, complete for a discrete valuation, whose residue field k is perfect. Then K contains a unique subfield mapped isomorphically onto k by reduction, and for every uniformizer π the resulting map k((t))→K, t↦π, is an isomorphism. In particular a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic p is isomorphic to F_q((t)).

title: Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind
description: For an integer k≥0, T_k is the real polynomial of degree k with T_k(cos θ)=cos(kθ) for every real θ; equivalently T_k(t)=cos(k arccos t) for t∈[−1,1].

title: Smooth uniformly convex body
description: A convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, n≥2, whose support function, extended positively homogeneously, is smooth on ℝⁿ∖{0} and has a positive definite curvature matrix at every unit vector. These are the bodies of class C^∞_+ in Schneider’s terminology.

title: Purely discontinuous local martingale
description: A real càdlàg local martingale X is purely discontinuous if its quadratic covariation [X,C] vanishes identically for every continuous local martingale C.

title: Jordan block
description: For a scalar λ of a field and an integer k≥1, the Jordan block J_k(λ) is the k×k matrix with every diagonal entry λ, every superdiagonal entry 1 and all other entries 0.

title: Matrix of a linear map with respect to bases
description: For a linear map T:V→W between finite-dimensional vector spaces with ordered bases (v₁,…,v_n) of V and (w₁,…,w_m) of W, the matrix of T is the m×n array (a_ij) determined by Tv_j=∑_i a_ij w_i. For an endomorphism the same basis is used on both sides.

title: Martingale property of M²−[M]
description: If M is a right-continuous square-integrable martingale and [M] is its quadratic variation, then M_t²−[M]_t is a martingale. If M is a right-continuous locally square-integrable martingale, then M²−[M] is a local martingale.

title: Characterization of the jump processes of local martingales
description: Under the usual conditions, let H be a thin process, i.e. an optional process with {H≠0} contained in a countable union of stopping-time graphs. Then H=ΔX for a local martingale X iff (∑_{s≤t}H_s²)^{1/2} is locally integrable and E[1_{τ<∞}H_τ|F_{τ−}]=0 a.s. for every predictable stopping time τ. X can be chosen purely discontinuous with X₀=0, and is then unique up to indistinguishability.

title: Stochastic integrals against local martingales are local martingales
description: If M is a real càdlàg local martingale and H is a locally bounded predictable process, then the stochastic integral ∫H dM is again a local martingale.

title: Finite Vitali covering lemma for Euclidean balls
description: Every finite family of open balls in ℝᵈ has a pairwise disjoint subfamily whose concentric threefold enlargements cover the union of the family. Hence the Lebesgue measure of that union is at most 3ᵈ times the total measure of the subfamily.

title: Generalized eigenspace decomposition
description: Let A be a linear endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space V with distinct eigenvalues λ₁,…,λ_r. Then V is the direct sum of the generalized eigenspaces E_k=⋃_m ker(A−λ_kI)^m; each E_k is A-invariant and A−λ_kI is nilpotent on E_k.

title: Jordan basis of a nilpotent linear operator
description: If N is a nilpotent linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space V, then V has a basis that is a union of chains v₁,…,v_p with Nv₁=0 and Nv_{j+1}=v_j. In such a basis the matrix of N is block diagonal with Jordan blocks of eigenvalue 0.

title: Sublinear functions are support functions
description: Every sublinear function f:ℝⁿ→ℝ, that is, positively homogeneous and subadditive, is the support function of a unique nonempty compact convex set K⊂ℝⁿ.

title: Hausdorff distance of convex sets via support functions
description: For nonempty compact convex sets K,L⊂ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff distance between K and L equals sup_{u∈S^{n−1}}|h_K(u)−h_L(u)|, the uniform distance of their support functions on the unit sphere.

title: Hausdorff and symmetric-difference metrics induce the same topology on convex bodies
description: On the space of convex bodies with nonempty interior in ℝⁿ, the Hausdorff metric and the symmetric-difference metric vol(KΔL) induce the same topology (Shephard–Webster).

title: Divergence of a Euclidean vector field
description: For a vector field F=(F₁,…,F_n) on an open subset of ℝⁿ whose components have first partial derivatives, its divergence is the scalar function div F=∑ᵢ∂F_i/∂x_i.

title: Surface measure on the boundary of a C¹ domain
description: For a C¹ domain Ω⊂ℝⁿ, surface measure dS on ∂Ω is the restriction of (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure to ∂Ω. Where ∂Ω is, after a rigid motion, the graph x_n=g(x′) of a C¹ function, it is the image of √(1+|∇g(x′)|²)dx′ under x′↦(x′,g(x′)).

title: Outward unit normal of a C¹ domain
description: At a boundary point of a C¹ domain Ω⊂ℝⁿ, the outward unit normal ν is the unit vector orthogonal to the tangent hyperplane of ∂Ω pointing away from Ω: if near the point, after a rigid motion, Ω={x_n<g(x′)}, then ν=(−∇g(x′),1)/√(1+|∇g(x′)|²). It is a continuous map ∂Ω→S^{n−1}.

title: Schwartz–Bruhat function on an adelic vector space
description: For a number field F and n≥1, a Schwartz–Bruhat function on A_Fⁿ is a finite linear combination of products ∏_v f_v, where f_v is a Schwartz function on F_vⁿ (viewed as a real vector space) at archimedean places, a locally constant compactly supported function on F_vⁿ at finite places, and f_v is the indicator function of O_vⁿ for all but finitely many v.

title: Adelic Fourier transform and self-dual Haar measure
description: For a number field F, a nontrivial unitary character ψ of A_F trivial on F, and a Haar measure dx on A_Fⁿ, the Fourier transform of a Schwartz–Bruhat function f is f̂(y)=∫f(x)ψ(x₁y₁+⋯+x_ny_n)dx, again Schwartz–Bruhat. The self-dual Haar measure for ψ is the unique normalization for which f̂̂(x)=f(−x) for every such f.

title: Extension of C¹ functions from the closure of a bounded C¹ domain
description: If Ω⊂ℝⁿ is a bounded C¹ domain and F is C¹ on Ω̄ (C¹ in Ω with first derivatives extending continuously to Ω̄), then F is the restriction of a compactly supported C¹ function on ℝⁿ.

title: Sobolev inequality on a bounded Lipschitz domain
description: For a bounded Lipschitz domain D⊂ℝⁿ, integers k≥1 and 1≤p<∞ with kp<n, W^{k,p}(D) embeds continuously into L^q(D) for 1/q=1/p−k/n: ‖u‖_{L^q(D)}≤c‖u‖_{W^{k,p}(D)} with c depending only on k,p,n,D.

title: Morrey embedding on a bounded Lipschitz domain
description: For a bounded Lipschitz domain D⊂ℝⁿ and n<p<∞, every u∈W^{1,p}(D) has a representative that is Hölder continuous of exponent 1−n/p on D̄, with Hölder norm at most c‖u‖_{W^{1,p}(D)} for a constant c depending only on p,n,D.

title: Continuous weak derivatives give classical C¹ functions
description: If a continuous function u on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ has weak first partial derivatives that are continuous, then u is C¹ on Ω and its classical partial derivatives equal the weak ones.

title: Self-duality of the adeles of a number field
description: For a number field F and a nontrivial unitary character ψ of A_F trivial on F, a↦ψ(a·) is an isomorphism of topological groups from A_F onto its Pontryagin dual, and it maps F onto the characters of A_F trivial on F, so the dual of A_F/F is identified with F.

title: Unit volume of the adele quotient for the self-dual measure
description: For a number field F and a nontrivial unitary character ψ of A_F trivial on F, the Haar measure on A_F that is self-dual for ψ, together with counting measure on F, gives the compact quotient A_F/F total volume 1.

title: Fourier inversion on a compact abelian group
description: Let K be a compact abelian group with Haar probability measure and dual group K̂. If f is continuous on K and its Fourier coefficients f̂(χ)=∫f(x)χ(x)⁻¹dx are absolutely summable over K̂, then f(x)=∑_{χ∈K̂}f̂(χ)χ(x) for every x∈K.

title: Kodaira–Néron classification of elliptic special fibers
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a complete discretely valued field with perfect residue field k. The special fiber of its minimal proper regular model has one of the Kodaira types I₀, I_v (v≥1), II, III, IV, I₀*, I_v* (v≥1), IV*, III*, II*. The geometric component group of the Néron special fiber is respectively trivial, ℤ/v, trivial, ℤ/2, ℤ/3, (ℤ/2)², (ℤ/2)² for even v or ℤ/4 for odd v, ℤ/3, ℤ/2, trivial; its identity component is geometrically an elliptic curve, 𝔾_m or 𝔾_a for good, multiplicative and additive types.

title: Heegner CM point of conductor n on X₀(N)
description: Let K⊂ℂ be imaginary quadratic and 𝔑⊂O_K an ideal with O_K/𝔑≅ℤ/Nℤ. For n≥1 prime to N let O_n=ℤ+nO_K and 𝔑_n=𝔑∩O_n, an invertible O_n-ideal with O_n/𝔑_n≅ℤ/Nℤ. The cyclic N-isogeny ℂ/O_n→ℂ/𝔑_n⁻¹ defines the Heegner point x_n∈X₀(N)(ℂ) of conductor n; both curves have complex multiplication by O_n, and x₁ is the Heegner point for O_K.

title: Field of definition of a conductor-n Heegner point
description: For K imaginary quadratic, 𝔑⊂O_K with O_K/𝔑≅ℤ/Nℤ and n prime to N, the Heegner point x_n of conductor n on X₀(N) is rational over the ring class field K_n of conductor n. Consequently, for a modular parametrization φ:X₀(N)→E over ℚ, y_n=φ(x_n) lies in E(K_n).

title: Galois groups of ring class fields at inert prime conductors
description: Let K be imaginary quadratic with K≠ℚ(i),ℚ(√−3), and K_c its ring class field of conductor c. For a rational prime ℓ inert in K, Gal(K_ℓ/K₁)≅(O_K/ℓO_K)^×/(ℤ/ℓℤ)^×=𝔽_(ℓ²)^×/𝔽_ℓ^× is cyclic of order ℓ+1. For a squarefree product n of such primes, restriction gives Gal(K_n/K₁)≅∏_(ℓ|n)Gal(K_ℓ/K₁), and Gal(K_n/K_(n/ℓ))≅Gal(K_ℓ/K₁).

title: Kolyvagin derived Heegner point
description: Fix E/ℚ of conductor N, a modular parametrization φ:X₀(N)→E and K imaginary quadratic, K≠ℚ(i),ℚ(√−3), with 𝔑⊂O_K, O_K/𝔑≅ℤ/Nℤ. For squarefree λ prime to N whose prime factors are inert in K, let y_λ=φ(x_λ)∈E(K_λ) be the Heegner point of conductor λ, choose generators t_q of the cyclic groups Gal(K_q/K₁) of order q+1, put I_q=∑_(i=1)^q i·t_q^i and I_λ=∏_(q|λ)I_q in ℤ[Gal(K_λ/K₁)], and let S represent Gal(K_λ/K)/Gal(K_λ/K₁). Then P_λ=∑_(σ∈S)σ(I_λy_λ)∈E(K_λ); P₁=Tr_(K₁/K)y₁=y_K.

title: Mazur’s formal-immersion criterion for potentially good reduction
description: Let K be a number field, N squarefree, and 𝔭 a prime of K of residue characteristic p with ramification index e_𝔭(K/ℚ)<p−1. Let E/K have a K-rational cyclic subgroup of order N with moduli point x∈X₀(N)(K). If some optimal quotient f:J₀(N)^new→A, composed with X₀(N)→J₀(N) sending ∞ to 0, maps x to a point of finite order in A(K), then E has potentially good reduction at 𝔭.

title: Finiteness of the Mordell–Weil group of the Eisenstein quotient
description: For a prime N, let J̃ be Mazur’s Eisenstein quotient of J₀(N), the optimal quotient attached to the components of the Hecke algebra meeting the Eisenstein ideal. The projection J₀(N)→J̃ maps the cuspidal subgroup isomorphically onto J̃(ℚ); in particular J̃(ℚ) is finite.

title: Serre’s lifting lemma for closed subgroups of SL₂(ℤ_p)
description: Let p≥5 be prime and G a closed subgroup of SL₂(ℤ_p) whose reduction modulo p is all of SL₂(𝔽_p). Then G=SL₂(ℤ_p).

title: Perfectness of SL₂ over a field with more than three elements
description: For a field F with more than three elements, SL₂(F) equals its commutator subgroup. In particular SL₂(𝔽_p) is perfect for every prime p≥5, whereas SL₂(𝔽₂) and SL₂(𝔽₃) are not.

title: Dedekind domains with finitely many primes are principal
description: A Dedekind domain with only finitely many prime ideals is a principal ideal domain.

title: Integral closure commutes with localization
description: Let A⊆L be an integral domain inside a field, B the integral closure of A in L, and S⊆A a multiplicative subset not containing0. Then S⁻¹B is the integral closure of S⁻¹A in L.

title: Fractional ideals of a localized Dedekind domain
description: Let A be a Dedekind domain and S a multiplicative subset not containing0. Then 𝔞↦S⁻¹𝔞 is an isomorphism from the subgroup of fractional ideals of A generated by the nonzero primes disjoint from S onto the group of fractional ideals of S⁻¹A; in particular prime factorizations extend along localization.

title: Forward-invariant subset of a self-map
description: For a map T:X→X, a subset A⊆X is forward invariant (positively invariant) if T(A)⊆A; then every forward orbit x,Tx,T²x,… starting in A stays in A.

title: Absorbing set of a self-map
description: For a map T:X→X and a subset Y⊆X, a set M⊆X is absorbing for Y if M is forward invariant and the forward orbit (Tⁿx)_(n≥0) of every x∈Y meets M; from its first visit on, the orbit stays in M.

title: Heine–Borel theorem in Euclidean space
description: A subset of ℝⁿ with the Euclidean metric is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

title: Monotone real sequence
description: A real sequence (xₙ) is monotone increasing if xₙ≤xₙ₊₁ for all n, monotone decreasing if xₙ≥xₙ₊₁ for all n, and monotone if it is either.

title: Bounded real sequence
description: A real sequence (xₙ) is bounded if some real B satisfies |xₙ|≤B for all n; it is bounded above (below) if some B satisfies xₙ≤B (xₙ≥B) for all n.

title: Subsequence of a sequence
description: For a sequence (xₙ) and a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers n₁<n₂<n₃<⋯, the sequence (x_(n_k))_k is a subsequence of (xₙ).

title: Generalized conditional expectation
description: For X≥0 and a sub-σ-algebra G, E[X|G] is the a.s. unique G-measurable [0,∞]-valued variable with E[X1_A]=E[E[X|G]1_A] for A∈G. If E[X⁺|G]<∞ a.s. or E[X⁻|G]<∞ a.s., for example when X⁺ is integrable, the generalized conditional expectation is E[X⁺|G]−E[X⁻|G].

title: Continuous-time Galton–Watson process
description: A population process in which each individual lives for an independent exponential time of rate β and at death is replaced by an independent number of offspring with a fixed law on the nonnegative integers; offspring evolve in the same way, independently. Also called a Markov branching process.

title: Extinction of a subcritical Galton–Watson process
description: If the offspring mean m satisfies m<1, a Galton–Watson process started from finitely many individuals becomes extinct almost surely; since E Z_n=Z_0mⁿ, its total progeny has finite mean Z_0/(1−m).

title: Extension of a uniformly continuous map to the closure
description: A uniformly continuous map from a subset S of a metric space into a complete metric space extends uniquely to a continuous map on the closure of S, and the extension is uniformly continuous.

title: Differentiability of C₀-semigroup orbits on the generator domain
description: If A generates a strongly continuous semigroup T on a Banach space and x∈D(A), then T(t)x∈D(A), t↦T(t)x is continuously differentiable, and d/dt T(t)x=AT(t)x=T(t)Ax for all t≥0.

title: Exponential bound for a strongly continuous semigroup
description: For every strongly continuous semigroup T of bounded operators on a Banach space there are constants M≥1 and ω∈ℝ with ‖T(t)‖≤Me^{ωt} for all t≥0.

title: Uniform boundedness principle
description: A family of bounded linear operators from a Banach space into a normed space that is pointwise bounded on every vector is uniformly bounded in operator norm. Also called the Banach–Steinhaus theorem.

title: Skorokhod divergence preserves Malliavin smoothness
description: For separable Hilbert spaces K, the Skorokhod divergence maps Malliavin smooth H⊗K-valued Wiener functionals into Malliavin smooth K-valued ones, with Lᵖ bounds on δu and its Malliavin derivatives by finitely many Lᵠ norms of the derivatives of u.

title: Sobolev embedding of Hˢ(ℝᵈ) into bounded Cᵏ functions
description: For real s>k+d/2, every element of the Fourier-defined Sobolev space Hˢ(ℝᵈ) has a representative in C_bᵏ(ℝᵈ), and its Cᵏ_b norm is bounded by a constant times its Hˢ norm.

title: Continuity theorem for Laplace transforms of nonnegative random variables
