description: If nonnegative random variables X_n satisfy E e^{−αX_n}→E e^{−αX} for every α>0, where X is a nonnegative random variable, then X_n converges to X in distribution.

title: Jordan’s inequality for the sine function
description: For 0≤x≤π/2, (2/π)x≤sin x≤x. Equivalently |sin(πy)|≥2‖y‖ for every real y, where ‖y‖ is the distance from y to the nearest integer.

title: Hadamard factorization theorem for entire functions of finite order
description: Let f be an entire function of finite order ρ with f(0)≠0 and zeros z₁,z₂,… counted with multiplicity, and let k be an integer with 0≤k≤ρ and ∑|z_n|^(−1−k)<∞. Then f(z)=e^(g(z))∏_n(1−z/z_n)exp(z/z_n+(z/z_n)²/2+⋯+(z/z_n)^k/k) for a polynomial g of degree at most ρ, the product converging absolutely and locally uniformly.

title: Van der Corput first derivative integral test
description: If Φ is a real C² function on a bounded interval [a,b] whose derivative Φ′ is monotonic with |Φ′(x)|≥μ>0 throughout, then |∫_a^b e^(iλΦ(x))dx|≤3/(λμ) for every λ>0; the bound does not depend on the length of [a,b].

title: Eichler transformation of a quadratic space
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space V with Q(x)=B(x,x), an isotropic vector u and a vector w orthogonal to u, the Eichler transformation is E_(u,w)(x)=x+B(x,u)w−B(x,w)u−½Q(w)B(x,u)u. It is an isometry of V; for a lattice L one considers those E_(u,w) that preserve L.

title: Eichler transformations are rotations with trivial spinor norm
description: Every Eichler transformation of a nondegenerate quadratic space over a field of characteristic other than two has determinant one and spinor norm equal to the trivial square class.

title: O’Meara–Pollak generation theorem for dyadic integral orthogonal groups
description: Let L be a lattice on a nondegenerate quadratic space over a dyadic local field F. If L is modular, or if 2 is unramified in F, then the integral orthogonal group O(L) is generated by the symmetries and the Eichler transformations that preserve L. In particular this holds for every lattice over ℚ₂.

title: Cartan–Dieudonné theorem
description: Over a field of characteristic other than two, every isometry of an n-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space is a product of at most n reflections (symmetries).

title: Unit spinor norms of unimodular dyadic lattices of rank at least three
description: If L is a unimodular lattice of rank at least three on a quadratic space over a dyadic local field F, with unit group U of its valuation ring, then θ(O⁺(L)) contains every unit square class: U(F×)²⊆θ(O⁺(L)). This is O’Meara’s 93:20 as cited by Hsia.

title: Geometrically connected scheme over a field
description: A scheme X over a field k is geometrically connected if its base change X×_k Spec k̄ to an algebraic closure k̄ of k is connected as a topological space; equivalently X×_k Spec L is connected for every field extension L of k.

title: Chevalley structure theorem for algebraic groups
description: Over a perfect field k, every smooth connected group scheme G of finite type over k contains a unique smooth connected normal affine algebraic subgroup H such that the quotient G/H is an abelian variety; H is the largest smooth connected affine algebraic subgroup of G.

title: Torus–unipotent decomposition of a commutative affine group over a perfect field
description: Over a perfect field, a smooth connected commutative affine algebraic group H is the direct product S×U of its largest subtorus S and its largest unipotent algebraic subgroup U.

title: Descent of properness along faithfully flat quasi-compact base change
description: Let S′→S be a faithfully flat quasi-compact morphism of schemes and f:X→S a morphism of schemes. If the base change X×_S S′→S′ is proper, then f is proper.

title: Proper open and closed part through a proper closed fiber over a complete local ring
description: Let A be a complete Noetherian local ring and X a separated A-scheme of finite type whose closed fiber is proper over the residue field. Then X is the disjoint union of two open subschemes Z and Z′ with Z proper over A and containing the closed fiber.

title: Zariski’s connectedness theorem
description: Let f:X→Y be a proper morphism of schemes with Y locally Noetherian and f_*O_X=O_Y. Then f is surjective and every fiber of f is geometrically connected.

title: Resolvent of a closed symmetric form
description: For a closed symmetric form E with domain D on a real Hilbert space H and α>0, the α-resolvent G_α:H→D sends f to the unique u∈D with E(u,v)+α(u,v)_H=(f,v)_H for every v∈D. Existence and uniqueness follow from the Riesz representation theorem on D with the complete inner product E_α=E+α(·,·)_H.

title: Sobolev space H¹ on the circle
description: H¹(S¹) consists of real 2π-periodic L² functions whose first distributional derivative, tested against smooth periodic functions, is also in L². Functions are identified almost everywhere; the inner product (u,v)_{L²}+(u′,v′)_{L²} defines its norm.

title: Energy identity for the positive part of a parabolic Sobolev function
description: Let V=H¹(S¹), or V=H₀¹(Ω) for an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ, with the Gelfand triple V⊂L²⊂V*. If w∈L²(0,T;V) has weak time derivative w′∈L²(0,T;V*), then w⁺∈L²(0,T;V) and t↦‖w(t)⁺‖²_{L²} has an absolutely continuous version whose derivative is 2⟨w′(t),w(t)⁺⟩ for almost every t.

title: Normal algebraic field extension
description: An algebraic field extension L/k is normal if every irreducible polynomial in k[X] with a root in L splits into linear factors over L. Equivalently, the minimal polynomial over k of every element of L splits over L.

title: Structure of discrete subgroups of a finite-dimensional real vector space
description: Every discrete subgroup Λ of a finite-dimensional real vector space V is generated over ℤ by a finite ℝ-linearly independent family; in particular Λ is a free abelian group of rank at most dim V. The quotient V/Λ is compact exactly when that family is a real basis of V.

title: Noetherian topology and irreducible decomposition of affine algebraic sets
description: For a field k, the Zariski topology on any algebraic subset V of kⁿ is Noetherian. Hence V, in particular any affine variety over an algebraically closed field, is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets; an irredundant such union is unique up to order and consists exactly of the irreducible components of V.

title: Smoothness of algebraic groups in characteristic zero
description: Every algebraic group, that is every group scheme of finite type, over a field of characteristic zero is smooth. This extends Cartier’s theorem for affine algebraic groups to arbitrary, possibly non-affine, algebraic groups.

title: Anti-affine algebraic group
description: An algebraic group G over a field k is anti-affine if its only global regular functions are constants, O(G)=k. Complete connected group varieties, such as abelian varieties, are examples.

title: Affinization of an algebraic group
description: For an algebraic group G over a field k, the k-algebra O(G) of global regular functions is finitely generated and G^aff=Spec O(G) is an affine algebraic group. The natural homomorphism G→G^aff is faithfully flat, universal among homomorphisms from G to affine algebraic groups, and has anti-affine kernel.

title: Anti-affine algebraic groups are smooth and connected
description: Every anti-affine algebraic group over a field is smooth and connected.

title: Smoothness of extensions and quotients of algebraic groups
description: For an exact sequence e→N→G→Q→e of algebraic groups over a field, if N and Q are smooth then G is smooth, and if G is smooth then Q is smooth.

title: Complex line integral along a piecewise smooth path
description: For a piecewise C¹ path γ:[a,b]→ℂ and a complex function f continuous on its image, the line (contour) integral is ∫_γf(z)dz=∫_a^bf(γ(t))γ′(t)dt, summed over the finitely many C¹ pieces, with real and imaginary parts integrated separately.

title: Limit inferior of a real or extended-real sequence
description: For a sequence (a_n) of real or extended real numbers, liminf a_n=sup_N inf_{n≥N}a_n, a value in the extended real line [−∞,∞].

title: Approximation of convex bodies by smooth uniformly convex bodies
description: Every convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, n≥2, is a Hausdorff limit of smooth uniformly convex bodies: bodies whose support functions are C^∞ on ℝⁿ∖{0} with positive definite curvature matrices (class C^∞_+).

title: Dual of L¹ for a σ-finite measure
description: For a σ-finite measure μ, every bounded linear functional on real L¹(μ) is uniquely integration against an element of L^∞(μ), and its operator norm is that element’s essential supremum norm.

title: Separability of Lᵖ for a countably generated σ-algebra
description: If μ is a σ-finite measure on a countably generated σ-algebra and 1≤p<∞, then Lᵖ(μ) is separable; for example the Borel σ-algebra of a separable metric space is countably generated.

title: Strong operator topology on bounded operators
description: On the bounded linear operators X→Y between normed spaces, the strong operator topology is the coarsest topology making T↦Tx continuous for every x∈X; a net T_i converges to T exactly when ‖(T_i−T)x‖→0 for each x. For Hilbert spaces H→K this is the usual strong operator topology.

title: Product of ideals in a commutative ring
description: For ideals a and b of a commutative ring R, the product ab is the ideal of all finite sums ∑a_ib_i with a_i∈a and b_i∈b. Ideal multiplication is associative and commutative with identity R, and aⁿ is the n-fold product. An ideal a divides b if b=ac for some ideal c; then b⊆a.

title: Fractional ideal of an integral domain
description: For an integral domain A with fraction field K, a fractional ideal of A is a nonzero A-submodule a⊆K with da⊆A for some nonzero d∈A; every nonzero finitely generated A-submodule of K is one. Products ab of fractional ideals are defined as for ideals, principal fractional ideals are bA with b∈K×, and the nonzero ideals of A are the integral fractional ideals.

title: Divisibility and units in a commutative ring
description: In a commutative ring R, a divides b, written a|b, if b=ac for some c∈R, equivalently bR⊆aR. A unit is an element dividing 1, that is, an invertible element; a and b are associates if b=ua for a unit u, which in an integral domain holds exactly when aR=bR.

title: Torsion submodule of a module over an integral domain
description: For a module M over an integral domain R, the torsion submodule M_tors consists of the m∈M with rm=0 for some nonzero r∈R; it is a submodule. M is a torsion module if M_tors=M and torsion-free if M_tors=0.

title: Direct sum of modules over a commutative ring
description: For modules M_i over a commutative ring R, the direct sum ⊕M_i is the direct sum of the underlying abelian groups with coordinatewise scalar multiplication. A module M is the internal direct sum of submodules N_i when the addition map ⊕N_i→M is an isomorphism.

title: Elementary divisor theorem for submodules of a finite free module over a PID
description: Let R be a principal ideal domain, M a free R-module of rank n and N⊆M a nonzero submodule. There are a basis v₁,…,v_n of M, an integer m≤n and nonzero a₁|a₂|⋯|a_m in R such that a₁v₁,…,a_mv_m is a basis of N.

title: Sheaf of modules on a scheme
description: For a scheme X, an O_X-module is a sheaf of abelian groups F on X with an O_X(U)-module structure on each F(U), compatible with the restriction maps; each stalk F_x is then an O_(X,x)-module. Homomorphisms of O_X-modules are sheaf maps that are O_X(U)-linear on every open U, and F|_U is the restriction to an open subscheme.

title: Quasi-coherent sheaf on a scheme
description: An O_X-module F on a scheme X is quasi-coherent if X is covered by affine opens U=Spec A with F|_U≅M̃ for an A-module M, where M̃ is the O_U-module with M̃(D(f))=M⊗_A A_f for f∈A; then F(U)=M. The structure sheaf O_X is quasi-coherent.

title: Coherent sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme
description: On a locally Noetherian scheme X, a coherent sheaf is a quasi-coherent O_X-module F such that F(U) is a finitely generated O_X(U)-module for every affine open U; it suffices to check this on the affine opens of one cover.

title: Tensor product of quasi-coherent sheaves
description: For quasi-coherent O_X-modules F and G on a scheme X, F⊗_(O_X)G is the quasi-coherent O_X-module with (F⊗G)(U)=F(U)⊗_(O_X(U))G(U) for every affine open U, and stalks F_x⊗G_x. The n-fold tensor power is written F^(⊗n), with F^(⊗0)=O_X.

title: Invertible sheaf on a scheme
description: An O_X-module L on a scheme X is invertible if every point has an open neighbourhood U with L|_U≅O_U. Invertible sheaves are quasi-coherent and closed under tensor products and powers L^(⊗n). A global section s of L defines the open set X_s of points x where s generates the stalk L_x.

title: Sheaf of modules generated by global sections
description: An O_X-module F on a scheme X is generated by global sections if for every x∈X the images of the global sections F(X) generate the stalk F_x as an O_(X,x)-module.

title: Very ample invertible sheaf over a field
description: An invertible sheaf L on a scheme X over a field k is very ample if there is an immersion of X into some projective space Pⁿ_k, that is, a closed immersion into an open subscheme, such that L is isomorphic to the restriction O_X(1) of the twisting sheaf O(1).

title: Relatively ample invertible sheaf
description: For a quasi-compact morphism of schemes f:X→S, an invertible sheaf L on X is f-ample (relatively ample, ample on X/S) if for every affine open V⊆S the scheme U=f⁻¹(V) is covered by the affine open sets U_s, for s a global section of L^(⊗n) over U with n≥1. For X of finite type over a field k and S=Spec k this is ampleness of L.

title: Projective space over a scheme
description: For a scheme S, projective n-space Pⁿ_S is the base change Pⁿ_ℤ×_(Spec ℤ)S, where Pⁿ_ℤ is glued from the n+1 affine charts Spec ℤ[x₀/x_i,…,x_n/x_i] exactly as over a field. Over S=Spec A it is glued from Spec A[x₀/x_i,…,x_n/x_i], and over a field it is the usual projective space.

title: Flat module over a commutative ring
description: A module M over a commutative ring R is flat if N↦N⊗_R M carries injective homomorphisms of R-modules to injective homomorphisms, equivalently preserves exact sequences. It is faithfully flat if moreover N⊗_R M=0 only for N=0.

title: Flat and faithfully flat morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is flat if for every x∈X the local ring O_(X,x) is a flat O_(S,f(x))-module, and faithfully flat if it is flat and surjective on underlying points. For affine schemes Spec B→Spec A this means B is flat, respectively faithfully flat, over A.

title: Algebraic subgroup of an algebraic group over a field
description: An algebraic subgroup of an algebraic group G over a field k is a closed subscheme H⊆G such that H(R) is a subgroup of G(R) for every k-algebra R, where X(R) denotes the k-morphisms Spec R→X; it is then an algebraic group. H is normal if H(R) is normal in G(R) for every R.

title: Homomorphism of algebraic groups over a field and its kernel
description: A homomorphism φ:G→H of algebraic groups over a field k is a k-morphism with φ∘m_G=m_H∘(φ×φ), equivalently inducing group homomorphisms G(R)→H(R) for all k-algebras R. Its kernel is the fibre G×_H Spec k over the identity of H, a normal algebraic subgroup with kernel points ker(G(R)→H(R)).

title: Field ℂ_p of p-adic complex numbers
description: ℂ_p is the completion of an algebraic closure of ℚ_p for the unique extension of the p-adic absolute value. It is algebraically closed, contains every finite extension of ℚ_p, its ring of integers O_(ℂ_p)={x:|x|_p≤1} is p-adically complete, and the absolute Galois group of ℚ_p, hence of each finite extension K, acts on ℂ_p by continuous isometric field automorphisms.

title: Witt vectors of a perfect ring of characteristic p
description: For a commutative ring A of prime characteristic p whose Frobenius x↦x^p is bijective, the ring W(A) of p-typical Witt vectors is, up to unique isomorphism, the p-torsion-free p-adically complete ring with W(A)/pW(A)≅A. Each element is uniquely ∑_(n≥0)[a_n]pⁿ with a_n∈A, where the Teichmüller lift [a] is the unique multiplicative section of reduction, and the Frobenius of A lifts to a ring automorphism φ of W(A). For example W(𝔽_p)=ℤ_p.

title: Tilt O_(ℂ_p)^♭ of the ring of integers of ℂ_p
description: O_(ℂ_p)^♭ is the inverse limit of O_(ℂ_p)/p along x↦x^p, the ring of sequences (x_n) with x_(n+1)^p=x_n under coordinatewise operations; it is a perfect ring of characteristic p with an action of the absolute Galois group of ℚ_p. Reduction gives a multiplicative bijection with p-power compatible sequences (x^((n))) in O_(ℂ_p); for example a compatible system of p-power roots of unity gives ε=(1,ζ_p,ζ_(p²),…).

title: Fontaine’s map θ
description: Fontaine’s map θ:W(O_(ℂ_p)^♭)→O_(ℂ_p) is given by θ(∑[x_n]pⁿ)=∑x_n^((0))pⁿ. It is a surjective ring homomorphism compatible with the Galois actions, and its kernel is the principal ideal generated by ξ=[p̃]−p for any p̃∈O_(ℂ_p)^♭ with p̃^((0))=p.

title: Divided-power envelope of an ideal in a torsion-free ring
description: For a commutative ring A without additive torsion and an ideal I⊆A, the divided-power envelope of A along I is the A-subalgebra of A⊗ℚ generated by the divided powers xᵐ/m! with x∈I and m≥1; if I=(ξ) it is A[ξᵐ/m!:m≥1]. These elements satisfy the identities of a divided-power structure, such as (x+y)ᵐ/m!=∑_(i+j=m)(xⁱ/i!)(yʲ/j!).

title: Kato’s length bound for the Iwasawa cohomology of a newform
description: For a newform f of weight k≥2 and a λ-adic realization V of f, let H¹ and H² be the Iwasawa cohomology over the cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower and Z(f)⊆H¹ the submodule generated by Kato’s zeta elements. For every height-one prime 𝔭 of the Iwasawa algebra not containing p, length H²_𝔭≤length(H¹/Z(f))_𝔭+length H²_loc,𝔭, and the local term vanishes except in one explicit weight-two case (Kato, Theorem 12.5(3)).

title: Tate’s Euler–Poincaré characteristic formulas for p-adic representations
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_ℓ and a p-adic representation V of G_K, ∑(−1)ⁱdim Hⁱ(G_K,V) is −[K:ℚ_p]dim V if ℓ=p and 0 otherwise. For a number field K, a finite set Σ of places containing those above p and ∞, and V a representation of G_(K,Σ), ∑(−1)ⁱdim Hⁱ(G_(K,Σ),V)=∑_(v|∞)dim H⁰(K_v,V)−[K:ℚ]dim V.

title: Dimension of the Bloch–Kato local finite subspace
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a de Rham p-adic representation V of G_K, dim_(ℚ_p)H¹_f(K,V)=dim_(ℚ_p)(D_dR(V)/D_dR⁺(V))+dim_(ℚ_p)H⁰(K,V). It follows from the exact sequence 0→ℚ_p→B_cris⊕B_dR⁺→B_cris⊕B_dR→0 tensored with V.

title: Bloch–Kato duality of local finite conditions
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a de Rham p-adic representation V of G_K, the subspaces H¹_f(K,V) and H¹_f(K,V*(1)) are exact orthogonal complements under the local Tate pairing H¹(K,V)×H¹(K,V*(1))→ℚ_p.

title: Bloch–Kato dual exponential map
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a de Rham representation V of G_K, the dual exponential exp*:H¹(K,V)→Fil⁰D_dR(V) is the composite of H¹(K,V)→H¹(K,B_dR⁺⊗V) with the inverse of the isomorphism H⁰(K,B_dR⁺⊗V)→H¹(K,B_dR⁺⊗V) given by cup product with log χ_cyc. It vanishes on H¹_f(K,V).

title: Duality between the Galois representations of a newform and its conjugate
description: For a newform f of weight k with complex-conjugate newform f*, and a finite prime λ of the coefficient field, the λ-adic representation of f* is isomorphic to Hom(V_λ(f),F_λ)(1−k) as a G_ℚ-representation. Hence lattices T in V_λ(f)(r) have duals T*(1) that are lattices in V_λ(f*)(k−r).

title: p-adic Hodge properties of the Galois representation of a newform
description: For a newform f of weight k≥2 and level N and a prime λ over p, the restriction of V_λ(f) to G_(ℚ_p) is de Rham, its Hodge filtration has D_dR/Fil^r one-dimensional over F_λ for 1≤r≤k−1, and for p∤N it is crystalline with det(1−φu|D_cris)=1−a_pu+ε(p)p^(k−1)u².

title: Absolute values of Euler-factor roots of a newform
description: For a normalized newform f=∑a_nqⁿ of weight k, level N and nebentypus ε (a Dirichlet character modulo N, so ε(ℓ)=0 when ℓ|N) and a prime ℓ, let α∈ℂ be nonzero with 1−αu dividing 1−a_ℓu+ε(ℓ)ℓ^(k−1)u². Then |α|=ℓ^((k−1)/2) or |α|=ℓ^((k−2)/2), and |α|=ℓ^((k−1)/2) when ℓ∤N.

title: Courant–Fischer min-max theorem for Hermitian matrices
description: If A is an n×n Hermitian matrix with eigenvalues λ₁≥⋯≥λₙ counted with multiplicity, then λᵢ=max over i-dimensional subspaces L⊆ℂⁿ of min over nonzero u∈L of u*Au/u*u; dually λᵢ=min over (n−i+1)-dimensional L of the maximum.

title: Linear dependence lemma
description: If v₁,…,v_m is a linearly dependent list in a vector space, some v_k lies in the span of v₁,…,v_(k−1), and removing such a v_k does not change the span of the list.

title: Derivative of the natural logarithm
description: The natural logarithm is differentiable on (0,∞) with ln′(x)=1/x.

title: Standard function of a Hermitian matrix
description: For a real function f on a set I⊆ℝ and a Hermitian matrix A=U diag(λ₁,…,λₙ)U* with U unitary and all λⱼ∈I, f(A)=U diag(f(λ₁),…,f(λₙ))U*; this Hermitian matrix does not depend on the chosen unitary diagonalization.

title: Operator monotone function
description: A real function f on an interval I⊆ℝ is operator monotone on I if A≼H implies f(A)≼f(H) in the Löwner order for all Hermitian matrices A,H of any common size with eigenvalues in I, where f(A) is the standard matrix function.

title: Subharmonic function on an open Euclidean set
description: A function v:Ω→[−∞,∞) on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ is subharmonic if −v is superharmonic: v is upper semicontinuous, not identically −∞ on any connected component, and v(x) is at most the surface-measure average of v over the sphere S(x,r) whenever the closed ball of radius r about x lies in Ω. For n=2 this is the subharmonic function on a planar domain.

title: Poisson integral on a Euclidean ball
description: For a ball B(a,R)⊂ℝⁿ and a function f on its boundary sphere S(a,R) that is surface-integrable, or measurable and bounded below (or above), its Poisson integral is P_f(x)=∫_{S(a,R)}(R²−|x−a|²)/(|S^{n−1}|R|x−y|ⁿ)f(y)dS(y) for x in the open ball, possibly +∞ (or −∞). The kernel is positive with total mass one.

title: Newtonian fundamental solution of −Δ in dimension n≥3
description: For n≥3 the locally integrable function Γ(x)=|x|^{2−n}/((n−2)|S^{n−1}|) on ℝⁿ, where |S^{n−1}| is the surface area of the unit sphere, satisfies −ΔΓ=δ₀ in the distributional sense.

title: Newton’s shell theorem for the fundamental solution of the Laplacian
description: Let Γ be the fundamental solution of −Δ on ℝⁿ, n≥2 (a multiple of log(1/|x|) for n=2, of |x|^{2−n} for n≥3). For R>0 the surface-measure average of y↦Γ(x−y) over the sphere |y|=R equals Γ(x) when |x|≥R and equals the constant value of Γ on the sphere of radius R when |x|≤R.

title: Local criterion for superharmonicity
description: Let u:Ω→(−∞,∞] be lower semicontinuous on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ and not identically +∞ on any connected component. If every x∈Ω has radii r_m(x)→0 for which u(x) is at least the sphere average, or the ball average, of u over radius r_m(x) about x, then u is superharmonic. In particular superharmonicity is a local property.

title: Jacobi theta inversion formula
description: For real x>0 the theta function θ(x)=∑_(n∈ℤ)e^(−πn²x) satisfies θ(1/x)=√x·θ(x). Equivalently ϑ(τ)=∑_(n∈ℤ)e^(πin²τ) satisfies ϑ(−1/τ)=√(τ/i)·ϑ(τ) on the upper half-plane, with the principal square root.

title: Holomorphy of integrals depending holomorphically on a parameter
description: Let (X,μ) be a measure space, U⊆ℂ open and F:X×U→ℂ with F(·,s) measurable for each s and F(x,·) holomorphic for each x. If every compact K⊆U has an integrable g_K with |F(x,s)|≤g_K(x) for s∈K, then s↦∫F(x,s)dμ(x) is holomorphic on U and its derivative is ∫∂_sF(x,s)dμ(x).

title: Holomorphy of a Dirichlet series in its half-plane of convergence
description: If a Dirichlet series ∑a_n n^(−s) converges at s₀, then it converges for every s with Re s>Re s₀, uniformly on compact subsets of that half-plane. Its sum is holomorphic there, with derivative −∑a_n(log n)n^(−s).

title: Compact-open topology
description: For topological spaces X and Y, the compact-open topology on the set C(X,Y) of continuous maps X→Y is the coarsest topology in which every set {f: f(K)⊆U}, with K⊆X compact and U⊆Y open, is open.

title: Pontryagin dual of a locally compact abelian group
description: For a locally compact abelian group A, its Pontryagin dual Â is the group of unitary characters A→𝕋={z∈ℂ:|z|=1} under pointwise multiplication, with the compact-open topology. Writing 𝕋 as ℝ/ℤ gives the same topological group.

title: Self-duality of the additive group of a local field
description: For a local field F and a nontrivial unitary character ψ of its additive group, the map a↦ψ_a with ψ_a(x)=ψ(ax) is an isomorphism of topological groups from F onto its Pontryagin dual F̂.

title: Pontryagin dual of a restricted product
description: Let G=∏′_v(G_v,H_v) be the restricted product of locally compact abelian groups G_v with respect to compact open subgroups H_v defined for almost all v. Restricting characters to the factors is an isomorphism of topological groups from Ĝ onto the restricted product ∏′_v(Ĝ_v,H_v^⊥), where H_v^⊥ is the compact open subgroup of characters of G_v trivial on H_v.

title: Triviality of Tate’s standard adelic character on the number field
description: For a number field F let ψ_v be Tate’s standard additive character of F_v: x↦e^(−2πix) on ℝ, the character of ℚ_p trivial on ℤ_p sending p^(−n) to e^(2πi/p^n), and these composed with the trace to ℝ or ℚ_p at other places. At every finite place unramified over ℚ the largest fractional ideal on which ψ_v is trivial is O_v, so ψ=∏_vψ_v is a nontrivial unitary character of A_F; and ψ is trivial on the diagonally embedded F.

title: Unique ergodicity of the fibres of a Host–Kra cube nilmanifold
description: Let (X=G/Γ,μ,T) be an ergodic (k−1)-step nilsystem with Haar measure μ and T translation by τ∈G. Then the Host–Kra cube measure μ^[k] is the Haar measure of a sub-nilmanifold X_k⊆X^(2^k), invariant and ergodic under the diagonal map T^[k] and the face transformations T_i^[k], 1≤i≤k; and for every x∈X the closed fibre W_(k,x)={𝐱∈X_k: x_0=x} is uniquely ergodic under T_1^[k],…,T_k^[k], i.e. carries exactly one invariant Borel probability measure.

title: Function of locally bounded variation on a Euclidean open set
description: A locally integrable function f on an open set U⊆ℝⁿ has locally bounded variation, f∈BV_loc(U), if for every open V⊆U with compact closure in U, sup{∫_V f div φ dx : φ a compactly supported C¹ vector field on V with |φ|≤1 everywhere} is finite. A vector-valued function is BV_loc when each component is.

title: Matrix-valued signed Radon measure on a Euclidean open set
description: An m×k matrix-valued signed Radon measure on an open U⊆ℝⁿ is an array μ=(μ^(ij)) in which each entry is a difference of two nonnegative Radon measures on U, evaluated on Borel sets with compact closure in U. For m=k it is symmetric if μ^(ij)=μ^(ji), and positive semidefinite if ∑_(i,j)ξ_iξ_jμ^(ij) is a nonnegative measure for every ξ∈ℝ^k.

title: Second-order criterion for convexity
description: A twice differentiable real function on an open convex subset D of ℝⁿ is convex if and only if its Hessian matrix is positive semidefinite at every point of D.

title: Riesz representation of nonnegative functionals on test functions
description: If L:C_c^∞(ℝⁿ)→ℝ is linear and nonnegative, meaning L(f)≥0 whenever f≥0, then there is a nonnegative Radon measure μ on ℝⁿ with L(f)=∫f dμ for every f∈C_c^∞(ℝⁿ).

title: Local Lipschitz continuity of convex functions on Euclidean space
description: Every convex function f:ℝⁿ→ℝ is locally Lipschitz: on every ball it is bounded, and for each r>0 it is Lipschitz on B(x,r) with constant (2/r)·sup_{B(x,2r)}|f|.

title: Locally Lipschitz functions are locally W^{1,∞}
description: A function f on an open U⊆ℝⁿ is locally Lipschitz if and only if (after modification on a Lebesgue-null set) f and its weak first partial derivatives are locally bounded, f∈W^{1,∞}_loc(U).

title: Convergence of mollifications on Euclidean open sets
description: Let η_ε be the standard mollifiers and f^ε=η_ε*f on U_ε={x∈U: dist(x,∂U)>ε} for f∈L¹_loc(U), U⊆ℝⁿ open. Then f^ε is smooth on U_ε; f^ε→f uniformly on compact subsets if f is continuous, and f^ε→f in L^p_loc(U) if f∈L^p_loc(U), 1≤p<∞.

title: Classical inhomogeneous Triebel–Lizorkin space F^s_{p,q}
description: For s∈ℝ, 0<p<∞ and 0<q≤∞, fix an admissible Schwartz pair with inhomogeneous family (φ_j)_(j≥0). F^s_(p,q)(ℝⁿ) consists of the tempered distributions f whose quasi-norm ‖(∑_(j≥0)(2^(js)|φ_j*f|)^q)^(1/q)‖_(L^p(ℝⁿ)) is finite, with the supremum over j when q=∞.

title: Bessel potential space L^p_s
description: For s∈ℝ and 1<p<∞, the Bessel potential (inhomogeneous fractional Sobolev) space L^p_s(ℝⁿ), also written H^s_p, consists of the tempered distributions u for which ((1+|ξ|²)^(s/2)û)^∨ is a function in L^p(ℝⁿ), normed by its L^p norm.

title: Mikhlin multiplier theorem
description: If m is C^k on ℝⁿ∖{0} with k=⌊n/2⌋+1 and |∂^αm(ξ)|≤A|ξ|^(−|α|) for all |α|≤k, then for 1<p<∞ the Fourier multiplier operator f↦(m f̂)^∨ extends from Schwartz functions to a bounded operator on L^p(ℝⁿ), with norm bounded by a constant depending on n,p times A+‖m‖_∞.

title: Littlewood–Paley square function theorem on Lᵖ
description: Let Ψ be a Schwartz function on ℝⁿ whose Fourier transform is supported in an annulus and satisfies ∑_(j∈ℤ)Ψ̂(2^(−j)ξ)=1 for ξ≠0, and Δ_jf=Ψ_(2^(−j))*f. For 1<p<∞, ‖(∑_j|Δ_jf|²)^(1/2)‖_p is comparable to ‖f‖_p for f∈L^p(ℝⁿ); moreover for any Schwartz θ with annular Fourier support, ‖∑_jθ_(2^(−j))*f_j‖_p≤C‖(∑_j|f_j|²)^(1/2)‖_p for sequences of functions f_j.

title: Independence of Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norms from the dyadic resolution
description: For s∈ℝ, 0<p<∞ and 0<q≤∞, the classical inhomogeneous Triebel–Lizorkin quasi-norms ‖(∑_j(2^(js)|φ_j*f|)^q)^(1/q)‖_(L^p) defined with two different admissible dyadic resolutions, Littlewood–Paley partitions of unity included, are equivalent; hence the space F^s_(p,q)(ℝⁿ) does not depend on the resolution.

title: Integral morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is integral if it is affine and, for every affine open Spec R⊆S with f⁻¹(Spec R)=Spec A, every element of A is integral over R via the ring map R→A.

title: Going up and closedness of the induced map on spectra
description: For a ring map R→S, the going-up property holds (whenever 𝔭⊆𝔭′ are primes of R and 𝔮 is a prime of S over 𝔭, there is a prime 𝔮′⊇𝔮 of S over 𝔭′) if and only if the induced map Spec S→Spec R is a closed map.

title: Finite ring maps are integral
description: If a ring map R→S makes S a finitely generated R-module, then every element of S is integral over R: multiplication by s∈S satisfies a monic polynomial over R obtained from the determinant trick applied to S.

title: Flat pullback of algebraic cycles
description: For a flat morphism f:X→Y of relative dimension r between schemes of finite type over a field, f*[V]=[f⁻¹(V)] for an integral closed subscheme V⊆Y of dimension k, where [f⁻¹(V)] is the cycle of the scheme-theoretic inverse image with multiplicities the lengths of its local rings at generic points of its components. Extended linearly, f*:Z_k(Y)→Z_(k+r)(X) preserves rational equivalence and induces f*:A_k(Y)→A_(k+r)(X).

title: Proper pushforward of algebraic cycles
description: For a proper morphism f:X→Y of schemes of finite type over a field and an integral closed subscheme V⊆X of dimension k, f_*[V]=deg(V/f(V))[f(V)] if dim f(V)=k, where deg is the degree of the extension of function fields, and f_*[V]=0 otherwise. Extended linearly, f_*:Z_k(X)→Z_k(Y) preserves rational equivalence and induces f_*:A_k(X)→A_k(Y).

title: Effective Cartier divisor
description: A closed subscheme D of a scheme X is an effective Cartier divisor if X is covered by affine opens Spec A on which D is Spec A/(f) for a nonzerodivisor f∈A. Its ideal sheaf is then invertible; O_X(D) denotes the dual invertible sheaf, whose canonical section 1 vanishes exactly along D.

title: Capping with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf
description: For an invertible sheaf L on a scheme X of finite type over a field and an integral closed subscheme V⊆X of dimension k+1, c₁(L)∩[V] is the class of the Weil divisor of any nonzero rational section of L restricted to V. This is well defined up to rational equivalence and gives homomorphisms c₁(L)∩−:A_(k+1)(X)→A_k(X).

title: Projective bundle of a finite locally free sheaf
description: For a finite locally free sheaf E of rank r on a scheme X, the projective bundle π:P(E)=Proj_X(Sym*E)→X comes with a tautological invertible sheaf O_P(1) and a surjection π*E→O_P(1); over any open where E is free it is the projective space P^(r−1) over that open. Its points over X correspond to invertible quotients of the pulled-back E.

title: Localization exact sequence for Chow groups
description: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a field, Z⊆X a closed subscheme and U=X∖Z. Proper pushforward along Z→X and restriction to U give an exact sequence A_k(Z)→A_k(X)→A_k(U)→0 for every k.

title: Surjectivity of flat pullback along affine-space bundles
description: Let f:X→Y be a flat morphism of relative dimension r between schemes of finite type over a field such that Y is covered by opens U over which f is isomorphic to the projection U×A^r→U. Then flat pullback f*:A_k(Y)→A_(k+r)(X) is surjective for every k.

title: Projective bundle formula for Chow groups
description: Let E be a finite locally free sheaf of rank r on a scheme X of finite type over a field, with projective bundle π:P→X and tautological sheaf O_P(1). Then (α₀,…,α_(r−1))↦Σ_i c₁(O_P(1))^i∩π*α_i is an isomorphism ⊕_(i=0)^(r−1)A_(k+i)(X)→A_(k+r−1)(P).

title: First Chern class of a relative effective Cartier divisor on flat pullbacks
description: Let p:X→Y be a flat morphism of relative dimension r between schemes of finite type over a field and i:D→X an effective Cartier divisor flat over Y. For α∈A_(k+1)(Y), c₁(O_X(D))∩p*α=i_*((p|_D)*α) in A_(k+r)(X), and the Gysin restriction of p*α to D is (p|_D)*α.

title: Projection formula for first Chern classes under proper pushforward
description: For a proper morphism p:X→Y of schemes of finite type over a field, an invertible sheaf L on Y and α∈A_(k+1)(X), p_*(c₁(p*L)∩α)=c₁(L)∩p_*α in A_k(Y).

title: Principal divisor through the closure of the graph of a rational function
description: Let X be an integral scheme of finite type over a field and f a nonzero rational function, regular and invertible on a dense open U. Let Y⊆X×P¹ be the closure of the graph of f|_U, with projections p:Y→X (proper, an isomorphism over U) and q:Y→P¹. Then div_Y(f)=[q⁻¹(0)]−[q⁻¹(∞)] and div_X(f)=p_*div_Y(f).

title: Finiteness of a proper dominant morphism over codimension-one points
description: Let f:X→Y be a proper dominant morphism of integral schemes with Y locally Noetherian and R(Y)⊆R(X) a finite extension of function fields. If ξ∈Y has dim O_(Y,ξ)=1, then f is finite over some open neighbourhood of ξ.

title: Torsion-free modules over a Dedekind domain are flat
description: A module over a Dedekind domain, in particular over a discrete valuation ring, is flat if and only if it is torsion free.

title: Finite flat morphisms of finite presentation are finite locally free
description: A morphism of schemes is finite locally free if and only if it is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. In particular a finite flat morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme is finite locally free.

title: Pushforward of a flat pullback along a finite locally free morphism
description: If f:X→Y is a finite locally free morphism of degree d between schemes of finite type over a field, then f is proper and flat of relative dimension zero and f_*f*α=dα for every cycle α on Y.

title: Elliptic curve over a field
description: An elliptic curve over a field k is a pair (E,O) of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve E over k of genus one and a k-rational point O. Every such curve is isomorphic to a nonsingular Weierstrass cubic y²z+a₁xyz+a₃yz²=x³+a₂x²z+a₄xz²+a₆z³ with O=[0:1:0], and conversely; its points over any extension of k form an abelian group under the chord-and-tangent rule with identity O.

title: Separable degree of a finite field extension
description: For a finite field extension L/K, the separable degree [L:K]_s is the degree over K of the separable closure of K in L (the largest subextension separable over K); it equals the number of K-embeddings of L into an algebraic closure of K. The inseparable degree [L:K]/[L:K]_s is a power of the characteristic.

title: Moving the support of a divisor away from finitely many points
description: On a nonsingular variety X over an algebraically closed field, for every divisor D and finitely many points x₁,…,x_m there is a divisor D′ linearly equivalent to D whose support contains none of the x_i.

title: Number of points in the fibres of a finite separable map
description: Let f:X→Y be a finite surjective map of irreducible varieties over an algebraically closed field with Y normal. Every fibre has at most deg f points, and if k(X)/f*k(Y) is separable then the points of Y with exactly deg f preimages form a nonempty open subset.

title: Frobenius factorization of a map of curves
description: Over a perfect field of characteristic p>0, every nonconstant map φ:C₁→C₂ of smooth curves factors as C₁→C₁^(q)→C₂, the q-power Frobenius morphism followed by a separable map, where q is the inseparable degree of φ. The Frobenius morphism is purely inseparable of degree q and, on points over an algebraically closed field, raises coordinates to the q-th power, a bijection.

title: Irreducibility from irreducible equidimensional fibres
description: Let f:X→Y be a surjective regular map of projective varieties over an algebraically closed field with Y irreducible. If all fibres f⁻¹(y) are irreducible and of the same dimension, then X is irreducible.

title: Irreducibility of the variety of rank-deficient matrices
description: Over an algebraically closed field, for m≥n the m×n matrices of rank less than n, the common zero locus of the maximal minors, form an irreducible closed subvariety of the affine space of all m×n matrices.

title: ε-subdifferential of a convex function on a Banach space
description: For a proper convex f:X→(−∞,∞] on a real Banach space X, a point x with f(x)<∞ and ε>0, the ε-subdifferential is ∂_εf(x)={x*∈X*: f(y)≥f(x)+⟨x*,y−x⟩−ε for every y∈X}; its elements are the ε-subgradients (approximate subgradients) of f at x.

title: Hahn–Banach separation theorem for an open convex set
description: In a real normed space, if A and B are disjoint nonempty convex sets and A is open, there are a nonzero continuous linear functional ℓ and a real α with ℓ(a)<α≤ℓ(b) for all a∈A and b∈B.

title: Hahn–Banach strict separation of a closed convex set from a compact convex set
description: In a real normed space E, if A and B are disjoint nonempty convex sets with A closed and B compact, there are a continuous linear functional f on E, α∈ℝ and ε>0 with f(a)≤α−ε for all a∈A and f(b)≥α+ε for all b∈B. This is the second geometric form of the Hahn–Banach theorem.

title: Epigraph of an extended-real function
description: For f:X→(−∞,∞], epi f={(x,λ)∈X×ℝ: f(x)≤λ}. On a real vector space f is convex exactly when epi f is convex; on a topological space f is lower semicontinuous exactly when epi f is closed in X×ℝ.

title: Affine minorants of a convex function at relative interior points of its domain
description: If f:ℝⁿ→(−∞,∞] is convex and not identically ∞ and x₀ lies in the relative interior of dom f={f<∞}, there is s in the linear subspace parallel to aff dom f with f(x)≥f(x₀)+⟨s,x−x₀⟩ for every x; thus f has an affine minorant agreeing with it at x₀ and its subdifferential at x₀ is nonempty.

title: Relative interior and closure of a convex set in ℝᵈ
description: For a convex C⊆ℝᵈ, the closure cl C is convex, ri(cl C)=ri C and cl(ri C)=cl C; in particular int(cl C)=int C, so the boundary of cl C is cl C∖int C.

title: Riemann mapping theorem
description: Every simply connected open connected subset of ℂ other than ℂ itself is conformally equivalent to the open unit disc: there is a bijective holomorphic map from it onto the disc, whose inverse is then holomorphic.

title: Koebe one-quarter theorem
description: If f is holomorphic and injective on the open unit disc U with f(0)=0 and f′(0)=1, then f(U) contains the open disc of radius 1/4 about 0; the Koebe function z/(1−z)² shows that 1/4 cannot be improved.

title: Simple connectivity of a plane region via its complement in the Riemann sphere
description: A connected open subset Ω of ℂ is simply connected exactly when its complement in the Riemann sphere ℂ∪{∞} is connected.

title: Cauchy–Riemann operator ∂̄ on the plane
description: For a differentiable complex function f of z=x+iy on an open subset of ℂ=ℝ², ∂̄f=½(∂f/∂x+i∂f/∂y), the Wirtinger derivative with respect to z̄; the Cauchy–Riemann equations for f are ∂̄f=0.

title: Cauchy–Pompeiu formula for compactly supported C¹ functions
description: If f is a continuously differentiable complex function on ℂ with compact support, then f(z)=−(1/π)∬_ℂ (∂̄f)(ζ)/(ζ−z) dξ dη for every z∈ℂ, where ζ=ξ+iη and ∂̄ is the Cauchy–Riemann operator.

title: Laurent expansion of a holomorphic function on an annulus
description: A function holomorphic on an annulus {r<|z−a|<R}, 0≤r<R≤∞, equals Σ_{n∈ℤ}c_n(z−a)ⁿ there, with locally uniform convergence and c_n=(2πi)⁻¹∮_{|ζ−a|=ρ}f(ζ)(ζ−a)^{−n−1}dζ for any r<ρ<R; the coefficients are unique.

title: Bezuglyi–Handelman dimension-group criterion for quotients of simple dimension groups
description: Let (G,u) be a simple dimension group and L a convex subgroup such that for every l∈L and ε>0 there are l₁,l₂∈L with l=l₁−l₂ and l̂₁,l̂₂≥−ε on the normalized trace space S(G,u). Then G/L with the quotient ordering is a dimension group. This applies when J=P(J), where J is the closure of the image of L in Aff S(G,u) and P(J) the subgroup generated by its nonnegative elements.

title: Basic sequence in a Banach space and its basis constant
description: A sequence (xₙ) of nonzero vectors in a Banach space is basic if it is a Schauder basis of its closed linear span. Its basis constant is supₙ∥Pₙ∥ for the partial-sum projections Pₙ(∑aᵢxᵢ)=∑_{i≤n}aᵢxᵢ on that span, that is, the least K with ∥∑_{i≤m}aᵢxᵢ∥≤K∥∑_{i≤n}aᵢxᵢ∥ for all m≤n and all scalars.

title: Mazur’s basic-sequence selection from a weak-star null set
description: Let X be a Banach space and S⊆X** a set whose weak-star closure contains 0 but whose norm closure does not. Then for every ε>0, S contains a basic sequence with basis constant at most 1+ε.

title: Nash-Williams theorem: open sets of infinite subsets of ℕ are Ramsey
description: Give the set [ℕ]^ω of infinite subsets of ℕ the topology inherited from the product topology on {0,1}^ℕ. If U⊆[ℕ]^ω is open, then every infinite L⊆ℕ has an infinite M⊆L such that either every infinite subset of M lies in U or none does.

title: Well-ordering theorem
description: Every set admits a well-ordering, that is, a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element. Over Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory it is equivalent to the axiom of choice.

title: Steiner formula for Minkowski sums with a cube
description: For a compact convex S⊆ℝⁿ, K=[−1,1]ⁿ and t≥0, Vol(S+tK)=∑_{k=0}^{n}(∑_{|I|=n−k}Vol_{n−k}(P_I S))2ᵏtᵏ, where P_I is the coordinate projection onto ℝ^I and Vol₀=1; equivalently the mixed volumes of S with the cube are averages of volumes of coordinate projections of S.

title: Pajor’s two-letter subcube lemma for p-ary words
description: For an integer p≥2 and α>0 there is c=c(p,α)>0 such that for every n≥1 and every S⊆{1,…,p}ⁿ with |S|≥2^{αn}, there are a set I⊆{1,…,n} with |I|≥cn and two distinct letters ℓ,m such that the coordinate restriction of S to I contains {ℓ,m}^I.

title: Nuclear C*-algebra
description: A C*-algebra A is nuclear if there are contractive completely positive maps φₙ:A→M_{k(n)}(ℂ) and ψₙ:M_{k(n)}(ℂ)→A with ∥ψₙ(φₙ(a))−a∥→0 for every a∈A (the completely positive approximation property).

title: Commutative C*-algebras are nuclear
description: Every commutative C*-algebra is nuclear; for C(X) with X compact Hausdorff the approximating maps come from partitions of unity subordinate to finite open covers.

title: Nuclear C*-algebras are exact
description: If B is a nuclear C*-algebra and J is a closed two-sided ideal of a C*-algebra A, then 0→J⊗_min B→A⊗_min B→(A/J)⊗_min B→0 is exact; in particular nuclear C*-algebras are exact.

title: Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring dynamical entropy
description: For a unital C*-algebra A with a state ϕ and a ϕ-preserving automorphism α, h_ϕ(α) is the supremum over channels γ:B→A (unital completely positive maps from finite-dimensional C*-algebras) of lim_n n⁻¹H_ϕ(γ,α∘γ,…,α^{n−1}∘γ), where H_ϕ is the Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring mutual entropy defined by optimizing over decompositions of ϕ (abelian models).

title: Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring entropy is bounded by Voiculescu–Brown entropy
description: If α is an automorphism of a unital exact C*-algebra A and ϕ is an α-invariant state, then the Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring entropy satisfies h_ϕ(α)≤ht(α), the Voiculescu–Brown topological entropy.

title: Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring entropy of a commutative system is Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy
description: If T is a homeomorphism of a compact metrizable space X, μ is a T-invariant Borel probability measure, ϕ(f)=∫f dμ and α(f)=f∘T⁻¹ on C(X), then the Connes–Narnhofer–Thirring entropy h_ϕ(α) equals the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h_μ(T).

title: Variational principle for topological entropy
description: For a continuous map T of a compact metrizable space X, h_top(T)=sup_μ h_μ(T), the supremum of Kolmogorov–Sinai entropies over T-invariant Borel probability measures μ.

title: Cohomology of a sheaf of modules on a scheme
description: For a scheme X the O_X-modules form an abelian category with enough injectives, and the cohomology groups H^i(X,F) of an O_X-module F are the right derived functors of the left exact global-sections functor F↦F(X), so H⁰(X,F)=F(X). For X over a field k they are k-vector spaces. If X is proper over k and F is coherent, each H^i(X,F) is finite-dimensional, only finitely many are nonzero, and χ(X,F)=∑(−1)^i dim_k H^i(X,F) is the Euler characteristic of F.

title: Morphism to projective space defined by generating sections
description: Let X be a scheme over a field k, L an invertible O_X-module and s₀,…,s_n∈H⁰(X,L) global sections that generate L, i.e. the open sets X_{s_i} where s_i generates the stalk cover X. They define the unique k-morphism φ:X→P^n_k with φ⁻¹(D₊(x_i))=X_{s_i}, given on X_{s_i} by x_j/x_i↦s_j/s_i. A basis of H⁰(X,L), when it generates L, defines such a morphism, unique up to a linear change of coordinates.

title: Diffeomorphism between smooth manifolds
description: A diffeomorphism between smooth manifolds M and N is a smooth bijection F:M→N whose inverse map N→M is also smooth. Open subsets of smooth manifolds are smooth manifolds, so one speaks of a diffeomorphism from an open neighbourhood of a point onto an open subset.

title: Splitting field of a polynomial
description: A splitting field of a nonzero polynomial f over a field k is a field extension K/k in which f factors as a product of linear polynomials and which is generated over k by the roots of f in K. Splitting fields exist and are unique up to k-isomorphism; an extension K/k is the splitting field of f inside a given field containing K if K is generated by the roots of f there.

title: Cohomology of coherent sheaves with zero-dimensional support on a proper scheme
description: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k and F a coherent O_X-module whose support has dimension at most 0. Then F is generated by global sections, H⁰(X,F)=⊕_{x∈Supp F}F_x, H^i(X,F)=0 for i>0, and χ(X,F)=dim_k H⁰(X,F).

title: Local triviality of invertible sheaves over the base of a finite morphism
description: Let π:X→Y be a finite morphism of schemes and L an invertible O_X-module. Every y∈Y has an open neighbourhood V such that L|_{π⁻¹(V)} is trivial. In particular every invertible module on a scheme finite over a field is trivial.

title: Ampleness of positive-degree invertible sheaves on a proper curve
description: Let X be a proper curve over a field k (an integral separated scheme of finite type of dimension one, proper over k) and L an invertible O_X-module. Then L is ample if and only if deg(L)>0, where deg(L)=χ(X,L)−χ(X,O_X).

title: Projective scheme of the section ring of an ample invertible sheaf
description: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k and L an ample invertible O_X-module. Then the canonical morphism X→Proj(⊕_{d≥0}H⁰(X,L^{⊗d})) is an isomorphism; more generally this holds for an f-ample invertible sheaf along a universally closed morphism f:X→S, with the relative Proj of ⊕f_*L^{⊗d}.

title: Closed immersion of Proj induced by a surjection of graded rings
description: Let A→B be a homomorphism of graded rings with A generated by A₁ over A₀, which is surjective in all sufficiently large degrees. Then it induces a morphism Proj B→Proj A defined on all of Proj B, this morphism is a closed immersion, and it pulls back O_{Proj A}(n) to O_{Proj B}(n). In particular a graded quotient of k[T₀,…,T_n] gives a closed subscheme of P^n_k.

title: Smooth dependence of ODE solutions on initial data and parameters
description: Let F(t,x,λ) be a smooth map from an open subset of ℝ×ℝⁿ×ℝᵐ to ℝⁿ. The solutions of x′=F(t,x,λ), x(t₀)=x₀ form a smooth map (t,t₀,x₀,λ)↦x(t;t₀,x₀,λ) on an open domain containing every (t₀,t₀,x₀,λ). The same holds, via charts, for the flows of smooth vector fields on manifolds depending smoothly on parameters.

title: Dixmier–Malliavin approximate-delta lemma for Schwartz functions on the real line
description: Given positive bounds B_j, there are constants 0<b_j<B_j and ψ∈S(ℝ) such that ∑_{j=0}^{n}(−1)^j b_j ψ^{(2j)} converges to the Dirac distribution δ in S′(ℝ) as n→∞. One may take ψ̂(ξ)=∏_{n≥1}(1+ξ²/a_n²)⁻¹, the reciprocal of the entire function ∑_j(2π)^j b_jξ^{2j}, with a_n≥n increasing; then sup|ψ^{(j)}| is bounded independently of the chosen sequence.

title: Differentiability of limits under uniform convergence of derivatives
description: Let f_n be continuously differentiable functions on an open interval I such that f_n(x₀) converges for some x₀∈I and f_n′ converges uniformly on I. Then f_n converges locally uniformly to a continuously differentiable f with f′=lim f_n′. Consequently, if every derivative of a sequence of smooth functions converges locally uniformly, the limit is smooth and derivatives may be taken termwise.

title: Projective general linear group over a field and its fractional linear action
description: For a field F, PGL_n(F)=GL_n(F)/F^×, the quotient by the nonzero scalar matrices. PGL₂(F) acts faithfully on the projective line P¹(F) by linear fractional transformations z↦(az+b)/(cz+d), and for a field extension K/F it acts in the same way on P¹(K)=K∪{∞}.

title: Cayley–Hamilton theorem
description: Every square matrix A over a commutative ring satisfies its characteristic polynomial: if det(xI−A)=xⁿ+c_{n−1}x^{n−1}+⋯+c₀, then Aⁿ+c_{n−1}A^{n−1}+⋯+c₀I=0. For a 2×2 matrix this reads A²−tr(A)A+det(A)I=0.

title: Rational canonical form of a matrix over a field
description: Every square matrix A over a field F is similar over F to a unique block-diagonal matrix of companion matrices of monic polynomials d₁∣d₂∣⋯∣d_r (the invariant factors of F[x]-module Fⁿ with x acting by A), with d_r the minimal polynomial. In particular two n×n matrices whose minimal polynomials both equal their common characteristic polynomial are similar over F.

title: Alternating multilinearity of the determinant
description: For n×n matrices over a commutative ring, the determinant is linear in each row when the other rows are fixed, and permuting the rows by a permutation σ multiplies it by sgn(σ); in particular it vanishes when two rows coincide. The same holds for columns.

title: Archimedean property of the real numbers
description: For every real number x there is a natural number n with n>x; equivalently, for every ε>0 there is a natural number n with 1/n<ε.

title: Euclid’s lemma for primes
description: If a prime p divides a product ab of integers, then p divides a or p divides b.

title: Diameter of a subset of a metric space
description: For a nonempty subset A of a metric space (X,d), its diameter is diam A=sup{d(x,y):x,y∈A}, an element of [0,∞].

title: Universality of nondegenerate isotropic quadratic spaces
description: Over a field of characteristic different from two, a nondegenerate isotropic quadratic space V splits as V≅H⊥W with H a hyperbolic plane; in particular V represents every element of the field.

title: Complex cosine function
description: The entire function cos z=(e^{iz}+e^{−iz})/2, which restricts to the real cosine function on ℝ.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Ray-integral representation of the Hankel functions
description: For Re(ν+½)>0 and an acute angle β, H_ν^{(1)}(z)=(2/(πz))^{1/2}e^{i(z−νπ/2−π/4)}Γ(ν+½)^{−1}∫_0^{∞e^{iβ}}e^{−u}u^{ν−½}(1+iu/(2z))^{ν−½}du for −π/2+β<arg z<3π/2+β, and H_ν^{(2)}(z) has the conjugate representation, with i replaced by −i, for −3π/2+β<arg z<π/2+β.
field: Random matrix asymptotics and complex analysis

title: Diagram of a link or tangled trivalent graph
description: A compact subset of the plane, or of a disc meeting its boundary in finitely many endpoints, that is locally an arc, three arcs meeting at a trivalent vertex, or two arcs crossing transversally at a double point away from the vertices, each double point being marked with the arc that passes over. Closed loops are allowed. It depicts a link or a trivalent graph embedded in three-dimensional space.

title: Regular isotopy of link and trivalent-graph diagrams
description: The equivalence relation on diagrams of links and tangled trivalent graphs generated by planar isotopy, the second and third Reidemeister moves, and the moves sliding a strand over or under a trivalent vertex. The first Reidemeister move, which adds or removes a kink, is not allowed, so regular isotopy invariants see the blackboard framing.

title: Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant of coloured ribbon graphs
description: In a ribbon category, a diagram of a link or tangled trivalent graph with oriented edges coloured by objects and vertices coloured by morphisms between the tensor products of the incident colours evaluates to a morphism: crossings are read as braidings, caps and cups as duality maps, and vertices as their colours. The value is invariant under regular isotopy.

title: Clasped G₂ web space
description: For a sequence C of clasps, each a string of symbols 1 and 2 at consecutive boundary points whose weight is the sum of the G₂ fundamental weights λ₁ for each 1 and λ₂ for each 2, Kuperberg’s W(C) is the subspace of the G₂ web space, with type-2 strands drawn as double edges, spanned by the non-elliptic webs without internal double edges in which every clasp is non-convex: every path transverse to the web that cuts off the clasp has weight at least the clasp’s weight in the dominance order.

title: Schwarz’s first fundamental theorem of invariant theory for G₂
description: For the compact group G₂ acting on its seven-dimensional representation, the imaginary octonions, every multilinear invariant form is a linear combination of products of the invariant bilinear form B(a,b), the invariant trilinear form T(a,b,c)=B(a×b,c) and its Hodge-dual four-form, evaluated on the arguments in some order.

title: Quantum Weyl dimension formula
description: For a generic Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group and a dominant integral weight λ, the quantum dimension of the simple module L(λ), the trace of the element K_{2ρ}, equals ∏_{α>0}[(λ+ρ,α)]/[(ρ,α)] over the positive roots, where ρ is half the sum of the positive roots and [n]=(q^{n/2}−q^{−n/2})/(q^{1/2}−q^{−1/2}).

title: Linear system of divisors
description: Let X be a scheme over a field k, L an invertible sheaf on X and V⊆H⁰(X,L) a finite-dimensional subspace. The linear system |V| is the family of zero schemes div(s) of the nonzero sections s∈V, parametrized by the projective space P(V) of lines in V. Its base locus B is the closed set where all sections in V vanish; on X∖B, V defines a morphism φ_V:X∖B→P(V^∨) to the projective space of hyperplanes of V, sending x to the sections vanishing at x, and the members of |V| restricted to X∖B are the pullbacks of hyperplanes.

title: Unramified morphism of schemes over a field
description: A morphism f:X→Y of schemes locally of finite type over a field k is unramified if the natural map f*Ω¹_(Y/k)→Ω¹_(X/k) is surjective, i.e. its relative differentials Ω_(X/Y) vanish. At a k-rational point x this says that the differential T_xX→T_(f(x))Y of Zariski tangent spaces is injective; over an algebraically closed field f is unramified exactly when this holds at every closed point.

title: Smoothness and regularity over a perfect field
description: A scheme locally of finite type over a perfect field (for instance of characteristic zero) is smooth if and only if all its local rings are regular. Over an arbitrary field, smooth schemes are regular.

title: Differential criterion for smoothness of an integral algebra over a field
description: A finitely generated integral algebra B over a field K is smooth over K if and only if its module of Kähler differentials Ω_(B/K) is projective of constant rank dim B.

title: Conormal exact sequence of Kähler differentials
description: For a surjection of K-algebras C→B=C/I there is an exact sequence I/I²→Ω_(C/K)⊗_C B→Ω_(B/K)→0, the first map sending f to 1⊗df.

title: Height plus dimension formula for affine domains
description: For a finitely generated integral algebra A over a field and a prime ideal 𝔭⊆A, ht(𝔭)+dim(A/𝔭)=dim A. In particular such algebras are catenary.

title: Étale characterization of henselian local rings
description: A local ring (R,𝔪,k) is henselian if and only if every étale morphism X→Spec R is a local isomorphism at each point x over the closed point with κ(x)=k; then for such x there is exactly one section Spec R→X sending the closed point to x.

title: Étale quasi-sections of smooth morphisms
description: Let X→S be smooth, s∈S and x a closed point of the fibre X_s with κ(x) separable over κ(s). Then there are an étale morphism S′→S, a point s′ over s with κ(s′)=κ(x), and a section of X×_S S′→S′ through a point over x at s′.

title: Fibrewise criterion for flatness
description: Let X→S and Y→S be locally of finite presentation and f:X→Y an S-morphism. If X is flat over S and every fibre f_s:X_s→Y_s is flat, then f is flat and Y is flat over S at the points of f(X); conversely these conditions follow from flatness of f and of Y over S along f(X).

title: Smoothness as flatness plus smooth fibres
description: A morphism f:X→S locally of finite presentation is smooth at x if and only if it is flat at x and the fibre X_(f(x)) is smooth over κ(f(x)) at x; in particular f is étale at x if and only if it is flat at x and the fibre is étale at x.

title: Flatness criterion for homomorphisms of smooth algebraic groups
description: For a homomorphism f:G→G′ of smooth group schemes of finite type over a field with dim G=dim G′, the following are equivalent: f is flat; f maps the identity component G⁰ onto G′⁰; ker f is finite; f is quasi-finite; f is finite.

title: Differential criterion for étaleness between smooth schemes
description: Let f:X→Y be a morphism of S-schemes with X smooth over S at x and Y smooth over S at f(x). Then f is étale at x if and only if the canonical map (f*Ω¹_(Y/S))_x→(Ω¹_(X/S))_x is bijective.

title: Artinian local ring
description: A local ring (A,𝔪) is Artinian if it is Noetherian of Krull dimension zero; equivalently it has finite length as a module over itself, equivalently it is Noetherian and 𝔪ⁿ=0 for some n.

title: Versal formal deformation of a complete local algebra
description: Let k be a field and A a complete local Noetherian k-algebra with residue field k. A deformation of A over a local Artinian k-algebra B with residue field k is a flat B-algebra A_B with an isomorphism A_B⊗_B k≅A; it pulls back along local homomorphisms B→B′ by A_B⊗_B B′. A formal deformation over a complete local Noetherian k-algebra R with residue field k is a compatible family of deformations over the R/𝔪_Rⁿ. It is versal if, for every surjection B′→B of local Artinian k-algebras, every deformation over B′ whose restriction to B is pulled back along a local homomorphism R→B is pulled back along a local homomorphism R→B′ lifting it.

title: Elkik’s theorem on henselian versal deformations of isolated singularities
description: Let S be the spectrum of a henselian local ring and X₀ a scheme of finite type over its residue field, smooth outside a closed point x. Then X₀ at x has a henselian versal S-deformation, unique up to non-unique isomorphism; over a Noetherian S a henselian deformation is versal if and only if it induces a formal versal deformation over the completion of its base.

title: Chevalley’s theorem on subgroups as stabilizers of lines
description: For every algebraic subgroup H of an affine algebraic group G over a field k, there is a finite-dimensional algebraic representation V of G and a one-dimensional subspace L⊆V such that H is the stabilizer of L in G.

title: Flag variety of a finite-dimensional vector space
description: A flag in an n-dimensional vector space V over k is a chain 0=V₀⊊V₁⊊…⊊V_r=V of subspaces; it is maximal (complete) when r=n, so dim V_i=i. For fixed dimensions d₁<…<d_r=n the flags form the flag variety, the closed subvariety of the product of Grassmannians Gr(d₁,V)×…×Gr(d_r,V) cut out by the inclusions V_i⊆V_{i+1}. It is projective, and GL_V acts transitively on it, identifying it with GL_V/B(F) for the stabilizer B(F) of one such flag F.

title: Lie–Kolchin theorem
description: A smooth connected solvable affine algebraic group G over an algebraically closed field is trigonalizable: every finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G stabilizes a maximal flag, i.e. has a basis in which G acts by upper triangular matrices.

title: Closed orbit lemma for algebraic group actions
description: Let a smooth algebraic group G act on an algebraic variety X over an algebraically closed field. Every orbit is open in its closure, and the complement of an orbit in its closure is a union of orbits of strictly smaller dimension. In particular, every orbit of minimum dimension is closed.

title: Dimension formula for quotients of algebraic groups
description: For an algebraic subgroup H of an algebraic group G over a field, the quotient G/H satisfies dim G = dim H + dim G/H.

title: Closed immersions are proper
description: Every closed immersion of schemes is proper. Consequently a closed subscheme of a scheme proper over a base is proper over that base; in particular closed subschemes of complete schemes over a field are complete.

title: Borel fixed point theorem
description: Let G be a smooth connected solvable algebraic group over a field k acting on a nonempty complete algebraic scheme X. Then G has a fixed point in X(k̄); over an algebraically closed field, there is a k-point fixed by G.

title: Weierstrass equation and its invariants
description: A Weierstrass equation over a commutative ring R is y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆ with a_i∈R. Its invariants are b₂=a₁²+4a₂, b₄=a₁a₃+2a₄, b₆=a₃²+4a₆, b₈=a₁²a₆+4a₂a₆−a₁a₃a₄+a₂a₃²−a₄², c₄=b₂²−24b₄, c₆=−b₂³+36b₂b₄−216b₆ and the discriminant Δ=−b₂²b₈−8b₄³−27b₆²+9b₂b₄b₆, with j=c₄³/Δ when Δ is invertible. The substitution x=u²x′+r, y=u³y′+su²x′+t with u a unit and r,s,t∈R gives a Weierstrass equation with u⁴c₄′=c₄, u⁶c₆′=c₆ and u¹²Δ′=Δ. Over a field the projective cubic of the equation is nonsingular exactly when Δ≠0, and the isomorphisms between the resulting elliptic curves carrying O=[0:1:0] to O are exactly these substitutions.

title: Tate curve over a p-adic field
description: For a p-adic field K (a finite extension of ℚ_p) and q∈K^× with |q|<1, put s_k(q)=∑_{n≥1}n^kqⁿ/(1−qⁿ), a₄(q)=−5s₃(q) and a₆(q)=−(5s₃(q)+7s₅(q))/12. These are power series in q with integer coefficients, so they converge in K. The Tate curve E_q is the Weierstrass equation y²+xy=x³+a₄(q)x+a₆(q) over K.

title: Dedekind zeta function of a number field
description: For a number field K, ζ_K(s)=∑_𝔞N(𝔞)^{−s}, summed over the nonzero ideals 𝔞 of its ring of integers O_K with N(𝔞)=|O_K/𝔞|. It converges absolutely for real s>1 (indeed for Re s>1) and has the Euler product ζ_K(s)=∏_𝔭(1−N(𝔭)^{−s})^{−1} over the nonzero prime ideals; for K=ℚ it is the Riemann zeta function.

title: Analytic class number formula for a number field
description: For a number field K of degree n=r₁+2r₂ with r₁ real and r₂ pairs of complex embeddings, class number h, regulator R, discriminant D and w roots of unity, lim_{s→1+}(s−1)ζ_K(s)=2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂}hR/(w√|D|). For an imaginary quadratic field this reads lim_{s→1+}(s−1)ζ_K(s)=2πh/(w√|D|).

title: Decomposition of rational primes in a quadratic field
description: Let K be a quadratic field with discriminant D and quadratic character χ=χ_D. A rational prime p splits as pO_K=𝔭𝔭′ with 𝔭≠𝔭′ and N𝔭=N𝔭′=p if χ(p)=1, remains prime with norm p² if χ(p)=−1, and ramifies as pO_K=𝔭² with N𝔭=p if χ(p)=0, i.e. p∣D. Consequently ζ_K(s)=ζ(s)L(s,χ_D).

title: Value at s=1 of the L-function of a primitive Dirichlet character
description: Let χ be a primitive Dirichlet character of modulus m>1 with Gauss sum τ(χ)=∑_{x mod m}χ(x)e^{2πix/m}. If χ is even, L(1,χ)=−(τ(χ)/m)∑_{0<x<m}χ̄(x)log sin(πx/m); if χ is odd, L(1,χ)=(πiτ(χ)/m²)∑_{0<x<m}χ̄(x)x.

title: Analytic uniformization of the Tate curve
description: Let K be a p-adic field and q∈K^× with |q|<1. The Tate curve E_q is an elliptic curve over K with discriminant Δ=q∏_{n≥1}(1−qⁿ)²⁴ and j-invariant j(E_q)=1/q+744+196884q+⋯, a power series with integer coefficients. Convergent series X(u,q), Y(u,q) define a surjective homomorphism φ:K̄^×→E_q(K̄) with kernel q^ℤ that commutes with the action of Gal(K̄/K); hence E_q(L)≅L^×/q^ℤ for every algebraic extension L/K.

title: Compositional inverse of a formal power series
description: Let R be a commutative ring and f(T)=a₁T+a₂T²+⋯∈R[[T]] with a₁ a unit of R. There is a unique g(T)=a₁⁻¹T+⋯∈R[[T]] with f(g(T))=T, and then also g(f(T))=T.

title: Twisting invariant γ=−c₄/c₆ of an elliptic curve
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a field K of characteristic different from 2 and 3 with j(E)≠0,1728. Then γ(E/K)=−c₄/c₆∈K^×/(K^×)² is independent of the Weierstrass equation. Another such E′ is isomorphic to E over K if and only if j(E′)=j(E) and γ(E′/K)=γ(E/K); if j(E′)=j(E) but the γ differ, E′ is the quadratic twist of E by L=K(√(γ(E/K)/γ(E′/K))), via an isomorphism ψ with ψ(P^σ)=χ(σ)ψ(P)^σ for the quadratic character χ of L/K.

title: Discriminant and c₄ criterion for the reduction type
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a nonarchimedean local field given by a minimal Weierstrass equation. Then E has good reduction if and only if v(Δ)=0, multiplicative reduction if and only if v(Δ)>0 and v(c₄)=0, and additive reduction if and only if v(Δ)>0 and v(c₄)>0.

title: Minimal proper regular model of an elliptic curve
description: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and E an elliptic curve over K. A proper regular model of E is a regular integral scheme 𝒞, proper and flat over R, with generic fibre isomorphic to E. It is minimal if its special fibre contains no exceptional curve (a smooth rational component of self-intersection −1) that can be blown down. Such a model exists and is unique up to unique isomorphism; its smooth locus over R is the Néron model of E.

title: Direct limit of a directed system of modules
description: For a directed set I, a directed system of modules over a commutative ring R consists of R-modules M_i and homomorphisms φ_ji:M_i→M_j for i≤j with φ_ii=id and φ_kj∘φ_ji=φ_ki. Its direct limit lim→M_i is the set of pairs (i,x), x∈M_i, modulo (i,x)∼(j,y) when φ_ki(x)=φ_kj(y) for some k≥i,j, with operations computed in a common M_k. With the induced maps M_i→lim→M_i it is universal among compatible families of homomorphisms into a fixed module. Every element comes from some M_i, and x∈M_i maps to 0 exactly when φ_ki(x)=0 for some k≥i. Abelian groups are the case R=ℤ.

title: Classification of the places of a number field
description: For a number field K, the nonarchimedean places correspond bijectively to the nonzero prime ideals 𝔭 of O_K, the place of 𝔭 being represented by |x|_𝔭=N(𝔭)^(−ord_𝔭(x)); the archimedean places correspond to the real embeddings K→ℝ and to the pairs of complex-conjugate embeddings K→ℂ. Thus K has r₁+r₂ archimedean places.

title: Open normal subgroups of a profinite group form a basis at the identity
description: In a profinite group G the open normal subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of the identity, and each of them has finite index in G.

title: Petersson adjoints of the Hecke and diamond operators
description: On the space S_k(Γ₁(N)) of weight-k cusp forms with the Petersson inner product, for every prime p∤N the diamond operator ⟨p⟩ and the Hecke operator T_p have adjoints ⟨p⟩*=⟨p⟩⁻¹ and T_p*=⟨p⟩⁻¹T_p. Hence the operators ⟨n⟩ and T_n with (n,N)=1 are normal.

title: Power-bounded operator
description: A bounded linear operator T on a normed space is power-bounded if its powers are uniformly bounded in operator norm: sup_{n≥0}‖Tⁿ‖<∞, with T⁰ the identity.

title: Hennion's quasi-compactness theorem for Doeblin–Fortet operators
description: Let T be a bounded operator on a complex Banach space (L,‖·‖) with spectral radius ρ(T), and let |·| be a norm on L such that T is compact from (L,‖·‖) to (L,|·|). If for every n≥1 there are R_n,r_n≥0 with ‖Tⁿf‖≤R_n|f|+r_n‖f‖ for all f∈L, and r=liminf_n r_n^{1/n}<ρ(T), then T is quasi-compact and its essential spectral radius is at most r. This strengthens the Ionescu Tulcea–Marinescu theorem.

title: Essential spectral radius of the Banach-space adjoint
description: For a bounded operator Q on a complex Banach space B and its adjoint Q′ on the dual space B*, the essential spectral radii agree: r_ess(Q′)=r_ess(Q). Since Q and Q′ also have the same spectral radius, Q is quasi-compact exactly when Q′ is.

title: Dual of a normed vector lattice
description: The dual E′ of a normed vector lattice E, ordered by φ≥0 when φ(f)≥0 for all f≥0, is an order complete Banach lattice under the dual norm. The modulus of φ is given on positive elements by |φ|(f)=sup{|φ(g)|:|g|≤f}, so |φ(g)|≤|φ|(|g|) and ‖|φ|‖=‖φ‖.

title: Peripheral decomposition of a quasi-compact Markov kernel on a weighted-supremum space
description: Let P be a Markov kernel with Pw/w bounded for a weight w≥1. If P is quasi-compact on B_w, then r(P)=1 and P=L+N with LN=NL=0, r(N)<1 and Lf=∑_{k=1}^sλ_kφ_k(f)f_k, where |λ_k|=1, the f_k are bounded measurable eigenfunctions (Pf_k=λ_kf_k), the φ_k are complex measures with ∫w d|φ_k|<∞, and φ_j(f_k)=δ_{jk}. In particular P is power-bounded on B_w.

title: Range of a positive projection on a Banach lattice
description: If P is a positive projection on a Banach lattice E, its range PE, ordered by the cone E₊∩PE, is a vector lattice with sup_{PE}(x,y)=P(x∨y), and a Banach lattice under a norm equivalent to the norm of E. If P is strictly positive, PE is a vector sublattice of E.

title: Classification of finite-dimensional Archimedean vector lattices
description: A real vector lattice of finite dimension n≥1 is Archimedean if and only if it is lattice isomorphic to ℝⁿ with the coordinatewise order; equivalently it has a basis of pairwise disjoint positive elements whose coordinate functionals are positive.

title: Separation of points and tangents by meromorphic functions on a compact Riemann surface
description: On every compact Riemann surface X the field M(X) of global meromorphic functions separates points and tangents: for distinct p,q∈X some f∈M(X) has f(p)≠f(q) (poles allowed), and for every p some f∈M(X) has multiplicity one at p, i.e. f−f(p) has a simple zero or f has a simple pole there. In particular X has nonconstant meromorphic functions.

title: Riemann–Roch theorem for compact Riemann surfaces
description: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g, K the divisor of a nonzero meromorphic 1-form and L(D)={f∈M(X): f=0 or div f+D≥0} for a divisor D. Then dim L(D)−dim L(K−D)=deg D+1−g. In particular dim L(D)=deg D+1−g when deg D>2g−2.

title: Very ampleness of divisors of degree at least 2g+1 on a compact Riemann surface
description: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g and D a divisor with deg D≥2g+1. Then the complete linear system |D| has no base points and the map φ_D:X→Pⁿ given by a basis of L(D) is a holomorphic embedding onto a smooth projective curve of degree deg D. Hence every compact Riemann surface embeds holomorphically into projective space.

title: Chow’s theorem on analytic subsets of projective space
description: Every closed complex-analytic subset of complex projective space Pⁿ(ℂ) is algebraic, i.e. the zero set of finitely many homogeneous polynomials. Consequently every compact analytic subset of a complex algebraic variety is Zariski closed.

title: Regularity of holomorphic maps between complex algebraic varieties
description: Every holomorphic map from a complete (compact) complex algebraic variety X to a complex algebraic variety Y is a regular map, i.e. a morphism of varieties. Consequently a compact complex-analytic space carries at most one structure of algebraic variety.

title: Comparison of algebraic and analytic local rings of a complex variety
description: For a complex algebraic variety X and a point x, the inclusion of the local ring O_{X,x} into the ring of germs of holomorphic functions at x induces an isomorphism of their completions. Hence both rings have the same dimension, and X is nonsingular at x exactly when the analytic space X^h is a complex manifold near x.

title: Weierstrass division theorem for power series over a complete discrete valuation ring
description: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 and f=∑a_iT^i∈O[[T]] with a_i∈𝔪 for i<n and a_n a unit. Every g∈O[[T]] can be written uniquely as g=qf+r with q∈O[[T]] and r∈O[T] a polynomial of degree at most n−1.

title: Landau’s determination of h(−4n)=1
description: For a positive integer n, every primitive positive definite binary quadratic form of discriminant −4n is properly equivalent to x²+ny², i.e. the form class number h(−4n) equals 1, if and only if n=1, 2, 3, 4 or 7.

title: Number of genera of binary quadratic forms
description: For a negative integer D≡0,1 mod 4, the primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant D fall into 2^(μ−1) genera, where μ is the number of assigned characters (for D≡1 mod 4, the number of odd primes dividing D); the principal genus consists of the squares in the form class group C(D).

title: Reduction theory of positive definite binary quadratic forms
description: Every primitive positive definite binary quadratic form is properly equivalent to a unique reduced form ax²+bxy+cy², meaning |b|≤a≤c with b≥0 whenever |b|=a or a=c. Hence the form class number h(D) is the number of reduced forms of discriminant D, and it is finite.

title: Form class group and ideal class group of an imaginary quadratic order
description: Let O be the order of discriminant D<0 in an imaginary quadratic field. Sending a primitive positive definite form ax²+bxy+cy² of discriminant D to the lattice [a,(−b+√D)/2] induces an isomorphism from the form class group C(D) onto the group of proper fractional O-ideals modulo principal ideals; in particular h(D)=h(O).

title: Class number formula for an imaginary quadratic order
description: Let O be the order of conductor f in an imaginary quadratic field K of discriminant d_K. Then h(O)=h(O_K)·f/[O_K×:O×]·∏_(p|f)(1−(d_K/p)/p), with (d_K/p) the Kronecker symbol; in particular h(O) is a multiple of h(O_K).

title: Singular j-invariants generate ring class fields
description: Let O be an order in an imaginary quadratic field K⊂ℂ and 𝔞 a proper fractional O-ideal. Then j(𝔞) is an algebraic integer and K(j(𝔞)) is the ring class field of O, so [K(j(𝔞)):K]=h(O).

title: Weber modular functions
description: With q=e^(2πiτ) for τ in the upper half-plane, Weber’s functions are f(τ)=q^(−1/48)∏_(n≥1)(1+q^(n−1/2)), f₁(τ)=q^(−1/48)∏(1−q^(n−1/2)) and f₂(τ)=√2·q^(1/24)∏(1+qⁿ). They satisfy f(τ)f₁(τ)f₂(τ)=√2 and f₁(2τ)f₂(τ)=√2, and γ₂(τ)=(f(τ)²⁴−16)/f(τ)⁸ is the cube root of j(τ) that is real on the imaginary axis.

title: Weber’s theorem on the cube root of a singular j-invariant
description: Let O be an order of discriminant D in an imaginary quadratic field K with 3∤D, and write O=[1,τ₀] with τ₀=√−m if D=−4m and τ₀=(3+√−m)/2 if D=−m≡1 mod 4. Then γ₂(τ₀), the cube root of j(τ₀) real on the imaginary axis, is an algebraic integer, K(γ₂(τ₀)) is the ring class field of O, and ℚ(γ₂(τ₀))=ℚ(j(τ₀)).

title: Weber function values generating ring class fields
description: Let m be a positive integer not divisible by 3 and O=ℤ[√−m]⊂K=ℚ(√−m). If m≡6 mod 8, then f₁(√−m)² is an algebraic integer generating the ring class field of O over K; if m≡3 mod 4, the same holds for f(√−m)², where f, f₁ are Weber’s functions.

title: Euler’s theorem on y²=x³+1
description: The only rational solutions of y²=x³+1 are (x,y)=(−1,0), (0,±1) and (2,±3). Euler proved this in 1738 by Fermat’s method of infinite descent.

title: Rank formula for descent via a rational 2-isogeny
description: Let E:y²=x(x²+ax+b) over ℚ with a,b∈ℤ and b(a²−4b)≠0, and let E′:y²=x(x²−2ax+a²−4b) be its quotient by the 2-torsion point (0,0). The map α:E(ℚ)→ℚ×/ℚ×² with α(O)=1, α(0,0)=b and α(x,y)=x otherwise is a homomorphism with finite image; with α′ defined likewise on E′(ℚ), |α(E(ℚ))|·|α′(E′(ℚ))|=2^(r+2), where r is the Mordell–Weil rank of E.

title: Mazur’s rank-zero theorem for prime-conductor curves with rational torsion
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over ℚ of prime conductor with a ℚ-rational point of prime order p∈{2,3,5}. Then E(ℚ) has rank zero, and the p-primary part of the Tate–Shafarevich group of E is trivial.

title: Order of the cuspidal divisor class on X₀(p)
description: For a prime p, the two cusps 0 and ∞ of X₀(p) are rational over ℚ, and the class of the degree-zero divisor (0)−(∞) in the Jacobian J₀(p) has order n, the numerator of (p−1)/12 written in lowest terms (Ogg).

title: Hyperelliptic involution of a genus-two curve
description: A smooth projective curve G of genus two over a field k has a unique involution S, defined over k, whose quotient G/S has genus zero; it is induced by the canonical linear system and therefore commutes with every automorphism of G. In characteristic other than two, S has exactly six geometric fixed points.

title: Integral implicit function theorem over a complete nonarchimedean field
description: Let K be complete for a discrete nonarchimedean absolute value, with valuation ring O and uniformizer π. If F∈O[[x,y]]^m, F(0,0)=0 and det(∂F/∂y)(0,0) is a unit of O, the formal solution y=f(x) of F(x,f(x))=0 with f(0)=0 has coefficients in O.
