description: Every Siegel modular form of weight 0 for the full modular group Sp₂ₙ(ℤ), n≥1, is a constant function on the Siegel upper half-space.

title: Z_l-extensions are unramified outside l
description: Every ℤ_ℓ-extension of a number field K is unramified at all finite places of K not dividing ℓ and at all infinite places; in particular it lies in the maximal abelian pro-ℓ extension of K unramified outside ℓ.

title: Galois group of the maximal abelian l-ramified pro-l extension over the l-Hilbert class field
description: For a number field K and a prime ℓ, let M be the maximal abelian pro-ℓ extension of K unramified outside ℓ and H its maximal unramified abelian ℓ-extension. Class field theory gives Gal(M/H)≅U_K/s_K(E_K), where U_K=∏_{𝔩|ℓ}U¹_{K_𝔩} is the product of local principal units above ℓ, E_K=ℤ_ℓ⊗O_K× and s_K is the diagonal (semi-localization) map.

title: Structure of the principal units of a p-adic field
description: For a finite extension F/ℚ_p, the group U¹_F=1+𝔪_F of principal units is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module isomorphic to μ_{p^∞}(F)×ℤ_p^([F:ℚ_p]), where μ_{p^∞}(F) is the finite group of p-power roots of unity in F.

title: Accessible stopping time
description: A stopping time T is accessible if there are predictable stopping times T₁,T₂,… whose graphs cover its graph {(T(ω),ω):T(ω)<∞} up to an evanescent set; that is, almost surely T∈{T₁,T₂,…} on {T<∞}.

title: Functional monotone class theorem
description: Let 𝒜 be a π-system on a set E and H a vector space of bounded real functions on E containing the constant 1 and the indicators of members of 𝒜, such that the limit of every uniformly bounded increasing sequence of nonnegative members of H is in H. Then H contains every bounded σ(𝒜)-measurable real function.

title: Generators of the predictable σ-algebra
description: On a filtered probability space the predictable σ-algebra on [0,∞)×Ω, generated by the adapted left-continuous processes, is also generated by the predictable rectangles {0}×A with A∈F₀ and (t,∞)×A with t≥0 and A∈F_t; equivalently by the continuous adapted processes, or by the stochastic intervals [τ,∞) of predictable stopping times τ.

title: Strict past of a predictable time generated by an announcing sequence
description: If stopping times τ_n≤τ converge to τ with τ_n<τ whenever 0<τ<∞, in particular if (τ_n) announces a predictable stopping time τ, then F_(τ−) is the σ-algebra generated by ⋃_nF_(τ_n), and also the one generated by ⋃_nF_(τ_n−).

title: Predictable projection of a measurable process
description: On a complete filtered probability space, a measurable process X with E[1_(τ<∞)|X_τ||F_(τ−)] almost surely finite for every predictable stopping time τ has a predictable projection: the predictable process ᵖX, unique up to evanescence, with ᵖX_τ1_(τ<∞)=E[X_τ1_(τ<∞)|F_(τ−)] almost surely for every predictable stopping time τ.

title: Jacobi polynomial
description: For real α,β>−1 and an integer n≥0, P_n^{(α,β)}(x)=((α+1)_n/n!)∑_{k=0}^{n}(−n)_k(n+α+β+1)_k/(k!(α+1)_k)·((1−x)/2)^k, a real polynomial of degree n, where (a)_k is the rising factorial.

title: Rodrigues formula for Jacobi polynomials
Gegenbauer polynomials as symmetric Jacobi polynomials
description: For λ>0 and n≥0, C_n^λ(x)=((2λ)_n/(λ+1/2)_n)P_n^{(λ−1/2,λ−1/2)}(x): with this normalization the symmetric Jacobi polynomials have generating function (1−2xt+t²)^{−λ}.

title: Orthogonality of Gegenbauer polynomials
description: For λ>0, ∫_{−1}^{1}C_m^λ(x)C_n^λ(x)(1−x²)^{λ−1/2}dx=0 when m≠n, and for m=n it equals √π(2λ)_nΓ(λ+1/2)/(n!(n+λ)Γ(λ)).

title: Integration of zonal functions over the sphere
description: For d≥2, a point p of S^{d−1} and a bounded Lebesgue integrable Φ on [−1,1], u↦Φ(u·p) is integrable for spherical area σ and ∫Φ(u·p)dσ(u)=|S^{d−2}|∫_{−1}^{1}Φ(t)(1−t²)^{(d−3)/2}dt; moreover {u:u·p∈N} is σ-null for every Lebesgue-null N⊆[−1,1].

title: Binomial series for a real exponent
description: For a real number a and real x with |x|<1, (1−x)^{−a}=∑_{n≥0}(a)_n xⁿ/n!, the series converging absolutely, where (a)_n is the rising factorial.

title: Nonexpansiveness of the metric projection onto a closed convex set
description: For a nonempty closed convex set A⊆ℝⁿ, the nearest-point map p(A,·) is 1-Lipschitz: |p(A,x)−p(A,y)|≤|x−y| for all x,y∈ℝⁿ.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the maximal-volume ellipsoid in a convex body
description: Every convex body K⊂ℝⁿ contains an ellipsoid whose volume is maximal among all ellipsoids contained in K, and any two such maximal ellipsoids coincide.

title: Minkowski’s determinant inequality
description: For positive definite real symmetric n×n matrices A and B, det(A+B)^{1/n}≥det(A)^{1/n}+det(B)^{1/n}, with equality exactly when A and B are proportional; equivalently det((1−λ)A+λB)≥det(A)^{1−λ}det(B)^λ for 0≤λ≤1, with equality for 0<λ<1 only if A=B.

title: Polar of a subset of Euclidean space
description: For A⊆ℝⁿ, its polar is A°={y∈ℝⁿ:⟨x,y⟩≤1 for every x∈A}; it is a closed convex set containing the origin.

title: Bipolar theorem in Euclidean space
description: If A⊆ℝⁿ is closed, convex and contains the origin, then (A°)°=A; equivalently a∈A exactly when ⟨y,a⟩≤1 for every y∈A°.

title: Fritz John’s multiplier rule for infinitely many inequality constraints
description: Let F be C¹ on an open U⊆ℝᴺ, S a compact metric space and G:U×S→ℝ continuous with ∇_uG(u,s) existing and continuous in (u,s). If u₀ maximizes F on {u∈U:G(u,s)≤0 for all s∈S}, then ∇F(u₀)=0 or there are s₁,…,s_m∈S with m≤N, G(u₀,s_i)=0 and λ_i≥0 such that ∇F(u₀)=∑λ_i∇_uG(u₀,s_i).

title: Successive minima of a symmetric convex body
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ symmetric about the origin and 1≤i≤n, the i-th successive minimum λ_i(K) is the least λ>0 such that λK contains i linearly independent points of ℤⁿ, so 0<λ₁≤⋯≤λ_n; the integer lattice may be replaced by any full lattice.

title: Minkowski’s second theorem on successive minima
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ symmetric about the origin with successive minima λ₁,…,λ_n relative to ℤⁿ, 2ⁿ/n!≤λ₁λ₂⋯λ_n·vol(K)≤2ⁿ.

title: Davenport’s lemma on rescaled parallelepipeds
description: Let L₁,…,L_n be real linear forms of determinant 1 and λ₁,…,λ_n the successive minima of the parallelepiped |L_i(x)|≤1. If ρ₁≥⋯≥ρ_n>0, ρ₁λ₁≤⋯≤ρ_nλ_n and ρ₁⋯ρ_n=1, then after a permutation of the forms the parallelepiped |ρ_iL_i(x)|≤1 has successive minima λ′_i with c₁(n)λ_iρ_i≤λ′_i≤c₂(n)λ_iρ_i for every i.

title: Mahler’s theorem on successive minima of reciprocal parallelepipeds
description: If Π is the parallelepiped |L_i(x)|≤1 given by n independent real linear forms and Π* is the reciprocal (polar) parallelepiped given by the dual forms, then their successive minima satisfy c₁(n)≤λ_jλ*_{n+1−j}≤c₂(n) for j=1,…,n, with constants depending only on n.

title: Mahler’s theorem on successive minima of compound parallelepipeds
description: Let Π be a parallelepiped in ℝⁿ given by n independent linear forms, with successive minima λ₁,…,λ_n, and 1≤p≤n. Its p-th compound (pseudocompound) parallelepiped in Λ^pℝⁿ≅ℝ^ℓ, ℓ=C(n,p), has successive minima ν₁≤⋯≤ν_ℓ comparable, up to constants depending only on n, to the products λ_{i₁}⋯λ_{i_p} over p-element index sets arranged in increasing order.

title: Siegel’s lemma
description: If M<N and L₁,…,L_M are linear forms in N variables with integer coefficients of absolute value at most A≥1, then the system L₁(z)=⋯=L_M(z)=0 has a nonzero integer solution z with max_k|z_k|≤(NA)^{M/(N−M)}.

title: Index of a multivariate polynomial at a point with respect to weights
description: For a nonzero P∈ℝ[X₁,…,X_m], a point α∈ℝᵐ and positive integers r₁,…,r_m, the index of P at α relative to (r₁,…,r_m) is the least value of i₁/r₁+⋯+i_m/r_m over multi-indices with ∂^{i₁+⋯+i_m}P/∂X₁^{i₁}⋯∂X_m^{i_m}(α)≠0; the zero polynomial has index +∞. Schmidt’s variant replaces α by blocks of linear forms.

title: Roth’s lemma on the index at rational points
description: Let m≥1, 0<ε<1/12 and ω=24·2^{−m}(ε/12)^{2^{m−1}}. Suppose positive integers r₁,…,r_m satisfy ωr_h≥r_{h+1}, and coprime pairs (p_h,q_h) with q_h>0 satisfy q_h^{r_h}≥q₁^{r₁} and q_h≥2^{3m/ω}. Then every nonzero integer polynomial P of degree at most r_h in X_h with coefficients of absolute value at most q₁^{ωr₁} has index less than ε at (p₁/q₁,…,p_m/q_m) relative to (r₁,…,r_m).

title: Topological generating set of a topological group
description: A subset X of a topological group G topologically generates G if the subgroup generated by X is dense in G. G is topologically finitely generated if some finite subset topologically generates it.

title: Frattini subgroup of a profinite group
description: For a profinite group G, the Frattini subgroup Φ(G) is the intersection of all maximal open subgroups of G, the proper open subgroups contained in no larger proper open subgroup (Φ(G)=G if G is trivial). It is a closed normal subgroup, and G/Φ(G) is the Frattini quotient of G.

title: p-adic powers of an element of a pro-p group
description: For a pro-p group Π, an element π∈Π and a∈ℤ_p, the power π^a is the limit of the integer powers π^(a_n) for any integers a_n converging to a in ℤ_p. It is well defined, lies in the closure of the cyclic subgroup generated by π, and satisfies π^(a+b)=π^aπ^b and (π^a)^b=π^(ab).

title: Reduced row echelon form of a matrix
description: A matrix over a field is in reduced row echelon form if its zero rows come last, the leading (leftmost nonzero) entry of each nonzero row lies strictly to the right of the leading entry of the row above, every leading entry equals 1, and each leading 1 is the only nonzero entry of its column.

title: Degree and leading coefficient of a polynomial
description: For a nonzero polynomial f=a₀+a₁X+⋯+a_nX^n over a commutative ring with a_n≠0, the degree deg f is n and the leading coefficient is a_n. By convention the zero polynomial has degree −∞.

title: Monic polynomial over a commutative ring
description: A polynomial over a commutative ring is monic if it is nonzero and its leading coefficient, the coefficient of its highest-degree term, equals 1.

title: Simple group
description: A group is simple if it is nontrivial and its only normal subgroups are the trivial subgroup and the whole group.

title: Perfect group
description: A group G is perfect if it equals its commutator subgroup [G,G]; equivalently, G has no nontrivial abelian quotient.

title: Projective special linear group over a field
description: For a field F and n≥1, PSL_n(F)=SL_n(F)/Z, where Z=SL_n(F)∩F^×I is the group of scalar matrices of determinant 1, which is the centre of SL_n(F).

title: Finiteness of open subgroups of given index in a finitely generated profinite group
description: Let G be a topologically finitely generated profinite group. For each n there are only finitely many open subgroups of index n in G; consequently the identity has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods consisting of a descending chain of open characteristic subgroups.

title: Frattini subgroup of a pro-p group from p-th powers and commutators
description: For a pro-p group G, every maximal closed subgroup is open, normal and of index p, the Frattini quotient G/Φ(G) is an elementary abelian p-group, and Φ(G) is the closed subgroup G^p[G,G] generated by the p-th powers and the commutators.

title: Nontrivial normal subgroups of a finite p-group meet the centre
description: Let P be a finite p-group and N a nontrivial normal subgroup of P. Then N contains a nontrivial element of the centre of P. In particular a nontrivial finite p-group has nontrivial centre.

title: Schur–Zassenhaus theorem for finite groups
description: Let N be a normal subgroup of a finite group G whose order is coprime to its index. Then N has a complement H in G, a subgroup with N∩H=1 and NH=G, and any two complements are conjugate in G. Conjugacy is classically proved when N or G/N is solvable, and in general follows from the Feit–Thompson theorem.

title: Nonemptiness of inverse limits of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces
description: The inverse limit of an inverse system of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces and continuous maps, indexed by a directed set, is nonempty. In particular an inverse limit of nonempty finite sets over a directed set is nonempty.

title: Schur’s lemma for simple objects of an abelian category
description: In an abelian category every nonzero morphism between simple objects is an isomorphism. Hence morphisms between nonisomorphic simple objects are zero and the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division ring.

title: Isomorphism theorems for subobjects in an abelian category
description: Let X be an object of an abelian category. For subobjects A and B of X, (A+B)/A≅B/(A∩B). For subobjects A⊆B⊆X, (X/A)/(B/A)≅X/B, and the subobjects of X/A correspond bijectively to the subobjects of X containing A.

title: Left modules over a ring form an abelian category
description: For a ring R, the category of left R-modules and R-linear maps is abelian: it is additive, kernels and cokernels are the usual submodule and quotient module, and every injective (surjective) homomorphism is the kernel (cokernel) of its cokernel (kernel).

title: Iwasawa’s simplicity criterion
description: Let a perfect group G act doubly transitively on a set X, and suppose the stabilizer of some point has an abelian normal subgroup whose conjugates in G generate G. Then G/K is simple, where K is the kernel of the action.

title: Doubly transitive group action
description: An action of a group G on a set X with at least two elements is doubly transitive if for any two ordered pairs (x₁,x₂) and (y₁,y₂) of distinct elements of X there is g∈G with gx₁=y₁ and gx₂=y₂.

title: Generation of SL_n over a field by elementary transvections
description: For a field F and n≥2, the group SL_n(F) is generated by the elementary transvections I+λE_ij with i≠j and λ∈F, where E_ij is the matrix unit.

title: Serre’s ℓ-adic openness theorem for elliptic curves without complex multiplication
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K without complex multiplication over K̄. For every prime ℓ the image of Gal(K̄/K) in Aut(T_ℓE)≅GL₂(ℤ_ℓ) is open; equivalently its Lie algebra is all of End(V_ℓE). In particular this image is not abelian and V_ℓE is irreducible under every open subgroup of the Galois group.

title: Serre’s description of inertia on the p-torsion of an elliptic curve over an unramified p-adic field
description: Let K be a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p and E/K an elliptic curve with good or multiplicative reduction. For good ordinary (height one) or multiplicative reduction, inertia acts on E[p] by matrices (θ *; 0 1) with θ the level-one fundamental character, so its image has order p−1 or p(p−1). For good supersingular (height two) reduction, E[p] is a line over 𝔽_(p²) on which inertia acts by the level-two fundamental character; its image is a nonsplit Cartan subgroup of order p²−1.

title: Subgroups of GL₂(𝔽_p) containing a Cartan subgroup
description: Let p be prime and G a subgroup of GL₂(𝔽_p) containing a Cartan subgroup, or containing a half split Cartan subgroup (conjugate to the diagonal matrices diag(a,1)) with p≠5 in that case. Then G=GL₂(𝔽_p), or G lies in a Borel subgroup, or G lies in the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup.

title: Density zero of supersingular primes for a non-CM elliptic curve
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K without complex multiplication. The set of finite places of K where E has good supersingular reduction, i.e. reduction whose formal group has height two, has Dirichlet density zero.

title: Serre’s criterion for compatible systems with abelian reductions
description: Let (ρ_ℓ) be a system of semisimple ℓ-adic representations of a number field K that is rational and strictly compatible, with Frobenius polynomials in ℚ[t] independent of ℓ. Suppose that for infinitely many ℓ the semisimplified reduction of ρ_ℓ modulo ℓ is abelian and its characters, restricted to the local units at ℓ via class field theory, are products of conjugates of the inverse reduction map with exponents bounded by a fixed N. Then the system comes from a representation of one of Serre’s groups S_m over ℚ; in particular every ρ_ℓ is abelian.

title: Strict compatibility of the ℓ-adic representations of an elliptic curve
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K and v a finite place of good reduction with residue field k_v of Nv elements. For every prime ℓ not dividing Nv, the action on T_ℓE is unramified at v and Frobenius has characteristic polynomial T²−a_vT+Nv with a_v=Nv+1−#Ẽ_v(k_v)∈ℤ independent of ℓ. Thus (V_ℓE) is a strictly compatible system of rational ℓ-adic representations whose exceptional set is the set of places of bad reduction.

title: Local reciprocity and the fundamental characters of tame inertia
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of q elements and L/K an abelian tamely ramified extension. The local reciprocity map sends the units O_K^× onto the inertia group I(L/K), factoring through k^×, and the composite of the tame inertia group I_t→I(L/K) with this identification is the inverse of the fundamental character θ_(q−1):I_t→k^×: an element s acts as the reciprocity image of θ_(q−1)(s)^(−1).

title: Trace criterion for supersingular elliptic curves over finite fields
description: An elliptic curve over a finite field of characteristic p is supersingular, i.e. its formal group has height two, if and only if the trace of its Frobenius endomorphism is divisible by p. In particular an elliptic curve whose Frobenius trace is zero is supersingular.

title: Open mapping theorem for Banach spaces
description: A surjective bounded linear operator between Banach spaces maps open sets to open sets.

title: Continuity of linear operators between normed spaces
description: For a linear map T between normed spaces the following are equivalent: T is bounded; T is continuous; T is continuous at one point. A bounded T satisfies ‖Tx−Ty‖≤‖T‖‖x−y‖.

title: Riemann sphere
description: The extended complex plane Ĉ=ℂ∪{∞}, topologized as the one-point compactification of ℂ, with the coordinate w=1/z (1/∞=0) used near the point ∞.

title: Lévy–Prokhorov metric
description: For Borel probability measures μ,ν on a metric space, d_P(μ,ν)=inf{ε>0: μ(B)≤ν(B^ε)+ε and ν(B)≤μ(B^ε)+ε for every Borel set B}, where B^ε={x: d(x,B)<ε}. It is a metric on the Borel probability measures.

title: Alexandrov’s portmanteau theorem for nets of probability measures
description: For Borel probability measures on a metric space, a net μ_α converges to μ in the weak topology iff limsup μ_α(F)≤μ(F) for every closed F, iff liminf μ_α(G)≥μ(G) for every open G, iff μ_α(E)→μ(E) for every Borel E with μ(∂E)=0. Equivalently the sets {ν: ν(F_i)<μ(F_i)+ε, i≤n}, F_i closed, ε>0, form a neighbourhood base of μ.

title: Ranga Rao’s uniform convergence theorem for weakly convergent measures
description: If a net of Borel probability measures μ_α on a separable metric space converges weakly to μ, then ∫f dμ_α→∫f dμ uniformly over every uniformly bounded, pointwise equicontinuous family of bounded continuous real functions f.

title: Limit of a function at infinity
description: For a real- or complex-valued function f defined on a subset of ℝ that is unbounded above, lim_{x→∞}f(x)=L means that for every ε>0 there is M such that |f(x)−L|<ε for every x>M in the domain.

title: Dirichlet integral of sin x/x
description: The integrals S(T)=∫₀ᵀ(sin x)/x dx converge to π/2 as T→∞, so the improper integral ∫₀^∞(sin x)/x dx equals π/2, although sin x/x is not Lebesgue integrable on (0,∞); in particular S is bounded on [0,∞).

title: Equality case of Jensen’s inequality for strictly convex functions
description: If φ is strictly convex on an interval containing the values of an integrable real random variable X, φ(X) is integrable and Eφ(X)=φ(EX), then X is almost surely constant.

title: Conditional expectation of a variable independent of the σ-algebra
description: If an integrable random variable X is independent of a sub-σ-algebra G, then E[X|G]=E[X] almost surely.

title: Hausdorff spaces are characterized by a closed diagonal
description: A topological space X is Hausdorff if and only if its diagonal {(x,x):x∈X} is closed in X×X with the product topology.

title: Continuity of maps into a product space
description: A map f:Z→∏_iX_i into a product of topological spaces is continuous for the product topology if and only if every coordinate map π_i∘f is continuous; in particular f×g:X×Z→Y×W is continuous when f and g are.

title: Differentiability implies continuity for real functions
description: If a real function f is differentiable at a point x₀, then f is continuous at x₀.

title: Limit laws for sums, products and quotients of real functions
description: If lim_{x→x₀}f(x)=L₁ and lim_{x→x₀}g(x)=L₂ for real functions, then f+g, f−g and fg have limits L₁+L₂, L₁−L₂ and L₁L₂ at x₀, and f/g has limit L₁/L₂ when L₂≠0.

title: Chain rule for a holomorphic function along a differentiable path
description: If F is holomorphic on an open set G⊆ℂ and γ:[a,b]→G is differentiable at t, then F∘γ is differentiable at t with (F∘γ)′(t)=F′(γ(t))γ′(t).

title: Unordered sum of a family in a normed space
description: For a family (v_s)_{s∈S} in a normed space indexed by an arbitrary set, ∑_{s∈S}v_s=v means that for every ε>0 there is a finite F₀⊆S with ‖v−∑_{s∈F}v_s‖<ε for every finite F with F₀⊆F⊆S.

title: Orthonormal expansion with respect to an arbitrary orthonormal basis
description: If (e_s)_{s∈S} is an orthonormal basis of a Hilbert space H, indexed by an arbitrary set, then every h∈H satisfies h=∑_{s∈S}⟨h,e_s⟩e_s as an unordered norm-convergent sum and ‖h‖²=∑_{s∈S}|⟨h,e_s⟩|²; only countably many coefficients are nonzero.

title: Lebesgue measure as the restriction of Lebesgue outer measure
description: Every Lebesgue measurable set E⊆ℝⁿ satisfies m(E)=m*(E), where m* is Lebesgue outer measure; m* has the same value whether computed with countable covers by open boxes, closed boxes or closed cubes.

title: Outer unit normal of a Lipschitz domain
description: Let E⊂ℝⁿ be a Lipschitz domain and y∈∂E. If near y, after a rotation, E lies above the graph of a Lipschitz u:ℝⁿ⁻¹→ℝ with y=(z,u(z)) and u is differentiable at z, the outer unit normal is ν(y)=(∇u(z),−1)/√(1+|∇u(z)|²); it does not depend on the chosen graph representation.

title: Rademacher’s theorem on differentiability of Lipschitz maps
description: Every Lipschitz map f:ℝⁿ→ℝᵐ is (Fréchet) differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every point of ℝⁿ.

title: Area of the graph of a Lipschitz function
description: If u:ℝⁿ⁻¹→ℝ is Lipschitz, then for every Lebesgue measurable G⊆ℝⁿ⁻¹ the graph Γ(u;G)={(z,u(z)):z∈G} satisfies H^{n−1}(Γ(u;G))=∫_G√(1+|∇u(z)|²)dz, and H^{n−1} restricted to the graph of u is a Radon measure on ℝⁿ.

title: Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation theorem for Radon measures
description: If μ and ν are Radon measures on ℝⁿ, then D_μν(x)=lim_{r→0}ν(B(x,r))/μ(B(x,r)) exists for μ-almost every x, is locally μ-integrable, and ν=(D_μν)μ+ν^s with ν^s singular with respect to μ; the same holds componentwise for ℝᵐ-valued Radon measures ν.

title: Quasimartingale
description: An adapted càdlàg process X on [0,∞], with X_∞=0 if X is indexed by [0,∞), such that E|X_t|<∞ for all t and Var(X)=sup_τ E∑_i|E[X_{t_i}−X_{t_{i+1}}|F_{t_i}]|<∞, the supremum over finite subdivisions τ of [0,∞].

title: Quasimartingales as differences of positive supermartingales
description: A process X indexed by [0,∞) is a quasimartingale if and only if X=Y−Z for positive right-continuous supermartingales Y and Z.

title: Hausdorff maximality theorem
description: Every nonempty partially ordered set contains a maximal totally ordered subset (a chain not properly contained in any other chain). It is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to Zorn’s lemma.

title: Density of differences of support functions on the sphere
description: Every twice continuously differentiable function f on S^{n−1} can be written f=h_K−h_{rBⁿ} on S^{n−1} for a convex body K and some r>0. Consequently the linear span of support functions of convex bodies, restricted to S^{n−1}, is dense in C(S^{n−1}) for the maximum norm.

title: Modulus of continuity of a function on a metric space
description: For a real function f on a metric space (G,d) and t>0, ω(t,f)=sup{|f(x)−f(y)|: d(x,y)≤t}. It is nondecreasing in t, and f is uniformly continuous exactly when ω(t,f)→0 as t→0; a λ-Lipschitz f has ω(t,f)≤λt.

title: Positive linear operator on a space of continuous functions
description: A linear operator A from the real continuous functions C(G) on a compact space G to C(G) is positive if f≥0 on G implies Af≥0 on G. For each point x, f↦(Af)(x) is then a positive linear functional.

title: Gauss quadrature for a positive measure on an interval
description: Let μ be a positive Borel measure on [−1,1] whose support has at least m+1 points, and p_{m+1} its orthogonal polynomial of degree m+1. Then p_{m+1} has m+1 simple zeros λ_1<…<λ_{m+1} in (−1,1), and there are positive weights (Christoffel or Cotes numbers) c_i with ∫P dμ=∑c_iP(λ_i) for every real polynomial P of degree at most 2m+1.

title: Bruns’ inequality for the zeros of Legendre polynomials
description: Write the zeros of the Legendre polynomial P_n as cos θ_1>…>cos θ_n with 0<θ_1<…<θ_n<π. Then (ν−1/2)π/(n+1/2)<θ_ν<νπ/(n+1/2) for ν=1,…,n; in particular the ν largest zeros exceed cos(νπ/(n+1/2)).

title: Khintchine inequality
description: For independent Rademacher signs ε_1,…,ε_n, real a_1,…,a_n and 0<p<∞, A_p(∑a_i²)^{1/2}≤(E|∑ε_ia_i|^p)^{1/p}≤B_p(∑a_i²)^{1/2} with constants depending only on p; B_p≤C√p for p≥2, so ∑ε_ia_i has ψ₂ norm at most an absolute multiple of (∑a_i²)^{1/2}.

title: ψ_α Orlicz norm of a random variable
description: For α>0 and a real random variable X, ‖X‖_{ψ_α}=inf{λ>0: E exp(|X/λ|^α)≤2} (a quasi-norm for α<1). Up to constants depending on α it is equivalent to sup_{p≥1}p^{−1/α}(E|X|^p)^{1/p} and to the tail bound P(|X|>t)≤2exp(−ct^α/‖X‖_{ψ_α}^α); ψ₂ variables are subgaussian and ψ₁ variables subexponential.

title: Expected maximum of ψ₂ random variables
description: If X_1,…,X_N (N≥2) are random variables, not necessarily independent, with ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}≤K, then E max_i|X_i|≤CK√(log N) for an absolute constant C.

title: Concentration of measure on the Euclidean sphere
description: Let σ be the normalized rotation-invariant measure on S^{n−1}. Every 1-Lipschitz f:S^{n−1}→ℝ satisfies σ{|f−M_f|>ε}≤2exp(−cnε²) for its median (or mean) M_f and an absolute c (Lévy). In particular σ{x: |⟨x,θ⟩|>ε}≤√(π/2)·exp(−ε²n/2) for every unit vector θ.

title: Gromov–Milman concentration on the orthogonal group
description: Let μ_n be normalized Haar measure on O(n) with the Hilbert–Schmidt metric. Every L-Lipschitz F:O(n)→ℝ satisfies μ_n{|F−∫F dμ_n|≥ε}≤C exp(−cnε²/L²) for absolute constants c,C.

title: ψ₁ bound for a Rademacher chaos of order two
description: If ε, ε′ are independent Rademacher sequences and X=∑_{j,k}a_{jk}ε_jε′_k with real coefficients, then (E|X|^p)^{1/p}≤(p−1)(EX²)^{1/2} for p≥2 (hypercontractivity), hence ‖X‖_{ψ₁}≤C(∑a_{jk}²)^{1/2} for an absolute C.

title: Deviation inequality for sums of i.i.d. ψ_α random variables
description: For 0<α≤1 and i.i.d. copies X_1,…,X_n of a ψ_α random variable, there are constants C,c depending on α and ‖X_1‖_{ψ_α} with P(∑_{i≤n}X_i>Cn)≤exp(−cn^α); this is a Bernstein-type inequality (Schmuckenschläger 1993).

title: Cramér’s large deviation theorem
description: Let X_1,X_2,… be i.i.d. real random variables with E e^{tX_1}<∞ for t in a neighbourhood of 0, and I(a)=sup_t(ta−log E e^{tX_1}). Then (1/n)log P(∑_{i≤n}X_i≥an)→−I(a) for a>EX_1 and (1/n)log P(∑X_i≤an)→−I(a) for a<EX_1; the upper bounds P(…)≤e^{−nI(a)} hold for every n.

title: Normalized standard Gaussian vector is uniform on the sphere
description: If g is a standard Gaussian vector in ℝⁿ, then g/|g| is distributed according to the normalized rotation-invariant measure on S^{n−1} and is independent of |g|.

title: Bourgain–Lindenstrauss–Milman almost-orthogonal partition lemma
description: Let {w_α}_{α∈A}⊂S^{n−1} satisfy sup_{y∈S^{n−1}}(#A)^{−1}∑_α|⟨w_α,y⟩|≤δ, let 0<λ<1 and k≤n. Then A contains disjoint families F_β={β_1,…,β_k}, β∈B, covering more than (1−λ)#A−k indices, such that each family lies within δ4^k/λ of an orthonormal set: |v_{β_i}−w_{β_i}|≤δ4^k/λ for orthonormal v_{β_1},…,v_{β_k}.

title: Unconditional convex body
description: A convex body K⊂ℝⁿ is unconditional with respect to an orthonormal basis (e_i) if it is invariant under every reflection x↦x−2⟨x,e_i⟩e_i, equivalently under all sign changes of the coordinates in that basis.

title: Cross-polytope bound for unconditional convex bodies
description: There is an absolute constant c such that every convex body K⊂ℝⁿ that is unconditional with respect to an orthonormal basis (e_i) satisfies K⊂c√n M*(K)·conv{±e_1,…,±e_n}, where M*(K) is the half mean width (Klartag 2000, Lemma 3.2).

title: Total degree of a multivariate polynomial
description: For a nonzero polynomial f in R[X₁,…,X_n] over a commutative ring, its total degree deg f is the largest value of e₁+⋯+e_n over the monomials X₁^(e₁)⋯X_n^(e_n) occurring in f with nonzero coefficient. By convention the zero polynomial has degree −∞.

title: Prime-power order of a finite field
description: A finite field F has prime characteristic p, and its number of elements is q=p^f, where f is the dimension of F as a vector space over its prime field 𝔽_p. In particular q·1=0 in F.

title: Multiplicativity of the sign of a permutation
description: For permutations σ,τ of {1,…,n}, sgn(σ∘τ)=sgn(σ)·sgn(τ). Hence the sign is a group homomorphism from the symmetric group to {±1}, and sgn(σ⁻¹)=sgn(σ).

title: Indecomposable module category
description: A module category M over a monoidal category C is indecomposable if it is nonzero and is not equivalent, as a C-module category, to a direct sum M₁⊕M₂ of two nonzero C-module categories; the direct sum is the product category M₁×M₂ with componentwise action, associativity and unit constraints.

title: Relative tensor product over an algebra in a tensor category
description: For an algebra A in a tensor category C, a right A-module (M,p) and a left A-module (N,q), M⊗_AN is the cokernel of p⊗id_N−id_M⊗q: M⊗A⊗N→M⊗N, the coequalizer of the two actions. If M is a B–A bimodule and N an A–D bimodule, M⊗_AN inherits a B–D bimodule structure.

title: Right exact functor between abelian categories
description: An additive functor F between abelian categories is right exact if, for every short exact sequence 0→X→Y→Z→0, the sequence F(X)→F(Y)→F(Z)→0 is exact.

title: Fully faithful essentially surjective functors are equivalences
description: A functor F:C→D is an equivalence of categories if and only if it is fully faithful and essentially surjective, meaning every object of D is isomorphic to F(X) for some object X of C.

title: Action of a group scheme on a scheme
description: For a group scheme (G,m,e) over a scheme S and an S-scheme X, a left action is an S-morphism a:G×_SX→X with a∘(e×id_X)=id_X and a∘(m×id_X)=a∘(id_G×a); equivalently, for every S-scheme T the maps G(T)×X(T)→X(T) are group actions, functorial in T. Right actions X×_SG→X are defined symmetrically.

title: Nilpotent algebraic group
description: An algebraic group G over a field k is nilpotent if it has a central normal series G=G₀⊇G₁⊇⋯⊇G_t=e: normal algebraic subgroups such that the image of G_i in G/G_(i+1) is central, i.e. its points over every k-algebra R commute with all of (G/G_(i+1))(R).

title: Base change of smooth morphisms
description: If X→S is a smooth morphism of schemes and S′→S is any morphism, then the base change X×_SS′→S′ is smooth.

title: Valuation ring
description: An integral domain A with fraction field K is a valuation ring if for every nonzero x∈K either x∈A or x⁻¹∈A. Valuation rings are local; the valuation ring of a discretely valued field is an example.

title: Valuative criterion of properness
description: A quasi-separated morphism of finite type f:X→Y is proper if and only if, for every valuation ring A with fraction field K and every commutative square Spec K→X, Spec A→Y over f, there is exactly one morphism Spec A→X making both triangles commute.

title: Spreading out an abelian variety to an abelian scheme
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field K there are a finite set S of places of K, containing the archimedean places, and an abelian scheme over the ring of S-integers O_(K,S) whose generic fibre is A; equivalently A has good reduction at all but finitely many places.

title: Strict henselization of a local ring
description: For a local ring (R,𝔪,k) and a separable closure k^s of k, the strict henselization R^sh is the colimit of the local rings, at points over 𝔪 with residue field embedded in k^s, of étale R-algebras. It is a henselian local ring with residue field k^s, flat and local over R; for a discrete valuation ring it is a discrete valuation ring unramified over R.

title: Finiteness of Galois cohomology unramified outside a finite set
description: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places containing the archimedean ones, and M a finite discrete Gal(K^s/K)-module unramified outside S whose order is an S-unit. Then the subgroup of H¹(K,M) of classes unramified at every place outside S is finite.

title: Unitriangular embedding of a unipotent group
description: A unipotent affine algebraic group over a field k is isomorphic to an algebraic subgroup of the group U_n of upper unitriangular n×n matrices over k, for some n.

title: Central series of the unitriangular group
description: For the group U_n of upper unitriangular matrices over a field, ordering the entries above the diagonal by distance from it, the subgroups U_n^(r) where the first r entries vanish form a central normal series U_n=U_n^(0)⊇U_n^(1)⊇⋯⊇e whose successive quotients are isomorphic to 𝔾_a.

title: Isomorphism theorems for algebraic groups
description: For algebraic groups over a field, the Noether isomorphism theorems hold: a homomorphism factors as a quotient map followed by an embedding with image its quotient by the kernel, and for algebraic subgroups H and normal N of G, H∩N is normal in H and H/(H∩N)≅HN/N ⊆ G/N.

title: Pseudo-abelian variety
description: A pseudo-abelian variety over a field is a smooth connected algebraic group in which every smooth connected affine normal algebraic subgroup is trivial.

title: Largest smooth connected affine normal subgroup of an algebraic group
description: Every algebraic group G over a field contains a largest smooth connected affine normal algebraic subgroup N, and G/N contains no nontrivial such subgroup; if G is smooth and connected, N is the unique smooth connected affine normal subgroup with G/N a pseudo-abelian variety.

title: Pseudo-abelian varieties over perfect fields are abelian varieties
description: Every pseudo-abelian variety over a perfect field is complete, hence an abelian variety.

title: Affine subgroups of abelian varieties are finite
description: Every affine algebraic subgroup of an abelian variety over a field is finite; consequently every homomorphism from a smooth connected affine algebraic group to an abelian variety is trivial.

title: Subgroups, quotients and extensions of unipotent groups
description: Algebraic subgroups and quotients of unipotent affine algebraic groups are unipotent, and an extension of a unipotent algebraic group by a unipotent algebraic group is unipotent.

title: Additive-character criterion for multiplicative type
description: An affine algebraic group G over a field is of multiplicative type if and only if it is commutative and every homomorphism G→𝔾_a is trivial; equivalently, G becomes diagonalizable over a separable closure.

title: Homomorphisms between unipotent and multiplicative-type groups are trivial
description: Over a field there are no nontrivial homomorphisms from a unipotent algebraic group to an algebraic group of multiplicative type, nor from an algebraic group of multiplicative type to a unipotent one.

title: Splitting of extensions of unipotent groups by diagonalizable groups
description: Over an algebraically closed field, every extension e→D→G→U→e of a unipotent algebraic group U by a diagonalizable algebraic group D splits: D→G has a retraction homomorphism, so G≅D×U.

title: Smooth connected groups of multiplicative type are tori
description: A smooth connected algebraic group of multiplicative type over a field is an algebraic torus.

title: Cusp form of half-integral weight with a multiplier
description: A modular form of weight κ∈(1/2)ℤ with a multiplier on a congruence subgroup Γ is a cusp form if it vanishes at every cusp: for each cusp, the Fourier expansion obtained after the slash action of a metaplectic element sending that cusp to ∞ has zero constant term. These form the subspace S_κ(Γ,χ). Weight-3/2 cusp forms on Γ₁(N), 4|N, are the case κ=3/2 with the cube of the theta multiplier.

title: Petersson inner product of half-integral weight cusp forms
description: For cusp forms f,g of the same weight κ∈(1/2)ℤ and multiplier on a congruence subgroup Γ, ⟨f,g⟩=∫_D f(z)·conj(g(z))·y^(κ−2)dxdy, z=x+iy, over a fundamental domain D for Γ on the upper half-plane. The integrand is Γ-invariant, the integral converges and does not depend on D, and it is a positive definite Hermitian form on the cusp space; orthogonal complements of subspaces of cusp forms are taken for it.

title: Unary theta series of weight 3/2
description: For a squarefree integer t≥1 and an odd Dirichlet character ψ, h_(t,ψ)(z)=∑_(m≥1)ψ(m)m e^(2πitm²z). It is a cusp form of weight 3/2, with character, on Γ₁(N) whenever 4t·cond(ψ)² divides N. For a level N, U⊆S_(3/2)(Γ₁(N)) denotes the span of the unary theta series lying in that space; their coefficients are supported on finitely many square classes tℤ².

title: Shimura lift of a half-integral weight cusp form
description: Let f=∑a(n)qⁿ be a cusp form of weight λ+1/2, λ≥1, with character χ on Γ₀(4N), and t a squarefree positive integer. Apart from its constant term, the t-th Shimura lift S_t f=∑A_t(n)qⁿ is defined by ∑A_t(n)n^(−s)=L(s−λ+1,χ_t)∑_(m≥1)a(tm²)m^(−s), where χ_t(m)=χ(m)((−1)^λt/m) with the Kronecker symbol. Shimura proved that S_t f is a modular form of weight 2λ on Γ₀(2N) with character χ². Forms on Γ₁(4N) are lifted componentwise along their decomposition into character eigenspaces.

title: Hecke operator T(p²) on half-integral weight modular forms
description: For a modular form f=∑a(n)qⁿ of weight λ+1/2 with character χ on Γ₀(4N) and a prime p∤4N, Shimura’s Hecke operator gives T(p²)f=∑b(n)qⁿ with b(n)=a(p²n)+χ(p)((−1)^λn/p)p^(λ−1)a(n)+χ(p)²p^(2λ−1)a(n/p²), where a(n/p²)=0 unless p²|n. It preserves the modular and cusp forms of that weight, level and character; T(m²) for m coprime to 4N is defined multiplicatively.

title: Normality of the Hecke operators T(p²) on half-integral weight cusp forms
description: For primes p∤4N the Hecke operators T(p²) on S_(λ+1/2)(Γ₀(4N),χ) commute with one another and are normal for the Petersson inner product; a unimodular multiple of each is Hermitian. Hence the cusp space has an orthogonal basis of simultaneous eigenforms of all T(p²), p∤4N, and each T(p²) commutes with the orthogonal projection onto any subspace stable under all of them, such as the span U of the unary theta series and its complement U^⊥.

title: Eichler commutation relation for theta series
description: Let L be a positive definite integral quadratic ℤ-lattice of rank k and level N, and p∤N a prime. The Hecke operator T(p²) of weight k/2 maps θ_L to a linear combination, with coefficients depending only on p, k and L_p, of θ_L and the sum of θ_K over the Kneser p-neighbours K of L (for even k also T(p) when p is a similitude norm). Thus T(p²) acts on the theta series of the classes in the genus of L through a neighbour-counting matrix (Eichler 1952, §§11, 21).

title: Kneser p-neighbour of a quadratic lattice
description: For a prime p, two integral quadratic ℤ-lattices L and K on the same rational quadratic space are p-neighbours if L∩K has index p in both L and K. Then K_q=L_q for every prime q≠p; when p∤2disc(L) also K_p≅L_p, so K lies in the genus of L. The p-neighbour graph has these lattices as vertices and p-neighbour pairs as edges.

title: Connectedness of the Kneser p-neighbour graph
description: Let L be an integral quadratic ℤ-lattice of rank at least 3 and p∤2disc(L) a prime. Every lattice K on the same rational quadratic space with K_q=L_q for all primes q≠p and K_p≅L_p is joined to L by a finite chain of successive p-neighbours (Kneser 1957).

title: Spin group of a quadratic space
description: For a nondegenerate quadratic space V of dimension at least 3 over a field F of characteristic not two, Spin(V) is the group of units g of the even Clifford algebra C⁺(V) with gVg⁻¹=V and gḡ=1 for the canonical involution. Conjugation gives an exact sequence 1→{±1}→Spin(V)→SO(V)→F×/F×² whose last map is the spinor norm. As an algebraic group Spin(V) is simply connected, and absolutely almost simple when dim V=3 or dim V≥5.

title: Hecke equivariance of the Shimura lift
description: For f∈S_(λ+1/2)(Γ₀(4N),χ), λ≥1, a squarefree t and primes p∤4N, the t-th Shimura lift satisfies S_t(T(p²)f)=T(p)S_t f, with the weight-2λ Hecke operator for the character χ². Hence if f is an eigenform of all T(p²), p∤4N, the lift is an eigenform of all T(p) with the same eigenvalues, and for n coprime to 4N, a(tn²)=a(t)∑_(d|n)μ(d)χ_t(d)d^(λ−1)A(n/d), where A(m) is the T(m)-eigenvalue of the lift (Shimura 1973, Corollary 1.8).

title: Cuspidality criterion for Shimura lifts of weight-3/2 cusp forms
description: Let f be a cusp form of weight 3/2 with character on Γ₀(4N) and t a squarefree positive integer. Its t-th Shimura lift, a modular form of weight 2, is a cusp form if and only if f is Petersson-orthogonal to the unary theta series ∑ψ(m)m e^(2πitm²z) of that level and character. Thus all Shimura lifts of f are cusp forms exactly when f is orthogonal to the whole span U of unary theta series (Kojima 1980; Cipra 1983; Sturm 1982).

title: Maass form of half-integral weight
description: For k∈(1/2)ℤ and a multiplier system ν of weight k on Γ₀(N), a Maass form of weight k is a smooth function f on the upper half-plane with f(γz)=ν(γ)((cz+d)/|cz+d|)^k f(z) for γ∈Γ₀(N), which is an eigenfunction of the weight-k Laplacian Δ_k=y²(∂_x²+∂_y²)−iky∂_x and has polynomial growth at every cusp; it is a Maass cusp form if its constant terms at all cusps vanish. If F is a holomorphic modular form of weight k for ν, then y^(k/2)F is a Maass form with eigenvalue (k/2)(1−k/2).

title: Kloosterman sum attached to a multiplier system
description: For a multiplier system ν of weight k on Γ₀(N), integers m,n and c>0 with N|c, K(m,n;c)=∑ν(γ)^(−1)e((ma+nd)/c), summed over the double cosets Γ_∞γΓ_∞ in Γ₀(N) with lower row (c,d), i.e. over d mod c coprime to c. For half-integral k and the theta multiplier on Γ₀(4N) it equals ∑_(d mod c,(d,c)=1)(c/d)ε_d^(2k)e((md̄+nd)/c), where dd̄≡1 mod c and ε_d is 1 or i according as d≡1 or 3 mod 4.

title: Kuznetsov–Proskurin sum formula for weights 0, 1/2, 1, 3/2
description: For k∈{0,1/2,1,3/2}, a multiplier of weight k on Γ₀(N), positive integers m,n and a smooth test function φ on [0,∞) with φ(0)=φ′(0)=0 and suitable decay, the sum ∑_(c≡0 mod N)c^(−1)K(m,n;c)φ(4π√(mn)/c) equals a spectral expansion: a sum over an orthonormal basis of Maass cusp forms of weight k of products of their m-th and n-th Fourier coefficients times an explicit Bessel transform of φ at their spectral parameters, plus the corresponding Eisenstein-series integrals and a sum over holomorphic cusp forms of weights k+2j weighted by a second Bessel transform (Kuznetsov; Proskurin 1979).

title: Iwaniec’s bound for half-integral weight Kloosterman sums averaged over levels
description: Let n be squarefree and 8|N. For a level Q, x≥1 and |ν|≤1 let K_Q(x) be the sum over c≤x with Q|c of c^(−1/2)K(n,n;c)e(2νn/c), where K(n,n;c) are half-integral weight Kloosterman sums for the theta multiplier. For P≥1 and the levels Q=pN with primes P<p≤2P, p∤n, Iwaniec (1987, Theorem 3) proved ∑_Q|K_Q(x)|≪[xP^(−1/2)+xn^(−1/4)+(x+n)^(5/8)(x^(1/4)P^(3/8)+n^(1/8)x^(1/8)P^(1/4))]τ(n)(log nx)^(O(1)) with an absolute constant, improving on Weil’s bound for suitable P.

title: Petersson formula for half-integral weight cusp forms
description: Let 4|N and k=l+1/2 with l≥2, with the theta multiplier on Γ₀(N). For an orthonormal basis {f_j} of S_k(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients f̂_j(n) and n≥1, Γ(k−1)(4πn)^(1−k)∑_j|f̂_j(n)|²=1+2πi^(−k)∑_(c≡0 mod N)c^(−1)K(n,n;c)J_(k−1)(4πn/c). It follows from expressing the Fourier coefficients of Poincaré series through Kloosterman sums and Bessel functions (Petersson 1932).

title: Schulze-Pillot’s lower bound for primitive representation measures of ternary half-genera
description: Let L be a positive definite integral ternary ℤ-lattice and a a positive squarefree integer whose square class is spinor exceptional for gen L, so that the genus splits into two half-genera H₁, H₂ with respect to a. There is C₀=C₀(L,a)>0 such that for every m≥1 and i=1,2, if the primitive representation measure r*(am²,H_i) is nonzero then r*(am²,H_i)≥C₀r*(am²,gen L); here r* denotes Siegel-weighted averages of primitive representation numbers (Schulze-Pillot 1984, Korollar 2).

title: Kneser–Hsia theorem on representation measures of ternary spinor genera
description: Let L be a nondegenerate ternary quadratic ℤ-lattice on V and a≠0 with −2a·det V not a square; put E=ℚ(√(−2a det V)). Unless θ(O⁺_A(L))⊆N_(E/ℚ)(I_E), which happens for a in at most finitely many square classes, the Siegel-weighted representation measure of a is the same for every spinor genus in gen L. Otherwise gen L splits into two half-genera with equally many spinor genera, and spinor genera in the same half-genus have equal measure. The same holds for primitive representations (Kneser 1961; Hsia 1976 for definite forms).

title: Siegel lower bound for primitive representations by a ternary genus
description: For a positive definite integral ternary ℤ-lattice L and ε>0 there is c=c(L,ε)>0, not effectively computable, such that the Siegel-weighted genus average r*(n,gen L) of primitive representation numbers satisfies r*(n,gen L)≥c n^(1/2−ε) for every positive integer n primitively represented by L_p at every prime p. It follows from Siegel’s product formula in local densities and Siegel’s bound L(1,χ)≫n^(−ε) for the quadratic character of ℚ(√(−n det L)).

title: Maximal lattice of an anisotropic local quadratic space
description: Let V be an anisotropic nondegenerate quadratic space over ℚ_p and a∈ℚ_p×. Then {x∈V:Q(x)∈aℤ_p} is a lattice, the unique (a)-maximal lattice on V. Consequently for every lattice L on V there is r₀ such that each x∈V with Q(x)∈p^(r₀+2s)ℤ_p lies in p^sL for all s≥0 (Eichler 1952, Satz 9.4; O’Meara 91:1).

title: Jaulent’s Hilbertian description of the Hilbert kernel of K₂
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), let K_n be the finite layers of its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞, Γ_n=Gal(K∞/K_n), and H_(K∞) the union of their Hilbertian radicals. Under Tate’s surjection (T_ℓ⊗ℛ_(K∞))^(Γ_n)→K₂(K_n)_ℓ, the subgroup (T_ℓ⊗H_(K∞))^(Γ_n) maps onto the ℓ-primary Hilbert kernel, the kernel of all Hilbert symbols at noncomplex places. It is exactly the subgroup of elements of infinite height in (T_ℓ⊗ℛ_(K∞))^(Γ_n); in particular it contains the maximal divisible subgroup.

title: Kummer description of the Bertrandias–Payan radical in a cyclotomic tower
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ), let K_n be the finite layers of its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞, Γ_n=Gal(K∞/K_n), T̄_ℓ the dual of the Tate module, and H_(K∞) the union of their Hilbertian radicals. Then (T̄_ℓ⊗H_(K∞))^(Γ_n) is exactly the subgroup of elements of infinite height in (T̄_ℓ⊗ℛ_(K∞))^(Γ_n). By Kummer theory it is the radical over K∞ of the compositum of the cyclic ℓ-extensions of K_n that embed in cyclic ℓ-extensions of arbitrarily large degree; it contains the maximal divisible subgroup, the radical of the compositum of the ℤ_ℓ-extensions of K_n.

title: Galois descent of Hilbertian radicals in a cyclotomic tower
description: Let K contain μ_(2ℓ) and let K_n be the finite layers of its cyclotomic ℤ_ℓ-extension K∞. Inside ℛ_(K∞), for m≥n the Hilbertian radical of K_m meets ℛ_(K_n) in the Hilbertian radical of K_n. Hence H_(K_n)=H_(K∞)^(Gal(K∞/K_n)), where H_(K∞) is the union of the H_(K_m).

title: Open map between topological spaces
description: A map f:X→Y between topological spaces is open if the image f(U) of every open subset U of X is open in Y.

title: Uniquely ergodic topological dynamical system
description: A compact topological dynamical system (X,T) is uniquely ergodic if X carries exactly one T-invariant Borel probability measure. For an action of a group of homeomorphisms the measure is required to be invariant under every element of the group.

title: Ellis enveloping semigroup of a flow
description: For a group T acting by homeomorphisms on a compact Hausdorff space X, the enveloping semigroup E(X) is the closure, in the product space X^X of all self-maps with pointwise convergence, of the maps x↦xt for t∈T. Under composition it is a compact semigroup, each evaluation p↦xp is continuous, and xE(X) is the orbit closure of x.

title: Ellis’s characterization of distal flows by the enveloping semigroup
description: A flow of a group T on a compact Hausdorff space X is distal if and only if its enveloping semigroup E(X) is a group; its elements are then bijections of X.

title: Parry’s ergodicity criterion for nilrotations
description: Let X=G/Γ be a compact nilmanifold of a nilpotent Lie group G, and let a finitely generated group act on X by left translations by elements of G. If N is the subgroup generated by the identity component of G and the translating elements, the action is ergodic for the Haar probability measure of X if and only if the induced action on the compact abelian group [N,N]∖X is ergodic.

title: Minimal translations of compact abelian groups are ergodic
description: If a group of translations of a compact abelian group Z has a dense orbit, so that the translation action is minimal, then it is ergodic for the Haar probability measure of Z.

title: Lagrange interpolation formula
description: For distinct elements x₀,…,x_n of a field K and any y₀,…,y_n∈K there is a unique polynomial P∈K[x] of degree at most n with P(x_i)=y_i, namely P(x)=∑_i y_i∏_(j≠i)(x−x_j)/(x_i−x_j). In particular a real polynomial of degree at most n taking rational values at n+1 rational points has rational coefficients.

title: Coarea formula for Lipschitz maps
description: Let f:ℝⁿ→ℝ^m be Lipschitz with n≥m and let Jf=√det(Df Dfᵀ) be its Jacobian, defined almost everywhere by Rademacher’s theorem. For every Lebesgue measurable g≥0, and for every integrable g, ∫_(ℝⁿ) g Jf dx=∫_(ℝ^m)∫_(f⁻¹(y)) g dH^(n−m) dy, where H^(n−m) is Hausdorff measure.

title: Functor category
description: For categories C and D, the functor category Fun(C,D) has functors C→D as objects and natural transformations as morphisms, composed componentwise. The presheaf category of C is Fun(C^op,Set), with Set the category of sets and functions; U↦Hom(−,U) defines the Yoneda functor C→Fun(C^op,Set).

title: Category of finite-dimensional representations of an affine algebraic group
description: For an affine algebraic group G over a field k, Rep_k(G) has the finite-dimensional algebraic representations as objects and the G-equivariant k-linear maps as morphisms. It carries the tensor product V⊗W, on which g∈G(R) acts by r_V(g)⊗r_W(g), with unit the trivial one-dimensional representation k, and a forgetful functor to finite-dimensional k-vector spaces.

title: Regular representation of an affine algebraic group
description: For an affine algebraic group G over k, the (right) regular representation is the rational representation of G on its coordinate algebra O(G) given by (gf)(x)=f(xg), corresponding to the comodule structure Δ:O(G)→O(G)⊗O(G). Every finite-dimensional representation embeds into a finite direct sum of copies of it.

title: Transfer homomorphism to a subgroup of finite index
description: For a subgroup H of finite index in a group G with right coset representatives g₁,…,g_n, the transfer (Verlagerung) V:G→H/[H,H] sends g to ∏ᵢ gᵢ g φ(gᵢg)⁻¹, where φ(x) is the representative of Hx. It is a homomorphism independent of the representatives and induces G^ab→H^ab.

title: Group-theoretic principal ideal theorem
description: For a finite group G with commutator subgroup G′, the transfer homomorphism G/G′→G′/[G′,G′] is trivial. Conjectured by Artin and proved by Furtwängler (1930); simpler proofs are due to Iyanaga and Witt.

title: Compatibility of the Artin map with extension of ideals and transfer
description: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension of number fields and K⊆K′⊆L. For ideals 𝔞 of K prime to the ramification, the Artin symbol of the extended ideal 𝔞O_(K′) in Gal(L/K′)^ab is the transfer of the Artin symbol of 𝔞 in Gal(L/K)^ab (Artin).

title: Opposite parabolic subgroups and the big cell
description: For a parabolic k-subgroup P of a connected reductive k-group G there is a parabolic k-subgroup P⁻ opposite to P, i.e. P∩P⁻ is a Levi subgroup of both, and two such are conjugate by a unique element of R_u(P)(k). For opposite P and P⁻ the product map R_u(P⁻)×P→G is an isomorphism onto an open subvariety of G.

title: Grothendieck’s theorem on maximal tori, splitting and density of rational points
description: Let G be a connected algebraic group over a field k. Then G has a maximal torus defined over k. If G is reductive, it splits over a finite separable extension of k, and if moreover k is infinite then G(k) is Zariski dense in G (Grothendieck, SGA 3 XIV; Rosenlicht for perfect k).

title: Normalizer theorem for parabolic subgroups
description: Let P be a parabolic subgroup of a connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed field. Then P is its own normalizer, N_G(P)=P, and P is the only conjugate of P containing the unipotent radical R_u(P).

title: Splitness of unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups
description: For a parabolic k-subgroup P of a connected reductive group G over a field k, the unipotent radical R_u(P) is defined over k and is k-split, i.e. it has a composition series of connected k-subgroups with successive quotients isomorphic to the additive group.

title: Rational fixed points of split solvable group actions
description: Let H be a connected k-split solvable algebraic group acting on a complete k-variety V. If V(k) is nonempty then H has a fixed point in V(k) (Rosenlicht; Borel–Tits 2.7). In particular every homogeneous space of H over k has a k-point.

title: Representability of normalizers of smooth subgroup schemes with connected fibers
description: Let G be a smooth affine group scheme over a scheme S and Y,Y′⊆G finitely presented closed subschemes with Y smooth with nonempty geometrically connected fibers. The transporter functor of Y into Y′ is represented by a finitely presented closed subscheme of G; in particular the normalizer N_G(Y) is a finitely presented closed subgroup scheme.

title: Quotient of a group scheme by a self-normalizing smooth subgroup
description: Let G→S be a smooth affine group scheme with connected fibers and H a smooth closed subgroup with connected fibers and H=N_G(H). The étale quotient sheaf G/H is a smooth S-scheme, quasi-projective Zariski-locally on S, equal to the functor of closed subgroups étale-locally conjugate to H. If every geometric fiber G_s/H_s is projective then G/H→S is proper with S-ample line bundle det(Lie ℋ)^∨ for the universal conjugate ℋ.

title: Normal commutative ring
description: A commutative ring R is normal if for every prime ideal 𝔭 the localization R_𝔭 is an integrally closed integral domain. A normal domain is a normal ring that is an integral domain.

title: Normal scheme
description: A scheme X is normal if for every point x the local ring O_(X,x) is an integrally closed integral domain.

title: Regular local ring
description: A Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) with residue field κ=R/𝔪 is regular if dim_κ 𝔪/𝔪² equals the Krull dimension of R.

title: Cohen–Macaulay local ring
description: A Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) is Cohen–Macaulay if its depth, the 𝔪-depth of R as a module over itself, equals its Krull dimension. A Noetherian ring is Cohen–Macaulay if all its localizations at prime ideals are, and a locally Noetherian scheme is Cohen–Macaulay if all its local rings are.

title: Serre’s conditions (R_k) and (S_k)
description: For an integer k≥0, a Noetherian ring R satisfies (R_k) if R_𝔭 is a regular local ring for every prime 𝔭 with dim R_𝔭≤k, and (S_k) if depth R_𝔭≥min(k, dim R_𝔭) for every prime 𝔭. A locally Noetherian scheme satisfies (R_k) or (S_k) if all its local rings satisfy the corresponding local condition; (R₁) is called regularity in codimension one.

title: Reducedness criterion (R₀)+(S₁) for Noetherian rings
description: A Noetherian ring is reduced if and only if it satisfies Serre’s conditions (R₀) and (S₁): its localizations at minimal primes are fields and every localization at a prime of positive height has positive depth.

title: Characterizations of discrete valuation rings
description: For a ring A the following are equivalent: A is a discrete valuation ring; A is a Noetherian valuation ring that is not a field; A is a regular local ring of dimension one; A is a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by one nonzero element; A is a one-dimensional Noetherian local normal domain. Then every nonzero element is uπⁿ with u a unit and π a generator of the maximal ideal.

title: Kollár’s alternative for Noetherian local rings of depth less than two
description: For a Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪) exactly one of the following holds: R is Artinian; R is regular of dimension one; depth R≥2; or there is a finite ring map R→R′ with R′≠0, not an isomorphism, whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝔪, such that 𝔪 is not an associated prime of R′.

title: Normality of reduced rings with finitely many minimal primes
description: For a reduced ring R with finitely many minimal primes the following are equivalent: R is normal; R is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions Q(R), the localization at the set of nonzerodivisors; R is a finite product of normal domains.

title: Support criterion for annihilation by a power of an ideal
description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring R and an ideal I, some power Iⁿ annihilates M if and only if the support of M, the set of primes 𝔭 with M_𝔭≠0, is contained in V(I), the set of primes containing I.

title: Pullback of a quasi-coherent sheaf along a morphism of schemes
description: For a morphism f:X→Y of schemes and a quasi-coherent O_Y-module G, the pullback f*G is the quasi-coherent O_X-module such that, whenever Spec A⊆X and Spec B⊆Y are affine opens with f(Spec A)⊆Spec B and G|_(Spec B)≅M̃, one has f*G|_(Spec A)≅(M⊗_B A)~. It is compatible with composition, (g∘f)*≅f*g*, and with tensor products, and it sends invertible sheaves to invertible sheaves.

title: Theorem of the square for invertible sheaves on an abelian variety
description: For an invertible sheaf L on an abelian variety A over a field k and points a,b∈A(k), t_(a+b)*L⊗L≅t_a*L⊗t_b*L, where t_a:A→A is translation by a.

title: Cartier divisor on an integral scheme
description: Let X be an integral scheme with function field K, the local ring at its generic point. A Cartier divisor D is given by an open cover {U_i} and nonzero f_i∈K with f_i/f_j a unit of O_X(U_i∩U_j), two such data being identified when their local equations differ by units on a common refinement; f_i is a local equation of D on U_i. Divisors form an abelian group, written additively, under multiplication of local equations. D is effective if its local equations can be chosen in O_X(U_i), its support is the closed set of points where a local equation is not a unit, the principal divisor div(f) of f∈K× has the single local equation f, and D,D′ are linearly equivalent, D∼D′, if D−D′ is principal.

title: Invariance of intersection numbers of divisors under linear equivalence
description: Let V be a smooth projective variety of dimension g over an algebraically closed field k, D₁,…,D_(g−1) divisors and D∼D′ linearly equivalent divisors such that both (D₁,…,D_(g−1),D) and (D₁,…,D_(g−1),D′) have finite common support. Then ∑_v(D₁⋯D_(g−1)·D)_v=∑_v(D₁⋯D_(g−1)·D′)_v, where for effective divisors with local equations f₁,…,f_g at an isolated common point v the local multiplicity is dim_k O_(V,v)/(f₁,…,f_g), extended multilinearly to differences of effective divisors.

title: Theorem of the cube
description: Let U, V, W be complete varieties over a field k with k-points u₀, v₀, w₀. An invertible sheaf on U×V×W whose restrictions to {u₀}×V×W, U×{v₀}×W and U×V×{w₀} are trivial is itself trivial.

title: Closed-immersion criterion by separation of points and tangent vectors
description: Let X be a proper scheme over an algebraically closed field k and V⊆H⁰(X,L) a finite-dimensional space of sections of an invertible sheaf with no base points. The induced morphism X→P(V^∨) is a closed immersion if and only if V separates points (for distinct closed points x,y some member of |V| contains x but not y) and separates tangent vectors (for every closed point x and nonzero tangent vector t at x some member through x does not contain t in its tangent space).

title: Tensor products of ample invertible sheaves are ample
description: On a scheme of finite type over a field, the tensor product of two ample invertible sheaves is ample; more generally L⊗M is ample when L is ample and M is generated by its global sections.

title: Finite length of quotients by ideals containing a power of the maximal ideal
description: If (O,𝔪) is a Noetherian local ring and 𝔞 an ideal containing 𝔪^r for some r>0, then O/𝔞 is an O-module of finite length.

title: Length formula for principal ideals in one-dimensional local rings
description: Let O be a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring with minimal primes 𝔭₁,…,𝔭_n and a∈O a nonzerodivisor lying in no 𝔭_i. Then ℓ_O(O/aO)=∑_i ℓ_(O_(𝔭_i))(O_(𝔭_i))·ℓ_O(O/(𝔭_i+aO)), lengths as modules.

title: Semilocal ring of finitely many nonsingular points of a curve
description: For finitely many nonsingular points x₁,…,x_r of an irreducible curve, the intersection Õ of their local rings in the function field is a principal ideal domain with exactly r maximal ideals; there are t_i∈Õ with v_(x_i)(t_j)=δ_ij, and every nonzero u∈Õ is t₁^(k₁)⋯t_r^(k_r)·v with k_i=v_(x_i)(u) and v a unit of Õ.

title: Normalization of a projective curve is projective
description: For an irreducible projective curve C over an algebraically closed field, its normalization ν:C^ν→C, the finite birational morphism from the normal curve obtained by integral closure of the local rings in the function field, has C^ν a nonsingular projective curve.

title: Abscissa of absolute convergence of a Dirichlet series
description: For a Dirichlet series ∑a_n n^(−s), its abscissa of absolute convergence σ_a∈[−∞,+∞] is the infimum of the real numbers σ for which ∑|a_n|n^(−σ) converges. The series converges absolutely for Re s>σ_a and for no s with Re s<σ_a.

title: Minimal discriminant ideal of an elliptic curve over a number field
description: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, the minimal discriminant 𝔇_(E/K) is the integral ideal ∏_v 𝔭_v^(ord_v(Δ_v)) of O_K, the product over the finite places v, where 𝔭_v={x∈O_K:|x|_v<1} and Δ_v is the discriminant of a minimal integral Weierstrass model of E over the completion K_v. Almost all exponents are zero.

title: Roth’s theorem over a number field
description: Let K be a number field, v a place of K with its absolute value extended to an algebraic closure, α algebraic over K, ε>0 and C>0. Then only finitely many x∈K satisfy |x−α|_v<C·H_K(x)^(−2−ε), where H_K is the relative multiplicative height on K. Over ℚ with the real absolute value this is Roth’s irrationality-exponent theorem.

title: Compactness of the points of a projective variety over a local field
description: For a local field F (ℝ, ℂ or a nonarchimedean local field), ℙⁿ(F) with the quotient topology from Fⁿ⁺¹∖{0} is compact. Hence for a projective variety X over F, the set X(F), closed in ℙⁿ(F), is compact in its F-adic topology.

title: Banks–Freiberg–Maynard exceptional-character lemma for smooth moduli
description: There is an absolute c>0 such that for T≥3 and P≥T^(1/log log T), among all primitive Dirichlet characters χ mod q with q≤T and largest prime factor P⁺(q)≤P, at most one has L(s,χ) vanishing in the region Re s>1−c/log P, |Im s|≤exp(log P/√(log T)). If such χ exists it is real, L(s,χ) has a single simple real zero there, and P⁺(q)≫log q≫log log T. It rests on Chang’s character-sum bound for smooth moduli.

title: Banks–Freiberg–Maynard modified Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem
description: Fix C>0 and θ=1/2−δ∈(0,1/2). For ε>0 small enough in terms of C, δ and the exceptional-character constant, let q₀<N^ε be squarefree with P⁺(q₀)<N^(ε/log log N), and let Z be the largest prime factor of the possible exceptional modulus at level N^(2ε) (Z=1 if none). Then ∑ over q<N^θ with q₀|q and (q,Z)=1 of max_((a,q)=1)|ψ(N;q,a)−ψ(N)/φ(q)| is ≪_(δ,C) N/(φ(q₀)(log N)^C).

title: Banks–Freiberg–Maynard sieve estimates for Maynard–Tao weights on varying tuples
description: Let H={h₁,…,h_k} be admissible with 0≤h_i≤N and with every prime factor of ∏(h_j−h_i) at most w=ε log N, let W be the product of the primes ≤w other than the exceptional prime, and b a residue with each b+h_i coprime to W. For weights w(n)=∑_(d_i|n+h_i)λ_d with λ_d=∏μ(d_i)·∑_j∏_ℓF_(ℓ,j)(log d_ℓ/log N), supported on ∏d_i≤N^δ coprime to the exceptional prime, sums over N<n≤2N, n≡b (mod W) satisfy ∑w(n)²∼(N/W)B^(−k)I_k(F), ∑1_P(n+h_j)w(n)²∼(N/W)B^(−k)J_k(F), and ∑1_P(n+h_j)1_P(n+h_ℓ)w(n)²≤(4+O(δ))(N/W)B^(−k)L_k(F) for j≠ℓ, where B=φ(W)log N/W and I_k,J_k,L_k are the usual integrals of the symmetric function F=∑_j∏_ℓF′_(ℓ,j).

title: Banks–Freiberg–Maynard Erdős–Rankin-type tuple construction
description: Fix k and β_k≥…≥β₁≥0. For y large in terms of β and k, numbers x≥1 and z with 2y(1+(1+β_k)x)≤2z≤y·log log y/log log log y, and any set Z of primes with ∑_(p∈Z,p≥p′)1/p≪1/p′≪1/log z for p′∈Z, there are residues a_p (p≤y, p∉Z) and an admissible k-tuple {h₁,…,h_k} that is exactly the set of integers in (0,z] lying in no class a_p mod p. Moreover p|(h_j−h_i) implies p≤y, and h_i=β_ixy+y+O(y·exp(−(log y)^(1/4))).

title: Approximately divisible dimension group with order unit
description: A dimension group G with order unit u is approximately divisible if no extreme point σ of the normalized trace space S(G,u) has discrete image σ(G) in ℝ; equivalently (Goodearl–Handelman), the affine representation G→Aff S(G,u) has norm-dense image. Simple dimension groups other than ℤ are approximately divisible.

title: Kernel of a group homomorphism
description: For a group homomorphism f:G→H, the subgroup ker f={g∈G: f(g)=e_H} of elements sent to the identity.

title: Refinable set of traces on an ordered abelian group with order unit
description: For a partially ordered abelian group G with order unit u and a set U⊆S(G,u) of normalized traces, U is refinable if whenever b,a′₁,…,a′_n∈G⁺ satisfy τ(b)=∑ᵢτ(a′ᵢ) for every τ∈U, there are aᵢ∈G⁺ with b=∑ᵢaᵢ and τ(aᵢ)=τ(a′ᵢ) for every τ∈U and every i. For U={τ} this is refinability of τ.

title: Good set of traces on an ordered abelian group with order unit
description: For a partially ordered abelian group G with order unit u and U⊆S(G,u), U is good if whenever a∈G and b∈G⁺ satisfy τ(b)−τ(a)≥δ for some δ>0 and all τ∈U, there is c∈G⁺ with c≤b and τ(c)=τ(a) for all τ∈U. For a singleton this is goodness of the trace; it differs from goodness of U relative to Aff S(G,u).

title: Riesz interpolation property for an ordered abelian group
description: A partially ordered abelian group has Riesz interpolation if whenever a₁,a₂≤b₁,b₂ there is c with a₁,a₂≤c≤b₁,b₂.

title: Order units of an unperforated group are detected by normalized traces
description: Let G be an unperforated partially ordered abelian group with order unit u. An element g∈G is an order unit exactly when σ(g)>0 for every normalized trace σ∈S(G,u); without unperforation, strict positivity on S(G,u) only makes some multiple of g an order unit (Goodearl).

title: Equivalence of Riesz interpolation, decomposition and refinement
description: For a partially ordered abelian group the following are equivalent: Riesz interpolation; Riesz decomposition (0≤a≤b+c with b,c≥0 gives a=b₁+c₁ with 0≤b₁≤b, 0≤c₁≤c); and Riesz refinement (a₁+a₂=b₁+b₂ with all terms ≥0 gives c_ij≥0 with a_i=∑_jc_ij and b_j=∑_ic_ij) (Goodearl, Proposition 2.1).

title: Choquet simplex of states of an interpolation group with order unit
description: If G is a partially ordered abelian group with Riesz interpolation and order unit u, its normalized state (trace) space S(G,u), a compact convex subset of ℝ^G in the topology of pointwise convergence, is a Choquet simplex (Goodearl, Theorem 10.17).

title: Cofiniteness of an additive semigroup of positive integers with gcd one
description: If a set S of positive integers is closed under addition and the greatest common divisor of its elements is 1, then S contains every sufficiently large integer.

title: Cauchy–Riemann equations for a complex differentiable function
description: If f=u+iv is complex differentiable at z₀=x₀+iy₀, its partial derivatives exist there and satisfy f_x=−i f_y, that is u_x=v_y and u_y=−v_x, with f′(z₀)=f_x(z₀). Conversely, if f_x and f_y exist near z₀, are continuous at z₀ and satisfy f_x=−i f_y there, then f is complex differentiable at z₀.

title: Segment chains in open connected subsets of the plane
description: Any two points of an open connected subset G of ℂ can be joined by a finite chain of horizontal and vertical line segments lying in G; in particular G is path connected. Conversely, a subset of ℂ in which any two points are joined by a path is connected.

title: Continuity of sums and products of real functions on ℝⁿ
description: If f and g are real functions continuous on a set S⊆ℝⁿ, then f+g, f−g and fg are continuous on S, and f/g is continuous at each point of S where g≠0. Since the coordinate functions are continuous, every real polynomial function on ℝⁿ is continuous.

title: Arc-length integral formula for C¹ curves
description: If γ:[a,b]→ℝⁿ is continuously differentiable, its length (the supremum of inscribed polygon lengths) is finite and equals ∫_a^b|γ′(t)|dt. Summing over pieces gives the same formula for piecewise C¹ curves.

title: Watson’s lemma for Laplace integrals in a complex sector
description: Let q on (0,∞) have finitely many discontinuities and infinities, with q(t)∼∑_{s≥0}a_s t^{(s+λ−μ)/μ} as t→0⁺ for some μ>0 and Re λ>0, and let ∫_0^∞e^{−zt}q(t)dt converge for some z. Then this Laplace integral satisfies I(z)∼∑_{s≥0}Γ((s+λ)/μ)a_s z^{−(s+λ)/μ} as z→∞ uniformly in |arg z|≤π/2−δ, for each δ>0, with principal powers.

title: Derivatives of order estimates for holomorphic functions in sectors
description: If f is holomorphic in a region containing a closed annular sector S and f(z)=O(z^ρ) (or o(z^ρ)) as z→∞ in S, then f^{(m)}(z)=O(z^{ρ−m}) (respectively o(z^{ρ−m})) as z→∞ in every closed annular sector properly interior to S with the same vertex. Hence asymptotic power-type expansions of such f may be differentiated termwise in interior subsectors.

title: Mutually singular measures
description: Two measures μ and ν on the same measurable space are mutually singular, ν⊥μ, if there is a measurable set B with μ(B)=0 and ν(X∖B)=0, so that they are concentrated on disjoint sets.

title: Lebesgue decomposition of Radon measures on Euclidean space
description: If μ and ν are Radon measures on ℝⁿ, then ν=ν_ac+ν_s for Radon measures ν_ac≪μ and ν_s⊥μ, called the absolutely continuous and singular parts of ν with respect to μ. Applied to positive and negative parts, signed and matrix-valued Radon measures decompose entrywise.

title: Aleksandrov Hessian of a convex function
description: Let φ be convex on ℝⁿ and differentiable at an interior point x₀ of its domain. A symmetric n×n matrix A is the Aleksandrov Hessian ∇²φ(x₀) if sup_(y∈∂φ(x))|y−∇φ(x₀)−A(x−x₀)|=o(|x−x₀|) as x→x₀, where ∂φ is the subdifferential.

title: Cyclically monotone subset of ℝᵈ×ℝᵈ
description: A set S⊆ℝᵈ×ℝᵈ is cyclically monotone if for all finitely many (x₁,y₁),…,(x_k,y_k)∈S one has ⟨y₁,x₂−x₁⟩+⟨y₂,x₃−x₂⟩+⋯+⟨y_k,x₁−x_k⟩≤0; equivalently ∑|x_i−y_i|²≤∑|x_i−y_(i−1)|² cyclically.

title: Rockafellar’s theorem on cyclically monotone sets
description: A nonempty set S⊆ℝᵈ×ℝᵈ is cyclically monotone if and only if it is contained in the subdifferential of a proper lower semicontinuous convex function on ℝᵈ; maximal cyclically monotone sets are exactly such subdifferentials.

title: Krein–Milman theorem
description: In a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space, every compact convex set is the closed convex hull of its extreme points.

title: Hausdorff dimension
description: The Hausdorff dimension of a subset A of a metric space is inf{s≥0: H^s(A)=0}, equivalently sup{s: H^s(A)=∞}, where H^s is s-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

title: Anderson–Klee theorem on nondifferentiability of convex functions
description: The set of points in the interior of its domain where a convex function on ℝᵈ is not differentiable has Hausdorff dimension at most d−1; in particular it is Lebesgue null.

title: Max formula for directional derivatives of a convex function
description: If φ is convex on ℝᵈ and finite near p, then ∂φ(p) is nonempty, convex and compact, and the one-sided directional derivative is φ′(p;v)=lim_(h↓0)(φ(p+hv)−φ(p))/h=max_(y∈∂φ(p))⟨y,v⟩.

title: Convergence of subgradients at a point of differentiability
description: Let φ be convex on ℝᵈ and x in the interior of its domain. Then φ is differentiable at x if and only if ∂φ(x) is the single point ∇φ(x), and in that case y_n→∇φ(x) whenever x_n→x and y_n∈∂φ(x_n).

title: Hausdorff measure of a Lipschitz image
description: If g is a Lipschitz map between metric spaces with constant k and A is a subset of its domain, then H^s(g(A))≤k^s H^s(A) for every s≥0.

title: Aleksandrov’s theorem on second differentiability of convex functions
description: A convex function φ on ℝⁿ has a second-order expansion φ(y)=φ(x)+∇φ(x)·(y−x)+½(y−x)ᵀA(x)(y−x)+o(|y−x|²) at Lebesgue-almost every interior point x of its domain, where A(x) is the density of the absolutely continuous part of the matrix measure D∇φ; A(x) is the Aleksandrov Hessian at x.

title: Restriction of a Radon measure to a measurable set
description: If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝⁿ and A is μ-measurable with μ(A)<∞, or A is Borel and μ is Radon, then the restriction μ⌊A(B)=μ(A∩B) is a Radon measure.

title: Modulus of a number field
description: A modulus of a number field F is a formal product 𝔪=𝔪₀𝔪_∞ of a nonzero ideal 𝔪₀ of the ring of integers O_F and a set 𝔪_∞ of real places of F. A prime 𝔭 divides 𝔪 if it divides 𝔪₀, and a real place divides 𝔪 if it lies in 𝔪_∞.

title: Ray class group of a number field
description: For a modulus 𝔪=𝔪₀𝔪_∞ of a number field F, let I^𝔪 be the group of fractional ideals whose prime factorization involves no prime dividing 𝔪₀, and P_(𝔪,1)⊆I^𝔪 the subgroup of principal ideals aO_F with a∈F× such that ord_𝔭(a−1)≥ord_𝔭(𝔪₀) for every 𝔭|𝔪₀ and σ(a)>0 for every real place σ in 𝔪_∞. The ray class group is Cl_𝔪(F)=I^𝔪/P_(𝔪,1); for 𝔪=1 it is the ideal class group.

title: Artin map of a finite abelian extension of number fields
description: Let L/F be a finite abelian extension of number fields and 𝔪 a modulus of F divisible by every prime of F that ramifies in L. The Artin map ψ_(L/F):I^𝔪→Gal(L/F) is the homomorphism on the group of fractional ideals prime to 𝔪₀ sending each prime 𝔭∤𝔪₀ to its Frobenius element in Gal(L/F), extended multiplicatively through prime factorization.

title: Ray class field of a number field
description: For a modulus 𝔪=𝔪₀𝔪_∞ of a number field F, a ray class field modulo 𝔪 is a finite abelian extension F_𝔪 of F in a fixed algebraic closure, unramified at every prime not dividing 𝔪₀ and at every real place not in 𝔪_∞ (such places stay real), whose Artin map I^𝔪→Gal(F_𝔪/F) is surjective with kernel P_(𝔪,1).

title: Modular curves X₁(N)→X₀(N) over ℤ[1/N]
description: For an integer N≥5, X₁(N) over ℤ[1/N] is the Deligne–Rapoport compactification by cusps of the moduli scheme Y₁(N) of elliptic curves E over ℤ[1/N]-schemes with a point P of exact order N, and X₀(N) over ℤ[1/N] that of the coarse moduli scheme Y₀(N) of pairs (E,C) with C a cyclic subgroup scheme of order N; their generic fibres are the modular curves over ℚ, with complex points Γ₁(N)\ℍ* and Γ₀(N)\ℍ*. The rule (E,P)↦(E,⟨P⟩) gives a finite morphism X₁(N)→X₀(N), and d∈(ℤ/Nℤ)× acts on X₁(N) over X₀(N) by the diamond operator (E,P)↦(E,dP), with d=−1 acting trivially.

title: Galois covering of normal integral schemes
description: A finite surjective morphism f:Y→X of normal integral schemes is a Galois covering with group G if the finite group G acts on Y by automorphisms over X and the induced action on function fields makes K(Y)/K(X) a Galois extension with Galois group G. It is cyclic of degree n if G is cyclic of order n.

title: Ramification of X₁(N)→X₀(N) at prime level
description: Let N≥5 be prime and k an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from N. The Galois covering X₁(N)→X₀(N) over k, with group (ℤ/Nℤ)×/{±1}, is unramified at the cusps and at every point with j≠0,1728; it is ramified exactly at the points of X₀(N) with j=1728 when N≡1 mod 4, with inertia cyclic of order 2, and with j=0 when N≡1 mod 3, with inertia cyclic of order 3 (wildly ramified of first type in characteristics 2 and 3).

title: Sylow theorems for finite groups
description: Let G be a finite group and p a prime with |G|=p^a·m, p∤m. Then G has a subgroup of order p^a; any two such Sylow p-subgroups are conjugate, every p-subgroup of G lies in one, and their number n_p divides m and satisfies n_p≡1 (mod p).

title: Degeneracy maps between modular curves X₀(N)→X₀(M)
description: For positive integers d and M with dM|N, the degeneracy map B_d:X₀(N)→X₀(M) over ℚ sends an elliptic curve E with cyclic subgroup C of order N to E/C[d] with the subgroup of order M of the image of C, C[d] being the subgroup of order d of C. It extends to the compactified curves, and on the upper half-plane it is induced by τ↦dτ.

title: New quotient J₀(N)^new of the Jacobian of X₀(N)
description: Let J₀(N) be the Jacobian of X₀(N) over ℚ. Its old subvariety is the abelian subvariety generated by the images of the homomorphisms J₀(M)→J₀(N) induced by pullback of divisors along the degeneracy maps B_d:X₀(N)→X₀(M), for all M|N with M<N and d|N/M. The new quotient J₀(N)^new is the quotient of J₀(N) by its old subvariety.

title: Optimal quotient of an abelian variety
description: An optimal quotient of an abelian variety J over a field k is a surjective homomorphism J→A onto an abelian variety A whose kernel is connected, hence an abelian subvariety B, so that A≅J/B. An optimal quotient of a quotient J→J′ is a composite J→J′→A with J′→A optimal.

title: Formal immersion of schemes at a point
