description: A morphism f:X→Y of noetherian schemes of finite type is a formal immersion at x∈X if the induced map of completed local rings Ô_(Y,f(x))→Ô_(X,x) is surjective; equivalently f induces an isomorphism of residue fields k(f(x))≅k(x) and is formally unramified at x.

title: Mazur’s formal immersion of X₀(N) into an optimal new quotient at the cusp ∞
description: Let m be the largest square dividing N, J₀(N)→A a nontrivial optimal quotient of the new quotient J₀(N)^new, and f the morphism over ℤ[1/m] from the smooth locus of the minimal regular model of X₀(N) to the Néron model of A extending x↦class of (x)−(∞). Then f is a formal immersion along the cusp section ∞ in every residue characteristic p≠2.

title: Raynaud’s specialization lemma for finite flat group schemes
description: Let R be a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) whose absolute ramification index e satisfies e<p−1, and G a finite flat commutative group scheme over R. Then every x∈G(R) has the same order as its reduction in G(k), k the residue field. More generally a homomorphism of finite flat R-group schemes that is injective on generic fibres is a closed immersion.

title: Deligne–Rapoport model of X₀(N) over ℤ
description: The Deligne–Rapoport compactified coarse moduli scheme X₀(N)/ℤ of generalized elliptic curves with a Γ₀(N)-structure is a proper flat curve over ℤ with generic fibre X₀(N)/ℚ, smooth over ℤ[1/N]. The cusps 0 and ∞ extend to ℤ-sections in its smooth locus, the j-map to ℙ¹_ℤ has the cuspidal locus as preimage of j=∞, and the Tate curve identifies the formal completion along ∞ with Spf ℤ[[q]].

title: De Rham property of the p-adic Tate module of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the rational p-adic Tate module V_pA is a de Rham representation of G_K (Fontaine), and D_dR(V_pA)/Fil⁰D_dR(V_pA) is identified with the tangent space of A at the origin.

title: Bloch–Kato exponential map
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a de Rham representation V of G_K, the Bloch–Kato exponential exp:D_dR(V)/Fil⁰D_dR(V)→H¹(K,V) is the connecting map of the fundamental exact sequence 0→ℚ_p→B_cris^(φ=1)⊕B_dR⁺→B_dR→0 tensored with V. Its image is H¹_e(K,V)⊆H¹_f(K,V), and H¹_f(K,V)/H¹_e(K,V)≅D_cris(V)/(1−φ)D_cris(V).

title: Compatibility of the Bloch–Kato exponential with the exponential of a formal group
description: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p and G a commutative formal Lie group of finite height over O_K with rational Tate module V. Then V is de Rham, D_dR(V)/Fil⁰ is the tangent space of G_K, and the Bloch–Kato exponential agrees with the classical exponential tan(G_K)→G(O_K)⊗ℚ followed by the Kummer coboundary G(O_K)⊗ℚ→H¹(K,V); in particular H¹_e(K,V)=H¹_f(K,V).

title: Grothendieck’s semistable reduction theorem for abelian varieties
description: An abelian variety over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring acquires semistable reduction after a finite separable extension: the identity component of the special fibre of its Néron model becomes an extension of an abelian variety by a torus.

title: Weil’s Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties over finite fields
description: For an abelian variety B over 𝔽_q and a prime ℓ∤q, the eigenvalues of the q-power Frobenius on the Tate module T_ℓB are algebraic integers all of whose complex conjugates have absolute value q^(1/2). In particular 1 is not an eigenvalue.

title: Mattuck’s theorem on points of an abelian variety over a p-adic field
description: For an abelian variety A of dimension d over a finite extension K of ℚ_p, the group A(K) is compact and contains an open subgroup of finite index isomorphic to ℤ_p^(d[K:ℚ_p]), given by the formal group logarithm. Hence A(K) has no nonzero divisible elements and A(K)⊗ℚ_ℓ=0 for ℓ≠p.

title: Eisenstein ideal of the Hecke algebra of prime level
description: For a prime N, let 𝕋⊂End(J₀(N)) be Mazur’s Hecke algebra, the subring generated by the Hecke operators T_ℓ (ℓ≠N) and the Atkin–Lehner involution w. The Eisenstein ideal 𝔍⊂𝕋 is generated by 1+ℓ−T_ℓ for all primes ℓ≠N and by 1+w; the prime ideals of 𝕋 containing 𝔍 are the Eisenstein primes.

title: Eisenstein quotient of J₀(N) at prime level
description: For a prime N with Hecke algebra 𝕋 and Eisenstein ideal 𝔍, let γ_𝔍 be the kernel of the map from 𝕋 to its 𝔍-adic completion and γ_𝔍J₀(N) the abelian subvariety generated by the images αJ₀(N), α∈γ_𝔍. Mazur’s Eisenstein quotient is J̃=J₀(N)/γ_𝔍J₀(N), an optimal quotient of J₀(N) over ℚ on which 𝕋 acts through the components of Spec 𝕋 meeting the support of 𝔍.

title: Cuspidal subgroup of J₀(N) at prime level
description: For a prime N, the cusps 0 and ∞ of X₀(N) are ℚ-rational, and the cuspidal subgroup C⊂J₀(N)(ℚ) is the subgroup generated by the class of the degree-zero divisor (0)−(∞).

title: Rational torsion of J₀(N) and its Eisenstein quotient at prime level
description: For a prime N, the rational torsion of J₀(N) is its cuspidal subgroup C (Ogg’s conjecture, proved by Mazur), and the natural projections induce isomorphisms C=J₀(N)(ℚ)_tors→J⁻(ℚ)_tors→J̃(ℚ)_tors, where J⁻=J₀(N)/(1+w)J₀(N) and J̃ is the Eisenstein quotient.

title: Mazur’s admissible group schemes over ℤ
description: For a prime N, put S=Spec ℤ and S′=Spec ℤ[1/N]. An admissible p-group over S is a commutative quasi-finite separated flat S-group scheme, finite flat over S′ and killed by a power of p, whose restriction to S′ has a filtration by finite flat subgroup schemes with successive quotients isomorphic to ℤ/p or µ_p.

title: Mazur’s flat-cohomology bound for admissible groups
description: For an admissible p-group G over S=Spec ℤ, write hⁱ(G)=log_p#Hⁱ_fppf(S,G), δ(G) for its defect (log_p of the order of G over S′ minus log_p of the order of its fibre at N) and α(G) for the number of constituents ℤ/p in an admissible filtration. Then h¹(G)−h⁰(G)≤δ(G)−α(G).

title: Admissibility of Eisenstein torsion in J₀(N)
description: For a prime N and a maximal ideal 𝔓 of Mazur’s Hecke algebra 𝕋, the Jordan–Hölder constituents of the Galois module J₀(N)[𝔓] are one-dimensional over 𝕋/𝔓 exactly when 𝔓 is an Eisenstein prime; in that case the closure of J₀(N)[𝔓^r] in the Néron model is an admissible group scheme for every r.

title: Rank-one Tate modules of J₀(N) over completed Hecke algebras
description: For a prime N and a maximal ideal 𝔓 of 𝕋 of residue characteristic p≠N, let J_𝔓 be the 𝔓-component of the p-divisible group of the Néron model of J₀(N). The Tate modules of the toric part of its fibre at N and of the corresponding defect module are 𝕋_𝔓-modules of rank one; if J_𝔓 is ordinary at p (as when T_p∉𝔓, e.g. for Eisenstein primes), the Tate modules of its étale and multiplicative parts are 𝕋_𝔓-modules of rank one.

title: Fppf cohomology of a commutative group scheme
description: For a scheme S and a commutative S-group scheme G, the fppf cohomology groups Hⁱ_fppf(S,G) are the derived-functor cohomology groups of the sheaf represented by G on the big fppf site of S, whose coverings are jointly surjective families of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Short exact sequences of fppf sheaves, such as 0→G[n]→G→G→0 for n surjective, give long exact cohomology sequences.

title: P-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group
description: For a prime p and a scheme S, a p-divisible group of height h over S is an inductive system of finite locally free commutative S-group schemes G_ν of order p^(νh) with closed immersions identifying G_ν with the p^ν-torsion of G_(ν+1). For an abelian scheme A over S, A[p^∞]=(A[p^ν])_ν is p-divisible of height 2 dim A.

title: Decomposition of the p-adic completion of a finite ℤ-algebra
description: Let T be a commutative ring finitely generated as a ℤ-module and p a prime. Then T⊗ℤ_p is the product of the completions T_𝔪 of T at the finitely many maximal ideals 𝔪 containing p, the factors being cut out by orthogonal idempotents e_𝔪 with ∑e_𝔪=1.

title: Support of a module over a commutative ring
description: The support of a module M over a commutative ring A is the set of prime ideals 𝔭 of A containing the annihilator ideal Ann(x) of some x∈M, equivalently those with localization M_𝔭≠0. For finitely generated M it is the closed subset V(Ann M) of Spec A.

title: Torsion of positive-degree cohomology of a profinite group
description: For a profinite group G and a discrete G-module M, the cohomology groups Hⁱ(G,M) are torsion for all i≥1, being direct limits of cohomology groups of finite quotients G/U, each killed by the order of G/U.

title: Standard Néron n-gon
description: For n≥1 and a base ring R, the standard n-gon over R is obtained from n copies of ℙ¹_R indexed by ℤ/n by gluing the section ∞ of the i-th copy to the section 0 of the (i+1)-th; for n=1 it is ℙ¹_R with 0 and ∞ identified, the nodal cubic. Its smooth locus is 𝔾_m×ℤ/n, a commutative group scheme acting on the polygon by rotations, and µ_n⊂𝔾_m lies in it.

title: Generalized elliptic curve (Deligne–Rapoport)
description: A generalized elliptic curve over a scheme S is a proper flat morphism E→S of finite presentation whose geometric fibres are either smooth connected curves of genus one or standard Néron polygons, together with a morphism E^sm×_S E→E that makes the smooth locus E^sm a commutative S-group scheme and is an action of E^sm on E inducing rotations on the singular geometric fibres.

title: Tate curve over ℤ[[q]]
description: The Tate curve Tate(q) is the generalized elliptic curve over ℤ[[q]] given by y²+xy=x³+a₄(q)x+a₆(q) with a₄=−5∑_(n≥1)σ₃(n)qⁿ and a₆=−∑_(n≥1)(5σ₃(n)+7σ₅(n))/12·qⁿ (integral coefficients), whose discriminant is q∏_(n≥1)(1−qⁿ)²⁴. Its fibre over ℤ((q)) is an elliptic curve, its fibre at q=0 is the standard 1-gon, and µ_N⊂𝔾_m in that fibre extends to a closed subgroup scheme µ_N↪Tate(q)^sm.

title: Formal completion of a scheme along a closed subscheme
description: For a locally noetherian scheme X and a closed subscheme Z with ideal sheaf ℐ, the formal completion X̂_Z is the topological space of Z with the sheaf of rings lim←O_X/ℐⁿ. For X=Spec A and Z=V(I) it is the formal spectrum Spf Â of the I-adic completion; e.g. the completion of the affine line over ℤ along its zero section is Spf ℤ[[q]].

title: Cartier dual of a finite Galois module
description: For a field K of characteristic zero with algebraic closure K̄, and a finite discrete G_K-module M, the Cartier (Tate) dual is M′=Hom(M,μ), the group of homomorphisms from M to the roots of unity μ⊂K̄^×, with G_K acting by (g·f)(m)=g(f(g⁻¹m)). It is a finite discrete G_K-module of the same order as M. If K is a number field, M is a G_(K,S)-module and S contains the places above the primes dividing #M, then M′ is again a G_(K,S)-module.

title: Invariant isomorphism for the Brauer group of a local field
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k with separable closure k̄, there is a canonical isomorphism inv_k:H²(G_k,k̄^×)→ℚ/ℤ (the invariant map): every class is split by the maximal unramified extension k̃, and on H²(Gal(k̃/k),k̃^×) the map is induced by the normalized valuation and evaluation of characters at Frobenius. If k has characteristic zero, the Kummer sequences identify H²(G_k,μ), for the group μ of all roots of unity in k̄, with H²(G_k,k̄^×), so H²(G_k,μ)≅ℚ/ℤ canonically.

title: Class field axiom for cyclic extensions of local fields
description: For a finite cyclic extension K/k of nonarchimedean local fields, the Tate cohomology of K^× satisfies #Ĥ⁰(Gal(K/k),K^×)=[K:k] and H¹(Gal(K/k),K^×)=1; equivalently the Herbrand quotient of K^× equals [K:k].

title: Cohomological triviality of units in unramified extensions of local fields
description: For an unramified Galois extension K/k of nonarchimedean local fields, the unit group U_K and the principal units U_K¹ are cohomologically trivial Gal(K/k)-modules: all their Tate cohomology groups vanish for every subgroup. If K/k is tamely ramified, U_K¹ is still cohomologically trivial.

title: Injectivity of restriction to a Sylow subgroup on p-primary cohomology
description: For a profinite (or finite) group G, a discrete G-module A, a prime p and a p-Sylow subgroup G_p, restriction Ĥⁿ(G,A)(p)→Ĥⁿ(G_p,A) on the p-primary part is injective for n≥1 (all n if G is finite); more generally restriction to a closed subgroup of index prime to p is injective on p-primary parts.

title: Corestriction after restriction is multiplication by the index
description: For an open subgroup U of a profinite group G and a discrete G-module A, cor∘res:Hⁿ(G,A)→Hⁿ(U,A)→Hⁿ(G,A) is multiplication by the index (G:U) in every degree n; if U is normal, res∘cor is the norm N_(G/U).

title: Tate’s duality theorem for profinite groups
description: Let G be a profinite group with cd_P G=n<∞ for a set of primes P, and D_P its dualizing module at P. Then cup product and the trace map give isomorphisms Hⁱ(G,Hom(A,D_P))≅H^(n−i)(G,A)^* for all i and all finite P-primary discrete G-modules A if and only if lim→_U Hⁱ(U,ℤ/pℤ)^*=0 for all p∈P and all i<n, the limit over open subgroups U dual to corestriction; G is then a duality group at P of dimension n.

title: Dualizing module of the absolute Galois group of a local field
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k, the dualizing module D=lim→_(K,n)H²(K,ℤ/nℤ)^* of the category of discrete torsion G_k-modules is canonically isomorphic, as a G_k-module, to the group μ of all roots of unity in the separable closure (the prime-to-p part if char k=p>0).

title: Cohomological dimension of a nonarchimedean local field
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k and a prime p different from char k, the absolute Galois group has cd_p(G_k)=2 and strict cohomological dimension scd_p(G_k)=2; if p=char k then cd_p(G_k)=1. Moreover cd_p(L)≤1 for every algebraic extension L/k of degree divisible by p^∞.

title: Local reciprocity law of local class field theory
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k and a finite Galois extension K/k there is a canonical isomorphism k^×/N_(K/k)K^×≅Gal(K/k)^ab (the local reciprocity map), and the norm groups N_(K/k)K^× of finite Galois extensions are exactly the open subgroups of finite index in k^×.

title: Finiteness of Galois cohomology of a local field with finite coefficients
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k and a finite discrete G_k-module A of order prime to char k, the groups Hⁱ(G_k,A) are finite for all i≥0; if A is a G_k-module finitely generated over ℤ with torsion of order prime to char k, then H¹(G_k,A) is finite.

title: Tate’s global duality theorem for S-idèle class coefficients
description: For a number field k, a nonempty set S of places containing the archimedean ones, G_S=Gal(k_S/k) and C_S the S-idèle class group of k_S (with norm-one part C_S⁰), and a discrete G_S-module A finitely generated over ℤ, cup product into H²(G_S,C_S⁰)≅(1/#G_S)ℤ/ℤ induces topological isomorphisms Ĥⁱ(G_S,Hom(A,C_S⁰))≅Ĥ^(2−i)(G_S,A)^∨ for all i≤0, and for all i if A is ℤ-free.

title: Poitou–Tate duality of Tate–Shafarevich groups of a Galois module
description: For a number field k, a set S of places containing the archimedean ones, and a finitely generated G_S-module A whose torsion has order invertible on S, with A′=Hom(A,O_S^×), cup product induces a perfect pairing of finite groups Ш¹(G_S,A′)×Ш²(G_S,A)→ℚ/ℤ, where Шⁱ(G_S,A) is the kernel of the localization map Hⁱ(G_S,A)→∏_(v∈S)Hⁱ(k_v,A).

title: Tate’s local Euler–Poincaré characteristic formula for finite modules
description: For a nonarchimedean local field k and a finite discrete G_k-module A of order a prime to char k, the groups Hⁱ(k,A) are finite and #H⁰(k,A)·#H²(k,A)/#H¹(k,A)=‖a‖_k, the normalized absolute value of a; for k/ℚ_p finite this is p^(−[k:ℚ_p]v_p(a)), and it equals 1 if a is prime to the residue characteristic.

title: Euler–Poincaré formula for finite Galois modules over ℝ and ℂ
description: For k=ℝ or ℂ and a finite G_k-module A of order a with dual A′=Hom(A,μ), #H⁰(k,A)·#H⁰(k,A′)/#H¹(k,A)=‖a‖_k, where ‖a‖_ℝ=a and ‖a‖_ℂ=a²; equivalently the Tate-cohomology quotient #Ĥ⁰(k,A)/#H¹(k,A) times #H⁰(k,A′) equals ‖a‖_k.

title: Triviality of the Herbrand quotient of a finite module
description: For a finite cyclic group G and a finite G-module A, the Herbrand quotient h(G,A)=#Ĥ⁰(G,A)/#Ĥ¹(G,A) equals 1. More generally, for commuting endomorphisms f,g of a finite abelian group with fg=gf=0, #(ker f/im g)=#(ker g/im f).

title: Simple p-primary modules of a pro-p group
description: For a pro-p group G, every simple discrete p-primary G-module is isomorphic to ℤ/pℤ with trivial action. Equivalently, a nonzero discrete p-primary G-module has a nonzero G-fixed element, so finite p-primary G-modules have composition series with factors ℤ/pℤ.

title: Class formation of S-idèle classes of a number field
description: For a number field k and a set S of places containing the archimedean places, the pair (G_S,C_S), with G_S the Galois group of the maximal extension unramified outside S and C_S the S-idèle class group of k_S, is a class formation: H¹(G(K|L),C_S(K))=0 and H²(G(K|L),C_S(K))≅(1/[K:L])ℤ/ℤ compatibly with restriction for finite Galois subextensions K/L of k_S/k.

title: Tate’s global Euler–Poincaré characteristic formula for finite modules
description: For a number field k, a finite set S of places containing the archimedean places, and a finite G_S-module A whose order is a unit away from S, #H⁰(G_S,A)·#H²(G_S,A)/#H¹(G_S,A)=∏_(v|∞)#H⁰(k_v,A)/‖#A‖_v, where ‖a‖_v=a for v real and a² for v complex.

title: Tate’s comparison of continuous cohomology of a p-adic representation and its lattices
description: Let G be a profinite group whose cohomology groups with finite p-primary coefficients are finite, V a p-adic representation of G and Λ⊂V a G-stable ℤ_p-lattice. Then the continuous cohomology Hⁱ(G,Λ) is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module, Hⁱ(G,Λ)≅lim←_n Hⁱ(G,Λ/pⁿΛ), and the natural map Hⁱ(G,Λ)⊗_(ℤ_p)ℚ_p→Hⁱ(G,V) is an isomorphism (Tate).

title: Cohomological dimension of the Galois group unramified outside S
description: For a number field k, a prime p and a set S of places containing the archimedean places and those above p, cd_p(G_(k,S))≤2 provided k is totally imaginary when p=2; in general, for i≥3 and finite p-primary A, restriction gives Hⁱ(G_(k,S),A)≅⊕_(v real)Hⁱ(k_v,A).

title: Tate–Sen theorem on the Galois cohomology of ℂ_p(r)
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and r∈ℤ, let ℂ_p(r) be ℂ_p with G_K acting semilinearly twisted by χ_cyc^r. Then H⁰(G_K,ℂ_p)=K and H⁰(G_K,ℂ_p(r))=0 for r≠0; in continuous cohomology H¹(G_K,ℂ_p(r))=0 for r≠0, and H¹(G_K,ℂ_p) is one-dimensional over K, spanned by the class of log∘χ_cyc, so cup product with log χ_cyc is an isomorphism H⁰(G_K,ℂ_p)→H¹(G_K,ℂ_p).

title: Vanishing of the cohomology of ℂ_p-representations over the cyclotomic tower
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p, its cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower K_∞ and H=Gal(K̄/K_∞), and a finite-dimensional ℂ_p-vector space W with continuous semilinear G_K-action, Hⁿ_cont(H,W)=0 for n≥1, and inflation Hⁿ(Gal(K_∞/K),W^H)→Hⁿ(G_K,W) is an isomorphism for all n≥0 (Tate–Sen formalism).

title: Tate’s normalized traces on the cyclotomic tower
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p with cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower K_n, the normalized traces p^(−m)Tr_(K_(n+m)/K_n) extend to continuous K_n-linear projections R_n of the completion K̂_∞ onto K_n, commuting with Gal(K_∞/K). On X_n=ker R_n, γ−1 is bijective with bounded inverse for a generator γ of Gal(K_∞/K_n) (n large), and for a 1-unit λ∈K that is not a root of unity, γ−λ is bijective on K̂_∞.

title: Completed unramified descent for semilinear modules
description: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k, and R′ the completion of its maximal unramified extension, with G_k acting. For a finitely generated R′-module M with continuous semilinear G_k-action, M^(G_k) is finitely generated over R and R′⊗_R M^(G_k)→M is an isomorphism; in particular M↦M^(G_k) is exact.

title: Serre–Tate inequality for Hodge–Tate multiplicities
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p and a continuous semilinear ℂ_p-representation W of G_K, the natural map ⊕_(q∈ℤ)ℂ_p(−q)⊗_K(W(q))^(G_K)→W is injective. Hence for a p-adic representation V, ∑_q dim_K(ℂ_p(q)⊗V)^(G_K)≤dim V, with equality exactly when V is Hodge–Tate.

title: Deligne’s λ-adic Galois representation of a newform
description: For a normalized newform f=∑a_nqⁿ of weight k≥2, level N and character ε, with coefficient field F, and a finite prime λ of F over p, there is a continuous semisimple representation ρ_(f,λ):G_ℚ→GL₂(F_λ), unique up to isomorphism, unramified outside Np, such that for every prime ℓ∤Np an arithmetic Frobenius at ℓ has trace a_ℓ and determinant ε(ℓ)ℓ^(k−1) (Deligne; Eichler–Shimura for k=2). Kato’s realization V_(F_λ)(f), cut out of the étale cohomology of modular curves, is its contragredient: det(1−Fr_ℓ⁻¹u|V_(F_λ)(f))=1−a_ℓu+ε(ℓ)ℓ^(k−1)u².

title: Completed group algebra of a profinite group
description: For a profinite group G and the valuation ring O of a finite extension of ℚ_p, the completed group algebra (Iwasawa algebra) is O[[G]]=lim←_U O[G/U], the inverse limit of the finite group algebras over open normal subgroups U, with its compact topology. For G=Gal(ℚ(ζ_(p^∞))/ℚ)≅ℤ_p^× it is Kato’s Λ=O[[G_∞]], a two-dimensional complete semilocal ring.

title: Iwasawa cohomology over the cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower
description: For a finitely generated ℤ_p-module T with continuous G_ℚ-action unramified at almost all primes, Kato sets H^q(ℤ[ζ_(pⁿ),1/p],T)=lim←_m H^q_ét(Spec ℤ[ζ_(pⁿ),1/p],j_*(T/p^mT)), j the inclusion of the generic point, and H^q(T)=lim←_n H^q(ℤ[ζ_(pⁿ),1/p],T) under corestriction (trace) maps; similarly H^q_loc(T)=lim←_n H^q(ℚ_p(ζ_(pⁿ)),T) in continuous Galois cohomology. These are modules over Λ=ℤ_p[[Gal(ℚ(ζ_(p^∞))/ℚ)]], and H^q(V)=H^q(T)⊗ℚ for a lattice T in V.

title: Height of a prime ideal
description: The height of a prime ideal 𝔭 of a commutative ring R is the supremum of the lengths r of chains of prime ideals 𝔭₀⊊𝔭₁⊊⋯⊊𝔭_r=𝔭; equivalently the Krull dimension of the localization R_𝔭.

title: Localization of a module at a prime ideal
description: For a module M over a commutative ring R and a prime ideal 𝔭, the localization M_𝔭=(R∖𝔭)⁻¹M consists of fractions m/s with s∉𝔭, where m/s=m′/s′ when t(s′m−sm′)=0 for some t∉𝔭; it is an R_𝔭-module, isomorphic to M⊗_R R_𝔭.

title: Euler system over cyclotomic fields (Kato’s definition)
description: Let L/ℚ_p be finite with valuation ring O_L, T a free O_L-module of finite rank with continuous O_L-linear G_ℚ-action unramified outside a finite set Σ of primes containing p, and Ξ={m≥1: the primes dividing m and lying in Σ are exactly p}. An Euler system for (T,L,Σ) is a family z_m∈H¹(ℤ[ζ_m,1/p],T), m∈Ξ, such that for m|m′ the norm (corestriction) sends z_(m′) to (∏_ℓ P_ℓ(σ_ℓ⁻¹))z_m, ℓ over primes dividing m′ but not m, where P_ℓ(t)=det(1−Fr_ℓ⁻¹t|T) and σ_ℓ is the arithmetic Frobenius of ℓ in Gal(ℚ(ζ_m)/ℚ) acting through O_L[Gal(ℚ(ζ_m)/ℚ)].

title: Crystalline p-adic representation
description: For a finite extension K of ℚ_p with maximal unramified subfield K₀, a p-adic representation V of G_K is crystalline if D_cris(V)=(B_cris⊗_(ℚ_p)V)^(G_K), a K₀-vector space with Frobenius φ induced from B_cris, has dimension dim_(ℚ_p)V (B_cris-admissibility).

title: Algebra of formal power series in noncommuting variables
description: For a set X and a field k, k⟨⟨X⟩⟩ consists of all formal sums ∑a_w w over the words w in X, with coefficientwise addition and the product extending concatenation; it is the degree completion ∏ₙ of the free algebra k⟨X⟩. If k has characteristic zero, exp(z)=∑zⁿ/n! and log(1+z)=∑(−1)ⁿ⁺¹zⁿ/n are defined on the ideal 𝔪 of series without constant term and are mutually inverse bijections 𝔪→1+𝔪.

title: Friedrichs’s theorem on primitive elements of an enveloping algebra
description: Over a field of characteristic zero, the elements u of the universal enveloping algebra U(𝔤) of a Lie algebra with Δu=u⊗1+1⊗u for the coproduct are exactly the elements of 𝔤. Since the free associative algebra on X is the enveloping algebra of the free Lie algebra on X, the latter is the set of primitive elements of the free associative algebra.

title: Finiteness of extensions of bounded degree of a p-adic field
description: Let K be a field of characteristic zero complete for a discrete valuation with finite residue field, that is, a finite extension of ℚ_p. For every n≥1 there are, up to K-isomorphism, only finitely many field extensions of K of degree n. The proof uses Krasner’s lemma and compactness of the space of Eisenstein polynomials of degree n.

title: Hermite’s theorem on number fields of bounded discriminant
description: For every B>0 there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many number fields K with |d_K|≤B (Hermite 1857). Minkowski’s bound shows that the degree is bounded in terms of |d_K|, and for fixed degree a generator with bounded conjugates is found by Minkowski’s lattice point theorem.

title: Tower formula for discriminants of number fields
description: For number fields K⊆L, the absolute discriminants and the relative discriminant ideal satisfy |d_L|=|d_K|^[L:K]·N_(K/ℚ)(𝔡_(L/K)), where N_(K/ℚ) is the absolute norm of ideals. In particular |d_L| is bounded once [L:K] and the norm of 𝔡_(L/K) are bounded.

title: Normalization of an integral scheme
description: For an integral scheme X with function field K, the normalization ν:X^ν→X glues the spectra of the integral closures of the rings O_X(U) in K over the affine opens U⊆X. X^ν is an integral scheme with function field K whose local rings are integrally closed domains, ν is affine and dominant, and ν is universal for dominant morphisms to X from such schemes. Normalizing in a finite extension L of K is defined in the same way.

title: Equivalence between integral varieties with dominant rational maps and finitely generated field extensions
description: For a field k, sending an integral variety X over k to its function field k(X) is an anti-equivalence from integral k-varieties with dominant rational maps to finitely generated field extensions of k with k-embeddings. Every finitely generated K/k is the fraction field of a finitely generated k-algebra, hence the function field of an affine variety.

title: Projective compactification of a reduced curve over a field
description: Let X be a reduced separated scheme of finite type and dimension at most one over a field k. There is an open immersion X→X̄ with dense image into a closed subscheme X̄ of some projective space over k such that X̄∖X is a finite set of closed points whose local rings are discrete valuation rings. A proper scheme of dimension at most one over k is projective.

title: Global functions detect geometric connectedness of a proper scheme
description: For a proper scheme X over a field k, H⁰(X,O_X) is a finite-dimensional k-algebra, a product of Artinian local algebras indexed by the connected components of X. If X is geometrically reduced, then X is geometrically connected if and only if H⁰(X,O_X)=k.

title: Picard group of a scheme
description: For a scheme X, Pic(X) is the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible O_X-modules under tensor product, the inverse of L being its dual L^∨=Hom(L,O_X). A morphism f:Y→X induces the pullback homomorphism f*:Pic(X)→Pic(Y).

title: Jacobian variety of a smooth projective curve
description: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C of genus g over a field k, let P⁰_C(T) be the group of invertible sheaves on C×_k T of degree zero on every fibre modulo pullbacks of invertible sheaves on T. The Jacobian J=Jac(C) is the g-dimensional abelian variety over k with a morphism of functors P⁰_C→J that is an isomorphism whenever C(T)≠∅. It exists without a rational point, is unique up to unique isomorphism and commutes with field extension; J(k′)=Pic⁰(C_(k′)) when C(k′)≠∅.

title: Polarization of an abelian variety
description: A polarization of an abelian variety A over a field k is an isogeny λ:A→A^∨ to the dual abelian variety that, after base change to an algebraic closure k̄, equals φ_L for an ample invertible sheaf L on A_k̄. It is principal if λ is an isomorphism. A principally polarized abelian variety is a pair (A,λ), and an isomorphism (A,λ)→(A′,λ′) is an isomorphism β:A→A′ with β^∨∘λ′∘β=λ.

title: Canonical principal polarization of a Jacobian
description: Let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g≥1 over k with Jacobian J. Over k̄ choose P∈C(k̄) with Abel–Jacobi map ι_P:C→J and let Θ be the theta divisor, the image of C^(g−1)→J, (P₁,…,P_(g−1))↦∑ι_P(Pᵢ). Changing P translates Θ, so λ_C=φ_(L(Θ)):J→J^∨ does not depend on P and is defined over k; it is an isomorphism, the canonical principal polarization of J.

title: Jacobian scheme of a smooth proper relative curve
description: Let π:𝒞→S be proper and smooth with geometrically connected one-dimensional fibres. Let P⁰_(𝒞/S)(T) be the group of invertible sheaves on 𝒞×_S T of degree zero on all fibres modulo pullbacks from T. The Jacobian scheme Pic⁰_(𝒞/S) is an S-group scheme J with a morphism of functors P⁰_(𝒞/S)→J that is injective and an isomorphism whenever 𝒞×_S T→T has a section. It is unique, commutes with base change, and its fibre over s∈S is the Jacobian variety of the curve 𝒞_s.

title: Symmetric power of a smooth curve
description: For a smooth projective curve C over a field and r≥1, the symmetric power C^(r)=C^r/S_r is the quotient by the symmetric group permuting the factors. It is a smooth projective variety of dimension r whose points over an algebraically closed field are the effective divisors of degree r on C; it represents the functor of relative effective divisors of degree r.

title: Hyperelliptic curve
description: A smooth projective connected curve of genus g≥2 over an algebraically closed field is hyperelliptic if it admits a finite morphism of degree two to ℙ¹, equivalently a linear system of degree two and dimension one; such a linear system is then unique and its fibres are exchanged by the hyperelliptic involution.

title: Pullback of translates of the theta divisor to a curve
description: Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g≥1 over an algebraically closed field, f:C→J the Abel–Jacobi map attached to a point, Θ=W^(g−1) the image of C^(g−1) and κ the image of a canonical divisor. If a∈J(k) and f(C) is not contained in the translate Θ_a, there is a unique effective divisor D(a) of degree g with f(D(a))=a+κ, and the pullback of Θ_a to C is the divisor D(a) (Riemann’s theorem on the theta divisor).

title: Representability of the Picard functor of a projective flat curve
description: Let X→S be a projective flat curve locally of finite presentation whose geometric fibres are reduced and irreducible. Then the relative Picard functor Pic_(X/S) is represented by a smooth separated S-scheme, the disjoint union of open and closed subschemes (Pic_(X/S))ⁿ of line bundles of degree n; (Pic_(X/S))⁰ is the identity component Pic⁰_(X/S), quasi-projective over S, and each (Pic_(X/S))ⁿ is a Pic⁰_(X/S)-torsor (Grothendieck).

title: Properness of the Jacobian scheme of a smooth proper curve
description: If X→S is a proper smooth morphism whose geometric fibres are connected curves and the identity component Pic⁰_(X/S) of its Picard functor is representable, then Pic⁰_(X/S) is proper over S; this is checked with the valuative criterion, extending degree-zero line bundles from the generic fibre over a discrete valuation ring.

title: Projectivity of proper relative curves with integral fibres
description: Let X→S be a proper flat curve of finite presentation whose geometric fibres are reduced irreducible curves of genus g and which is a relative complete intersection. Then its relative dualizing sheaf is invertible; for g≥2 it is S-ample, and for g=0,1 a suitable invertible sheaf is S-ample, so X→S is projective. In particular proper smooth curves with connected fibres are projective, at least étale locally on S.

title: Effectivity of descent for quasi-projective schemes with ample sheaves
description: Let S′→S be faithfully flat and quasi-compact. A descent datum on a scheme X′ quasi-projective over S′ that is compatible with a descent datum on an S′-ample invertible sheaf on X′ is effective: X′ descends to an S-scheme X, quasi-projective over S. Group structures and properties such as properness and smoothness descend as well.

title: Extended Bruhat–Tits building of a reductive group over a local field
description: For a connected reductive group G over a nonarchimedean local field F, the reduced building B(G,F) is the building of the valued root datum of G(F) relative to a maximal F-split torus. The extended building is B¹=B×V¹, V¹ the real dual of the rational characters of G, with g·(x,v)=(gx,v+θ(g)) where ⟨θ(g),χ⟩=−ω(χ(g)). Its apartments A(S)×V¹ correspond to maximal F-split tori S; a point is special if its image in A(S) is a special point. The stabilizer of (x,v) is the stabilizer of x in G(F)¹=ker θ.

title: Iwasawa decomposition with respect to an Iwahori subgroup
description: Let G be connected reductive over a field with a discrete valuation whose ring of integers is Henselian with perfect residue field, S a maximal split torus with normalizer N, U the unipotent radical of a minimal parabolic subgroup containing the centralizer of S, and P_C the Iwahori subgroup of a chamber C in the apartment of S. Then G(k)=U(k)·N(k)·P_C.

title: Parahoric subgroup of a reductive group over a local field
description: For a connected reductive group G over a discretely valued field k with Henselian integers and perfect residue field, and a point or facet x of its Bruhat–Tits building, the parahoric subgroup P_x=G(k)⁰_x is the connected stabilizer of x, the group of o-points of the connected Néron-type model of the stabilizer; it is contained in the stabilizer G(k)¹_x with finite index. For a chamber it is the Iwahori subgroup.

title: Maximality of vertex stabilizers in the Bruhat–Tits building
description: For a connected reductive group G over a discretely valued field with Henselian integers and perfect residue field, every bounded subgroup of G(k) fixes a point of the building B(G), and for a vertex x the stabilizer G(k)¹_x is a maximal bounded subgroup of G(k); it is open. Every maximal bounded subgroup has the form G(k)¹_y.

title: Compactness of closed bounded subsets of points over a local field
description: For an affine variety X over a locally compact nondiscrete valued field k, a subset of X(k) is bounded if its coordinates are bounded in some, equivalently any, affine embedding; closed bounded subsets of X(k) are compact. Hence the bounded open subgroups of G(k) are exactly its compact open subgroups.

title: Reductive integral models are hyperspecial point stabilizers
description: Let G be a connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field k with valuation ring o. For every reductive o-group scheme 𝒢 with generic fiber G there is a hyperspecial vertex x of the Bruhat–Tits building such that the identity of G extends to an isomorphism 𝒢≅𝒢⁰_x with the connected parahoric group scheme; for hyperspecial x the stabilizer scheme 𝒢_x is connected, so 𝒢(o) is the full stabilizer G(k)¹_x.

title: Mostow’s self-adjoint realization of a real reductive group
description: For a reductive algebraic ℝ-subgroup G⊆GL_n there is a∈GL_n(ℝ) such that aGa⁻¹ is self-adjoint, i.e. stable under transpose (Mostow).

title: Polar decomposition of the real points of a reductive group
description: For a self-adjoint reductive ℝ-subgroup G⊆GL_n, every element of G(ℝ) factors uniquely as kc with k orthogonal and c positive definite symmetric, both in G(ℝ). Hence K₁=G(ℝ)∩O(n) is a maximal compact subgroup, G(ℝ)/K₁ is homeomorphic to a vector space, every compact subgroup lies in a maximal one, and all maximal compact subgroups of G(ℝ) are conjugate.

title: Iwasawa decomposition of the real general linear group
description: The multiplication map O(n)×A×U→GL_n(ℝ), where A is the group of positive diagonal matrices and U the group of upper unitriangular matrices, is a homeomorphism; existence follows from Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization.

title: Structure and rational conjugacy of minimal parabolic subgroups
description: Let G be connected reductive over a field k and S a maximal k-split torus. For each positive system Φ⁺ of relative roots, Z_G(S)·U_(Φ⁺) is a minimal parabolic k-subgroup with unipotent radical U_(Φ⁺), every minimal parabolic k-subgroup is of this form for some maximal split torus, and any two minimal parabolic k-subgroups are conjugate under G(k) (Borel–Tits).

title: Parabolic subgroups of a Weil restriction
description: For a finite separable field extension L/k and a connected reductive L-group G, P↦R_(L/k)P is a bijection from parabolic L-subgroups of G onto parabolic k-subgroups of R_(L/k)G, preserving inclusions; in particular minimal parabolics correspond, and for L algebraically closed R_(L/k)B is a minimal parabolic k-subgroup for every Borel B.

title: Faltings height of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A of dimension g over a number field K with a semiabelian model 𝒜 over O_K, let ω be the invertible O_K-module s*Ω^g_(𝒜/O_K) metrized at each complex place by ‖α‖²=(i/2)^g∫|α∧ᾱ|. The Faltings height is h(A)=[K:ℚ]⁻¹ times the Arakelov degree of ω; it is invariant under finite extension of K for semistable models (stable height).

title: Faltings’s finiteness of principally polarized abelian varieties of bounded height
description: For a number field K, an integer g and a real c, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of pairs consisting of a semiabelian scheme over O_K with abelian generic fiber of dimension g and a principal polarization of that generic fiber, whose Faltings height is at most c (Faltings 1983, Satz 1).

title: Change of the Faltings height under isogeny
description: If φ:A₁→A₂ is an isogeny of semiabelian schemes over O_K with abelian generic fibers and kernel G (a quasi-finite flat group scheme), then h(A₂)=h(A₁)+½log deg φ−[K:ℚ]⁻¹log #(s*Ω¹_(G/O_K)). In particular exp(2[K:ℚ](h(A₂)−h(A₁))) is a rational number whose numerator and denominator involve only primes dividing deg φ (Faltings 1983, Lemma 5).

title: Finiteness of isogeny classes of abelian varieties with good reduction outside S
description: For a number field K, a finite set S of places and g≥1, there are only finitely many isogeny classes of g-dimensional abelian varieties over K with good reduction outside S (Faltings 1983, Satz 5).

title: Isogeny from a polarized to a principally polarized abelian variety
description: If an abelian variety A over a field k has a polarization λ, then after a finite extension of k there is an isogeny A→B of degree dividing deg λ onto an abelian variety B with a principal polarization, obtained as the quotient by a maximal isotropic subgroup of ker λ for the Weil pairing.

title: Raynaud’s determinant character of a finite flat group scheme
description: Let G be a finite flat group scheme over the ring of integers of a p-adic field K, killed by p, of order p^h. If the ramification of K is small (e<p−1), the Galois action on the top exterior power of G(K̄) is χ^d for the mod-p cyclotomic character χ, where p^d is the order of s*Ω¹_(G); in general this holds on inertia up to a character of finite order (Raynaud 1974).

title: Weil height associated to an invertible sheaf
description: For a projective variety X over a number field K, Weil’s height machine assigns to each invertible sheaf L on X a function h_L:X(K̄)→ℝ, well defined up to a bounded function, such that h_L=h∘φ+O(1) when L≅φ*O(1) for a morphism φ:X→ℙⁿ with h the absolute logarithmic height, and h_(L⊗M)=h_L+h_M+O(1).

title: Symmetric invertible sheaf on an abelian variety
description: An invertible sheaf L on an abelian variety A is symmetric if [−1]*L≅L, where [−1] is the inversion morphism of A; antisymmetric if [−1]*L≅L⁻¹.

title: Quadratic form on an abelian group
description: A function q:Γ→ℝ on an abelian group Γ is a quadratic form if q(−x)=q(x) and ⟨x,y⟩=q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y) is biadditive. Equivalently q satisfies the parallelogram law q(x+y)+q(x−y)=2q(x)+2q(y); then ⟨,⟩ is a symmetric pairing with ⟨x,x⟩=2q(x).

title: Positivity and Northcott finiteness for Weil heights
description: Let X be a projective variety over a number field K and h_L a Weil height. Then h_L is bounded below on the complement of the base locus of L, and if L is ample then for every finite extension K′/K and real B the set {P∈X(K′):h_L(P)≤B} is finite (Weil height machine, parts (e) and (g)).

title: Quasi-parallelogram law for Weil heights on abelian varieties
description: For an abelian variety A over a number field and a symmetric invertible sheaf L, the Weil height satisfies h_L([m]P)=m²h_L(P)+O(1) for each integer m and h_L(P+Q)+h_L(P−Q)=2h_L(P)+2h_L(Q)+O(1), with constants independent of the points.

title: Tate’s limit construction of canonical heights
description: Let φ:X→X be a morphism of a projective variety over a number field and L an invertible sheaf with φ*L≅L^⊗a for some a>1. Then ĥ(P)=lim a⁻ⁿh_L(φⁿ(P)) exists, ĥ=h_L+O(1) and ĥ∘φ=aĥ, and ĥ is the unique function with these two properties (Néron, Tate).

title: Hermite polynomial
description: The n-th Hermite polynomial is H_n(x)=((−1)ⁿ/n!)e^{x²/2}(dⁿ/dxⁿ)e^{−x²/2}, with H₀=1; equivalently exp(tx−t²/2)=∑_{n≥0}tⁿH_n(x). H_n has degree n and leading coefficient 1/n!; many authors use the monic normalization n!H_n.

title: Polynomial Wiener functional
description: For an isonormal Gaussian process W on a real Hilbert space H, a polynomial Wiener functional (polynomial random variable) is a random variable p(W(h₁),…,W(h_n)) with n≥1, h₁,…,h_n∈H and p a real polynomial in n variables.

title: Uniqueness theorem for multivariate Laplace transforms
description: If ν is a finite signed Borel measure on ℝᵐ such that ∫e^{⟨t,x⟩}|ν|(dx)<∞ and ∫e^{⟨t,x⟩}ν(dx)=0 for every t∈ℝᵐ, then ν=0. Thus a Laplace transform finite on all of ℝᵐ determines the measure.

title: Doob–Dynkin factorization lemma
description: If Y is a random vector in ℝᵐ and Z is a real random variable measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by Y, then Z=φ(Y) for some Borel function φ:ℝᵐ→ℝ.

title: Nelson’s hypercontractivity of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup
description: For the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup P_t of an isonormal Gaussian process, 1<p<∞ and t>0, ‖P_tF‖_{q(t)}≤‖F‖_p for all F∈Lᵖ, where q(t)=1+e^{2t}(p−1). Consequently all Lᵖ norms, 1<p<∞, are equivalent on each Wiener chaos.

title: Mehler’s formula for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup
description: If W′ is an independent copy of the isonormal Gaussian process W and F=ψ_F(W), then P_tF=E′[ψ_F(e^{−t}W+√(1−e^{−2t})W′)] for t≥0, where P_t=∑_ne^{−nt}J_n. Hence P_t extends to a positive contraction on Lᵖ for every 1≤p<∞.

title: M. Riesz theorem on Lᵖ boundedness of the Hilbert transform
description: The Hilbert transform Hf(x)=p.v.(1/π)∫f(x−t)t^{−1}dt, defined on test functions, extends to a bounded operator on Lᵖ(ℝ) for every 1<p<∞. It is not bounded on L¹ or L^∞.

title: Chaos characterization of the Malliavin derivative
description: For F in L²(Ω,σ(W),P) with Wiener chaos projections J_nF, F∈D^{1,2} if and only if ∑_n n‖J_nF‖₂²<∞; then E‖DF‖_H²=∑_n n‖J_nF‖₂² and D(J_nF)=J_{n−1}(DF). Thus D maps the n-th chaos into the (n−1)-th H-valued chaos.

title: α-excessive function of a Dirichlet form
description: For a Dirichlet form on L²(X,m) with L² semigroup (T_t) and α>0, a function u∈L²(X,m) is α-excessive if e^{−αt}T_tu≤u m-a.e. for every t>0. Such u are nonnegative; for u in the form domain this is equivalent to E_α(u,v)≥0 for every nonnegative v in the domain.

title: Banach–Saks theorem for Hilbert spaces
description: Every weakly convergent sequence in a Hilbert space has a subsequence whose Cesàro means (u_{n₁}+⋯+u_{n_k})/k converge in norm to the weak limit.

title: Choquet property of the capacity of a Dirichlet form
description: For a Dirichlet form and an admissible reference function h=G₁φ, the capacity Cap_h is a Choquet capacity: it is monotone, Cap_h(⋃A_n)=lim Cap_h(A_n) for increasing sets, Cap_h(⋂K_n)=lim Cap_h(K_n) for decreasing compact sets, and it is countably subadditive.

title: 1-capacity of a regular Dirichlet form
description: For a regular Dirichlet form on L²(X,m), Cap(U)=inf{E₁(u,u): u in the domain, u≥1 m-a.e. on U} for open U (∞ if no such u), and Cap(A)=inf{Cap(U): A⊂U open}. For open U of finite capacity the unique minimizer e_U is the 1-equilibrium potential of U.

title: Kolmogorov extension theorem
description: If T is an index set and (μ_J) a projectively consistent family of Borel probability measures on S^J, J⊂T finite, for a Polish space S, then there is a unique probability measure on the product σ-algebra of S^T whose finite-dimensional marginals are the μ_J.

title: Absorption at zero of nonnegative right-continuous supermartingales
description: If (Z_t) is a nonnegative right-continuous supermartingale and T=inf{t: Z_t=0 or Z_{t−}=0}, then almost surely Z_t=0 for all t≥T on {T<∞}.

title: L² Cauchy integral operators on Lipschitz graphs
description: For a Lipschitz graph Γ={x+iν(x):x∈ℝ} in ℂ (ν′ bounded) and f∈L²(Γ), the Cauchy integral (2πi)⁻¹∫_Γf(s)(s−z)⁻¹ds has nontangential boundary values C_±f almost everywhere on Γ from above and below. C_± are bounded on L²(Γ), with norms bounded in terms of ‖ν′‖_∞, and satisfy C_+f−C_−f=f. This is the Coifman–McIntosh–Meyer theorem.

title: Inverse image of étale sheaves
description: For a morphism of schemes f:Y→X and an étale abelian sheaf F on X, the inverse image f^(−1)F is the étale sheaf on Y associated to the presheaf sending an étale V→Y to the colimit of F(U) over étale U→X with an X-morphism V→U. Its stalk at a geometric point ȳ of Y is F at the geometric point f∘ȳ, so f^(−1) is exact. For an immersion or étale map it is the restriction F|_Y.

title: Higher direct images of étale sheaves
description: For a morphism of schemes f:Y→X, the higher direct images R^if_* are the right derived functors of the left exact direct image f_* from étale abelian sheaves on Y to those on X. R^if_*F is the étale sheaf associated to the presheaf U↦H^i(U×_X Y,F), and R⁰f_*=f_*.

title: Torsion étale abelian sheaf
description: An étale abelian sheaf F on a scheme X is torsion if every local section is locally killed by a positive integer: for s∈F(U) there are an étale covering {U_i→U} and integers n_i≥1 with n_i·s|_(U_i)=0. Equivalently every stalk of F at a geometric point is a torsion abelian group, and F is the union of its subsheaves F[n] of sections killed by n.

title: Constructible étale sheaf of modules
description: Let X be a Noetherian scheme and Λ a Noetherian ring. An étale sheaf of Λ-modules F on X is locally constant if there is an étale covering {U_i→X} with each F|_(U_i) the sheaf associated to a constant presheaf, and constructible if X is a finite union of locally closed subschemes X_j such that each restriction F|_(X_j) is locally constant with finitely generated stalks.

title: Constructible ℓ-adic sheaf
description: Let X be a Noetherian scheme on which ℓ is invertible, E a finite extension of Q_ℓ with valuation ring R and maximal ideal m. A constructible R-sheaf is a projective system (F_n) of constructible étale sheaves of R/mⁿ-modules with F_(n+1)⊗R/mⁿ≅F_n. Constructible E-sheaves are R-sheaves modulo torsion sheaves, and constructible Q̄_ℓ-sheaves are their colimit over all E⊂Q̄_ℓ. A sheaf is lisse if each F_n is locally constant; its stalk F_x̄ at a geometric point is then lim F_(n,x̄), tensored with E or Q̄_ℓ.

title: Frobenius action on stalks of an ℓ-adic sheaf
description: Let X₀ be a scheme of finite type over F_q and F a constructible Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on X₀. For a closed point x with residue field k(x) of N(x) elements and a geometric point x̄ over x, Gal(k̄(x)/k(x)) acts on the stalk F_x̄ by transport of structure. F_x denotes the action of the geometric Frobenius, the inverse of a↦a^(N(x)); it is well defined up to conjugation, so det(1−F_x t,F) and the eigenvalues of F_x on F_x̄ are well defined.

title: Étale cohomology with coefficients in a constructible ℓ-adic sheaf
description: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a separably closed field k with ℓ invertible and F=(F_n) a constructible Z_ℓ-sheaf. Then H^i(X,F)=lim_n H^i(X,F_n) and H^i_c(X,F)=lim_n H^i_c(X,F_n), with E- and Q̄_ℓ-coefficients obtained by tensoring. If X=X₀⊗_(F_q)F̄_q and F is the inverse image of a sheaf on X₀, Gal(F̄_q/F_q) acts on these groups by transport of structure, and the geometric Frobenius acts as the endomorphism F* induced by the Frobenius correspondence.

title: ι-pure and ι-mixed ℓ-adic sheaves
description: Fix a field isomorphism ι:Q̄_ℓ→C. For α∈Q̄_ℓ^× and a prime power q, the ι-weight of α relative to q is w_q(α)=2log_q|ια|. A constructible Q̄_ℓ-sheaf F on a scheme X₀ of finite type over F_q is pointwise ι-pure of weight β∈R if w_(N(x))(α)=β for every closed point x and every eigenvalue α of F_x on F_x̄, and ι-mixed if it has a finite filtration whose graded pieces are pointwise ι-pure. The same terms apply to Q̄_ℓ-representations of Gal(F̄_q/F_q). Duals negate ι-weights, and the Tate twist Q_ℓ(1) is ι-pure of weight −2.

title: Weil group of a nonarchimedean local field
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of q elements and inertia subgroup I⊂Gal(K̄/K). The Weil group W(K̄/K) is the inverse image in Gal(K̄/K) of the subgroup of Gal(k̄/k) generated by the geometric Frobenius, the inverse of x↦x^q, topologized so that I is an open subgroup. A Frobenius lift is an element of W(K̄/K) mapping to the geometric Frobenius.

title: Grothendieck’s ℓ-adic local monodromy theorem
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field of characteristic p, ℓ≠p a prime, and V a finite-dimensional ℓ-adic representation of Gal(K̄/K) or of the Weil group W(K̄/K). Then the inertia group I acts quasi-unipotently: some open subgroup I₁⊂I acts unipotently, and there is a unique nilpotent map N:V(1)→V with σ acting as exp(N·t_ℓ(σ)) for σ∈I₁, where t_ℓ:I→Z_ℓ(1) is the ℓ-adic tame character σ↦(σ(π^(1/ℓⁿ))/π^(1/ℓⁿ))_n. N is the logarithm of the unipotent part of the local monodromy.

title: Monodromy filtration of a nilpotent endomorphism
description: For a nilpotent endomorphism N of an object V of an abelian category there is a unique finite increasing filtration M of V by subobjects M_i such that N(M_i)⊆M_(i−2) and, for every k≥0, N^k induces an isomorphism Gr^M_k V≅Gr^M_(−k) V, where Gr^M_i V=M_i/M_(i−1). When N²=0 it is M_(−1)=im N⊆M₀=ker N⊆M₁=V.

title: Local monodromy filtration of an ℓ-adic representation
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field of characteristic p≠ℓ and V an ℓ-adic representation of the Weil group W(K̄/K). The local monodromy filtration M of V is the monodromy filtration of the nilpotent logarithm N of the unipotent part of the local monodromy, given by Grothendieck’s monodromy theorem (after identifying V(1) with V). It is stable under W(K̄/K), so its graded pieces Gr^M_i V are again representations of the Weil group.

title: ι-weights of a representation of a local Weil group
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field of q elements, ι:Q̄_ℓ→C a field isomorphism, ℓ∤q, and V a Q̄_ℓ-representation of the Weil group W(K̄/K). Two Frobenius lifts have the same eigenvalues on V up to roots of unity, by Grothendieck’s monodromy theorem, so the ι-weights w_q(α)=2log_q|ια| of the eigenvalues α of any Frobenius lift are well defined. V is ι-pure of weight β if all these weights equal β, and ι-mixed in general.

title: Universal homeomorphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:Y→X is a universal homeomorphism if for every morphism X′→X the base change Y×_X X′→X′ is a homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces.

title: Deligne’s upper bound for weights of j_*F at missing points of a curve
description: Let X₀ be a smooth geometrically irreducible curve over F_q, j:U₀→X₀ a dense open immersion with complement S₀, and F a lisse sheaf on U₀ pointwise ι-pure of weight β. Then for every x∈S₀ each eigenvalue α of F_x on the stalk (j_*F)_x̄ satisfies w_(N(x))(α)≤β (Weil II, Lemma 1.8.1).

title: Primitive decomposition and tensor/dual compatibility of the monodromy filtration
description: For a nilpotent endomorphism N of a finite-dimensional vector space V over a field of characteristic zero, with monodromy filtration M and primitive parts P_(−i)=ker(N:Gr^M_(−i)→Gr^M_(−i−2)), one has Gr^M_i V≅⊕_(j≥|i|, j≡i mod 2) P_(−j), and the formation of Gr^M and of the primitive parts is compatible with tensor products (V′⊗V″, N′⊗1+1⊗N″) and duals (V^∨,−N^∨), via the Jacobson–Morozov sl₂-action (Weil II 1.6.4–1.6.14).

title: Deligne’s upper weight bound for H¹_c of pure lisse sheaves on curves
description: Let U₀ be a smooth curve over F_q and F a lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on U₀ pointwise ι-pure of weight β. Then every eigenvalue α of the Frobenius F on H¹_c(U,F) satisfies w_q(α)≤β+1 (Weil II, Lemma 3.2.4 for all k and Corollary 3.2.5).

title: Poincaré duality for j_* of a lisse sheaf on a smooth projective curve
description: Let X be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field, j:U→X a dense open immersion and F a lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaf on U with dual F^∨. Cup product and the trace map give a perfect pairing H¹(X,j_*F)×H¹(X,j_*(F^∨(1)))→Q̄_ℓ, compatible with Frobenius when everything is defined over F_q (SGA 4½ [Dualité] 1.3, 2.1).

title: Stalks of étale higher direct images via strict henselization
description: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism f:X→S, an étale abelian sheaf F on X and a geometric point s̄ of S, (R^nf_*F)_s̄≅H^n(X×_S Spec O^(sh)_(S,s̄),p^(−1)F), where O^(sh)_(S,s̄) is the strict henselization and p the projection (Stacks Theorem 59.53.1).

title: Global sections of étale sheaves on schemes proper over a henselian local ring
description: Let A be a henselian local ring, f:X→Spec A proper and X₀ the closed fibre. For every étale sheaf F on X the restriction Γ(X,F)→Γ(X₀,F|_(X₀)) is bijective, and for finite constant coefficients H¹(X,M)≅H¹(X₀,M) (Stacks Lemmas 59.91.2–59.91.3 and 59.85.1).

title: Gabber’s affine analogue of proper base change
description: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair, X an affine scheme over Spec A and X₀=X×Spec(A/I). For every torsion étale abelian sheaf F on X, H^q(X,F)→H^q(X₀,F|_(X₀)) is an isomorphism for all q (Stacks Section 59.82, Lemma 59.82.8).

title: Invariance of cohomology of proper curves under extension of separably closed fields
description: Let k′/k be an extension of separably closed fields, X a proper k-scheme of dimension at most one and F a torsion étale abelian sheaf on X. Then H^q(X,F)→H^q(X_(k′),F|_(X_(k′))) is an isomorphism for all q (Stacks Lemma 59.83.12).

title: Exactness of étale direct image along finite morphisms
description: For a finite morphism of schemes f:Y→X the direct image f_* on étale abelian sheaves is exact, so R^if_*F=0 for i>0; its stalk at a geometric point x̄ is ⊕ of the stalks of F at the geometric points of Y over x̄, and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change (Milne LEC Prop. 8.4, Ex. 12.3; Stacks 59.55.2–59.55.3).

title: Characterization of universal homeomorphisms as integral universally injective surjections
description: A morphism of schemes is a universal homeomorphism if and only if it is integral, universally injective and surjective (Stacks Morphisms Lemma 29.46.5).

title: Equivalence of étale sites under thickenings
description: If X₀→X is a thickening of schemes (a closed immersion with locally nilpotent ideal, or more generally a closed immersion that is a homeomorphism), then V↦V×_X X₀ is an equivalence from schemes étale over X to schemes étale over X₀ (EGA IV 18.1.2; Stacks Étale Morphisms Theorem 41.15.1).

title: Descent of étale morphisms along surjective integral universally injective morphisms
description: For a surjective integral universally injective morphism S′→S, base change from schemes étale over S to étale schemes over S′ with descent data relative to S′/S is fully faithful, and every descent datum on a quasi-compact separated étale S′-scheme is effective (Stacks Étale Morphisms Lemma 41.20.3 and Proposition 41.20.6).

title: Finiteness of higher direct images with proper support
description: Let f:X→Y be a separated morphism of finite type of Noetherian schemes and Λ a Noetherian torsion ring. Then the higher direct images with proper support R^if_! carry constructible sheaves of Λ-modules to constructible sheaves, vanish for i>2·dim of the fibres, and Rf_! preserves bounded complexes of finite Tor-dimension with constructible cohomology (SGA 4 XVII 5.3.6; SGA 4½ [Th. finitude]).

title: Structure of the inertia group of a local field
description: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field with residue field k of characteristic p and q elements. The wild inertia group P is the unique pro-p Sylow subgroup of the inertia group I, and I/P≅∏_(ℓ≠p)Z_ℓ(1)=lim μ_n (n prime to p) via σ↦σ(π^(1/n))/π^(1/n). Conjugation by a Frobenius lift acts on I/P through the cyclotomic character, i.e. as raising to the q-th power for the arithmetic Frobenius.

title: Labelling of a chamber complex
description: A labelling (typing) of a chamber complex X by a finite set I is a map λ from the vertices of X to I whose restriction to the vertex set of every chamber is a bijection onto I; the type of a simplex is the image of its vertices (Garrett records the complementary cotype). X is uniquely labellable if any two labellings differ by a bijection of the label sets. A simplicial automorphism g of a labelled X is type preserving if λ∘g=λ.

title: Standard parabolic subgroups of a Coxeter system
description: Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system and W_T=⟨T⟩ for T⊆S. Then (W_T,T) is a Coxeter system whose length function is the restriction of that of (W,S); every reduced expression of an element of W_T uses only letters from T; T↦W_T is an inclusion-preserving bijection from subsets of S onto these subgroups; and W_T∩W_T′=W_(T∩T′).

title: Poset criterion for a simplicial complex
description: A partially ordered set is isomorphic to the face poset of an abstract simplicial complex (with finite simplices, ordered by inclusion) if and only if each lower set {y: y≤x} is isomorphic to the poset of nonempty subsets of a finite nonempty set, and any two elements having a common lower bound have a greatest lower bound.

title: Chamber theorem for reflection groups of locally finite hyperplane families
description: Let H be a locally finite set of affine hyperplanes in a Euclidean space, stable under the orthogonal reflections in its members, C a chamber (component of the complement of their union) and S the set of reflections in the walls of C. Then W=⟨S⟩ is the group generated by all reflections in H and acts simply transitively on chambers; the length of w is the number of hyperplanes separating C from wC; the closure of C is a fundamental domain whose point stabilizers are generated by the elements of S fixing the point; and (W,S) satisfies the deletion condition, so is a Coxeter system.

title: Satake’s Hecke eigenvalue formula for spherical functions of PGL₂
description: Let k be a p-adic field with residue field of order q, G=PGL₂(k), K=PGL₂(𝒪), and ω_s(g)=∫_K |a(kg)/d(kg)|^(1/2+s)dk the zonal spherical function of the unramified principal series with parameter s∈ℂ. If τ_m is the characteristic function of the image of the integral matrices whose determinant has valuation m, then ∫τ_m ω_s = q^(m/2)(q^((m+1)s)−q^(−(m+1)s))/(q^s−q^(−s)) for Haar measure with K of volume 1, read as (m+1)q^(m/2) at s=0.

title: Canonical integral model of the centralizer of a maximal split torus
description: Let K♮ be complete for a discrete valuation ω with perfect residue field and ring of integers O♮, G a connected reductive K♮-group, S♮ a maximal K♮-split torus and Z its centralizer. There is a smooth affine O♮-group scheme 𝔷 of finite type with generic fibre Z (the canonical model) whose O♮-points are {z∈Z(K♮): ω(χ(z))=0 for every K♮-rational character χ of Z}; if the connected centre of G is anisotropic, this is the kernel of the action of Z(K♮) on the apartment of S♮.

title: Exchange, deletion and folding characterizations of Coxeter systems
description: For a group W generated by a set S of elements of order 2, with word length ℓ, the following are equivalent: (W,S) is a Coxeter system; the deletion condition (a word of length d>ℓ(w) for w can be shortened by deleting two letters); the exchange condition; and the folding condition (if ℓ(sw)=ℓ(w)+1=ℓ(wt) and ℓ(swt)<ℓ(w)+2 for s,t∈S, then sw=wt).

title: σ-compact topological space
description: A topological space is σ-compact if it is the union of countably many compact subsets. A subset of a space is σ-compact if it is σ-compact in the subspace topology, equivalently a countable union of compact subsets of the space.

title: Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation of positive functionals on C_c(X)
description: For a locally compact Hausdorff space X, every positive linear functional I on the space C_c(X) of compactly supported continuous real functions is I(f)=∫f dμ for a unique Radon measure μ (finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets, inner regular on open sets). Moreover μ(U)=sup{I(f): 0≤f≤1, supp f⊆U} for open U and μ(K)=inf{I(f): f≥1_K} for compact K.

title: Regularity of σ-finite Radon measures
description: A σ-finite Radon measure μ on a locally compact Hausdorff space is inner regular by compact sets and outer regular by open sets on every Borel set. Moreover, for every Borel set B and ε>0 there are a closed set F and an open set U with F⊆B⊆U and μ(U∖F)<ε.

title: Open subsets of second-countable locally compact Hausdorff spaces are σ-compact
description: In a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space, every open subset, in particular the whole space, is a countable union of compact subsets.

title: Conditional Fatou lemma
description: For nonnegative random variables X_n on a probability space and a sub-σ-algebra G, E[liminf_n X_n|G]≤liminf_n E[X_n|G] almost surely, where conditional expectations of nonnegative variables are taken with values in [0,∞].

title: Cauchy integral formula for closed curves with winding numbers
description: Let f be holomorphic on a simply connected open set U⊆ℂ and γ a closed piecewise C¹ curve in U. For every z∈U not on γ, (2πi)⁻¹∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ−z)dζ=n(γ,z)f(z), where n(γ,z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_γ dζ/(ζ−z) is the winding number of γ about z; in particular the integral vanishes when z lies outside γ.

title: Helly selection theorem for bounded Borel measures on the real line
description: Every sequence of Borel measures μ_n on ℝ with μ_n(ℝ)≤M has a subsequence converging vaguely, that is ∫f dμ_n→∫f dμ for every compactly supported continuous f, to a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ)≤M.

title: Borel transforms of finite measures are Herglotz functions
description: For a finite positive Borel measure μ on ℝ, the Borel transform F(z)=∫_ℝ dμ(λ)/(λ−z) is holomorphic on ℂ∖ℝ, satisfies F(z̄)=F(z)‾ and Im F(z)=Im z·∫_ℝ dμ(λ)/|λ−z|², and obeys |F(z)|≤μ(ℝ)/Im z on the upper half-plane; in particular it maps the upper half-plane into the closed upper half-plane.

title: Quantitative Kronecker theorem for linear sequences on a torus
description: Let m≥1, 0<δ<1/2 and α∈ℝ^m. If the finite sequence (nα mod ℤ^m)_(n∈[N]) is not δ-equidistributed on ℝ^m/ℤ^m, that is |E_(n∈[N])F(nα)−∫F|>δ‖F‖_Lip for some Lipschitz F:ℝ^m/ℤ^m→ℂ, then some k∈ℤ^m with 0<|k|≪δ^(−O_m(1)) satisfies ‖k·α‖_(ℝ/ℤ)≪δ^(−O_m(1))/N (Green–Tao, Proposition 3.1).

title: Almost k-simple algebraic group
description: A nontrivial connected semisimple algebraic group G over a field k is almost k-simple if every proper normal closed k-subgroup of G is finite, i.e. G has no proper positive-dimensional connected normal k-subgroup. Absolutely almost simple groups are almost k-simple; a Weil restriction of an absolutely almost simple group is almost k-simple without being absolutely almost simple.

title: Cartan decomposition for reductive groups over nonarchimedean local fields
description: Let G be a connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field k, S a maximal k-split torus with centralizer Z, Φ⁺ a positive system of relative roots, and K the stabilizer in G(k) of a special vertex of the apartment of S in the Bruhat–Tits building. Then G(k)=K·Z⁺·K, where Z⁺ consists of the z∈Z(k) with |α(z)|≥1 for every α∈Φ⁺ (via the valuation homomorphism of Z(k)). Since A⁺=Z⁺∩S(k) has finite index in Z⁺ modulo the maximal compact subgroup of Z(k), G(k)=K·A⁺·Ω·K for a finite subset Ω⊂Z(k).

title: Harish-Chandra function of PGL₂ over a nonarchimedean local field
description: Let k be a nonarchimedean local field with ring of integers O and absolute value |·|, G=PGL₂(k), B its upper-triangular subgroup and K=PGL₂(O). Normalized induction from the trivial character of B gives right translation on functions f:G→ℂ with f(bg)=|a/d|^(1/2)f(g) for b with diagonal entries a,d, normed by ∫_K|f|²dk for the Haar probability measure of K, using G=BK. With f₀ the K-fixed vector equal to 1 on K, the Harish-Chandra function is Ξ(g)=⟨π(g)f₀,f₀⟩=∫_K|a(kg)/d(kg)|^(1/2)dk; it is K-biinvariant with Ξ(e)=1. For k=ℚ_p it is the Harish-Chandra function of PGL₂(ℚ_p).

title: Subgroup G(k)⁺ generated by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups
description: For a connected reductive group G over a field k, G(k)⁺ is the subgroup of G(k) generated by the groups U(k) of k-points of the unipotent radicals U of the parabolic k-subgroups of G; equivalently (Borel–Tits) by the k-points of the k-split unipotent k-subgroups. It is a normal subgroup of G(k), trivial when G is k-anisotropic.

title: Finite vector of a representation under a subgroup
description: For a representation π of a group G on a complex vector space V and a subgroup U of G, a vector v∈V is U-finite if the linear span ⟨Uv⟩ of {π(u)v: u∈U} is finite-dimensional. For a unitary representation and a compact subgroup U these vectors form a dense subspace.

title: Affine Bruhat decomposition for reductive groups over local fields
description: Let G be a connected reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field k, S a maximal k-split torus with normalizer N, and I the Iwahori subgroup of a chamber in the apartment of S in the Bruhat–Tits building. Then G(k)=I·N(k)·I, and I n I↦ n gives a bijection of I∖G(k)/I with the Iwahori–Weyl group N(k)/(N(k)∩I).

title: Tempered unitary representation of a reductive group over a local field
description: Let G be the k-points of a connected reductive group over a local field k with a good maximal compact subgroup K and Harish-Chandra function Ξ_G. A unitary representation ρ of G is tempered if |⟨ρ(g)v,w⟩|≤(dim⟨Kv⟩dim⟨Kw⟩)^(1/2)Ξ_G(g) for all g∈G and all K-finite unit vectors v,w (Oh’s convention); by Cowling–Haagerup–Howe and Oh this is equivalent to weak containment in the regular representation.

title: Harish-Chandra function of a reductive group over a local field
description: For the k-points G of a connected reductive group over a local field, with minimal parabolic subgroup B, modular function δ_B and good maximal compact subgroup K with G=BK, the Harish-Chandra function is Ξ_G(g)=∫_K δ_B(gk)^(−1/2)dk, the diagonal matrix coefficient of the K-fixed unit vector of the representation unitarily induced from the trivial character of B. It is continuous, bi-K-invariant, takes values in (0,1] and is L^(2+ε) modulo the centre.

title: Oh’s temperedness of restrictions to strongly orthogonal root subgroups
description: Let k be a local field with char(k)≠2, G the k-points of a connected reductive group of k-semisimple rank at least 2 with G/Z(G) almost k-simple (and not locally Sp_(2n)(ℂ)), S a strongly orthogonal system of positive nonmultipliable roots, and G_S the k-points of the reductive subgroup generated by a maximal k-split torus and the root groups U_(±α), α∈S. Then for every unitary representation ρ of G without nonzero G⁺-invariant vectors, the restriction ρ|G_S is tempered (Oh, Theorem 5.5).

title: Holomorphic function with values in a complex Banach space
description: A map f from an open subset U of ℂ to a complex Banach space X is holomorphic if for every z₀∈U the difference quotients (f(z)−f(z₀))/(z−z₀) converge in the norm of X as z→z₀; the limit is the complex derivative f′(z₀). For X=ℂ this is ordinary holomorphy.

title: Locally compact subspaces of Hausdorff spaces are open in their closure
description: If A is a subset of a Hausdorff space X that is locally compact in the subspace topology, then A is open in its closure, i.e. A is locally closed in X. In particular a dense locally compact subspace of a Hausdorff space is open.

title: Closure of a subgroup of a topological group is a subgroup
description: In a topological group G the closure of a subgroup H is again a subgroup of G, because multiplication and inversion are continuous; the closure of a normal subgroup is normal.

title: Open subgroups of a topological group are closed
description: Every open subgroup H of a topological group G is closed, since its complement is the union of the cosets xH with x∉H, each open because translations are homeomorphisms.

title: Spectra in a unital closed subalgebra of a Banach algebra
description: Let B be a closed subalgebra of a unital complex Banach algebra A containing the identity of A. For every b∈B, σ_A(b)⊆σ_B(b) and the topological boundary of σ_B(b) is contained in σ_A(b) (indeed in its boundary). Hence σ_B(b)=σ_A(b) whenever σ_B(b) has empty interior, e.g. when it lies in ℝ.

title: Kneser–Tits conjecture for classical groups over local and global fields
description: Let K be a local or global field and G a simply connected absolutely almost simple K-isotropic group of classical type A_n, B_n, C_n or D_n, excluding the trialitarian forms ³D₄ and ⁶D₄. Then G(K)=G(K)⁺. For inner type A this is the triviality of the reduced Whitehead group SK₁(D), for outer type A that of the reduced unitary Whitehead group.

title: Prasad–Raghunathan reduction of the Kneser–Tits problem to K-rank one
description: Let G be a simply connected absolutely almost simple group of K-rank at least 2, S a maximal K-split torus and H its centralizer. Then H(K) is generated by the groups H_i(K)=H(K)∩G_i(K), where G_i are the K-isotropic K-simple components of K-rank one obtained from the Tits index by keeping one Galois orbit of distinguished vertices; hence G(K)=G(K)⁺ if this holds for every G_i.

title: Quasi-splitness of exceptional groups over nonarchimedean local fields
description: Over a nonarchimedean local field K every absolutely almost simple simply connected K-group of type E₈, F₄ or G₂ is K-split; every group of type ³D₄, ⁶D₄ or ²E₆ is quasi-split; every group of type B_n, C_n or E₇ splits over a quadratic extension, and every inner form of type E₆ splits over an extension of degree 3. These follow from Kneser’s vanishing of H¹(K,G) for simply connected G.

title: Kneser’s classification of anisotropic simply connected groups over local fields
description: Every simply connected absolutely almost simple group that is anisotropic over a nonarchimedean local field K is isomorphic to SL₁(D), the group of reduced-norm-one elements of a finite-dimensional central division algebra D over K; in particular it is an inner form of type A.

title: Canonical factorization of Hardy H² functions with exponential outer factor
description: Every nonzero f∈H² of the unit disk has log|f*|∈L¹ of the circle, the function Q_f(z)=exp∫(ζ+z)/(ζ−z)·log|f*(ζ)|dm(ζ) lies in H², and f=M_f·Q_f with M_f an inner function. Here m is normalized arc measure; M_f is constant exactly when log|f(0)|=∫log|f*|dm.

title: Completeness of the Hausdorff metric on compact subsets of ℝⁿ
description: The nonempty compact subsets of ℝⁿ form a complete metric space under the Hausdorff distance: every Cauchy sequence converges to a nonempty compact set.

title: Closed regularity of finite Borel measures on a metric space
description: Every finite Borel measure μ on a metric space is closed regular: for each Borel set B, μ(B) is the supremum of μ(F) over closed sets F⊆B, equivalently the infimum of μ(U) over open sets U⊇B.

title: Weak convergence of finite Borel measures on a metric space
description: Finite positive Borel measures μ_j on a metric space converge weakly to a finite Borel measure μ if ∫f dμ_j→∫f dμ for every bounded continuous real function f. For probability measures this is the usual weak convergence; testing f=1 shows that total masses converge.

title: Affine hull and dimension of a subset of ℝⁿ
description: The affine hull aff A of a nonempty A⊆ℝⁿ is the set of affine combinations ∑λ_ix_i of finitely many x_i∈A with ∑λ_i=1; it is the smallest affine subspace x+V, V a linear subspace, containing A. The dimension of A, in particular of a convex set, is dim V.

title: Minkowski–Weyl theorem for convex polytopes
description: A subset of ℝⁿ is a convex polytope, the convex hull of finitely many points, if and only if it is a bounded intersection of finitely many closed halfspaces.

title: Radius of convergence of a complex power series
description: For a complex power series ∑c_k(z−z₀)^k, its radius of convergence is R=sup{|z−z₀|: the series converges at z}∈[0,∞]. The open disk |z−z₀|<R is its disk of convergence (all of ℂ when R=∞).

title: Cauchy–Hadamard theorem for complex power series
description: A complex power series ∑c_k(z−z₀)^k with radius of convergence R satisfies 1/R=limsup|c_k|^{1/k}. It converges absolutely for |z−z₀|<R, absolutely and uniformly on |z−z₀|≤r for each r<R, and diverges for |z−z₀|>R.

title: Morera’s theorem
description: A continuous complex function f on an open set G⊆ℂ whose integral ∫_γf(z)dz vanishes for every closed piecewise smooth path γ in G is holomorphic on G.

title: Uniform limits and complex line integrals
description: If continuous functions f_n converge uniformly to f on the image of a piecewise smooth path γ in ℂ, then ∫_γf_n(z)dz→∫_γf(z)dz. Consequently a uniformly convergent series of continuous functions can be integrated termwise along γ.

title: Anderson–Klee bound on singular boundary points of a convex body
description: For a convex body K⊂ℝⁿ with nonempty interior and 0≤r≤n−1, the boundary points whose normal cone has dimension at least n−r can be covered by countably many compact sets of finite r-dimensional Hausdorff measure. In particular the boundary points with more than one outer unit normal form an H^{n−1}-null set.

title: Area formula for Lipschitz maps
description: For a Lipschitz map f:ℝ^m→ℝⁿ with m≤n, its Jacobian Jf=√det(Df^TDf) exists almost everywhere, and for every Lebesgue measurable A⊆ℝ^m, ∫_A Jf dx=∫_{ℝⁿ}#(A∩f⁻¹{y})dH^m(y), where H^m is m-dimensional Hausdorff measure and # counts points.

title: Commutator subgroup of two subgroups
description: For subgroups H and K of a group G, [H,K] is the subgroup of G generated by all commutators hkh⁻¹k⁻¹ with h∈H and k∈K. Since the inverse of such a commutator is a commutator of k and h, [H,K]=[K,H].

title: Three subgroup lemma
description: For subgroups A, B, C of a group G and a normal subgroup N of G containing [[B,C],A] and [[C,A],B], also [[A,B],C]⊆N. In particular, for normal subgroups A, B, C one has [[A,B],C]⊆[[B,C],A]·[[C,A],B]. It follows from the Hall–Witt identity.

title: Normal closure of a subset of a group
description: For a subset B of a group G, the normal closure of B in G is the smallest normal subgroup of G containing B; it is the subgroup generated by all conjugates gbg⁻¹ with b∈B and g∈G.

title: Central series with infinite cyclic factors in a finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group
description: Every finitely generated nilpotent group G with no nonidentity elements of finite order has a central series 1=H₀⊆H₁⊆⋯⊆H_s=G of normal subgroups in which each H_i/H_(i−1) lies in the centre of G/H_(i−1) and is infinite cyclic.

title: Change of variables for analytic isomorphisms over a local field
description: Let K be a local field with normalized absolute value |·| and additive Haar measure dx on Kⁿ, and let φ:U→V be an analytic isomorphism of open subsets of Kⁿ. Then ∫_V f(y)dy=∫_U f(φ(x))|det Dφ(x)| dx for every nonnegative measurable or integrable f on V. Equivalently, the measures |ω| defined by top-degree analytic forms satisfy |φ*ω|=φ*|ω|.

title: Haar measure on a restricted product of locally compact groups
description: Let G=∏′_v(G_v,K_v) be the restricted product of locally compact groups G_v with respect to compact open subgroups K_v given for almost all v, and let μ_v be left Haar measures with μ_v(K_v)=1 for almost all v. There is a unique left Haar measure μ on G whose restriction to each open subgroup ∏_(v∈S)G_v×∏_(v∉S)K_v is the product of the μ_v; its modular quasi-character is Δ_G(g)=∏_vΔ_(G_v)(g_v).

title: Modular quasi-character of a closed normal subgroup
description: If N is a closed normal subgroup of a locally compact group G, then the modular quasi-character of N is the restriction to N of the modular quasi-character of G: Δ_N=Δ_G|_N. In particular N is unimodular whenever Δ_G is trivial on N.

title: Semialgebra of subsets of a set
description: A family S of subsets of a set Ω that is closed under finite intersections and such that the complement in Ω of each member is a finite disjoint union of members of S; for example ∅ together with the half-open intervals (a,b], −∞≤a<b≤∞, in ℝ.

title: Measure on an algebra of sets (premeasure)
description: A set function μ from an algebra A of subsets of Ω to [0,∞] with μ(∅)=0 such that μ(⋃ᵢAᵢ)=∑ᵢμ(Aᵢ) for every sequence of pairwise disjoint Aᵢ∈A whose union also lies in A.

title: Countably generated σ-algebra
description: A σ-algebra F on a set Ω is countably generated (separable) if F=σ(C) for some countable family C of subsets of Ω.

title: ε–δ criterion for absolute continuity of a finite measure
description: Let μ be a positive measure and ν a complex (in particular a finite signed or finite positive) measure on the same σ-algebra. Then ν≪μ if and only if for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that |ν(A)|<ε for every measurable A with μ(A)<δ. Finiteness of ν is needed for the forward implication.

title: Herbrand function of a Galois extension of local fields
description: For a finite Galois extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields with lower ramification groups G_t (t≥−1), the Herbrand function is φ_(L/K)(u)=∫₀^u dt/[G₀:G_t] for u≥−1, where [G₀:G_t] means [G_t:G₀]^(−1) for −1≤t≤0, so φ_(L/K)(u)=u on [−1,0]. It is a continuous, strictly increasing, piecewise linear bijection of [−1,∞) onto itself; its inverse is denoted ψ_(L/K).

title: Equivalence of norms on a finite-dimensional space over a complete valued field
description: Let K be a field complete for an absolute value and E a finite-dimensional K-vector space. Any two norms on E are equivalent and E is complete for each of them; in particular the norm topology is the product topology of Kⁿ for any choice of basis.

title: Norm formula for the unique extension of a complete valuation
description: Let K be complete for a nonarchimedean valuation v and L/K a finite extension of degree n. Then w(x)=v(N_(L/K)x)/n is a valuation on L extending v; it is the only valuation on L extending v, and L is complete for w. Equivalently |x|_L=|N_(L/K)x|_K^(1/n).

title: Monogenicity of integer rings of extensions of complete discretely valued fields
description: Let K be complete for a discrete valuation with valuation ring o, and L/K a finite extension whose residue field extension is separable, with O the valuation ring of L. Then O=o[ω] for some ω∈O.
