title: Different of a monogenic local extension via the derivative of the minimal polynomial
description: Let L/K be a finite separable extension of complete discretely valued fields with valuation rings O⊇o. If O=o[α] and f∈o[T] is the minimal polynomial of α, then the different of L/K is 𝔇_(L/K)=f′(α)O. The proof uses Euler’s formula: the trace-dual basis of 1,α,…,α^(n−1) is b₀/f′(α),…,b_(n−1)/f′(α), where f(T)/(T−α)=∑b_iT^i.

title: Inertia group and ramification index of a Galois extension of complete discretely valued fields
description: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension of complete discretely valued fields with separable residue field extension l/k. Reduction gives an exact sequence 1→G₀→Gal(L/K)→Gal(l/k)→1, where the inertia group G₀ consists of the automorphisms acting trivially on l, and |G₀| equals the ramification index e(L/K).

title: Genus of a compact Riemann surface
description: The genus of a compact Riemann surface X is g(X)=dim_ℂΩ¹_hol(X), the dimension of the complex vector space of holomorphic differentials on X. It is finite, and by the Riemann–Roch theorem it equals the number of handles of the underlying closed surface.

title: Atkin–Lehner–Li newform decomposition of cusp forms on Γ₁(N)
description: For integers k,N≥1, the normalized newforms of level N form a basis of the new subspace S_k(Γ₁(N))^new, distinct newforms having distinct systems of Hecke eigenvalues, and S_k(Γ₁(N))=⊕_(M|N)⊕_(d|N/M)α_d(S_k(Γ₁(M))^new) with α_d(f)(τ)=f(dτ). Thus the forms f(dτ), for newforms f of level M dividing N and d dividing N/M, form a basis of S_k(Γ₁(N)).

title: Galois conjugates of weight-two normalized eigenforms
description: Let f=∑a_nqⁿ∈S₂(Γ₀(N),χ) be a normalized eigenform for all Hecke operators, with coefficient field K_f. For every field embedding σ:K_f→ℂ the conjugate f^σ=∑σ(a_n)qⁿ is a normalized eigenform in S₂(Γ₀(N),σ∘χ), and if f is a newform then so is f^σ.

title: Degeneracy maps between modular curves X₁(N)→X₁(M)
description: For M|N and d|N/M there is a morphism B_d:X₁(N)→X₁(M) of curves over ℚ given on the upper half-plane by τ↦dτ. By Albanese functoriality it induces a homomorphism J₁(N)→J₁(M) over ℚ, and pulling back the differential f(τ)dτ along B_d gives d·f(dτ)dτ, so on weight-two cusp forms it is d times the degeneracy map α_d.

title: Analytic Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface
description: For a compact Riemann surface X of genus g, the analytic Jacobian is the complex torus Jac(X)=Ω¹_hol(X)^∧/H₁(X,ℤ), where a homology class γ gives the functional ω↦∫_γω on holomorphic differentials. It has dimension g, and by Abel’s theorem it is isomorphic to the degree-zero divisor class group Pic⁰(X).

title: Local algebraicity of rational abelian ℓ-adic representations of G_ℚ
description: Let ρ be a semisimple abelian ℓ-adic representation of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) that is rational: unramified outside a finite set with Frobenius characteristic polynomials having rational coefficients. Then ρ is locally algebraic; in particular each one-dimensional constituent agrees with an integral power χ_ℓ^n of the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character on an open subgroup of an inertia group at ℓ.

title: Semisimplicity of restrictions to finite-index subgroups
description: Let ρ be a semisimple finite-dimensional linear representation of a group G over a field of characteristic zero, and H a subgroup of finite index in G. Then the restriction of ρ to H is semisimple.

title: Dichotomy for subgroups of GL₂ with infinite projective image
description: Let F be a field of characteristic zero and G⊆GL₂(F) a non-abelian subgroup acting semisimply on F² whose image in PGL₂(F) is infinite. Then either every subgroup of finite index in G acts irreducibly and non-abelianly on F², or G lies in the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup C of GL₂(F) with [G:G∩C]=2, and a finite-index subgroup of G is abelian exactly when it lies in C.

title: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma on the real line
description: If f is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ, then ∫f(x)cos(λx)dx and ∫f(x)sin(λx)dx tend to 0 as the real parameter λ→∞; equivalently the Fourier transform of f tends to 0 at infinity.

title: Möbius action of SL₂(ℝ) on the upper half-plane
description: The upper half-plane is ℍ={τ∈ℂ: Im τ>0}. A matrix [[a,b],[c,d]]∈SL₂(ℝ) acts on ℍ by τ↦(aτ+b)/(cτ+d); this is a group action, since Im((aτ+b)/(cτ+d))=Im τ/|cτ+d|² and composition of these maps corresponds to matrix multiplication. The matrices ±I act trivially. Restriction gives the action of SL₂(ℤ) and of its subgroups on ℍ.

title: Ring ℤ/nℤ of integers modulo n
description: For a positive integer n, ℤ/nℤ is the quotient ring of the integers by the ideal nℤ: its n elements are the residue classes of integers modulo n, added and multiplied through representatives.

title: L-function of a compatible system of ℓ-adic Galois representations
description: Let F be a number field and (ρ_ℓ) a family of continuous representations of G_F on finite-dimensional ℚ_ℓ-vector spaces V_ℓ, compatible in the sense that for each finite place v the polynomial P_v(T)=det(1−Frob_v⁻¹T|(V_ℓ^∨)^(I_v)), for ℓ prime to v, has rational coefficients independent of ℓ. Here I_v is an inertia group at v, Frob_v an arithmetic Frobenius and V^∨ the dual representation. The L-function is the Euler product L(ρ,s)=∏_v P_v((Nv)^(−s))^(−1) over all finite places, including ramified ones.

title: Gowers uniformity norm on a finite abelian group
description: For f:G→ℂ on a finite abelian group G and d≥1, ‖f‖_(U^d) is the 2^d-th root of the average over x,h₁,…,h_d∈G of ∏_(ω∈{0,1}^d) C^(|ω|)f(x+ω₁h₁+⋯+ω_dh_d), where C is complex conjugation. The average is nonnegative, and ‖·‖_(U^d) is a norm for d≥2.

title: Gowers–Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
description: For functions f_ω:G→ℂ, ω∈{0,1}^d, on a finite abelian group G, the Gowers inner product ⟨(f_ω)⟩_(U^d), the average over x,h₁,…,h_d of ∏_ω C^(|ω|)f_ω(x+ω₁h₁+⋯+ω_dh_d), satisfies |⟨(f_ω)⟩_(U^d)|≤∏_ω‖f_ω‖_(U^d).

title: Wigert’s maximal-order bound for the divisor function
description: The number d(n) of positive divisors of n satisfies log d(n)≤(log 2+o(1))·log n/log log n as n→∞, and this order is attained infinitely often. In particular d(n)≤exp(C log n/log log n) for an absolute constant C and all n≥3.

title: Goldston–Yıldırım truncated divisor sum Λ_R
description: For a parameter R≥1 and a positive integer n, Λ_R(n)=∑_(d|n, d≤R) μ(d)log(R/d), with μ the Möbius function. It truncates the identity Λ(n)=∑_(d|n)μ(d)log(n/d) for the von Mangoldt function; Λ_R(n)=log R whenever n is a prime larger than R.

title: Goldston–Yıldırım correlation estimates for W-tricked truncated divisor sums
description: Let W be the product of the primes up to a sufficiently slowly growing w(N) and R a small fixed power of N. For fixed m,t, affine-linear forms ψ_i on ℤ^t with integer linear parts bounded by √w(N)/2, nonzero and pairwise non-proportional, and a box B with sides at least R^(10m), the average of ∏_iΛ_R(Wψ_i(x)+1)² over B is (1+o(1))(W log R/φ(W))^m. For distinct h_i with |h_i|≤N² and an interval B of length at least R^(10m), the average of ∏_iΛ_R(W(x+h_i)+1)² is at most (1+o(1))(W log R/φ(W))^m∏_(p|Δ)(1+O(p^(−1/2))), where Δ=∏_(i<j)|h_i−h_j|.

title: Quasi-projectivity of torsors under smooth group schemes over a Dedekind scheme
description: Let S be a Dedekind scheme and G a smooth, separated S-group scheme of finite type. Every G-torsor X over S is quasi-projective over S; in particular G itself is quasi-projective over S. This is Raynaud’s theorem, Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models, 6.4/1.

title: Finite sets of points of a quasi-projective scheme lie in an affine open
description: If X is quasi-projective over an affine scheme, then every finite set of points of X is contained in some affine open subscheme of X.

title: Infinitesimal lifting criterion for smoothness
description: A morphism of schemes X→S locally of finite presentation is smooth if and only if, for every affine S-scheme T and closed subscheme T₀⊂T defined by a square-zero ideal, every S-morphism T₀→X extends to an S-morphism T→X.

title: Uniformly elliptic operator in nondivergence form
description: A second-order linear operator Lu=∑_{i,j}a_ij∂_iju+∑_ib_i∂_iu+cu on an open Ω⊆ℝⁿ with real coefficient functions, a_ij=a_ji, and constants 0<λ≤Λ such that λ|ξ|²≤∑a_ij(x)ξ_iξ_j≤Λ|ξ|² for all x∈Ω and ξ∈ℝⁿ. Derivatives are classical, or weak for Sobolev functions.

title: Trace theorem for W¹,ᵖ on bounded Lipschitz domains
description: For a bounded Lipschitz domain U⊂ℝⁿ and 1≤p<∞ there is a bounded linear operator T:W¹,ᵖ(U)→Lᵖ(∂U;Hⁿ⁻¹) with Tf=f|∂U for every f∈W¹,ᵖ(U)∩C(Ū). Tf is the trace of f; boundary values f=g on part of ∂U mean Tf=Tg Hⁿ⁻¹-almost everywhere there.

title: Density of functions smooth up to the boundary in W¹,ᵖ of a Lipschitz domain
description: If U⊂ℝⁿ is bounded with Lipschitz boundary and 1≤p<∞, every f∈W¹,ᵖ(U) is a W¹,ᵖ-limit of functions in W¹,ᵖ(U)∩C^∞(Ū); if also f∈C(Ū), the approximants can be chosen to converge uniformly on Ū.

title: Interior W²,ᵖ estimate for the Poisson equation
description: For 1<p<∞, if f∈Lᵖ(B₁) and u∈W²,ᵖ(B₁) satisfies Δu=f almost everywhere in the unit ball B₁⊂ℝⁿ, then ‖u‖_{W²,ᵖ(B₁/₂)}≤C(‖u‖_{Lᵖ(B₁)}+‖f‖_{Lᵖ(B₁)}) with C depending only on n and p.

title: Dynkin’s formula for Markov chains
description: For a Markov chain (X_k) with natural filtration (F_k), nonnegative adapted Z_k and a stopping time τ, put τⁿ=min{n,τ,inf{k:Z_k≥n}}. Then E_x[Z_{τⁿ}]=E_x[Z₀]+E_x[∑_{i=1}^{τⁿ}(E[Z_i|F_{i−1}]−Z_{i−1})] for every initial state x and every n.

title: Lebesgue decomposition theorem for σ-finite measures
description: If μ and ν are σ-finite measures on one measurable space, then ν=ν_a+ν_s uniquely with ν_a absolutely continuous and ν_s singular with respect to μ; ν_a has a Radon–Nikodym density with respect to μ.

title: Martingale differentiation of measures along refining partitions
description: Let φ and ν be finite measures on a measurable space whose σ-algebra is generated by a refining sequence of countable partitions 𝓑_i, and let B_i(y) be the cell of 𝓑_i containing y. Then ν(B_i(y))/φ(B_i(y)) converges for φ-almost every y to the Radon–Nikodym density of the absolutely continuous part of ν with respect to φ (Doob’s differentiation theorem).

title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equations for a Markov kernel
description: For a Markov kernel P on a measurable space with iterates Pⁿ, P^{n+m}(x,B)=∫Pⁿ(x,dy)P^m(y,B) for all n,m≥0, states x and measurable B; for a Markov chain with kernel P, Pⁿ(x,B)=P_x(X_n∈B).

title: Feller’s boundary criteria for a diffusion on natural scale
description: For a regular one-dimensional diffusion on natural scale with speed measure ν, right endpoint b and interior point u: b is accessible iff b is finite and ∫_u^b(b−x)ν(dx)<∞; accessible and reflecting iff b is finite and ν(u,b]<∞; an entrance boundary iff b=∞ and ∫_u^∞xν(dx)<∞. Left endpoints are symmetric.

title: Feller property of a regular one-dimensional diffusion
description: A regular one-dimensional diffusion on an interval I extends, after adjoining its entrance boundaries to I, to a continuous Feller process on the enlarged interval; in particular its transition operators preserve continuous functions vanishing at the remaining inaccessible ends.

title: Strong Markov property of Feller processes
description: A canonical right-continuous Feller process is strong Markov: for every initial law, optional time τ and measurable path functional ξ≥0, E[ξ∘θ_τ|F_τ]=E_{X_τ}[ξ] almost surely on {τ<∞}, where θ_τ shifts the path by τ.

title: Ratio ergodic theorem for recurrent one-dimensional diffusions
description: For a regular recurrent one-dimensional diffusion on natural scale with speed measure ν, and measurable f,g≥0 with νf<∞ and νg>0, ∫₀ᵗf(X_s)ds/∫₀ᵗg(X_s)ds→νf/νg almost surely under every P_x as t→∞ (Derman; Motoo and Watanabe).

title: Locally integrable stochastic process
description: A real process X on a filtered probability space is locally integrable if there are stopping times T_n increasing to ∞ almost surely such that each variable 1_(T_n>0)sup_(t≤T_n)|X_t| is integrable. For a nonnegative increasing process A with A₀=0 this means E[A_(T_n)]<∞ for every n.

title: Kunita–Watanabe covariation characterization of the stochastic integral
description: For locally square-integrable càdlàg martingales M,L and a predictable G that is locally square-integrable against [M], the stochastic integral G·M satisfies [G·M,L]_t=∫_(0,t]G_s d[M,L]_s, and it is the unique locally square-integrable martingale Y with Y₀=0 having this covariation with every such L. In particular [G·M,H·N]=∫GH d[M,N].

title: Strict-past variables placed at a predictable time give predictable processes
description: If T is a predictable stopping time and U is an F_(T−)-measurable random variable, then the processes U1_[T,∞) and U1_[T] (equal to U at time T and 0 elsewhere) are predictable.

title: Doléans’ theorem: natural increasing processes are exactly the predictable ones
description: On a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, an integrable increasing process A (adapted, right-continuous, nondecreasing, A₀=0, EA_∞<∞) is natural, meaning E∫_(0,∞)ΔM_t dA_t=0 for every bounded càdlàg martingale M, if and only if A is predictable.

title: Dunford–Pettis weak compactness criterion in L¹
description: For a subset H of L¹ of a probability space the following are equivalent: H is uniformly integrable; H is relatively compact for the weak topology σ(L¹,L^∞); every sequence in H has a weakly convergent subsequence.

title: Quasi-compact morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is quasi-compact if f⁻¹(V) is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open subset V⊆S; it suffices to check this over the members of an affine open cover of S. A scheme is quasi-compact if its underlying topological space is.

title: Quasi-separated morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is quasi-separated if its diagonal morphism X→X×_S X is quasi-compact. A scheme X is quasi-separated if X→Spec ℤ is, equivalently if the intersection of any two affine open subschemes of X is quasi-compact.

title: Morphism of schemes of finite presentation
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is of finite presentation if it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For affine X=Spec A and S=Spec R this says that A is a finitely presented R-algebra.

title: Locally constructible subset of a topological space
description: In a topological space X an open subset U is retrocompact if U∩W is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open W⊆X. A subset E⊆X is constructible if it is a finite union of sets U∖V with U and V retrocompact open subsets, and locally constructible if X has an open cover by subsets V_i such that each E∩V_i is constructible in V_i. In a Noetherian space both notions reduce to finite unions of locally closed subsets.

title: Quasi-finite morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S locally of finite type is quasi-finite at x∈X if x is an isolated point of its fibre X_(f(x)). The morphism f is quasi-finite if it is of finite type and every point of X is isolated in its fibre; equivalently f is of finite type and every fibre is a finite discrete space.

title: Normalizer and centralizer of a subgroup scheme
description: Let G be a group scheme over S and H⊆G a closed subgroup scheme. The normalizer N_G(H) and the centralizer Z_G(H) are the subgroup functors of G assigning to an S-scheme S′ the set of g∈G(S′) with gH_(S′)g⁻¹=H_(S′), respectively the set of g∈G(S′) whose conjugation action on H_(S′) is trivial. When represented by closed subgroup schemes of G these are denoted by the same symbols; Z_G(H) is normal in N_G(H).

title: Quotient of a group scheme by a flat subgroup scheme
description: For an S-group scheme G and a flat, finitely presented closed subgroup scheme H, a quotient G/H is an S-scheme Q with a morphism π:G→Q, constant on the cosets of H, that makes G a right H-torsor over Q; it is unique up to unique isomorphism when it exists. If H is normal in G, the quotient is an S-group scheme and π is a homomorphism with kernel H.

title: Irreducible-subset criterion for constructibility in a Noetherian space
description: A subset E of a Noetherian topological space X is constructible if and only if, for every irreducible closed subset Z⊆X, the intersection E∩Z either contains a nonempty open subset of Z or is not dense in Z.

title: Generic constancy of the number of geometric connected components of fibres
description: Let f:X→Y be a morphism of schemes of finite type and y∈Y. There is a nonempty open subset V of the closure of {y} such that the number of connected components of the geometric fibres (X_v)_K, for K a separably closed extension of κ(v), is constant for v∈V.

title: Connected components under extension of a separably closed field
description: If X is a scheme over a separably closed field k and K/k is any field extension, the projection X_K→X induces a bijection on connected components. Hence the number of connected components of X×_k K, for K a separably closed extension of k, does not depend on K, and for a morphism of schemes this number for the fibres is compatible with arbitrary base change.

title: Finiteness of the integral closure in a finite separable extension
description: Let A be an integrally closed domain with fraction field K and B its integral closure in a finite separable extension L/K of degree m. Using a K-basis of L contained in B and its dual basis for the trace pairing, B lies between two free A-submodules of L of rank m. Hence B is a finitely generated A-module when A is Noetherian, and free of rank m when A is a principal ideal domain.

title: Finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian
description: If A is a Noetherian commutative ring, every finitely generated A-module M is Noetherian: every submodule of M is finitely generated, equivalently every ascending chain of submodules of M is eventually constant.

title: Transitivity of integrality
description: If A⊆B⊆C are commutative rings with B integral over A and C integral over B, then C is integral over A. Consequently the integral closure of A in C is integrally closed in C; for an integral domain A, its integral closure in an algebraic extension of its fraction field is an integrally closed domain.

title: Integral domains algebraic over a field are fields
description: If an integral domain B contains a field k and every element of B is algebraic over k, then B is a field: for nonzero b∈B, multiplication by b is an injective k-linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional k-vector space k[b], hence surjective, so b is invertible.

title: Radicial morphism of schemes
description: A morphism of schemes f:X→S is radicial if it is injective on underlying points and every residue field extension κ(x)/κ(f(x)) is purely inseparable; equivalently f is universally injective, meaning every base change of f is injective on underlying points.

title: Fibral criterion for smooth and étale morphisms
description: Let X and Y be S-schemes locally of finite presentation with X flat over S, and f:X→Y an S-morphism. Then f is smooth (respectively étale) if and only if every fibre f_s:X_s→Y_s is smooth (respectively étale), and Y is then flat over S at the points of f(X); pointwise, f is étale at x if f_s is étale at x (EGA IV₄ 17.8.2–17.8.3, resting on the fibral flatness criterion EGA IV₃ 11.3.10).

title: Separatedness of Proj of a graded ring
description: For a graded commutative ring S=⊕_(d≥0)S_d, the scheme Proj(S) is separated over Spec(S₀). In particular projective space Pⁿ_ℤ is a separated scheme.

title: Valuative criterion for Proj of a finitely generated graded ring
description: If a graded ring S is finitely generated as an S₀-algebra, then Proj(S)→Spec(S₀) satisfies the existence and uniqueness parts of the valuative criterion: for a valuation ring A with fraction field K, every morphism Spec K→Proj(S) compatible with a given Spec A→Spec(S₀) extends uniquely to Spec A→Proj(S).

title: Stability of proper morphisms under composition and base change
description: Closed immersions of schemes are proper, a composition of proper morphisms of schemes is proper, and the base change of a proper morphism along any morphism of schemes is proper.

title: Morphisms from proper schemes to separated schemes are proper
description: Let X→S be proper and Y→S separated. Then every S-morphism X→Y is proper, as the composite of the graph X→X×_S Y, a closed immersion, with the base-changed projection X×_S Y→Y; in particular its image is closed in Y.

title: Representability and smoothness of normalizers of multiplicative-type subgroups
description: Let G be a finitely presented affine group scheme over S and Y,Y′⊆G finitely presented closed subschemes with Y finite flat over S or a subgroup of multiplicative type. The transporter of Y into Y′ is represented by a finitely presented closed subscheme of G, so the normalizer N_G(Y) is a finitely presented closed subgroup. If G is smooth and Y,Y′ are subgroups of multiplicative type, these schemes are smooth (SGA 3 XI 2.4bis; Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 2.1.2).

title: Representability of Hom-schemes out of finite flat schemes
description: If X→S is finite, flat and finitely presented and Y→S is affine of finite presentation, the functor S′↦Hom_(S′)(X_(S′),Y_(S′)) is represented by an affine S-scheme of finite presentation. Likewise group homomorphisms from a finite flat finitely presented S-group to an affine finitely presented S-group are classified by an affine finitely presented S-scheme Hom_(S-gp)(G,G′).

title: Relative schematic density of torsion in groups of multiplicative type
description: If H is a group scheme of multiplicative type over a scheme S, the torsion subgroups H[n], n≥1, are relatively schematically dense in H: after any base change S′→S, the only closed subscheme of H_(S′) containing every H[n]_(S′) is H_(S′) itself (EGA IV₃ 11.10.8–11.10.10).

title: Algebraic space
description: An algebraic space over a scheme S is a sheaf of sets F on the category of S-schemes with the fppf topology whose diagonal F→F×_S F is representable by schemes and which admits a surjective étale morphism U→F from a scheme U. Every scheme is an algebraic space; quotients of schemes by flat equivalence relations are in general algebraic spaces rather than schemes.

title: Artin’s theorem on quotients by flat equivalence relations
description: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a Noetherian scheme S and R⊆X×_S X an equivalence relation represented by a closed subscheme such that both projections R→X are flat. Then the fppf quotient sheaf X/R is a separated algebraic space of finite type over S (M. Artin, Versal deformations and algebraic stacks, 1974, Corollary 6.3).

title: Quasi-finite separated algebraic spaces over Noetherian schemes are schemes
description: An algebraic space that is quasi-finite and separated over a Noetherian scheme is a scheme (Knutson, Algebraic Spaces, II 6.15); Laumon–Moret-Bailly remove the Noetherian hypothesis.

title: Normalization of a scheme in a morphism
description: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism f:Y→X, let 𝒪′ be the integral closure of 𝒪_X in the quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebra f_*𝒪_Y. The normalization of X in Y is the integral morphism ν:X′=Spec_X(𝒪′)→X, through which f factors as Y→X′→X.

title: Relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent algebra
description: For a scheme S and a quasi-coherent sheaf of 𝒪_S-algebras 𝒜, the relative spectrum π:Spec_S(𝒜)→S is the S-scheme glued from the affine schemes Spec 𝒜(U) over affine opens U⊆S. It is affine over S with π_*𝒪=𝒜, and 𝒜↦Spec_S(𝒜) is an anti-equivalence between quasi-coherent 𝒪_S-algebras and schemes affine over S.

title: Quasi-finite separated morphisms are quasi-affine
description: Let f:X→S be quasi-finite and separated, and let X→S′→S be its factorization through the normalization S′ of S in X. Then X→S′ is a quasi-compact open immersion and S′→S is integral; in particular f is quasi-affine (EGA IV₃ 18.12.12).

title: Integral quasi-coherent algebras are directed colimits of finite ones
description: On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme X, every integral quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebra is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-subalgebras, and it is also a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-algebras.

title: Limit of an inverse system of schemes with affine transition morphisms
description: A directed inverse system of schemes S_i with affine transition morphisms has a limit S=lim S_i in the category of schemes; S is affine over each S_i, being the relative spectrum over a fixed S_0 of the colimit of the pushed-forward structure sheaves. If the S_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every quasi-compact open subset of S is the inverse image of a quasi-compact open subset of some S_i.

title: Immersions into a limit of schemes descend to a finite stage
description: Let X=lim X_i be a directed limit of S-schemes with affine transition morphisms and Y→X an S-morphism. If Y→X is a closed immersion, the X_i are quasi-compact and Y is locally of finite type over S, then Y→X_i is a closed immersion for all large i; if Y→X is an immersion, Y is quasi-compact and the X_i are quasi-separated, then Y→X_i is an immersion for large i; and if the transition morphisms are closed immersions, X_i→S is locally of finite type and Y→S is locally of finite presentation, an isomorphism Y→X is already an isomorphism onto X_i for large i.

title: Factorization of quasi-compact immersions
description: A quasi-compact immersion of schemes Z→X factors as an open immersion of Z into its scheme-theoretic closure followed by a closed immersion of that closure into X.

title: Finite morphisms are limits of finitely presented finite morphisms
description: If X→S is a finite morphism and S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then X is a directed limit lim X_i of schemes finite and of finite presentation over S whose transition morphisms are closed immersions.

title: Geometrically reduced scheme over a field
description: A scheme X over a field k is geometrically reduced if its base change X×_k Spec K is reduced for every field extension K/k; for X locally of finite type it suffices that the base change to an algebraic closure of k is reduced. A k-algebra A is geometrically reduced when Spec A is, i.e. A⊗_k K is reduced for every field extension K.

title: Dimension of local rings at closed points of an irreducible algebraic scheme
description: If X is an irreducible scheme of finite type over a field and x is a closed point of X, then the local ring O_(X,x) has Krull dimension dim X; equivalently every maximal ideal of a finitely generated algebra over a field whose nilradical is prime has height equal to its dimension (Noether normalization).

title: Connected components of an algebraic group are irreducible and equidimensional
description: For an algebraic group G over a field, every connected component of G is irreducible, so the irreducible components are the connected components, and they all have dimension dim G; consequently every local ring O_(G,x) at a closed point has Krull dimension dim G. The proof uses translations by points over an algebraic closure.

title: Dense smooth locus of a geometrically reduced algebraic scheme
description: If X is a geometrically reduced scheme of finite type over a field k, the set of points at which X→Spec k is smooth is a dense open subset of X. For X irreducible this follows from the existence of a separating transcendence basis of its function field, which makes X birational to a hypersurface f(T₁,…,T_(d+1))=0 with ∂f/∂T_(d+1)≠0.

title: Regular local rings are integral domains
description: Every regular Noetherian local ring is an integral domain (indeed a unique factorization domain, by the Auslander–Buchsbaum theorem); in particular it is reduced.

title: Reduced algebras over a perfect field are geometrically reduced
description: If k is a perfect field and A is a reduced k-algebra, then A⊗_k K is reduced for every field extension K of k. Hence every reduced scheme over a perfect field is geometrically reduced.

title: Quotient of a topological group by a normal subgroup
description: If N is a normal subgroup of a topological group G, then the quotient group G/N with the quotient topology is a topological group and the projection G→G/N is open; G/N is Hausdorff if and only if N is closed in G.

title: ℓ-adic logarithmic valuation of a p-adic field
description: For a prime ℓ and a finite extension F of ℚ_p, Jaulent’s ℓ-adic logarithmic valuation is ṽ_F=−Log_ℓ|·|_F/deg F on the ℓ-adic completion ℛ_F of F×. Here Log_ℓ is Iwasawa’s ℓ-adic logarithm, |x|_F is the principal ℓ-adic absolute value ⟨N𝔭^(−v_F(x))⟩ for p≠ℓ and ⟨N_(F/ℚ_ℓ)(x)N𝔭^(−v_F(x))⟩ for p=ℓ (⟨·⟩ the projection of ℤ_ℓ^× onto its principal units), and deg F=f̃_F·deg p with f̃_F=[F∩ℚ̂_p^c:ℚ_p] the logarithmic inertia degree, deg p=Log_ℓ p for p≠ℓ and deg ℓ=ℓ (4 if ℓ=2).

title: Kernel and image of the ℓ-adic logarithmic valuation
description: For a prime ℓ and a finite extension F of ℚ_p, the ℓ-adic logarithmic valuation ṽ_F is a surjective ℤ_ℓ-linear map from the ℓ-adic completion ℛ_F of F× onto ℤ_ℓ whose kernel is the local logarithmic unit group (the cyclotomic norms in ℛ_F). If p≠ℓ it is proportional to the ordinary normalized valuation: ṽ_F=(f_F/f̃_F)·v_F, where the ratio of the ordinary and logarithmic inertia degrees is a power of p (Jaulent 1994, Théorème 1.4).

title: Richardson’s closed-orbit theorem for fixed-point subgroups
description: Let G be a connected reductive closed normal subgroup of an affine algebraic group H over an algebraically closed field, S a linearly reductive closed subgroup of H and Z=(G^S)° the identity component of the S-centralizer of G. If H acts morphically on an affine variety X and x is an S-fixed point of X, then some one-parameter subgroup λ of Z has lim_(t→0)λ(t)·x in the unique closed G-orbit in the closure of G·x; in particular G·x is closed if and only if Z·x is closed (Richardson 1982, Theorem C).

title: Conjugacy classes of semisimple elements are closed
description: In an affine algebraic group G over an algebraically closed field, the conjugacy class of every semisimple element is Zariski closed in G (Humphreys, Linear Algebraic Groups §18.2; Steinberg 1965, 6.14).

title: Jordan decomposition in an affine algebraic group
description: Every element g of an affine algebraic group over an algebraically closed field has a unique factorization g=g_s g_u=g_u g_s with g_s semisimple and g_u unipotent (its image in a faithful representation is unipotent). The factors are preserved by homomorphisms of algebraic groups, in particular by conjugation, and lie in every closed subgroup containing g.

title: Unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup as a product of root subgroups
description: Let G be a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field, B a Borel subgroup and T⊆B a maximal torus, with positive roots Φ⁺ determined by B. Then B=T⋉U for the unipotent radical U of B, and for any ordering of Φ⁺ the product map ∏_(α∈Φ⁺)U_α→U of root subgroups is an isomorphism of varieties; thus each u∈U is uniquely ∏_α x_α(c_α).

title: Surjectivity of linearly independent characters of a torus
description: If χ₁,…,χ_n are characters of an algebraic torus T over an algebraically closed field k that are linearly independent in the character group X(T), then t↦(χ₁(t),…,χ_n(t)) maps T(k) onto (k^×)^n.

title: Inverse limit of a directed inverse system of groups
description: For a directed set I, an inverse system of groups consists of groups G_i and homomorphisms p_ij:G_j→G_i for i≤j with p_ii=id and p_ij∘p_jk=p_ik. Its inverse limit lim G_i is the subgroup of ∏G_i of families (g_i) with p_ij(g_j)=g_i for all i≤j, with the coordinate projections; it is universal among families of homomorphisms into the G_i compatible with the p_ij. For topological groups and continuous p_ij it carries the subspace topology of the product topology, finite groups being discrete.

title: One-sided shift on sequences over a finite alphabet
description: For a finite set 𝒜, the one-sided shift is the map σ:𝒜^ℕ₀→𝒜^ℕ₀, (σx)_n=x_{n+1}, on one-sided sequences, with the product of the discrete topologies on 𝒜. A closed subset X with σ(X)⊆X is a one-sided subshift.

title: Weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation
description: A probability-preserving transformation T of (X,𝔅,μ) is weakly mixing if N⁻¹∑_{n=1}^N|μ(A∩T⁻ⁿB)−μ(A)μ(B)|→0 for all measurable A,B, equivalently N⁻¹∑_{n=1}^N(∫f·g∘Tⁿdμ−∫f dμ∫g dμ)²→0 for all f,g∈L²(μ). This holds exactly when T×T is ergodic for μ×μ.

title: Compact measure-preserving system
description: A probability-preserving system (X,𝔅,μ,T) is compact if for every f∈L²(μ) the orbit {f,Tf,T²f,…} under the Koopman operator Tf=f∘T has compact closure in the norm topology of L²(μ); a function with this property is called almost periodic. Ergodic rotations of compact groups are examples.

title: Rokhlin disintegration theorem for probability measures
description: Let π:(X,𝔅,μ)→(Y,𝔇,ν) be a measurable map of standard Borel probability spaces with π_*μ=ν. There is a ν-almost everywhere unique measurable family y↦μ_y of Borel probability measures on X with μ_y(π⁻¹{y})=1 for ν-a.e. y and μ(A)=∫μ_y(A)dν(y) for every measurable A; then f↦∫f dμ_{π(x)} is the conditional expectation given π⁻¹𝔇. If π is a factor map from (X,μ,T) to (Y,ν,S), then T_*μ_y=μ_{Sy} for ν-a.e. y.

title: Relative product of a measure-preserving system over a factor
description: For a factor map π from a probability-preserving system (X,μ,T) to (Y,ν,S), with disintegration μ=∫μ_y dν(y), the relative product X×_Y X is the system (X×X, μ×_Yμ, T×T) with μ×_Yμ=∫(μ_y×μ_y)dν(y). It is probability-preserving, has Y as a factor, and ∫f(x)g(x′)d(μ×_Yμ)=∫E(f|Y)E(g|Y)dν.

title: Relatively weakly mixing extension of measure-preserving systems
description: An extension π:(X,μ,T)→(Y,ν,S) of ergodic probability-preserving systems is relatively weakly mixing if the relative product X×_Y X with T×T is ergodic. Over the one-point factor this is weak mixing of T.

title: Compact extension of measure-preserving systems
description: An extension π:(X,μ,T)→(Y,ν,S) of probability-preserving systems, with disintegration μ=∫μ_y dν(y), is compact if the functions almost periodic relative to Y are dense in L²(μ); f is almost periodic relative to Y if for every δ>0 there are g_1,…,g_m∈L²(μ) such that for every n, min_s‖Tⁿf−g_s‖_{L²(μ_y)}<δ for ν-almost every y. Over the one-point factor this is a compact system.

title: Product estimate for bounded elements of a Dirichlet form domain
description: For a symmetric Dirichlet form E on L²(X,m), if u and v are essentially bounded elements of its domain then uv lies in the domain and E(uv,uv)^{1/2}≤‖u‖_∞E(v,v)^{1/2}+‖v‖_∞E(u,u)^{1/2}; hence the bounded elements of the domain form an algebra.

title: Normal contractions operate on a Dirichlet form
description: If E is a symmetric Dirichlet form on L²(X,m) and φ:ℝ→ℝ is a normal contraction, φ(0)=0 and |φ(s)−φ(t)|≤|s−t|, then φ∘u lies in the domain and E(φ∘u,φ∘u)≤E(u,u) for every u in the domain. Conversely, a closed symmetric form on which the unit contraction operates has this property.

title: Leibniz rule for energy measures of a strongly local Dirichlet form
description: For a strongly local regular symmetric Dirichlet form and bounded u,v,w in its domain, the mutual energy measures satisfy dν_(uv,w)=ũ dν_(v,w)+ṽ dν_(u,w), where ũ and ṽ are quasi-continuous modifications of u and v.

title: Beurling–Deny decomposition of a regular Dirichlet form
description: Every regular symmetric Dirichlet form E on L²(X,m) satisfies, for u,v in its domain with compact support and continuous, E(u,v)=E^(c)(u,v)+∫∫_{X×X∖diag}(u(x)−u(y))(v(x)−v(y))J(dx,dy)+∫uv dk, where E^(c) is a strongly local symmetric form, J is a symmetric positive Radon measure off the diagonal (jumping measure) and k is a positive Radon measure (killing measure). E^(c), J and k are uniquely determined by E; in particular E is strongly local exactly when J=0 and k=0.

title: Proper map between topological spaces
description: A continuous map f:X→Y between topological spaces is proper if the preimage f⁻¹(K) of every compact subset K⊆Y is compact. Between locally compact Hausdorff spaces, an injective proper map is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset.

title: Open mapping theorem for σ-compact locally compact group actions
description: If a σ-compact locally compact group G acts continuously and transitively on a locally compact Hausdorff space X, then for every x∈X the orbit map G/G_x→X, gG_x↦gx, is a homeomorphism. In particular a continuous surjective homomorphism from a σ-compact locally compact group onto a locally compact Hausdorff group is open.

title: Markov–Kakutani fixed point theorem
description: A family of pairwise commuting continuous affine maps of a nonempty compact convex subset C of a Hausdorff topological vector space into itself has a common fixed point. For a single map T, every cluster point of the averages n⁻¹∑_(j<n)Tʲx is fixed.

title: Ergodic measures are the extreme invariant probability measures
description: For a family of measurable self-maps of a measurable space, in particular a continuous map of a compact space with its Borel σ-algebra, an invariant probability measure is an extreme point of the convex set of invariant probability measures exactly when it is ergodic.

title: Choquet’s representation theorem for metrizable compact convex sets
description: If K is a metrizable compact convex subset of a locally convex Hausdorff space, its set of extreme points is a G_δ and every x∈K is represented by a Borel probability measure μ on K with μ(ext K)=1, i.e. f(x)=∫f dμ for every continuous affine f on K.

title: Choquet–Meyer uniqueness theorem
description: A compact convex subset K of a locally convex Hausdorff space, embedded in a closed hyperplane not containing 0, is a Choquet simplex (each point has a unique maximal representing measure) exactly when the cone generated by K is a lattice in its own order. For metrizable K the unique maximal measure is the unique representing measure concentrated on ext K.

title: L² stochastic integral against a square-integrable martingale
description: For a càdlàg square-integrable martingale M and a predictable X with E∫_(0,t]X_s²d[M]_s<∞ for all t, X·M is the càdlàg square-integrable martingale, unique up to indistinguishability, with E[((X·M)−(Xⁿ·M))_t²]→0 for every t whenever simple predictable Xⁿ=∑ξ_i1_(t_i,t_(i+1)] (ξ_i bounded F_(t_i)-measurable) approximate X in the norms (E∫_(0,t]|X−Xⁿ|²d[M])^(1/2); here (Xⁿ·M)_t=∑ξ_i(M_(t_(i+1)∧t)−M_(t_i∧t)).

title: Kronecker factor of an ergodic system
description: For an ergodic probability-preserving system (X,μ,T), its Kronecker factor is the factor determined by the T-invariant sub-σ-algebra generated by the eigenfunctions of the Koopman operator, i.e. the f∈L²(μ) with f∘T=λf for a constant λ. It is realized by an ergodic rotation of a compact abelian group, and is the largest factor of this kind.

title: C*-dynamical system
description: A C*-dynamical system (A,G,α) consists of a C*-algebra A, a locally compact group G and a group homomorphism α:G→Aut(A) into the star automorphisms (bijective star homomorphisms A→A) that is continuous for pointwise norm convergence: s↦α_s(a) is norm-continuous for each a∈A.

title: Operator system in a unital C*-algebra
description: An operator system is a self-adjoint linear subspace S of a unital C*-algebra A containing the unit. Each M_n(S)⊆M_n(A) inherits a positive cone, so positive and completely positive maps on S are defined as for C*-algebras.

title: Arveson extension theorem for operator systems
description: If S is an operator system in a unital C*-algebra A and φ:S→B(H) is completely positive, then φ extends to a completely positive map A→B(H); that is, B(H) is injective in the category of operator systems and completely positive maps.

title: Paulsen off-diagonal lemma
description: Let X be a subspace of a unital C*-algebra A, φ:X→B a linear map into a unital C*-algebra, and S_X={[λ1,x;y*,μ1]:λ,μ∈ℂ,x,y∈X}⊆M₂(A) the Paulsen operator system. Then [λ1,x;y*,μ1]↦[λ1,φ(x);φ(y)*,μ1] is completely positive on S_X if and only if φ is completely contractive.

title: Order reversal of inversion in a unital C*-algebra
description: If x and y are invertible positive elements of a unital C*-algebra with x≤y, then y⁻¹≤x⁻¹.

title: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for positive semidefinite Hermitian forms
description: If s is a positive semidefinite Hermitian sesquilinear form on a complex vector space V, then |s(x,y)|²≤s(x,x)s(y,y). Hence N={x:s(x,x)=0} is a linear subspace and s induces an inner product on V/N.

title: Nontangential limit at a point of the unit circle
description: A function F on the unit disk 𝔻 has nontangential limit L at ζ∈𝕋 if F(z)→L as z→ζ within each Stolz angle S_α(ζ)={z∈𝔻:|z−ζ|<α(1−|z|)}, α>1. Radial approach is the special case z=rζ.

title: Simple polytope
description: An n-dimensional convex polytope in ℝⁿ is simple if each of its vertices (0-dimensional faces) lies in exactly n facets ((n−1)-dimensional faces).

title: Strongly isomorphic convex polytopes
description: Convex polytopes P,Q⊂ℝⁿ are strongly isomorphic if dim F(P,u)=dim F(Q,u) for every unit vector u, where F(P,u)=P∩{x:⟨x,u⟩=h(P,u)} is the face of P with outer normal u. Strongly isomorphic polytopes are combinatorially isomorphic.

title: Fatou’s theorem on nontangential limits of Poisson integrals
description: Let μ be a finite complex Borel measure on the unit circle with Lebesgue decomposition dμ=h dm+dμ_s, h∈L¹(m), μ_s⊥m. Then at every ζ where dμ/dm(ζ)=h(ζ) exists, hence for m-almost every ζ, the Poisson integral P[μ](z) tends to h(ζ) as z→ζ within every Stolz angle.

title: Identification of Hardy Hᵖ functions with their boundary functions
description: For 1≤p≤∞ and f∈Hᵖ(𝔻) there is a unique f̃∈Lᵖ(𝕋) with vanishing negative Fourier coefficients such that f(r·)=f̃∗P_r on 𝕋 for 0<r<1, so f is the Poisson integral of f̃; f(r·)→f̃ in Lᵖ as r↑1 (weak-* when p=∞), and ‖f‖_{Hᵖ}=‖f̃‖_p.

title: Irreducible positive operator on a Banach lattice
description: A positive operator T on a Banach lattice E is irreducible if {0} and E are the only closed ideals J of E with T(J)⊆J. For a positive kernel operator on Lᵖ(μ), 1≤p<∞, this means the kernel gives positive mass to (X∖S)×S whenever S and X∖S have positive measure.

title: Ando–Krieger theorem on positive spectral radius
description: Let E be a Banach lattice with order continuous norm and T>0 an irreducible positive operator in the band of regular operators generated by the order continuous finite-rank operators, for example an irreducible positive kernel operator on Lᵖ(μ), 1≤p<∞. Then the spectral radius r(T) is strictly positive.

title: Kernel operators on Lᵖ as the band generated by finite-rank operators
description: For σ-finite measure spaces (X,μ),(Y,ν) and 1≤p,q≤∞, a regular operator T:Lᵖ(μ)→L^q(ν) belongs to the band generated by the order continuous finite-rank operators exactly when it is given by a measurable kernel, Tf(t)=∫K(s,t)f(s)dμ(s); T↦K is a lattice isomorphism onto an ideal of measurable kernels.

title: Spectral radius of a positive operator lies in its spectrum
description: For a positive operator T on a complex Banach lattice, the spectral radius r(T) belongs to the spectrum σ(T).

title: Riesz–Schauder theory for operators with a compact power
description: If T is a bounded operator on a complex Banach space and some power Tᵏ is compact, then σ(T)∖{0} is at most countable with 0 as its only possible accumulation point, and each nonzero λ∈σ(T) is a pole of the resolvent and an eigenvalue whose spectral projection has finite rank.

title: Perron–Frobenius theorem for irreducible positive operators with a resolvent pole
description: Let T>0 be an irreducible positive operator on a Banach lattice with r(T)>0 a pole of the resolvent. Then r(T) is a pole of order one with residue a rank-one projection φ⊗u, φ strictly positive and u quasi-interior; the eigenspace for r(T) is spanned by u; each peripheral eigenvalue is simple; and r(T) is the only eigenvalue with a positive eigenvector.

title: Trivial peripheral point spectrum of eventually quasi-interior positive operators
description: Let T>0 on a Banach lattice have r(T)=1 and a nonzero positive fixed vector of its adjoint, and suppose that for each x>0 some Tⁿx is a quasi-interior point of the positive cone. Then 1 is the only eigenvalue of T of modulus one.

title: Power-series representability of Cauchy integrals of measures
description: Let μ be a finite complex measure on a measure space X and φ a bounded complex measurable function on X. Then f(z)=∫dμ(ζ)/(φ(ζ)−z) is representable by convergent power series, hence holomorphic, on every open set disjoint from the closure of φ(X).

title: Cauchy formula on a compact set via a cycle in its neighbourhood
description: If K is a compact subset of an open set Ω⊆ℂ, there is a cycle Γ in Ω∖K, made of finitely many oriented segments, such that f(z)=(2πi)⁻¹∫_Γ f(w)(w−z)⁻¹dw for every f holomorphic on Ω and every z∈K.

title: Boundary H² regularity for second-order elliptic Dirichlet problems
description: Let U⊂ℝⁿ be bounded with C² boundary and L=−∑∂_j(a^{ij}∂_i)+∑b^i∂_i+c uniformly elliptic with a^{ij}∈C¹(Ū), b^i,c∈L^∞(U). If f∈L²(U) and u∈H₀¹(U) weakly solves Lu=f, then u∈H²(U) and ‖u‖_{H²}≤C(‖f‖_{L²}+‖u‖_{L²}) with C depending only on U and the coefficients.

title: Openness of the invertible group and continuity of inversion in a Banach algebra
description: In a unital complex Banach algebra the invertible elements form an open set G: if x∈G and ‖h‖<‖x⁻¹‖⁻¹ then x+h∈G. Inversion is a homeomorphism of G, differentiable with derivative h↦−x⁻¹hx⁻¹.

title: Normal cones and support sets of a Minkowski sum
description: For nonempty compact convex K,L⊂ℝⁿ, x∈K and y∈L, the normal cone of K+L at x+y is N(K,x)∩N(L,y), and the support set of K+L at x+y is the sum of the support sets of K at x and of L at y.

title: Normal cones of a polytope generated by facet normals
description: If P⊂ℝⁿ is an n-dimensional polytope with facets F₁,…,F_k and outer unit facet normals u₁,…,u_k, then for each proper face F the normal cone N(P,F) is the positive hull of the u_i with F⊆F_i.

title: Vertex normal-cone criterion for strongly isomorphic polytopes
description: Two convex polytopes in ℝⁿ are strongly isomorphic exactly when they have the same set of normal cones at their vertices: {N(P,x):x a vertex of P}={N(Q,y):y a vertex of Q}.

title: Geometrically integral scheme over a field
description: A scheme X over a field k is geometrically integral if for every field extension k′/k the base change X_(k′)=X×_(Spec k)Spec k′ is an integral scheme.

title: Lie subalgebra
description: A Lie subalgebra of a Lie algebra 𝔤 over a field is a vector subspace 𝔥⊆𝔤 closed under the bracket, [𝔥,𝔥]⊆𝔥; with the restricted bracket it is itself a Lie algebra.

title: Immersion of smooth manifolds
description: A smooth map F:M→N of smooth manifolds is an immersion if its differential dF_x:T_xM→T_(F(x))N is injective at every point x∈M. An injective immersion need not be a homeomorphism onto its image.

title: Canonical sheaf and canonical divisor of a smooth variety
description: For a scheme X smooth of pure dimension n over a field k, the canonical sheaf is ω_X=∧ⁿΩ¹_(X/k), the top exterior power of the sheaf of Kähler differentials. If X is moreover integral, a canonical divisor K_X is a Cartier divisor whose associated invertible sheaf O_X(K_X) is isomorphic to ω_X; it is well defined up to linear equivalence.

title: Arithmetic genus of a projective curve
description: For a projective curve C over a field k, that is a projective k-scheme of dimension one, the arithmetic genus is p_a(C)=1−χ(C,O_C)=1−dim_k H⁰(C,O_C)+dim_k H¹(C,O_C).

title: Regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay
description: Every regular local ring (R,𝔪) of dimension d is Cohen–Macaulay: a minimal system of generators x₁,…,x_d of 𝔪 is a regular sequence, and each R/(x₁,…,x_c) is regular of dimension d−c.

title: Dimension criterion for regular sequences in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring
description: In a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring (R,𝔪), elements x₁,…,x_c∈𝔪 form a regular sequence if and only if dim R/(x₁,…,x_c)=dim R−c; in that case every quotient R/(x₁,…,x_i) is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension dim R−i.

title: Localizations of Cohen–Macaulay local rings are Cohen–Macaulay
description: If R is a Cohen–Macaulay Noetherian local ring and 𝔭 is a prime ideal of R, then the localization R_𝔭 is Cohen–Macaulay; hence a Noetherian ring is Cohen–Macaulay as soon as its localizations at maximal ideals are.

title: Local rings of a polynomial ring at maximal ideals are regular
description: For a field k, the localization of the polynomial ring k[x₁,…,x_n] at any maximal ideal is a regular local ring of dimension n; in particular k[x₁,…,x_n] is a regular ring.

title: Cotangent exact sequence of Kähler differentials
description: For ring maps A→B→C there is an exact sequence C⊗_BΩ_(B/A)→Ω_(C/A)→Ω_(C/B)→0, and for morphisms of schemes X→Y→Z the corresponding sequence π*Ω_(Y/Z)→Ω_(X/Z)→Ω_(X/Y)→0 of quasi-coherent sheaves on X is exact.

title: Differentials of a smooth morphism are locally free
description: If π:X→Y is a smooth morphism of schemes of relative dimension n, then the sheaf of relative Kähler differentials Ω_(X/Y) is locally free of rank n. In particular a smooth k-scheme of pure dimension n has Ω_(X/k) locally free of rank n.

title: Kähler differentials vanish for separable algebraic field extensions
description: If L/K is a separable algebraic field extension, then the module of Kähler differentials Ω_(L/K) is zero.

title: Global Frobenius theorem for involutive distributions
description: Let 𝒟 be a smooth involutive distribution of rank c on a smooth manifold M. Through every point m∈M passes a unique maximal connected integral manifold of 𝒟, and every connected integral manifold of 𝒟 through m is contained in it.

title: Smooth factorization through integral manifolds of involutive distributions
description: Let (P,φ) be an integral manifold of a smooth involutive distribution on M and ψ:N→M a smooth map with ψ(N)⊆φ(P). Then the unique map ψ₀:N→P with φ∘ψ₀=ψ is continuous and hence smooth.

title: Seesaw principle for invertible sheaves on products
description: Let V be a complete variety and T a variety over a field, and L an invertible sheaf on V×T. The set of t∈T with L|_(V×{t}) trivial is closed in T. If L|_(V×{t}) is trivial for all t and L|_({v}×T) is trivial for some v∈V(k), then L is trivial.

title: Translation-invariant invertible sheaves on an abelian variety
description: For an invertible sheaf L on an abelian variety A with group law m and projections p,q:A×A→A, the following are equivalent: t_a*L≅L for all a∈A(k^al); the kernel K(L) of φ_L is all of A; m*L≅p*L⊗q*L. Such sheaves constitute Pic⁰(A).

title: Mumford homomorphism of an ample sheaf is onto Pic⁰
description: If L is an ample invertible sheaf on an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field, then every invertible sheaf in Pic⁰(A) is isomorphic to t_a*L⊗L⁻¹ for some a∈A; that is, φ_L maps A onto Pic⁰(A)=A^∨(k).

title: Euler-characteristic formula for intersection numbers on a surface
description: For divisors C,D on a smooth projective surface X over a field, the intersection number satisfies C·D=χ(O_X)−χ(O_X(−C))−χ(O_X(−D))+χ(O_X(−C−D)), and if C is an effective curve then C·D=deg_C(O_X(D)|_C).

title: Serre duality for smooth projective varieties
description: For a smooth projective variety X of pure dimension n over a field k with canonical sheaf ω_X and a locally free sheaf F of finite rank, H^i(X,F) is naturally dual to H^(n−i)(X,F^∨⊗ω_X) for all i; in particular χ(X,F)=(−1)ⁿχ(X,F^∨⊗ω_X).

title: Maximal abelian extension of a field
description: For a field K with a fixed separable closure K^sep, the maximal abelian extension K^ab is the compositum in K^sep of all finite Galois extensions of K whose Galois group is abelian.

title: Norm functoriality of the local Artin map
description: For local fields L⊇E⊇K with L/K Galois, the local Artin maps satisfy φ_(L/K)(Nm_(E/K)a)=φ_(L/E)(a) in Gal(L/K)^ab for a∈E^×, the right side mapped through Gal(L/E)⊆Gal(L/K); equivalently φ_E(a)|_(K^ab)=φ_K(Nm_(E/K)a).

title: Idelic norm groups contain open subgroups
description: For a finite extension L/K of number fields, the norm group Nm_(L/K)(I_L) contains an open subgroup of the idele group I_K.

title: Second inequality of global class field theory
description: For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields, the index (I_K:K^×·Nm_(L/K)I_L) is finite and divides [L:K]; equivalently H¹(Gal(L/K),C_L)=0 and the order of H²(Gal(L/K),C_L) divides [L:K].

title: Frobenius elements generate the Galois group of a solvable extension
description: If L/K is a finite solvable Galois extension of number fields and T a finite set of primes containing the ramified ones, then the Frobenius elements of the primes outside T generate Gal(L/K).

title: Local Artin map of ℚ_p on cyclotomic extensions
description: For a=u·p^t with u∈ℤ_p^×, the local Artin map of ℚ_p acts on a p^r-th root of unity by ζ↦ζ^(u₀⁻¹), u₀≡u mod p^r, and on an m-th root of unity with p∤m by ζ↦ζ^(p^t).

title: Cup-product formula for the local Artin map
description: For a finite abelian extension L/K of local fields with group G, a∈K^× and a character χ:G→ℚ/ℤ with coboundary δχ∈H²(G,ℤ), one has χ(φ_(L/K)(a))=inv_K(a∪δχ), where a∪δχ∈H²(G,L^×).

title: Splitting of global Brauer classes by cyclic cyclotomic extensions
description: For a number field K, every element of H²(Gal(K^al/K),K^al×) maps to zero in H²(Gal(K^al/L),K^al×) for some cyclic cyclotomic extension L of K.

title: Analytic continuation of ray class L-series
description: For a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K of degree d and a character χ of the ray class group, L(s,χ)=∏_(𝔭∤𝔪)(1−χ(𝔭)N𝔭^(−s))^(−1) extends analytically to Re s>1−1/d if χ is nontrivial, while the Dedekind zeta function ζ_K is analytic there except for a simple pole at s=1.

title: Nonvanishing at s=1 of ray class L-series
description: For a modulus 𝔪 of a number field K and a nontrivial character χ of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(K), the L-series L(s,χ) does not vanish at s=1.

title: Curve y^p=f(x) as a cyclic cover of the projective line
description: For a prime p, a perfect field k of characteristic not p and a nonconstant f∈k[x] whose roots in an algebraic closure all have multiplicity less than p, the curve y^p=f(x) is the smooth projective geometrically connected curve X over k with function field k(x)[y]/(y^p−f(x)). The function x gives a degree-p cover X→ℙ¹, and if k contains a primitive p-th root of unity ζ, then (x,y)↦(x,ζy) is an automorphism of X over ℙ¹.

title: Weil reciprocity on a curve
description: For nonzero rational functions f,g with disjoint divisors on a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field, f(div g)=g(div f), where a function is evaluated on a divisor ∑n_PP as ∏f(P)^(n_P).

title: Generalized Jacobian of a curve with a modulus
description: For a smooth projective curve X over a field and an effective divisor 𝔪, the generalized Jacobian J_𝔪 is the commutative algebraic group whose points classify degree-zero divisors prime to 𝔪 modulo divisors of functions congruent to 1 modulo 𝔪; it is an extension of the Jacobian of X by a connected linear algebraic group.

title: Unramified image of the descent map under good reduction
description: Let A be an abelian variety with good reduction over a nonarchimedean local field whose residue characteristic does not divide the degree of an isogeny φ:A→B. Then the image of the descent map B(K)/φA(K)→H¹(K,A[φ]) consists of unramified classes.

title: Rational 1−ζ torsion of the Jacobian of y^p=f(x)
description: For the Jacobian J of y^p=f(x) over a field k containing μ_p, with φ=1−ζ, if f has n distinct irreducible factors over k and at least one has degree prime to p, then dim_(𝔽_p) J(k)[φ]=n−2.

title: Local index of 1−ζ on the Jacobian of y^p=f(x)
description: For the Jacobian J of genus g of y^p=f(x) over a finite extension k_v of ℚ_ℓ containing μ_p, with φ=1−ζ, one has #J(k_v)/φJ(k_v)=|p|_v^(−g[k_v:ℚ_ℓ]/(p−1))·#J(k_v)[φ].

title: Mordell–Weil rank of a cyclic-cover Jacobian over a cyclotomic extension
description: Let k be a global field of characteristic not p, f∈k[x] p-th-power-free, J the Jacobian of y^p=f(x) and ζ a primitive p-th root of unity. Then rank J(k)=rank J(k(ζ))/[k(ζ):k].

title: Conductor of a Dirichlet character
description: The conductor f_χ of a Dirichlet character χ modulo n is the least positive divisor f of n such that χ is induced from a character modulo f, i.e. χ(a)=χ(b) whenever a≡b (mod f) and a,b are prime to n; the inducing character modulo f is primitive. With the usual convention, a product χψ of Dirichlet characters denotes the primitive character associated with a↦χ(a)ψ(a).

title: Analytic and meromorphic functions on a p-adic disc
description: Let K be a field complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value, such as ℂ_p. A function on a disc D={s∈K:|s−a|<R} is analytic if it is given by a power series ∑c_n(s−a)ⁿ with c_n∈K converging at every point of D. A function on D minus a point b is meromorphic with at most a simple pole at b if (s−b)f(s) extends to an analytic function on D; the pole is simple when that function is nonzero at b.

title: Identity principle for p-adic power series
description: Let K be a field complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value. If a power series with coefficients in K converges on a disc D and vanishes on a subset of D having an accumulation point in D, then it is identically zero on D. In particular two analytic functions on D that agree on such a set coincide.

title: Analyticity of p-adic binomial-coefficient series with geometric decay
description: Let p be prime and 0<r<p^(−1/(p−1)). If f(X)=∑_(n≥0)a_n·C(X,n) with a_n∈ℂ_p and |a_n|≤M·rⁿ for some M, then f is given by a power series ∑b_nXⁿ with |b_n|≤M·R^(−n), where R=(r·p^(1/(p−1)))^(−1)>1; thus f is analytic on the disc |X|<R, which contains ℤ_p.

title: Kummer’s Bernoulli criterion for the relative class number of ℚ(ζ_p)
description: For an odd prime p, p divides the relative class number h⁻(p) of ℚ(ζ_p) if and only if p divides the numerator of one of the Bernoulli numbers B₂,B₄,…,B_(p−3), written in lowest terms.

title: Kummer’s formula for the relative class number of ℚ(ζ_p)
description: Let p=2m+1 be an odd prime, g a primitive root modulo p, g_s the least positive residue of g^s modulo p, θ a primitive (p−1)th root of unity and F(X)=∑_(s=0)^(p−2)g_sXˢ. Then the relative class number of ℚ(ζ_p) is h⁻(p)=|F(θ)F(θ³)⋯F(θ^(p−2))|/(2p)^(m−1).

title: Wilson’s theorem
description: For every prime p, (p−1)!≡−1 (mod p).

title: Non-modularity modulo p of the p-depleted Eisenstein divisor series
description: Let p≥5 be prime and k a positive integer divisible by p−1. The reduction modulo p of ∑_(n≥1, p∤n)σ_(k−1)(n)qⁿ is not the reduction of any level-one modular form with p-integral rational coefficients and weight divisible by p−1.

title: Level-one modular forms modulo 2 and 3
description: For p=2 or 3, the algebra of reductions modulo p of level-one modular forms with p-integral rational q-expansion coefficients is the polynomial algebra 𝔽_p[Δ̃] generated by the reduction of the Ramanujan Δ-function, since E₄ and E₆ both reduce to 1.

title: Bernoulli’s formula for sums of powers
description: For integers m≥1 and n≥1, the power sum S_m(n)=0^m+1^m+⋯+(n−1)^m satisfies (m+1)S_m(n)=∑_(k=0)^m C(m+1,k)B_k n^(m+1−k), where B_k are the Bernoulli numbers (B₁=−1/2).

title: Transformation law of the weight-two Eisenstein series
description: For τ in the upper half-plane and (a b; c d)∈SL₂(ℤ), the normalized weight-two Eisenstein series E₂(τ)=1−24∑_(n≥1)σ₁(n)qⁿ satisfies E₂((aτ+b)/(cτ+d))=(cτ+d)²E₂(τ)+(12/(2πi))c(cτ+d). Thus E₂ is quasimodular but not modular.

title: Maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field
description: For n≥3 and a primitive nth root of unity ζ_n∈ℂ, the maximal real subfield of the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_n) is ℚ(ζ_n)⁺=ℚ(ζ_n)∩ℝ. It equals ℚ(ζ_n+ζ_n⁻¹) and is the fixed field of complex conjugation restricted to ℚ(ζ_n).

title: Divisor-sum identity for the Möbius function
description: For every positive integer n, ∑_(d|n)μ(d) equals 1 if n=1 and 0 if n>1; in Dirichlet-convolution notation μ*1=δ. Equivalently (Möbius inversion) g=f*1 holds if and only if f=g*μ.

title: Divisor-sum identity for the von Mangoldt function
description: For every positive integer n, ∑_(d|n)Λ(d)=log n, i.e. Λ*1=log as arithmetic functions; it follows from the prime factorisation of n. By Möbius inversion, Λ=μ*log.

title: Mean values of divisor-type multiplicative functions
description: Let k≥0 be an integer and f a multiplicative function with f(p)=k+O_k(1/p) for all primes p and f(p^j)=O_k(j^(O_k(1))) for j≥1, and let 𝔖=∏_p(1−1/p)^k(1+f(p)/p+f(p²)/p²+⋯). Then ∑_(n≤x)f(n)/n=𝔖(log x)^k/k!+O_k((log(2+x))^(k−1)) for x≥1, and for k≥1 also (1/x)∑_(n≤x)f(n)=𝔖(log x)^(k−1)/(k−1)!+O_k((log(2+x))^(k−2)) (Tao, 254A Notes 1, Theorem 36).

title: Analytic large sieve inequality
description: Let a_n be complex numbers for M<n≤M+N, S(α)=∑_n a_n e(nα) with e(t)=exp(2πit), and let α_1,…,α_R be points of ℝ/ℤ with ‖α_r−α_s‖≥δ for r≠s. Then ∑_r|S(α_r)|²≤(N−1+δ⁻¹)∑_n|a_n|² (Selberg; Montgomery–Vaughan proved N+δ⁻¹). Taking the Farey fractions a/q with q≤Q, (a,q)=1, which are Q⁻²-spaced, gives ∑_(q≤Q)∑_(a mod q)*|S(a/q)|²≤(N+Q²)∑|a_n|².

title: Gallagher’s comparison of primitive character sums with additive sums
description: For complex numbers a_n (finitely many nonzero) and an integer q≥1, (q/φ(q))∑*_(χ mod q)|∑_n a_nχ(n)|²≤∑_(1≤a≤q,(a,q)=1)|∑_n a_n e(an/q)|², where ∑* runs over primitive Dirichlet characters modulo q and e(t)=exp(2πit). It follows from writing χ̄(n)τ(χ)=∑_a χ(a)e(an/q) for primitive χ, with |τ(χ)|²=q (Gallagher).

title: Frobenius morphisms of a scheme in characteristic p
description: For a scheme X over a field k of characteristic p>0, the absolute Frobenius of X is the identity on the underlying space with f↦f^p on O_X, and the relative Frobenius F_(X/k):X→X^((p)) is the induced k-morphism to the base change of X along x↦x^p on k; in coordinates it raises them to the pth power. For k=𝔽_q, q=p^r, the q-power Frobenius F_X:X→X is the 𝔽_q-endomorphism obtained by iterating r times. It commutes with every 𝔽_q-morphism, and its fixed points in X(𝔽̄_q) are X(𝔽_q), those of F_Xⁿ being X(𝔽_(qⁿ)). For an abelian variety A over 𝔽_q, F_A fixes 0 and is an endomorphism of A.

title: Properness and smoothness of the Γ₁(N) moduli stack of generalized elliptic curves
description: For N≥1 the moduli stack M_Γ₁(N) of Γ₁(N)-structures on generalized elliptic curves (a point of exact order N in the smooth locus whose multiples form an ample divisor) is a proper flat algebraic stack over ℤ with geometrically connected fibres of pure dimension one, and it is smooth over ℤ[1/N]; over ℤ[1/N] it is the Deligne–Rapoport compactified moduli space of X₁(N), with generic fibre the modular curve X₁(N)/ℚ (Deligne–Rapoport; Conrad 2007, Theorems 3.2.7, 3.3.1 and 4.2.1(1)).

title: Fine moduli scheme for Γ₁(N)-structures when N≥5
description: For N≥5, Γ₁(N)-structures on generalized elliptic curves over algebraically closed fields of characteristic prime to N have no nontrivial automorphisms, and the restriction of the moduli stack M_Γ₁(N) to ℤ[1/N] is a scheme, a fine moduli scheme for these structures (Conrad 2007, Theorem 4.2.1(2) and Remark 4.2.2; Katz–Mazur).

title: Reduction of degree-zero divisor classes and morphisms of curves at a good prime
description: Let C be a smooth projective curve over ℚ with good reduction at p and C̃ its reduction over 𝔽̄_p, defined using a maximal ideal of ℤ̄ over p. Reducing points, ∑n_P(P)↦∑n_P(P̃), sends principal degree-zero divisors to principal divisors and induces a surjection Pic⁰(C)→Pic⁰(C̃). For a morphism h:C→C′ to another such curve of positive genus, the pushforwards h_* and h̃_* on Pic⁰ commute with reduction (Diamond–Shurman, Theorem 8.5.9).

title: Reduction of an isogeny of elliptic curves at a good prime
description: Let φ:E→E′ be an isogeny over ℚ̄ of elliptic curves over ℚ̄ with good reduction at a maximal ideal 𝔭 of ℤ̄ over p. Then φ reduces to an isogeny φ̃:Ẽ→Ẽ′ over 𝔽̄_p of the same degree, compatible with reduction of points and with composition of isogenies; in particular the reductions of φ and of its dual ψ satisfy ψ̃∘φ̃=[deg φ] (Diamond–Shurman, Theorem 8.5.10).

title: Reduction of torsion and of p-isogenous images at a good prime
description: Let E be an elliptic curve over ℚ̄ with good reduction at a maximal ideal 𝔭 of ℤ̄ over p. The reduction map E[N]→Ẽ[N] is surjective for every N≥1, and for every subgroup C⊂E of order p the quotient E/C again has good reduction at 𝔭, which is ordinary if that of E is ordinary and supersingular if that of E is supersingular (Diamond–Shurman, Proposition 8.4.4).

title: Ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves
description: An elliptic curve E over a field k of characteristic p>0 is ordinary if E[p](k̄)≅ℤ/pℤ and supersingular if E[p](k̄)=0; exactly one of these holds. An elliptic curve over a number field with good reduction at a prime above p has ordinary or supersingular reduction there according to the type of its reduction.

title: Moduli description of the Hecke operator T_p on X₁(N)
description: Let S₁(N) be the set of isomorphism classes [E,Q] of complex (or algebraic) elliptic curves E with a point Q of exact order N, mapped to X₁(N) by the moduli map. For a prime p, the operator [E,Q]↦∑_C[E/C,Q+C] on divisors of S₁(N), summed over subgroups C⊂E of order p with C∩⟨Q⟩=0, corresponds under the moduli map to the Hecke operator T_p on divisors and on Pic⁰ of X₁(N), whose action on S₂(Γ₁(N)) is the usual T_p (Diamond–Shurman, §§5.2, 6.3, 7.9, diagram (7.18)).

title: Cartier dual of a finite commutative group scheme
description: For a finite locally free commutative group scheme G over a scheme S, its Cartier dual is G^∨=Hom_(S-gr)(G,𝔾_m), the sheaf of group homomorphisms to the multiplicative group. It is again finite locally free commutative of the same order, the evaluation pairing G×G^∨→𝔾_m is perfect and G^∨∨≅G. Over a field k, for G étale of order prime to char k, G^∨ corresponds to the Galois module Hom(G(k^sep),μ(k^sep)).

title: Cartier duality of the kernels of an isogeny and its dual
description: If f:A→B is an isogeny of abelian varieties over a field with kernel N, then the dual homomorphism f^∨:B^∨→A^∨ is an isogeny whose kernel is canonically the Cartier dual N^∨ of N; equivalently the exact sequence 0→N→A→B→0 dualizes to 0→N^∨→B^∨→A^∨→0 (Mumford, Abelian Varieties §15; Milne 1986, Theorem 11.1).

title: Weil’s trace formula for an endomorphism of a curve
description: Let C be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field k, α:C→C a nonconstant morphism and α′ the endomorphism of the Jacobian J of C induced by α. Then the intersection number on C×C of the graph Γ_α with the diagonal Δ is (Γ_α·Δ)=1−Tr(α′)+deg α, where Tr(α′) is the trace of α′ on the Tate module T_ℓJ for any prime ℓ≠char k (Weil; Milne, Abelian Varieties 2008, III Proposition 11.2).

title: Characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of an abelian variety
description: For an endomorphism α of an abelian variety A of dimension g over a field k there is a unique monic polynomial P_α∈ℤ[X] of degree 2g with P_α(n)=deg(n−α) for all integers n, where deg is zero on non-isogenies. For every prime ℓ≠char k, P_α is the characteristic polynomial of α acting on V_ℓA=T_ℓA⊗ℚ_ℓ, so its roots are the eigenvalues of α on the Tate module and Tr(α) is minus its coefficient of X^(2g−1) (Milne, Abelian Varieties 1986, 12.9; 2008, I 10.20).

title: Pic⁰ of an abelian variety
description: For an abelian variety A over a field k, Pic⁰(A) is the subgroup of the Picard group Pic(A) consisting of the classes of invertible sheaves L that are translation-invariant over an algebraic closure: t_a*L≅L on A_(k^al) for every a∈A(k^al), where t_a is translation by a.

title: Classification of order-p group schemes over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring
description: Let R be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with fraction field of characteristic 0, residue characteristic p and absolute ramification index e=v(p). Every finite flat commutative R-group scheme of order p has equation X^p=δX for some δ∈R with 0≤v(δ)≤e, and isomorphism classes correspond bijectively to the integers v(δ) in [0,e] (Oort–Tate; Raynaud’s case F=𝔽_p).

title: Normal sheaf of a closed subscheme
description: For a closed subscheme Y of a scheme X with ideal sheaf I⊆O_X, the conormal sheaf I/I² is an O_Y-module, and the normal sheaf is its dual N_(Y/X)=Hom_(O_Y)(I/I²,O_Y). When I/I² is locally free, for instance for a local complete intersection in a smooth scheme, N_(Y/X) is the normal bundle.

title: Flatness criterion over a square-zero extension
description: Let A′→A be a surjection of Noetherian rings whose kernel J satisfies J²=0. An A′-module M′ is flat over A′ if and only if M=M′⊗_(A′)A is flat over A and the natural map M⊗_A J→M′ is injective. This is a special case of the local criterion of flatness.

title: Hilbert polynomial of a coherent sheaf on a proper scheme over a field
description: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k with an invertible sheaf L, and F a coherent O_X-module. The Hilbert polynomial of F with respect to L is the unique Φ_F∈ℚ[λ] with Φ_F(m)=χ(X,F⊗L^(⊗m)) for every integer m (Snapper's lemma gives polynomiality). The Hilbert polynomial of a closed subscheme Z⊆X is that of O_Z, computed with L|_Z.

title: Invertible sheaf of a divisor on a smooth projective curve
description: For a divisor D on a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over a field k, O_C(D) is the sheaf of rational functions with O_C(D)(U)={f∈k(C)×:(div f+D)|_U≥0}∪{0}. It is invertible, its global sections are L(D)={f:div f+D≥0}∪{0}, O_C(D)⊗O_C(D′)≅O_C(D+D′), and linearly equivalent divisors give isomorphic sheaves.

title: Cyclotomic units of a cyclotomic field
description: For n≢2 (mod 4) and a primitive nth root of unity ζ_n, let V_n be the multiplicative group generated by ±ζ_n and the numbers 1−ζ_n^a, 1≤a≤n−1. The cyclotomic units of ℚ(ζ_n) are C_n=V_n∩E_n, where E_n is the unit group of ℤ[ζ_n]; those of the maximal real subfield ℚ(ζ_n)⁺ are C_n⁺=C_n∩ℚ(ζ_n)⁺.

title: Hurwitz genus formula for separable morphisms of curves
description: Let φ:C₁→C₂ be a nonconstant separable morphism of smooth projective curves over an algebraically closed field, of genera g₁ and g₂. Then 2g₁−2≥(deg φ)(2g₂−2)+∑_(P∈C₁)(e_φ(P)−1), with equality exactly when the characteristic divides no ramification index e_φ(P); in particular equality holds when φ is unramified.

title: Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of a coherent sheaf on projective space
description: For an integer m, a coherent sheaf F on projective space Pⁿ over a field is m-regular if H^i(Pⁿ,F(m−i))=0 for every i≥1, where F(r)=F⊗O(r).

title: Castelnuovo's lemma on m-regular sheaves
description: If a coherent sheaf F on Pⁿ over a field is m-regular, then it is m′-regular for every m′≥m; for every r≥m the multiplication map H⁰(O(1))⊗H⁰(F(r))→H⁰(F(r+1)) is surjective, F(r) is generated by global sections and H^i(Pⁿ,F(r))=0 for i≥1.

title: Mumford's uniform regularity bound for subsheaves of a trivial bundle
description: For integers p,n≥0 there is a polynomial F_(p,n) with integer coefficients in n+1 variables such that, over every field k, every coherent subsheaf F of O_(Pⁿ_k)^(⊕p) whose Hilbert polynomial is χ(F(r))=∑_(i=0)^n a_i·binom(r,i) is m-regular for m=F_(p,n)(a₀,…,a_n).

title: Representability of the Grassmannian functor of locally free quotients
description: For a scheme S, a coherent O_S-module E and d≥0, the functor sending an S-scheme T to the set of locally free rank-d quotients of E_T (up to isomorphism of quotients) is represented by a proper S-scheme Grass(E,d) with a universal quotient; the determinant of the universal quotient gives a closed Plücker embedding into P(∧^dE) when E is locally free, so Grass(E,d) is projective over S.

title: Cohomology and base change for flat coherent sheaves
description: Let π:X→S be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes and F a coherent O_X-module flat over S. Then s↦dim H^i(X_s,F_s) is upper semicontinuous and s↦χ(X_s,F_s) is locally constant; if (R^iπ_*F)_s→H^i(X_s,F_s) is surjective it is an isomorphism near s and R^iπ_*F commutes with base change there, and it is locally free near s exactly when the map in degree i−1 is also surjective. In particular, if H^i(X_s,F_s)=0 for all s and i≥1, then π_*F is locally free and commutes with every base change.

title: Flattening stratification of a coherent sheaf on projective space
description: Let S be a Noetherian scheme and F a coherent sheaf on Pⁿ_S. Only finitely many Hilbert polynomials f occur for the restrictions of F to the fibres, and there are locally closed subschemes S_f⊆S whose underlying sets are the points with fibre polynomial f, such that a morphism T→S factors through S_f exactly when the pullback of F to Pⁿ_T is flat over T with every fibre Hilbert polynomial equal to f.

title: Closed vanishing locus of a homomorphism into a flat coherent sheaf
description: Let π:X→S be a projective morphism with S Noetherian, E and F coherent O_X-modules with F flat over S, and f:E→F a homomorphism. There is a closed subscheme S′⊆S such that a morphism T→S factors through S′ exactly when the pullback f_T:E_T→F_T on X_T is zero; it is the zero locus of the linear scheme Spec Sym Q representing T↦Hom(E_T,F_T) (EGA III 7.7.6).

title: Frobenius–Dedekind determinant formula for a finite abelian group
description: For a finite abelian group G and a complex function f on G, det[f(ab⁻¹)]_(a,b∈G)=∏_χ∑_(a∈G)χ(a)f(a), the product over all characters χ of G, and det[f(ab⁻¹)−f(a)]_(a,b≠1)=∏_(χ≠1)∑_(a∈G)χ(a)f(a).

title: Factorization of the Dedekind zeta function of an abelian number field
description: If K is an abelian number field and X is its group of primitive Dirichlet characters (those of Gal(K/ℚ) via a cyclotomic field containing K), then ζ_K(s)=∏_(χ∈X)L(s,χ).

title: Fricke operator on weight-k cusp forms with character
description: For f∈S_k(Γ₀(N),χ) put (f|W_N)(z)=N^(k/2)(Nz)^(−k)f(−1/(Nz)), the weight-k slash action of [[0,−1],[N,0]] normalized by its determinant. W_N maps S_k(Γ₀(N),χ) onto S_k(Γ₀(N),χ̄) and satisfies W_N²=(−1)^k.

title: Petersson adjoint of the Fricke operator
description: On weight-k cusp forms on Γ₀(N) with character, ⟨f|W_N,g⟩=(−1)^k⟨f,g|W_N⟩ for the Petersson inner product. Since W_N²=(−1)^k, the Fricke operator is a Petersson isometry: ⟨f|W_N,g|W_N⟩=⟨f,g⟩.

title: Fricke operator intertwines Hecke operators with their adjoints
description: On S_k(Γ₀(N),χ), conjugation by the Fricke operator W_N carries each Hecke operator T(n) (including U_p for p|N) to its Petersson adjoint T*(n): (f|W_N)|T(n)=(f|T*(n))|W_N. Hence if f is a common eigenform with T(n)-eigenvalues a_n, then f|W_N has T(n)-eigenvalues ā_n.

title: Rankin–Selberg residue formula for a cusp form
description: For a cusp form F=∑a(n)qⁿ of weight k on Γ₀(N), the Dirichlet series ∑_(n≥1)|a(n)|²n^(−(s+k−1)) converges for Re s>1 and extends meromorphically past s=1, where it has a simple pole whose residue is c(N,k)⟨F,F⟩ with ⟨,⟩ the Petersson inner product and c(N,k)≠0 depending only on N and k (Rankin 1939).

title: Rational basis of a space of cusp forms
description: For N,k≥1 the space S_k(Γ₁(N)) (and S_k(Γ₀(N))) of cusp forms has a ℂ-basis consisting of forms whose q-expansion coefficients are rational integers (Shimura, Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions, Theorem 3.52).

title: Interchange of double series over a complete nonarchimedean field
description: Let K be complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value. If a_mn→0 as max(m,n)→∞, then ∑_m∑_n a_mn and ∑_n∑_m a_mn converge and are equal. In particular, if ∑a_m and ∑b_n converge in K, their Cauchy product converges to (∑a_m)(∑b_n), with no absolute-convergence hypothesis.

title: Termwise differentiation of power series over a complete nonarchimedean field
description: Over a field K complete for a nonarchimedean absolute value, a power series f(x)=∑a_nxⁿ is differentiable on its disc of convergence with f′(x)=∑na_nx^(n−1); hence a_n=f^((n))(0)/n!, the coefficients are unique, and two power series (or analytic functions) on a common disc with equal derivatives differ by a constant there.

title: Iwasawa p-adic logarithm on ℚ_p×
description: Iwasawa’s p-adic logarithm Log_p:ℚ_p×→ℚ_p is the unique group homomorphism that agrees with the logarithm series log(1+x)=∑_(n≥1)(−1)^(n−1)xⁿ/n on the principal units 1+pℤ_p and satisfies Log_p(p)=0. It vanishes on the roots of unity of ℚ_p.

title: Components of the special fiber of a minimal regular elliptic model
description: Let 𝒞 be the minimal proper regular model over a discrete valuation ring of an elliptic curve, with special fiber ∑n_iF_i. Then the fiber is connected, some n_i=1, the arithmetic genus of the fiber is 1, and K·F_i=0 for the canonical divisor K. If there are at least two components, each F_i is a smooth rational curve with F_i²=−2, so ∑_(j≠i)n_jF_j·F_i=2n_i.

title: Néron identity component as the smooth locus of a minimal Weierstrass model
description: For an elliptic curve E over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring with minimal Weierstrass model W, the canonical map from the R-smooth locus W^sm to the Néron model is an isomorphism onto its identity component 𝒩⁰. Geometrically 𝒩⁰ of the special fiber is an elliptic curve, 𝔾_m or 𝔾_a according as the reduced cubic is smooth, nodal or cuspidal.

title: Raynaud’s component-group formula for Néron models of Jacobians
description: Let X be a regular proper flat curve over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with geometrically irreducible generic fiber, special-fiber components X_i of multiplicities δ_i, and residue field perfect or a section present. Then the component group of the Néron model of the Jacobian of X_K is ker β/im α, where α:ℤ^I→ℤ^I is given by the intersection matrix (X_i·X_j) (divided by geometric multiplicities) and β(a)=∑a_iδ_i.

title: O’Meara’s isometry criterion for lattices over a dyadic local field
description: Let L,K be lattices on the same regular quadratic space over a dyadic local field with the same fundamental invariants (number of Jordan components, their dimensions and scales, norm groups, weights and norm generators a_i), and Jordan chains L_(i),K_(i). Then L≅K iff for each i<t: dL_(i)/dK_(i)≅1 mod 𝔣_i; FL_(i)→FK_(i)⊥⟨a_(i+1)⟩ when 𝔣_i⊆4a_(i+1)𝔴_(i+1)⁻¹; and FL_(i)→FK_(i)⊥⟨a_i⟩ when 𝔣_i⊆4a_i𝔴_(i+1)⁻¹ (O’Meara 93:28).

title: Local square theorem
description: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with ring of integers 𝔬 and uniformizer π. For every α∈𝔬 there is β∈𝔬 with 1+4πα=(1+2πβ)²; thus every element of 1+4π𝔬 is a square (O’Meara 63:1). Over ℚ₂, units congruent to 1 modulo 8 are squares.

title: Witt’s cancellation theorem
description: Over a field of characteristic not two, if U⊥W≅U⊥W′ for nondegenerate quadratic spaces, then W≅W′. Equivalently (Witt’s extension theorem) every isometry between subspaces of a nondegenerate quadratic space extends to an isometry of the whole space.

title: Cancellation of hyperbolic lattice components over a dyadic local field
