description: Let L be a lattice on a regular quadratic space over a dyadic local field with splittings L=J⊥K=J′⊥K′, J≅J′. If J is the hyperbolic binary lattice A(0,0) (or an orthogonal sum of copies of it), then K≅K′ (O’Meara 93:14); Corollary 93:14a extends this to 𝔞-modular J whose norm group is contained in suitable norm groups of K and K′.

title: Classification of unimodular lattices on a dyadic quadratic space by norm groups
description: Two unimodular lattices on the same quadratic space over a dyadic local field are isometric if and only if they have the same norm group 𝔤L=Q(L)+2𝔰L (O’Meara 93:16).

title: Euler-system relations for Heegner points of ring class conductor
description: Let y_λ∈E(K_λ) be Heegner points of squarefree conductor λ built from inert primes p∤N. If λ=pλ′, then Tr_(K_λ/K_λ′)y_λ=a_p y_λ′; for each prime of K_λ above p, y_λ≡Frob_p(y_λ′) modulo that prime; and complex conjugation satisfies y_λ≡ε·σ(y_λ) modulo torsion for some σ∈Gal(K_λ/K), with ε=±1 the negative of the sign of the functional equation of E.

title: Bohr compactification of a topological abelian group
description: The Bohr compactification B(Z) of a topological abelian group Z is the Pontryagin dual of the group of continuous characters of Z taken with the discrete topology. It is a compact abelian group with a continuous homomorphism Z→B(Z) of dense image through which every continuous homomorphism of Z to a compact group factors.

title: Eigenvalue of a topological dynamical system
description: For a topological dynamical system (X,T), λ∈S¹ is an eigenvalue if f∘T=λf for some nonzero continuous f:X→ℂ (an eigenfunction). The eigenvalues form a subgroup of S¹; one also writes them as t∈ℝ/ℤ with λ=e^(2πit).

title: Compact connected abelian Lie groups are tori
description: Every compact connected abelian Lie group of dimension d is isomorphic, as a topological group, to the torus ℝ^d/ℤ^d.

title: Symplectic basis theorem for alternating forms
description: A nondegenerate alternating bilinear form on a finite-dimensional vector space over a field F has even dimension 2d and admits a symplectic basis, in which its Gram matrix is J=[[0,I_d],[−I_d,0]]; equivalently every invertible alternating matrix B over F can be written B=ΦᵀJΦ with Φ∈GL_(2d)(F).

title: Jacobi triple product identity
description: For complex q,z with |q|<1 and z≠0, ∑_(n∈ℤ)q^(n²)zⁿ=∏_(m≥1)(1−q^(2m))(1+zq^(2m−1))(1+z⁻¹q^(2m−1)); both sides converge absolutely and locally uniformly. Shifting the summation lattice gives the product formula for ∑_(m∈ℤ+r)q^(m²/2)z^m for every real r.

title: Theta functions with rational characteristic are Jacobi forms
description: For rational r the theta function ϑ_r(τ,σ)=∑_(m∈ℤ+r)q^(m²/2)e^(2πimσ), q=e^(2πiτ), satisfies the modular and elliptic transformation laws of a Jacobi form of weight 1/2 and index 1/2 (with a multiplier system) for a congruence subgroup of SL₂(ℤ) depending on r.

title: Taylor coefficients of a Jacobi form are quasimodular
description: If φ(τ,z) is a Jacobi form of weight k for a subgroup Γ of SL₂(ℤ) with Taylor expansion φ=∑_(m≥0)φ_m(τ)z^m in z, then each φ_m is a quasimodular form of weight k+m for Γ; equivalently (∂/∂z)^mφ(τ,0) is quasimodular of weight k+m (Eichler–Zagier, §3).

title: Right-continuous filtration
description: For a filtration (F_t)_(t≥0), the σ-algebras F_(t+)=⋂_(s>t)F_s form a filtration (F_(t+)), which is itself right-continuous. A filtration is right-continuous if F_t=F_(t+) for every t.

title: Left-continuous path
description: A path x:[0,∞)→E in a metric space is left-continuous if d(x(t−h),x(t))→0 as h↓0 for every t>0.

title: Locally square-integrable martingale
description: A right-continuous adapted real process M is a locally square-integrable martingale if there are stopping times τ_k↑∞ almost surely such that each stopped process M^(τ_k)=(M_(t∧τ_k))_(t≥0) is a martingale with E[M_(t∧τ_k)²]<∞ for every t.

title: Quadratic variation of a stopped locally square-integrable martingale
description: If M is a right-continuous square-integrable or locally square-integrable martingale and τ is a stopping time, then the quadratic variation of the stopped process M^τ=(M_(t∧τ)) is the stopped quadratic variation: [M^τ]=[M]^τ up to indistinguishability.

title: Bounded-energy limits in the domain of a closed form
description: Let E be a closed nonnegative symmetric form on a real Hilbert space H. If u_n lie in its domain, sup_n E(u_n,u_n)<∞ and u_n→u in H, then u lies in the domain, u_n→u weakly in the Hilbert space (D(E),E₁) with E₁=E+(·,·)_H, and E(u,u)≤liminf_n E(u_n,u_n).

title: Weak Harnack inequality for weak supersolutions of divergence-form elliptic equations
description: Let L u=D_i(a^(ij)D_ju+b^iu)+c^iD_iu+du be strictly elliptic on Ω⊆ℝⁿ with bounded measurable coefficients, and f^i∈L^q, g∈L^(q/2) with q>n. If u∈W^(1,2)(Ω) is a weak supersolution of Lu=g+D_if^i that is nonnegative on a ball B_(4R)(y)⊆Ω, then for 1≤p<n/(n−2) (any p≥1 if n≤2), R^(−n/p)‖u‖_(L^p(B_(2R)(y)))≤C(ess inf_(B_R(y))u+k(R)), with k(R)=λ^(−1)(R^(1−n/q)‖f‖_q+R^(2−2n/q)‖g‖_(q/2)) and C depending only on n, the ellipticity ratio, the scaled coefficient bound, q and p.

title: Global boundedness of weak subsolutions of divergence-form elliptic equations
description: Let L u=D_i(a^(ij)D_ju+b^iu)+c^iD_iu+du be strictly elliptic with bounded measurable coefficients on a bounded domain Ω⊆ℝⁿ, and f^i∈L^q, g∈L^(q/2) with q>n. If u∈W^(1,2)(Ω) is a weak subsolution of Lu=g+D_if^i with u≤0 on ∂Ω in the sense u⁺∈W₀^(1,2)(Ω), then ess sup_Ω u≤C(‖u⁺‖_(L²(Ω))+λ^(−1)(‖f‖_q+‖g‖_(q/2))), where C depends only on n, the coefficient bounds, q and |Ω|.

title: Global Hölder estimate for weak solutions under an exterior cone condition
description: Let L be a strictly elliptic divergence-form operator with bounded measurable coefficients on Ω⊆ℝⁿ, f^i∈L^q and g∈L^(q/2) with q>n, and suppose Ω satisfies a uniform exterior cone condition on a boundary portion T. If u∈W^(1,2)(Ω) solves Lu=g+D_if^i and osc_(∂Ω∩B_R(x₀))u≤KR^(α₀) for all x₀∈T and R>0, then u is Hölder continuous on Ω∪T, with ‖u‖_(C^α(Ω′))≤C(sup_Ω|u|+K+k) for Ω′⊆Ω at positive distance from ∂Ω∖T.

title: Local extremum of a real-valued function on a metric space
description: A function f:X→ℝ on a metric space has a local (relative) maximum at c∈X if for some δ>0, f(x)≤f(c) for every x∈X with d(x,c)<δ; a local minimum reverses the inequality, and a local extremum is either. Subsets of ℝ and ℝⁿ carry the Euclidean metric.

title: Limits of real sequences preserve non-strict inequalities
description: If convergent real sequences satisfy xₙ≤yₙ for every n, then lim xₙ≤lim yₙ; in particular a≤xₙ≤b for every n gives a≤lim xₙ≤b.

title: Sequential characterization of limits of real functions
description: Let c be a cluster point of S⊆ℝ and f:S→ℝ. Then f(x)→L as x→c exactly when f(xₙ)→L for every sequence xₙ in S∖{c} converging to c.

title: Taylor’s theorem with mean-value remainder on ℝⁿ
description: Let f be a real function on an open U⊆ℝⁿ containing the segment from x to x+p. If f is C¹, then f(x+p)=f(x)+∇f(x+tp)ᵀp for some t∈(0,1); if f is C², then f(x+p)=f(x)+∇f(x)ᵀp+½pᵀ∇²f(x+tp)p for some t∈(0,1).

title: Tangent line inequality for a convex function
description: If f is convex on an open interval I and differentiable at h∈I, then f(a)≥f(h)+f′(h)(a−h) for every a∈I.

title: Generalized Klein inequality for Hermitian matrices
description: Let fᵢ,gᵢ be finitely many real functions on an interval I with Σᵢfᵢ(a)gᵢ(h)≥0 for all a,h∈I. Then Σᵢtr[fᵢ(A)gᵢ(H)]≥0 for all Hermitian matrices A,H of the same size with eigenvalues in I, where fᵢ(A) and gᵢ(H) are standard matrix functions.

title: Operator convex function
description: A real function f on an interval I⊆ℝ is operator convex on I if f(τA+(1−τ)H)≼τf(A)+(1−τ)f(H) in the Löwner order for all τ∈[0,1] and all Hermitian matrices A,H of any common size with eigenvalues in I, where f(A) is the standard matrix function. f is operator concave when −f is operator convex.

title: Operator concavity of the positive definite matrix logarithm
description: For positive definite complex matrices A,H of the same size and τ∈[0,1], τ log A+(1−τ)log H≼log(τA+(1−τ)H) in the Löwner order; that is, the logarithm is operator concave on (0,∞).

title: Matrix perspective of an operator convex function
description: For an operator convex f:(0,∞)→ℝ and positive definite matrices A,H of the same size, Ψ_f(A;H)=A^{1/2}f(A^{−1/2}HA^{−1/2})A^{1/2}, with A^{1/2} the positive square root. When A and H commute, Ψ_f(A;H)=A f(HA⁻¹).

title: Joint operator convexity of the matrix perspective
description: If f:(0,∞)→ℝ is operator convex, its matrix perspective satisfies Ψ_f(τA₁+(1−τ)A₂;τH₁+(1−τ)H₂)≼τΨ_f(A₁;H₁)+(1−τ)Ψ_f(A₂;H₂) in the Löwner order for positive definite matrices Aᵢ,Hᵢ of the same size and τ∈[0,1].

title: Simultaneous unitary diagonalization of commuting Hermitian matrices
description: If Hermitian complex matrices A and H of the same size commute, there is one unitary U with A=U diag(λ₁,…,λₙ)U* and H=U diag(μ₁,…,μₙ)U*, all λⱼ,μⱼ real.

title: Divisible module over an integral domain
description: A module M over an integral domain R is divisible if for every nonzero r∈R the map M→M, x↦rx, is surjective. Over R=ℤ these are exactly the divisible abelian groups.

title: Compactly supported ℓ-adic Euler characteristic
description: For a separated scheme X of finite type over a separably closed field and a prime ℓ invertible there, χ_c(X,Q_ℓ)=Σ_i(−1)^i dim_(Q_ℓ)H^i_c(X,Q_ℓ). The sum is finite because these spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish for i>2·dim X.

title: Mayer–Vietoris spectral sequence for a finite open cover in étale cohomology
description: For a scheme X covered by open subschemes U_1,…,U_r and an étale abelian sheaf F there is a spectral sequence E_1^(p,q)=⊕_(i_0<⋯<i_p)H^q(U_(i_0)∩⋯∩U_(i_p),F)⇒H^(p+q)(X_et,F), the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence of the cover. For r=2 it is the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence.

title: Katz affine weak Lefschetz theorem for general hyperplane sections
description: Let V⊂Aᴺ be a smooth connected affine variety of dimension n≥2 over an algebraically closed field and ℓ invertible. For all affine hyperplanes H in a dense open set, V∩H is smooth and connected of dimension n−1 and restriction H^i(V,Q_ℓ)→H^i(V∩H,Q_ℓ) is bijective for i≤n−2 and injective for i=n−1 (Katz, Affine cohomological transforms, 3.4.1 and 3.4.3).

title: Étale cohomology of affine space
description: For a separably closed field k, m≥0 and n invertible in k, H^0(A^m_k,Z/nZ)=Z/nZ and H^i(A^m_k,Z/nZ)=0 for i>0; hence H^i(A^m_k,Q_ℓ) is Q_ℓ for i=0 and zero otherwise. With compact supports, H^i_c(A^m_k,Q_ℓ) is Q_ℓ(−m) for i=2m and zero otherwise.

title: Étale cohomology with supports in a closed subscheme
description: For a closed subscheme Z of a scheme X with open complement U and an étale abelian sheaf F, Γ_Z(X,F) is the group of global sections of F whose restriction to U vanishes. Its right derived functors are the cohomology groups with supports H^q_Z(X,F), and there is a long exact sequence ⋯→H^q_Z(X,F)→H^q(X,F)→H^q(U,F)→H^(q+1)_Z(X,F)→⋯.

title: Excision for étale cohomology with supports
description: Let f:X′→X be an étale morphism, Z⊆X a closed subscheme and Z′=X′×_X Z. If Z′→Z is an isomorphism, then H^q_Z(X,F)≅H^q_(Z′)(X′,f^*F) for every étale abelian sheaf F on X and all q. In particular H^q_Z(X,F) depends only on an open neighbourhood of Z.

title: Cohomological purity for smooth pairs in étale cohomology
description: Let X be a smooth separated scheme of finite type over a field k, Z⊂X a closed subscheme smooth over k of pure codimension c, n invertible in k and F a locally constant constructible sheaf of Z/n-modules on X. Then H^q_Z(X,F)≅H^(q−2c)(Z,F|_Z(−c)) for all q, where (−c) is the twist by μ_n^⊗(−c); in particular H^q_Z(X,F)=0 for q<2c. Passing to the limit gives H^q_Z(X,Q_ℓ)≅H^(q−2c)(Z,Q_ℓ(−c)).

title: Gysin map in ℓ-adic cohomology for a smooth closed subscheme
description: Let X be a scheme of finite type over a separably closed field, ℓ invertible, and Y⊂X a closed subscheme contained in an open X′⊆X such that X′ and Y are smooth and Y has pure codimension r in X′. The Gysin map ι_*:H^(i−2r)(Y,Q_ℓ(−r))→H^i(X,Q_ℓ) is the composite of the purity isomorphism with H^i_Y(X′,Q_ℓ), the excision isomorphism H^i_Y(X′,Q_ℓ)≅H^i_Y(X,Q_ℓ) and the forget-supports map to H^i(X,Q_ℓ). It is Galois-equivariant when everything is defined over a subfield.

title: Proper linear section of a projective scheme
description: For a closed subscheme X⊆Pᴺ over a field, a proper linear section of codimension r is the scheme-theoretic intersection X∩E with a linear subvariety E⊆Pᴺ of codimension r, the common zero scheme of r linearly independent linear forms, such that X and E intersect properly: every irreducible component of X∩E has dimension dim X−r. For r=1 it is a proper hyperplane section.

title: Poincaré–Verdier duality for smooth morphisms
description: Let f:X→Y be a smooth compactifiable morphism of pure relative dimension d between schemes of finite type over a Noetherian scheme, n invertible and A a Noetherian ring with nA=0. The trace morphism Tr_f:Rf_!f^*L(d)[2d]→L induces an isomorphism f^*L(d)[2d]≅Rf^!L for L∈D⁺(Y,A); equivalently Hom(K,f^*L(d)[2d])≅Hom(Rf_!K,L) for all K (SGA 4 XVIII 3.2.5; Fu, Thm. 8.5.2).

title: Local constancy of higher direct images under smooth proper morphisms
description: If f:X→S is a smooth proper morphism and n is invertible on S, then for every locally constant constructible sheaf F of Z/n-modules on X the sheaves R^qf_*F are locally constant constructible and their formation commutes with arbitrary base change (SGA 4 XVI 2.2). The same holds for ℓ-adic coefficients.

title: ℓ-adic first Chern class of an invertible sheaf
description: For a scheme X on which ℓ is invertible, the Kummer sequences 0→μ_(ℓⁿ)→G_m→G_m→0 give boundary maps Pic(X)=H^1(X_et,G_m)→H^2(X_et,μ_(ℓⁿ)), compatible in n; their limit is the first Chern class c_1:Pic(X)→H^2(X,Z_ℓ(1)) (SGA 4½ Cycle; SGA 5 VII).

title: Étale cohomology commutes with limits of schemes
description: Let X=lim X_i be the limit of a directed system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, (F_i) a compatible system of abelian sheaves and F=colim f_i^(−1)F_i on X. Then colim_i H^p(X_(i,et),F_i)=H^p(X_et,F) for all p (SGA 4 VII 5.7; Stacks 09YQ).

title: Vanishing of torsion étale cohomology of curves
description: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type and dimension at most 1 over an algebraically closed field and F a torsion étale abelian sheaf. Then H^q(X_et,F)=0 for q>2, and for q>1 if X is affine (Stacks 03SC).

title: Vanishing of higher direct images for proper morphisms of bounded fibre dimension
description: If f:X→Y is a proper morphism of schemes all of whose fibres have dimension at most n, then R^qf_*F=0 for q>2n and every torsion étale abelian sheaf F on X (SGA 4 XII 5.2; Stacks 095U).

title: Torsion étale sheaves as filtered colimits of constructible sheaves
description: On a Noetherian scheme X every torsion abelian étale sheaf is a filtered colimit of constructible abelian sheaves. If its support lies in a subset E closed under specialization, the constructible sheaves can be chosen supported on closed subsets contained in E (SGA 4 IX 2.7.2; Stacks 0F0N).

title: Cup product in ℓ-adic étale cohomology
description: For a scheme X of finite type over a separably closed field and n invertible, tensoring resolutions gives cup products H^i(X,F)⊗H^j(X,G)→H^(i+j)(X,F⊗G) for sheaves of Z/n-modules, and H^i_c(X,F)⊗H^j(X,G)→H^(i+j)_c(X,F⊗G) for X separated. For F=Z/ℓ^m(a), G=Z/ℓ^m(b) they are compatible in m and give cup products H^i_c(X,Q_ℓ(a))×H^j(X,Q_ℓ(b))→H^(i+j)_c(X,Q_ℓ(a+b)).

title: Trace map in ℓ-adic cohomology of a smooth variety
description: For a smooth separated scheme X of pure dimension d over a separably closed field and n invertible, the trace map Tr_X:H^(2d)_c(X,Z/n(d))→Z/n is glued from étale coordinates U→A^d, using adjunction for étale maps and the degree map on Picard groups of curves. It is compatible with étale maps and composition (SGA 4 XVIII 2.9; Fu §8.2). Its limit over n=ℓ^m is Tr_X:H^(2d)_c(X,Q_ℓ(d))→Q_ℓ.

title: Irreducible element of an integral domain
description: A nonzero nonunit p of an integral domain such that whenever p=ab, one of a and b is a unit.

title: Prime element of a commutative ring
description: A nonzero nonunit p of a commutative ring such that p|ab implies p|a or p|b; equivalently, the principal ideal pR is a prime ideal.

title: Maximal ideals are prime
description: Every maximal ideal of a commutative ring is a prime ideal; equivalently, the quotient by a maximal ideal is a field and hence an integral domain.

title: Factorization into irreducibles under the ascending chain condition on principal ideals
description: In an integral domain in which every ascending chain of principal ideals becomes constant, for example a Noetherian domain, every nonzero nonunit is a finite product of irreducible elements.

title: Polynomial ring over an integral domain is an integral domain
description: If R is an integral domain, then R[X] is an integral domain: for nonzero f,g the leading coefficient of fg is the product of their leading coefficients, so deg(fg)=deg f+deg g.

title: Monomorphisms are kernels of their cokernels in an abelian category
description: In an abelian category every monomorphism is a kernel of its cokernel and every epimorphism is a cokernel of its kernel. Hence taking cokernels and kernels gives mutually inverse bijections between the subobjects and quotient objects of each object.

title: Gallery distance in a chamber complex
description: The gallery distance d(C,D) between chambers C and D of a chamber complex is the least length n of a gallery C=C₀,C₁,…,C_n=D; a gallery of that length is minimal. For a simplex A, d(A,D) is the least distance from a chamber having A as a face to D.

title: Convexity of apartments in a building
description: If an apartment A of a building contains chambers C and D, then every minimal gallery in the building from C to D lies in A.

title: Apartments of a building are Coxeter complexes
description: For an apartment system of a thick building there is a Coxeter system (W,S) such that every apartment is isomorphic as a chamber complex to the Coxeter complex Σ(W,S). This follows from Tits’ characterization of Coxeter complexes by foldings.

title: Projections and the gate property in a Coxeter complex
description: In a Coxeter complex, for a simplex A and a chamber C there is a unique chamber proj_A C having A as a face at least gallery distance from C; every minimal gallery from A to C starts with it, and d(C,D)=d(C,proj_A C)+d(proj_A C,D) for every chamber D having A as a face.

title: Sequential characterization of closed sets in a metric space
description: A subset F of a metric space is closed if and only if the limit of every convergent sequence of points of F lies in F; equivalently the closure of F is the set of limits of sequences in F.

title: Summatory bound for the r-fold divisor function
description: For an integer r≥1 let d_r(n) be the number of ordered r-tuples of positive integers with product n. Then ∑_(n≤x)d_r(n)=O(x(log x)^(r−1)) for x≥2; in fact the sum is asymptotic to x(log x)^(r−1)/(r−1)!.

title: Fourier inversion theorem for locally compact abelian groups
description: For a locally compact abelian group G with Haar measure there is a Haar measure on the dual group Ĝ, the dual measure, such that whenever f∈L¹(G) and f̂∈L¹(Ĝ), f(x)=∫_Ĝ f̂(ξ)ξ(x)dξ for almost every x, and for every x if f is continuous.

title: Dual Haar measure of a compact abelian group is counting measure
description: If G is a compact abelian group with Haar measure normalized by |G|=1, the Haar measure on its discrete dual group dual to it for Fourier inversion is counting measure; dually, counting measure on a discrete group has the normalized Haar probability on the compact dual as dual measure.

title: Axiom schema of replacement
description: The Zermelo–Fraenkel axiom schema stating that if a formula defines a rule assigning to every set A a unique set f(A), then for every set X the images {f(A): A∈X} form a set.

title: Every well-ordered set is isomorphic to a unique ordinal
description: Every well-ordered set is order-isomorphic to exactly one ordinal, by a unique order isomorphism; the ordinal is its order type. The construction uses the axiom of replacement.

title: The union of a set of ordinals is an ordinal
description: For every set S of ordinals, its union ⋃S is an ordinal, the least ordinal containing every member of S as a subset; in particular the class of all ordinals is not a set.

title: Successor of an ordinal
description: For an ordinal α, its successor α+1=α∪{α} is again an ordinal and is the least ordinal strictly greater than α. An ordinal of this form is a successor ordinal.

title: Uniform Cauchy criterion for series of functions
description: A series ∑u_n of real or complex functions on a set S converges uniformly on S exactly when for every ε>0 there is N, independent of z∈S, with |u_(n+1)(z)+⋯+u_(n+p)(z)|<ε for all n≥N, p≥1 and z∈S.

title: Bounded-below operators are injective with closed range
description: If T is a bounded linear operator from a Banach space X to a normed space Y with ∥Tx∥≥C∥x∥ for some C>0 and all x∈X, then T is injective and its range is closed in Y.

title: Kernel–range orthogonal decompositions for a bounded Hilbert-space operator
description: For a bounded operator T:H→K between Hilbert spaces, H=N(T)⊕closure(R(T*)) and K=N(T*)⊕closure(R(T)) orthogonally. In particular T has dense range exactly when its adjoint T* is injective, and T is injective exactly when T* has dense range.

title: Approximate eigenvalue of a bounded operator
description: A scalar λ is an approximate eigenvalue of a bounded operator T on a Banach space if there are unit vectors x_n with ∥Tx_n−λx_n∥→0. Every eigenvalue is one, every approximate eigenvalue lies in the spectrum σ(T), and they form the approximate point spectrum.

title: Compactness of the spectrum of a bounded operator
description: For a bounded operator T on a complex Banach space, the resolvent set is open and contains every λ with |λ|>∥T∥, so the spectrum σ(T) is a compact subset of the closed disc {|λ|≤∥T∥}.

title: Pointwise limits of measurable functions are measurable
description: On a measurable space, the pointwise limit of a sequence of measurable real- or complex-valued functions is measurable.

title: Monotonicity of ℓ^q quasi-norms in the exponent
description: For 0<q≤r≤∞ and every scalar sequence a, ∥a∥_(ℓ^r)≤∥a∥_(ℓ^q); hence ℓ^q⊆ℓ^r with inclusion of quasi-norm at most one.

title: Codimension-one normal subgroups containing a proper subgroup of a nilpotent Lie group
description: In a connected simply connected nilpotent Lie group G, every proper closed connected subgroup H lies in a closed connected normal subgroup of codimension one; on Lie algebras, every proper subalgebra of a nilpotent Lie algebra lies in an ideal of codimension one.

title: Derivative of a function from a real interval into a normed space
description: For f from a real interval I into a normed space X, the derivative at t∈I is the norm limit f′(t)=lim (f(t+h)−f(t))/h as h→0 with t+h∈I (one-sided at an endpoint), when it exists. f is continuously differentiable (C¹) on I if f′(t) exists for every t∈I and t↦f′(t) is continuous.

title: Linearity of the Banach-valued Riemann integral
description: If f,g:[a,b]→X are Riemann integrable into a Banach space X and α is a scalar, then αf and f+g are Riemann integrable with ∫αf=α∫f and ∫(f+g)=∫f+∫g; in particular the integral of a constant u is (b−a)u.

title: Interval additivity of the Banach-valued Riemann integral
description: If f:[a,b]→X is Riemann integrable into a Banach space X and a≤c≤b, then f is integrable on [a,c] and [c,b] and ∫_a^b f=∫_a^c f+∫_c^b f.

title: Muckenhoupt Aₚ weight
description: For 1<p<∞, a weight w on ℝⁿ (a locally integrable function with w>0 almost everywhere) belongs to A_p if [w]_{A_p}=sup_Q(|Q|⁻¹∫_Q w)(|Q|⁻¹∫_Q w^{−1/(p−1)})^{p−1}<∞, the supremum over all cubes Q; [w]_{A_p} is its A_p constant. Taking balls instead of cubes gives the same class with comparable constants.

title: Boundedness of the centered maximal operator with respect to a weight
description: For a weight w on ℝⁿ let M_c^w f(x)=sup_{δ>0}w(Q(x,δ))⁻¹∫_{Q(x,δ)}|f|w dy, the supremum over open cubes Q(x,δ) centred at x. Then M_c^w maps L¹(w) to weak L¹(w) with norm at most 24ⁿ and is bounded on Lᵠ(w) for 1<q≤∞, with constants depending only on n and q and not on w.

title: Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorem for Aₚ weights
description: Let 1<p₀<∞ and let F be a family of pairs (f,g) of nonnegative measurable functions on ℝⁿ with ∫f^{p₀}w≤C∫g^{p₀}w for every w∈A_{p₀}, C depending only on [w]_{A_{p₀}}. Then for every 1<p<∞ and w∈A_p, ∫f^pw≤C∫g^pw with C depending on [w]_{A_p}, and for 1<q<∞ also ∥(∑_jf_j^q)^{1/q}∥_{L^p(w)}≤C∥(∑_jg_j^q)^{1/q}∥_{L^p(w)} for sequences in F; the inequalities are asserted when the left side is finite.

title: Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem on Lᵖ
description: For 1<p≤∞ the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator is bounded on Lᵖ(ℝⁿ): ∥Mf∥_p≤C_{n,p}∥f∥_p with a constant depending only on n and p.

title: Dimension of the space of homogeneous harmonic polynomials
description: For n≥2 the space H_m(ℝⁿ) of homogeneous harmonic polynomials of degree m on ℝⁿ has dimension 1 for m=0, n for m=1, and C(n+m−1,n−1)−C(n+m−3,n−1) for m≥2. For fixed n this is asymptotic to 2m^{n−2}/(n−2)! as m→∞, so dim H_m(ℝⁿ)≤C_n m^{n−2} for m≥1.

title: Poisson integral of polynomial boundary data on the ball
description: If p is a polynomial on ℝⁿ of degree m, the Poisson integral over the unit ball of its restriction to the unit sphere is P[p|_S]=(1−|x|²)q+p for some polynomial q of degree at most m−2; in particular P[p|_S] is a polynomial of degree at most m.

title: Double complex in an abelian category
description: A double complex L^{•,•} in an abelian category consists of objects L^{p,q} (p,q∈ℤ) and morphisms d₁^{p,q}:L^{p,q}→L^{p+1,q} and d₂^{p,q}:L^{p,q}→L^{p,q+1} with d₁∘d₁=0, d₂∘d₂=0 and d₁∘d₂=d₂∘d₁; thus every column L^{p,•} and row L^{•,q} is a cochain complex. Some authors require anticommuting squares instead; the two conventions differ by signs.

title: Total complex of a double complex
description: For a double complex L^{•,•} with only finitely many nonzero L^{p,q} on each antidiagonal p+q=n (for instance a first-quadrant one), the total complex has Totⁿ(L)=⊕_{p+q=n}L^{p,q} and differential dⁿ=∑_{p+q=n}(d₁^{p,q}+(−1)^p d₂^{p,q}), which squares to zero.

title: Cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category
description: A cohomological spectral sequence starting at r₀ consists of objects E_r^{p,q} (p,q∈ℤ, r≥r₀) of an abelian category, differentials d_r:E_r^{p,q}→E_r^{p+r,q−r+1} with d_r∘d_r=0, and isomorphisms from E_{r+1}^{p,q} to the cohomology of d_r at (p,q). It is bounded if each total degree p+q has only finitely many nonzero E_{r₀}^{p,q}; then each E_r^{p,q} is constant for large r, with value E_∞^{p,q}. A bounded one converges to objects Hⁿ if each Hⁿ has a finite decreasing filtration F^pHⁿ with E_∞^{p,n−p}≅F^pHⁿ/F^{p+1}Hⁿ.

title: Spectral sequence of a filtered cochain complex
description: Let K• be a cochain complex in an abelian category with a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes F^pK•. There is a cohomological spectral sequence with E₀^{p,q}=F^pK^{p+q}/F^{p+1}K^{p+q}, d₀ induced by the differential, and E₁^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(F^pK•/F^{p+1}K•). If in each degree n the filtration is finite (F^pKⁿ=Kⁿ for p≪0 and F^pKⁿ=0 for p≫0), the spectral sequence is bounded and converges to H(K•) with the filtration F^pHⁿ=im(Hⁿ(F^pK•)→Hⁿ(K•)).

title: Quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes
description: A cochain map f:K•→L• between complexes in an abelian category is a quasi-isomorphism if every induced morphism Hⁿ(f):Hⁿ(K•)→Hⁿ(L•) on cohomology objects is an isomorphism.

title: Injective resolution of a bounded below complex
description: An injective resolution of a cochain complex K• in an abelian category is a quasi-isomorphism K•→I• into a bounded below complex (Iⁿ=0 for n≪0) of injective objects.

title: Homotopy lifting into bounded below complexes of injectives
description: In an abelian category let I• be a bounded below complex of injective objects and α:K•→L• a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes. Every cochain map γ:K•→I• is homotopic to β∘α for some cochain map β:L•→I•, and any two such β are homotopic. In particular two injective resolutions of a complex are homotopy equivalent by maps compatible with the augmentations up to homotopy.

title: Existence of Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions
description: In an abelian category with enough injectives, every bounded below cochain complex K• has a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution, which may be chosen with I^{p,•}=0 whenever Kᵖ=0 for all smaller degrees.

title: Subsets of a separable metric space are separable
description: Every subset of a separable metric space is separable in the restricted metric: it has a countable subset dense in it.

title: Conic intrinsic volumes of a closed convex cone
description: For a polyhedral cone C⊆ℝ^d and k=0,…,d, v_k(C) is the probability that the Euclidean projection of a standard Gaussian vector onto C lies in the relative interior of a k-dimensional face of C. For a general closed convex cone v_k(C) is the limit of v_k(C_i) for polyhedral cones C_i converging to C in the conic Hausdorff metric. The v_k(C) form a probability distribution on {0,…,d}.

title: Conic kinematic formula
description: Let C,K⊆ℝ^d be closed convex cones, not both linear subspaces, and Q a Haar-random orthogonal matrix. Then P(C∩QK≠{0})=∑_{i=0}^{d}(1+(−1)^{i+1})∑_{j=i}^{d}v_i(C)v_{d+i−j}(K), equivalently twice the sum of the conic intrinsic volumes v_k(C×K) over k≥d+1 with k−d−1 even. For K a (d−m)-dimensional subspace this is the Crofton formula 2∑_{j≥0}v_{m+1+2j}(C).

title: Concentration of conic intrinsic volumes
description: Let C be a closed convex cone with polar C°, ω(C)²=min(δ(C),δ(C°)) and p_C(λ)=4exp(−(λ²/8)/(ω(C)²+λ)). For the tail sums t_k(C)=∑_{j≥k}v_j(C) of the conic intrinsic volumes: if k≤δ(C)−λ+1 then t_k(C)≥1−p_C(λ), and if k≥δ(C)+λ then t_k(C)≤p_C(λ) (Amelunxen–Lotz–McCoy–Tropp).

title: Unique extension of an absolute value from a complete field
description: If K is complete for an absolute value |·|, archimedean or not, and L/K is a finite extension of degree n, then |·| has exactly one extension to an absolute value on L, namely |β|=|N_{L/K}(β)|^{1/n}, and L is complete for it.

title: First isomorphism theorem for rings
description: For a homomorphism φ:R→S of rings, its kernel is an ideal of R and φ induces an injective ring homomorphism R/ker φ→S with image φ(R); in particular a surjective φ gives R/ker φ≅S.

title: Multiplicative system of representatives for a perfect residue ring
description: Let A be Hausdorff and complete for a decreasing filtration by ideals 𝔞₁⊇𝔞₂⊇⋯ with 𝔞_n𝔞_m⊆𝔞_(n+m), and suppose k=A/𝔞₁ is a perfect ring of characteristic p. There is exactly one system of representatives f:k→A commuting with p-th powers; its image consists of the elements of A that are p^n-th powers for every n, and f is multiplicative. If A has characteristic p, f is also additive (Teichmüller representatives).

title: Uniformizer expansions in a complete discrete valuation ring
description: Let A be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k, S⊆A a system of representatives of k containing 0, and π a uniformizer. Every a∈A is uniquely a convergent series ∑_{n≥0}s_nπⁿ with s_n∈S, every such series converges, and every x∈K is uniquely ∑_{n≥n₀}s_nπⁿ with n₀∈ℤ.

title: Degree of a simple algebraic extension
description: If α is algebraic over a field F with minimal polynomial f of degree n, then F(α)=F[α]≅F[X]/(f), the elements 1,α,…,α^(n−1) form an F-basis, and [F(α):F]=n.

title: Existence of the Hilbert–Samuel polynomial
description: Let R be a Noetherian ring, q an ideal generated by r elements and M a finitely generated R-module with M/qM of finite length. Then every M/qⁿM has finite length, and n↦length(M/qⁿM) agrees for all large n with a polynomial p_q(M,n) with rational coefficients and degree at most r, the Hilbert–Samuel polynomial. Its degree does not change when q is replaced by its radical.

title: Induced module from a subgroup of finite index
description: For a subgroup H of finite index in a group G and an H-module W, Ind_H^G W is the group of functions f:G→W with f(hg)=h·f(g) for h∈H, with pointwise addition and G-action (g₀f)(g)=f(gg₀). Choosing representatives of H∖G identifies it with a direct sum of [G:H] copies of W.

title: Semisimple linear representation of a group
description: A linear representation of a group G on a vector space V is semisimple, or completely reducible, if V is a direct sum of irreducible subrepresentations; equivalently, every G-invariant subspace of V has a G-invariant complement.

title: Degree of Hilbert–Samuel polynomials in a short exact sequence
description: Let R be Noetherian, q an ideal and 0→M′→M→M″→0 an exact sequence of finitely generated modules. M/qM has finite length if and only if M′/qM′ and M″/qM″ do; then p_q(M′,n)−p_q(M,n)+p_q(M″,n) has degree less than deg p_q(M′,n) and positive leading coefficient, and deg p_q(M,n)=max(deg p_q(M′,n),deg p_q(M″,n)). The proof uses the Artin–Rees lemma.

title: Finite-length criterion for modules over a Noetherian ring
description: For a finitely generated module M over a Noetherian ring, the following are equivalent: M has finite length; every prime in the support of M is maximal; every associated prime of M is maximal. Then the associated primes and the support coincide and form a finite set.

title: Prime avoidance lemma
description: Let R be a commutative ring, a⊆R a subset closed under addition and multiplication (for example an ideal), and p₁,…,p_n ideals of which all but at most two are prime. If a⊆p₁∪⋯∪p_n, then a⊆p_i for some i.

title: Krull dimension of a module
description: For a nonzero module M over a commutative ring R, dim M is the supremum of the lengths r of chains p₀⊊⋯⊊p_r of prime ideals in the support of M. For M=R it is the Krull dimension of R.

title: Hilbert–Serre theorem on Hilbert series of graded modules
description: Let R=⊕_{n≥0}R_n be a graded ring with R₀ Artinian, generated over R₀ by finitely many homogeneous elements of positive degrees k₁,…,k_r, and M a finitely generated graded R-module. Then its Hilbert series ∑length(M_n)tⁿ is a rational function e(t)/(t^l(1−t^{k₁})⋯(1−t^{k_r})) with e∈ℤ[t]. If all k_i=1, length(M_n) agrees for large n with a polynomial of degree at most r−1.

title: Associated graded ring and module of an ideal filtration
description: For an ideal q of a commutative ring R, the associated graded ring is G(R)=⊕_{n≥0}qⁿ/qⁿ⁺¹ with multiplication induced from R. For a module M with a q-filtration M=F⁰M⊇F¹M⊇⋯ (qFⁿM⊆Fⁿ⁺¹M), G(M)=⊕_nFⁿM/Fⁿ⁺¹M is a graded G(R)-module; the q-adic filtration Fⁿ=qⁿM is the basic example.

title: Akizuki–Hopkins theorem
description: A commutative ring is Artinian if and only if it is Noetherian of Krull dimension zero; such a ring has only finitely many prime ideals.

title: Additivity of length
description: For a module M over a commutative ring and a submodule M′, length(M)=length(M′)+length(M/M′), with both sides infinite together; equivalently length is additive on short exact sequences.

title: Finitely generated modules over an Artinian ring have finite length
description: Every finitely generated module over an Artinian commutative ring has finite length, and its associated primes and support coincide and are finite.

title: Jacobson density theorem
description: Let E be a semisimple module over a ring R, R′=End_R(E) and f∈End_{R′}(E). For all x₁,…,x_n∈E there is α∈R with αx_i=f(x_i) for every i. If E is finitely generated over R′, the natural map R→End_{R′}(E) is surjective.

title: Induced and coinduced modules agree for finite index
description: For a subgroup H of a group G and an H-module M there is a natural G-map ℤ[G]⊗_{ℤ[H]}M→Hom_{ℤ[H]}(ℤ[G],M), identified after a choice of coset representatives with the inclusion of a direct sum into a direct product of copies of M; it is an isomorphism when [G:H] is finite. The coinduced module is the function model {f:G→M: f(hg)=hf(g)}.

title: Criterion for a module to be induced by transitively permuted summands
description: Let a G-module N be a direct sum ⊕_{i∈I}M_i of subgroups with gM_i=M_{gi} for an action of G on I. If the action is transitive and H is the stabiliser of i, then M_i is an H-module and N≅Ind_H^G M_i; in general N≅⊕Ind_{G_i}^G M_i over representatives i of the orbits, G_i the stabilisers.

title: Valence formula for level-one modular functions
description: Let f≢0 be meromorphic on the upper half-plane with f((aτ+b)/(cτ+d))=(cτ+d)^k f(τ) for all of SL₂(ℤ) and meromorphic at ∞ in q=e^(2πiτ). Then v_∞(f)+½v_i(f)+⅓v_ρ(f)+∑_p v_p(f)=k/12, where ρ=e^(2πi/3), v_p is the order of f at p (negative at poles), v_∞ is the order in q at q=0, and the sum runs over the SL₂(ℤ)-orbits in the upper half-plane other than those of i and ρ.

title: Siegel’s fundamental domain for Sp₂g(ℤ)
description: Let F_g be the set of Z=X+iY in the Siegel upper half-space ℍ_g with |det(CZ+D)|≥1 for every [[A,B],[C,D]]∈Sp₂g(ℤ), with Y reduced in Minkowski’s sense, and with every entry of X of absolute value at most 1/2. Every point of ℍ_g is Sp₂g(ℤ)-equivalent to a point of F_g (Siegel 1939).

title: Completion of a primitive integer vector to a unimodular matrix
description: For n≥2, every vector in ℤⁿ whose entries have greatest common divisor 1 is the first column of a matrix in SL_n(ℤ).

title: Siegel Φ-operator
description: For a Siegel modular form f of weight k and degree g≥1 for Sp₂g(ℤ), (Φf)(Z′)=lim_(t→+∞) f([[Z′,0],[0,it]]) for Z′∈ℍ_(g−1). Computed termwise on the Fourier expansion, it keeps the coefficients a([[T′,0],[0,0]]); it is a linear map from weight-k forms of degree g to those of degree g−1 (constants for g=1), whose kernel is the space of cusp forms.

title: Divisibility by χ₁₀ of genus-two forms vanishing on the diagonal
description: If F is a Siegel modular form of even weight k for Sp₄(ℤ) whose restriction F([[τ₁,0],[0,τ₂]]) to the diagonal vanishes identically, then F=χ₁₀G for a Siegel modular form G of weight k−10, where χ₁₀ is Igusa’s weight-10 cusp form (Igusa 1962; Freitag 1965).

title: Maass’s formula for Fourier coefficients of genus-two Siegel Eisenstein series
description: For even k≥4 and positive definite half-integral T=[[n,r/2],[r/2,m]], the Fourier coefficient of the normalized genus-two Siegel Eisenstein series E_k^(2) is (2/(ζ(1−k)ζ(3−2k)))∑_(d|gcd(n,r,m)) d^(k−1)H(k−1,(4nm−r²)/d²), where H is Cohen’s generalized class-number function; a nonzero singular T equivalent to diag(t,0) has the t-th coefficient of the elliptic E_k. In particular all coefficients are rational.

title: Transformation formula for Siegel theta constants
description: For M=[[A,B],[C,D]]∈Sp₂g(ℤ) and each half-integral characteristic m, θ[M·m](M⟨Z⟩)=c(M,m)det(CZ+D)^(1/2)θ[m](Z), where M·m is Igusa’s affine action of Sp₂g(ℤ) on characteristics modulo 2, which preserves parity, and c(M,m) is an eighth root of unity for a fixed branch of the square root. Thus Sp₂g(ℤ) permutes the even theta constants up to these factors.

title: Theta-constant expressions for E₄ and Δ
description: For the three even genus-one theta constants θ₀₀,θ₀₁,θ₁₀ on the upper half-plane, Jacobi’s identity θ₀₀⁴=θ₀₁⁴+θ₁₀⁴ holds, the normalized Eisenstein series is E₄=½(θ₀₀⁸+θ₀₁⁸+θ₁₀⁸), and (θ₀₀θ₀₁θ₁₀)⁸=2⁸Δ for the Ramanujan cusp form Δ.

title: Integral ring of level-one modular forms
description: The graded ring of modular forms for SL₂(ℤ) with integral Fourier coefficients is ℤ[E₄,E₆,Δ], where 1728Δ=E₄³−E₆². Its weight-4e part is free over ℤ with basis E₄^(e−3i)Δ^i for 0≤i≤e/3, its weight-(4e+6) part is E₆ times the weight-4e part, and all other weights are zero.

title: Formal power series over an integral domain form an integral domain
description: If R is an integral domain, the formal power series ring R[[X₁,…,X_n]] is an integral domain: the product of the lowest-degree nonzero homogeneous parts of two nonzero series is nonzero.

title: Invariant subring of a group action on a commutative ring
description: For a group G acting on a commutative ring R by ring automorphisms, the invariant subring R^G={r∈R: g·r=r for every g∈G} is the set of elements fixed by every group element. It is a subring of R containing 0 and 1.

title: Incomparability of primes in an integral ring extension
description: Let A⊆B be commutative rings with B integral over A. If 𝔮⊆𝔮′ are prime ideals of B with 𝔮∩A=𝔮′∩A, then 𝔮=𝔮′. Thus there are no strict inclusions among the primes of B lying over a given prime of A.

title: Local Kronecker–Weber theorem for ℚ_p
description: Every finite abelian extension of the p-adic field ℚ_p is contained in a cyclotomic extension ℚ_p(ζ_n) for some n≥1. More generally, for a nonarchimedean local field K with Lubin–Tate extension K_π of a uniformizer π, the maximal abelian extension is K_π·K^un.

title: Rational CM points of X₀(N) for the class-number-one primes
description: For N∈{11,19,43,67,163}, the modular curve X₀(N) has a ℚ-rational noncuspidal point fixed by the Atkin–Lehner involution w_N; it is the elliptic curve with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of ℚ(√−N), of class number one, with the cyclic N-isogeny given by √−N. For N=19,43,67,163 it is the only noncuspidal ℚ-rational point of X₀(N).

title: Rational points of the genus-one modular curves X₀(N)
description: For N∈{11,14,15,17,19,20,21,24,27,32,36,49}, the modular curve X₀(N) has genus one and its finitely many ℚ-rational points are explicitly known (Ligozat). Consequently no elliptic curve over ℚ has a ℚ-rational point of order N for these N, and none has a ℚ-rational cyclic subgroup of order 20, 24, 32, 36 or 49.

title: Nonexistence of rational points of order 13 on elliptic curves over ℚ
description: No elliptic curve over ℚ has a ℚ-rational point of order 13; equivalently, X₁(13)(ℚ) consists of cusps (Mazur–Tate 1973, independently Blass).

title: Nonexistence of rational points of order 16 on elliptic curves over ℚ
description: No elliptic curve over ℚ has a ℚ-rational point of order 16 (Lind 1940).

title: Nonexistence of rational cyclic subgroups of order 35 on elliptic curves over ℚ
description: No elliptic curve over ℚ has a Galois-stable cyclic subgroup of order 35: every ℚ-rational point of X₀(35) is a cusp. In particular no elliptic curve over ℚ has a ℚ-rational point of order 35.

title: Nonexistence of rational points of order 18 or 25 on elliptic curves over ℚ
description: No elliptic curve over ℚ has a ℚ-rational point of order 18 or of order 25: the ℚ-rational points of X₁(18) and X₁(25) are cusps (Kubert, via descent on their Jacobians).

title: Quotient of a variety by a finite group
description: Let a finite group G act on an algebraic variety V over an algebraically closed field such that every orbit lies in an affine open set, for example V quasi-projective. Then V/G exists: the projection V→V/G is finite, surjective and constant on orbits, its fibres are exactly the G-orbits, V/G is affine with coordinate ring A^G when V=Spec A is affine, k(V/G)=k(V)^G when V is irreducible, and V/G is normal when V is. If V and the action are defined over a subfield, so is V/G.

title: Admissible representation of GL_n over a nonarchimedean local field
description: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with valuation ring O. A representation π of GL_n(F) on a complex vector space V is smooth if every vector is fixed by some open subgroup of GL_n(O), and admissible if moreover, for every open subgroup K of GL_n(O), the space V^K of K-fixed vectors is finite-dimensional. It is irreducible if V≠0 and V has no proper nonzero GL_n(F)-stable subspace.

title: Automorphic representation of a classical newform
description: For a normalized newform f of weight k, level N and character χ, write GL₂(A_ℚ)=GL₂(ℚ)·GL₂⁺(ℝ)·∏_pK_p with K_p the closure of Γ₀(N) in GL₂(ℤ_p), and put φ_f(γg_∞k)=(f|_k g_∞)(i)·χ(k). The right translates of φ_f span an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation π_f of GL₂(A_ℚ), a restricted tensor product ⊗′_vπ_v whose finite components π_p are irreducible admissible infinite-dimensional representations of GL₂(ℚ_p).

title: Kirillov model of an irreducible representation of GL₂
description: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field and ψ a nontrivial additive character. Every irreducible admissible infinite-dimensional representation π of GL₂(F) is realized, uniquely, on a space of locally constant functions on F^× containing the compactly supported ones, with (a b;0 1) acting by f(x)↦ψ(bx)f(ax) and the centre acting by the central character; for π supercuspidal the space is exactly the Schwartz–Bruhat functions on F^×.

title: Action of the Weyl element in the Kirillov model of a supercuspidal representation
description: In the Kirillov model of a supercuspidal representation of GL₂(F) with central character ω, the Mellin components f̂(ν,t)=∑_nt^n∫_(O^×)f(uϖ^n)ν(u)du transform under w=(0 1;−1 0) by (π(w)f)^(ν,t)=C(ν,t)f̂(ν⁻¹ω₀⁻¹,t⁻¹z₀⁻¹), where ω₀=ω|O^×, z₀=ω(ϖ), and each C(ν,t)=C₀(ν)t^(n_ν) is a monomial with n_ν≤−2 (Jacquet–Langlands).

title: Principal series representation of GL₂ over a nonarchimedean local field
description: For quasi-characters μ₁,μ₂ of F^×, B(μ₁,μ₂) is the representation of GL₂(F) by right translation on locally constant functions f with f((a b;0 d)g)=μ₁(a)μ₂(d)|a/d|^(1/2)f(g). It is admissible; it is irreducible unless μ₁μ₂⁻¹=|·|^(±1), when it has a one-dimensional constituent and an infinite-dimensional special constituent. The irreducible ones are the principal series.

title: Jacquet–Langlands classification of irreducible admissible representations of GL₂
description: Every irreducible admissible representation of GL₂ over a nonarchimedean local field is exactly one of: a one-dimensional representation χ∘det, an irreducible principal series B(μ₁,μ₂) (with B(μ₁,μ₂)≅B(μ₂,μ₁) the only coincidences), a special representation σ(μ|·|^(1/2),μ|·|^(−1/2)), or a supercuspidal representation, one whose matrix coefficients are compactly supported modulo the centre.

title: Spherical vectors of irreducible admissible representations of GL₂
description: An irreducible admissible representation of GL₂(F), F nonarchimedean, has nonzero GL₂(O)-fixed vectors only if it is a one-dimensional representation χ∘det or a principal series B(μ₁,μ₂) with μ₁,μ₂ unramified; the space of GL₂(O)-fixed vectors then has dimension one. Supercuspidal and special representations have no GL₂(O)-fixed vectors.

title: Multiplicity one for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL₂
description: Each irreducible representation of GL₂(A_F), F a number field, occurs at most once in the space of cusp forms on GL₂(F)∖GL₂(A_F) (Jacquet–Langlands).

title: Tensor product factorization of irreducible admissible representations of GL₂ over the adeles
description: Every irreducible admissible representation π of GL₂(A_F), F a number field, is a restricted tensor product ⊗′_vπ_v of irreducible admissible representations of the local groups GL₂(F_v), with π_v containing a GL₂(O_v)-fixed vector for almost all v; the local components are determined by π up to isomorphism.

title: Totally real number field
description: A number field F is totally real if every field embedding F→ℂ has image contained in ℝ.

title: Discrete series representation D_(k,w) of GL₂(ℝ)
description: For integers k≥2 and w of the same parity, D_(k,w) is the irreducible essentially square-integrable representation of GL₂(ℝ) occurring in the representation unitarily induced from the characters t↦|t|^((k−1−w)/2)sgn(t)^k and t↦|t|^((1−k−w)/2) of the diagonal torus; its central character is t↦t^(−w). These are the archimedean components of automorphic representations attached to holomorphic modular forms of weight k.

title: Essentially square-integrable representation of GL_n over a local field
description: An irreducible admissible representation π of GL_n(F), F a local field, is essentially square-integrable if some twist π⊗|det|^s has unitary central character and matrix coefficients square-integrable on GL_n(F) modulo its centre. For GL₂ over a nonarchimedean field these are the special and the supercuspidal representations.

title: Weil–Deligne representation of a nonarchimedean local field
description: For a nonarchimedean local field K with Weil group W_K and residue field of q elements, a Weil–Deligne representation over a field E of characteristic zero is a pair (ρ,N) of a homomorphism ρ:W_K→GL(V) on a finite-dimensional E-vector space, trivial on an open subgroup of inertia, and a nilpotent endomorphism N of V with ρ(w)Nρ(w)⁻¹=q^(−v(w))N, v(w) the power of geometric Frobenius induced by w. It is Frobenius-semisimple if ρ is semisimple. For E=E_λ with λ prime to q, w↦ρ(w)exp(t_λ(w)N) is a continuous λ-adic representation of W_K, its λ-adic realization; by Grothendieck's monodromy theorem every continuous λ-adic representation of W_K arises in this way.

title: Jacquet–Langlands local functional equation for GL₂
description: Let π be an irreducible admissible infinite-dimensional representation of GL₂(F), F nonarchimedean, with central character ω, realized in its Kirillov model for a nontrivial additive character ψ. The zeta integrals Z(s,f,χ)=∫_(F^×)f(a)χ(a)|a|^(s−1/2)d^×a, for f in the model and χ a character of F^×, converge for Re s≫0 and span a fractional ideal of ℂ[q^(±s)] with a unique generator L(s,χπ)=P(q^(−s))⁻¹, P(0)=1; and there is a unit ε(s,χπ,ψ) of ℂ[q^(±s)] with Z(1−s,π(w)f,χ⁻¹ω⁻¹)/L(1−s,χ⁻¹π̃)=ε(s,χπ,ψ)Z(s,f,χ)/L(s,χπ) for all f, where π̃ is the contragredient.

title: Local L- and ε-factors of Weil–Deligne representations
description: For a Weil–Deligne representation σ=(ρ,N) of a nonarchimedean local field K over ℂ, L(s,σ)=det(1−q^(−s)ρ(Φ)|V_N^(I))⁻¹ with Φ a geometric Frobenius and V_N^(I) the inertia invariants of ker N. There is a unique family of factors ε(s,σ,ψ), for nontrivial additive characters ψ, additive in exact sequences, inductive in degree zero, and equal to Tate's local constants for one-dimensional σ (Langlands, Deligne); ε(s,σ,ψ)=ε(0,σ,ψ)q^(−a(σ)s) for ψ of conductor O_K, with a(σ) the Artin conductor exponent.

title: Local Langlands correspondence for GL₂
description: For a nonarchimedean local field F there is a unique bijection π↦σ(π) from irreducible admissible infinite-dimensional representations of GL₂(F) to two-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations of F over ℂ (with ρ irreducible or N≠0 when σ is not a sum of characters) such that, for every character χ of F^×, L(s,χπ)=L(s,χ⊗σ(π)) and ε(s,χπ,ψ)=ε(s,χ⊗σ(π),ψ); then det σ(π) corresponds to the central character and σ(χπ)=χ⊗σ(π). It was established by Jacquet–Langlands, Tunnell and Kutzko. Carayol's Hecke normalization is σ(π̃⊗|·|^(1/2)) in this normalization, compatible with automorphisms of the coefficient field.

title: Strictly compatible system of λ-adic representations
description: For number fields F and E, a family (σ_λ) of continuous representations of Gal(F̄/F) on finite-dimensional E_λ-vector spaces, indexed by the finite places λ of E, is a strictly compatible system if there is a finite set S of finite places of F such that, for every finite place v∉S, σ_λ is unramified at v whenever v does not divide the residue characteristic of λ, and the characteristic polynomial of a Frobenius element at v has coefficients in E independent of λ.

title: Shimura curves attached to a quaternion algebra over a totally real field
description: Let F be totally real of degree d and B a quaternion algebra over F split at exactly one real place. For G=Res_(F/ℚ)B^× and small compact open K⊂G(A_f), the Shimura curve M_K, with M_K(ℂ)=G(ℚ)∖(G(A_f)×(ℂ∖ℝ))/K, is a proper smooth curve over F (affine modular curves when F=ℚ, B=M₂(ℚ)); the M_K form a projective system acted on by G(A_f).

title: Jacquet–Langlands correspondence between quaternion algebras and GL₂
description: For a quaternion algebra B over a number field F, there is an injection π′↦π from automorphic representations of B^×(A_F) that are not one-dimensional into cuspidal automorphic representations of GL₂(A_F), with π_v≅π′_v where B splits and π_v the essentially square-integrable representation corresponding to π′_v where B ramifies; its image consists of the π that are essentially square-integrable at every place where B ramifies. The local correspondence matches characters on regular elliptic elements.

title: Integral models and bad reduction of Shimura curves
description: For a Shimura curve M_K over a totally real field F attached to a quaternion algebra split at a finite place 𝔭 and level K=K^𝔭·K_𝔭 with K_𝔭 a principal congruence subgroup, Carayol constructs a regular model over O_(F,𝔭) via Drinfeld level structures on divisible O_𝔭-modules of height two; its special fibre is a union of Igusa-type curves meeting at supersingular points, whose completed local rings are universal deformation rings of formal O_𝔭-modules of height two with level structure.

title: Vanishing cycles exact sequence for a curve over a henselian discrete valuation ring
description: For a proper flat curve X over a henselian discrete valuation ring with special fibre X_s, generic geometric fibre X_η̄ and ℓ invertible, there is a Galois-equivariant long exact sequence relating H^i(X_s̄,Λ), H^i(X_η̄,Λ) and the vanishing cycles R^iΦΛ at the singular points; for semistable X the vanishing cycles are concentrated at the double points and the monodromy N is given by the Picard–Lefschetz formula (SGA 7).

title: Semistable reduction theorem for curves
description: A smooth proper geometrically connected curve over the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring acquires semistable reduction after a finite separable extension of the base: it extends to a proper flat model whose special fibre is reduced with only ordinary double points (Deligne–Mumford).

title: Universal deformations of formal modules with Drinfeld level structure
description: For a nonarchimedean local field F with valuation ring O, a one-dimensional formal O-module of height h over the algebraic closure of the residue field has a universal deformation over a formal power series ring in h−1 variables over the completed maximal unramified extension of O (Lubin–Tate); adding Drinfeld level-𝔭^n structures gives finite flat regular local covers, carrying commuting actions of GL_h(O) and of the units of the division algebra of invariant 1/h (Drinfeld).

title: Galois representations of Hilbert modular forms at almost all places
description: For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F), F totally real, with archimedean components D_(k_τ,w), k_τ≥2 (and, for [F:ℚ] even, essentially square-integrable at some finite place), there is a strictly compatible system of two-dimensional λ-adic Galois representations whose restriction to the Weil group at almost every finite place corresponds to π_𝔭 by the Hecke correspondence; it is cut out from the ℓ-adic cohomology of Shimura curves via the Eichler–Shimura congruence relation (Ohta; Rogawski–Tunnell; for F=ℚ Eichler–Shimura–Deligne).

title: Automorphic induction from a Hecke character of a quadratic extension
description: For a quadratic extension L/F of number fields and a Hecke character ξ of A_L^× not factoring through the norm, the Weil representation construction gives a cuspidal automorphic representation π(ξ) of GL₂(A_F) whose local components are the representations attached to (L_v/F_v,ξ_v), so that its L-function is L(s,ξ) and at each place it corresponds to the induced representation of the local character (Jacquet–Langlands §12).

title: Langlands base change for GL₂
description: For a cyclic extension L/F of number fields of prime degree, every cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F) has a base change Π to GL₂(A_L), automorphic, whose local components are the local base changes of π_v; at unramified places it corresponds to restriction of the Satake parameters, and locally base change corresponds to restriction of Weil–Deligne representations (Langlands 1980).

title: Langlands–Tunnell theorem
description: Every continuous two-dimensional complex representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field with solvable image, in particular of tetrahedral or octahedral projective type, is automorphic: there is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂ whose local components correspond to its local restrictions at every place (Artin conjecture for these representations).

title: Globalization of primitive local Galois representations
description: Given an irreducible primitive two-dimensional representation σ of the Weil group of a p-adic field F with finite image, there are a number field k, a place v₀ of k with k_(v₀)≅F, and a Galois representation of k of tetrahedral or octahedral projective type with finite image whose restriction to the decomposition group at v₀ is σ (Tunnell 1978, Theorem 1.3).

title: Finite subgroups of PGL₂(ℂ)
description: Every finite subgroup of PGL₂(ℂ)≅SO(3,ℂ) is cyclic, dihedral, or isomorphic to the tetrahedral group A₄, the octahedral group S₄ or the icosahedral group A₅.

title: Local Galois representations of classical modular forms at bad primes via modular curves
description: For a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_ℚ) attached to a newform of weight ≥2 and every prime p≠ℓ at which the local component is not supercuspidal extraordinary, the restriction to the Weil group at p of its ℓ-adic Galois representation corresponds to the local component under the Hecke correspondence; this was proved by Langlands and Deligne from the bad reduction of modular curves (Deligne, 'Formes modulaires et représentations de GL(2)', and letter to Piatetski-Shapiro).

title: Atom of a Markov chain
description: For a Markov kernel P on a measurable space, a measurable set α is an atom if all its points have the same transition law: there is a probability measure ν with P(x,·)=ν for every x∈α. For a ψ-irreducible chain, an atom with ψ(α)>0 is called accessible.

title: Maximal irreducibility measure of a Markov kernel
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel P, an irreducibility measure ψ′ is maximal if every irreducibility measure of P is absolutely continuous with respect to ψ′. Maximal irreducibility measures exist and are mutually absolutely continuous, so the sets of positive maximal measure depend only on P.

title: Positive recurrent ψ-irreducible Markov chain
description: A ψ-irreducible Markov chain is recurrent if ∑_{n≥1}Pⁿ(x,A)=∞ for every state x and every measurable set A of positive maximal irreducibility measure. It is positive recurrent if it is recurrent and admits an invariant probability measure.

title: f-geometrically regular set of a Markov chain
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain and a measurable f≥1, a measurable set A is f-geometrically regular if for every measurable B of positive maximal irreducibility measure there is r>1 with sup_{x∈A}E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_B−1}f(X_k)r^k]<∞, where τ_B=inf{n≥1:X_n∈B} is the first return time to B. For f=1 such a set is called geometrically regular.

title: m-skeleton of a Markov chain
description: For an integer m≥1, the m-skeleton of a Markov chain with kernel P is the Markov chain with kernel Pᵐ, the m-fold iterate of P; observing a chain (X_n) at the times 0,m,2m,… gives the m-skeleton (X_{mn}).

title: Petite sets have maximal irreducibility minorizations
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel P on a countably generated state space, every petite set A is ψ_b-petite for some sampling distribution b: ∑_n b(n)Pⁿ(x,·)≥ψ_b on A, where ψ_b is a maximal irreducibility measure. Consequently inf_{x∈A}P_x(τ_B<∞)>0 for every set B of positive maximal irreducibility measure.

title: Cyclic decomposition of a ψ-irreducible Markov chain
description: Let P be ψ-irreducible with ψ maximal, and let C be a ν_M-small set with ψ(C)>0 and ν_M(C)>0. Let d be the greatest common divisor of E_C={n≥1: Pⁿ(x,·)≥δ_nν_M on C for some δ_n>0}. Then there are disjoint measurable D_1,…,D_d with P(x,D_{i+1})=1 for x∈D_i (indices mod d) and ψ-null complement of their union; d is the largest length of such a cycle, independent of C. Hence the chain is aperiodic exactly when d=1.

title: Nonempty absorbing sets of a ψ-irreducible chain are full
description: If a Markov chain is ψ-irreducible, every nonempty absorbing set A is full: its complement is null for a maximal irreducibility measure.

title: Sublevel sets of a drift function towards a petite set are petite
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain, if V:X→[0,∞] satisfies PV≤V−1+b1_C for a petite set C and b<∞, then every sublevel set {V≤ℓ} with ℓ<∞ is petite: V is unbounded off petite sets. In particular this holds when V≥1 satisfies the geometric drift PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C with β>0.

title: Regular sets of a ψ-irreducible chain are petite
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain on a countably generated state space, call a measurable set A regular if sup_{x∈A}E_x[τ_B]<∞ for every measurable B of positive maximal irreducibility measure, with τ_B the first return time to B. Every regular set is petite.

title: Sure return to a set implies infinitely many returns
description: For a Markov chain and a measurable set A with first return time τ_A=inf{n≥1:X_n∈A}, if P_x(τ_A<∞)=1 for every x∈A, then for every initial state x the probability of visiting A infinitely often equals P_x(τ_A<∞); in particular A is visited infinitely often almost surely from each of its points.

title: Skeletons of an aperiodic ψ-irreducible Markov chain
description: If a Markov chain on a countably generated state space is ψ-irreducible and aperiodic, then every m-skeleton (the chain with kernel Pᵐ) is ψ-irreducible and aperiodic, and some m-skeleton is strongly aperiodic: there are a set A and a measure ν with ν(A)>0 and Pᵐ(x,·)≥ν for every x∈A.

title: Regenerative decomposition for a Markov chain with an atom
description: Let a positive Harris recurrent Markov chain with invariant probability π have an accessible atom α with first return time τ_α. Put a_λ(n)=P_λ(τ_α=n), u(n)=Pⁿ(α,α) and t_f(n)=E_α[f(X_n)1{τ_α≥n}]. Then for every initial law λ, f≥0 and n≥1, |E_λf(X_n)−π(f)|≤E_λ[f(X_n)1{τ_α≥n}]+(|a_λ∗u−π(α)|∗t_f)(n)+π(α)∑_{j>n}t_f(j), where ∗ is convolution of sequences on the positive integers.

title: Geometric convergence at a Kendall atom
description: If a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain has an accessible atom α that is a Kendall atom, E_α[κ^{τ_α}]<∞ for some κ>1 with τ_α the first return time, then the chain has an invariant probability π and there are r>1 and R<∞ with |Pⁿ(α,α)−π(α)|≤Rr^{−n} for every n≥0.

title: Erdős–Feller–Pollard renewal theorem
description: Let p be a probability distribution on the positive integers whose support has greatest common divisor 1 and whose mean is m≤∞, and define the renewal sequence u(0)=1, u(n)=∑_{k=1}^{n}p(k)u(n−k). Then u(n)→1/m as n→∞, with 1/m=0 when m=∞.

title: Return-time representation of the invariant measure of a recurrent chain
description: For a recurrent ψ-irreducible Markov chain on a countably generated state space, the invariant measure π is unique up to constant multiples and equivalent to a maximal irreducibility measure, and for every set A of positive maximal irreducibility measure and measurable B, π(B)=∫_Aπ(dy)E_y[∑_{k=1}^{τ_A}1_B(X_k)]=∫_Aπ(dy)E_y[∑_{k=0}^{τ_A−1}1_B(X_k)], where τ_A is the first return time to A.

title: Petite sets admit sampling distributions with finite mean
description: For a ψ-irreducible Markov kernel on a countably generated state space, every petite set is also petite for a uniform sampling distribution on {1,…,m} for some m, or for a geometric sampling distribution a_ε(n)=(1−ε)εⁿ; either choice has finite mean ∑_n n a(n).

title: Spanning of the symmetric subspace by tensor powers
description: For n,t≥1, the symmetric subspace Sym^t(ℂⁿ)⊆(ℂⁿ)^(⊗t) is the linear span of the tensor powers v^(⊗t), v∈ℂⁿ. Indeed it suffices to take v with all coordinates in any fixed set A⊆ℂ with at least t+1 elements.

title: Averaging projection onto the invariant vectors of a unitary representation
description: Let G be a group with a left-invariant probability measure μ, such as normalized Haar measure on a compact group or the uniform measure on a finite group, and let R be a unitary representation of G on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space V with g↦R(g) measurable. Then Π=∫_G R(g)dμ(g) is the orthogonal projection onto the fixed subspace V^G={v:R(g)v=v for all g∈G}.

title: Number of multisets of a given size (stars and bars)
description: For integers n≥1 and k≥0, the number of multisets of size k with elements from an n-element set, equivalently of functions φ:{1,…,n}→ℕ with φ(1)+⋯+φ(n)=k, is binom(n+k−1,k)=binom(n+k−1,n−1).

title: Oseledets multiplicative ergodic theorem for real matrix cocycles
description: Let T preserve a probability measure on X and let A:X→GL(d,ℝ) be measurable with log‖A‖ and log‖A⁻¹‖ integrable; put A_n(x)=A(Tⁿ⁻¹x)⋯A(x). For almost every x the limit Λ(x)=lim_n(A_n(x)ᵀA_n(x))^(1/2n) exists. If e^(χ₁)<⋯<e^(χ_s) are its eigenvalues, with eigenspaces of dimensions k_i, and V_i is the sum of the eigenspaces for χ₁,…,χ_i, then lim n⁻¹log‖A_n(x)v‖=χ_i for v∈V_i∖V_(i−1). The exponents and multiplicities are T-invariant functions, and ∑k_iχ_i=lim n⁻¹log|det A_n(x)|.

title: Ergodicity of Bernoulli shifts on a finite alphabet
description: For a finite set S and a probability vector p with positive entries, the left shift T on S^ℕ preserves the Bernoulli measure μ, determined by μ[a₀,…,a_(n−1)]=p_(a₀)⋯p_(a_(n−1)) on cylinders, and is mixing: μ(E∩T⁻ᵏF)→μ(E)μ(F) for all measurable E,F. In particular (S^ℕ,μ,T) is ergodic.

title: Locally finite k-linear abelian category
description: A k-linear abelian category over a field k is locally finite if every morphism space is finite-dimensional and every object has finite length.

title: Finite k-linear abelian category
description: A k-linear abelian category is finite if it is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional left modules over a finite-dimensional associative k-algebra.

title: Multitensor category
description: A locally finite k-linear abelian rigid monoidal category whose tensor product bifunctor is bilinear on morphisms. The unit object need not be simple; a finite multitensor category is one whose underlying abelian category is finite.

title: Dual category of a module category over a multitensor category
description: For a module category M over a multitensor category C, the dual category C*_M=Fun_C(M,M) is the category of right exact C-module endofunctors of M and module natural transformations, made monoidal by composition of functors.

title: Deligne tensor product of multitensor categories
description: For multitensor categories C and D over k, the Deligne tensor product C⊠D is a multitensor category with tensor product determined by (X⊠Y)⊗(X′⊠Y′)=(X⊗X′)⊠(Y⊗Y′), unit 1⊠1, and associativity constraints and duals induced from those of C and D.

title: Existence and exactness of the Deligne tensor product
description: For locally finite k-linear abelian categories C and D, a Deligne tensor product C⊠D exists, is locally finite and is unique up to unique equivalence; for coalgebras it is (C⊗D)-comod. The functor ⊠ is exact in each variable with Hom(X₁⊠X₂,Y₁⊠Y₂)≅Hom(X₁,Y₁)⊗Hom(X₂,Y₂), and bilinear bifunctors exact in each variable induce exact functors on C⊠D.

title: Module endofunctors of the regular module category
description: For a multitensor category C regarded as a left module category over itself, every C-module endofunctor of C is isomorphic to right tensoring −⊗X by an object X, with module structure given by the associativity constraint, and X↦(−⊗X) is a tensor equivalence C^op→C*_C.

title: Stochastic Fubini theorem for continuous semimartingales
description: Let X be a continuous semimartingale, μ a finite measure on a measurable space A, and H(a,t,ω) bounded and measurable for the product of the σ-algebra of A with the predictable σ-algebra. Then a↦∫₀ᵗH(a,s)dX_s has a measurable version and ∫_A(∫₀ᵗH(a,s)dX_s)μ(da)=∫₀ᵗ(∫_AH(a,s)μ(da))dX_s almost surely.

title: Representation of a convex function by its second-derivative measure
description: If f:ℝ→ℝ is convex and the Stieltjes measure f″(da) of its left derivative is finite, then there are constants α,β with f(x)=α+βx+½∫|x−a|f″(da) and f′₋(x)=β+½∫sgn(x−a)f″(da) for all x, where sgn(0)=−1.

title: Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold
description: For a Riemannian manifold (M,g) with Levi-Civita connection ∇ and R(X,Y)=∇_X∇_Y−∇_Y∇_X−∇_[X,Y], the (0,4)-tensor Rm(X,Y,Z,W)=g(R(X,Y)W,Z), normalized so that Rm(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₂) is the sectional curvature of an orthonormal pair (the convention of Brendle–Schoen, who write R(X,Y,Z,W) and R_ijkl). At each point it is an algebraic curvature tensor: antisymmetric in each pair, symmetric under exchanging the pairs, and satisfying the first Bianchi identity.

title: Algebraic curvature tensor on a Euclidean vector space
description: A 4-linear form R on a Euclidean space V≅ℝⁿ with R(x,y,z,w)=−R(y,x,z,w)=−R(x,y,w,z)=R(z,w,x,y) and R(x,y,z,w)+R(y,z,x,w)+R(z,x,y,w)=0. Equivalently a self-adjoint endomorphism of ∧²V satisfying the first Bianchi identity (an algebraic curvature operator); the space of these is written S²_B(so(n)) and carries the natural action of O(n). The curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold at a point is an algebraic curvature tensor.

title: First Bianchi identity for the Riemann curvature tensor
description: The Riemann curvature tensor of a Riemannian manifold (more generally of any torsion-free connection) satisfies R(X,Y)Z+R(Y,Z)X+R(Z,X)Y=0; in covariant form Rm(x,y,z,w)+Rm(y,z,x,w)+Rm(z,x,y,w)=0.

title: Sectional curvature of a two-plane
description: For a two-plane π⊂T_pM spanned by an orthonormal pair e₁,e₂, the sectional curvature is K(π)=Rm(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₂), independent of the orthonormal basis of π; the same formula defines the sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor. Positive (nonnegative) sectional curvature means K(π)>0 (≥0) for all two-planes.

title: Ricci curvature tensor
description: The symmetric 2-tensor Ric(x,y)=Σᵢ Rm(x,eᵢ,y,eᵢ), the trace of the curvature tensor over an orthonormal basis eᵢ; it is defined for Riemannian manifolds and for algebraic curvature tensors. Its trace-free part is Ric₀=Ric−(scal/n)g. Positive Ricci curvature means Ric(x,x)>0 for x≠0.

title: Scalar curvature
description: The trace scal=Σᵢ Ric(eᵢ,eᵢ) of the Ricci tensor with respect to the metric; for an algebraic curvature tensor it is Σ_{i,j}R(eᵢ,eⱼ,eᵢ,eⱼ).

title: Curvature operator of an algebraic curvature tensor
description: The self-adjoint endomorphism ℛ of ∧²T_pM (or of ∧²ℝⁿ for an algebraic curvature tensor R) determined by ⟨ℛ(x∧y),z∧w⟩=R(x,y,z,w), so that R(φ,φ)=⟨ℛφ,φ⟩ is a quadratic form on two-vectors. The curvature operator is nonnegative (positive) if R(φ,φ)≥0 (>0) for all φ≠0; nonnegative curvature operator implies nonnegative sectional curvature.

title: Spherical space form
description: A Riemannian manifold Sⁿ/Γ obtained as the quotient of the round unit sphere by a finite subgroup Γ⊂O(n+1) acting freely, with the induced metric of constant sectional curvature 1; up to scaling these are exactly the compact connected Riemannian manifolds of constant positive sectional curvature.

title: Killing–Hopf theorem for constant positive curvature
description: A complete connected Riemannian n-manifold (n≥2) of constant sectional curvature 1 is isometric to Sⁿ/Γ for a finite subgroup Γ⊂O(n+1) acting freely on Sⁿ; in particular a simply connected one is isometric to the round unit sphere.

title: Isometry group of a Riemannian manifold
description: The group Isom(M,g) of diffeomorphisms F:M→M with F*g=g, under composition.

title: Pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvature
description: A Riemannian manifold has pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures if its sectional curvatures are positive and at every point p, 0<K(π₁)<4K(π₂) for all two-planes π₁,π₂⊂T_pM; the ratio bound is required at each point separately, so no global curvature bounds are assumed.

title: Positive and nonnegative isotropic curvature
description: An algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ, n≥4, has nonnegative isotropic curvature if R₁₃₁₃+R₁₄₁₄+R₂₃₂₃+R₂₄₂₄−2R₁₂₃₄≥0 for every orthonormal four-frame {e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄}, and positive isotropic curvature (PIC) if the inequality is always strict; a Riemannian manifold of dimension at least four has PIC if its curvature tensor does at every point. Equivalently, the complexified curvature is positive on totally isotropic two-planes span{e₁+ie₂,e₃+ie₄} of T_pM⊗ℂ.

title: Ricci flow
description: A smooth one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics g(t) on a manifold M satisfying ∂g/∂t=−2Ric_{g(t)}, introduced by Hamilton in 1982.

title: Normalized Ricci flow
description: On a compact n-manifold, the volume-preserving flow ∂g/∂t=−2Ric_{g(t)}+(2/n)r_{g(t)}g(t), where r_{g(t)} is the mean value of the scalar curvature of g(t); its solutions differ from Ricci flows by rescaling the metric and reparametrizing time.

title: Hamilton's evolution equation for the curvature tensor under Ricci flow
description: Under Ricci flow, the curvature tensor written in an orthonormal frame evolving with the metric (Uhlenbeck's trick) satisfies ∂R/∂t=ΔR+Q(R), where Q(R)_{ijkl}=R_{ijpq}R_{klpq}+2R_{ipkq}R_{jplq}−2R_{iplq}R_{jpkq} is an O(n)-equivariant quadratic map on algebraic curvature tensors. The associated ODE dR/dt=Q(R) on S²_B(so(n)) is Hamilton's curvature ODE.

title: Hamilton's maximum principle for curvature conditions under Ricci flow
description: Let g(t) be a Ricci flow on a compact manifold and K a closed, convex, O(n)-invariant set of algebraic curvature tensors that is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R). If the curvature tensor of g(0) lies in K at every point (in orthonormal frames), then the curvature tensor of g(t) lies in K at every point for all t in the interval of existence. This is the Ricci-flow case of Hamilton's maximum principle for reaction–diffusion systems on vector bundles (Hamilton 1986, Theorem 4.3).

title: Short-time existence and uniqueness of Ricci flow on compact manifolds
description: For every smooth Riemannian metric g₀ on a compact manifold there is T>0 and a smooth Ricci flow g(t), t∈[0,T), with g(0)=g₀, and any two such flows agree on their common interval (Hamilton 1982; simplified proof via DeTurck's trick). By uniqueness and diffeomorphism invariance of the equation, isometries of g₀ remain isometries of every g(t).

title: Kulkarni–Nomizu product of symmetric bilinear forms
description: For symmetric bilinear forms A,B on ℝⁿ, the 4-tensor (A⊙B)_{ijkl}=A_{ik}B_{jl}−A_{il}B_{jk}−A_{jk}B_{il}+A_{jl}B_{ik}, which is an algebraic curvature tensor; with this normalization I=½ id⊙id is the curvature tensor of the round unit sphere.

title: Böhm–Wilking linear transformation ℓ_{a,b} of algebraic curvature tensors
description: For real a,b, the linear map ℓ_{a,b}(R)=R+b Ric₀⊙id+(a/n) scal id⊙id on algebraic curvature tensors on ℝⁿ, as printed by Brendle–Schoen; Böhm–Wilking display it as R+2(n−1)a R_I+(n−2)b R_{Ric₀}, and the parameter curves used in Brendle–Schoen Propositions 13-14 coincide with those of Böhm–Wilking Lemmas 3.4-3.5. Böhm and Wilking showed that ℓ_{a,b}^{-1}Q(ℓ_{a,b}R)−Q(R) does not depend on the Weyl part of R and is computable from the Ricci tensor, which allows Q-invariant cones to be deformed into new invariant cones.

title: Böhm–Wilking invariant cones ℓ_{a,b}(nonnegative curvature operators with Ricci pinching)
description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Lemmas 3.4–3.5): for b∈[0,1/2] with a=((n−2)b²+2b)/(2+2(n−2)b²), p=(n−2)b²/(1+(n−2)b²), and for b=1/2, a=(1+s)/2, p=1−4/(n+2+4s), s≥0, the sets ℓ_{a,b}({R≥0 : Ric≥(p/n) scal}) built from the cone of nonnegative curvature operators are invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R), transversally so for b>0; together they join the nonnegative cone to cones shrinking to the ray of the round-sphere curvature tensor.

title: Pinching family of cones (Böhm–Wilking)
description: Böhm–Wilking (2008, §3): a continuous family C(s), s∈[0,1), of closed convex O(n)-invariant full-dimensional cones of algebraic curvature tensors such that every nonzero element has positive scalar curvature, Q(R) lies in the interior of the tangent cone of C(s) at every nonzero R∈C(s) for s∈(0,1), and C(s) converges in the pointed Hausdorff topology to the ray ℝ₊I of the round-sphere curvature tensor as s→1.

title: Böhm–Wilking convergence theorem for pinching families
description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Theorem 5.1): let C(s), s∈[0,1), be a pinching family of cones in dimension n≥3. If the curvature tensor of a compact Riemannian manifold (M,g₀) lies in the interior of C(0) at every point, then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature.

title: Hamilton's convergence theorem for Ricci flow with curvature in a pinching set
description: Hamilton (J. Differential Geom. 1986, §5): if the curvature tensor of a compact Riemannian manifold (M,g₀) lies at every point in a pinching set, a closed convex O(n)-invariant set of algebraic curvature tensors preserved by dR/dt=Q(R) on which the trace-free part of R becomes small relative to the scalar curvature as the curvature grows, then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature. The exact quantitative form of Hamilton's pinching condition is not verified here.

title: Tangent cone of a closed convex set
description: For a closed convex set C in a finite-dimensional real vector space and x∈C, the tangent cone T_xC is the closure of ⋃_{t>0} t(C−x); a vector in the interior of T_xC points strictly into C.

title: Berger's curvature inequality
description: If all sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor R (for example of a Riemannian manifold at a point) lie in [K_min,K_max], then |R(e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄)|≤(2/3)(K_max−K_min) and |R(e₁,e₂,e₁,e₃)|≤(1/2)(K_max−K_min) for all orthonormal e₁,…,e₄.

title: Orthogonal normal form of a real skew-symmetric bilinear form
description: For a skew-symmetric bilinear form ω on a Euclidean space, equivalently a real skew-symmetric matrix or a two-vector, there is an orthonormal basis v₁,…,v_n with ω=a₁v₁∧v₂+a₂v₃∧v₄+⋯; that is, the matrix is block diagonal with 2×2 blocks [[0,a_k],[−a_k,0]] and zeros. On ℝ⁴ the basis may be taken positively oriented.

title: Self-dual and anti-self-dual two-forms in dimension four
description: On an oriented four-dimensional Euclidean space V the Hodge star *:∧²V→∧²V satisfies *²=1 and φ∧ψ=⟨*φ,ψ⟩vol; ∧²V splits orthogonally into the three-dimensional eigenspaces ∧²₊ (self-dual, *φ=φ) and ∧²₋ (anti-self-dual, *φ=−φ), and φ∧φ=(|φ₊|²−|φ₋|²)vol.

title: Brendle–Schoen differentiable sphere theorem for pointwise 1/4-pinched manifolds
description: A compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures (at each point 0<K(π₁)<4K(π₂) for all two-planes) admits a metric of constant positive sectional curvature, and is therefore diffeomorphic to a spherical space form.
