In particular a compact simply connected manifold whose sectional curvatures lie in (1,4] is diffeomorphic to Sⁿ, settling the differentiable version of the Rauch–Berger–Klingenberg sphere theorem. The proof deforms the metric by the normalized Ricci flow.

title: Equivariant differentiable sphere theorem for pointwise 1/4-pinched manifolds
description: Let M be a compact simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures, G a compact Lie group and ρ:G→Isom(M) a homomorphism. Then there are a homomorphism σ:G→O(n+1) and a diffeomorphism F:M→Sⁿ with F∘ρ(g)=σ(g)∘F for all g∈G. It follows because the normalized Ricci flow deforms the metric canonically, hence G-equivariantly, to a round metric.

title: Brendle–Schoen convergence theorem for Ricci flow under positive complex sectional curvature (strict PIC2)
description: Let (M,g₀) be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 such that R₁₃₁₃+λ²R₁₄₁₄+μ²R₂₃₂₃+λ²μ²R₂₄₂₄−2λμR₁₂₃₄>0 for all orthonormal four-frames and all λ,μ∈[−1,1]; equivalently, at every point the curvature tensor lies in the interior of the cone of tensors whose zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature, i.e. g₀ has positive complex sectional curvature. Then the normalized Ricci flow from g₀ exists for all time and converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature.

title: Preservation of positive isotropic curvature under Ricci flow in all dimensions
description: For n≥4, the set of algebraic curvature tensors on ℝⁿ with nonnegative isotropic curvature is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R); consequently, on a compact manifold of dimension n≥4, nonnegative isotropic curvature and positive isotropic curvature of g(0) are preserved along the Ricci flow g(t).

title: Nonnegative complex sectional curvature (PIC2 cone Ĉ)
description: An algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ has nonnegative complex sectional curvature if R(Z,W,Z̄,W̄)≥0 for all Z,W∈ℂⁿ, with R extended complex-multilinearly. Equivalently, its zero extension R̂ to ℝⁿ×ℝ², the curvature tensor of M×ℝ², has nonnegative isotropic curvature (Ni–Wolfson 2007, Prop. 5.1, after N. Wallach and a communication from Brendle–Schoen). These tensors form a closed convex O(n)-invariant cone Ĉ that contains every nonnegative curvature operator and lies in the cone of nonnegative sectional curvature; its interior is positive complex sectional curvature (strict PIC2).

title: PIC1 condition: positive isotropic curvature of M×ℝ
description: For an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ let R̃ be its extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ by zero in the added direction, i.e. the curvature tensor of M×ℝ. R satisfies PIC1 if R̃ has positive isotropic curvature (nonnegative PIC1 if R̃ has nonnegative isotropic curvature). PIC1 implies R₁₂₁₂+R₁₃₁₃>0 for all orthonormal three-frames (2-positive flag curvature) and hence positive Ricci curvature.

title: Ricci flow preserves nonnegative complex sectional curvature (PIC2)
description: For n≥4, the cone Ĉ of algebraic curvature tensors whose zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature (equivalently, nonnegative complex sectional curvature) is invariant under Hamilton's ODE dR/dt=Q(R), because zero extension commutes with Q; hence the condition is preserved by Ricci flow on compact manifolds. The same argument on ℝⁿ×ℝ shows that PIC1 is preserved.

title: Brendle–Schoen characterization of the PIC2 condition
description: For an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ (n≥4), the zero extension R̂ to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature if and only if R(e₁,e₃,e₁,e₃)+λ²R(e₁,e₄,e₁,e₄)+μ²R(e₂,e₃,e₂,e₃)+λ²μ²R(e₂,e₄,e₂,e₄)−2λμR(e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄)≥0 for all orthonormal four-frames {e₁,…,e₄} of ℝⁿ and all λ,μ∈[−1,1].

title: Pointwise 1/4-pinched curvature implies nonnegative complex sectional curvature
description: If all sectional curvatures of an algebraic curvature tensor R on ℝⁿ lie in [κ,4κ] with κ≥0, then R has nonnegative complex sectional curvature; equivalently, its zero extension to ℝⁿ×ℝ² has nonnegative isotropic curvature. If the sectional curvatures are strictly pointwise 1/4-pinched, R has positive complex sectional curvature. Yau–Zheng (1991) state the sign-reversed form for negatively 1/4-pinched curvature.

title: Böhm–Wilking pinching set theorem
description: Böhm–Wilking (Ann. of Math. 2008, Theorem 4.1): given a continuous family C(s), s∈[0,1), of closed convex O(n)-invariant full-dimensional cones whose nonzero elements have positive scalar curvature and on whose nonzero elements Q points into the interior of the tangent cone for s∈(0,1), and given ε,h₀>0, there is a closed convex O(n)-invariant set F, invariant under dR/dt=Q(R), with C(ε)∩{tr R≤h₀}⊂F and F∖C(s) bounded for every s∈[ε,1) (a generalized pinching set).

title: Rauch–Berger–Klingenberg topological sphere theorem
description: A compact simply connected Riemannian n-manifold whose sectional curvatures lie in (1,4] is homeomorphic to Sⁿ. Rauch posed the problem and proved a version with a stronger pinching constant; Berger and Klingenberg proved the 1/4-pinched statement around 1960 by comparison geometry.

title: Globally δ-pinched Riemannian manifold
description: For 0<δ≤1, a Riemannian manifold is globally δ-pinched if, after scaling, all its sectional curvatures at all points lie in (1,1/δ]; for δ=1/4 this is the hypothesis of the topological sphere theorem.

title: Gromoll–Calabi differentiable sphere theorem
description: For each n there is δ(n)∈(0,1), with δ(n)→1 as n→∞, such that every compact simply connected globally δ(n)-pinched Riemannian n-manifold is diffeomorphic to Sⁿ (Gromoll 1966, and independently Calabi). Later work (Sugimoto–Shiohama–Karcher, Ruh, Grove–Karcher–Ruh) obtained pinching constants independent of n.

title: Grove–Karcher–Ruh equivariant sphere theorem
description: There is a universal constant δ<1 (δ=0.98 in the original, later improved by Im Hof–Ruh) such that if a compact Lie group G acts by isometries on a compact simply connected globally δ-pinched Riemannian n-manifold M, then M is G-equivariantly diffeomorphic to Sⁿ with a linear orthogonal G-action.

title: Hamilton's theorem on three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature
description: A compact three-manifold with a Riemannian metric of positive Ricci curvature admits a metric of constant positive sectional curvature: the normalized Ricci flow exists for all time and converges to such a metric (Hamilton 1982).

title: Hamilton's theorem on four-manifolds with positive curvature operator
description: A compact four-manifold with a metric of positive curvature operator is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form (S⁴ or ℝP⁴): the normalized Ricci flow converges to a constant curvature metric (Hamilton 1986).

title: H. Chen's theorem on four-manifolds with 2-positive curvature operator
description: H. Chen (Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 1991): a compact four-manifold with 2-positive curvature operator is diffeomorphic to S⁴ or ℝP⁴ (via Ricci flow), and a compact pointwise 1/4-pinched four-manifold is diffeomorphic to S⁴ or ℝP⁴ or, in the weakly pinched case, isometric to ℂP² up to scaling.

title: Andrews–Nguyen theorem on four-manifolds with 1/4-pinched flag curvature
description: Compact four-manifolds with pointwise 1/4-pinched flag curvature (in the sense of Andrews–Nguyen) are diffeomorphic to spherical space forms; proved with the Ricci flow.

title: Huisken's theorem: sufficiently pinched manifolds are space forms
description: For each n≥4 there is ε(n)>0 such that a compact n-manifold of positive scalar curvature whose curvature tensor is pointwise ε(n)-close to constant curvature, in the sense that the Weyl and trace-free Ricci parts are small relative to the scalar curvature, is deformed by the normalized Ricci flow to a metric of constant curvature (Huisken 1985; also Margerin, Nishikawa).

title: Böhm–Wilking theorem: manifolds with 2-positive curvature operator are space forms
description: On a compact Riemannian manifold with 2-positive curvature operator (in particular positive curvature operator), the normalized Ricci flow converges to a metric of constant positive sectional curvature, so the manifold is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form (Böhm–Wilking, Ann. of Math. 2008). The theorem was previously known in dimensions at most four (Hamilton, Chen).

title: Micallef–Moore sphere theorem for positive isotropic curvature
description: A compact simply connected Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with positive isotropic curvature is a homotopy sphere, hence homeomorphic to Sⁿ by the generalized Poincaré conjecture; the proof uses minimal two-spheres from the variational theory of the energy of maps S²→M and an index estimate from the second variation (Micallef–Moore 1988).

title: Ricci flow with surgery
description: A procedure that runs the Ricci flow until high-curvature regions form, cuts along nearly round necks, caps the pieces with standard caps and restarts the flow, with controlled surgery parameters. Introduced by Hamilton for four-manifolds with positive isotropic curvature and developed by Perelman in dimension three; Chen–Zhu completed the four-dimensional positive isotropic curvature case.

title: Brendle–Schoen classification of manifolds with weakly 1/4-pinched curvature
description: A compact Riemannian manifold of dimension n≥4 with pointwise weakly 1/4-pinched sectional curvatures (0≤K(π₁)≤4K(π₂) at each point) is either diffeomorphic to a spherical space form or isometric to a locally symmetric space (Brendle–Schoen, Acta Math. 2008).

title: Compact rank one symmetric space
description: A compact Riemannian symmetric space of rank one: a round sphere, real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley projective plane. With suitably normalized canonical metrics the complex, quaternionic and Cayley projective spaces have sectional curvatures ranging over [1,4] at every point.

title: 2-positive curvature operator
description: An algebraic curvature tensor (or a Riemannian manifold, at every point) has 2-positive curvature operator if the sum of the two smallest eigenvalues of its curvature operator on ∧² is positive, and 2-nonnegative curvature operator if this sum is nonnegative.

title: Nonnegativity of the trace of a product of positive semidefinite matrices
description: If A and B are real symmetric positive semidefinite n×n matrices, then tr(AB)≥0.
